paper_title: Turning up the heat on COVID-19: heat as a therapeutic intervention
paper_abstract: Enveloped viruses such as SAR-CoV-2 are sensitive to heat and are destroyed by temperatures tolerable to humans. All mammals use fever to deal with infections and heat has been used throughout human history in the form of hot springs, saunas, hammams, steam-rooms, sweat-lodges, steam inhalations, hot mud and poultices to prevent and treat respiratory infections and enhance health and wellbeing. This paper reviews the evidence for using heat to treat and prevent viral infections and discusses potential cellular, physiological and psychological mechanisms of action. In the initial phase of infection, heat applied to the upper airways can support the immune system’s first line of defence by supporting muco-ciliary clearance and inhibiting or deactivating virions where they first lodge. This may be further enhanced by the inhalation of steam containing essential oils with anti-viral, mucolytic and anxiolytic properties. Heat applied to the whole body can further support the immune system’s second line of defence by mimicking fever and activating innate and acquired immune defences and building physiological resilience. Heat-based treatments also offer psychological benefits and enhanced mental wellness by focusing attention on positive action, enhancing relaxation and sleep, inducing 'forced-mindfulness', and invoking the power of positive thinking and ‘remembered wellness’. Heat is a cheap, convenient and widely accessible therapeutic modality and while no clinical protocols exist for using heat to treat COVID-19, protocols that draw from traditional practices and consider contraindications, adverse effects and infection control measures could be developed and implemented rapidly and inexpensively on a wide scale. While there are significant challenges in implementing heat-based therapies during the current pandemic, these therapies present an opportunity to integrate natural medicine, conventional medicine and traditional wellness practices, and support the wellbeing of both patients and medical staff, while building community resilience and reducing the likelihood and impact of future pandemics.
review_content:
This is a timely, interesting, and generally well-written article summarizing many of the positive benefits of thermal therapies, provided in the context of potential therapies for patients with COVID-19. In general, the authors cover a wide range of literature related to applications (local/regional, whole body, topical) of elevated temperature. My comments related only to organization and some references and distinguishing better the difference between fever and hyperthermia. Heat treatments are likely to be hyperthermia treatments. While fever contains a thermal element, fever and hyperthermia represent very different physiological circumstances.

For example, statements such as that in Paragraph 2, right column, page3 "Fever has multiple actions with dealing with infections that include direct inhibition of pathogens, stimulation of both the innate and adaptive arms of the immune system and activation....". While the authors provide a review article as a reference here, most of this literature deals with hyperthermia and not actual infectious fever and this difference needs to be highlighted better. One would not be treated with fever. Moreover, there are other fundamental differences. Febrile individuals are usually quite cold and surface vessels constricted to conserve heat and help raise body temperature. Hyperthermia causes sweating and surface blood vessel dilation because the set point is not elevated.
Moreover, there is a massive literature on heat stress/stroke (from hyperthermia, not fever) that can kill people because of excessive adhesion of platelets and white blood cells in capillaries. While the authors do rightly mention some safety concerns, it is perhaps a bit insufficient with regard to the impact of both hyperthermia (and fever). At the same time, the scope of the beneficial effects of mild elevation of body temperature and local temperature (in particular with respect to viral infections) is quite important to remember and hopefully expand upon in future clinical applications.

Some topics should be highlighted more. For example, there is a substantial literature using electromagnetic heating and infrared heating for cancer therapy and so there is already safe equipment available for both local/regional as well as surface heating. Reviews on this topic have been available for some time. This technology could already be available for COVID-19 patients.

I found some of the referencing related to the direct impact of heat on viral replication (either in vivo (e.g., nasal cavities or in vitro) to be scattered a bit throughout the review. Some better reorganization of these various sections would help the reader to assess this very important point.
paper_title_zh: "加热对抗COVID-19：热作为一种治疗干预手段"
paper_abstract_zh: 包膜病毒如SARS-CoV-2对热敏感，并在人类可耐受的温度下被破坏。所有哺乳动物都使用发热来应对感染，而在人类历史上，热一直以温泉、桑拿、土耳其浴、蒸汽房、汗屋、蒸汽吸入、热泥和膏药等形式被用于预防和治疗呼吸道感染，并增强健康和福祉。本文综述了使用热治疗和预防病毒感染的证据，并讨论了潜在的细胞、生理和心理机制。在感染的初始阶段，将热应用于上呼吸道可以通过支持粘液纤毛清除和抑制或灭活病毒初次寄居的位置来支持免疫系统第一道防线。通过吸入含有抗病毒、化痰和抗焦虑特性的精油蒸汽，这一效果可能进一步增强。全身加热可以通过模拟发热和激活先天和后天免疫防御以及建立生理韧性来进一步支持免疫系统的第二道防线。热疗还通过集中注意力于积极行动、增强放松和睡眠、诱导“强制正念”、唤起积极思考和“记忆中的健康”的力量，提供心理益处和增强心理健康。热是一种廉价、便捷且广泛可及的治疗方式，尽管目前尚无使用热治疗COVID-19的临床方案，但可以迅速且低成本地开发和实施基于传统实践并考虑禁忌症、不良反应和感染控制措施的方案。尽管在当前大流行期间实施热疗存在显著挑战，但这些疗法提供了一个整合自然医学、常规医学和传统健康实践的机会，并支持患者和医务人员的福祉，同时增强社区韧性并降低未来大流行发生的可能性和影响。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇及时、有趣且总体上写得很好的文章，总结了热疗的许多积极益处，特别是在针对COVID-19患者的潜在疗法背景下。总体而言，作者涵盖了与升高温度应用（局部/区域性、全身性、局部应用）相关的广泛文献。我的评论仅涉及文章的组织结构、一些参考文献以及更好地区分发热和过热之间的差异。热疗很可能属于过热治疗。尽管发热包含热元素，但发热和过热代表非常不同的生理状况。

例如，第3页右栏第2段中的陈述：“发热在应对感染方面有多种作用，包括直接抑制病原体，刺激先天性和适应性免疫系统以及激活……”。尽管作者在此处提供了一篇综述文章作为参考，但大部分文献涉及的是过热而非实际的感染性发热，这一差异需要更好地突出。人们不会通过发热来治疗。此外，还有其他一些基本差异。发热个体通常感觉非常寒冷，表面血管收缩以保存热量并帮助升高体温。而过热则会导致出汗和表面血管扩张，因为设定点并未升高。

此外，有关热应激/中暑（由过热而非发热引起）的文献浩如烟海，这种情况可能导致人们因血小板和白细胞在毛细血管中过度粘附而死亡。尽管作者确实提到了一些安全担忧，但相对于过热（和发热）的影响，或许还略显不足。同时，轻度升高体温和局部温度的益处（特别是针对病毒感染）非常重要，值得记住，并希望在未来的临床应用中进一步拓展。

有些主题应该更加突出。例如，已有大量文献使用电磁加热和红外加热进行癌症治疗，因此已经存在用于局部/区域以及表面加热的安全设备。关于这一主题的综述已经存在一段时间。这项技术可能已经可以用于COVID-19患者。

我发现有关热对病毒复制直接影响的参考文献（无论是体内实验，如鼻腔，还是体外实验）在综述中有些分散。对这些各部分进行更好的重新组织将有助于读者评估这一非常重要的问题。

reasons: In general, the authors cover a wide range of literature related to applications (local/regional, whole body, topical) of elevated temperature.
While the authors provide a review article as a reference here, most of this literature deals with hyperthermia and not actual infectious fever and this difference needs to be highlighted better.

This is a timely, interesting, and generally well-written article summarizing many of the positive benefits of thermal therapies, provided in the context of potential therapies for patients with COVID-19.
Heat treatments are likely to be hyperthermia treatments. While fever contains a thermal element, fever and hyperthermia represent very different physiological circumstances.
While the authors do rightly mention some safety concerns, it is perhaps a bit insufficient with regard to the impact of both hyperthermia (and fever).

At the same time, the scope of the beneficial effects of mild elevation of body temperature and local temperature (in particular with respect to viral infections) is quite important to remember and hopefully expand upon in future clinical applications.

paper_title: Autophagy and airway fibrosis: Is there a link?
paper_abstract: In the past decade, an emerging process named “autophagy” has generated intense interest in many chronic lung diseases. Tissue remodeling and fibrosis is a common feature of many airway diseases, and current therapies do not prevent or reverse these structural changes. Autophagy has evolved as a conserved process for bulk degradation and recycling of cytoplasmic components to maintain basal cellular homeostasis and healthy organelle populations in the cell. Furthermore, autophagy serves as a cell survival mechanism and can also be induced by chemical and physical stress to the cell. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that autophagy plays an essential role in vital cellular processes, including tissue remodeling. This review will discuss some of the recent advancements made in understanding the role of this fundamental process in airway fibrosis with emphasis on airway remodeling, and how autophagy can be exploited as a target for airway remodeling in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
review_content:
Summary –

The current manuscript has reviewed the literature on relationship between autophagy and airway fibrosis in chronic lung disease, especially asthma and COPD. This topic is of great interest and very little work has been done to understand the underlying mechanisms. I think this article is a timely reminder and will stimulate research into this area, which is much needed. Overall, this a well presented article but I have some suggestions, which will enhance readability and understanding on the diseases discussed.

Major comments –
 1. Before authors go into the details for role of autophagy in asthma/remodeling, I think they need to add a separate section on airway remodeling and autophagy first.
 2. Please list the airway remodeling changes described in asthma so far and then discuss which might be related to autophagy.
 3. I think authors need to add a reference if there is any work done on fibroblast populations in asthma to make the case for fibrosis or suggest as potential future work.
 4. Similar changes I think need to be made for the COPD section, especially listing airway remodeling changes described so far, for example Rbm fragmentation, vascularity, epithelial mesenchymal transition (EMT) etc.
 5. Authors stated in the evidence for autophagy in COPD section that major features are emphysema and chronic bronchitis. I think it is very important to describe small airway destructive pathology in COPD. The classic fixed airflow obstruction described in COPD comes from the small airways. These airways are destroyed by up to nearly 40% well before the diagnosis of COPD. So damage starts quite early on and it is this site where fibrosis really occurs and EMT is central to this. Airway disease is the primary phenomenon in COPD.
 6. EGFR has also been regarded as one of the important drivers of airway remodeling in asthma and COPD, that needs to be discussed.
paper_title_zh: 自噬与气道纤维化：是否存在关联？
paper_abstract_zh: 在过去十年中，一种名为“自噬”的新兴过程在许多慢性肺部疾病中引起了强烈兴趣。组织重塑和纤维化是许多气道疾病的共同特征，而当前的治疗方法并不能预防或逆转这些结构变化。自噬已经演变为一种保守的过程，用于大量降解和回收细胞质成分，以维持基本的细胞内稳态和细胞内健康细胞器的数量。此外，自噬作为一种细胞生存机制，也可以由化学和物理应激诱导。越来越多的证据表明，自噬在重要的细胞过程中发挥着关键作用，包括组织重塑。本综述将讨论一些在理解这一基本过程在气道纤维化中的作用方面的最新进展，重点讨论气道重塑，以及如何将自噬作为哮喘和慢性阻塞性肺疾病中气道重塑的靶点。
review_content_zh:
摘要 –

当前手稿回顾了慢性肺部疾病，尤其是哮喘和慢性阻塞性肺病（COPD）中自噬与气道纤维化关系的文献。这一主题极具研究价值，且关于其潜在机制的研究非常少。我认为这篇文章是一个及时的提醒，并将激发对该领域的研究，这是非常必要的。总体而言，这是一篇呈现良好的文章，但我有一些建议，可以增强对所讨论疾病的可读性和理解。

主要意见 –
1. 在作者深入探讨自噬在哮喘/重塑中的作用之前，我认为他们首先需要添加一个关于气道重塑和自噬的独立部分。
2. 请列出迄今为止在哮喘中描述的气道重塑变化，然后讨论哪些可能与自噬相关。
3. 我认为作者需要添加参考文献，如果有关于哮喘中成纤维细胞群体的研究，以支持纤维化的论点，或建议作为未来的研究工作。
4. 我认为COPD部分也需要进行类似的修改，特别是列出迄今为止描述的气道重塑变化，例如Rbm片段化、血管生成、上皮间质转化（EMT）等。
5. 作者在COPD自噬证据部分指出，主要特征是肺气肿和慢性支气管炎。我认为描述COPD中小气道破坏性病理非常重要。COPD中描述的经典固定气流阻塞来自小气道。这些气道在COPD诊断前几乎被破坏了40%。因此，损伤在早期就开始了，正是在这个部位纤维化真正发生，而EMT是其中的核心。气道疾病是COPD的主要现象。
6. 表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）也被认为是哮喘和COPD中气道重塑的重要驱动因素，这需要进行讨论。

paper_title: The rise of pathogen genomics in Africa
paper_abstract: The routine genomic surveillance of pathogens in diverse geographical settings and equitable data sharing are critical to inform effective infection control and therapeutic development. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic highlighted the importance of routine genomic surveillance of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) to detect emerging variants of concern. However, the majority of high-income countries sequenced >0.5% of their COVID-19 cases, unlike low- and middle-income countries. By the end of 2022, many countries around the world had managed to establish capacity for pathogen genomic surveillance. Notably, Beta and Omicron; 2 of the 5 current SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern were first discovered in Africa through an aggressive sequencing campaign led by African scientists. To sustain such infrastructure and expertise beyond this pandemic, other endemic pathogens should leverage this investment. Therefore, countries are establishing multi-pathogen genomic surveillance strategies. Here we provide a catalog of the current landscape of sequenced and publicly shared pathogens in different countries in Africa. Drawing upon our collective knowledge and expertise, we review the ever-evolving challenges and propose innovative recommendations.
review_content:
The authors discuss an important issue regarding the significant threat that new pathogens pose to humanity. Specifically, the article addresses the situation in the African continent and the need for a Pan-African developed early surveillance system.

The authors accurately describe the use of NGS technologies and the necessity of high-throughput computing systems and high-speed internet to share and analyse common sequence data.

However, the article lacks a more detailed discussion about the need for a critical mass of researchers with the bioinformatics competence to perform these tasks at a pan-African level. The article should address and mention some of the existing education initiatives (e.g., AI4D Africa, H3Abionet, EANBiT, University programmes, etc.) and the imperative need to educate more African scientists in using Artificial Intelligence, HPC systems, NGS sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis.
International collaboration relies on the integration of ethics and law across national legal systems. The article would benefit from discussing the challenges and problems that can arise when considering ethical and legal issues in such collaborations.
paper_title_zh: 病原体基因组学在非洲的兴起
paper_abstract_zh: 在不同地理环境下对病原体进行常规基因组监测以及公平的数据共享对于指导有效的感染控制和治疗开发至关重要。2019年冠状病毒病（COVID-19）大流行凸显了常规基因组监测严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2（SARS-CoV-2）以检测新兴关注变异株的重要性。然而，大多数高收入国家对超过0.5%的COVID-19病例进行了测序，而低收入和中等收入国家则不然。到2022年底，世界上许多国家已设法建立病原体基因组监测能力。值得注意的是，当前5个SARS-CoV-2关注变异株中的2个——Beta和Omicron，是通过非洲科学家领导的积极测序活动首先在非洲发现的。为了在此大流行之外维持此类基础设施和专业知识，其他地方性病原体应利用这一投资。因此，各国正在建立多病原体基因组监测策略。本文提供了非洲不同国家已测序和公开共享的病原体的当前概况目录。基于我们的集体知识和专长，我们回顾了不断演变的挑战，并提出了创新的建议。
review_content_zh:
作者讨论了一个关于新病原体对人类构成重大威胁的重要问题。具体而言，文章探讨了非洲大陆的形势以及建立泛非开发的早期监测系统的必要性。

作者准确地描述了下一代测序（NGS）技术的应用，以及高通量计算系统和高速互联网在共享和分析常见序列数据中的必要性。

然而，文章缺乏对在泛非层面执行这些任务所需的具备生物信息学能力的研究人员临界数量的更详细讨论。文章应提及并讨论一些现有的教育倡议（例如，AI4D Africa、H3Abionet、EANBiT、大学项目等），以及培养更多非洲科学家使用人工智能、高性能计算系统、NGS测序和生物信息学分析的迫切需求。

国际合作依赖于伦理和法律在不同国家法律体系中的整合。文章若能讨论在考虑此类合作中的伦理和法律问题时可能出现的挑战和问题，将有所裨益。

paper_title: Herbarium specimens can reveal impacts of climate change on plant phenology; a review of methods and applications
paper_abstract: Studies in plant phenology have provided some of the best evidence for large-scale responses to recent climate change. Over the last decade, more than thirty studies have used herbarium specimens to analyze changes in flowering phenology over time, although studies from tropical environments are thus far generally lacking. In this review, we summarize the approaches and applications used to date. Reproductive plant phenology has primarily been analyzed using two summary statistics, the mean flowering day of year and first-flowering day of year, but mean flowering day has proven to be a more robust statistic. Two types of regression models have been applied to test for associations between flowering, temperature and time: flowering day regressed on year and flowering day regressed on temperature. Most studies analyzed the effect of temperature by averaging temperatures from three months prior to the date of flowering. On average, published studies have used 55 herbarium specimens per species to characterize changes in phenology over time, but in many cases fewer specimens were used. Geospatial grid data are increasingly being used for determining average temperatures at herbarium specimen collection locations, allowing testing for finer scale correspondence between phenology and climate. Multiple studies have shown that inferences from herbarium specimen data are comparable to findings from systematically collected field observations. Understanding phenological responses to climate change is a crucial step towards recognizing implications for higher trophic levels and large-scale ecosystem processes. As herbaria are increasingly being digitized worldwide, more data are becoming available for future studies. As temperatures continue to rise globally, herbarium specimens are expected to become an increasingly important resource for analyzing plant responses to climate change.
review_content: Reviewer 1 (Qianqian Ma) “The authors need to briefly introduce how the phenology data (such as mean flowering day of year or first flowering day of year) are obtained from the herbarium specimens. Are they the dates when herbarium specimens were collected? This is important information for readers who are unfamiliar with this type of data.” This information is now provided on lines 88-99. “Many studies have shown that the inferences from herbarium specimen data are comparable to findings from field observations. What are the advantages and disadvantages of using herbarium specimens than field observations, especially in the future when field observations are being recorded more? Do herbarium specimens provide any extra data than field observations? Please briefly discuss it.” We have added discussion of these issues on lines 388-394. “temperature regressed on year” does not represent the changes in phenology. Please rephrase this sentence. We removed temperature regressed on year and redundancies about regression types (line 54-56). “but other approaches may be suitable in some cases” Please clearly point out what are “other approaches”, and “some cases”. We removed “other approaches” from the abstract to be succinct and we included discussion about other approaches under Averaging Temperatures (lines 57 and 236-278). “the last sentence in the abstract is loosely related to the approach reviewed by this study. Please revise it to focus on the important role of herbarium specimens in studying the changing rate of phenology under continued warming.” Revised on lines 63-68 “please provide the reference for Carl Linnaeus’s study of phenology.” This reference is included in the text on lines 72 - 74 and in references on lines 514 and 611. “please provide the original reference for “Charles Morren who introduced the term around 1850”.” This reference is included on line 74 and in references on lines 536-536. “2017 -> 2015?” Revised on line 129 “Please explain why herbarium specimens may be useful for these different cases.” This revision was included on lines 388 to 395 to reduce redundancy. “model set”? Do you mean “procedure”? Revised on line 88 L97: correlations of what? Change of what? Please specify. Revised on line 97 “or some combination of these with multiple regression models”. Please explain or delete. Deleted from line 113 “This could be more concise. For example, “whether flowering day was earlier in warmer years, whether …” Deleted to reduce redundancy and replaced on line 111 “Is there any reason herbarium specimens were not used in tropical region? I don’t think the availability …” We did not find specific reasons for the lack of tropical studies. While several studies have used herbarium specimens to better understand tropical phenology, none have specifically analyzed long-term changes due to climate change. This may be due to the lack of climate data, or the lack of a signal supporting changing climate in those regions, but no specific reasons have been stated. “provide -> provided” Revised on line 126 “This is redundant: “we only selected studies that met the all three eligibility criteria” Deleted to reduce redundancy (lines 132-135) “ some significant trends? paper_title_zh: 植物标本可以揭示气候变化对植物物候的影响；方法与应用综述
paper_abstract_zh: 植物物候学的研究为近年来对气候变化的 largescale 响应提供了最佳证据之一。在过去十年中，已有三十多项研究利用植物标本馆的标本分析了随时间推移的开花物候变化，尽管热带环境的研究目前普遍缺乏。在这篇综述中，我们总结了迄今为止所采用的方法和应用。植物的生殖物候主要通过对两个汇总统计量进行分析：年度平均开花日和年度首次开花日，但年度平均开花日已被证明是一个更稳健的统计量。为了检验开花、温度和时间之间的关联，已应用了两种类型的回归模型：开花日对年份的回归和开花日对温度的回归。大多数研究通过计算开花日前三个月的平均温度来分析温度的影响。平均而言，已发表的研究使用了每个物种55份植物标本馆的标本以表征随时间推移的物候变化，但在许多情况下使用的标本数量较少。地理空间网格数据正越来越多地被用于确定植物标本馆标本采集地点的平均温度，从而允许对物候与气候之间的更精细尺度对应关系进行测试。多项研究表明，基于植物标本馆标本数据的推断与系统收集的野外观察结果相当。理解物候对气候变化的响应是认识对更高营养级和 largescale 生态系统过程影响的关键步骤。随着全球植物标本馆数字化程度的提高，更多数据将可用于未来的研究。随着全球温度持续上升，预计植物标本馆的标本将成为分析植物对气候变化响应的越来越重要的资源。
review_content_zh: 审稿人1（马倩倩）：“作者需要简要介绍如何从植物标本馆标本中获取物候数据（如年均开花日或年首次开花日）。这些数据是植物标本馆标本采集的日期吗？这对于不熟悉这类数据的读者来说是非常重要的信息。”该信息现在已在第88-99行提供。“许多研究表明，从植物标本馆标本数据中得出的推论与实地观察结果相当。使用植物标本馆标本而非实地观察的优势和劣势是什么，尤其是在未来实地观察记录更多的情况下？植物标本馆标本是否提供了实地观察之外的额外数据？请简要讨论。”我们已在第388-394行添加了这些问题的讨论。“温度对年份的回归”并不能代表物候的变化。请重新措辞这句话。我们删除了温度对年份的回归以及关于回归类型的冗余内容（第54-56行）。“但在某些情况下，其他方法可能适用”请明确指出“其他方法”是什么，以及“某些情况”是什么。我们为了简洁从摘要中删除了“其他方法”，并在“平均温度”部分（第57行和第236-278行）讨论了其他方法。“摘要中的最后一句话与本研究综述的方法关系松散。请修改，以聚焦于植物标本馆标本在研究持续变暖下物候变化率中的重要作用。”已在第63-68行修改。“请提供卡尔·林奈物候研究的参考文献。”该参考文献已包含在文本的第72-74行以及参考文献的第514和611行。“请提供‘查尔斯·莫伦在大约1850年引入该术语’的原始参考文献。”该参考文献已包含在第74行以及参考文献的第536-536行。“2017 -> 2015？”已在第129行修改。“请解释为什么植物标本馆标本可能对这些不同情况有用。”这一修改已包含在第388至395行，以减少冗余。“模型集”？你是指“程序”吗？已在第88行修改。L97：什么的相关性？什么的改变？请具体说明。已在第97行修改。“或这些与多元回归模型的某种组合”。请解释或删除。已从第113行删除。“这可以更简洁。例如，‘开花日是否在较暖年份更早，是否…’”已删除以减少冗余，并在第111行替换。“是否有任何原因植物标本馆标本未在热带地区使用？我认为可用性…”我们未找到具体原因解释热带研究的缺乏。尽管有几项研究使用植物标本馆标本以更好地理解热带物候，但尚未有研究专门分析由于气候变化引起的长期变化。这可能是因为缺乏气候数据，或这些地区缺乏支持气候变化的信号，但未提出具体原因。“提供 -> 已提供”已在第126行修改。“这是冗余的：‘我们只选择了符合所有三个资格标准的研究’”已删除以减少冗余（第132-135行）“一些显著趋势？表达模糊。请具体说明。”已删除并简化在第150行。L354：讨论 -> 已讨论已在第377行修改。

paper_title: Approaches for containerized scientific workflows in cloud environments with applications in life science
paper_abstract: Containers are gaining popularity in life science research as they provide a solution for encompassing dependencies of provisioned tools, simplify software installations for end users and offer a form of isolation between processes. Scientific workflows are ideal for chaining containers into data analysis pipelines to aid in creating reproducible analyses. In this article, we review a number of approaches to using containers as implemented in the workflow tools Nextflow, Galaxy, Pachyderm, Argo, Kubeflow, Luigi and SciPipe, when deployed in cloud environments. A particular focus is placed on the workflow tool’s interaction with the Kubernetes container orchestration framework.
review_content:
The paper provides a review of approaches for using containers in scientific workflows in clouds, with the particular focus on life-science applications. The topic is timely and relevant for the computational life science research community, as workflow systems and container technologies are state of the art approaches and still under active development. The paper gives a short introduction to cloud computing, containers, and workflow management systems (WMS). Subsequently, it shortly describes how containers are supported in Nextflow, Galaxy, Pachyderm, Argo, Kubeflow, Luigi and SciPipe systems. From the description we can learn that all the systems use Kubernetes to manage containers, and what are the main features of WMS-Kubernetes integration. The paper is generally well written and of good quality, but there are several items that are worth improving.
  * In general, the paper provides a nice high-level introduction and overview of the solutions, but I would expect more rigorous and systematic description, with definitions of key concepts, list of criteria for comparison, perhaps a taxonomy of the features and approaches. This would make the review more structured and comprehensive.
  * From a review, I would expect some structured summary and comparison of systems, approaches, and solutions in the from of a table, with clearly defined set of criteria. The discussion section is quite superficial in the current form.
  * To systematically and fairly compare all the WMS, a common reference architecture should be defined, in a more detailed way than presented in Fig. 1, taking into account not only the container layer, but also the cloud (IaaS/VM) layer.
  * The paper does not provide an appropriate introduction to Kubernetes, which seems to be a central orchestration in this review. An introduction including the architecture and definition of pods, helms, etc. should be provided to make the paper self-contained. Scoping the paper on Kubernetes-based approaches would make the paper more focused.
  * The description of Nextflow seems to be incomplete, as it does not describe how it is integrated with Kubernetes, only a diagram is provided in Fig. 3. Fig 3, however, is a copy of the documentation from here, which is provided without a reference.
  * An important issue is how the WMS handles the dynamic allocation of resources: can the additional VMs be added to the Kubernetes cluster, or additional pods added to the workflow during execution? This is mentioned briefly in the discussion, but in my opinion this is worth emphasizing as a separate criterion for evaluation.
  * An interesting discussion is provided regarding error management, but there is only one paragraph on that which touches the problem, so a more detailed discussion would be much appreciated.
  * The performance and scalability of the systems is an important criteria, which can be measured and compared, especially in the cloud environment and for large-scale applications. The paper mentions some performance issues with Luigi, but there is no similar discussion regarding other systems. Does it mean that there are no scalability issues, or not? To make a comparison fair, all the systems should be evaluated regarding the performance and scalability.
  * In conclusions, there should be some recommendations on which system is better for which purpose, in which application scenario or for which infrastructure.
  * To make a discussion more complete, it would be worth referring to other general-purpose scientific WMS, in which container technologies have been employed. These may include Pegasus, Condor, Makeflow or Airflow.
paper_title_zh: 云环境中容器化科学工作流的方法及其在生命科学中的应用
paper_abstract_zh: 容器在生命科学研究中的普及正在增加，因为它们为包含预置工具的依赖项提供了解决方案，简化了最终用户的软件安装，并在进程之间提供了一种隔离形式。科学工作流非常适合将容器链接到数据分析管道中，以帮助创建可复现的分析。在本文中，我们回顾了在云环境中部署时，工作流工具Nextflow、Galaxy、Pachyderm、Argo、Kubeflow、Luigi和SciPipe中实现的多种使用容器的方法。特别关注的是工作流工具与Kubernetes容器编排框架的交互。
review_content_zh:
该论文综述了在云环境中使用容器进行科学工作流的方法，特别关注生命科学应用。这一主题对于计算生命科学研究社区来说是及时且相关的，因为工作流系统和容器技术是当前最先进的方法，并且仍在积极发展中。论文简要介绍了云计算、容器和工作流管理系统（WMS）。随后，简要描述了Nextflow、Galaxy、Pachyderm、Argo、Kubeflow、Luigi和SciPipe系统中如何支持容器。从描述中我们可以了解到，所有系统都使用Kubernetes来管理容器，以及WMS与Kubernetes集成的主要特点。论文总体上写得很好，质量较高，但有几处值得改进。
* 总的来说，论文提供了一个很好的高层介绍和解决方案概览，但我期望有更严格和系统的描述，包括关键概念的定义、比较标准的列表，或许还有特征和方法的分类。这将使综述更具结构性和全面性。
* 从综述中，我期望看到对系统、方法和解决方案的结构化总结和比较，以表格形式呈现，并明确定义一组标准。目前的讨论部分相当肤浅。
* 为了系统和公平地比较所有WMS，应定义一个共同的参考架构，比图1中展示的更详细，不仅考虑容器层，还要考虑云（IaaS/VM）层。
* 论文没有提供对Kubernetes的适当介绍，而Kubernetes似乎是该综述中的核心编排工具。应提供包括架构和定义_Pods、Helm等_的介绍，使论文自成一体。将论文范围限定在基于Kubernetes的方法上会使论文更加聚焦。
* Nextflow的描述似乎不完整，因为它没有描述如何与Kubernetes集成，只在图3中提供了一个图表。然而，图3是从这里的文档复制而来，且未提供引用。
* 一个重要问题是WMS如何处理资源的动态分配：是否可以在Kubernetes集群中添加额外的VM，或在执行过程中向工作流添加额外的_Pods？这在讨论中简要提及，但在我看来，这值得作为单独的评估标准加以强调。
* 关于错误管理的讨论很有趣，但只有一段触及了这个问题，因此更详细的讨论将非常受欢迎。
* 系统的性能和可扩展性是重要标准，可以在云环境和大规模应用中进行测量和比较。论文提到了Luigi的一些性能问题，但未对其他系统进行类似讨论。这是否意味着没有可扩展性问题？为了公平比较，所有系统都应在性能和可扩展性方面进行评估。
* 在结论中，应有关于哪种系统更适合哪种用途、哪种应用场景或哪种基础设施的建议。
* 为了使讨论更加完整，值得参考其他采用容器技术的通用科学WMS，这些可能包括Pegasus、Condor、Makeflow或Airflow。

paper_title: Assessment of activities of daily living in patients post COVID-19: a systematic review
paper_abstract: Background: Coronavirus disease has provoked much discussion since its first appearance. Despite it being widely studied all over the world, little is known about the impact of the disease on functional ability related to performing activities of daily living (ADL) in patients post COVID-19 infection.
review_content: Reviewer 3 2. In the results part, the authors searched, evaluated, and selected the available studies. Line 217, "a total of 1465 patients were studied in the articles included". However, if the authors could not integrate information from different studies, they failed to reach high statistical power and robust results by large numbers of patients. Thank you for this comment. In the results section, we included a synthesis of the ADL information reported by each test. Your comment leads us to include in the introduction a short reference from WHO explaining the role of intrinsic capacity and context in functional ability. We consider these changes to give us a more comprehensive integration of the results, despite Additionally, we added a sentence in the limitations regarding the included studies' heterogeneity.
paper_title_zh: "COVID-19后患者日常生活活动评估：系统综述"
paper_abstract_zh: 背景：自冠状病毒病首次出现以来，引发了大量讨论。尽管该病在全球范围内得到了广泛研究，但关于COVID-19感染后患者进行日常生活活动（ADL）相关功能能力的影响仍知之甚少。
review_content_zh: 审稿人3 2. 在结果部分，作者搜索、评估并选择了可用的研究。第217行，“在所包含的文章中，共有1465名患者被研究”。然而，如果作者无法整合来自不同研究的信息，他们就无法通过大量患者达到高统计效能和稳健的结果。感谢您的这一评论。在结果部分，我们包含了每项测试报告的ADL信息的综合。您的评论促使我们在引言中加入了一段来自世界卫生组织的简短引用，解释内在能力和情境在功能能力中的作用。我们认为这些更改使我们能够更全面地整合结果，尽管此外，我们在局限性部分增加了一句关于所包含研究异质性的说明。

paper_title: Prayers for Sickness: What do people pray for and how do they deal with unanswered prayer?
paper_abstract:
Background 
    This paper focuses upon prayer for sickness. What do individuals suffering from illness, their families and the wider community pray for? How do they deal with unanswered prayer? Do they pray for cure, to guide medical professionals or to cope with their sickness? What rationalisations do they proffer for unanswered prayer? 
  
  
    Methods 
    Based on a critical literature review and deploying secondary data from the Twenty First Century Evangelical research programme, the data suggest that prayers for guiding medical professionals and coping are more common than for cure, at least in Global North countries such as the UK and US. But why do those who believe in miracles not ask God for divine healing? Furthermore, unanswered prayer can conflict with Christian views of God as omnipotent and all loving. 
  
  
    Results 
    Respondents use a number of theodical rationalisations to resolve this conflict. 
  
  
    Conclusions 
    The results are discussed in relation to cognitive dissonance theory, learned helplessness, the need to conserve a relationship with the Divine, and desire to manage risk of disappointment and reduce consequent emotional pain.
review_content:
This research report shares secondary findings from a quarterly online survey of Evangelical Christians that inform about what their perspectives are regarding unanswered prayers for health (presumably physical and psychological).

* The strength of this reporting is in the very rich bookends: the review of literature and theory to introduce the findings, and the Discussion. These clearly show the authors are well-versed and think deeply on the topic--indeed, a relevant and highly interesting and helpful topic.

* My only complaint, and it is a serious one, is that the Methods are not adequately described. Tell us more about how the survey was conducted and where. Were the empirical indicators validated and reliable? How was the qualitative data generated and analyzed? Did a theoretical framework guide that analysis? Were any measures instituted to insure trustworthiness of the qual data/findings?

* Reflections: This article reminds me that the 21st century priest is the psychologist. Science is superseding theology, it seems. As former NIH Director and Templeton Prize winner Francis Collins would say, however, God's word (holy scripture, inspirations) and God's ways (creation, the natural world that science studies) are both valid.

* The blueprint vs warfare worldviews were helpful to cite. Carl Jung's thinking about God enveloping evil/darkness is pertinent to the blueprint thinking.
paper_title_zh: 疾病祈祷：人们为何祈祷以及如何应对未获回应的祈祷？
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
本文关注于疾病祈祷。患病个体、他们的家人以及更广泛社区的人们为哪些方面祈祷？他们如何应对未获回应的祈祷？他们是祈祷治愈、指引医疗专业人员还是应对疾病？对于未获回应的祈祷，他们提出了哪些合理化解释？

方法
基于批判性文献综述，并利用二十一世紀福音派研究计划的二手数据，数据显示，至少在英国和美国等全球北方国家，祈祷指引医疗专业人员和应对疾病的祈祷比祈祷治愈更为常见。但为何那些相信奇迹的人不向上帝祈求神迹治愈？此外，未获回应的祈祷可能与基督教对上帝全能全爱的看法相冲突。

结果
受访者使用多种神正论合理化解释来化解这一冲突。

结论
结果在认知失调理论、习得性无助、保持与神圣关系的需求，以及管理失望风险和减少相应情感痛苦的愿望等方面进行了讨论。
review_content_zh:
本研究报告分享了针对福音派基督徒进行的季度在线调查的次级发现，这些发现揭示了他们对未获回应的健康祈祷（推测包括身体和心理方面）的看法。

* 该报告的强项在于其丰富的首尾部分：通过文献和理论的回顾来引出发现，以及讨论部分。这些清楚地表明作者对这一主题非常熟悉且思考深刻——确实，这是一个相关且极具趣味性和帮助性的主题。

* 我唯一的抱怨，且这是一个严重的抱怨，是方法部分描述不足。请更多地告诉我们调查是如何进行的以及在哪里进行的。实证指标是否经过验证且可靠？定性数据是如何生成和分析的？是否有理论框架指导该分析？是否采取了任何措施以确保定性数据/发现的可靠性？

* 反思：这篇文章让我想起，21世纪的牧师是心理学家。科学似乎正在超越神学。然而，正如前美国国立卫生研究院院长和邓普顿奖得主弗朗西斯·柯林斯所言，上帝的话语（神圣经文、灵感）和上帝的方式（创造、科学研究的自然界）都是有效的。

paper_title: A Survey of Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning from Game Theoretical Perspective
paper_abstract: Following the remarkable success of the AlphaGO series, 2019 was a booming year that witnessed significant advances in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) techniques. MARL corresponds to the learning problem in a multi-agent system in which multiple agents learn simultaneously. It is an interdisciplinary domain with a long history that includes game theory, machine learning, stochastic control, psychology, and optimisation. Although MARL has achieved considerable empirical success in solving real-world games, there is a lack of a self-contained overview in the literature that elaborates the game theoretical foundations of modern MARL methods and summarises the recent advances. In fact, the majority of existing surveys are outdated and do not fully cover the recent developments since 2010. In this work, we provide a monograph on MARL that covers both the fundamentals and the latest developments in the research frontier. This survey is separated into two parts. From §1 to §4, we present the self-contained fundamental knowledge of MARL, including problem formulations, basic solutions, and existing challenges. Specifically, we present the MARL formulations through two representative frameworks, namely, stochastic games and extensive-form games, along with different variations of games that can be addressed. The goal of this part is to enable the readers, even those with minimal related background, to grasp the key ideas in MARL research. From §5 to §9, we present an overview of recent developments of MARL algorithms. Starting from new taxonomies for MARL methods, we conduct a survey of previous survey papers. In later sections, we highlight several modern topics in MARL research, including Q-function factorisation, multi-agent soft learning, networked multi-agent MDP, stochastic potential games, zero-sum continuous games, online MDP, turn-based stochastic games, policy space response oracle, approximation methods in general-sum games, and mean-field type learning in games with infinite agents. Within each topic, we select both the most fundamental and cutting-edge algorithms. The goal of our survey is to provide a self-contained assessment of the current state-of-the-art MARL techniques from a game theoretical perspective. We expect this work to serve as a stepping stone for both new researchers who are about to enter this fast-growing domain and existing domain experts who want to obtain a panoramic view and identify new directions based on recent advances.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
The authors present a review of (mostly) recent multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) literature, and game theoretical approches to such multi-agent problems, attempting at providing a fresh & game-theory centric view of MARL.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Let me first start by mentioning that I applaud the authors for attempting what few researches seem to be willimg to do in our field: writing detailed, overarching surveys about fast evolving, large, fields of research. We need more of these, and we need them to be of very high quality to help getting past the arxiv noise. Overal, I found the survey to be extremely helpful to brush back up on fundamental and recent proofs in theoretical game theory applied to agent learning, and overall found it quite decent to read compared to the foundational literature in the field. However, I believe the manuscript requires some good improvements before it can become the work the authors wish it to be. To summarise: ### Strengths 1. Really strong coverage of game-theoretical work. While it is not my primary area of research, I attempted a similar work as an exercise to review this manuscript, and overall found it to be quite reasonably covering of the most relevant parts of the field. Obviously this is not to say say that it is suffiecient, but it provides enough pointers and background to the willing reader to be a strong entry point for game theory applied to multi-atent deicison making problems. 2. A lot of complex work is explained in simple terms, with ; the paper is stated to be written (also) for a generalist researchers looking to work on the field, and it does so excellently; 3. It does a good job of summarising recent important (Deep)MARL work, which have not been meta-surveyed as of today; 4. Tackles the intersection of two popular and important (and perhaps growing) fields, so I believe this to be of great interestest to the TMLR community. ### Weaknesses 1. The writing is extremely handwavey at times. My expecatation is that a survey should be extremely precise when making statements about existing literature, and speculativge when declared so (to provide some kind of narrative and meta-take over a particular set of research work). 2. It is not clear to me the authors targeted a useful subset of researchers as the target audience. Very often in the manuscript will go over many important proofs and concepts in a short amount of lines, in such a way that forces the reader to essentially revert back to the original work when looking for specific mathematical details (and jargon!). At the same time, many perhaps simpler concepts are explained in perhaps unnecessary detail (again, for a semi-expert reader). 3. The review feels like it was primarily written as a survey of game theoretical work, and then MARL was retrofitted to be included as a strengthening point. Whilst there are indeed many references and overall a good overview of recent MARL work and the general state of the field, it does seem like for the vast majority of cited MARL algorithmic work, most of the details are left to the reader to go pick up from the original material, rather than providing the necessary info in text. 4. Following up on (2) and (3), the applied game-theoretical "taxonomy" makes it perhaps hard to compare cited MARL work appropriately between each other; it's not clear to me whether a new reader would find it a particularly useful view of the field.

**Requested Changes:**
Overall, I don't think this manuscript is ready for publication at TMLR, as its targeting is a bit confusing and could skew (particularly younger) memebers of the community towards misunderstanding rather than enlightnment over the field of MARL. Here's a list of improvements I would like to see to be able to improve my eventual score: 1. Improve some of the handwavy statements made when talking about MARL / deep learning (and combinations of the two). 2. Attempt to reduce the dependency on the original material where possible, especially on some of the more complex game-theoretical algorithmic details; 3. Focus and declare the targeting of a specific audience (IMO either incoming researchers, or existing members of game-theory / MARL folks), and generally work out the required level of details to use when discussing straightforward as well as complex work., More specifically, these are notes I took while reading the manuscript that loosely match the above points: ### Abstract - Seems to imply that MARL boomed up due to AphaGo, but that's unclear to me. Most theoretical MARL work happened before AlphaGo, and more recent applied work has been primarily driven due to the emergence of better testbeds and learning systems. ### Section 1 - Nit: a computer program that can perform certain task(s) -> Grammar: Either a certain task or certain tasks. - special kind of -> Why special? - which allows the software to train itself to perform new tasks rather than merely relying on the programmer for designing hand-crafted rules -> This is _very_ handwavey, and really applies to all of machine learning. ### 1.1 - Nit: sub-field -> subfield. - an image labelled with cats -> poor phrasing. - RL is goal-oriented: it constructs a learning model that learns to achieve the optimal long-term goal by improvement through trial and error, with the learner having no labelled data to obtain knowledge from. -> this is an imprecise characterisation of RL. RL technically is neither goal-orientied nor generally model-learning focused, furthermore a reward function is a type of label over a particular task (just a particularly poorly informative and indirect kind of label) - from DeepMind -> poor form to mention the company in question. Focus on the authors / manuscript unless making a meta-point. - As a result, RL methods can naturally be used to train a computer program (an agent) to a performance level comparable to that of a human on certain tasks. -> this does not follow from the previous sentence; ie the fact that some RL tasks can be successfully solved today is not due to RL being (eg) nature-inspired. - Nit: GO -> Go / go / baduk. ### 1.2 - It is possible that the AlphaGo series (Silver et al., 2016; 2017; 2018) has largely fulfilled people’s expectations for the effectiveness of RL methods, such that there is a lack of interest in further advancements in the field. -> seems to be a counterargument to a previously made point about the surging popularity of RL. Which is what? - One popular test-bed of MARL is StarCraft II (Vinyals et al., 2017) -> Pysc2 is not a multi-agent testbed. Did you mean to talk about SMAC here? - However, a breakthrough was accomplished by AlphaStar in 2019 (Vinyals et al., 2019b), which has exhibited grandmaster-level skills by ranking above 99.8% of human players. -> Arguably very much not a MARL breakthrough. - Another prominent video game-based test-bed for MARL is Dota2 -> Is it? Only handful of papers on DOTA in the litearature (and IIRC not many at all on MARL!), due to the interface being private. - Nit: test-bed -> testbed ### 2.1 - Define delta / simplex function in 3rd bullet point instead of later paragraph. - Generally worth stating whether you are talking about episodic vs non episodic MDPs. ### 2.3 - vice-versa -> not sure what this is referring to. Worth being clearer. - The word “learning" essentially means that the agent turns its experience gained during the interaction into knowledge about the model of the environment. -> not really? Even given a fairly generous interpretation of what RL does, this seems factually wrong. - What's the "solution target"? - contraction mapping -> Undefined, like some of the other perhaps more unusual mathematical terms across the manuscript. IMO too specific of a detail for beginners of the field, and too imprecise for experts. - replay buffer -> undefined; worth explaining more here. ### 2.3.2 - update the parameter θ in the direction that maximises the cumulative reward [equation] -> the equation of the weights update here is doing a lot; worth unpacking it... - When the policy is deterministic and the action set is continuous, one obtains the deterministic policy gradient (DPG) theorem (Silver et al., 2014) -> why was DPG singled out here in particular? - Important variants -> Why are they important? ### 3 - reward function that each agent receives -> Best to specify here that these could be different between different agents, think eg cooperative vs non-coop settings. ### 3.1 - The rewards have absolute values uniformly bounded by $$R_{max}$$ -> Why? Can you elaborate more here? - We use the superscript of (·i,·−i) -> Where does this notation come from? Perhaps Foerster 2017b? Helpful to mention why it helps. ### 3.2.1 - The single-agent Q-learning update in Eq. (7) still holds in the multi-agent case. -> where is this shown? ### 3.2.2 - This characteristic necessitates the development of policy-based algorithms with function approximations. -> Does it mean that PG methods don't suffer from the curse of dimensionality? Surely they do (just in different manners)? - Considering a continuous action set with a deterministic policy -> Again, why singleing out MADDPG amongst all of possible PG settings? ### 3.2.5 - However, the benefits of studying games in the partially observable setting come from the algorithmic advantages -> What does this mean? - I conclude Section 3 by presenting the relationships between the many different types of POSGs through a Venn diagram in Figure 6. -> Should be we? Also the section is not concluded... ### 3.3 - An important feature of EFGs is that they can handle imperfect information for multi-player decision making. -> Should probably be mentioned earlier in the section. ### 4 - MARL methods pose more theoretical challenges -> Do you mean MARL problems? - all result in the majority of MARL algorithms being capable of solving games with ⃝4 only two players -> I'm skeptical this is generally true. Very often MARL is not even concerned with the # of players, and scale issues come more from task complexity as well as # of agents (and they are not the same thing?). - I will -> we will. ### 4.1 - Q-function decomposition -> Needs definition. - Reaching both rationality and convergence gives rise to reaching the NE. -> Odd phrasing. ### 4.3 - The stationarity is thus maintained, so single-agent RL algorithms can still be applied. -> In principle many RL algorithms are commonly applied in these settings? - which provide the learning algorithms expressive function approximators. -> unsure what this means? ### 5 - I provide -> We provide. - (Again) I introduce -> We introduce. - I review -> ... ### 5.1 - unanimously defined -> Unsure about this. Very often it is hard to define the right MDP in a single agent problem. - learning objectives -> Are rationality and convergence here "learning objectives" in the same way maximising the reward function would be? Is that fair? ... and so on.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
The manuscript did not include a particular statement about societal impact. I believe it could use one that could focus on what the authors might perceive as weaknesses wrt. the particular set of materials they chose to review (particularly with the intention to figure out what effect this review might have on work that didn't get reviewed). The manuscript does attempt to list some of these at the end, but IMO it can do better.
paper_title_zh: 从博弈论视角对多智能体强化学习的综述
paper_abstract_zh: 继AlphaGO系列取得显著成功之后，2019年成为多智能体强化学习（MARL）技术取得重大进展的繁荣年份。MARL对应于多智能体系统中多个智能体同时学习的难题。它是一个具有悠久历史的跨学科领域，涵盖博弈论、机器学习、随机控制、心理学和优化。尽管MARL在解决现实世界游戏方面取得了相当大的实证成功，但文献中缺乏一个自包含的概述，详细阐述现代MARL方法的博弈论基础并总结近期进展。事实上，大多数现有综述已过时，并未完全涵盖2010年以来的最新发展。在本研究中，我们提供了一部关于MARL的专著，涵盖了基础知识和研究前沿的最新进展。本综述分为两部分。从第1节到第4节，我们介绍了MARL的自包含基础知识，包括问题表述、基本解决方案和现有挑战。具体而言，我们通过两个代表性框架，即随机博弈和扩展式博弈，以及可以解决的不同游戏变体，呈现了MARL的表述。这部分的目标是使读者，即使那些相关背景知识较少的读者，也能掌握MARL研究的关键思想。从第5节到第9节，我们概述了MARL算法的近期发展。从新的MARL方法分类开始，我们对以往的综述论文进行了调研。在后续章节中，我们突出了一些MARL研究中的现代主题，包括Q函数分解、多智能体软学习、网络化多智能体MDP、随机潜力博弈、零和连续博弈、在线MDP、回合制随机博弈、策略空间响应预言机、一般和博弈中的近似方法以及无限智能体博弈中的均值场类型学习。在每个主题中，我们选择了最基础和最前沿的算法。我们综述的目标是从博弈论角度提供一个自包含的当前最先进MARL技术评估。我们期望这项工作既能作为新研究人员进入这一快速成长领域的垫脚石，也能帮助现有领域专家获得全景视角并基于最新进展确定新方向。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
作者对（主要是）近年来的多智能体强化学习（MARL）文献以及针对此类多智能体问题的博弈论方法进行了综述，试图提供一个新颖且以博弈论为中心的MARL视角。

**优点与不足：**
首先，我要提到的是，我赞赏作者尝试做我们领域中似乎很少有研究者愿意做的事情：撰写关于快速演变、庞大研究领域的详细、全面的综述。我们需要更多这样的综述，并且它们需要非常高质量，以帮助我们从arxiv的噪音中筛选出有价值的内容。总体而言，我发现这篇综述对于回顾应用于智能体学习的理论博弈论的基本和最新证明非常有帮助，并且与该领域的基础文献相比，阅读起来相当不错。然而，我认为手稿在成为作者期望的作品之前还需要一些改进。总结如下：

### 优点
1. 对博弈论工作的覆盖面非常强。虽然这不是我的主要研究领域，但我曾尝试进行类似的工作以审查这篇手稿，总体上发现它对领域中最相关部分的覆盖相当合理。显然，这并不是说它足够全面，但它为愿意阅读的读者提供了足够的指针和背景，成为应用博弈论于多智能体决策问题的强有力切入点。
2. 许多复杂的工作用简单术语解释；论文声明也是为希望在该领域工作的普通研究者撰写的，并且做得非常出色；
3. 在总结尚未被元综述的近期重要（深度）MARL工作方面做得很好；
4. 涉及两个流行且重要（或许还在增长）的领域的交叉点，因此我相信这对TMLR社区具有极大兴趣。

### 不足
1. 写作有时过于笼统。我的期望是，综述在陈述现有文献时应极其精确，而在声明推测性内容时应明确指出（以提供某种叙事和对特定研究工作的元观点）。
2. 我不清楚作者是否针对有用的一组研究者作为目标受众。手稿中经常在短短几行内概述许多重要的证明和概念，以至于读者在寻找具体的数学细节（和术语！）时基本上需要回溯到原始工作。同时，许多可能更简单的概念被解释得或许过于详细（再次强调，对于半专家读者而言）。
3. 这篇综述感觉主要是作为博弈论工作的综述撰写的，然后MARL被事后添加作为强化点。 尽管确实有许多参考文献，并且总体上对近期多智能体强化学习（MARL）工作及其领域现状有很好的概述，但似乎对于绝大多数引用的MARL算法工作，大部分细节都留给读者去查阅原始材料，而不是在文本中提供必要的信息。4. 继续讨论（2）和（3），所应用的游戏理论“分类法”可能使得适当比较引用的MARL工作变得困难；我不清楚新读者是否会认为这是对该领域的特别有用的视角。

**请求的修改：**
总体而言，我认为这篇手稿尚未准备好在TMLR上发表，因为其目标定位有些混乱，可能会导致（尤其是较年轻的）社区成员对MARL领域的误解而非启发。以下是我希望看到的一些改进，以便能够提高我的最终评分：1. 改进在讨论MARL/深度学习（及其组合）时的一些含糊其辞的陈述。2. 尽可能减少对原始材料的依赖，尤其是某些更复杂的游戏理论算法细节；3. 专注于并声明针对特定受众的目标定位（我认为要么是即将进入的研究人员，要么是现有的游戏理论/MARL领域人士），并总体上确定在讨论简单和复杂工作时所需的细节水平。更具体地说，这些是我在阅读手稿时所做的笔记，大致符合上述要点：### 摘要 - 似乎暗示MARL的兴起是由于AlphaGo，但这一点对我来说并不清楚。大多数理论上的MARL工作发生在AlphaGo之前，而更近期的应用工作主要是由于更好的测试平台和学习系统的出现而推动的。### 第1节 - 小问题：一个可以执行某些任务（task(s)）的计算机程序 -> 语法：要么是特定任务（a certain task），要么是特定任务（certain tasks）。 - 特殊类型的 -> 为什么特殊？ - 这使得软件能够自行训练以执行新任务，而不是仅仅依赖程序员设计手工规则 -> 这非常含糊，并且实际上适用于所有机器学习。### 1.1 - 小问题：子领域（sub-field）-> 子领域（subfield）。 - 标有猫的图像 -> 表述不当。 - RL是目标导向的：它构建一个学习模型，通过试错改进来学习实现最优长期目标，学习者没有标记数据来获取知识。 -> 这是对RL的不准确描述。RL在技术上既不是目标导向的，也不一般地专注于模型学习，此外，奖励函数是一种特定任务上的标签（只是一种特别不具信息性和间接的标签） - 来自DeepMind -> 提及该公司是不良形式。除非进行元讨论，否则应关注作者/手稿。 - 因此，强化学习（RL）方法可以自然地用于训练计算机程序（即智能体）在某些任务上达到与人类相当的性能水平。但这并不从前一句中得出；即某些RL任务今天能够成功解决，并非因为RL是（例如）受自然启发的。- 细节：GO -> Go / go / baduk。### 1.2 - 可能AlphaGo系列（Silver等，2016；2017；2018）已经很大程度上满足了人们对RL方法有效性的期望，以至于对这一领域进一步发展的兴趣不足。这似乎是对之前关于RL日益流行观点的反驳。那么之前的观点是什么？- 一个流行的多智能体强化学习（MARL）测试平台是StarCraft II（Vinyals等，2017）-> Pysc2并不是一个多智能体测试平台。你是指SMAC吗？- 然而，2019年AlphaStar取得了突破（Vinyals等，2019b），其表现出了超越99.8%人类玩家的宗师级技能。-> 可以说这并不是一个MARL的突破。- 另一个基于视频游戏的重要MARL测试平台是Dota2 -> 是吗？文献中关于DOTA的论文寥寥无几（我记得关于MARL的也不多！），因为接口是私有的。- 细节：test-bed -> testbed ### 2.1 - 在第三点中定义delta / simplex函数，而不是在后面的段落中。- 通常值得说明你是在讨论阶段性还是非阶段性的马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）。### 2.3 - vice versa -> 不确定这是指什么。值得更明确。- “学习”一词本质上意味着智能体将其在交互过程中获得的经验转化为关于环境模型的知识。-> 并不完全如此？即使对RL的作用进行相当宽泛的解释，这似乎在事实上也是错误的。- “解决方案目标”是什么？- 收缩映射 -> 未定义，像手稿中其他一些可能更不寻常的数学术语一样。我认为这对领域初学者来说过于具体，对专家来说又不够精确。- 回放缓冲区 -> 未定义；值得在这里解释更多。### 2.3.2 - 沿着最大化累积奖励的方向更新参数θ [方程] -> 这里权重更新的方程做了很多工作；值得展开...- 当策略是确定性的且动作集是连续的时，可以得到确定性策略梯度（DPG）定理（Silver等，2014）-> 为什么特别提到DPG？- 重要变体 -> 为什么它们重要？### 3 - 每个智能体接收的奖励函数 -> 最好在这里说明这些在不同智能体之间可能是不同的，例如在合作与非合作设置中。### 3.1 - 奖励的绝对值均匀地被$$R_{max}$$所限制 -> 为什么？你能在这里详细说明吗？- 我们使用（·i,·−i）的上标 -> 这种表示法来自哪里？可能是Foerster 2017b？有帮助说明其作用。 ### 3.2.1 - 式(7)中的单智能体Q-learning更新在多智能体情况下仍然适用。-> 这是在哪里显示的？### 3.2.2 - 这一特性需要开发带有函数近似的基于策略的算法。-> 这是否意味着PG方法不受维度诅咒的影响？当然它们也会（只是以不同的方式）？- 考虑具有确定性策略的连续动作集 -> 再次，为什么在所有可能的PG设置中单独挑出MADDPG？### 3.2.5 - 然而，研究部分可观测设置中的博弈的益处来自于算法优势 -> 这是什么意思？- 我通过图6中的维恩图展示了多种不同类型POSG之间的关系，以此结束第3节。-> 应该是我们？而且这一节并没有结束...### 3.3 - EFG的一个重要特征是它们可以处理多玩家决策中的不完美信息。-> 可能应该在节的前面提到。### 4 - MARL方法提出了更多的理论挑战 -> 你是指MARL问题？- 所有结果导致大多数MARL算法能够解决只有两个玩家的博弈 -> 我怀疑这通常是真的。很多时候MARL甚至不关心玩家数量，而且规模问题更多来自于任务复杂性以及智能体数量（而且它们不是一回事？）。- 我将 -> 我们将。### 4.1 - Q函数分解 -> 需要定义。- 达到理性和收敛导致达到NE。-> 表述奇怪。### 4.3 - 因此保持了平稳性，所以单智能体RL算法仍然可以应用。-> 原则上许多RL算法通常在这些设置中应用？- 它们为学习算法提供了表达性函数近似器。-> 不确定这是什么意思？### 5 - 我提供 -> 我们提供。- （再次）我介绍 -> 我们介绍。- 我回顾 -> ...### 5.1 - 一致定义 -> 不确定这一点。很多时候很难在单智能体问题中定义正确的MDP。- 学习目标 -> 这里理性和收敛是“学习目标”，与最大化奖励函数的方式相同吗？这是公平的吗？...等等。

**更广泛的影响关注：**
手稿没有包括关于社会影响的特定声明。我认为它可以包含一个，重点讨论作者可能认为他们选择回顾的材料集合的弱点（特别是为了弄清楚这篇综述对未涉及的工作可能产生的影响）。手稿确实试图在最后列出一些这些内容，但在我看来它可以做得更好。

paper_title: Systematic review of the application of Machine Learning in the detection and classification of transposable elements
paper_abstract: Background. Transposable elements (TEs) constitute the most common repeated sequences in eukaryotic genomes. Recent studies demonstrated their deep impact on species diversity, adaptation to the environment, and diseases. Although there are many conventional bioinformatic algorithms for detecting and classifying TEs, none have achieved reliable results on different types of TEs. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques can automatically extract hidden patterns and novel information from labeled or non-labeled data and have been applied to solving several scientific problems.
review_content: Reviewer 3 Basic reporting The authors should clearly define what they mean with the TE tasks they are addressing. They mainly talk about TE detection and TE classification, but it would be good to properly define these tasks. Moreover, in the text they also talk about TE identification, TE prediction, TE analysis,... It is not clear whether these are considered as synonyms for detection or classification, or denote different tasks. Thank you for your recommendations. We standardize the use of TE tasks to avoid possible confusion in this regard. As we were interested in the task of detection and classification in the review, we replaced all other words when they were applied to TEs (such as identification, prediction, analysis, among others) with their respective names. The formulation of the research questions should not involve methodological details (e.g. question Q2). Thank you. We removed methodological details from the formulation of the research questions. The structure could be improved. Some paragraphs in the response to the research questions (e.g. Q1: the paragraph starting with "In plants, TEs have been related") are more suited for the introduction. We agree with you. We moved a paragraph from Q1 section and another from Q3 section to the introduction. It would be good to end each research question response with a small paragraph, summarizing the answer to the research question. Following this suggestion, we added a paragraph at the end of each research question response. Experimental design In the Survey Methodology section, the text is well structured into the different steps, but it would be clearer for the reader if the exact same terminology as in Fig 2 is used (throughout the text and for the section titles). Thank you for your recommendation. The titles in Survey Methodology were adapted to fix exactly the same terminology as shown in Fig 2. I'm wondering whether there was a search criterion related to the publication date, since all included articles date from 2009 or later. Does it mean that there were no publications on this topic prior to 2009? (This would seem to contradict the fact that there is a review paper from 2010 on this topic.). Due to the few publications found in this topic, we do not include any time filter in the search. However, publications that met the inclusion criteria and were then selected were published after 2009. This fact does not indicate that there are no publications published before 2009. To be clearer, we added the phrase "and any time limitations" in the section "Search design and study selection". The response to research question Q2 also involves publications that apply ML to data similar to TEs. However, here the article seems to be less systematic in its review. In any case, it is not clear how the discussed publications are selected. Thank you for your valuable opinion. The publications discussed in section Q2 are included in the 35 relevant publications selected in the review. These publications are listed in Table 2. In order to avoid confusion, we added "these publications are in Table 2" at the beginning of the paragraph. Validity of the findings The results seem valid. However, in the response to Q2, I'm not sure what an analysis of the programming language used to implement the machine learning algorithms adds to the contribution of this paper. Thank you for your recommendation. We removed this paragraph and the Fig 7. Also, for Q3, concepts of training/validation/test set, cross validation, and all the evaluation measures considered are not at all specific for TE detection or classification. These are concepts used in any machine learning study. Furthermore, I assume the evaluation measure will depend on the task, i.e. TE detection will require different evaluation measures than TE classification. We are in complete agreement. Therefore, we include a new column in Table 5, which indicates whether the metric has been used in detection or classification tasks (or both). In addition, we add that "these methods should be used in problems with information of any kind. Particularly with data of genomic origin, k-cross-validation seems to be the most popular" to be clearer in the division methods are standard for any problem in ML. Comments for the author My main comments have been covered by the 3 areas above. Some minor comments: - The caption of Fig 6 seems to be incomplete. Done. - As far as I know, "neuronal networks" is not standard terminology. Please change to "neural networks". Done.
paper_title_zh: 机器学习在转座元件检测和分类中应用的系统综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。转座元件（TEs）是真核生物基因组中最常见的重复序列。近期研究表明，它们对物种多样性、环境适应性和疾病有着深远的影响。尽管存在许多用于检测和分类TEs的传统生物信息学算法，但没有任何一种算法能在不同类型的TEs上取得可靠的结果。机器学习（ML）和深度学习（DL）技术能够自动从标记或未标记的数据中提取隐藏模式和新型信息，并已被应用于解决多个科学问题。
review_content_zh:
### 审稿人3的基本报告

**基本报告**

作者应明确界定他们所讨论的TE任务的含义。他们主要谈论TE检测和TE分类，但最好能恰当地定义这些任务。此外，在文本中，他们还提到了TE识别、TE预测、TE分析等。不清楚这些是否被视为检测或分类的同义词，还是表示不同的任务。感谢您的建议。我们标准化了TE任务的使用，以避免在这方面可能产生的混淆。由于我们在综述中感兴趣的是检测和分类任务，我们将所有其他应用于TE的词汇（如识别、预测、分析等）替换为相应的名称。研究问题的表述不应涉及方法细节（例如问题Q2）。感谢。我们从研究问题的表述中删除了方法细节。结构可以改进。在回应研究问题的一些段落中（例如Q1：以“In plants, TEs have been related”开头的段落）更适合放在引言部分。我们同意您的观点。我们将Q1部分和Q3部分的一个段落移至引言。最好在每个研究问题回应的末尾加上一个小段落，总结对研究问题的回答。按照这个建议，我们在每个研究问题回应的末尾添加了一个段落。

**实验设计**

在“调查方法学”部分，文本结构良好，分为不同的步骤，但为了使读者更清楚，最好使用与图2完全相同的术语（贯穿全文及章节标题）。感谢您的建议。调查方法学的标题已调整，以与图2中显示的术语完全一致。我想知道是否有与出版日期相关的搜索标准，因为所有包含的文章都来自2009年或之后。这是否意味着2009年之前没有关于这个主题的出版物？（这似乎与2010年有一篇关于这个主题的综述论文相矛盾。）由于在这个主题上找到的出版物较少，我们在搜索中没有包含任何时间过滤器。然而，符合纳入标准并被选中的出版物是在2009年之后发表的。这一事实并不表明2009年之前没有出版物。为了更清楚，我们在“搜索设计和研究选择”部分添加了“及任何时间限制”的短语。对研究问题Q2的回应也涉及将ML应用于与TE相似数据的出版物。然而，在这里，文章的综述似乎不那么系统。无论如何，不清楚所讨论的出版物是如何选择的。感谢您宝贵的意见。Q2部分讨论的出版物包含在综述中选出的35篇相关出版物中。这些出版物列在表2中。为了避免混淆，我们在段落开头添加了“这些出版物在表2中”。

**结果的有效性**

结果似乎是有效的。然而，在回应Q2时，我不确定分析用于实现机器学习算法的编程语言对本文的贡献有何增加。感谢您的建议。我们删除了这一段落和图7。此外，对于Q3，训练/验证/测试集、交叉验证以及所有考虑的评价指标根本不是TE检测或分类特有的。这些是任何机器学习研究中使用的概念。此外，我假设评价指标将取决于任务，即TE检测将需要与TE分类不同的评价指标。我们完全同意。因此，我们在表5中添加了一个新列，指明该指标是否用于检测或分类任务（或两者）。此外，我们添加了“这些方法应适用于任何类型的信息问题。特别是对于基因组数据，k交叉验证似乎是最受欢迎的”，以更清楚地划分这些方法是ML中任何问题的标准方法。

**对作者的意见**

我的主要意见已涵盖在上述三个领域中。一些次要意见：

- 图6的标题似乎不完整。已修正。
- 据我所知，“neuronal networks”不是标准术语。请改为“neural networks”。已修正。

paper_title: Class Incremental Learning from First Principles: A Review
paper_abstract: Continual learning systems attempt to efficiently learn over time without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. In recent years, there has been an explosion of work on continual learning, mainly focused on the class-incremental learning (CIL) setting. In this review, we take a step back and reconsider the CIL problem. We reexamine the problem definition and describe its unique challenges, contextualize existing solutions by analyzing non-continual approaches, and investigate the implications of various problem configurations. Our goal is to provide an alternative perspective to existing work on CIL and direct attention toward unexplored aspects of the problem.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper provides an alternative perspective to existing work on CIL. Considering resource constraints revisiting the problem definition and describing its unique challenges. A principled way of developing solutions to the CIL problem is provided by analysing discontinuous methods and providing an overview of existing work. Five specific dimensions of the CIL problem are then analysed and how existing work deals with various problem configurations is described. Recommendations for future work are summarised at the end of the article, arguing that future solutions can and should make assumptions regarding the data generation process.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
**Strengths:** 1) The paper is well-organized and easy to follow. 2) The perspective is novel, and directing attention to unexplored aspects of the CIL problem. 3) The article redefines the problem of Class Incremental Learning (CIL), explicitly pointing out the shortcomings in the existing definition, especially in the discussion of resource constraints. This re-examination of the problem provides a clearer direction and framework for subsequent research, and helps to advance the field. 4) The article delves into three core challenges involved in class incremental learning: stability-plasticity balance, cross-task discriminative learning, and knowledge migration. These analyses not only explain the complexity of CIL compared to traditional machine learning, but also suggest directions worth exploring for future research. 5) The article not only summarises existing methods, but also points out their shortcomings in terms of computational efficiency, cross-task differentiation, and so on. In particular, the discussion of ‘naive’ approaches provides valuable background information for understanding the difficulties and directions of CIL development. **Weaknesses:** 1) Although the paper differentiates itself from other reviews of continuous learning, it covers fewer of some of the most recent advances in the field of class-based incremental learning (CIL) beyond 2023, particularly emerging hybrid methods and new benchmarking. This may limit its reference value to researchers seeking to understand the latest advances in the field. 2) The challenges of class-incremental learning are discussed primarily at a high level. A more nuanced breakdown with a focus on specific subfields (e.g., task-agnostic versus task-aware incremental learning) could provide a more granular understanding and be beneficial to different categories of readers. 3) The section dedicated to discussing "naive" approaches such as single discriminative models, task-specific models, and class-specific generative models, while providing historical context, takes up significant space and repeats insights that are well-known. This may not add much value to the paper’s intended audience, who may already be familiar with these basic approaches. 4) The argument for framing CIL in terms of resource constraints instead of unavailability of past data is interesting. However, the discussion could be expanded to address specific practical implementations and comparisons, especially around the computational cost of different methods. This would make the argument more compelling and actionable for real-world applications. 5) While the conclusion does suggest some future directions, the suggestions are somewhat broad and lacking in concrete specifics on how certain challenges (e.g., learning across-task discrimination or computational efficiency) might be addressed. This limits the practical impact and future utility of the paper.

**Requested Changes:**
1) It is recommended that the authors add a discussion of recent research results in the field of Class Incremental Learning (CIL) beyond 2023, especially hybrid models and new benchmarking methods. You can discuss recent review papers such as; Class-incremental learning: A survey; A survey on few-shot class-incremental learning; and others. 2) The paper provides a broader discussion of the challenges in class-based incremental learning, and it is recommended that this section be augmented with some more detailed analyses of sub-domains, such as the differences between task-independent incremental learning and task-related incremental learning, as well as the distinctive challenges they each face. This would allow for a more nuanced discussion and meet the needs of a diverse group of readers. 3) The paper discusses too much about the basic ‘naive’ methods (e.g., single discriminant model, task-specific model, category-generating model), and it is suggested to simplify this part of the paper and devote more space to the in-depth analyses and comparisons of the existing state-of-the-art methods, so as to emphasise the innovativeness and unique insights of the paper. 4) When discussing the impact of resource constraints on the CIL problem, it is recommended that this section be further refined and expanded, especially the specific implementation, comparison and analysis of experimental results for different resource constraints (e.g. computation and memory), to provide more empirical support and make this part of the discussion more robust and comprehensive. 5) In the future work section, it is suggested that more specific research directions are proposed, especially providing actionable suggestions on how to deal with cross-task discrimination learning, knowledge transfer, and how to optimise in terms of computational efficiency. This will make the article more instructive for future research. 6) Need to summarise previous incremental learning reviews and plot them in a table showing the differences between this review compared to them, etc. 7) Clearly state the timeframe covered by this review, i.e. all classes of incremental learning methods discussed are research results published before a specific point in time. For example, ‘This review covers all relevant work published up to October 2024’.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
1) The CIL framework proposed in the article may rely on storing some of the old data or generating data for playback by generating models. However, this may lead to privacy and data security issues, especially when models are trained on tasks containing sensitive data, with an increased risk of data leakage. Models may ‘remember’ old data and inadvertently disclose sensitive information, especially when applied in domains such as healthcare or finance. It is recommended that the authors explore how to enhance privacy protection mechanisms in CIL. 2) Class incremental learning (CIL) methods may inherit biases in existing data when applied to real-world scenarios. For example, when applied to sensitive domains such as autonomous driving or facial recognition, models may amplify racial, gender, or other social biases in the data as they incrementally learn new tasks. Discussion of these social and ethical issues is lacking in the paper, so it is recommended that content be added on how to address bias and fairness issues in CIL methods.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Changes in revision in response to Reviewer EWou: We have uploaded a revised version of the draft with changes listed in green text. We highlight how the changes address the reviewer's concerns below, in 1-to-1 correspondence with the "Requested Changes" provided by the review: 1. Added subsection on pretraining and few-shot CIL in Section 5 2. Added subsection on related problem statements (few-shot CIL, TIL, DIL, online CL) in Section 2 3. We appreciate this feedback, however we are unsure if other readers (particularly those less familiar with continual learning) would find parts this section redundant. For now, we will leave this section unchanged, but welcome additional feedback from the action editor. 4. Added potential real-world application of resource-constrained CIL in Section 2 along with discussion of potential solutions 5. Added brief discussion in Section 7 as well as a new subsection 7.2 on actionable insights for CIL researchers 6. Added Table in Section 1 summarizing existing reviews at a high-level -- we agree that this is a cleaner way to present content from the introduction -- thanks for this suggestion 7. Stated timeframe in Section 5 Regarding broader impacts: the points brought up are pertinent, however we are unsure if a broader impacts section is required given that this work is a survey. We will defer to the recommendation of the action editor. Again, we appreciate the detailed feedback, and feel that the requested changes have improved the paper. Thank you for your help! | Preliminary response to reviewer EWou: Thank you for your detailed feedback. Especially helpful were the suggestions to (i) expand the resource constraint discussion, (ii) clarify our contributions relative to other reviews/recent work, and (iii) discuss privacy-related broader impacts in CIL. We are working on the changes now, but will wait until all reviews are submitted prior to uploading a revised draft. We appreciate your help in improving the paper!
paper_title_zh: 基于第一性原理的类别增量学习综述
paper_abstract_zh: 持续学习系统旨在高效地随时间学习，同时不遗忘已获得的知识。近年来，关于持续学习的研究呈爆炸性增长，主要集中在类别增量学习（CIL）设置上。在这篇综述中，我们退一步重新审视CIL问题。我们重新审视了问题定义，并描述了其独特的挑战，通过分析非持续学习方法来情境化现有解决方案，并探讨了不同问题配置的影响。我们的目标是提供对CIL现有工作的替代视角，并将注意力引向该问题的未探索方面。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文为现有关于类别增量学习（CIL）的工作提供了替代视角。考虑到资源约束，重新审视了问题定义并描述了其独特挑战。通过分析非连续方法并提供现有工作的概述，提出了一种原则性的解决CIL问题的方法。随后分析了CIL问题的五个具体维度，并描述了现有工作如何处理各种问题配置。文章最后总结了未来工作的建议，认为未来的解决方案可以且应该对数据生成过程做出假设。

**优点与不足：**
**优点：** 1) 文章组织良好，易于理解。2) 视角新颖，关注了CIL问题中未探索的方面。3) 文章重新定义了类别增量学习（CIL）的问题，明确指出了现有定义中的不足，尤其是在资源约束的讨论中。这种重新审视为后续研究提供了更清晰的方向和框架，有助于推动该领域的发展。4) 文章深入探讨了类别增量学习中的三个核心挑战：稳定性-可塑性平衡、跨任务判别学习和知识迁移。这些分析不仅解释了CIL与传统机器学习的复杂性，还指出了未来研究值得探索的方向。5) 文章不仅总结了现有方法，还指出了它们在计算效率、跨任务区分等方面的不足。特别是对“朴素”方法的讨论，为理解CIL发展的困难和方向提供了宝贵的背景信息。

**不足：** 1) 尽管本文与其他关于连续学习的综述有所不同，但涵盖的2023年之后的类别增量学习（CIL）领域的最新进展较少，尤其是新兴的混合方法和新的基准测试。这可能限制了其对希望了解该领域最新进展的研究人员的参考价值。2) 对类别增量学习挑战的讨论主要停留在较高层次。更细致的分解，特别是关注特定子领域（例如，任务无关增量学习与任务相关增量学习）的分析，可以提供更细致的理解，并有益于不同类别的读者。3) 专门讨论“朴素”方法（如单一判别模型、任务特定模型和类别生成模型）的部分，虽然提供了历史背景，但占据了大量篇幅并重复了众所周知的内容。这可能对已经熟悉这些基本方法的预期读者增加不了多少价值。4) 将CIL框架在资源约束而非过去数据不可用方面的论点是有趣的。然而，讨论可以进一步扩展，以解决具体的实际实施和比较，尤其是不同方法的计算成本。这将使论点更具说服力和实际应用性。5) 结论部分虽然提出了一些未来方向，但建议较为宽泛，缺乏具体细节，例如如何解决跨任务判别学习或计算效率等挑战。这限制了文章的实际影响和未来效用。

**建议修改：**
1) 建议作者添加对2023年之后类别增量学习（CIL）领域最新研究成果的讨论，特别是混合模型和新的基准测试方法。可以讨论最近的综述文章，如《类别增量学习：综述》、《少样本类别增量学习综述》等。2) 文章对类别增量学习的挑战进行了更广泛的讨论，建议在此部分增加一些子领域的详细分析，如任务无关增量学习与任务相关增量学习的区别及其各自面临的独特挑战。这将使讨论更加细致，满足不同读者的需求。3) 文章对基本“朴素”方法（如单一判别模型、任务特定模型、类别生成模型）讨论过多，建议简化这部分内容，并腾出更多空间进行现有最先进方法的深入分析和比较，以强调文章的创新性和独特见解。4) 在讨论资源约束对CIL问题的影响时，建议进一步细化和扩展这部分内容，特别是对不同资源约束（如计算和内存）的具体实施、比较和实验结果分析，以提供更多实证支持，使这部分讨论更加稳健和全面。5) 在未来工作部分，建议提出更具体的研究方向，特别是提供关于如何处理跨任务判别学习、知识迁移以及如何在计算效率方面进行优化的可操作建议。这将使文章对未来的研究更具指导性。6) 需要总结以前的增量学习综述，并在表格中展示它们与本文的异同。7) 明确本文综述的时间范围，即所讨论的所有类别增量学习方法均为特定时间点之前发表的研究成果。例如，“本综述涵盖截至2024年10月发布的所有相关工作”。

**更广泛的影响关注：**
1) 文章中提出的CIL框架可能依赖于存储部分旧数据或通过生成模型生成数据以供回放。然而，这可能导致隐私和数据安全问题，尤其是当模型在包含敏感数据的任务上进行训练时，数据泄露的风险增加。模型可能“记住”旧数据并无意中泄露敏感信息，特别是在医疗或金融等领域应用时。建议作者探讨如何在CIL中增强隐私保护机制。2) 类别增量学习（CIL）方法在应用于现实场景时可能继承现有数据的偏见。例如，在自动驾驶或面部识别等敏感领域应用时，模型可能在增量学习新任务时放大数据中的种族、性别或其他社会偏见。文章缺乏对这些社会和伦理问题的讨论，因此建议增加关于如何在CIL方法中解决偏见和公平性问题的内容。

paper_title: Approaches for containerized scientific workflows in cloud environments with applications in life science
paper_abstract: Containers are gaining popularity in life science research as they provide a solution for encompassing dependencies of provisioned tools, simplify software installations for end users and offer a form of isolation between processes. Scientific workflows are ideal for chaining containers into data analysis pipelines to aid in creating reproducible analyses. In this article, we review a number of approaches to using containers as implemented in the workflow tools Nextflow, Galaxy, Pachyderm, Argo, Kubeflow, Luigi and SciPipe, when deployed in cloud environments. A particular focus is placed on the workflow tool’s interaction with the Kubernetes container orchestration framework.
review_content:
The manuscript “Approaches for containerized scientific workflows in cloud environments with applications in life science” by Spjuth et. al. presents a review of containerized workflow managers currently available. The manuscript is well written in a clear and concise way. In my opinion, the manuscript’s sections are organized correctly giving to the readers the idea of how these complex systems are organized. However, I consider, as this manuscript intend to review scientific workflows in cloud environments, that some introduction should be added describing the most important public cloud providers and the tools they provide for cloud computing and workflow execution.

In page 5 paragraph 2, the terms "Amazon Web Services (AWS) Batch service and the Google Genomics Pipelines service" are used without previous definition or explanation of what they are. I would also highlight that “Google Genomics Pipelines service” no longer exist. The current solution in GCP is named “Cloud Life Sciences” (https://cloud.google.com/life-sciences/).

Additionally, the review should describe what is a workflow language, which is at the end, the core of each manager. It should also include main advantages and differences for each workflow language. Users choose the workflow manager depending on the capability of the workflow language to run their specific pipeline.

This review is not mentioning a set of established workflow managers based on the Common Workflow Language (CWL, https://www.commonwl.org) like Arvados (https://arvados.org/), Toil (https://github.com/BD2KGenomics/toil), CWL-Airflow (https://github.com/Barski-lab/cwl-airflow) and StreamFlow (https://streamflow.di.unito.it/). There are also other CWL based manager like REANA (https://docs.reana.io/), Calrissian (https://github.com/Duke-GCB/calrissian) and Mariner (https://github.com/uc-cdis/mariner) that use Kubernetes as well. They also should mention that Galaxy is able to work with CWL and describe the advantages of running Galaxy with CWL.

In my opinion, the manuscript is presenting an incomplete review of workflow managers for scientific computing using the cloud. The discussion is incomplete as important workflow managers like CWL are not mentioned. Also, there should be an introduction and description of workflow language.
paper_title_zh: 云环境中面向生命科学应用的容器化科学工作流方法
paper_abstract_zh: 容器在生命科学研究中的普及度正在提升，因为它们为包含预置工具的依赖项提供了解决方案，简化了最终用户的软件安装过程，并在进程之间提供了一种隔离形式。科学工作流非常适合将容器链接到数据分析管道中，以帮助创建可复现的分析。在本文中，我们回顾了在云环境中部署时，工作流工具Nextflow、Galaxy、Pachyderm、Argo、Kubeflow、Luigi和SciPipe中实现的多种使用容器的方法。特别关注的是工作流工具与Kubernetes容器编排框架的交互。
review_content_zh:
Spjuth等人撰写的论文《云环境中面向生命科学应用的容器化科学工作流方法》对当前可用的容器化工作流管理器进行了综述。该论文写作清晰、简洁。在我看来，论文的各部分组织得当，使读者能够了解这些复杂系统的组织方式。然而，我认为，由于该论文旨在综述云环境中的科学工作流，因此应添加一些介绍，描述最重要的公共云提供商及其提供的云计算和工作流执行工具。

在第5页第2段中，使用了“亚马逊网络服务（AWS）Batch服务和谷歌基因组学Pipelines服务”这些术语，但未事先定义或解释它们是什么。我还想指出，“谷歌基因组学Pipelines服务”已不再存在。当前在GCP中的解决方案名为“云生命科学”（https://cloud.google.com/life-sciences/）。

此外，综述应描述什么是工作流语言，这毕竟是每个管理器的核心。还应包括每种工作流语言的主要优势和差异。用户根据工作流语言运行其特定管道的能力来选择工作流管理器。

该综述未提及基于通用工作流语言（CWL，https://www.commonwl.org）的一组已确立的工作流管理器，如Arvados（https://arvados.org/）、Toil（https://github.com/BD2KGenomics/toil）、CWL-Airflow（https://github.com/Barski-lab/cwl-airflow）和StreamFlow（https://streamflow.di.unito.it/）。还有其他基于CWL的管理器，如REANA（https://docs.reana.io/）、Calrissian（https://github.com/Duke-GCB/calrissian）和Mariner（https://github.com/uc-cdis/mariner），它们也使用Kubernetes。还应提及Galaxy能够与CWL协同工作，并描述使用CWL运行Galaxy的优势。

在我看来，该论文对使用云的科学计算工作流管理器的综述是不完整的。讨论不全面，因为未提及重要的工作流管理器如CWL。此外，应有工作流语言的介绍和描述。

paper_title: MicroRNAs in the development and neoplasia of the mammary gland
paper_abstract: Study on the role of microRNAs (miRs) as regulators of gene expression through posttranscriptional gene silencing is currently gaining much interest,due to their wide involvement in different physiological processes. Understanding mammary gland development, lactation, and neoplasia in relation to miRs is essential. miR expression profiling of the mammary gland from different species in various developmental stages shows their role as critical regulators of development. miRs such as miR-126, miR-150, and miR-145 have been shown to be involved in lipid metabolism during lactation. In addition, lactogenic hormones influence miR expression as evidenced by overexpression of miR-148a in cow mammary epithelial cells, leading to enhanced lactation. Similarly, the miR-29 family modulates lactation-related gene expression by regulating DNA methylation of their promoters. Besides their role in development, lactation and involution, miRs are responsible for breast cancer development. Perturbed estrogen (E2) signaling is one of the major causes of breast cancer. Increased E2 levels cause altered expression of ERα, and ERα-miR cross-talk promotes tumour progression. miRs, such as miR-206, miR-34a, miR-17-5p, and miR-125 a/b are found to be tumour suppressors; whereas miR-21, miR-10B, and miR-155 are oncogenes. Oncogenic miRs like miR-21, miR-221, and miR-210 are overexpressed in triple negative breast cancer cases which can be diagnostic biomarker for this subtype of cancer.  This review focuses on the recent findings concerning the role of miRs in developmental stages of the mammary gland (mainly lactation and involution stages) and their involvement in breast cancer progression. Further studies in this area will help us to understand the molecular details of mammary gland biology, as well as miRs that could be therapeutic targets of breast cancer.
review_content:
The review entitled "MicroRNAs in the development and neoplasia of the mammary gland" has briefly presented recent studies in the relevant studies in mammary gland microRNAs field. This kind of review is very good for scientists to update their knowledge without reading informative reviews. However, minor comments are below to make the review suitable for indexing:

Introduction:
  * More information is needed to understand the mechanism of microRNA roles in the mammary gland.

miRs in mammary gland:
  * Along with Alsaweed et al. study, Modepalli et al. (2014, BMC Genomics) has provided evidence that mammary gland is the main source of microRNAs in milk. Therefore, milk microRNAs are not considered as nutrients as stated, so better to not use "whether they are only simple nutrients".
  * Examples about the milk microRNAs are important as the mammary gland is synthesized and secreted milk.

miRs controlling lactation:
  * Highly expressed microRNAs in milk/mammary gland have different roles in synthesize various milk nutrient contents such as triacylglycerols and lactose, so the role of highly expressed microRNAs must be linked to related functions (Alsaweed et al 2016, PLoS ONE and IJMS).
  * Li et al. (2012, BMC Genomics) has presented very important aspects of the microRNAs and lactation performance.

miRs controlling involution and breast cancer:
  * Zhang et al. (2013, Nature Cell Biology) has provided breast cancer inhibits progression by microRNAs expression roles, so it must be considered in this review.
paper_title_zh: 乳腺发育与肿瘤发生中的微小RNA
paper_abstract_zh: 对微RNA（miRs）作为基因表达调控因子通过转录后基因沉默作用的研究目前正受到广泛关注，这是由于它们在不同生理过程中的广泛参与。理解miRs与乳腺发育、泌乳和肿瘤形成之间的关系至关重要。对不同物种在不同发育阶段的乳腺进行miR表达谱分析显示，它们在发育过程中扮演着关键调控者的角色。例如，miR-126、miR-150和miR-145已被证实参与泌乳期间的脂质代谢。此外，泌乳激素影响miR表达，如牛乳腺上皮细胞中miR-148a的过表达可增强泌乳。同样，miR-29家族通过调节其启动子的DNA甲基化来调控与泌乳相关的基因表达。除了在发育、泌乳和退化中的作用外，miRs还负责乳腺癌的发展。雌激素（E2）信号通路紊乱是乳腺癌的主要原因之一。E2水平升高导致ERα表达改变，ERα与miR的交叉对话促进肿瘤进展。研究发现，miR-206、miR-34a、miR-17-5p和miR-125a/b是肿瘤抑制因子；而miR-21、miR-10B和miR-155则是致癌基因。在 triple negative 乳腺癌病例中，致癌miRs如miR-21、miR-221和miR-210的过表达可以作为该亚型癌症的诊断生物标志物。本文综述了关于miRs在乳腺发育阶段（主要是泌乳和退化阶段）的作用及其在乳腺癌进展中参与的最新发现。进一步的研究将有助于我们理解乳腺生物学的分子细节，以及可能作为乳腺癌治疗靶点的miRs。
review_content_zh:
标题为“MicroRNAs在乳腺发育和肿瘤形成中的作用”的综述简要介绍了乳腺微RNA领域相关研究的最新进展。这类综述对于科学家更新知识而不必阅读信息量大的综述非常有帮助。然而，为了使综述适合索引，以下是一些小建议：

引言：
  * 需要更多信息来理解微RNA在乳腺中的作用机制。

乳腺中的miRs：
  * 除了Alsaweed等人的研究，Modepalli等人（2014，BMC Genomics）提供了证据表明乳腺是牛奶中微RNA的主要来源。因此，牛奶中的微RNA不应被视为如所述的营养物质，所以最好不要使用“它们是否仅仅是简单的营养物质”。
  * 关于牛奶微RNA的例子很重要，因为乳腺合成并分泌牛奶。

控制泌乳的miRs：
  * 在牛奶/乳腺中高表达的微RNA在合成各种牛奶营养成分（如三酰甘油和乳糖）中具有不同作用，因此高表达微RNA的作用必须与相关功能联系起来（Alsaweed等人2016，PLoS ONE和IJMS）。
  * Li等人（2012，BMC Genomics）提出了微RNA和泌乳性能的非常重要方面。

控制乳腺退化及乳腺癌的miRs：
  * Zhang等人（2013，Nature Cell Biology）提供了乳腺癌通过微RNA表达作用抑制进展的证据，因此必须在综述中考虑这一点。
