paper_title: Who participates in computer science education studies? A literature review on K-12 subjects Anna van der Meulen
paper_abstract: Computer science education (CSEd) research within K-12 makes extensive use of empirical studies in which children participate. Insight in thedemographics of these children is important for the purpose of understanding the representativeness of the populations included. This literature review studies the demographics of subjects included in K-12 CSEd studies. We have manually inspected the proceedings of three of the main international CSEd conferences: SIGCSE, ITiCSE and ICER, of five years (2014)(2015)(2016)(2017)(2018), and selected all papers pertaining to K-12 CSEd experiments. This led to a sample of 134 papers describing 143 studies. We manually read these papers to determine the demographic information that was reported on, investigating the following categories: age/grade, gender, race/ethnic background, location, prior computer science experience, socio-economic status (SES), and disability. Our findings show that children from the United States, boys and childrenwithout computer science experience are included most frequently. Race and SES are frequently not reported on, and for race as well as for disabilities there appears a tendency to report these categories only when they deviate from the majority. Further, for several demographic categories different criteria are used to determine them. Finally, most studies take place within schools. These insights can be valuable to correctly interpret current knowledge from K-12 CSEd research, and furthermore can be helpful in developing standards for consistent collection andreporting of demographic information in this community.
review_content: Reviewer 1 Basic reporting Comment #1 The authors note that similar review work has been completed (McGill et al., 2018; Schlesinger et al., 2017), although they seem to indicate that their review is distinct in that it evaluates additional demographic information, disability status in particular. I am not certain that the authors have convinced me that this sensitive information can be widely and appropriately asked across K-12 studies, at least those that occur in the United States Response #1: We agree that the disability factor requires more background and discussion. Consequently we added information on this factor through the paper, in the introduction, results, and discussion section, including on the feasibility of obtaining this information. Below (in response to comments #5 and #9) we provide more detail on these changes. Experimental design Comment #2 The authors do a commendable job of detailing their process and justifying their use of the three conference proceedings. They do note in Limitations that there was no attempt at inter-rater reliability, or double-coding. This does seem potentially problematic as the authors indicated they deduced information context, rather than from details overtly stated in the studies. It may be that one researcher missed vital information or misunderstood. Such double checking is important to the validity of the authors’ claims. Response #2: Thank you for bringing this point to our attention. In the previous version we had omitted to add details about our collaboration process, that could indeed leave room for doubt on the validity of the encoded information. After practicing with reading and encoding the first papers together, we held working sessions where all papers and information flagged as uncertain or inferred was checked and agreed upon. Coding conventions for demographic information we encountered being reported on in a diverse manner were also set during these sessions. As a result of this process, the pieces of information that we did not cross check were the ones explicitly stated in the papers that we examined. In this version, we have updated the methods (page 4, lines 141-144) and limitations (page 9, lines 421-425) sections with these points. Comment #3 Additionally, the authors do not address what safeguards were in place to ensure that an intervention was not submitted to and accepted at more than one of these conferences and therefore those data were considered more than once. Response #3: We agree to this point and we have updated the limitations section accordingly (page 9, lines 413-415). Comment #4 The authors cite appropriately, although I am used to alphabetizing in-text citations when there is more than one cite. Relatedly, there are several places (lines 61, 69, and 74) where the formatting of the citation is incorrect. Response #4: We alphabetized the order of all multiple in-text citations, as well as corrected the citations on lines 61, 69, and 74 (in the new document lines 65, 71, 77). Validity of the findings Comment #5 I provide more specific information below in General Comments, but overall I am struggling to see the feasibility of including disability status as a socio-demographic metric. I understand the authors’ contention that such a characteristic needs to be considered for generalizability purposes; however, the reality of receiving such information, at least in the US, is highly complicated and would not lend itself to generalizability. This aside, the authors complete their literature review as they set out in the Introduction. I feel the authors could strengthen their argument and the paper overall by delving more deeply into the articles that report on disability status, as this seems to be their major interest, especially those not focused solely on a certain population of students (ie., blind students). How did these articles report on these disabilities? What was their institutional review policy? How did they obtain this information (ie., from the students, teachers, or parents)? What major findings/conclusions did they offer? The number of articles that fall into this category is quite small, so more closely exploring them may help draw out and support your contention that disability status is a metric essential to report. Given this small number, perhaps it would be wise to broaden your search beyond the flagship conferences. In other words, the authors could share their literature review findings, including the small number of articles that report on disability status, and then provide a detailed overview of articles in CSEd at large (conferences and journals) that do report on disability status. Response #5 As indicated in our response to Comment #1, we agree that the disability factor requires more information and discussion. We made the following adaptations: First, in the introduction (on page 2, lines 29-33) we briefly provide more context on our consideration to include disability as a demographic factor. In addition to providing the prevalence of disabilities worldwide we indicate how understanding the support of specific subpopulations of learners can increase inclusivity of CSEd. We also acknowledge the especially sensitive nature of this information here. We further elaborate on this in the section on ‘Research on Demographics in Computer Science’ (on page 3, lines 85-95), describing the underrepresentedness of individuals with disabilities in the fields of computing and software engineering as well as the emerging research lines in inclusive CSEd research. Together, we provide more substantiation of the importance of, when possible, including disability as a demographic factor. We fully agree that the feasibility of obtaining this information also requires further attention, which we added in the discussion section (see below). Second, we examined the papers in our review that report on disability more closely and added more elaborate information in the results section ‘Disabilities’ (page 6). We added specificities, or the lack of such specificities, on how the information provided on disabilities was obtained and which specific syndromes were present. This includes the observation that in two studies the target groups (learners with visual impairments or with autism) are part of the research context (a camp specifically for these learners), which suggests the prevalence of disability in these participants was not explicitly obtained. Further, we note that all studies that report on disabilities take place within the US. Third, in the discussion section we now pay attention to the interpretation of our (extended) findings on the disabilities factor, as well as to the sensitive nature of this information and to practical considerations for future empirical studies: • We moved some of the information from the results section on what we interpret as a ‘reporting bias’ that might take place for the factors race/ethnic background, SES, and disabilities, to the discussion section (on page 7-8, lines 314-331). As reviewer 2 pointed out, this information goes beyond describing the results and consequently should be placed in the discussion. Furthermore, by placing the information on the reporting on these three factors in the discussion, we formed a combined discussion point on this ‘reporting bias’, where we also consider that for all three factors this bias could be related to the sensitive nature of this information. • We added a section in this discussion ‘Disability as a demographic factor’ (page 8, lines 341-375). Here, we discuss our findings of the papers in our review that included disability, and consider different appropriate ways to refer to this sensitive information. We also briefly look into options from studies from other venues or journals outside of our three conferences, in order to gain a more elaborate perspective on how disability is currently being treated and could be included in the future. Additional comments Comments #6 Line 5 (Abstract): if space permits, it may be helpful to include the year range Lines 25, 38, and 50: authors appear to use ‘pre-college,’ ‘pre-university,’ and ‘K-12’ interchangeably. I think it would read better if one phrase were used; K-12 is most common. These phrases appear throughout the article. Line 99: it seems the RQ should end as “... in K-12 programming” and not into Line 156: grade 6 is included twice in both elementary and middle school; where did you ultimately include it? This does not seem to be consistently handled. Response #6: Line 5: we added the year range (2014-2018) in the abstract. Line 25, 38, and 50: we agree K-12 is the most common term, and replaced all occurrences of ‘pre-college’ and ‘pre-university’ by ‘K-12’. We clarify this term once for readers who are not familiar with it in line 41 by indicating: ‘K-12’ (pre-university)’ Line 99: we changed ‘into’ into ‘in’ Line 156: we clarified how we handled ‘grade 6’. As explained, specifically grade 6 is known to be considered either elementary or middle school, depending on the state or specific school even. Consequently, it can differ per study whether grade 6 is considered elementary school or middle school. We follow specific studies’ grouping of grade 6 into either of these levels, and where school level was not provided, we classified grade 6 as elementary school unless it was indicated as part of a range that includes higher grades a well (for instance, participants being from grades 6-8), in which case we classified the whole range as middle school (current version this is on page 5, in lines 172-177). Comment #7 Gender: is it important to include the gender options the studies permitted the participants to select, or that --% of studies permitted students to opt out or select Other? Also, the finding that males are overrepresented is not terribly surprising, but I feel this interacts with the context of the studies. For example, did the studies where males were overrepresented take place in elective classes or optional experiences such as camps? Response #7: First, we agree that it is important to indicate how many studies refer to the option ‘other’. We included this in the section on gender in the results (page 5, lines 201-202), referring to the two studies that report on other as a category of gender as well as the percentage of participants in both of these studies included in this category. Second, we explored the role of context by specifically looking at studies where the majority where boys or girls. As we describe in the result section on gender, the few studies where the majority are girls mostly take place in code clubs or after schools, whereas when the majority is boys this is not the case (page 5, lines 186-188). Comment #8 Race/Ethnic Background: Line 178: the sentence that begins on line 177 and includes “studies is represented in,” is poorly worded or missing a reference to a figure. “This is further confirmed by the large number of studies that report on mixed-racial experimental groups, as Figure 3 depicts, which does not correspond with how mixed classrooms typically are in the US (Stroub and Richards, 2013)”: what does this mean? What are mixed classrooms and how are they typically organized/studied in the US? Response #8: First, the sentence on 178 was indeed missing a reference to a figure. We added this reference in the sentence, which now reads: ‘The quantifiable information from the 37 studies is represented in Figure 2’ (line 199 in current version). Second, the interpretation on the large number of mixed-racial groups has been moved to the discussion and rephrased to clarify that more studies refer to ‘mixed-racial’ groups than can be expected from the general population within US classrooms, as the reference by Stroub et al. (2013) indicates. Comment #9 SES and Disabilities: I have combined these two subsections as my concerns with them are similar. As a US researcher, I have always used NSLP (free and reduced school lunch eligibility) as a proxy for SES. This follows because we have never found it appropriate to ask students about their family’s SES and this information is publicly available at the school level. When working with a single class or a subset of students in class, it feels inappropriate to report out the school level SES. No university IRB would approve US researchers asking K-12 students, deemed a vulnerable population, about their disability status. FERPA regulations prohibit school personnel from disclosing such information at an individual level to outside researchers. It may be that a teacher could tell a researcher something generic, such as “of the 30 students in this classroom, 5 have IEPs and 4 have 504 plans.” Line 216: “However, given the aforementioned prevalence of individuals with a disability, it seems unlikely that the participant groups of the other 128 papers did not include any of these children”: of course these classrooms included students with disabilities, but the practice of mainstreaming and not delineating students by ability, likely contributed to the small number of studies that report on this characteristic. Response #9: We agree that school level reporting is a very valid option for both SES and disability. As explained above in our response to Comment #5, we included especially for the disability factor the need for a tailored approach for such sensitive information which include general and/or school level reporting. Comment #10 Lines 273-4: the wording of the final sentence is problematic. You have set up a juxtaposition whereby poor inner city cannot include well-educated. Don’t conflate education and income here. Something like “it could be a school in a poor inner city area or a high-income neighborhood” would be better. Response #10: We have rephrased this sentence, which now reads as ‘it can refer to a school in a poor inner city area or a well-educated high-income neighborhood’ (lines 295-296 in current version). paper_title_zh: 《谁参与计算机科学教育研究？K-12阶段主题文献综述》 安娜·范德穆伦
paper_abstract_zh: 计算机科学教育（CSEd）在K-12阶段的研究广泛采用实证研究方法，其中儿童作为参与者。了解这些儿童的人口统计信息对于理解所包含人群的代表性至关重要。本文综述了K-12 CSEd研究中包含的受试者人口统计信息。我们手动审查了三个主要国际CSEd会议（SIGCSE、ITiCSE和ICER）五年的会议记录（2014、2015、2016、2017、2018年），并选取了所有与K-12 CSEd实验相关的论文。这导致了一个包含134篇论文的样本，描述了143项研究。我们手动阅读这些论文，以确定所报告的人口统计信息，调查了以下类别：年龄/年级、性别、种族/民族背景、地点、先前计算机科学经验、社会经济地位（SES）和残疾。我们的发现表明，来自美国的儿童、男孩和没有计算机科学经验的儿童被包含得最为频繁。种族和SES经常未被报告，并且对于种族以及残疾，似乎存在仅在它们偏离多数时才报告这些类别的倾向。此外，对于几个人口统计类别，使用了不同的标准来确定它们。最后，大多数研究在学校内进行。这些见解对于正确解释当前K-12 CSEd研究的知识具有重要价值，并且有助于在这一领域制定一致收集和报告人口统计信息的标准。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1 基本报告 评论#1 作者指出，类似的综述工作已经完成（McGill等人，2018年；Schlesinger等人，2017年），尽管他们似乎表明他们的综述是独特的，因为它评估了额外的人口统计信息，特别是残疾状况。我不确定作者是否已经说服我相信这种敏感信息可以在K-12研究中广泛且适当地询问，至少在美国进行的研究是这样。回应#1：我们同意残疾因素需要更多的背景和讨论。因此，我们在论文的引言、结果和讨论部分增加了关于这一因素的信息，包括获取这些信息的可行性。以下（针对评论#5和#9的回应）我们将提供更多关于这些变化的细节。实验设计 评论#2 作者在详细描述其过程和论证使用三个会议记录的合理性方面做得值得称赞。他们在“局限性”中确实指出，没有尝试进行评分者间信度或双重编码。这似乎确实可能存在问题，因为作者表示他们是推断信息背景，而不是从研究中明确陈述的细节中得出。可能有一位研究人员遗漏了重要信息或误解了信息。这种双重检查对作者主张的有效性很重要。回应#2：感谢您提出这一点。在之前的版本中，我们遗漏了关于我们合作过程的细节，这确实可能让人对编码信息的有效性产生怀疑。在共同阅读和编码第一批论文后，我们举行了工作会话，对所有论文和标记为不确定或推断的信息进行了检查并达成一致。在这些会话中，我们还设定了遇到多样化报告的人口统计信息的编码惯例。由于这一过程，我们没有交叉检查的信息是我们在所检查的论文中明确陈述的那些。在这个版本中，我们已经根据这些要点更新了方法（第4页，第141-144行）和局限性（第9页，第421-425行）部分。评论#3 此外，作者没有说明采取了哪些保障措施来确保一个干预措施不会被提交并接受于多个会议，从而这些数据被多次考虑。回应#3：我们同意这一点，并已相应地更新了局限性部分（第9页，第413-415行）。评论#4 作者引用得当，尽管我习惯于在有多处引用时对文中引用进行字母排序。相关地，有几处（第61行、第69行和第74行）引用的格式不正确。 回复 #4：我们对所有多个正文引用的顺序进行了字母排序，并更正了第61、69和74行的引用（在新文档中为第65、71、77行）。研究发现的效度

评论 #5：我在下面的“一般评论”中提供了更具体的信息，但总体上，我很难看到将残疾状况作为社会人口统计指标的可行性。我理解作者的观点，即出于普适性考虑，需要考虑这种特征；然而，至少在美国，获取此类信息的现实情况极为复杂，并且不利于普适性。撇开这一点不谈，作者按照引言中的设定完成了文献综述。我觉得作者可以通过更深入地探讨报告残疾状况的文章来加强他们的论点和整篇论文，这似乎是他们的主要兴趣，尤其是那些不仅仅关注特定学生群体（例如，盲生）的文章。这些文章是如何报告这些残疾的？他们的机构审查政策是什么？他们是如何获取这些信息的（例如，从学生、教师还是家长那里）？他们提供了哪些主要发现/结论？属于这一类别的文章数量相当少，因此更仔细地研究它们可能有助于突出和支持你们认为残疾状况是一个必须报告的指标的论点。鉴于这一数量较小，或许拓宽搜索范围，超出旗舰会议之外会是明智之举。换句话说，作者可以分享他们的文献综述发现，包括报告残疾状况的少量文章，然后提供关于CSEd领域（会议和期刊）中确实报告残疾状况的文章的详细概述。

回复 #5：正如我们在对评论 #1的回复中所指出的，我们同意残疾因素需要更多信息和研究。我们做了以下调整：首先，在引言部分（第2页，第29-33行），我们简要提供了更多关于将残疾作为人口统计因素的背景信息。除了提供全球残疾的普遍性外，我们还指出了解特定学习者亚群体的支持如何能增加CSEd的包容性。我们在此也承认这一信息的特别敏感性。我们在“计算机科学中的人口统计研究”部分（第3页，第85-95行）进一步阐述了这一点，描述了在计算和软件工程领域中残疾人的代表性不足以及包容性CSEd研究的新兴研究路线。综合来看，我们提供了更多关于在可能的情况下将残疾作为人口统计因素重要性的论证。 我们完全同意获取此类信息的可行性也需要进一步关注，这一点我们在讨论部分中已经补充（见下文）。其次，我们对综述中报告残疾情况的论文进行了更深入的研究，并在“残疾”结果部分（第6页）增加了更详细的信息。我们补充了关于如何获取残疾信息以及存在哪些具体综合征的细节，或者缺乏此类细节的情况。这包括观察到在两项研究中，目标群体（有视觉障碍或自闭症的学习者）是研究背景的一部分（专门为这些学习者设立的营地），这表明这些参与者中残疾的普遍性并未明确获得。此外，我们注意到所有报告残疾情况的研究均在美国进行。第三，在讨论部分，我们现在关注对我们（扩展的）关于残疾因素的发现进行解释，以及这一信息的敏感性和对未来实证研究的实际考虑：• 我们将结果部分中关于我们解释为可能发生在种族/民族背景、社会经济地位和残疾因素上的“报告偏差”的一些信息移至讨论部分（第7-8页，第314-331行）。正如评审员2所指出的，这些信息超出了描述结果的范畴，因此应放在讨论部分。此外，通过将这三个因素的报告信息放在讨论部分，我们形成了一个关于这种“报告偏差”的综合讨论点，我们也考虑到对所有三个因素而言，这种偏差可能与信息的敏感性有关。• 我们在讨论中增加了一个部分“残疾作为人口统计因素”（第8页，第341-375行）。在这里，我们讨论了综述中包含残疾的论文的发现，并考虑了引用这一敏感信息的不同适当方式。我们还简要探讨了来自我们三个会议之外的其他场所或期刊的研究选项，以便更全面地了解目前如何处理残疾问题以及未来如何将其纳入研究。附加评论评论#6第5行（摘要）：如果空间允许，可能有助于包括年份范围第25、38和50行：作者似乎交替使用“大学前”、“预科”和“K-12”。我认为如果使用一个短语会更好；K-12最为常见。这些短语在文章中多次出现。第99行：似乎研究问题应结束为“...在K-12编程中”而不是“进入”第156行：六年级在小学和中学中都被包括两次；你最终将其放在哪里？这似乎处理得不够一致。回复#6：第5行：我们在摘要中添加了年份范围（2014-2018）。 第25行、第38行和第50行：我们同意“K-12”是最常用的术语，并将所有出现的“pre-college”和“pre-university”替换为“K-12”。我们在第41行对不熟悉该术语的读者进行了一次澄清，指出：“K-12”（大学前）。第99行：我们将“into”改为“in”。第156行：我们澄清了如何处理“六年级”。如所解释的，特别是六年级被认为可能是小学或中学，这取决于州或具体学校。因此，不同研究对六年级是小学还是中学的分类可能有所不同。我们遵循特定研究对六年级的分类，将其归入这两个层次中的任何一个，而在未提供学校水平的情况下，我们将六年级归类为小学，除非它被指示为包括更高年级的范围的一部分（例如，参与者来自6-8年级），在这种情况下，我们将整个范围归类为中学（当前版本在第5页，第172-177行）。

评论#7 性别：是否需要包括研究中允许参与者选择的性别选项，或者有--%的研究允许学生选择退出或选择“其他”？此外，男性过度代表性的发现并不令人惊讶，但我觉得这与研究的背景有关。例如，男性过度代表性的研究是在选修课或如营地等可选体验中进行的吗？

回应#7：首先，我们同意指出有多少研究提到“其他”选项是重要的。我们在结果部分的性别部分中包括了这一点（第5页，第201-202行），提到了将“其他”作为性别类别的两项研究以及这两项研究中包含在此类别中的参与者的百分比。其次，我们通过特别关注大多数为男孩或女孩的研究，探讨了背景的作用。正如我们在性别结果部分所描述的，少数以女孩为主的研究大多在编程俱乐部或课后进行，而以男孩为主的研究则并非如此（第5页，第186-188行）。

评论#8 种族/民族背景：第178行：从第177行开始并包含“研究中有所体现”的句子措辞不当或缺少对图表的引用。“这进一步得到了大量报告混合种族实验组的研究的证实，如图3所示，这与美国混合课堂的典型情况不符（Stroub和Richards，2013）”：这是什么意思？混合课堂在美国是如何组织/研究的？

回应#8：首先，第178行的句子确实缺少了对图表的引用。我们在句子中添加了这一引用，现在该句子读作：“37项研究的量化信息体现在图2中”（当前版本的第199行）。 其次，对大量混血群体的解释已移至讨论部分，并重新措辞以澄清，正如Stroub等人（2013年）的参考文献所示，相较于美国课堂中的普通人群，更多研究提到了“混血”群体。评论#9 社会经济地位和残疾：我将这两个小节合并，因为我对它们的关注点是相似的。作为一名美国研究者，我通常使用NSLP（免费和减价学校午餐资格）作为社会经济地位的代理指标。这样做的原因是我们从未认为询问学生的家庭社会经济地位是合适的，而且这些信息在学校层面是公开可查的。当与单个班级或班级中的部分学生合作时，报告学校层面的社会经济地位似乎不恰当。没有任何大学的IRB会批准美国研究者询问K-12学生（被视为弱势群体）的残疾状况。FERPA法规禁止学校人员向外部研究者披露此类个人层面的信息。教师可能会告诉研究者一些泛泛的信息，例如“这个教室里的30名学生中，有5名有IEP，4名有504计划。”第216行：“然而，鉴于前述残疾个体的普遍存在，其他128篇论文的参与者群体中似乎不太可能不包含这些儿童”：当然，这些课堂中包括了残疾学生，但主流化和不按能力划分学生的做法，可能导致了报告这一特征的研究数量较少。回复#9：我们同意学校层面的报告对于社会经济地位和残疾都是一个非常有效的选项。正如我们在对评论#5的回复中所解释的，我们特别针对残疾因素 inclusion了需要为这类敏感信息采取定制方法的需求，包括一般和/或学校层面的报告。评论#10 第273-4行：最后一句的措辞存在问题。你设定了一个对立面，即贫困内城区不能包含受过良好教育的人。不要在这里混淆教育和收入。类似“它可能是一个贫困内城区的学校，也可能是一个高收入社区的学校”会更好。回复#10：我们已经重新措辞了这句话，现在读作“它可能是指一个贫困内城区的学校，也可能是一个受过良好教育的高收入社区的学校”（当前版本的第295-296行）。来自

reasons: The authors cite appropriately, although I am used to alphabetizing in-text citations when there is more than one cite.
Given this small number, perhaps it would be wise to broaden your search beyond the flagship conferences.

In other words, the authors could share their literature review findings, including the small number of articles that report on disability status, and then provide a detailed overview of articles in CSEd at large (conferences and journals) that do report on disability status.
The authors do a commendable job of detailing their process and justifying their use of the three conference proceedings.

This does seem potentially problematic as the authors indicated they deduced information context, rather than from details overtly stated in the studies. It may be that one researcher missed vital information or misunderstood. Such double checking is important to the validity of the authors’ claims.

Additionally, the authors do not address what safeguards were in place to ensure that an intervention was not submitted to and accepted at more than one of these conferences and therefore those data were considered more than once.
I provide more specific information below in General Comments, but overall I am struggling to see the feasibility of including disability status as a socio-demographic metric.

Gender: is it important to include the gender options the studies permitted the participants to select, or that --% of studies permitted students to opt out or select Other? Also, the finding that males are overrepresented is not terribly surprising, but I feel this interacts with the context of the studies.
The authors cite appropriately, although I am used to alphabetizing in-text citations when there is more than one cite.
Relatedly, there are several places (lines 61, 69, and 74) where the formatting of the citation is incorrect.
SES and Disabilities: I have combined these two subsections as my concerns with them are similar.

paper_title: Parents’ Sharenting Behaviours: A Systematic Review of Motivations, Attitudes, Perceptions, and Impression Management Perspectives
paper_abstract:
Introduction 
 Sharenting involves parents sharing photos, videos, or other information about their children on their social media profiles via online platforms. Research indicated the rising prevalence of parental sharenting behaviour among various countries. 
 
 
 Objective 
 The main aim of this article was to explore the role of motivations, perceptions, attitudes, and impression management on parental sharenting behaviours. 
 
 
 Methods 
 A systematic review examined empirical studies published from 2019 to 2024 regarding parental motivations, attitudes, perceptions, and impression management associated with sharenting. Relevant studies were identified via Scopus and manual reference searches, with data extraction concentrating on study characteristics, demographics, objectives, design, and principal findings. 
 
 
 Findings 
 Parental sharenting is motivated by intrinsic desires, social validation, and impression management, as parents curate content to improve their social image. While children value favourable representations, many object to sharing without consent. Notwithstanding privacy concerns, parents frequently prioritise advantages, raising ethical enquiries regarding children’s autonomy, privacy, and digital identity in digital self-representation. 
 
 
 Conclusion 
 Parental sharenting, motivated by emotional satisfaction, social validation, and impression management, frequently neglects privacy risks and ethical considerations. Such practices may compromise children’s autonomy, privacy, and digital identity, resulting in conflicts with their rights. Children’s varied responses underscore these dilemmas, highlighting the necessity of reconciling parental intentions with safeguarding children’s digital futures and overall well-being. 
 
 
 Recommendation 
 Parents should engage in mindful sharenting, policymakers must safeguard children’s digital rights, professionals should enhance awareness, and researchers should investigate methods to reconcile parental desires with children’s welfare.
review_content:
This paper provides an in-depth exploration of the phenomenon of sharenting, examining various aspects such as motivations, attitudes, perceptions, and impression management. One of the paper's strengths lies in its comprehensive analysis, which covers a wide range of topics related to sharenting, including intrinsic and extrinsic motivations, privacy concerns, and impression management. This thorough approach offers a nuanced understanding of the topic and its implications.
The paper also benefits from the inclusion of studies from diverse countries, employing various research methodologies. This diversity enriches the analysis by providing a broad cultural perspective on sharenting behaviors. Additionally, the integration of theoretical frameworks, such as self-determination theory and impression management theory, helps to frame the motivations and behaviors of parents in a structured manner, offering insights into the psychological underpinnings of sharenting.
Furthermore, the paper critically examines the ethical concerns associated with sharenting, such as privacy violations and the impact on children's autonomy and digital identity. This critical perspective is essential for understanding the potential risks of sharenting. The paper concludes by offering practical recommendations for parents, policymakers, and researchers. It advocates for mindful practices and regulatory measures to address the challenges posed by sharenting.
Despite its strengths, the paper could benefit from improvements in clarity and structure. Some sections might be more effectively communicated with more concise writing and clearer organization to enhance readability and flow. The reliance on self-reported data is acknowledged as a limitation, as such data may be subject to social desirability bias. Future research could incorporate more objective measures or observational studies to validate findings.
The analysis predominantly focuses on Western contexts, which might not fully capture the diversity of sharenting practices globally. Including more studies from non-Western contexts would provide a more balanced view. Additionally, the mention of studies published between 2019 and 2024 suggests an inclusion of future dates, which should be corrected to reflect the actual timeframe of the research covered.
While a narrative synthesis is provided, the absence of a meta-analysis limits the ability to quantify the strength of associations across studies. Including a meta-analysis where applicable could strengthen the statistical rigor of the findings. The discussion could also be enriched by exploring the role of digital literacy in shaping parents' sharenting behaviors and how education can mitigate risks.
Overall, this paper offers valuable insights and recommendations on sharenting. By addressing the identified areas for improvement, it could further enhance its contribution to understanding the complexities of parental sharing behaviors in the digital age.
paper_title_zh: 父母分享育儿行为：动机、态度、感知及印象管理视角的系统综述
paper_abstract_zh:
引言
“晒娃”行为涉及父母通过在线平台在其社交媒体个人资料上分享有关孩子的照片、视频或其他信息。研究表明，父母“晒娃”行为在不同国家中日益普遍。

目的
本文的主要目标是探讨动机、感知、态度和印象管理对父母“晒娃”行为的影响。

方法
系统综述了2019年至2024年间发表的关于父母动机、态度、感知和与“晒娃”相关的印象管理的实证研究。通过Scopus和手动参考文献搜索识别相关研究，数据提取集中在研究特征、人口统计信息、目标、设计和主要发现。

发现
父母的“晒娃”行为受内在欲望、社会认可和印象管理的驱动，父母精心挑选内容以改善其社会形象。尽管孩子们重视积极的形象展示，但许多孩子反对未经同意的分享。尽管存在隐私担忧，父母经常优先考虑优势，引发关于儿童自主权、隐私和数字身份在数字自我表现中的伦理问题。

结论
受情感满足、社会认可和印象管理驱动的父母“晒娃”行为，常常忽视隐私风险和伦理考量。此类做法可能损害儿童的自主权、隐私和数字身份，导致与儿童权利的冲突。儿童的不同反应凸显了这些困境，强调了调和父母意图与保护儿童数字未来和整体福祉的必要性。

建议
父母应进行审慎的“晒娃”，政策制定者必须保护儿童的数字权利，专业人士应提高意识，研究人员应探讨调和父母愿望与儿童福祉的方法。
review_content_zh:
本文深入探讨了“晒娃”现象，考察了动机、态度、感知和印象管理等多个方面。该论文的一大优势在于其全面分析，涵盖了与“晒娃”相关的广泛主题，包括内在和外在动机、隐私关切以及印象管理。这种彻底的方法提供了对主题及其影响的细致理解。

论文还受益于纳入了来自不同国家的研究，采用了多种研究方法。这种多样性通过提供对“晒娃”行为的广泛文化视角，丰富了分析。此外，整合了如自我决定理论和印象管理理论等理论框架，有助于以结构化的方式框定父母的动机和行为，提供了对“晒娃”心理基础的洞察。

此外，论文批判性地审视了与“晒娃”相关的伦理问题，如隐私侵犯以及对儿童自主权和数字身份的影响。这种批判性视角对于理解“晒娃”的潜在风险至关重要。论文最后为父母、政策制定者和研究人员提供了实际建议。它倡导谨慎的做法和监管措施，以应对“晒娃”带来的挑战。

尽管有其优势，但论文在清晰度和结构上仍有改进空间。某些部分可能通过更简洁的写作和更清晰的组织来更有效地传达，以提高可读性和流畅性。依赖自我报告数据的局限性被认可，因为此类数据可能受社会期望偏差影响。未来研究可以纳入更客观的测量或观察性研究以验证发现。

分析主要集中于西方背景，可能未能全面捕捉全球“晒娃”实践的多样性。包括更多来自非西方背景的研究将提供更平衡的视角。此外，提及2019年至2024年间发表的研究表明包含了未来日期，应更正以反映实际研究覆盖的时间范围。

虽然提供了叙述性综合，但缺乏元分析限制了量化跨研究关联强度的能力。在适用情况下纳入元分析可以增强发现的统计严谨性。讨论还可以通过探讨数字素养在塑造父母“晒娃”行为中的作用以及教育如何减轻风险来进一步丰富。

总体而言，本文对“晒娃”提供了宝贵的洞察和建议。通过解决已识别的改进领域，它可以在理解数字时代父母分享行为的复杂性方面进一步提升其贡献。

paper_title: The effect of surface treatments on the bond strength of polyetheretherketone posts: a systematic review protocol
paper_abstract:
Background 
 Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) is widely used in the biomedical field due to its outstanding biological and mechanical properties. Originally employed as a temporary abutment in implantology, recent research has expanded its indications for more definitive applications, such as frameworks and dental post and core. However, PEEK’s inert nature and low surface energy pose challenges for adhesion, necessitating surface modifications. Various physical and chemical modification techniques, including acid etching (e.g., 98% sulfuric acid), sandblasting with alumina oxide (Al₂O₃), plasma treatment, laser irradiation, silanization, and air abrasion with silica-coated particles, have been proposed to enhance PEEK’s bonding performance. Despite numerous clinical investigations, standardized protocols for surface treatment remain lacking. This systematic review aims to assess the impact of surface treatments on the bonding performance of PEEK posts. 
 
 
 Methods 
 A detailed search of the literature will be conducted across several databases including PubMed, Scopus and clinical trial registries. Additional databases such as Cochrane Central, EMBASE, Web of Science and EBSCO will also be included. The search strategy will target controlled randomized studies and non-randomized clinical trials evaluating the impact of surface treatments on PEEK post adhesion strength. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) will be used to assess bias in non-randomized studies, while the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB II) tool will be employed for evaluating randomized controlled trials. Data extraction will focus on study design, treatment methods, outcomes and results. 
 This systematic review protocol will adhere to the guidelines for systematic reviews outlined in the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). 
 
 
 Discussion 
 The discussion will explore the implications of findings on clinical practice, highlighting the importance of enhancing PEEK’s bioactivity and surface energy to improve bonding efficacy in dental procedures. Moreover, it will suggest areas for future research to advance dental materials science, aiming to optimize the utilization of PEEK in dental applications 
 
 
 Systematic review registration 
 PROSPERO: CRD42024529783 (Registered on 08/04/2024).
review_content:
I would like to thank the authors for their meticulous effort in developing this comprehensive protocol. This systematic review is particularly important as it aims to establish evidence on surface treatment techniques, offering insights that could lead to standardized protocols and improved clinical outcomes. The findings have the potential to bridge gaps in current knowledge and guide clinicians in selecting effective bonding strategies for PEEK posts, ultimately enhancing patient care and restoration longevity. Some points need to be addressed to ensure clarity and reliability of results
1- The PROSPERO registration number in the abstract (CRD42024529783) conflicts with the protocol section (CRD42024531175).
2- The introduction overlaps with the abstract’s background section. Streamline to avoid duplication.
3- Please provide more comprehensive introduction with focus on the latest surface treatment for posts bonding.
4- Each statement should be supported by evidence based reference. Please try to merge multiple sentences into one comprehensive paragraph.
5- The inclusion criteria mention "patients requiring dental restoration," yet bond strength is often tested in vitro. Revise the PICOS framework to state whether in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies are all eligible. If so, justify how heterogeneity between study types will be managed.
6- Please Provide a rationale for excluding patients with certain conditions. For example, explain how these factors might confound bonding outcomes.
7- The protocol lacks specific keywords/MeSH terms used. Please include a sample search string in the protocol to demonstrate how terms like "PEEK," "surface treatment," and "bond strength" will be combined.
8- There is no mention of whether non-English studies will be included or excluded.
9- Address how outcomes like "post-operative sensitivity" will be handled if absent in in vitro studies. Specify whether such outcomes are secondary or exploratory.
10- While PROSPERO registration is noted, ethical considerations regarding patient data from included studies are not addressed. The authors could include a statement about ensuring ethical compliance in included studies.
11- No discussion is provided on how this review differs from or builds upon existing systematic reviews on PEEK bonding.
12- I would suggest including newer surface treatments like nanotechnology-based coatings or bioactive materials to ensure relevance to advancing dental practices.
13- Standardize Outcome Reporting: for example (MPa for bond strength) to improve comparability across studies.
14- Acknowledge in the study design the potential challenges in data findings from in vitro vs. in vivo studies and propose strategies to mitigate them.
paper_title_zh: 表面处理对聚醚醚酮桩粘接强度的影响：系统综述方案
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
聚醚醚酮（PEEK）因其卓越的生物和机械性能而在生物医学领域得到广泛应用。最初作为植入学中的临时基台使用，近期研究已将其适应症扩展到更确定的应用，如框架和牙科桩核。然而，PEEK的惰性本质和低表面能对粘接构成挑战，需要表面改性。为提高PEEK的粘接性能，提出了多种物理和化学改性技术，包括酸蚀（例如98%硫酸）、氧化铝（Al₂O₃）喷砂、等离子处理、激光照射、硅烷化和使用二氧化硅涂层颗粒的空气喷磨。尽管进行了众多临床研究，但表面处理的标准协议仍缺乏。本系统综述旨在评估表面处理对PEEK桩粘接性能的影响。

方法
将在多个数据库中进行详细的文献检索，包括PubMed、Scopus和临床试验注册库。还将包括Cochrane Central、EMBASE、Web of Science和EBSCO等数据库。检索策略将针对评估表面处理对PEEK桩粘接强度影响的对照随机研究和非随机临床试验。非随机研究的偏倚评估将使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表（NOS），而随机对照试验的评估将使用Cochrane偏倚风险（ROB II）工具。数据提取将集中在研究设计、处理方法、结果和成果。
本系统综述协议将遵循系统综述和荟萃分析优先报告条目（PRISMA）中概述的指南。

讨论
讨论将探讨研究结果对临床实践的影响，强调提高PEEK的生物活性和表面能以改善牙科程序中粘接效果的重要性。此外，还将提出未来研究的方向，以推进牙科材料科学，旨在优化PEEK在牙科应用中的使用。

系统综述注册
PROSPERO: CRD42024529783（注册于2024年4月8日）。
review_content_zh:
我要感谢作者们在制定这份全面协议中所做的细致努力。这篇系统综述尤为重要，因为它旨在建立表面处理技术的证据，提供可能促成标准化协议和改善临床结果的见解。这些发现有可能填补当前知识的空白，并指导临床医生选择有效的PEEK桩粘接策略，最终提升患者护理和修复体的长期稳定性。为确保结果的清晰性和可靠性，以下几点需要解决：

1. 摘要中的PROSPERO注册号（CRD42024529783）与协议部分的注册号（CRD42024531175）冲突。
2. 引言部分与摘要的背景部分重叠。请精简以避免重复。
3. 请提供更全面的引言，重点介绍最新的桩粘接表面处理技术。
4. 每个陈述都应有基于证据的参考文献支持。请尝试将多个句子合并为一个综合段落。
5. 纳入标准提到“需要牙科修复的患者”，但粘接强度通常在体外测试。请修订PICOS框架，说明体外、体内和临床研究是否都符合条件。如果是，请说明如何管理不同研究类型之间的异质性。
6. 请提供排除某些条件患者的理由。例如，解释这些因素如何可能混淆粘接结果。
7. 协议中缺少具体的关键词/MeSH术语。请在协议中包含一个示例搜索字符串，展示如何组合“PEEK”、“表面处理”和“粘接强度”等术语。
8. 未提及是否包含或排除非英文研究。
9. 如果体外研究中缺少“术后敏感度”等结果，请说明如何处理。明确这些结果是次要的还是探索性的。
10. 虽然提到了PROSPERO注册，但未涉及纳入研究中患者数据的伦理考虑。作者可以包括一项关于确保纳入研究伦理合规的声明。
11. 未提供关于这篇综述与现有PEEK粘接系统综述有何不同或如何在其基础上发展的讨论。
12. 我建议包括基于纳米技术的涂层或生物活性材料等较新的表面处理技术，以确保与先进牙科实践的相关性。
13. 标准化结果报告：例如（以MPa表示粘接强度），以提高各研究间的可比性。
14. 在研究设计中承认从体外与体内研究中获取数据可能面临的挑战，并提出缓解这些挑战的策略。

paper_title: The ELIXIR Biodiversity Community: Understanding short- and long-term changes in biodiversity
paper_abstract: Biodiversity loss is now recognised as one of the major challenges for humankind to address over the next few decades. Unless major actions are taken, the sixth mass extinction will lead to catastrophic effects on the Earth’s biosphere and human health and well-being. ELIXIR can help address the technical challenges of biodiversity science, through leveraging its suite of services and expertise to enable data management and analysis activities that enhance our understanding of life on Earth and facilitate biodiversity preservation and restoration. This white paper, prepared by the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community, summarises the current status and responses, and presents a set of plans, both technical and community-oriented, that should both enhance how ELIXIR Services are applied in the biodiversity field and how ELIXIR builds connections across the many other infrastructures active in this area. We discuss the areas of highest priority, how they can be implemented in cooperation with the ELIXIR Platforms, and their connections to existing ELIXIR Communities and international consortia. The article provides a preliminary blueprint for a Biodiversity Community in ELIXIR and is an appeal to identify and involve new stakeholders.
review_content:
Peer Review: The ELIXIR Biodiversity Community: Understanding short- and long-term changes in biodiversity – RM Waterhouse et al
This article provides a concise overview of the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community which can serve as a hub for the molecular sciences and bioinformatics as it applies to biodiversity science. ELIXIR’s overarching mission has been stated to “support the management of public research data, integrate and coordinate life science resources, and foster the development of innovative services and technical solutions in Europe” (Harrow et al., 20211). Given unprecedented and escalating loss in biodiversity, there is increasing urgency for new scientific discovery, data processing, and data sharing of biodiversity information among scientists, conservation practitioners, and policy makers. This opinion piece summarizes biodiversity threats, societal challenges and global responses, and scientific opportunities in biodiversity research. It then discusses informatics challenges facing biodiversity infrastructures and resources, organizational opportunities for ELIXIR partners, and connections with ELIXIR platforms and communities. The piece concludes with a roadmap listing key goals and long-term objectives for the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community.

The article might best be viewed in the context of the large and growing field of scientists, practitioners, and policy analysts, in government, academic, and non-government (NGO) sectors responding to the emerging crisis of biodiversity loss. Starting in the mid-20th century with many academic researchers who initially documented biodiversity declines, biodiversity science - and biodiversity conservation - has been steadily mainstreamed worldwide (Locke et al.,20192). One of the founders of “conservation biology” the late Michael Soulé described this science as a “discipline with a deadline” working against accelerating extinctions to sustain the wellbeing of society and the environment (Soulé and Wilcox,19803). While encompassing the full spectrum from basic to applied, biodiversity conservation science has often emphasized practical ways to identify key information suitable for action on the ground. One good example coming from the North American NGO NatureServe network is the practical methods for systematic field inventories for natural communities and species to characterize their location, health, and status (Stein et al., 20004). In full disclosure, I have spent most of my working life in this network, first established by The Nature Conservancy in the 1970s.

With much biodiversity conservation initially focused on identifying local areas for nature preserves, the maturing disciplines of landscape ecology, meta-population dynamics, and now climate change research, forced consideration of increasing broader scales of conservation action (Lindenmayer and Franklin, 20135). With rapidly advancing technology and data, and emphasis on remote sensing and modeling with spatial data have become routine (Wiens et al., 20096). And increasingly (one could say belatedly), the value of social science been acknowledged as it has deepened our understanding of complex interactions of people and nature that underlay nearly all conservation strategies (Sandbrook et al., 20137).

Therefore, while I found this piece to be factual, accurate, and well supported by the current literature, it would benefit from a broader interpretation of biodiversity science and more directed treatment of ELIXIR’s potential contributions to the “broader ecosystem” of biodiversity conservation. For example, the rapid advances in genomic science and its application to biodiversity conservation has many parallels to several allied fields previously mentioned, such as in remote sensing and several variants of the social sciences. The ELIXIR Biodiversity Community could gain by considering this prior experience. Thus, avoiding prior mistakes and replicating prior successes. Among the many ways expanding genomic science could affect biodiversity conservation include ecosystem characterization and monitoring, support to biodiversity status assessment, and evaluating progress of conservation actions.

The article states that “A long-term vision sees a future where sequence-based biodiversity monitoring at scale becomes the default and provides the means for ecosystem biodiversity characterisation in space and time.” One area where we may see near-term progress here is in the links between genomic data and remote sensing; where our current forms of ecosystem characterization centered on measures of species composition, ecosystem structure, and environmental setting may be enhanced by remotely-sensed data (hyperspectral and others) indicating patterns within and among readily observed communities and species (Yamasaki et al., 20178). Relationships between measurable genetic diversity and detectable light spectra will always be complex and challenging, but with increasing frequency of remote data collection one can now envision substantial opportunities to identify leading indicators of ecosystem change through their combination.

Current standards to assess and document endangerment status of species and ecosystems – such as those of red listing under IUCN - require documented knowledge of changing health of populations and communities (IUCN 20129; Bland et al., 201710). These standards attempt to simplify complex ecological phenomena into standard categories to provide a reliable status assessment for use by policy makers and engaged stakeholders. Once clear health markers are identified with genomic data, this could contribute substantially to the rigor, efficiency, and impact of biodiversity status assessment.

This naturally follows on to the potential benefit of genomic data to contribute to evaluating success (or failure) of conservation actions. As noted in the article, that these data should contribute to understanding “population-level adaptation and migration processes, in the context of anthropogenic activities (e.g., climate change and urbanisation consequences), and understand[ing] key aspects necessary to restore ecosystem functions.” It is in planning and implementation of conservation actions where one can surely recognize biodiversity conservation as inherently a human-driven process, so once again, the information used must be clear and compelling to all involved, regardless of their interests and biases.

Prior experience in related fields suggest at least several considerations for the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community. As noted in the article, “ELIXIR can serve a critical function here, as a fundamental aspect of its mission is to make connections and coordinate across complex activities.” And “the biodiversity community needs to proactively seek common solutions (without unnecessary duplication of effort) that enable molecular technologies to advance biodiversity research. I would underscore the importance of limiting duplication of effort. Much of the history of biodiversity conservation in marked by unnecessary competition, stove-piping, and duplicated effort among those involved.

And while ELIXIR’s “current focus is on the informatics, databases, and tools more than on the biological questions, . . . as the Community grows, it will be important to widen the diversity of its membership to ensure that the technical developments will serve the needs of biodiversity researchers,” I would encourage this community to begin early to seek out and identify feedback loops from the full spectrum of user communities. As noted above, the users of genomic data for biodiversity conservation will be diverse and demanding, so deeper consideration of user needs (Dubois et al., 202011), and participatory biodiversity science (Zoellick et al., 201212) could have substantial payoffs into the future.

Biodiversity conservation is based on both ecological and social science that is both urgent and time sensitive. It is that applied side of the spectrum that requires urgent support from the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community.
paper_title_zh: ELIXIR生物多样性社区：理解生物多样性的短期和长期变化
paper_abstract_zh: 生物多样性丧失现已被公认为人类在未来几十年内必须应对的主要挑战之一。除非采取重大行动，否则第六次大灭绝将给地球生物圈以及人类健康和福祉带来灾难性影响。ELIXIR可以通过利用其一系列服务和专业知识，帮助解决生物多样性科学的技术挑战，从而实现数据管理和分析活动，增强我们对地球生命的理解，并促进生物多样性的保护和恢复。这份由ELIXIR生物多样性社区准备的白皮书，总结了当前状况和应对措施，并提出了一套计划，既包括技术方面的，也包括面向社区的，这些计划应能提升ELIXIR服务在生物多样性领域的应用，并促进ELIXIR与该领域内众多其他活跃基础设施之间的连接。我们讨论了最高优先级的领域，以及如何通过与ELIXIR平台合作实施这些领域，并探讨它们与现有ELIXIR社区和国际联盟的联系。本文为ELIXIR中的生物多样性社区提供了一个初步蓝图，并呼吁识别和涉及新的利益相关者。
review_content_zh:
同行评审：ELIXIR生物多样性社区：理解生物多样性的短期和长期变化——RM Waterhouse等

本文对ELIXIR生物多样性社区进行了简洁的概述，该社区可以作为分子科学和生物信息学在生物多样性科学应用中的枢纽。ELIXIR的总体使命已被阐述为“支持公共研究数据的管理，整合和协调生命科学资源，并在欧洲促进创新服务和技术的开发”（Harrow et al., 20211）。鉴于生物多样性的前所未有的且不断加剧的损失，科学家、保护实践者和政策制定者之间对新的科学发现、数据处理和生物多样性信息共享的需求日益迫切。这篇观点文章总结了生物多样性威胁、社会挑战和全球响应，以及生物多样性研究中的科学机遇。接着讨论了生物多样性基础设施和资源面临的信息学挑战，ELIXIR合作伙伴的组织机遇，以及与ELIXIR平台和社区的连接。文章最后以路线图的形式列出了ELIXIR生物多样性社区的关键目标和长期目标。

这篇文章最好在应对生物多样性损失这一新兴危机的广大且不断增长的科学家、实践者和政策分析师的背景下进行审视，这些人员分布在政府、学术界和非政府组织（NGO）部门。从20世纪中叶开始，许多学术研究人员最初记录了生物多样性的下降，生物多样性科学——以及生物多样性保护——在全球范围内逐渐主流化（Locke et al., 20192）。“保护生物学”的创始人之一、已故的Michael Soulé将这门科学描述为“有截止期限的学科”，旨在对抗加速的灭绝以维持社会和环境的福祉（Soulé and Wilcox, 19803）。虽然涵盖了从基础到应用的整个范围，生物多样性保护科学通常强调识别适合地面行动的关键信息的实用方法。来自北美非政府组织NatureServe网络的一个良好示例是，系统野外清查的自然群落和物种的实用方法，以表征其位置、健康状况和状态（Stein et al., 20004）。需要完全披露的是，我的大部分工作时间都在这个网络中度过，该网络最初由大自然保护协会在1970年代建立。

最初，生物多样性保护主要集中在识别自然保护区的局部区域，但随着景观生态学、meta-种群动力学以及现在的气候变化研究的成熟学科的发展，迫使人们考虑更大范围的保护区行动（Lindenmayer and Franklin, 20135）。随着技术的快速进步和数据的发展，对遥感技术和空间数据建模的重视已成为常规（Wiens et al., 20096）。而且，社会科学的价值也越来越多地（可以说是迟来的）得到认可，因为它加深了我们对支撑几乎所有保护策略的人和自然复杂相互作用的理解（Sandbrook et al., 20137）。

因此，虽然我发现这篇文章内容真实、准确，并且得到了当前文献的充分支持，但它将从对生物多样性科学的更广泛解释和更直接地处理ELIXIR对生物多样性保护“更广泛生态系统”的潜在贡献中受益。例如，基因组科学的快速进步及其在生物多样性保护中的应用与前面提到的几个相关领域有许多相似之处，如遥感和社会科学的几个变体。ELIXIR生物多样性社区可以通过考虑这一先前经验而获益，从而避免过去的错误并复制过去的成功。扩展基因组科学可能影响生物多样性保护的多种方式包括生态系统特征描述和监测、支持生物多样性状况评估以及评估保护行动的进展。

文章指出，“长期愿景是看到一个未来，即大规模的基于序列的生物多样性监测成为默认方式，并提供在空间和时间上表征生态系统生物多样性的手段。”我们可能在此看到近期进展的一个领域是基因组数据与遥感之间的联系；我们当前以物种组成、生态系统结构和环境设置为中心的生态系统特征描述可以通过遥感数据（高光谱和其他）得到增强，这些数据表明了易于观察的群落和物种内部和之间的模式（Yamasaki et al., 20178）。可测量的遗传多样性与可检测的光谱之间的关系总是复杂且具有挑战性，但随着遥感数据收集频率的增加，现在可以设想通过它们的结合来识别生态系统变化的领先指标的重大机会。

当前评估和记录物种和生态系统濒危状况的标准——如IUCN红色名录标准——需要记录种群和群落健康状况变化的知识（IUCN 20129; Bland et al., 201710）。这些标准试图将复杂的生态现象简化为标准类别，以提供可靠的状态评估供政策制定者和相关利益相关者使用。一旦通过基因组数据明确健康标志，这将对生物多样性状况评估的严谨性、效率和影响力做出重大贡献。

这自然引出了基因组数据对评估保护行动成功（或失败）的潜在益处。正如文章所指出的，这些数据应有助于理解“在人为活动（例如，气候变化和城市化的后果）背景下种群水平的适应和迁移过程，并理解恢复生态系统功能所必需的关键方面。”在保护行动的规划和实施中，人们当然可以认识到生物多样性保护本质上是一个人为驱动的过程，因此，所使用的信息必须对所有相关人员清晰且具有说服力，无论他们的兴趣和偏见如何。

相关领域的先前经验至少为ELIXIR生物多样性社区提供了几个考虑因素。正如文章所指出的，“ELIXIR可以在此发挥关键作用，因为其使命的一个基本方面是建立联系并协调复杂的活动。”并且“生物多样性社区需要主动寻求共同的解决方案（避免不必要的重复努力），以使分子技术能够推进生物多样性研究。”我要强调限制重复努力的重要性。生物多样性保护的历史在很大程度上标志着不必要的竞争、各自为政和参与者的重复努力。

虽然ELIXIR的“当前重点在于信息学、数据库和工具，而不是生物学问题，……但随着社区的发展，扩大其成员的多样性以确保技术发展满足生物多样性研究者的需求将非常重要”，我鼓励这个社区尽早寻求并识别来自整个用户社区的反馈循环。如上所述，基因组数据用于生物多样性保护的用户将是多样且要求严格的，因此，更深入地考虑用户需求（Dubois et al., 202011），以及参与式生物多样性科学（Zoellick et al., 201212）可能会在未来带来巨大的回报。

生物多样性保护基于既紧迫又时间敏感的生态和社会科学。正是光谱的应用侧需要来自ELIXIR生物多样性社区的紧急支持。

reasons: Therefore, while I found this piece to be factual, accurate, and well supported by the current literature, it would benefit from a broader interpretation of biodiversity science and more directed treatment of ELIXIR’s potential contributions to the “broader ecosystem” of biodiversity conservation.
The ELIXIR Biodiversity Community could gain by considering this prior experience. Thus, avoiding prior mistakes and replicating prior successes.

As noted above, the users of genomic data for biodiversity conservation will be diverse and demanding, so deeper consideration of user needs (Dubois et al., 202011), and participatory biodiversity science (Zoellick et al., 201212) could have substantial payoffs into the future.
This article provides a concise overview of the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community which can serve as a hub for the molecular sciences and bioinformatics as it applies to biodiversity science.
This opinion piece summarizes biodiversity threats, societal challenges and global responses, and scientific opportunities in biodiversity research.
It then discusses informatics challenges facing biodiversity infrastructures and resources, organizational opportunities for ELIXIR partners, and connections with ELIXIR platforms and communities.
The piece concludes with a roadmap listing key goals and long-term objectives for the ELIXIR Biodiversity Community.

paper_title: Searching basic units in memory traces: associative memory cells
paper_abstract: The acquisition of associated signals is commonly seen in life. The integrative storage of these exogenous and endogenous signals is essential for cognition, emotion and behaviors. In terms of basic units of memory traces or engrams, associative memory cells are recruited in the brain during learning, cognition and emotional reactions. The recruitment and refinement of associative memory cells facilitate the retrieval of memory-relevant events and the learning of reorganized unitary signals that have been acquired. The recruitment of associative memory cells is fulfilled by generating mutual synapse innervations among them in coactivated brain regions. Their axons innervate downstream neurons convergently and divergently to recruit secondary associative memory cells. Mutual synapse innervations among associative memory cells confer the integrative storage and reciprocal retrieval of associated signals. Their convergent synapse innervations to secondary associative memory cells endorse integrative cognition. Their divergent innervations to secondary associative memory cells grant multiple applications of associated signals. Associative memory cells in memory traces are defined to be nerve cells that are able to encode multiple learned signals and receive synapse innervations carrying these signals. An impairment in the recruitment and refinement of associative memory cells will lead to the memory deficit associated with neurological diseases and psychological disorders. This review presents a comprehensive diagram for the recruitment and refinement of associative memory cells for memory-relevant events in a lifetime.
review_content:
In the review, Dr. Wang has significantly expanded discussion on associative memory cells in the brain from the molecular and cellular levels to functional outcomes. The proposed model for learning and memory was supported by work from the author’s own laboratory, as well as from accumulated literature. This is a timely update that will help reveal novel mechanisms in learning and memory formation and loss, which may help to advance understanding of memory deficits in neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease.

In addition to general comments above, the following some suggestions that the author may consider for the future studies.
 1. The author has simply discussed the possible relationship between associative memory cells and affective disorders such as anxiety and major depression. It sounds interesting but lacks experimental support. I would suggest the author to give more literature view or conduct some proof-and-concept experiments on this aspect the future.
 2. Although the author intends to establish that basic units of memory traces, or engrams, are associative memory cells named by author’s laboratory. It would be more supportive if the author makes the systemic and comprehensive comparisons between cell assemblies in memory traces and associative memory cells. It seems to me that associative memory cells encode the storage of multiple signals, which has not been emphasized by the studies of engrams. As the author states that almost all of learning activities are associative learning, the units to memorize particular associative signals are called as associative memory cells is straight forward. Has the author thought to make a mutual agreement in that associative memory cells and engrams are presenting the same cell ensemble in relevance to memory formation?
 3. The theory of associative memory cells may apply in psychology, although numerous terms and theoretical models about learning and memory have been suggested in this field. Hopefully the author and the team would provide more evidence and information to support this theory.
paper_title_zh: 在记忆痕迹中寻找基本单元：联想记忆细胞
paper_abstract_zh: 关联信号的获取在日常生活中普遍存在。这些外源性和内源性信号的整合存储对于认知、情感和行为至关重要。就记忆痕迹或记忆印记的基本单元而言，关联记忆细胞在学习、认知和情绪反应过程中被招募到大脑中。关联记忆细胞的招募和精细化促进了与记忆相关事件的检索以及对已获取的重组单一信号的学习。关联记忆细胞的招募通过在共同激活的大脑区域之间生成相互的突触支配来实现。它们的轴突会聚和发散地支配下游神经元，以招募次级关联记忆细胞。关联记忆细胞之间的相互突触支配赋予了关联信号的整合存储和互惠检索。它们对次级关联记忆细胞的会聚突触支配支持整合认知。它们对次级关联记忆细胞的发散支配则允许多种关联信号的应用。记忆痕迹中的关联记忆细胞被定义为能够编码多个学习信号并接收携带这些信号的突触支配的神经细胞。关联记忆细胞的招募和精细化受损将导致与神经疾病和心理障碍相关的记忆缺陷。本文综述了关联记忆细胞在一生中与记忆相关事件的招募和精细化的全面图景。
review_content_zh:
在综述中，王博士显著扩展了从分子和细胞水平到功能结果的关于大脑联想记忆细胞的讨论。所提出的学习和记忆模型得到了作者自己实验室的工作以及累积文献的支持。这是一个及时的更新，有助于揭示学习和记忆形成及丧失的新机制，这可能有助于推进对神经退行性疾病（如阿尔茨海默病）中记忆缺陷的理解。

除了上述总体评论外，以下是一些建议，作者可能在未来的研究中考虑：
1. 作者简单地讨论了联想记忆细胞与焦虑和重度抑郁等情感障碍之间可能的关系。这听起来很有趣，但缺乏实验支持。我建议作者在未来提供更多的文献综述或进行一些概念验证实验。
2. 尽管作者试图确立记忆痕迹的基本单位，即记忆印迹，是由作者实验室命名的联想记忆细胞。如果作者对记忆痕迹中的细胞组合和联想记忆细胞进行系统和全面的比较，将更有支持力。在我看来，联想记忆细胞编码了多种信号的存储，这一点在记忆印迹的研究中并未强调。正如作者所言，几乎所有的学习活动都是联想学习，记忆特定联想信号的单元被称为联想记忆细胞是直接明了的。作者是否考虑过联想记忆细胞和记忆印迹在记忆形成的相关性上呈现相同的细胞组合这一相互认同？
3. 联想记忆细胞的理论可能适用于心理学，尽管该领域已提出了众多关于学习和记忆的术语和理论模型。希望作者和团队能提供更多证据和信息来支持这一理论。

paper_title: Epidemiological evidence relating environmental smoke to COPD in lifelong non-smokers: a systematic review
paper_abstract:
Background: Some evidence suggests environmental tobacco smoke (ETS) might cause chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We reviewed available epidemiological data in never smokers. 
 Methods:  We identified epidemiological studies providing estimates of relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) for various ETS exposure indices. Confounder-adjusted RRs for COPD were extracted, or derived using standard methods. 
Meta-analyses were conducted for each exposure index, with tests for heterogeneity and publication bias. For the main index (spouse ever smoked or nearest equivalent), analyses investigated variation in RR by location, publication period, study type, sex, diagnosis, study size, confounder adjustment, never smoker definition, and exposure index definition. 
 Results : Twenty-eight relevant studies were identified; nine European or Middle Eastern, nine Asian, eight American and two from multiple countries. Five were prospective, seven case-control and 16 cross-sectional. The COPD definition involved death or hospitalisation in seven studies, GOLD stage 1+ criteria in twelve, and other definitions in nine. For the main index, random-effects meta-analysis of 33 heterogeneous (p<0.001) estimates gave a RR of 1.20 (95%CI 1.08-1.34). Higher estimates for females (1.59,1.16-2.19, n=11) than males (1.29,0.94-1.76, n=7) or sexes combined (1.10,0.99-1.22, n=15 where sex-specific not available), and lower estimates for studies of 150+ cases (1.08,0.97-1.20, n=13) partly explained the heterogeneity. Estimates were higher for Asian studies (1.34,1.08-1.67, n=10), case-control studies (1.55,1.04-2.32, n=8), and COPD mortality or hospitalisation (1.40,1.12-1.74, n=11). Some increase was seen for severer COPD (1.29,1.10-1.52, n=7). Dose-response evidence was heterogeneous. Evidence for childhood (0.88,0.72-1.07, n=2) and workplace (1.12,0.77-1.64, n=4) exposure was limited, but an increase was seen for overall adulthood exposure (1.20,1.03-1.39, n=17). We discuss study weaknesses that may bias estimation of the association of COPD with ETS. 
 Conclusions : Although the evidence strongly suggests that ETS increases COPD, study weaknesses and absence of well-designed large studies preclude reliable effect estimation. More definitive evidence is required.
review_content:
The review is interesting, because it highlights methodological issues and gaps in surveys assessing the impact of environmental tobacco smoke on COPD incidence. These gaps and inconsistencies in surveys, lead to inadequacy on assessing the impact, and showing non-confirmative results (OR, RR, etc) on the association between ETS exposure and COPD.

I recommend it for indexing with minor changes.

However, the article should address three additional paragraphs or remark on:
 1. Public health message of awareness, it should address that, even if non association is found between ETS and COPD, it is still that ETS kills 90,0000 people per year and it is a global public health issue. Haahtela et al. Helsinki by nature. The nature step for respiratory health,Clinical and Transitional Allergy1.
 2. Should mention water pipe because it is wide spreading: Yousser Mohammad, Rafea Shaaban, Bassam Abou Al-Zahab, Nikolai Khaltaev, Jean Bousquet, Basim Dubaybo. Impact of active and passive smoking as risk factors for asthma and COPD in women presenting to primary care in Syria: first report by the WHO-GARD survey group2. WHO Advisory note 2015: waterpipe tobacco smoking: health effects, research needs and recommended actions by regulators – 2nd ed. World Health Organization. II.WHO Study Group on Tobacco Product Regulation. ISBN 978 92 4 150846 9 (NLM classification: QV 137)3.
 3. Should discuss the difference in the quality of ETS
Not only nicotine but how the smoke is modified in the air and becoming may be more harmful to small airways:
  * Lower ignition temperature
  * Particles become smaller
  * Higher proportion of CO, VOC
Ref found in the article: Mohammad Y. Passive smoking interference with wheezing and asthma Short Review of current knowledge4.

Wirth et al. Respiratory diseases related to passive smoking5.

Beside that, in one study6 the duration of exposure is 2 weeks, maybe we should omit it.
paper_title_zh: 终生非吸烟者中环境烟雾与慢性阻塞性肺疾病相关的流行病学证据：系统综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：一些证据表明，环境烟草烟雾（ETS）可能导致慢性阻塞性肺疾病（COPD）。我们回顾了从未吸烟者的流行病学数据。

方法：我们识别了提供各种ETS暴露指数相对风险（RR）及95%置信区间（CI）的流行病学研究。提取或使用标准方法推导出经混杂因素调整后的COPD的RR。对每个暴露指数进行荟萃分析，并进行异质性和发表偏倚的检验。对于主要指数（配偶曾吸烟或最接近的等价物），分析探讨了RR在不同地点、发表时期、研究类型、性别、诊断、研究规模、混杂因素调整、从未吸烟者定义和暴露指数定义中的变异。

结果：共识别了28项相关研究；其中9项来自欧洲或中东，9项来自亚洲，8项来自美洲，2项来自多个国家。5项为前瞻性研究，7项为病例对照研究，16项为横断面研究。COPD的定义在7项研究中涉及死亡或住院，12项采用GOLD 1+标准，9项采用其他定义。对于主要指数，随机效应荟萃分析33个异质性（p<0.001）估计值得出RR为1.20（95%CI 1.08-1.34）。女性（1.59, 1.16-2.19, n=11）高于男性（1.29, 0.94-1.76, n=7）或性别合并（1.10, 0.99-1.22, n=15，性别特异性不可用），以及病例数超过150的研究（1.08, 0.97-1.20, n=13）部分解释了异质性。亚洲研究（1.34, 1.08-1.67, n=10）、病例对照研究（1.55, 1.04-2.32, n=8）和COPD死亡或住院（1.40, 1.12-1.74, n=11）的估计值较高。较严重COPD（1.29, 1.10-1.52, n=7）也见增加。剂量-反应证据异质性较大。儿童期（0.88, 0.72-1.07, n=2）和工作场所（1.12, 0.77-1.64, n=4）暴露的证据有限，但成年期总体暴露（1.20, 1.03-1.39, n=17）见增加。我们讨论了可能导致COPD与ETS关联估计偏倚的研究弱点。

结论：尽管证据强烈表明ETS会增加COPD风险，但研究弱点和缺乏设计良好的大型研究使得难以进行可靠的效应估计。需要更确凿的证据。
review_content_zh:
该评论很有趣，因为它突出了在评估环境烟草烟雾对慢性阻塞性肺病（COPD）发病率影响的研究中所存在的方法论问题和空白。这些调查中的空白和不一致性导致了评估影响的不足，并且在环境烟草烟雾（ETS）暴露与COPD之间的关联上显示出非确凿的结果（如OR、RR等）。

我建议对其进行少量修改后进行索引。

然而，文章应增加三个额外的段落或评论：
1. 公共卫生意识的宣传信息，应指出即使未发现ETS与COPD之间的关联，ETS每年仍导致90万人死亡，这是一个全球性的公共卫生问题。参见Haahtela等人的《Helsinki by nature. The nature step for respiratory health》，Clinical and Transitional Allergy1。
2. 应提及水烟，因为其广泛传播：参见Yousser Mohammad, Rafea Shaaban, Bassam Abou Al-Zahab, Nikolai Khaltaev, Jean Bousquet, Basim Dubaybo的《Impact of active and passive smoking as risk factors for asthma and COPD in women presenting to primary care in Syria: first report by the WHO-GARD survey group2》。WHO 2015年咨询报告：《水烟烟草吸烟：健康影响、研究需求和监管机构推荐行动》第二版。世界卫生组织。II.WHO烟草产品监管研究组。ISBN 978 92 4 150846 9（NLM分类：QV 137）3。

paper_title: Sustainability communication on social media in the last decade: A review of research perspectives from Asia
paper_abstract: The past decade has been marked by increased discussions on sustainability; some of the prominent accelerators being, mounting natural disasters, vocal climate activism, and the UN Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development. The interest has crossed over from deliberations in global summits to grassroots-level communication. Additionally, the literature points to the increasing usage of social media in communicating sustainability with an increase of interest in this area among Asian researchers. This paper aims to understand the direction of sustainability communication and the usage of social media in the communication of sustainability, in the last decade (2013-2023), from an Asian perspective – researchers and respondents from Asia. A comprehensive search of the literature by Asian researchers on sustainability communication on social media in the past decade was conducted using the Scopus database. The studies were clustered around common directions and terminologies, basis an in-depth content analysis. Based on the analysis, the study presents the current direction of research in sustainability communication on social media in the areas of brand-generated sustainability communication, cause-generated content and user-generated content. Few prominent themes that emerged were of green marketing, greenwashing, social media as a platform for active engagement and environment related discussions. The studies analyzed in the scoping review affirm that sustainability communication on social media in Asia has substantial potential to improve the environmental awareness of the public and promote actual pro-environmental behavior in the broad areas of green purchase and conservation behavior. The review provides a holistic view of the recent trends and possible future directions for sustainability communication on social media.

paper_title_zh: 过去十年社交媒体上的可持续性传播：亚洲研究视角综述
paper_abstract_zh: 过去十年，关于可持续性的讨论显著增加，其中一些主要的推动因素包括频发的自然灾害、积极的气候行动主义以及联合国2030年可持续发展议程。这一兴趣已从全球峰会的审议扩展到基层水平的交流。此外，文献指出，社交媒体在传播可持续性方面的使用日益增加，亚洲研究人员对此领域的兴趣也在提升。本文旨在从亚洲视角（亚洲的研究人员和受访者）理解过去十年（2013-2023年）可持续性传播的方向以及社交媒体在可持续性传播中的使用。通过Scopus数据库，对亚洲研究人员在过去十年关于社交媒体上可持续性传播的文献进行了全面检索。基于深入的内容分析，将这些研究按共同方向和术语进行聚类。根据分析，研究呈现了社交媒体上可持续性传播研究的当前方向，涉及品牌生成的可持续性传播、由议题生成的内容以及用户生成的内容。一些突出的主题包括绿色营销、漂绿行为、社交媒体作为积极参与和环境相关讨论的平台。在范围综述中分析的研究证实，亚洲社交媒体上的可持续性传播具有显著潜力，能够提高公众的环保意识，并在绿色购买和环保行为等广泛领域促进实际的亲环境行为。该综述提供了社交媒体上可持续性传播近期趋势和未来可能方向的全面视角。

paper_title: Automated Design of Metaheuristic Algorithms: A Survey
paper_abstract: Metaheuristics have gained great success in academia and practice because their search logic can be applied to any problem with available solution representation, solution quality evaluation, and certain notions of locality. Manually designing metaheuristic algorithms for solving a target problem is criticized for being laborious, error-prone, and requiring intensive specialized knowledge. This gives rise to increasing interest in automated design of metaheuristic algorithms. With computing power to fully explore potential design choices, the automated design could reach and even surpass human-level design and could make high-performance algorithms accessible to a much wider range of researchers and practitioners. This paper presents a broad picture of automated design of metaheuristic algorithms, by conducting a survey on the common grounds and representative techniques in terms of design space, design strategies, performance evaluation strategies, and target problems in this field.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
Contributions * The authors formalize the auto-design of metaheuristic algorithms into four modules (design space, design strategy, performance evaluation strategy, and target problem). * Design options for each module are discussed. Each of the first three modules ends with a comment on usability of the options. * The design space module is highlighted, which is not covered in related surveys.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
As a survey paper, I find the main strengths are: * The paper is well structured and well written. While there are many in-depth discussions, I find the writing engaging and easy to follow. The paper should be very accessible to a wide range of audience from different communities (e.g., genetic programming, automated machine learning). * The role of the design space is highlighted, which is not emphasized in prior surveys. I think this is a great decision, since in practice, the design space has great impact on the search efficiency and the performance of the searched algorithm. The discussion is thoughtfully organized into two parts: space with low-level computational primitives and space with high-level algorithmic operators. For each space type, different representation options are given (tree, linear array, graph) and their pros and cons are clearly discussed. * The usability sections provide practical recommendation for researchers what options to consider for each module. * The authors provide valuable insights on why certain methods are appealing for certain cases. (e.g. the discussion of reinforcement learning algorithms in section 4.1) I don't see particular weaknesses in this survey.

**Requested Changes:**
[Optional] It could be useful to include a figure for the linear array representation (just like Figure 2 is for tree, and Figure 4 is for graph)

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 元启发式算法的自动化设计：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 元启发式算法在学术界和实践中取得了巨大成功，因为其搜索逻辑可以应用于任何具有可用解表示、解质量评估和一定局部性概念的问题。手动设计用于解决目标问题的元启发式算法被批评为费力、易出错且需要密集的专业知识。这引发了人们对元启发式算法自动设计的日益关注。凭借计算能力来全面探索潜在的设计选择，自动设计可以达到甚至超越人类水平的设计，并使高性能算法能够被更广泛的研究人员和从业者所使用。本文通过调查该领域的设计空间、设计策略、性能评估策略和目标问题的共同基础和代表性技术，呈现了元启发式算法自动设计的广阔图景。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
* 作者将元启发式算法的自动设计形式化为四个模块（设计空间、设计策略、性能评估策略和目标问题）。
* 讨论了每个模块的设计选项。前三个模块的每个模块都以对选项可用性的评论结束。
* 突出了设计空间模块，这在相关综述中未涉及。

**优点和缺点：**
作为一篇综述论文，我认为其主要优点如下：
* 论文结构清晰，文笔流畅。尽管有许多深入讨论，但我发现写作引人入胜且易于理解。该论文应能被来自不同领域（如遗传编程、自动化机器学习）的广泛读者所接受。
* 突出了设计空间的作用，这在之前的综述中未得到强调。我认为这是一个很好的决定，因为在实践中，设计空间对搜索效率和所搜索算法的性能有很大影响。讨论被周到地分为两部分：包含低级计算原语的空间和包含高级算法操作符的空间。对于每种空间类型，给出了不同的表示选项（树、线性数组、图），并清晰地讨论了其优缺点。
* 可用性部分为研究人员提供了每个模块应考虑哪些选项的实用建议。
* 作者提供了关于某些方法为何在某些情况下具有吸引力的宝贵见解（例如，第4.1节中对强化学习算法的讨论）。
我认为这篇综述没有特别的缺点。

**请求的更改：**
[可选] 包含一个线性数组表示的图可能会很有用（就像图2用于树，图4用于图一样）

**受众：**

paper_title: The emergence of a modern paradigm for urban health
paper_abstract: The importance of urban health in achieving global and planetary health goals is increasingly recognized. Cities offer important opportunities to improve health while also presenting significant challenges. As our understanding of and evidence for the importance of determinants of health beyond health care have grown, the need for urban health policies and actions that transcend disciplinary and sectoral boundaries and involve multiple stakeholders in urban decision-making has become clearer. Current urban health practice builds on decades of conceptual and operational work. This paper traces the evolution of the urban health paradigm through research, policy and practice in recent decades. We suggest that, despite the proven utility of urban health as a paradigm and its conceptual and practical evolution for effective urban health governance, significant challenges remain, especially related to implementing the systems approaches needed to improve health amidst the complexity of urban dynamics.
review_content:
I answered ‘partly’ to three of the four questions because :
a) it would be hard, if not impossible, to be comprehensive given such a large field of thought and practice extending over several decades. However, this review covers the major global developments and initiatives well.
b) language accessibiliutry depends upon the audience. This would not be accessible to the general public, and perhaps not to an academic audience not familiar with some of the concepts. However, it is well written and is accessible for me.
c) There is no ‘Conclusions’ section, but Section 7 is about ‘Moving Forward, and I have some thoughts, noted below, about how this section could be strengthened.
Here are my main comments; I also noted some minor typos that I list at the end.
1. Given “The modern urban context requires fresh thinking about how best to maximise urban health and wellbeing”, maybe change the title to read “The emergence of a modern paradigm for urban health and wellbeing”
2. Given several references to wellbeing, I was surprised to see no reference to the Geneva Charter for Well-being (WHO, 2021) and no expansion on the concept of a wellbeing society as it would apply to a city or community, one that would be committed to “achieving equitable health now and for future generations without breaching ecological limits”. This would be a useful idea to consider in Section 7
3. On P 5 – the section on HPP should reference the 1984 Beyond Health Care conference that launched the concept and the 1988 Second WHO Health Promotion conference on Healthy Public Policy in Adelaide that resulted in the Adelaide Statement, and included a section on Healthy Public Policy at the Local Level that resulted in an edited book (A. Evers et al. (eds.), Healthy Public Policy at the Local Level. Frankfurt/Boulder: Campus/Westview, 1990)
4. Towards the end of section 3, in the discussion of health and planetary boundaries and sustainability, it is worth noting that the links between health and sustainability were developed in the 1990s (see e.g. Hancock, Trevor (1996) “Planning and creating healthy and sustainable cities: the challenge for the 21st century.” In C. Price and A. Tsouros (eds.), Our Cities, Our Future: Policies and Action for Health and Sustainable Development. Copenhagen: WHO Healthy Cities Project Office; Hancock, Trevor (1996) Healthy, sustainable communities: concept, fledgling practice and implications for governance Alternatives 22 (2), pp 18-23; Hancock, Trevor (2000) Healthy Communities Must Be Sustainable Communities Too Public Health Reports 115 (2 and 3): 151–6)
5. There is no mention of ecology or ecosystems at all, and only a brief discussion of planetary boundaries in section 3.4 (Complexity and the ‘causes of the causes’ of ill-health ). I see a need for a paragraph or two expanding on “we are starting to see the creation of a more widespread contemporary understanding of urban health” that would incorporate the concept of the ecological determinants of health, planetary health and planetary boundaries (e.g. Hancock, 2018: “Healthy Cities 2.0: Transitioning towards ‘One Planet’ cities” (Key challenges facing 21st century cities, Part 3) Cities & Health 1 (3)
6. There is only a passing reference to the new economics (e.g. the application of Donut Economics at the urban level) and the importance of the commercial determinants for urban health (including the role of the private sector in urban development, housing, food systems and urban heating and urban pollution). These are new/emerging areas that merit some expanded discussion in section 7
7. P 12, section 7 – I would add to “Prodigious urbanisation . . .” the emerging threat to health posed by what the UN calls “the triple planetary crisis” of climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution as well as other global ecological changes that are crossing planetary boundaries. Also, a brief discussion of the ecological injustice dimensions of declining planetary health

Typos
P 7, first line – “towards a systemic approach to urban health.the WHO European Regional Office” should read “towards a systemic approach to urban health. The WHO European Regional Office”
P 7, section 4.2 - “a centre unique in its placement within in a built environment faculty” - delete ‘in’
P 7, section 4.2 - “the Health Map now been adopted by a wide range of actors” should read “the Health Map has now been adopted by a wide range of actors”
P 12, section 6 – “has been gleaned from implementation has accumulated in part” should read “has been gleaned from implementation that has accumulated in part”
P 12, section 6 – “those embracing a community assets-focussed and action-oriented agendas” – delete one ‘s’ in ‘focussed’ and the ‘s’ on ‘agendas’
paper_title_zh: 现代城市健康范式的兴起
paper_abstract_zh: 城市健康在实现全球和行星健康目标中的重要性日益得到认可。城市提供了改善健康的重要机会，同时也带来了显著挑战。随着我们对医疗保健之外的健康决定因素的重要性的理解和证据的增长，跨学科和部门界限并涉及多个城市决策利益相关者的城市健康政策和行动的需求变得更加明确。当前的城市健康实践建立在数十年的概念和操作性工作之上。本文追溯了近年来通过研究、政策和实践的城市健康范式的演变。我们认为，尽管城市健康作为一个范式已被证明具有实用价值，并在概念和实践上为有效的城市健康治理不断演变，但仍存在重大挑战，尤其是与在复杂的城市动态中实施改善健康所需的系统方法相关的问题。
review_content_zh:
我对四个问题中的三个回答了“部分”，原因如下：

a) 在如此庞大的思想与实践领域，涵盖数十年，要做到全面几乎是不可能的。然而，这篇综述很好地涵盖了主要的全球发展和倡议。

b) 语言的可及性取决于受众。这对于普通公众来说并不容易理解，对于那些不熟悉某些概念的学术受众来说也可能如此。然而，文章写得很好，对我来说是可理解的。

c) 没有专门的“结论”部分，但第7节是关于“向前迈进”的，我有一些关于如何加强这一部分的想法，如下所述。

以下是我的主要评论；我还注意到一些小错别字，列在最后。

1. 考虑到“现代城市背景要求重新思考如何最大限度地提升城市健康和福祉”，或许可以将标题改为“现代城市健康与福祉范式的兴起”。

2. 考虑到多次提到福祉，我惊讶地发现没有提及《日内瓦福祉宪章》（WHO，2021年），也没有扩展福祉社会的概念，尤其是如何将其应用于城市或社区，即致力于“在不突破生态限制的情况下，实现当前和未来几代人的健康公平”。在第7节中考虑这一想法将是有益的。

3. 在第5页——关于HPP的部分应提及1984年启动该概念的“超越医疗保健”会议，以及1988年在阿德莱德举行的第二次WHO健康促进会议，该会议产生了《阿德莱德声明》，并包括关于地方层面健康公共政策的部分，最终形成了一本编辑书籍（A. Evers等编，《地方层面的健康公共政策》。法兰克福/博尔德：Campus/Westview，1990年）。

4. 在第3节末尾，讨论健康与行星边界和可持续性时，值得指出的是，健康与可持续性之间的联系是在1990年代发展起来的（参见例如Hancock, Trevor (1996) “规划与创造健康和可持续城市：21世纪的挑战。” In C. Price and A. Tsouros (eds.), Our Cities, Our Future: Policies and Action for Health and Sustainable Development. Copenhagen: WHO Healthy Cities Project Office; Hancock, Trevor (1996) Healthy, sustainable communities: concept, fledgling practice and implications for governance Alternatives 22 (2), pp 18-23; Hancock, Trevor (2000) Healthy Communities Must Be Sustainable Communities Too Public Health Reports 115 (2 and 3): 151–6）。

5. 完全没有提到生态或生态系统，只在第3.4节（复杂性和疾病的“原因的原因”）中简要讨论了行星边界。我认为需要增加一两个段落，扩展“我们开始看到更广泛的对城市健康的当代理解的形成”，以包含健康生态决定因素、行星健康和行星边界的概念（例如Hancock, 2018: “Healthy Cities 2.0: Transitioning towards ‘One Planet’ cities” (Key challenges facing 21st century cities, Part 3) Cities & Health 1 (3)）。

6. 只简要提及了新经济学（例如在城市层面应用甜甜圈经济学）和商业决定因素对城市健康的重要性（包括私营部门在城市发展、住房、食品系统和城市供暖及污染中的作用）。这些是新/新兴领域，在第7节中值得进行更深入的讨论。

7. 第12页，第7节——我会在“惊人的城市化……”中加入联合国所称的“三重行星危机”（气候变化、生物多样性丧失和污染）对健康构成的威胁，以及其他跨越行星边界的全球生态变化。此外，简要讨论行星健康下降的生态不公维度。

错别字：

第7页，第一行——“towards a systemic approach to urban health.the WHO European Regional Office”应改为“towards a systemic approach to urban health. The WHO European Regional Office”。

第7页，第4.2节——“a centre unique in its placement within in a built environment faculty”——删除第二个“in”。

第7页，第4.2节——“the Health Map now been adopted by a wide range of actors”应改为“the Health Map has now been adopted by a wide range of actors”。

第12页，第6节——“those embracing a community assets-focussed and action-oriented agendas”——删除“focussed”中的一个“s”和“agendas”中的“s”。
