paper_title: Complex mechanisms linking neurocognitive dysfunction to insulin resistance and other metabolic dysfunction
paper_abstract: Scientific evidence has established several links between metabolic and neurocognitive dysfunction, and epidemiologic evidence has revealed an increased risk of Alzheimer’s disease and vascular dementia in patients with diabetes. In July 2015, the National Institute of Diabetes, Digestive, and Kidney Diseases gathered experts from multiple clinical and scientific disciplines, in a workshop entitled “The Intersection of Metabolic and Neurocognitive Dysfunction”, to clarify the state-of-the-science on the mechanisms linking metabolic dysfunction, and insulin resistance and diabetes in particular, to neurocognitive impairment and dementia. This perspective is intended to serve as a summary of the opinions expressed at this meeting, which focused on identifying gaps and opportunities to advance research in this emerging area with important public health relevance.
review_content:
This rather comprehensive review of the connections between the metabolic syndrome associated with Type-2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and cognitive impairment was inspired by a workshop held by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK). The article is so thorough and well organized that one assumes the proceedings of that meeting must have been only the starting point and that the thoughts and opinions arising from that brainstorming session have been embellished with considerable diligence and reflection here.

Most of the points covered in this “white paper” are well reasoned and well researched. And all the topics represent elements of pathology and pathogenesis that will be key to any faithful attempt to understand the intersection between T2DM, dementia, and milder forms of cognitive impairment. Other authors have often succumbed to the temptation to focus on Alzheimer’s disease (AD) as the tag-word for these discussions, but one of the triumphs of this review is its more general consideration of dementia and sub-demented deficiencies as per their connections to energy substrates, both in the central nervous system and peripherally. Indeed, the authors highlight a consideration that seems to be gaining in prominence and frequency in discussions of AD itself: the fact that heterogeneity—especially within certain classifications of age, gender, and genetics—suggests not only multiple routes to AD, but also multiple disease endpoints. Particularly within the “oldest-old” populations, APOE4-negative individuals, and high-risk populations such as military veterans, classic AD pathology correlates rather loosely with cognition. To their credit, the authors discuss the possibility that metabolic derangement may yet be shown to be the driving force for at least some of these cases:

"[I]t is still unclear if the relationship between diabetes and neurocognitive dysfunction and dementia is due to classic AD pathology, vascular processes such as infarcts or vessel pathology, other pathologies less closely related to AD or vascular disease (e.g., impaired brain insulin signaling), or some combination of these. Some have proposed that ‘all-cause’ dementia be employed in order to avoid the implication that we can classify etiologies accurately based on current knowledge."

Another important point made here regards the direction of causality. Hypotheses inspired by the earliest epidemiological links between dementia and T2DM presumed that complications of the latter drive the neuropathologies (mostly, those related to protein aggregation) that underlie AD and related dementias. But a more accurate picture of the relevant events in AD progression has been afforded—largely through advances in neuroimaging tools—and this insight sets the stage for researchers to now say,

"…the pathophysiological processes that lead to metabolic and neurocognitive dysfunction precede the development of clinical syndromes by years…. Indeed, AD neuropathology is detectable more than 10 years before the onset of the first clinical symptoms (Bateman et al., 2012) and pre-diabetes also precedes diabetes by years in most cases."

In fact, data indicate that changes in amyloid β-peptide (Aβ) precede reductions in cerebral glucose utilization, the latter of which may be an important index of metabolic syndrome (below). Supported by evidence from animal models, emerging trends in hypothesis-building include the supposition that CNS accumulation of Aβ, and perhaps other elements of neurodegeneration, are sufficient to perturb peripheral metabolism. This allows consideration of the possibility that correlations between cognitive impairment and cortical amyloid burden are so capricious because an important modulatory (or even instigating) factor is the accumulation of Aβ in subcortical regions:

"Therefore, it is plausible that AD pathology (amyloid-beta or Aβ, tauopathy) may be present in the hypothalamus prior to the onset of cognitive symptoms, and that this hypothalamic pathology could disrupt homeostatic functions such as energy balance and peripheral metabolism prior to the onset of detectable cognitive dysfunction (Ishii & Iadecola, 2015b)."

It is also encouraging to see the inclusion of information on effects of obesity and diet that appear to be independent of glycemic regulation. This is an intriguing body of data, considering the untoward effects of high-fat diets in rodents vis-à-vis the benefits that ketogenic diets and their mimics seem to have in humans 1. It seems that metabolic impacts on brain health could benefit from better understanding of the effects that are brought to bear by shifts between the prominent energy-substrate molecules, perhaps through impacts on such substances that also impact neurotransmitter pools, such as glutamate and glutamine. And it might be productive here to consider hypotheses regarding the finding that obesity in midlife is correlated with dementia manifest decades later 2, at a time when weight loss may be more common.

For all the salient points made in this white paper, the authors still find themselves perpetuating a conventional assumption that seems shortsighted in light of a substantial body of evidence; this is all the more disappointing because they consider what the implications would be “if metabolic disease impacts the brain in ways that differ from its effects on other end organs impacted by diabetes and other metabolic disease.” This is almost certainly the case. The traditional view that elevated glucose in the blood must, by necessity, produce elevated glucose in the brain ignores the existence of the blood-brain barrier (BBB); very little glucose can enter the cerebrum, or most other regions of the CNS, without regulated transport, the bulk of which is handled by glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1). Thus, it was quite surprising to read a major conclusion in the paper that seems to have been based primarily on a single publication, and moreover, one devoted not to the brain but to the retina:

"Diabetes is associated with upregulation of the GLUT1 glucose transporter (Kumagai et al., 1996); glucose provides the original source of glutamate in the brain (Bradford & Thomas, 1969), and chronic hyperglycemia may thus lead to excessive glutamate and increased risk of excitotoxicity."

This is subject to criticism on two counts: 1) Several studies show that AD and hyperglycemia are both associated with reductions in endothelial glucose transporters, likely reflecting—at least in the latter—a reactive feedback inhibition; this probably contributes to the diminished 2-deoxyglucose accumulation in both disorders. 2) Excitotoxicity is more likely to be a consequence of glucose deprivation; this is a well-established relationship 3,4, whereas the claim that high glucose elevates glutamate release is tenuous and unsupported by citations. Publications documenting a diminution of GLUT1 levels in hyperglycemia and/or the converse, an elevation in hypoglycemia, comprise an overwhelming body of evidence 5-10. The authors later provide some evidence suggesting effects on the BBB from metabolic abnormalities in rat models, particularly those brought on by diet, but data in humans is spotty and of unclear relevance to glucose delivery.

Less serious or less consequential issues arose with regard to a few other elements in the paper:

"Unlike other complications of diabetes…, neurocognitive complications of diabetes have not clearly been demonstrated to correlate with measures of peripheral glycemia (with the exception of very poor glycemic control, HbA1c > 10% and a potential role for glycemic variability) and there is only limited evidence for a modest association with other measures of peripheral glucose regulation…."

Why would it be necessary—or indeed, even helpful—to exclude HbA1c levels and glycemic control from the calculus? Which indices of peripheral glycemia would be more justifiable? To be sure, 10% is a quite high level for HbA1c, but lower levels might show a detectable effect in an adequately powered study. Moreover, HbA1c might not change dramatically under conditions of highly fluctuating blood-glucose concentrations, and yet such wild swings could easily produce intolerable strains on glucose-sensitive tissues—including brain endothelium—simply by virtue of their volatility.

The authors are to be applauded for their mention (however brief) of the apparent paradox between the ill effects of pathological insulin resistance versus the benefits of experimentally interrupting insulin signaling, at least in C. elegans. It should be noted that similar benefits (e.g., on live span) accrue in mammals from inhibition of signaling for insulin-like growth factor (IGF), and C. elegans have only one peptide to accomplish the roles of both insulin and IGF. Nevertheless, the conundrum is one that has vexed experimental gerontologists for decades, owing in part to the similar benefits afforded by attention of the insulin/IGF signaling (IIS) pathway and by dietary restriction, the latter of which certainly reduces overall insulin production. One should not expect the authors to have cracked this tough nut, but important rumination might result from a slightly more complete discussion of the differences between reactive (feedback-mediated) insulin resistance and the proactive sort effected by empirical manipulation of IIS.

Also given short shrift here is the undeniable connection of inflammation to both metabolic syndrome and neurocognitive disorders. This is obviously an underappreciated link that deserves greater attention among scientists seeking to synthesize these fields; reviewers of grants and papers continue to express befuddlement when the topic of neuroinflammation is broached in this context. Given the overwhelming evidence for inflammation-related events in the etiologies of both T2DM and AD, it is almost certain to contribute to their coincidence. In fact, compelling evidence has supported just this sort of causal involvement in animal models 11. The authors have included the word “inflammation,” distributed diffusely in the paper; perhaps it would create the appropriate emphasis if some of these references were consolidated in one or two paragraphs along with more specific information, e.g., the seminal role of IKK2 in insulin resistance 12 and Aβ effects 13.

Finally, the paper’s conclusion with “Some broad research needs” is doubtlessly faithful to the output of the workshop’s deliberations, but many of the points outlined in this list come across as rather vague. Without further elaboration, it is not clear what gaps in knowledge some of them would address. One wonders if several could be combined and embellished with a bit more elaboration.

In its overall contribution, this white paper provides a very useful and much-needed synthesis of data and concepts regarding the connections between cognition and metabolic derangement. Modifiable elements of lifestyle and environment have recently emerged as major considerations in the prevention of dementia. Stoeckel et al. have enhanced the conversation by broadening it to other categories of cognitive impairment. In addition, they largely succeeded in summarizing the current state of fields that can seem disparate, and they highlight opportunities to draw these fields closer.
paper_title_zh: 复杂机制连接神经认知功能障碍与胰岛素抵抗及其他代谢功能障碍
paper_abstract_zh: 科学证据已确立代谢功能与神经认知功能障碍之间的若干联系，流行病学证据显示，糖尿病患者患阿尔茨海默病和血管性痴呆的风险增加。2015年7月，美国国家糖尿病、消化和肾脏疾病研究所召集了来自多个临床和科学领域的专家，举办了一场名为“代谢与神经认知功能障碍的交汇点”的工作坊，旨在阐明关于代谢功能障碍，尤其是胰岛素抵抗和糖尿病与神经认知障碍和痴呆之间关联机制的科学现状。本观点旨在作为此次会议中表达意见的总结，会议重点在于识别这一新兴领域（对公共卫生具有重要意义）的研究差距和机遇，以推进相关研究。
review_content_zh:
这篇对2型糖尿病（T2DM）相关代谢综合征与认知障碍之间联系的全面综述，灵感来源于国立糖尿病、消化和肾脏疾病研究所（NIDDK）举办的一个研讨会。文章如此详尽且组织得当，以至于人们认为那次会议的成果仅仅是一个起点，而那次头脑风暴中产生的思想和观点在此得到了相当勤奋和深入的补充和反思。

这篇“白皮书”中涵盖的多数观点都经过了充分的推理和深入研究。所有主题都代表了病理和病理发生学的要素，这些要素对于任何试图理解T2DM、痴呆以及较轻认知障碍之间交叉点的忠实尝试都至关重要。其他作者常常禁不住诱惑，将阿尔茨海默病（AD）作为这些讨论的标签词，但本综述的一个成就是其对痴呆和亚痴呆缺陷的更广泛考虑，尤其是它们与中枢神经系统和外周能量底物的联系。事实上，作者们强调了一个在AD讨论中似乎越来越重要和频繁的观点：异质性——特别是在某些年龄、性别和遗传分类中——不仅提示了多种通往AD的途径，还提示了多种疾病终点。特别是在“最老老人”群体、APOE4阴性个体以及军事退伍军人等高风险群体中，经典AD病理与认知的相关性相当松散。值得称赞的是，作者们讨论了代谢紊乱可能至少在某些情况下是驱动力的可能性：

“目前尚不清楚糖尿病与神经认知功能障碍和痴呆之间的关系是由于经典AD病理、血管过程（如梗死或血管病理）、与AD或血管疾病关系较不密切的其他病理（例如，脑胰岛素信号受损），还是这些因素的某种组合。有人提议采用‘全因’痴呆，以避免基于当前知识准确分类病因的暗示。”

另一个重要观点涉及因果关系的方向。受早期痴呆与T2DM之间流行病学联系的启发，假设后者的并发症驱动了AD及相关痴呆的神经病理学（主要是与蛋白质聚集相关的那些）。但通过神经影像工具的进步，我们获得了对AD进展中相关事件的更准确描绘，这一洞察为研究人员现在所说的奠定了基础：

“……导致代谢和神经认知功能障碍的病理生理过程在临床综合征发展之前数年就已存在……。” 确实，阿尔茨海默病（AD）的神经病理学特征在首次临床症状出现前10多年即可检测到（Bateman等人，2012年），而在大多数情况下，前糖尿病也早在糖尿病发病前数年就已存在。

实际上，数据显示淀粉样β肽（Aβ）的变化先于脑葡萄糖利用的减少，后者可能是代谢综合征的一个重要指标（见下文）。在动物模型证据的支持下，假设构建的新趋势包括推测中枢神经系统（CNS）中Aβ的积累，以及可能的其他神经退行性元素，足以扰乱外周代谢。这使得我们可以考虑这样一种可能性：认知障碍与皮层淀粉样负担之间的相关性之所以如此多变，是因为一个重要的调节（甚至可能是引发）因素是Aβ在皮层下区域的积累：

“因此，AD病理学特征（淀粉样β或Aβ，tau蛋白病变）可能在认知症状出现之前就已存在于下丘脑中，并且这种下丘脑病理学可能在可检测的认知功能障碍出现之前就破坏了如能量平衡和外周代谢等稳态功能（Ishii & Iadecola，2015b）。”

同样令人鼓舞的是，看到关于肥胖和饮食影响的独立于血糖调节的信息被纳入。考虑到高脂饮食对啮齿动物的不利影响，以及生酮饮食及其类似物在人类中似乎带来的益处1，这是一组引人入胜的数据。看来，代谢对脑健康的影响可能受益于对能量底物分子之间转换所带来的影响的更好理解，或许通过影响如谷氨酸和谷氨酰胺等也影响神经递质库的物质。在这里考虑关于中年肥胖与数十年后出现的痴呆相关性的假设2可能是有成效的，因为在这个时期体重减轻可能更为常见。

尽管在这篇白皮书中提出了所有要点，作者们仍然发现自己延续了一个在大量证据面前显得短视的传统假设；这尤其令人失望，因为他们考虑了“如果代谢性疾病以不同于其对其他受糖尿病和其他代谢性疾病影响的终末器官的方式影响大脑”的潜在影响。这几乎肯定是事实。传统的观点认为，血液中葡萄糖升高必然导致脑内葡萄糖升高，忽视了血脑屏障（BBB）的存在；在没有调节转运的情况下，极少量葡萄糖可以进入大脑或CNS的大多数其他区域，而大部分转运由葡萄糖转运蛋白1（GLUT1）处理。 因此，读到论文中的一个主要结论时感到非常惊讶，这个结论似乎主要基于单一出版物，而且该出版物并非专注于大脑，而是视网膜：

“糖尿病与GLUT1葡萄糖转运蛋白的上调相关（Kumagai等，1996年）；葡萄糖为大脑中谷氨酸的原始来源（Bradford & Thomas，1969年），因此慢性高血糖可能导致谷氨酸过量，增加兴奋毒性的风险。”

这一结论在两个方面受到批评：1）多项研究表明，阿尔茨海默病和高血糖都与内皮葡萄糖转运蛋白的减少相关，这很可能反映了——至少在后一种情况下——一种反应性反馈抑制；这可能导致两种疾病中2-脱氧葡萄糖积累的减少。2）兴奋毒性更可能是葡萄糖缺乏的结果；这是一个已确立的关系3,4，而高血糖升高谷氨酸释放的说法则是站不住脚的，且缺乏文献支持。记录高血糖中GLUT1水平降低和/或相反情况下低血糖中GLUT1水平升高的出版物构成了压倒性的证据5-10。作者后来提供了一些证据，表明代谢异常（尤其是由饮食引起的）在大鼠模型中对血脑屏障（BBB）的影响，但人类数据零散且与葡萄糖输送的相关性不明确。

论文中其他一些元素也出现了一些不太严重或不太重要的问题：

“与其他糖尿病并发症不同……，糖尿病的神经认知并发症尚未明确显示与外周血糖测量值相关（除非常差的血糖控制，HbA1c > 10%以及血糖波动的潜在作用外），且与其他外周血糖调节指标的关联仅有有限证据……。”

为什么有必要——或者说甚至有帮助——将HbA1c水平和血糖控制排除在计算之外？哪些外周血糖指标更合理？诚然，10%的HbA1c水平相当高，但在足够有力的研究中，较低水平可能显示出可检测的效果。此外，在血糖浓度剧烈波动的情况下，HbA1c可能不会发生显著变化，然而这种剧烈波动仅凭其波动性就很容易对葡萄糖敏感组织——包括脑内皮——产生难以忍受的压力。

作者因提及（尽管简短）病理性胰岛素抵抗的负面影响与实验性中断胰岛素信号传导的益处之间的明显悖论而应受到赞扬，至少在秀丽隐杆线虫（C. elegans）中如此。应当指出，抑制胰岛素样生长因子（IGF）的信号传导在哺乳动物中也能带来类似益处（例如，延长寿命），而秀丽隐杆线虫只有一种肽来完成胰岛素和IGF的双重角色。 然而，这一难题已经困扰实验性老年学家数十年，部分原因在于胰岛素/IGF信号（IIS）通路和饮食限制所提供的类似益处，后者无疑会减少整体胰岛素的产生。不应期望作者们已经破解了这个难题，但通过对反应性（反馈介导的）胰岛素抵抗和通过实证操纵IIS所实现的主动性胰岛素抵抗之间差异的略微更全面的讨论，可能会产生重要的思考。

同样在这里被简略处理的是炎症与代谢综合征和神经认知障碍之间不可否认的联系。显然，这是一个被低估的关联，值得在试图综合这些领域的科学家中引起更多关注；当在这种背景下提出神经炎症的话题时，资助和论文的评审者继续表现出困惑。鉴于炎症相关事件在2型糖尿病（T2DM）和阿尔茨海默病（AD）病因中的压倒性证据，它几乎肯定会促成它们的共存。事实上，强有力的证据已经支持了动物模型中的这种因果参与11。作者们在论文中散布地使用了“炎症”一词；如果将这些引用中的一两个段落与更具体的信息（例如，IKK2在胰岛素抵抗12和Aβ效应13中的关键作用）结合起来，可能会产生适当的强调。

最后，论文以“一些广泛的研究需求”作为结论，无疑忠实于研讨会讨论的成果，但列出的许多要点显得相当模糊。如果没有进一步的阐述，不清楚其中一些要点将解决哪些知识空白。人们不禁要问，是否可以将其中几个要点合并，并稍加详细阐述。

总体而言，这份白皮书提供了关于认知与代谢紊乱之间联系的数据和概念的非常有用且急需的综合。生活方式和环境中的可修改因素最近已成为预防痴呆的主要考虑因素。Stoeckel等人通过将其扩展到其他类别的认知障碍，增强了这一对话。此外，他们大体上成功地总结了看似不同的领域的当前状态，并突出了将这些领域拉近的机会。

paper_title: A review of experimental models of focal cerebral ischemia focusing on the middle cerebral artery occlusion model
paper_abstract: Cerebral ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability, but current pharmacological therapies are limited in their utility and effectiveness. In vitro and in vivo models of ischemic stroke have been developed which allow us to further elucidate the pathophysiological mechanisms of injury and investigate potential drug targets. In vitro models permit mechanistic investigation of the biochemical and molecular mechanisms of injury but are reductionist and do not mimic the complexity of clinical stroke. In vivo models of ischemic stroke directly replicate the reduction in blood flow and the resulting impact on nervous tissue. The most frequently used in vivo model of ischemic stroke is the intraluminal suture middle cerebral artery occlusion (iMCAO) model, which has been fundamental in revealing various aspects of stroke pathology. However, the iMCAO model produces lesion volumes with large standard deviations even though rigid surgical and data collection protocols are followed. There is a need to refine the MCAO model to reduce variability in the standard outcome measure of lesion volume. The typical approach to produce vessel occlusion is to induce an obstruction at the origin of the middle cerebral artery and reperfusion is reliant on the Circle of Willis (CoW). However, in rodents the CoW is anatomically highly variable which could account for variations in lesion volume. Thus, we developed a refined approach whereby reliance on the CoW for reperfusion was removed. This approach improved reperfusion to the ischemic hemisphere, reduced variability in lesion volume by 30%, and reduced group sizes required to determine an effective treatment response by almost 40%. This refinement involves a methodological adaptation of the original surgical approach which we have shared with the scientific community via publication of a visualised methods article and providing hands-on training to other experimental stroke researchers.
review_content: This is an excellent review article summarising experimental models of ischaemic stroke. It not only provides introduction with critical comments on both in vitro and in vivo preclinical models of ischaemic stroke, but also puts forward some proposals to refine iMCAO, the most commonly used in vivo model of ischameic stroke. iMACO produces lesion volumes with large standard deviation, thus has low statistical power. The authors have previously reported an alterative surgical approach to iMCAO, e.g, avoidance ECA ligation, providing analgesia. In this review article, the authors highlight iMCAO CCA repair method to further reduce lesion volume variability.

paper_abstract_zh: 脑缺血性卒中是导致死亡和残疾的主要原因，但现有的药物疗法在实用性和有效性上均有限。已经开发出体外和体内缺血性卒中模型，使我们能够进一步阐明损伤的病理生理机制并研究潜在的药物靶点。体外模型允许对损伤的生化及分子机制进行机制性研究，但具有还原性，不能模拟临床卒中的复杂性。体内缺血性卒中模型直接复制了血流减少及其对神经组织的影响。最常用的体内缺血性卒中模型是线栓法大脑中动脉闭塞（iMCAO）模型，该模型在揭示卒中病理的各个方面中起到了基础性作用。然而，即使遵循严格的手术和数据收集协议，iMCAO模型产生的损伤体积仍具有较大的标准差。需要改进MCAO模型，以减少标准结局指标——损伤体积的变异性。产生血管闭塞的典型方法是在大脑中动脉起始处诱导阻塞，再灌注依赖于威利斯环（CoW）。然而，在啮齿动物中，CoW的解剖结构高度变异，这可能是损伤体积变异的原因。因此，我们开发了一种改进方法，去除了对CoW再灌注的依赖。这种方法改善了缺血半球的再灌注，将损伤体积的变异性减少了30%，并将确定有效治疗反应所需的组大小减少了近40%。这一改进涉及对原始手术方法的方法学调整，我们已通过发表可视化方法文章并与科学界共享，并为其他实验性卒中研究人员提供了实践培训。

paper_title: Aligning restricted access data with FAIR: a systematic review
paper_abstract: Understanding the complexity of restricted research data is vitally important in the current new era of Open Science. While the FAIR Guiding Principles have been introduced to help researchers to make data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable, it is still unclear how the notions of FAIR and Openness can be applied in the context of restricted data. Many methods have been proposed in support of the implementation of the principles, but there is yet no consensus among the scientific community as to the suitable mechanisms of making restricted data FAIR. We present here a systematic literature review to identify the methods applied by scientists when researching restricted data in a FAIR-compliant manner in the context of the FAIR principles. Through the employment of a descriptive and iterative study design, we aim to answer the following three questions: 1) What methods have been proposed to apply the FAIR principles to restricted data?, 2) How can the relevant aspects of the methods proposed be categorized?, 3) What is the maturity of the methods proposed in applying the FAIR principles to restricted data?. After analysis of the 40 included publications, we noticed that the methods found, reflect the stages of the Data Life Cycle, and can be divided into the following Classes: Data Collection, Metadata Representation, Data Processing, Anonymization, Data Publication, Data Usage and Post Data Usage. We observed that a large number of publications used 'Access Control' and 'Usage & License Terms' methods, while others such as 'Embargo on Data Release' and the use of 'Synthetic Data' were used in fewer instances. In conclusion, we are presenting the first extensive literature review on the methods applied to confidential data in the context of FAIR, providing a comprehensive conceptual framework for future research on restricted access data.

paper_title_zh: "将受限访问数据与FAIR原则对齐：系统综述"
paper_abstract_zh: 理解受限研究数据的复杂性在当前开放科学的新时代至关重要。尽管FAIR指导原则已被引入，以帮助研究人员使数据可查找、可访问、可互操作和可重用，但在受限数据背景下如何应用FAIR和开放性的概念仍不明确。为支持这些原则的实施，已提出多种方法，但科学界尚未就使受限数据符合FAIR原则的适当机制达成共识。本文通过系统文献综述，识别科学家在FAIR原则背景下以符合FAIR的方式研究受限数据所应用的方法。通过采用描述性和迭代的研究设计，我们旨在回答以下三个问题：1）已提出哪些方法将FAIR原则应用于受限数据？2）所提方法的相关方面如何分类？3）所提方法在将FAIR原则应用于受限数据方面的成熟度如何？在对40篇纳入的出版物进行分析后，我们注意到所发现的方法反映了数据生命周期的各个阶段，可分为以下类别：数据收集、元数据表示、数据处理、匿名化、数据发布、数据使用和后数据使用。我们观察到大量出版物使用了“访问控制”和“使用与许可条款”方法，而“数据发布禁令”和使用“合成数据”等方法则较少使用。总之，我们首次对在FAIR背景下应用于保密数据的方法进行了广泛的文献综述，为未来关于受限访问数据的研究提供了一个全面的概念框架。
review_content_zh:
### 审稿人1（匿名）的基本报告

1. **数据管理、访问和分析的敏感性**：
   迄今为止，如何管理、访问和分析敏感数据仍不明确（Cox等，2016）。——6年前的陈述被用来表达当前的情况。作者已为此陈述添加了更多最新的参考文献。我们现在添加了更多的参考文献，即：（Leonelli等，2021）和（Bender等，2022）。

2. **纳入标准的选取依据**：
   纳入标准的选取是否有坚实的依据？

3. **纳入标准的第四条**：
   纳入标准的第四条在大量文章中并不存在？纳入标准是基于作者希望纳入与FAIR原则有明确关联的文章而制定的。我们只纳入了用英语撰写的文章，因为这是作者之间唯一的共同语言，我们还排除了未经过同行评审且非科学研究论文的文章（如其他系统综述）。实际上，第四条标准是绝大多数论文被拒绝的依据，如图1所示。

4. **使用Rayyan工具的原因**：
   查询结果得到的文献集被导出到Rayyan——为什么使用这个特定工具？——这个工具在2016年提出。我们有最新的工具可用吗？——需要对此类工具的选择进行对比分析——似乎拟议的工作严重依赖于这个工具。如果这个工具被移除或替换为其他工具怎么办？——使用了哪个特定版本的工具？选择这个工具没有特定的理由，只是作者的个人偏好。由于Rayyan是一个软件即服务（SaaS）工具，我们发现其网页界面在此特定实例中更为友好。Rayyan只是一个引文管理工具。论文的纳入和排除过程完全不依赖于Rayyan，其他工具（如Zenodo）也可以选择以达到相同的结果。此外，由于Rayyan是SaaS，其网站上没有提供工具版本的详细信息。我们已在文本中明确指出，分析不依赖于该工具，实际上，其他工具也可以使用。

5. **数据生命周期管理的修改**：
   在本研究背景下，数据生命周期已稍作修改，以更好地适应我们的结果，并提高对数据处理阶段以及数据使用后所需步骤的认识。——如果没有其他修改数据生命周期管理的原因，那么修改过程似乎有点偏颇。——其次，做了哪些改动？我们已重新措辞了突出显示的部分，以更好地表达作者的意图，即不是修改周期，而是增加更多步骤。增加的步骤与数据处理阶段和数据使用后的阶段相关。在原始的数据生命周期管理中，这两个步骤并未明确，我们在自己的周期中添加了这两个步骤，以提高对属于这两个阶段的方法的认识。

6. **TRL水平细节缺失**。

7. **第244至251行可以更好地以表格形式呈现**：
   我们已添加一个表格（表1），以更好地描述TRL细节，并为每个类别提供描述。

8. **OWL本体是什么，为什么在此使用**？

9. **生成RDF本体以描述数据方法子类层次结构**：
   ——是否有上述表示的替代方法？——为什么需要这一步骤？我们已扩展文本，包括对OWL语言的描述及选择该语言的原因。我们还添加了为何决定构建本体的解释，这是为了与FAIR原则保持一致。我们认为，在此实例中，构建本体的最佳语义语言是使用OWL语言。

**是否具有广泛的跨学科兴趣且在期刊范围内？**
——是的。

**该领域最近是否有过综述？如果有，是否有充分的理由进行此次综述（不同的观点，面向不同的受众等）？**
——没有，作者的声称这是首次此类研究。

**引言是否介绍了主题并明确了受众/动机？**
——是的，在一定程度上。

**实验设计**
方法描述是否足够详细且信息充分以供复制？
——不，提供的细节难以复制结果，因为它是基于谷歌学术的结果。在不同时间，谷歌学术会返回不同的论文，这将影响结果。我们已报告了运行查询的日期（2021年9月16日），并指明了搜索查询的内容以及我们没有进一步过滤任何结果，因此导出了谷歌学术返回的完整论文集。这意味着在未来，如果想要复制结果，可以在谷歌学术上再次运行搜索查询，并将“时间范围”自定义到2022年9月16日结束。使用与我们研究相同的结束日期运行搜索查询将产生相同的文献集。

**综述方法是否与全面、无偏的主题覆盖一致？如果不一致，缺少什么？是否引用了来源？是否适当地引用或改写？**
——是的。

**综述是否逻辑清晰地组织成连贯的段落/子节？**
——是的。

**发现的有效性**
是否有充分发展和支持的论点，达到了引言中设定的目标？
——在此背景下，引言中并未设定目标。作者认为，论文的目标在引言的“问题陈述和贡献”部分中已设定。

**结论是否识别了未解决的问题/差距/未来方向？**
——文章中有一个关于此的“局限性”标题。

**总体而言，本文分为两部分：**
- 领域/问题介绍
- 拟议解决方案

第一部分呈现得很好，很好地涵盖了主题领域，例如引言、问题陈述、背景等，但当涉及到问题解决方案时，观察到一些技术上的薄弱之处，例如方法、纳入标准等。结果部分仅包含对所选数据集的详细解释。同样，论文的结果严重依赖于所选数据集。例如，不同的输入文章将产生不同的结果。

paper_title: The use of nutritional supplements to induce ketosis and reduce symptoms associated with keto-induction. A narrative review
paper_abstract: Background. Adaptation to a ketogenic diet (keto-induction) can cause unpleasant symptoms, and this can reduce tolerability of the diet. Several methods have been suggested as useful for encouraging entry into nutritional ketosis (NK) and reducing symptoms of keto-induction. This paper reviews the scientific literature on the effects of these methods on time-to-NK and on symptoms during the keto-induction phase.
review_content: Reviewer 1 1. References: 1.1. No reference has been listed to substantiate any of the sentences written in the ‘Short chain fatty acids’ section (Lines 92-98) References have been added to the lines above to substantiate the information contained in the SCFA section. 1.2. Lines 111-114 also need reference(s) References have been added in the text. 1.3. St. Pierre et al. mentioned in Line 122 is not listed in the References section Reference added. 2. The exogenous ketones are simply described as either salts or esters of BOHB. Since describing the use of ketone supplements to facilitate nutritional ketosis is a key objective of this review, it would be helpful to have a more detailed description of these supplements (types of salts, types of esters, biodegradation and bioavailability, adverse effects, proposed applications etc.) Additional information has been added, specifically in lines 231-238. 3. Additional and relevant data comparing ketone salts and MCT (described in Kesl et al., Nutrition & Metabolism, 2016; 13:9) is available and can be included to further improve this narrative review on supplements used to induce ketosis Added to discussion lines 293-303. 4. It is relevant to address that there’s lack of consensus on whether achieving greater ketosis necessarily means better physiological outcomes. Some of the questions in the field that are of importance and could be expanded upon in the text: We agree that the achievement of higher levels of ketones may not lead to better physiological outcomes but our clinical experience suggests that higher BOHB levels do mitigate symptoms of keto-induction and may improve mood. Newport et al. have suggested a correlation between cognition and mood and BOHB levels. Additional information has been added to the discussion on lines 290-293 and 312-316. 4.1. Would achieving higher levels of ketosis (by supplementing with exogenous esters, salts or MCTs) shorten the keto-induction period and/or enhance the physiological benefits observed with nutritional ketosis? We have changed the discussion/conclusions to clarify our position on this (similarly to changes above.) It’s unclear at this time whether an elevation in ketones over and above NK would improve outcomes. It has been observed that mood is improved within the first two weeks of a diet irrespective of macronutrient composition.1 One study (by Newport et al.) has demonstrated a correlation between ketone levels and memory performance.2 4.2. Is there any available scientific evidence that ketone supplements do actually mitigate the ‘keto-flu’ symptoms associated with the keto-induction period? We are not aware of any published literature on exogenous ketone supplements being used to mitigate the symptoms of keto-induction. However, our clinical experience suggests this use and it is becoming common for these supplements to be used for this purpose in the mainstream. Thus, we have considered this popular hypothesis as part of our overall context for this review. 4.3. Does chronic supplementation with exogenous ketones impair endogenous ketogenesis (as observed in Balasse et al., 1975)? This study had been noted in the text in the section on exogenous ketone supplementation (line 255). 5. When discussing MCTs, the authors describe their ketogenic effects, suggesting that acute ingestion of MCTs induces nutritional ketosis. However, it is important to differentiate between hepatic production of ketone bodies due to acute ingestion of MCTs and the biochemical shift in fuel utilization that occurs during prolonged nutritional ketosis (the physiological process described as keto-induction or keto-adaptation). I suggest addressing this difference and possibly emphasizing the acute/transient effects elicited by single or acute consumption of exogenous ketones, resulting in peripheral ketosis but not necessarily keto-adaptation. On that note (and according to lines 159-161), would the MCT ketogenic diet likely shorten the keto-induction period when compared to the classic KD? This is an important point and we believe that this has been addressed with respect to the studies included that indicate MCTs provide for ketonaemia acutely but also appear to increase ketogenesis in the medium to long term. We have also mentioned specifically that exogenous ketones provide for ketonaemia but not keto-adaptation necessarily and that they may, in fact, reduce ketogenesis. 6. The language is appropriate but a few typos were found: 6.1. Abstract: Line 20: dose-dependant instead of dose-dependent Corrected 6.2. Introduction: 6.2.1. Line 46: references 22 and 23 are listed not separated by a comma Corrected 6.2.2. Line 50: Fibre instead of fiber This paper is written in New Zealand English (with English spelling conventions), as compared to US English. The research facility and team are based in New Zealand and fibre is the accepted and correct spelling form for this word in the Commonwealth nations. The journal accepts both US and UK spelling. Experimental design A summary table with relevant articles on ketogenic diets (classic, modified MCT diet, MCT ketogenic diet and supplements) listing preclinical and clinical studies and main observations (levels of ketosis, time to achieve ketosis, physiological outcomes, adverse effects etc.) would provide greater support and structure for this narrative review. Because of the lack of consistency in definitions for ketosis, we believe that a table of this type would not clarify the article any more than the additions already made. Validity of the findings 7. The topic of ketogenic diets and ketone supplements has risen in popularity due to well-known benefits in weight management, diabetes, athletic performance and metabolic health. However, it is important to emphasize that, although this approach is promising as potential therapeutic intervention for many other conditions, clinical data is still lacking. For instance, the positive effects in anxiety described by Kashiwaya et al., (2013) were observed in transgenic models of amyloid and tau deposition. An additional report of ketone supplementation reducing anxiety-related behavior in rodents was published last year (Ari et al., Front Mol Neurosci, 2016; 9:137) using two different rat strains. Clinical studies on ketogenic diets and supplementation in populations of mental disorders patients are still lacking. Studies based on animal models of mental disorders have limited generalizability when translated into the same conditions in humans. Caution should be exercised and clinical studies remain necessary. This has been noted in the discussion. The primary topic of interest (induction of ketosis) in the paper has been limited, where possible, to studies in humans with animal studies mentioned only where there is a dearth of human evidence and/or to provide context and potential for future human application. 8. The same caution can be extrapolated to other areas such as cancer, autism spectrum disorders, Alzheimer’s disease etc., where mostly case reports are currently published and the vast majority of data is originated from animal studies and anecdotal reports. This does not invalidate these approaches, as sound medical hypothesis have been published (as in the cases of metabolic dysfunction associated with cancer and Alzheimer’s disease) but it does highlight the need for well-designed randomized, clinical trials to support the available hypothesis and preclinical data. We agree that much of the information is highly preliminary and there needs to more high-quality clinical trial data presented to determine the validity of the various hypotheses. We believe we have suggested as much through the paper and especially in our conclusions i.e. “more research is required to elucidate the role that supplementation may play in encouraging ketogenesis, improving time to NK, reducing symptoms associated with keto-induction, and the effect this might have on improving adherence to, and outcomes from a VLCKD.” We thank reviewer 1 for the timely and constructive comments. They have helped us to create a more robust paper.
paper_title_zh: 使用营养补充剂诱导酮症并减轻与酮症诱导相关症状的叙述性综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。适应生酮饮食（生酮诱导）可能会引起不愉快的症状，这会降低饮食的耐受性。已有几种方法被建议为有助于促进进入营养性酮症（NK）并减轻生酮诱导期的症状。本文综述了关于这些方法对进入NK时间及生酮诱导期症状影响的科学文献。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1

1. 参考文献：
1.1. 在“短链脂肪酸”部分（第92-98行）中，没有任何参考文献来支持所写的句子。
已在上文中添加参考文献，以支持SCFA部分所包含的信息。
1.2. 第111-114行也需要参考文献。
已在文本中添加了参考文献。
1.3. 第122行提到的St. Pierre等人未列在参考文献部分。
已添加参考文献。

2. 外源性酮体仅被描述为BOHB的盐或酯。由于描述使用酮补充剂以促进营养性酮症是本综述的一个关键目标，因此更详细地描述这些补充剂（盐的类型、酯的类型、生物降解性和生物利用度、不良反应、拟议应用等）将是有帮助的。
已添加额外信息，特别是在第231-238行。

3. Kesl等人（Nutrition & Metabolism, 2016; 13:9）描述的酮盐和MCT的比较数据是可用的，可以包括进来，以进一步改进关于用于诱导酮症的补充剂的叙述性综述。
已添加到讨论部分，第293-303行。

4. 讨论是否存在共识，即实现更高水平的酮症是否必然意味着更好的生理结果，这是相关的。该领域的一些重要问题可以在文本中进一步展开：
我们同意，更高水平的酮症可能不会导致更好的生理结果，但我们的临床经验表明，更高的BOHB水平确实可以缓解酮症诱导的症状，并可能改善情绪。Newport等人已提出认知、情绪与BOHB水平之间的相关性。已在讨论部分添加额外信息，第290-293行和第312-316行。

4.1. 通过补充外源性酯、盐或MCTs来实现更高水平的酮症，是否会缩短酮症诱导期和/或增强营养性酮症观察到的生理益处？
我们已更改讨论/结论部分，以澄清我们的立场（与上述更改类似）。目前尚不清楚酮体水平在NK之上是否会改善结果。已观察到，无论宏量营养素组成如何，在饮食的前两周内情绪有所改善。1 一项研究（由Newport等人进行）已证明酮体水平与记忆表现之间的相关性。2

4.2. 是否有科学证据表明酮补充剂确实可以缓解与酮症诱导期相关的“酮流感”症状？
我们不知道有任何关于外源性酮补充剂用于缓解酮症诱导症状的已发表文献。然而，我们的临床经验表明这种用途，并且这些补充剂用于此目的在主流中变得越来越普遍。因此，我们将这一流行假设作为本综述整体背景的一部分进行了考虑。

4.3. 长期补充外源性酮体是否会损害内源性酮生成（如Balasse等人1975年所观察到的）？
该研究已在关于外源性酮补充剂的文本部分中提到（第255行）。

5. 在讨论MCTs时，作者描述了它们的生酮效应，表明急性摄入MCTs会诱导营养性酮症。然而，重要的是要区分由于急性摄入MCTs引起的肝酮体生成与在长期营养性酮症期间发生的燃料利用的生化转变（生理过程被描述为酮症诱导或酮症适应）。我建议讨论这种差异，并可能强调单次或急性摄入外源性酮体所引发的急性/短暂效应，导致外周酮症但不一定酮症适应。顺便提一下（根据第159-161行），与经典KD相比，MCT生酮饮食是否可能缩短酮症诱导期？这是一个重要观点，我们相信这已在所包含的研究中得到解决，这些研究表明MCTs在急性情况下提供酮血症，但似乎也在中到长期内增加酮生成。我们还特别提到，外源性酮体提供酮血症但不一定酮症适应，并且它们实际上可能减少酮生成。

6. 语言是适当的，但发现了一些错别字：
6.1. 摘要：第20行：dose-dependant应为dose-dependent
已更正
6.2. 引言：
6.2.1. 第46行：参考文献22和23列出时未用逗号分隔
已更正
6.2.2. 第50行：Fibre应为fiber
本文使用新西兰英语（英语拼写惯例），与美国英语相比。研究设施和团队位于新西兰，fibre是在英联邦国家接受和正确的拼写形式。该期刊接受美国和英国拼写。

实验设计
一个总结表，列出有关生酮饮食（经典、改良MCT饮食、MCT生酮饮食和补充剂）的相关文章，列出临床前和临床研究及主要观察结果（酮症水平、达到酮症的时间、生理结果、不良反应等），将为这篇叙述性综述提供更大的支持和结构。由于酮症的定义缺乏一致性，我们认为这种类型的表格不会比已经添加的内容更清楚地阐明文章。

发现的有效性
7. 生酮饮食和酮补充剂的话题因其对体重管理、糖尿病、运动表现和代谢健康的众所周知的好处而日益流行。然而，重要的是要强调，尽管这种方法作为许多其他条件的潜在治疗干预措施很有前景，但临床数据仍然缺乏。例如，Kashiwaya等人（2013年）描述的焦虑阳性效应是在淀粉样蛋白和tau沉积的转基因模型中观察到的。去年发表的一份关于酮补充剂减少大鼠焦虑相关行为的额外报告（Ari等人，Front Mol Neurosci, 2016; 9:137），使用了两种不同的大鼠品系。关于生酮饮食和补充剂在精神疾病患者群体中的临床研究仍然缺乏。基于精神疾病动物模型的研究在转化为人类相同条件时具有有限的普适性。应谨慎行事，临床研究仍然是必要的。这已在讨论中提到。本文的主要兴趣主题（酮症诱导）已尽可能限于人类研究，仅在人类证据缺乏和/或提供背景和未来人类应用潜力时提及动物研究。

8. 同样的谨慎可以扩展到其他领域，如癌症、自闭症谱系障碍、阿尔茨海默病等，目前主要发表的是病例报告，绝大多数数据来自动物研究和轶事报告。这并不使这些方法无效，因为已发表合理的医学假设（如与癌症和阿尔茨海默病相关的代谢功能障碍的情况），但它确实突显了需要设计良好的随机临床试验来支持现有的假设和临床前数据。我们同意，许多信息非常初步，需要更多高质量的临床试验数据来确定各种假设的有效性。我们相信我们已在文中尤其是结论中提出了这一点，即“需要更多研究来阐明补充剂在促进酮生成、改善达到NK的时间、减少与酮症诱导相关的症状以及这可能对提高极低碳水化合物饮食（VLCKD）的依从性和结果产生的影响。” 我们感谢审稿人1及时且有建设性的评论。它们帮助我们创建了一篇更强大的论文。

A summary table with relevant articles on ketogenic diets (classic, modified MCT diet, MCT ketogenic diet and supplements) listing preclinical and clinical studies and main observations (levels of ketosis, time to achieve ketosis, physiological outcomes, adverse effects etc.) would provide greater support and structure for this narrative review.

paper_title: How to incorporate patient and public perspectives into the design and conduct of research
paper_abstract:
International government guidance recommends patient and public involvement (PPI) to improve the relevance and quality of research.  PPI is defined as research being carried out ‘with’ or ‘by’ patients and members of the public rather than ‘to’, ‘about’ or ‘for’ them ( http://www.invo.org.uk/ ). Patient involvement is different from collecting data from patients as participants.  Ethical considerations also differ.  PPI is about patients actively contributing through discussion to decisions about research design, acceptability, relevance, conduct and governance from study conception to dissemination.  Occasionally patients lead or do research.  The research methods of PPI range from informal discussions to partnership research approaches such as action research, co-production and co-learning. 
This article discusses how researchers can involve patients when they are applying for research funding and considers some opportunities and pitfalls.  It reviews research funder requirements, draws on the literature and our collective experiences as clinicians, patients, academics and members of UK funding panels.
review_content:
Thank you for the opportunity to review this paper. The aim of this paper is to discuss how researchers can involve patients when applying for research funding, and to outline opportunities and pitfalls. It uses a combination of knowledge about this process from literature and the authors' wide ranging experience.

This article provides a general background to patient and public involvement in research. The article very usefully includes in Box 1 and Table 1 current resources and guidelines that are available. The information is very comprehensive and relevant to the aims of the article - which is how to to incorporate PPI into the design and conduct of research. This overview is unique and in my view will be widely used. However can it be moved to later in the article? The tables do break up the flow of the paper and break up what I think is an important section about the difference between PPI and patient participation in research.

The section on the difference between patient involvement and patient participation in research is much needed as PPI is often conflated with qualitative research. This is still a common problem. I wondered if Figure 1 could come earlier, or if Box 2 can show the differences more explicitly instead of providing a list of definitions, can the differences be displayed side by side, using maybe column headings of differences and similarities. This will enable the reader to access the important distinctions more easily.

On page 10 in the section about action research, co-design and co-learning there is a sentence about how a partnership approach may interact with an intervention. I think this is the first time intervention studies are mentioned as previous text has stated that patient participation in research may be through interviews, focus groups and surveys. I wondered if this could be expanded to include that these can be undertaken in the context of trials, as then the text would align better with the material in the supplementary documents.

There are a lot of examples in the supplementary files and this can be quite difficult to navigate.

I have an observation on how the steps are characterised. At first I thought the text in italics are the recommended steps for researchers? For example on page 11 the first step for researchers outlined is to search the internet for organisations and guidelines to see if research priorities have been established in their area of interest. There is however some advice given earlier (written in italics) that recommends understanding what PPI will add and which uncertainties about patient perspectives may benefit from more exploration.

Then I realised that the steps are characterised in the blue subheadings. These are a mix of 1. advice (e.g. understand what PPI is (this is a conceptual issue)), 2. questions (e.g. how does PPI differ from patient participation?) and then 3. labels for different issues (e.g. patients doing research, which is a practical issue). Could there be more consistency across the paper? I wondered if it would work if they were all translated into specific statements / recommendations particularly as the aim is to provide guidance on how to incorporate PPI.

Related to the above - I wondered whether the section headings of "how does PPI differ from research participation" and action research, co-design, co-learning and co-production" should be at the same level as the others. They are very important - but I think are fundamentally about understanding what PPI is.

The text in italics is also a mix I think of statements of principles - e.g. seek to balance positive and negative views, rather than a statement of how to do that (the title of the paper is how to incorporate PPI....)

The section on how many patients to involve is again really helpful as this is the question that people often ask. This is usually asked in the context of "representativeness" of the patients' views. Can this section be expanded - with some examples of what teams can say when the "representativeness" of their patient advisors is questioned. It links to a later section on bias and conflict of interest.

The authors recommend that researchers select patients with balanced views. It is difficult to know what view people hold at the outset. Can this recommendation again be expanded upon - with ideas about how you may do this, or how you may get fresh perspectives over time.

Towards the end there is a heading about involving patients in writing a grant application. This made me realise that the advice spans both the process of PPI at pre-award and then outlining what to do post award. I wondered therefore whether this section should come earlier. PPI advisors will have an input into the design of the PPI throughout and the research design throughout, and therefore impact on decision making about earlier topics in the article.

I think this is a really valuable paper in providing such a comprehensive overview of resources and guidelines for PPI and in highlighting the key challenges of good PPI practice. My suggestions are really about structuring the content to make it more accessible to the reader by highlighting maybe two aspects. First the need to understand what PPI is and is not. Second the practical issues - how to do it.
paper_title_zh: 如何将患者和公众视角融入研究的设计与实施
paper_abstract_zh:
国际政府指南建议通过患者和公众参与（PPI）来提高研究的关联性和质量。PPI被定义为研究是“与”或“由”患者和公众成员“一起”或“进行”，而不是“对”、“关于”或“为他们”进行研究（http://www.invo.org.uk/）。患者参与不同于作为参与者从患者那里收集数据。伦理考量也有所不同。PPI涉及患者通过讨论积极贡献，从研究的构思到传播，对研究设计、可接受性、关联性、实施和治理做出决策。偶尔，患者会领导或进行研究。PPI的研究方法从非正式讨论到合作研究方法，如行动研究、共同生产和共同学习。

本文讨论了研究者在申请研究资金时如何涉及患者，并考虑了一些机会和陷阱。它回顾了研究资助者的要求，借鉴了文献以及我们作为临床医生、患者、学者和英国资助小组成员的集体经验。
review_content_zh:
感谢您提供机会审阅这篇论文。本文旨在讨论研究人员在申请研究经费时如何涉及患者，并概述其中的机会和陷阱。文章结合了文献中关于这一过程的知识以及作者广泛的经验。

本文为患者和公众参与研究提供了背景信息。文章非常有用地在框1和表1中包含了当前可用的资源和指南。这些信息非常全面，且与文章的目标——如何将患者和公众参与（PPI）融入研究的设计和实施——密切相关。这一概述独具特色，在我看来将会被广泛使用。然而，是否可以将这部分内容移至文章后部？表格确实打断了文章的流畅性，并且打断了我认为关于PPI与患者参与研究之间区别的重要部分。

关于患者参与和患者参与研究之间区别的部分非常必要，因为PPI常常与定性研究混淆。这仍然是一个常见问题。我想知道图1是否可以提前，或者框2是否能更明确地展示区别，而不是提供一系列定义，是否可以将区别并排列出，例如使用“区别”和“相似之处”的列标题。这将使读者更容易理解重要的区分。

在第10页关于行动研究、共同设计和共同学习的部分中，有一句话提到伙伴关系方法如何与干预措施相互作用。我认为这是首次提到干预研究，因为之前的文本指出患者参与研究可能通过访谈、焦点小组和调查。我想知道是否可以扩展这部分内容，包括这些可以在试验背景下进行，这样文本将与补充材料中的内容更好地对齐。

补充文件中有许多例子，这可能会让人难以导航。

我对步骤的描述有一个观察。起初我以为斜体字部分是给研究人员的推荐步骤？例如在第11页，研究人员的第一步是搜索互联网上的组织和指南，以查看其感兴趣领域的研究优先级是否已确定。然而，之前（用斜体字写的）有一些建议，建议理解PPI将带来什么，以及哪些关于患者视角的不确定性可能需要进一步探索。

然后我意识到步骤是在蓝色小标题中描述的。这些包括1.建议（例如理解PPI是什么（这是一个概念性问题）），2.问题（例如PPI与患者参与有何不同？）以及3.不同问题的标签（例如患者进行研究，这是一个实践性问题）。文章中是否可以更一致？我想知道如果将它们都转化为具体的陈述/建议是否可行，尤其是目标是提供如何融入PPI的指导。

与上述相关的是，我想知道“PPI与研究参与有何不同”以及“行动研究、共同设计、共同学习和共同生产”这些部分标题是否应与其他标题处于同一级别。它们非常重要，但我认为它们本质上是为了理解PPI是什么。

斜体字部分我认为也是原则性陈述的混合，例如寻求平衡正面和负面观点，而不是如何做到这一点的陈述（文章标题是如何融入PPI……）

关于涉及多少患者的那部分内容再次非常有帮助，因为这是人们经常问的问题。这通常是在患者观点“代表性”的背景下提出的。是否可以扩展这部分内容，提供一些当患者顾问的“代表性”受到质疑时，团队可以如何回应的例子。这与后面的偏见和利益冲突部分相关。

作者建议研究人员选择持有平衡观点的患者。在一开始很难知道人们持有何种观点。是否可以再次扩展这一建议，提供一些关于如何做到这一点或在一段时间内获得新视角的想法。

在文章末尾有一个关于涉及患者撰写资助申请的标题。这让我意识到建议涵盖了PPI在预奖励阶段的过程以及概述了奖励后要做的事情。因此，我想知道这部分内容是否应该提前。PPI顾问将在整个过程中对PPI的设计和研究设计提供输入，并因此影响文章中早期话题的决策。

我认为这是一篇非常有价值的论文，提供了关于PPI资源和指南的全面概述，并突出了良好PPI实践的关键挑战。我的建议主要是关于如何组织内容，使其对读者更易理解，可能通过突出两个方面：第一，理解PPI是什么和不是什么；第二，实践问题——如何去做。

paper_title: Infective endocarditis today
paper_abstract:
Endocarditis is an infectious disease caused by numerous microorganisms, many of which habitually colonize the oral cavity and skin. Various bacteria and bacterial factors influence the duration of bacteremia and the possible colonization of cardiac valves. If not recognized and treated early, the disease may have serious consequences until death: despite the possibility of setting up targeted antibiotic therapy, it may occur in 30% of cases. This event is related to sepsis that develops in these patients and can result in cellular functional alterations in many districts, resulting in multi-organ failure (MOF) status. 
This paper is aimed to present an overview of this condition, based on the author’s own clinical experience and literature review.
review_content:
1. Is the topic of the review discussed comprehensively in the context of the current literature? No

Most writers would accept that the current literature reflects work published over the past 10 years. The majority of citations in this article are significantly older than this and largely relate to the field of dentistry rather than clinical medicine. I do not feel that the article reflects current practice, nor does it explore current controversies in the field.

There is no mention of the Duke Criteria or the modified update for the diagnosis of infective endocarditis. Diagnosis is usually made without histological confirmation at the time of surgery, which is reflected in the Duke Major criteria. Most would agree that the pathological criteria of endocarditis are largely historical.

In 2015 new imaging modalities were introduced into the ESC guideline to aid diagnosis including PET/SPECT, CT and imaging for distal embolic events. The article makes no reference to any imaging outside of TOE. Both the AHA and ESC would also recommend TTE rather than TOE as the first-line test for suspected disease.

In terms of antibiotic prophylaxis, the author does highlight that this is a controversial area. However, it might be helpful to reference current UK guidelines that do not recommend any prophylaxis, which has been the case since 2008. Potentially as a result of this, UK endocarditis rates are now rising.

The article does not reference or highlight the shift in microbiology from Streptococcus to staphylococcus or why this might be.

There is no mention of newer percutaneous valves and the signal regarding potential higher endocarditis rates.

2. Are all factual statements correct and adequately supported by citations? No

There are frequent factual statements made throughout the article that are not referenced. These need to be addressed prior to publication. At present the article reads like an opinion piece.

For example.

“endocarditis site in 50% of cases”
“12-15% of cases”
“injecting drugs (up to 30% in some cases)”
“oral microorganisms (especially Streptococcus app.) are seldom found in bacterial endocarditis”
‘Statistically 5-20% of endocarditis has negative emoculture”

3. Is the review written in accessible language? Partly

There are a number of esoteric terms used in the article that are not commonly used and make it challenging to read:

Emoculture
Anatomopathological
Odontostomatologic
Asthenia
Anamnesis
Hyperpyretis

The structure of some sentences is confusing:

“All age groups may be potentially affected but with different clinical picture between young immunosupressed subjects and older than 65 years have an incidence of about 9 times that of subjects with lower age”

“In the elderly population, in the lungs, the presence of Streptococcus bovis, a microorganism associated with polyps and colon carcinoma, or enterococci (Group D streptococci as Enterococcus faecalis) is commonly found in the gastrointestinal tract and can cause subacute infections after gastrointestinal clinical procedures”

“Despite the possibility of performing microbiological and instrumental elective investigations and the wide availability of drugs capable of resolving pathological conditions, IE is still associated with a high mortality rate”

“It’s application in everyday practice is based on other than efficacy tests: simply empirical or traditional tests”

“which is attempted to prevent antibiotic-prophylaxis during dental procedures”

4. Are the conclusions drawn appropriate in the context of the current research literature? Partly

No mention of more current risk factors for endocarditis: dialysis, immunosuppression, implantable cardiac devices or indwelling venous catheters. Agreed that mortality remains high. However, might be nice to discuss why this could be?

The reference to MOF in the second paragraph of the conclusion is rather confusing. It has not been mentioned in the article, the acronym is not described and I am unsure that mortality in endocarditis is “usually” due to it.

Agreed that antibiotic prophylaxis remains controversial.

The reference to diabetic patients at the end of the article comes out of the blue. Diabetes is a risk factor for endocarditis, but it is not highlighted anywhere else in the article. This needs to be introduced earlier.

The throw-away statement regarding cigarette smoke and electronic cigarettes is also confusing. It bears no relation to the article and seems an odd thing to conclude what is quite a traditional article on endocarditis.

Summary

All factual statements need to be referenced, ideally with articles <10 years old to ensure they reflect the current literature.

Clean up some sentences and try to move away from esoteric terms to make the article easier to read.

The second and last paragraphs of the conclusion need to be tightened up. At present they do not bear any relation to the overall article.
paper_title_zh: 今日感染性心内膜炎
paper_abstract_zh:
心内膜炎是由多种微生物引起的一种感染性疾病，其中许多微生物习惯性地定植于口腔和皮肤。各种细菌及细菌因素影响着菌血症的持续时间以及心脏瓣膜可能发生的定植。如果未能早期识别和治疗，该疾病可能导致严重后果甚至死亡：尽管有可能进行针对性的抗生素治疗，但在30%的病例中仍可能发生。这一事件与这些患者中发生的败血症有关，并可导致多个区域的细胞功能改变，最终导致多器官衰竭（MOF）状态。
本文旨在基于作者自身的临床经验和文献综述，对该病症进行概述。
review_content_zh:
### 1. 综述的主题是否在当前文献背景下进行了全面讨论？ 否

大多数作者会认同，当前文献反映了过去10年内发表的工作。本文中的大多数引用文献远早于这个时间段，且主要与牙科领域相关，而非临床医学。我认为这篇文章既不反映当前实践，也未探讨该领域的当前争议。

文中未提及杜克标准（Duke Criteria）或其修订版，用于感染性心内膜炎的诊断。诊断通常在手术时无需组织学确认，这一点在杜克主要标准中有所体现。大多数人会同意，心内膜炎的病理标准基本上是历史性的。

2015年，ESC指南引入了新的影像学检查手段以辅助诊断，包括PET/SPECT、CT以及远端栓塞事件的影像学检查。本文未提及TOE（经食管超声心动图）以外的任何影像学检查。AHA和ESC也都推荐TTE（经胸超声心动图）而非TOE作为疑似疾病的首次检查手段。

在抗生素预防方面，作者确实指出这是一个有争议的领域。然而，引用当前英国指南可能会有所帮助，这些指南自2008年以来不推荐任何预防性用药。可能因此，英国心内膜炎的发病率现在正在上升。

本文未提及或强调微生物学从链球菌到葡萄球菌的转变，也未解释其原因。

文中未提及新型经皮瓣膜及其潜在更高心内膜炎发病率的信号。

### 2. 所有事实性陈述是否正确且得到了充分的文献支持？ 否

文章中频繁出现未引用的事实性陈述。这些需要在发表前予以解决。目前，文章读起来像一篇观点性文章。

例如：

“50%的病例中，心内膜炎的部位”
“12-15%的病例”
“注射毒品（在某些情况下高达30%）”
“口腔微生物（尤其是链球菌属）在细菌性心内膜炎中很少见”
“统计上有5-20%的心内膜炎病例培养结果为阴性”

### 3. 综述是否使用了易于理解的语言？ 部分

文章中使用了一些不常用的术语，使其难以阅读：

- Emoculture（血培养）
- Anatomopathological（解剖病理学）
- Odontostomatologic（口腔牙科）
- Asthenia（虚弱）
- Anamnesis（病史）
- Hyperpyretis（高热）

一些句子的结构令人困惑：

“所有年龄组都可能受到影响，但年轻免疫抑制个体和65岁以上老年人的临床表现不同，其发病率约为低年龄组的9倍”

“在老年人群中，肺部常见链球菌（与息肉和结肠癌相关）或肠球菌（如粪肠球菌，D组链球菌），这些微生物常见于胃肠道，并在胃肠道临床操作后引起亚急性感染”

“尽管可以进行微生物学和仪器选择性检查，且药物广泛可用以解决病理状况，但感染性心内膜炎仍与高死亡率相关”

“其在日常实践中的应用基于除疗效测试之外的其他因素：仅仅是经验性或传统测试”

“试图在牙科操作期间预防抗生素预防”

### 4. 结论在当前研究文献背景下是否适当？ 部分

未提及心内膜炎的更当前风险因素：透析、免疫抑制、植入性心脏设备或留置静脉导管。同意死亡率仍然很高。然而，讨论其原因可能会更好？

结论第二段中提到的MOF（多器官衰竭）相当令人困惑。文章中未提及此缩写，也未描述，我不确定心内膜炎的死亡率“通常”是由其引起的。

同意抗生素预防仍然是有争议的。

文章末尾提到的糖尿病患者显得突兀。糖尿病是心内膜炎的风险因素，但文章其他部分未提及。这需要在前面引入。

关于香烟烟雾和电子香烟的随意陈述也很令人困惑。这与文章无关，作为一篇关于心内膜炎的传统文章的结论显得很奇怪。

### 总结

所有事实性陈述都需要引用，理想情况下应引用近10年内的文章，以确保其反映当前文献。

清理一些句子，尽量不用生僻术语，使文章更易读。

结论的第二段和最后一段需要收紧。目前它们与整篇文章无关。

paper_title: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation as a standard of care in the future: a literature review
paper_abstract:
Background: The use of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is limited generally to situations where traditional CPR failed to restore a patient's heart rhythm. Although ECPR is not regarded as the standard of care for cardiac arrest patients, it might be a more effective treatment for some forms of cardiac arrest. This literature review explores the efficacy of ECPR as a potential standard of care for cardiac arrest in the future. 
 Methods: English language publications fulfilling eligibility criteria from 2010 to 2023 were found through a literature search using four electronic databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, Cochrane, and IEEE Explore). Articles were included in this literature review for fulfilling following criteria: empirical primary studies evaluating ECPR in human subjects with either IHCA or OHCA; articles published in English between 2010 and 2023; articles exploring ECPR in cardiac arrest across all ages of patients. 
 Results : 12 studies out of 1,092 search results met the inclusion criteria for data extraction and synthesis. Data extracted included the efficacy of ECPR in both IHCA and OHCA patients based on the PICO framework. The quality of study done by NOS (Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Scale for Cohort Studies) resulted in three studies with moderate quality while nine were of high quality. 
 Conclusions:   ECPR was associated with neurologically intact survival with favorable neurological outcomes compared to a standard CRP for cardiac arrest patients. This study also demonstrates that, at the moment, ECPR is the most successful in centers with a well-trained multidisciplinary ECMO team of experts. On the other hand, cardiac arrest patients in semi-rural areas and underdeveloped locations are likely to benefit less from ECPR interventions due to the lack of necessary ECPR expertise and infrastructure. Those individuals eligible for ECPR benefit from better neurological outcomes and associated higher survival rates.
review_content:
In this manuscript, the authors presented a literature review on the use of ECPR for cardiac arrest, either IHCA or OHCA. From an extended search collecting 1092 papers between 2010 and 2023, they retained 12 studies which met their inclusion criteria. They concluded that ECPR has better survival rates and neurological outcomes than standard CPR for CA. One very pertinent point is the consideration of rural OHCA and the minimum recruitment in ECPR centers to get sufficient training and expertise.

General Comments:
This literature review is interesting and seems to have been accurately performed. The results and conclusions of the authors are relevant. Moreover, the text of the manuscript the figure and the tables are clear and well presented.
The Reviewer has no major concern or criticism on this study.
Minor Comments
Introduction, 3rd line : please correct motality to mortality
paper_title_zh: 体外心肺复苏作为未来护理标准的探讨：文献综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：体外心肺复苏（ECPR）的使用通常限于传统心肺复苏未能恢复患者心律的情况。尽管ECPR不被视为心脏骤停患者的标准治疗方法，但它可能对某些类型的心脏骤停更有效。本文献综述探讨了ECPR作为未来心脏骤停潜在标准治疗的有效性。

方法：通过使用四个电子数据库（PubMed、Google Scholar、Cochrane和IEEE Explore）进行文献搜索，找到了2010年至2023年间符合资格标准的英文出版物。符合以下标准的文章被纳入本文献综述：实证性初级研究，评估在院内心脏骤停（IHCA）或院外心脏骤停（OHCA）患者中使用的ECPR；2010年至2023年间发表的英文文章；探讨各年龄段患者心脏骤停中ECPR的文章。

结果：在1,092个搜索结果中，有12项研究符合数据提取和综合的纳入标准。提取的数据包括基于PICO框架的ECPR在IHCA和OHCA患者中的有效性。通过NOS（纽卡斯尔-渥太华队列研究质量评估量表）评估的研究质量结果显示，有三项研究质量中等，而九项研究质量较高。

结论：ECPR与神经功能完好的生存率相关，且与标准心肺复苏相比，心脏骤停患者的神经学预后更佳。本研究还表明，目前ECPR在拥有训练有素的多学科ECMO专家团队的中心最为成功。另一方面，由于缺乏必要的ECPR专业知识和基础设施，半农村地区和欠发达地区的心脏骤停患者从ECPR干预中获益较少。符合ECPR条件的个体受益于更好的神经学预后和相应的更高生存率。
review_content_zh:
在这篇手稿中，作者对使用ECPR（体外心肺复苏）治疗心脏骤停（无论是院内心脏骤停[IHCA]还是院外心脏骤停[OHCA]）进行了文献综述。通过广泛搜索，收集了2010年至2023年间的1092篇论文，他们保留了符合纳入标准的12项研究。他们得出结论，ECPR相较于标准CPR在心脏骤停（CA）中的生存率和神经学结局更好。一个非常相关的问题是考虑农村地区的OHCA以及ECPR中心的最小招募人数，以确保获得足够的培训和专业知识。

总体评论：
这篇文献综述很有趣，似乎进行了准确的执行。作者的结果和结论是相关的。此外，手稿的文本、图表和表格清晰且呈现得当。
审稿人对这项研究没有重大关切或批评。
次要评论：
引言，第三行：请将motality更正为mortality。

paper_title: Towards generalisable hate speech detection: a review on obstacles and solutions
paper_abstract: Hate speech is one type of harmful online content which directly attacks or promotes hate towards a group or an individual member based on their actual or perceived aspects of identity, such as ethnicity, religion, and sexual orientation. With online hate speech on the rise, its automatic detection as a natural language processing task is gaining increasing interest. However, it is only recently that it has been shown that existing models generalise poorly to unseen data. This survey paper attempts to summarise how generalisable existing hate speech detection models are, reason why hate speech models struggle to generalise, sums up existing attempts at addressing the main obstacles, and then proposes directions of future research to improve generalisation in hate speech detection.

paper_title: The long reads ahead: de novo genome assembly using the MinION
paper_abstract: Nanopore technology provides a novel approach to DNA sequencing that yields long, label-free reads of constant quality. The first commercial implementation of this approach, the MinION, has shown promise in various sequencing applications. This review gives an up-to-date overview of the MinION's utility as a de novo  sequencing device. It is argued that the MinION may allow for portable and affordable de novo sequencing of even complex genomes in the near future, despite the currently error-prone nature of its reads. Through continuous updates to the MinION hardware and the development of new assembly pipelines, both sequencing accuracy and assembly quality have already risen rapidly. However, this fast pace of development has also lead to a lack of overview of the expanding landscape of analysis tools, as performance evaluations are outdated quickly. As the MinION is approaching a state of maturity, its user community would benefit from a thorough comparative benchmarking effort of de novo assembly pipelines in the near future. An earlier version of this article can be found on  bioRxiv .
review_content:
This paper by Carlos de Lannoy et al. is a timely review of the choices available for genome sequencing based on Oxford Nanopore technology. This is a fast-moving field, and potential entrants will be well served by this exposition of the many options available. However, precisely because it is a fast-moving field, several of these options are already obsolete (yet relevant in providing context for recent developments). In addition, the many options in bioinformatics are confounded with a multiplicity of genome types (small prokaryotic to large repetitive) and nanopore chemistries.

Many readers would benefit from additional support in navigating these multiple menageries. For this reason, we would like to ask the authors to address the following issues in more detail:
 1. All methods discussed have been tested using nanopore data, but never using comparable datasets. Therefore, evaluating for example the percentages of sequence correctness is not straightforward. A table simply listing the methods with some of their key characteristics/assembly statistics/nanopore chemistries/genomes assembled would be helpful.

    Similar confusion is always looming because of the many nanopore chemistries that have been available. For example, on page 7, on the improvement of the Metrichor basecallers: the improvement here, from 68% to 95%, also coincides with the shift from R7.3 to R9. While this is mentioned as ‘numerous improvements in chemistry and hardware’, it would be clearer if the nanopore chemistry generation is explicitly mentioned whenever such percentages are listed.
 2. The in-depth discussion of assembly methodology is clearly delimited to methods focusing on nanopore data only. But is this actually already a feasible option, and if not, what is needed to make this happen? All of the assembly pipelines discussed still fall short of reference genome quality. At the moment, sequence correction using short-read data (Pilon) remains necessary. Why/when should one choose for nanopore-only assembly, as opposed to hybrid?
 3. Both basecalling and polishing are nanopore-specific bioinformatics tasks, however the de novo assemblers are in principle (and often in practice) suitable for any long-read technology. Therefore, a brief discussion comparing PacBio and nanopore for genome assembly is appropriate. PacBio-specific assemblers are briefly mentioned (SMARTdenovo, Falcon), but how do they relate to e.g. Canu?


A few minor issues:
  * p2, p6: please change ‘chapter’ to ‘paper’.
  * p3, second column, modifications of the R9/CsgG pore: this is a good location to briefly introduce R9.4/R9.5
  * p5: ‘multiple reads may be linked together by hairpins into chimeric reads’ -> multiple molecules
  * Figure 5: explain that the white wells are ignored.
  * p8, Canu: ‘Where possible, gaps between unique unitigs are filled with repetitive elements.’ This may need some rephrasing, ‘repetitive element’ is a specific term – not necessarily identical with ‘non-unique genome content’.
  * p8: percentages for DeepNano: ‘more accurate … (approximately 70% versus 77%) and … (approximately 88% versus 87%)’. Which is which?
  * Figure 7, 3rd kmer: the reverse complement of CTC isn’t TCT.
  * p11: a few extra days of CPU time spent on polishing is acceptable for large genomes, but a major bottleneck for bacteria – polishing then takes longer than sequencing. Do these timings refer to prokaryotic genomes?
paper_title_zh: "长读长之路：利用MinION进行从头基因组组装"
paper_abstract_zh: 纳米孔技术为DNA测序提供了一种新颖的方法，能够产生长片段、无需标记且质量恒定的读数。该方法的首次商业实现，即MinION，已在各种测序应用中显示出潜力。本文综述了MinION作为全新测序设备的最新应用情况。文章认为，尽管MinION目前的读数存在误差，但在不久的将来，它可能实现便携且经济的新基因组测序，即使是复杂基因组也不例外。通过不断更新MinION硬件和开发新的组装流程，测序准确性和组装质量已迅速提升。然而，这种快速的发展也导致了对分析工具不断扩展的领域缺乏全面了解，因为性能评估很快就会过时。随着MinION逐渐成熟，其用户社区将受益于对全新组装流程进行彻底比较基准测试的努力。本文的早期版本可在bioRxiv上找到。
review_content_zh:
Carlos de Lannoy等人的这篇论文及时地综述了基于牛津纳米孔技术进行基因组测序的可选方案。这是一个快速发展的领域，潜在的新进入者将受益于对众多可选方案的详细阐述。然而，正因为这是一个快速发展的领域，其中一些选项已经过时（但在提供近期发展背景方面仍具相关性）。此外，生物信息学的众多选项与多种基因组类型（从小型原核生物到大型重复序列）和纳米孔化学性质相混淆。

许多读者将受益于在导航这些多重复杂选项时获得额外支持。为此，我们希望作者能更详细地探讨以下问题：
1. 所讨论的方法均使用纳米孔数据进行了测试，但从未使用过可比较的数据集。因此，例如评估序列正确性的百分比并非直接明了。一个简单列出方法及其关键特征/组装统计/纳米孔化学性质/组装基因组的表格将有所帮助。

    由于存在多种纳米孔化学性质，类似的困惑始终存在。例如，在第7页关于Metrichor碱基调用器改进的讨论中：从68%到95%的改进也与从R7.3到R9的转变相吻合。尽管这被提及为“化学和硬件的众多改进”，但如果在列出此类百分比时明确提及纳米孔化学性质的代际，将会更清晰。
2. 对组装方法的深入讨论显然仅限于专注于纳米孔数据的方法。但这实际上是否已经是一个可行的选项？如果不是，还需要什么来实现这一点？所有讨论的组装流程仍未能达到参考基因组质量。目前，使用短读数据（Pilon）进行序列修正仍然是必要的。为什么/何时应选择仅使用纳米孔的组装，而不是混合组装？
3. 碱基调用和抛光都是纳米孔特有的生物信息学任务，然而从头组装器在原则上（且通常在实践中）适用于任何长读技术。因此，简要比较PacBio和纳米孔在基因组组装中的表现是适当的。PacBio特定的组装器（如SMARTdenovo、Falcon）被简要提及，但它们与例如Canu有何关联？

一些小问题：
  * 第2页、第6页：请将“章节”改为“论文”。
  * 第3页，第二列，R9/CsgG孔的修改：这是一个简要介绍R9.4/R9.5的好位置。
  * 第5页：“多个读数可能通过发夹连接成嵌合读数” -> 多个分子。
  * 图5：解释白色孔被忽略的原因。
  * 第8页，Canu：“在可能的情况下，独特单元之间的间隙用重复元素填充。”这可能需要重新措辞，“重复元素”是一个特定术语——不一定等同于“非唯一基因组内容”。
  * 第8页：DeepNano的百分比：“更准确……（大约70%对77%）和……（大约88%对87%）”。哪个是哪个？
  * 图7，第三个kmer：CTC的反向互补不是TCT。
  * 第11页：对于大型基因组，多花几天CPU时间进行抛光是可接受的，但对于细菌来说是一个主要瓶颈——抛光时间比测序时间还长。这些时间是否指原核基因组？

paper_title: Patient education for individuals with Interstitial Lung Disease: A scoping review.
paper_abstract:
Objectives 
     Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) is a severe and rapidly progressing disease with a high fatality rate. Patient education (PE) has been demonstrated to promote long-term adherence to exercise and lifestyle improvements by assisting patients in developing self-management techniques. Our scoping review's goal was to chart out the prevailing level of research about the content, processes, and effectiveness of PE for patients with ILD. 
   
   
     Methods 
     The relevant databases were searched using the rules provided by Arksey and O'Malley in 2005 and the Joanna Briggs Institute reviewers' manual 2015: an approach for JBI scoping reviews. Individuals with ILD, published in English between the years of inception and 2020, and describing PE administered by various healthcare practitioners were among the 355 studies found and reviewed. Thirteen studies met these criteria. 
   
   
     Results 
     PE delivery process, delivery techniques, quality of life assessments, common PE themes, and healthcare professional participation were all recognized and cataloged. 
   
   
     Conclusion 
     Despite the fact that healthcare professionals (physicians, nurses, and physiotherapists) provide PE to patients with ILD regularly, the PE provided varies greatly (contents of PE, process of delivery and delivery techniques). During the scoping review, a significant variation in the themes was addressed. They could not provide any evidence-based specific recommendations for all healthcare practitioners due to the studies' heterogeneity and lack of effectiveness measures.
review_content:
1. The justification for performing a scoping review to map the existing knowledge gaps in PE for patients with ILD is explained in the introduction. You could explain on why previous studies on PE for ILD patients is insufficient or inadequate, emphasizing the necessity for additional study.
 2. The introduction discusses the lack of studies on the content, delivery, and efficacy of PE for ILD patients.
    To highlight the need of filling this knowledge gap, you could briefly discuss how it might affect clinical practice or patient outcomes.
 3. There is discussion of a transparent method for selecting and screening articles, which includes independent evaluation by multiple reviewers.
    You could discuss any steps performed, such inter-rater reliability tests or calibration exercises, to guarantee consistency and reliability amongst reviewers.
 4. The study emphasizes critical elements such medication management, oxygen therapy, nutrition, and exercise and acknowledges the significance of a multidisciplinary approach in the management of ILD.
    You may be more specific about how each member of the healthcare team contributes to patient education and care coordination.
 5. Some terms or concepts mentioned, such as "reactive oxygen species" and "telerehabilitation" may need further explanation.
 6. The conclusions and implications of the review should include combining the major themes that were covered throughout, such as the importance of outcome measures, the lack of standardized approaches to PE delivery.
paper_title_zh: 间质性肺病患者教育：一项范围综述。
paper_abstract_zh:
**目的**
间质性肺病（ILD）是一种严重且进展迅速的疾病，具有较高的死亡率。患者教育（PE）已被证明可以通过帮助患者发展自我管理技巧，促进长期坚持锻炼和生活方式的改善。我们范围综述的目标是梳理关于ILD患者PE的内容、过程和有效性的现有研究水平。

**方法**
使用Arksey和O'Malley在2005年提供的规则以及Joanna Briggs Institute评审员手册2015：JBI范围综述的方法，搜索相关数据库。在355项被发现和审查的研究中，包括描述由各种医疗保健从业者提供的、发表于起始年至2020年间的、以英语发表的ILD患者的研究。有13项研究符合这些标准。

**结果**
PE的交付过程、交付技巧、生活质量评估、常见的PE主题以及医疗保健专业人员的参与都被识别并编目。

**结论**
尽管医疗保健专业人员（医生、护士和物理治疗师）经常为ILD患者提供PE，但所提供的PE差异很大（PE的内容、交付过程和交付技巧）。在范围综述期间，针对主题的显著差异进行了讨论。由于研究的异质性和缺乏有效性衡量标准，他们无法为所有医疗保健从业者提供任何基于证据的具体建议。
review_content_zh:
1. 引言部分解释了进行范围审查以绘制ILD患者PE现有知识空白的合理性。您可以进一步说明为何以往对ILD患者PE的研究不足或不充分，强调额外研究的必要性。
2. 引言讨论了关于ILD患者PE的内容、传递和效力的研究缺乏。为突出填补这一知识空白的需求，您可以简要讨论这可能如何影响临床实践或患者结局。
3. 讨论了选择和筛选文章的透明方法，包括多位评审员的独立评估。您可以讨论为确保评审员之间的一致性和可靠性所采取的任何步骤，例如评分者间信度测试或校准练习。
4. 研究强调了药物管理、氧疗、营养和锻炼等关键要素，并承认多学科方法在ILD管理中的重要性。您可以更具体地说明医疗团队的每个成员如何贡献于患者教育和护理协调。
5. 提到的一些术语或概念，如“活性氧 species”和“远程康复”，可能需要进一步解释。
6. 审查的结论和影响应包括整合全文涵盖的主要主题，如结局指标的重要性、PE传递标准化方法的缺乏。

paper_title: Prayers for Sickness: What do people pray for and how do they deal with unanswered prayer?
paper_abstract:
Background 
    This paper focuses upon prayer for sickness. What do individuals suffering from illness, their families and the wider community pray for? How do they deal with unanswered prayer? Do they pray for cure, to guide medical professionals or to cope with their sickness? What rationalisations do they proffer for unanswered prayer? 
  
  
    Methods 
    Based on a critical literature review and deploying secondary data from the Twenty First Century Evangelical research programme, the data suggest that prayers for guiding medical professionals and coping are more common than for cure, at least in Global North countries such as the UK and US. But why do those who believe in miracles not ask God for divine healing? Furthermore, unanswered prayer can conflict with Christian views of God as omnipotent and all loving. 
  
  
    Results 
    Respondents use a number of theodical rationalisations to resolve this conflict. 
  
  
    Conclusions 
    The results are discussed in relation to cognitive dissonance theory, learned helplessness, the need to conserve a relationship with the Divine, and desire to manage risk of disappointment and reduce consequent emotional pain.

受访者使用多种神义论合理化解释来化解这一冲突。

结果在认知失调理论、习得性无助、保持与神圣关系的需求，以及管理失望风险和减少相应情感痛苦的愿望等方面进行了讨论。

paper_title: Fostering healthcare system sustainability through efficient practices: Can adopting biosimilars ease the financial burden of rheumatoid arthritis?
paper_abstract: Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases like rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have been successfully treated using biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. These medications are not utilized as first-line treatment, in part because of their high cost, but they are frequently seen to be cost-effective for RA patient populations that do not respond adequately to conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Moreover, not all RA patients who meet clinical eligibility criteria can access biologics, not even as second-line therapy. Recently, there has been an increasing interest in biosimilars that are highly comparable to their originator biologics in terms of efficacy and safety but generally come at a lower price. This review summarizes the potential role of biosimilars in reducing RA expenditure and increasing RA patient access to biologic therapies. As the global landscape for biosimilars continues to evolve, it is essential to consider the unique challenges and opportunities in different healthcare systems. By leveraging the potential of biosimilars, healthcare systems can improve RA management, ease its economic burden and ensure that patients have access to effective and affordable treatments. The future of RA treatment lies in the integration of biosimilars into clinical practice, offering hope for more sustainable and equitable healthcare systems.
review_content:
* The paper presents a comprehensive and well-researched examination of biosimilars in rheumatoid arthritis treatment. It effectively integrates recent findings, making it a valuable contribution to the ongoing discussion on biologic therapies in rheumatology.
  * The topic is timely and relevant, given the increasing utilization of biosimilars in various healthcare systems and the implications for treatment accessibility and cost-effectiveness.
  * The paper demonstrates a good review of existing recent literature that addresses the management of RA with biosimilars. The authors adopt a comprehensive approach by considering clinical, economic and societal perspectives, which is essential for understanding the complexities of biosimilar adoption and usage in different healthcare contexts.
  * Studies from various countries are included, which enhances the paper's relevance. The paper highlights the importance of patient access to biosimilars and the economic burden of RA treatments.
To enhance clarity and applicability, I suggest the following revisions:
  * The authors could further enhance the discussion by incorporating more qualitative studies on patient experiences and attitudes toward biosimilars, in terms of acceptance and adherence.
  * Adding case studies from countries or healthcare systems that have successfully integrated biosimilars for rheumatoid arthritis treatmen could strengthen the practical applicability of the findings.
With these revisions, the paper has the potential to make a significant contribution to the literature and serve as a valuable resource for both clinicians and policymakers.
