paper_title: Taxonomy of interventions at academic institutions to improve research quality
paper_abstract:
Background 
     Research waste has become an increasing issue for research institutions and researchers due to poor research reproducibility and replicability. Interventions to improve research quality at research institutions are important to reduce research waste. This review aims to identify and classify possible interventions to improve research quality, reduce waste, and improve reproducibility and replicability within research-performing institutions. 
   
   
     Methods 
     Steps to develop the taxonomy were 1) Use an exemplar paper looking at journal-level interventions to improve research quality, 2) Adapt intervention titles to align with Michie’s behaviour change wheel, 3) Conduct a 2-stage search in PubMed using seed articles and reviews, and a forward and backward citation search to identify articles that evaluated or described the implementation of interventions to improve research quality, 4) Pilot draft taxonomy with researchers at an openscience conference workshop, and 5) Iterative drafting and revisions by the research team. 
   
   
     Results 
     Overall, 93 individual interventions were identified through the peer-review literature and researcher reporting. Eleven peer-reviewed articles were identified. Interventions identified covered research stages from before, during, and after study conduct, and whole of institution. Types of intervention included: Tools, Education & Training, Incentives, Modelling and Mentoring, Review & Feedback, Expert involvement, and Policies & Procedures. The taxonomy identified areas for research institutions to focus on to improve research quality, reproducibility, and replicability. 
   
   
     Conclusions 
     Areas of focus and future research include improving incentives to implement quality research practices, evaluating current interventions, encouraging no- or low-cost and high-benefit interventions, examining institution culture and individual research ethos, and encouraging researcher mentor-mentee relationships.
review_content:
Overview and main concerns:
This paper aims to provide a taxonomy of possible interventions to improve research quality, reduce waste, and improve reproducibility and replicability within research-performing institutions. The authors state that, through an iterative process of 5 stages, they identified 93 individual interventions and 11 supporting peer-reviewed articles. They state in the Abstract that the types of interventions included Tools, Education & Training, Incentives, Modelling and Mentoring, Review & Feedback, Expert involvement, and Policies & Procedures.

Whilst I was impressed by the Abstract of this article, and the overarching goal, I was unfortunately left disappointed by the full manuscript itself due to a lack of detail, clarity, and interpretation. Most importantly, the article does not outline the 93 interventions identified or refer the reader to a list of these – I was unable to locate a list of the 93 interventions on the author’s OSF page, which shows an example table of only 12 interventions. Furthermore, the Results section does not report these in detail and the Discussion section focuses more on general international/government-level priorities and interventions for open science, whilst the article’s focus was outlined to focus on institutional interventions. It is imperative that you share the full inputs and outputs of this research to aid reader interpretation and reuse of the taxonomy, and to aid transparency and reproducibility of this work, and further detail about these would make this paper a lot more useful and impactful. For example, you could outline the interventions in the Results section using the categories you outline in the Abstract (i.e. Tools, Education & Training etc.).

Furthermore, I found the description of Methods confusing/inconsistent between the Abstract and the Methods sections; clarification here is key so that the reader fully understands how this taxonomy was developed.

Nevertheless, I do think that this paper has merit so I am hoping that the authors are able to revise it accordingly. I hope my comments are useful to the authors in improving the manuscript.

Major comments regarding clarity and accuracy:
 1. You state throughout, e.g. third sentence of the Abstract, that this paper is a ‘review’. However, this is not a review in the formal sense (e.g., systematic, narrative etc.). Given that the aim of this paper is to create a taxonomy of interventions, it would be better to consistently phrase it as such.
 2. Introduction: You state that “Low reproducibility means that original protocol, materials or data sets may not be available to conduct analysis to reproduce the results” but this is not completely true – even when protocols, materials, and datasets are available, there is evidence of low reproducibility due to non-transparent reporting and/or errors. See Obels et al. (2020) where this problem is also demonstrated in registered reports that aim to incorporate these practices [ref 1]. I also disagree with your definition of replicability, “low replicability relates to the inability to re-conduct or re-conduct well an entire study or experiment, regardless of whether the results replicate” – many studies focus on low replicability rates of replication attempts (e.g., the OSC 2015 who estimated a 36% successful replications), so the definition of low replicability does indeed include consideration of ‘whether the results replicate’. I would simply rephrase your definitions of reproducibility and replication to more accurately describe them. I tend to use the definitions provided by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, 2019: [ ref 2 ] which is also used nicely in this paper: [ ref 3 ]
 3. Introduction, “The flow-on effects impact research users such as industry” – in what way does it impact? Can you expand on this seemingly important point?
 4. “Some key stakeholders in improving the research system to improve quality are researchers, journals, and research funders, as well as research institutions” a paper that may help support your point here is: [ ref 4 ]. To clarify, I am a co-author of this paper, but it supports the identical point that you currently make without a reference to support it. The paper is titled “Reforms to improve reproducibility and quality must be coordinated across the research ecosystem” and states “In this commentary, we—the Local Network Leads of the UK Reproducibility Network—outline our response to the UK House of Commons Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on research integrity and reproducibility. We argue that coordinated change is needed to create (1) a positive research culture, (2) a unified stance on improving research quality, (3) common foundations for open and transparent research practice, and (4) the routinisation of this practice. For each of these areas, we outline the roles that individuals, institutions, funders, publishers, and Government can play in shaping the research ecosystem. Working together, these constituent members must also partner with sectoral and coordinating organisations to produce effective and long-lasting reforms that are fit-for-purpose and future-proof. These efforts will strengthen research quality and create research capable of generating far-reaching applications with a sustained impact on society”.
 5. It would be helpful to include a figure of Michie’s behaviour change wheel in the Introduction to guide the reader (if you search “Michie behaviour change wheel” in Google images, you can see lots of different ways that researchers have done this, and I see that you do use a figure in your video abstract, which is great!).
 6. Other research teams have applied Michie’s behaviour change wheel to meta-scientific research and these should be cited so as to better situate this paper and not oversell its novelty, e.g. [ ref 5 ] and [ ref 6 ]. To transparently outline, I am a co-author on the 1st recommended article; my recommendation is not based on my co-authorship here, but because we specifically use the COM-B model within the context of open science practices. The paper at current outlines no other work that has used Michie’s behaviour change wheel in meta-scientfic research, but the two references here highlight that work does indeed apply such model and is proving to be very useful in this regard. Inclusion of these references therefore bolsters the point made my the authors.
 7. I recommend moving the aim of this ‘review/taxonomy’ upwards so that it comes directly after “What might research institutions do to improve the quality and reproducibility of their research?”… “This review aims to develop a taxonomy of possible interventions to improve research quality…”. I was searching for a specific aim in this paragraph and only got to it at the end. Situating it first will aid reader interpretation.
 8. The end of the Introduction states “To assist this process, we first aimed to identify and classify published and unpublished examples, including studies that assessed the interventions” but the Abstract states that the first step was to “1) Use an exemplar paper looking at journal-level interventions to improve research quality”. Can you clarify the steps in each of these sections to ensure consistency/accuracy. Furthermore, the Introduction ends after you state “we first aimed to…”, meaning that the reader does not know what happened in the other stages. You could either delete this sentence from the Introduction and use the Method section to accurately outline the steps, or add all steps after this sentence in the Introduction.
 9. I am confused by the Methods section because of the Abstract – the Abstract states that the first step was to “use an exemplar paper looking at journal-level interventions…” but the Methods then suggests that multiple articles were used (“a set of seed articles”). Please clarify the Methods throughout the paper. These seed articles should also be specified and cited here.
10. Results: Please include the direct URL to the OSF site where the supplementary materials (i.e., the full taxonomy) are held. I was able to find this by searching OSF to guide my review (https://osf.io/gfw72/).
11. In Table 1, for the Chauvin (2019) paper, under “Population” it states “ECRs (although at the journal-level, is translatable?” – what do you mean by this? Is the sentence in brackets meant to be there?
12. Discussion: You suggest that your taxonomy aligns with both Michie’s behaviour change wheel and the Nosek pyramid. First, it would be helpful to expand what you mean by the ‘Nosek pyramid’ because this not a well-known term. The citation is also to the OSC (2015) paper – is this correct? Second, you may be interested in also mapping your taxonomy to a recent paper that categorises open research initiatives into procedural, community, and structural change [ ref 7 ]. For full transparency, I am a co-author on this paper and we are currently in the process of writing up a systematic literature review of such initiatives. It occurs to me that your taxonomy fits these three thematic categories.

Minor stylistic recommendations:
 1. [Abstract]: The first two sentences of the Abstract use the word ‘research’ six times – can you rephrase or remove this term so that is doesn’t appear so much? E.g. it can be removed from before ‘reproducibility and replicability’.
 2. [Introduction]: At the term ‘rates’ to the end of this sentence: ”Studies in disciplines as diverse as economics, cancer biology, psychology, machine learning, ecology, and social sciences have found disappointingly low reproducibility and replicability”.
 3. [Methods]: Remove the duplication of the word ‘potential’ in the following sentence: “Because the potential range of potential interventions..”.
paper_title_zh: 学术机构提升研究质量干预措施分类学
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
研究浪费已成为研究机构和研究人员日益关注的问题，原因在于研究结果的重复性和可复制性较差。在研究机构中实施提高研究质量的干预措施对于减少研究浪费至关重要。本综述旨在识别和分类可能用于提高研究质量、减少浪费以及提升研究重复性和可复制性的干预措施。

方法
开发分类法的步骤包括：1）使用一篇关于期刊层面干预措施以提高研究质量的示范性论文；2）调整干预措施的标题以与Michie的行为改变轮相一致；3）在PubMed中进行两阶段搜索，使用种子文章和综述，以及前向和后向引文搜索，以识别评估或描述实施提高研究质量干预措施的文章；4）在开放科学会议工作坊中与研究人员试用草拟的分类法；5）研究团队进行迭代草拟和修订。

结果
通过同行评审文献和研究人员的报告，共识别出93项单独的干预措施。确定了11篇同行评审文章。识别出的干预措施涵盖了研究的前期、中期、后期以及整个机构。干预类型包括：工具、教育与培训、激励、建模与指导、审查与反馈、专家参与以及政策与程序。该分类法为研究机构指明了提高研究质量、重复性和可复制性的重点领域。

结论
重点关注领域和未来研究方向包括：改善实施高质量研究实践的激励措施，评估当前干预措施，鼓励无成本或低成本且高收益的干预措施，考察机构文化和个人研究理念，以及鼓励研究人员之间的导师-学徒关系。
review_content_zh:
概述及主要关切：
本文旨在提供一个可能的干预措施分类，以改善研究质量、减少浪费，并在研究执行机构内提高研究的可重复性和可复制性。作者表示，通过一个5阶段的迭代过程，他们识别了93项个体干预措施和11篇支持性同行评审文章。他们在摘要中指出，干预措施的类型包括工具、教育与培训、激励措施、建模与指导、审查与反馈、专家参与以及政策与程序。

尽管我对这篇文章的摘要及其总体目标印象深刻，但遗憾的是，由于全文缺乏细节、清晰度和解释，我对完整手稿感到失望。最重要的是，文章没有概述所识别的93项干预措施，也没有引导读者查阅这些措施的列表——我在作者的开源框架（OSF）页面上无法找到这93项干预措施的列表，该页面仅展示了一个包含12项干预措施的示例表格。此外，结果部分没有详细报告这些干预措施，而讨论部分更多地关注于国际/政府层面的开放科学优先事项和干预措施，而文章的重点是机构层面的干预措施。必须分享这项研究的完整输入和输出，以帮助读者理解和重用这一分类法，并提高这项工作的透明度和可重复性，更多细节将使这篇文章更有用和更具影响力。例如，您可以在结果部分按照摘要中概述的类别（即工具、教育与培训等）来概述这些干预措施。

此外，我发现方法部分的描述在摘要和方法部分之间存在混淆/不一致；这里的澄清是关键，以便读者完全理解这一分类法是如何开发的。

尽管如此，我认为这篇文章仍有其价值，因此我希望作者能够相应地进行修订。我希望我的评论对作者改进手稿有所帮助。

关于清晰度和准确性的主要评论：
1. 您在全文中多次提到，例如摘要的第三句，称这篇文章为“综述”。然而，这并不是严格意义上的综述（如系统综述、叙述综述等）。鉴于本文的目的是创建一个干预措施分类法，最好将其一致地表述为分类法。
2. 引言部分：您提到“低可重复性意味着原始协议、材料或数据集可能无法用于进行分析以重现结果”，但这并不完全正确——即使协议、材料和数据集可用，由于非透明报告和/或错误，也存在低可重复性的证据。参见Obels等人。 (2020) 在注册报告中同样展示了这一问题，这些报告旨在纳入这些实践 [ref 1]。我也不同意你对可复制性的定义，“低可复制性涉及无法重新进行或良好地重新进行整个研究或实验，无论结果是否可复制”——许多研究关注复制尝试的低可复制率（例如，OSC 2015年估计的成功复制率为36%），因此低可复制性的定义确实包括对“结果是否可复制”的考虑。我会简单地重新表述你对可重复性和复制的定义，以更准确地描述它们。我倾向于使用美国国家科学院、工程与医学院2019年提供的定义：[ref 2]，该定义也在这篇论文中得到了很好的应用：[ref 3]。

3. 引言，“连锁效应影响研究用户如工业界”——以何种方式产生影响？能否扩展这一看似重要的观点？

4. “改善研究系统以提高质量的一些关键利益相关者包括研究人员、期刊、研究资助者以及研究机构”，一篇可能有助于支持你观点的论文是：[ref 4]。需要澄清的是，我是这篇论文的合著者，但它支持了你目前提出的相同观点，只是没有引用来支持。该论文题为“改革必须在整个研究生态系统中协调以改善可重复性和质量”，并指出“在这篇评论中，我们——英国可重复性网络的地方网络负责人——概述了我们对英国下议院科学与技术委员会关于研究诚信和可重复性调查的回应。我们认为需要协调变革以创建（1）积极的研究文化，（2）统一提高研究质量的立场，（3）开放和透明研究实践的共同基础，（4）这一实践的常规化。对于这些领域中的每一个，我们都概述了个人、机构、资助者、出版商和政府可以在塑造研究生态系统中扮演的角色。共同努力，这些组成部分成员还必须与行业和协调组织合作，制定有效且持久的改革，这些改革适合目的且面向未来。这些努力将加强研究质量，并创造能够产生深远应用并对社会产生持续影响的研究。”

5. 在引言中包含Michie行为改变轮的图示将有助于引导读者（如果你在谷歌图片中搜索“Michie行为改变轮”，可以看到许多研究者不同的展示方式，我看到你在视频摘要中确实使用了图示，这很棒！）。

6. 其他研究团队已将Michie行为改变轮应用于元科学研究，这些研究应被引用，以便更好地定位本文，避免过度宣传其新颖性，例如。 [参考文献5]和[参考文献6]。为了透明地说明，我是第一篇推荐文章的合著者；我的推荐并非基于我的合著身份，而是因为我们特别在开放科学实践的背景下使用了COM-B模型。当前的文章概述中没有提及其他在元科学研究中使用Michie行为改变轮的工作，但这里的两个参考文献表明确实有此类工作，并且在这方面证明非常有用。因此，包含这些参考文献可以增强作者所提出的观点。

7. 我建议将这篇“综述/分类法”的目标上移，使其直接位于“研究机构可以做些什么来提高其研究的质量和可重复性？”之后……“本综述旨在开发一个可能的干预措施分类法以提高研究质量……”。我在这一段中寻找具体目标，但直到最后才找到。将其放在首位将有助于读者的理解。

8. 引言的结尾部分提到“为了协助这一过程，我们首先旨在识别和分类已发表和未发表的示例，包括评估干预措施的研究”，但摘要中提到第一步是“1）使用一篇关于期刊层面干预措施以提高研究质量的示例论文”。您能否澄清这两个部分中的步骤，以确保一致性和准确性。此外，引言在“我们首先旨在……”之后结束，这意味着读者不知道其他阶段发生了什么。您可以选择从引言中删除这句话，并在方法部分准确概述步骤，或者在引言中的这句话之后添加所有步骤。

9. 由于摘要，我对方法部分感到困惑——摘要中提到第一步是“使用一篇关于期刊层面干预措施的示例论文……”，但方法部分则暗示使用了多篇文章（“一组种子文章”）。请在整个论文中澄清方法。这些种子文章也应在此处具体说明并引用。

10. 结果：请包括OSF网站上补充材料（即完整分类法）的直接URL。我通过搜索OSF找到了这个链接，以指导我的评审（https://osf.io/gfw72/）。

11. 在表1中，对于Chauvin（2019）的文章，在“人群”下写道“ECRs（尽管在期刊层面，可翻译吗？）”——这是什么意思？括号中的句子是应该存在的吗？

12. 讨论：您建议您的分类法与Michie的行为改变轮和Nosek金字塔都一致。首先，扩展说明“Nosek金字塔”的含义会很有帮助，因为这不是一个广为人知的术语。引用的也是OSC（2015）的论文——这是正确的吗？ 其次，您可能还希望将您的分类法与一篇最近的论文进行映射，该论文将开放研究倡议分为程序性、社区性和结构性变革[参考文献7]。为了完全透明，我是这篇论文的合著者，我们目前正在撰写关于此类倡议的系统文献综述。我意识到您的分类法符合这三个主题类别。

一些小的风格建议：
1. [摘要]：摘要的前两句话中使用了六次“研究”一词——您能否重新措辞或删除这个术语，以避免出现频率过高？例如，可以将其从“可重复性和可复制性”之前删除。
2. [引言]：在此句末尾添加“比率”一词：“在经济学、癌症生物学、心理学、机器学习、生态学和社会科学等众多学科的研究中发现，可重复性和可复制性的比率令人失望地低”。
3. [方法]：删除以下句子中“潜在”一词的重复：“因为潜在干预的潜在范围…”。

paper_title: Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCS) in India and their compliance with government benchmarks: A scoping review
paper_abstract: Background: Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCs) are one of the critical pillars of India’s Adolescent Health Programme-Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram that seeks to enable all adolescents to realize their full potential by making informed decisions concerning their health and by accessing the services. Thus, a review was conceptualised to assess the compliance of AFHCs with the benchmark proposed by the Government under Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram. Methods: Three databases (PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar) were searched for articles published between 2014 and December 2022. A snowball search strategy was also used to retrieve all published articles. Based on the search strategy  eight studies were included. Results: AFHCs are not fully compliant with all the benchmarks proposed by the government of India. Evidence from the primary studies showed that the benchmarks need attention as privacy was lacking (six out of seven studies), unavailability of Information Education and Communication material (four out of five), signages (two out of four), referrals (one out of two), and judgemental attitude of health care providers (one out of 3). Conclusions: There is a pressing need to focus on  the  fulfilment of these gaps to make the clinics adolescent-friendly. This might increase the utilisation of available services in AFHCs by adolescents and will improve their health. The improved health will catalyse achieving the Sustainable Development Goals indicators that are associated with nutrition, reproductive health, sexual and intimate partner violence, child marriage, education, and employment.
review_content:
It is a well-written document and is of great interest in public health in India. Some of my comments are:
 1. Some of the abbreviations are not explained by the author, and it will be helpful if they can be expanded upon. Example: GoI, IEC etc. IEC is expanded somewhere in the middle of the study; it will be better to explain when it is used for the first time in the manuscript.
 2. The authors utilize benchmarks proposed by the Government under Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram. It will be helpful to know what the benchmarks are, how those benchmarks are measured (which indicators are used). Also, if there is a report or website which have those benchmarks listed, adding that will be helpful.
 3. This review has a limitation on the number of manuscripts available, and not all the studies have measured the benchmarks, which makes it hard to be replicated and results must be used with caution.
paper_title_zh: 印度青少年友好健康诊所（AFHCs）及其对政府基准的符合情况：一项范围综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景：青少年友好健康诊所（AFHCs）是印度青少年健康计划——拉什特里亚·基绍尔·斯瓦斯塔亚·卡亚卡尔姆（Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram）的关键支柱之一，旨在通过使所有青少年能够就其健康做出知情决策并获取服务，从而充分发挥其潜力。因此，进行了一项综述，以评估AFHCs是否符合政府在该计划下提出的基准。方法：检索了三个数据库（PubMed、Scopus和Google Scholar）中2014年至2022年12月期间发表的文章。还使用了滚雪球搜索策略以检索所有已发表的文章。基于搜索策略，共纳入了八项研究。结果：AFHCs并未完全符合印度政府提出的所有基准。来自主要研究的证据显示，以下基准需要关注：缺乏隐私（七项研究中有六项）、信息教育及传播材料不足（五项研究中有四项）、标识缺失（四项研究中有两项）、转诊不足（两项研究中有一项）以及医疗服务提供者的评判态度（三项研究中有一项）。结论：迫切需要关注这些差距的填补，以使诊所对青少年友好。这可能会增加青少年对AFHCs中可用服务的利用率，并改善其健康状况。改善的健康状况将有助于实现与营养、生殖健康、性暴力和亲密伴侣暴力、童婚、教育及就业相关的可持续发展目标指标。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇写得很好的文档，对印度的公共卫生具有重要意义。我的一些评论如下：

paper_title: Quality assessment of systematic literature on uterine fibroids: a systematic review
paper_abstract:
Background 
     A systematic literature review (SLR) is a research methodology that examines data and findings of other authors relative to specified research questions (RQ), collects multiple research studies, and summarises them to answer a research question using rigorous methods. Many SLRs have been published on uterine fibroids (UFs) in the last two decades but there is a dearth of knowledge on assessment of the quality to determine the reliability of results. 
   
   
     Methods 
     This study employed the SLR method to identify available SLRs published on UFs. Dybå and Dingsøyr quality standards and dichotomous grading scales were employed to determine the quality of primary studies. On February 3rd, 2022, an auto search was conducted twice over Citeseer, EBSCO, ACM, Springer Link, IEE Computer society digital library, and Scopus using 17 search strings. Two teams independently screened papers and compared notes with the inclusion/exclusion criteria. 11 criterial were adapted to evaluate the quality of the SLR’s. 
   
   
     Results 
     33 SLRs were subjected to data extraction after inclusion/exclusion criteria. Answers to our primary research question was positive as the aims and contexts of the SLRs are generally clear and the methodologies employed are all inclusive. The research outputs of the primary studies are valid and justifiable as their research statements were clear and findings unambiguous. Although some studies failed some quality criteria, answers to all RQs were affirmative as the percentage scores of the studies on each of the quality conditions is favourably high. 
   
   
     Conclusions 
     The auto search may be incomplete because some qualified SLRs may have been missed as the choice of search strings was limited and may have omitted terminologies. Notwithstanding, with average quality scores of 83% in reporting, 81.2% in rigour, and 79% in credibility, this study concludes that majority of the meta-analysis published so far on UF are valid and reliable.
review_content:
A systematic review of systematic reviews is an interesting concept and should be helpful.

However, it is always important to remember that all systematic reviews are only as good as the studies included in them and the methodologies used.

The authors state that they give more account to the results and their plausibility than the methodology and I feel this is rather a pity as it misses an opportunity to do something really meaningful.

It was done very quickly which surprised me and I do not generally use these databases for a search such as this. However, the use of the 11 criteria is certainly valid but I would like to have had more detail on this and how it was assessed.

I do not think it true that all SLRs do not assess quality, particularly those in the better journals. I also wondered about the use of the examples of choosing non-hysteroscopic myomectomy which I would rate well and the 2nd on pychosocial burden.

Assessment of non-randomised studies is fraught with problems and are unlikely to be high quality studies by definition. Thus drawing conclusions from an SLR is unlikely to be useful. In addition there is an incorrect reference (No 16 which I think should perhaps be 26.

RQ2 worried me considerably:
'Although 10 of the 33 primary studies did not employ appropriate recruitment strategies for their studies, and the research objectives of 11 are inappropriately designed. Exactly 10 are also silent on the control group(s) required to compare their research methods. However, all of them gave extensive description of their analysis processes and present sufficient data to support their findings (Q7 and Q8); they were simple in data collection and detailed in sample analysis.'
I can't help feeling that any conclusions drawn here would be meaningless.

Overall this is a methodology worth developing further but I think I think must include consideration of methods use and not just results to be meaningful.

I look forward to hearing more about the ideas in this article.
paper_title_zh: 子宫肌瘤系统文献质量评估：一项系统综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
系统文献综述（SLR）是一种研究方法，它检查其他作者相对于特定研究问题（RQ）的数据和发现，收集多项研究，并使用严格的方法总结它们以回答研究问题。在过去二十年中，已发表了许多关于子宫肌瘤（UFs）的SLRs，但对评估质量以确定结果可靠性的知识却相对匮乏。

方法
本研究采用SLR方法识别已发表的关于UFs的SLRs。使用Dybå和Dingsøyr质量标准及二元评分量表来确定初级研究的质量。2022年2月3日，在Citeseer、EBSCO、ACM、Springer Link、IEEE计算机学会数字图书馆和Scopus上使用17个搜索字符串进行了两次自动搜索。两个团队独立筛选论文，并按照纳入/排除标准进行对比。采用11个标准来评估SLR的质量。

结果
根据纳入/排除标准，33篇SLRs进行了数据提取。对我们主要研究问题的回答是肯定的，因为SLRs的目标和背景通常清晰，所采用的方法全面。初级研究的输出结果是有效且合理的，因为它们的研究声明清晰，发现明确。尽管一些研究未达到某些质量标准，但对所有RQs的回答都是肯定的，因为各研究在每个质量条件上的百分比得分都较高。

结论
自动搜索可能不完整，因为一些合格的SLRs可能因搜索字符串的选择有限而遗漏了术语。尽管如此，报告的平均质量得分为83%，严谨性为81.2%，可信度为79%，本研究得出结论，迄今为止发表的多数关于UF的元分析是有效且可靠的。
review_content_zh:
对系统评价的系统评价是一个有趣的概念，应该是有帮助的。

然而，始终重要的是要记住，所有系统评价的质量仅取决于所包含的研究及其使用的方法论。

作者表示，他们更重视结果及其合理性，而不是方法论，我觉得这颇为遗憾，因为这错失了一个做出真正有意义事情的机会。

这项工作完成得非常快，这让我感到惊讶，我通常不会使用这些数据库进行此类搜索。然而，使用11个标准无疑是有效的，但我想了解更多关于这些标准及其评估方式的细节。

我认为并非所有的系统评价都不评估质量，尤其是那些发表在较好期刊上的评价。我还对选择非宫腔镜下肌瘤切除术的例子感到疑惑，我认为这个例子不错，第二个例子是关于心理社会负担的。

非随机研究的评估充满了问题，从定义上讲不太可能是高质量的研究。因此，从系统评价中得出结论可能不太有用。此外，还有一个错误的参考文献（第16条，我认为可能是第26条）。

RQ2让我非常担忧：
“尽管33项原始研究中有10项没有采用适当的招募策略，11项的研究目标设计不当。恰好还有10项对所需比较研究方法的对照组保持沉默。然而，它们都对其分析过程进行了详尽的描述，并提供了足够的数据来支持其发现（Q7和Q8）；它们在数据收集上简单，在样本分析上详细。”
我不禁觉得这里得出的任何结论都将是无意义的。

总体而言，这是一种值得进一步发展的方法论，但我认为必须包括对方法使用的考虑，而不仅仅是结果，才能使其有意义。

我期待听到更多关于这篇文章中的想法。

reasons: I do not think it true that all SLRs do not assess quality, particularly those in the better journals.
A systematic review of systematic reviews is an interesting concept and should be helpful.
However, the use of the 11 criteria is certainly valid but I would like to have had more detail on this and how it was assessed.

paper_title: Preclinical models of acute liver failure -a comprehensive review
paper_abstract: Acute liver failure is marked by the rapid deterioration of liver function in a previously well patient over period of days to weeks. Though relatively rare, it is associated with high morbidity and mortality. This makes it a challenging disease to study clinically, necessitating reliance on preclinical models as means to explore pathophysiology and novel therapies. Preclinical models of acute liver failure are artificial by nature, and generally fall into one of three categories: surgical, pharmacologic or immunogenic. This article reviews preclinical models of acute liver failure and considers their relevance in modeling clinical disease.
review_content: Reviewer 3 Basic reporting None Experimental design None Validity of the findings None Additional comments This is well-written reviwe paper on the current state of preclinical models of acute liver failure. The authors have studied on the existing literature on the topic extensively and comprehensively and their presentation of the major fundings in these studies were accurate and clear. key information has been summarized in figures and table in ways that are concise and memorable to the readers. This reviewer finds this paper quite informative and only has the following suggestions to make: First, the authors may want to add the disadvantages of the Long-Evans model to talbe 1. Thank you for your comments. We have added this. Second, the authors may want to add overall mortality for both clinical and preclinical models in figure 1. We appreciate the suggestion. We added the information in the review.
paper_title_zh: 急性肝衰竭的动物模型研究综述
paper_abstract_zh: 急性肝衰竭的特征是先前健康的患者在数天至数周内肝功能迅速恶化。尽管相对罕见，但该病与高发病率和死亡率相关。这使得临床研究具有挑战性，需要依赖临床前模型来探索病理生理学和新型疗法。急性肝衰竭的临床前模型本质上属于人工构建，通常分为三类：手术模型、药物模型或免疫原性模型。本文综述了急性肝衰竭的临床前模型，并探讨了其在模拟临床疾病中的相关性。
review_content_zh: 审稿人3 基本报告 无 实验设计 无 研究结果的有效性 无 附加评论 这是一篇关于急性肝衰竭临床前模型现状的写得很好的综述文章。作者对这一主题的现有文献进行了广泛而全面的研究，并且他们对这些研究中主要发现的呈现准确且清晰。关键信息已以简洁且易于记忆的方式总结在图表和表格中。本审稿人认为这篇文章信息量很大，仅提出以下建议：首先，作者可能希望在表1中添加Long-Evans模型的缺点。感谢您的评论。我们已经添加了这一点。其次，作者可能希望在图1中添加临床和临床前模型的总体死亡率。我们感谢这一建议。我们已在综述中添加了该信息。

paper_title: Peripheral-physiological and neural correlates of flow experience while playing video games: A comprehensive review
paper_abstract: The flow state is defined by intense involvement in an activity with high degrees of concentration and focused attention, and accompanied by a sense of pleasure. Video games are effective tools for inducing flow, and keeping players in this state is considered to be one of the central goals of game design. Many studies have focused on the underlying physiological and neural mechanisms of flow. Results are inconsistent when describing a unified mechanism underling this mental state. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the physiological and neural correlates of flow and offers an explanation of the relationship between the reported physiological and the neural markers of flow experience. Despite the heterogeneous results, it seems possible to establish associations between reported markers and cognitive and experiential aspects of flow, particularly regarding arousal, attention control, reward processing, automaticity, and selfreferential processing.
review_content: Reviewer 1 (Birte Thissen) Basic reporting I commend the authors for giving an overview over the literature on peripheral-physiological and neural correlates of flow during video gaming. I believe that psychophysiological methods represent a promising approach to both research on flow experiences in particular and on gaming experiences in general. Given the in part contradictory findings and different research methods and designs employed so far, I think that this literature review will greatly benefit the field by summarizing our current knowledge and state of the art. Considering the various possible applications of flow research in health-related areas and the focus on psychophysiological methodology, I further believe that this article will be of high interest for PeerJ’s readers. In terms of English language and grammar, the manuscript satisfies professional standards required by PeerJ and can be allowed for publication. However, I would like to see a major revision of the manuscript’s structure before publication as I found it at times confusing to read and hard to grasp the main information from the text. Therefore, I will now make detailed recommendation on how to change the reporting: 1. When giving the definition of flow, processing fluency is not mentioned; however, apart from attentional absorption and intrinsic enjoyment, processing fluency should be considered a key dimension of flow (Csikszentmihalyi, 1975), from which many psycho- and neuropsychological hypotheses can be deduced. Therefore, the role of processing fluency during flow needs to be made explicit in lines 38-40, 46, and 120-124. We have addressed this comment in the manuscript line 40 – 44: “During this state, termed processing fluency, i.e. the ease with which information is processed, actions seem to happen effortlessly, fluently, and almost automatically. According to this theory, the clearest sign of flow is the merging of action and awareness in a way that “a person in flow is aware of his actions but not of the awareness itself” (Csikszentmihalyi, 1975, pp 38). “ 2. The flow factors given in lines 45-50 should be ordered into antecedents and components: The main antecedent for flow is the optimal balance of skills and challenges (theory: Csikszentmihalyi, 1975; correlation: e.g., Jackson & Marsh, 1996; experiment: e.g., Keller & Blomann, 2008; meta-analysis: Fong, Zaleski, & Leach, 2015); therefore, I would like to see a small paragraph dedicated to it (maybe directly referencing the flow channel model), to the experimental approach it inspired (lines 82-90), and to personality traits that modulate its causal relationship with flow (lines 90-98). This way, a single paragraph would summarize the theoretical background for the experiments you are about to report. I also think the statement from lines 468-469 should be part of this introductory paragraph, so the reader knows right away about potential methodological limitations. We rearranged dimensions of flow according to the reviewer’s comment. In lines 54-84 we discussed these dimensions of flow in terms of antecedents and components, explained the flow-channel model and described some personality traits which would influence the relationship between flow and skill-challenge balance. We also explained the function between performance and flow at the end of this paragraph. 3. Concerning the flow components, I suggest you group 2), 3), 7), and 8) together as they are all related to absorption. In contrast, 4), 5), and 6) are all related to fluency. At this point, it should be clarified that 4)-6) can both be regarded as activity characteristics and thus antecedents of flow, and as subjective perceptions during flow and thus flow components. Please also refer to Jackson and Marsh (1996), when giving these flow components since the differentiation between 4)-6) stems from their work. Also, include intrinsic enjoyment as another flow component, which is sometimes conceptionalized as an antecedent or a consequence of flow, too. This is important since some flow questionnaires measure intrinsic enjoyment as a flow component (e.g., Jackson’s flow scale). In referring to Jackson and Marsh (1996), the individual items of flow questionnaire FSS can be assigned to two sub-scales of fluency and absorption. Since the focus of our manuscript is on physiological and neural phenomenon of flow experience, we believe that explaining these subscales would add more complexity which is not helpful in our context (the discussion of these specific sub-scales is not taken up again later in the manuscript). Moreover, In Jackson and Marsh (1996) we could not find the assignment of these two sub-dimensions to the mentioned groupings 2, 3, 7, 8 and 4, 5, 6, respectively. We added autotelic experience or intrinsic enjoyment to the dimensions of flow lines 49-53. 4. In regard to experimental approaches in flow research, both the dynamic matching of skills and challenges (which you refer to in lines 66-68; e.g., Keller & Blomann, 2008) and pre-testing skills to assign matching challenge levels (e.g., Moller, Csikszentmihalyi, Nakamura, & Deci, 2007) should be mentioned in addition to creating a medium challenge level (lines 85-90). I would also recommend to at this point briefly state the possibility of having more than three experimental conditions as some of the experiments you are about to report feature another condition (immersion; autonomy), which might confuse the reader later on. Moreover, I know the terminology is not used consistently in flow research, but I think the reader would greatly benefit from you establishing standards for your paper, i.e. stating something along the lines of “When the game’s difficulty is set to a high level, the gamer is assumed to experience stress, frustration, or anxiety rather than flow. In the following, we will refer to the corresponding experimental condition as the overload condition when describing the results of a flow experiment.” Please also make sure that you then use consistent terms throughout lines 120-527. The experimental paradigms implemented in a laboratory setting are discussed now with more detailed information as suggested by the reviewer in lines 104-128. Having a self-selected level (autonomy) is also discussed in this paragraph and Immersion is explained. Also authors established a standard terminology for the reported experiments at the end of the paragraph lines 128-130. 5. I would also like to see a paragraph on flow measurement to early on give the reader an idea of how flow was assessed in the studies that you are about to report. In this paragraph, you should mention the ESM and flow questionnaires as direct, but retrospective flow measures as well as the dual task approach and physiological indicators as indirect, but non-disruptive flow measures. At this point, the limitations of assessing a state with retrospective self-reports should also be clearly stated, making the case for neural or peripheral-psychological indicators. Thus, please form a new paragraph on flow measurement from lines 69-73, 103-108, and 469-479. I would also prefer more references for flow questionnaires (line 73), ideally by adding a corresponding column to Tables 1-4. Necessary information regarding flow measurement earlier on in the text, post-task retrospective questionnaires, and limitation of these measures has been discussed all together in the manuscript lines 85-103.We also added more references for flow questionnaires used by the reviewed articles at lines 90-96. 6. Lines 51-64 need to be marked more clearly as speculation or more evidence on the 'beneficial nature of flow on psychiatric symptoms' needs to be given. Also, a clearer explanation of the reasoning behind flow being beneficial in a clinical context should be provided. Otherwise, I would just leave it out altogether. In lines 131-148 we clarify with more details the notion that inducing flow through playing video games can benefit people with psychiatric disorders. 7. In line 110, you refer to this manuscript as the first review of this kind. However, I am aware of at least one comparable review (Knierim, Rissler, Dorner, Maedche, & Weinhardt, 2018). Whereas I think, your work still adds valuable information and provides an important update, the other review (maybe there is even more?) should be referenced properly and the added value of your literature review should be explained. We appreciate the reviewer’s comment. We managed to find two reviews; nonetheless none of them where specifically in the context of playing video games and none of them have considered both physiological and neural correlates. E.g., Knierim et al. provide a systematic literature review on peripheral nervous system indicators of flow only and not specifically for video games. Both previous reviews as well as the added value of this manuscript have been discussed in detail in lines 159- 171. Experimental design I am confident that the manuscript cites relevant sources correctly and fulfills the methodological and ethical standards required by PeerJ. However, I believe improving the organization of subsections and of the overall structure of the manuscript is necessary to give the reader a clearer overview of the topic. Moreover, to ensure comprehensive, unbiased coverage, I strongly suggest to revise the methodological approach. Please consider my recommendations to improve the results section: 1. In regard to the method used to collect papers on peripheral-physiological and neural correlates of flow during video gaming, I strongly suggest to follow PRISMA guidelines (http://prisma-statement.org, see checklist and flowchart). This would also help the reader to evaluate the study-selection strategy. Specifically, the combinations of keywords used should be made explicit (e.g., ‘neural OR correlates OR brain activity AND flow’) as well as all eligibility criteria. I am also not convinced that Google Scholar can be used to obtain a comprehensive overview and therefore strongly encourage to further use PubMed and Web of Science. Maybe more specific keywords pertaining to certain methods/indices and flow would also help to make sure all relevant papers are found. Just to give you an idea, from my own literature research I can name papers on flow and psychophysiology that you have not included in your literature review: Kivikangas (2006), Drachen et al. (2010), Gaggioli et al. (2013), Bastarache-Roberge et al. (2015), Colzato et al. (2018), Plotnikov et al. (2012), Peifer et al. (2014b), and Tozman et al. (2017). I believe it is crucial to revise your literature review to ensure that no invalid conclusions are drawn due to the lack of certain relevant papers. We agree with the reviewer that we should provide detailed description of the selection procedure using other databases like Web of Science and PubMed. Information regarding method used for collecting studies and inclusion and exclusion criteria (using both databases) has now been updated in lines 173-184. According to the discipline specific standards of the PeerJ journals, our review manuscript is not a systematic or meta- analysis but the scoping review or literature review. Reports of systematic reviews must include a PRISMA flow diagram and complete PRISMA checklist. However, for scoping reviews it is mentioned just to have a Survey Methodology section in which it should be explained how to ensure comprehensive and unbiased coverage of the literature. Some of the references mentioned by the reviewer were not included in the manuscript as they were not in the inclusion criteria of this study. 2. Whereas I find structuring your report into a subsection for peripheral-physiological and neural correlates of flow very helpful, I think the subsections themselves need to be structured more clearly. I suggest to start with a paragraph summarizing theoretical assumptions about flow and the corresponding measures like you did in line 266-280 for the neural subsection. For the neural subsection, you mention the hypofrontality hypothesis (lines 273-274, 358-359) as well as synchronization theory (lines 275-280); however, I would in the same paragraph also mention the notion of effortless attention (lines 568-571), peak performance (lines 130-131, 378-380), and the flow components loss of self-awareness, attentional focus, and intrinsic enjoyment (please make sure to use a consistent terminology here as you also call the latter concentration or intrinsic reward at times), since they, too, inform about potential neuronal correlates of flow. That would help the reader understand which neural correlates are to be expected before learning the actual results. Please note that the link between flow and peak performance should be brought up and explained (!) already in the introduction, preferably when you write about processing fluency and optimal challenge. As of now, it comes a bit out of nowhere when it is used to explain certain results, which is a good example of what I mean by 'confusing to read'. According to the reviewer’s comment, paragraphs summarizing existing theoretical hypothesis and assumptions about flow have been added to the neural correlates of flow section (lines 376-403). We mention theories which were supported or failed to support by the empirical studies in the context of playing video game (including transient hypofrontality, synchronization of attentional and reward networks, and self-referential processing). Effortless attention is discussed as a theoretical hypothesis in the peripheral-physiological correlates of flow. We believe that peak performance should not be mentioned as a hypothetical background as it is not clear whether flow influences performance or vice versa. We discussed the relation between flow and peak performance both in the Introduction (lines 75-84) and in the discussion (lines 876-896). Furthermore, the studies were categorized according to each theory and hypothesis. 3. Similarly, I would recommend expanding on the theoretical background of peripheral-physiological flow correlates in a separate paragraph before presenting results. Please include the inverted U-shaped hypothesis by Peifer et al. (lines 181-184, 539-544), De Manzano et al.’s conceptualization of flow as a state of positive affect and high arousal (lines 160-162; you call it effortless attention but as far as I know De Manzano speaks of arousal and Bruya (2010) speaks of effortless attention, so that should not be confused), and the notion of co-activation of the parasympathetic and sympathetic system during flow (Ullén, De Manzano, Theorell, & Harmat, 2010) in this paragraph, as well as briefly effortless attention and peak performance as these two will reappear in the neural subsection. At this point also comment on assumptions about flow and high arousal/stress (lines 124-127), but please clarify right in the beginning that this is presumably highly dependent on the activity context. You bring up task-dependency only in the neural subsection in line 324, but it applies to all psychophysiological results and should be emphasized right in the beginning! A paragraph summarizing existing theoretical hypothesis and assumptions about flow was added to the peripheral-physiological correlates of flow section (lines 185-214). We mention theories which were supported or failed to support by the empirical studies in the context of playing video game (positive valence and heightened arousal, co-activation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system, effortless or effortful attention, and inverted U-shaped relationship between flow and activity of the stress system). Furthermore, the studies were categorized according to each theory and hypothesis. About the De Manzano et al. 2010, it was mentioned in their study that “flow is proposed to be a state of effortless attention, which arises through an interaction between positive affect and high attention”. So what is mentioned in their study, also mentioned by Bruya (2010) and Ullen et al. (2010). In the theoretical hypothesis part we also briefly mentioned task dependency (lines 213-214) which is later discussed in detail in the discussion. 4. In addition to presenting the theory in a clearer manner, I would also appreciate a clearer presentation of the indicators themselves. Even though PeerJ’s readers will most likely be familiar with psychophysiological indicators, you present a broad variety of methods from eye-tracking to tDCS in this literature review, so readers may not know about all of them. As of now, you explain some indicators when you present corresponding results (e.g. LF-HRV, lines 146-149), but I would like to see this done consistently for all measures employed (peripheral-physiological subsection: HR and HRV, EMG, cortisol, respiration, EDA, and eye-tracking; neuronal subsection: fMRI, perfusion MRI, fNIRS, tDCS, and EEG). Please make sure to refer back to the theory paragraph when you introduce the measures (e.g., cortisol, HPA-axis, stress, Peifer’s hypothesis), so that the reader knows right away how each measure can be related to flow experiences. I would suggest writing a separate paragraph on all indicators and placing it after the theory paragraph, before all results are reported, or writing a short disclaimer for each indicator before presenting the results for this indicator. As the studies are mentioned according to each theoretical hypothesis, we now try to describe all the indicators and measures used in the studies with a short explanation before presenting the actual results. Some of the methods like EEG or fMRI are not indicators but independent techniques and explaining them in this review would lead to redundancies. In order to avoid these redundancies we just mention the technique. 5. Please also reconsider the organization of your report of results: You seem to organize the studies according to when they were conducted; however, given the many different methodologies employed, I would recommend to organize them according to a) the indicators assessed or b) the theoretical background. Depending on which one you chose, the other one should be used to form subsections within the paragraph (e.g., if you choose to go by indictors, first present all evidence this indicator provided on for instance the effortless attention hypothesis, then on the arousal hypothesis, and so on… or the other way around. But keep this structure throughout the report. This is crucial as for instance in line 179-180 you draw a conclusion from the results you just reported and later on state that other results contradict this conclusion; however, it should be made clear within the same sentence or at least paragraph whether a conclusion can be considered valid or not as readers who only scan the text could otherwise pick up wrong information.) This also means that some studies might be brought up several times as they include different indicators or hypotheses – in that case the method should be explained in detail the first time and only briefly referred to from then on. For the sake of clarity, though, it would be very convenient for the reader to get all the information we have on a certain indicator or hypothesis in one single paragraph, instead of having to switch back and forth. Similarly, when you report EEG results, I would like to have different paragraphs/subsections dedicated to results on each frequency band. We agree with the reviewer. All the studies are now organized and mentioned according to the corresponding theoretical background. For each theory we described the results of studies categorized by the indicators assessed by that study. Similarly this categorization has been conducted for EEG studies and all studies in this filed grouped and mentioned based on the frequency bands. 6. Please carefully check lines 120-527 in regard to how you report the studies’ methodology. This should always include the name of the game stimulus, the experimental design/conditions or a statement that the study was correlational, and ideally the name or information on the flow measure (or its proxy). In doing so, you can also refer to your tables. In case no proper flow condition or flow measure was used, this should always be pointed out and briefly discussed to inform the reader about potential limitations. The name of the game used in studies, along with the experimental design/conditions and the utilized flow measure are now mentioned for each study in the manuscript. 7. I found that for some studies you do a very good job in relating results to hypotheses (e.g., lines 312-314, 430-436), but please really spell out the theoretical background (e.g., name the flow component that can be used to explain the result). Moreover, make sure that you do this for each of the reported studies in a similar way. I also really liked the format in which you presented the link between a theoretical construct and a physiological structure in lines 521-524 (putting the latter in parenthesis behind the former), so maybe use that more thoroughly. We now relate the results of the studies to the corresponding theoretical backgrounds. 8. I believe that certain results need clearer explanations on your part: the contradicting results on flow and arousal levels (which you also sometimes call tension or stress – again please use a more consistent terminology; lines 192-199); the meaning of LF-HRV (lines 146-147, 563-564; you do not bring up the substantial evidence that this may not be a direct indicator of sympathovagal balance after all except for one sentence in the discussion!; e.g., Reyes del Paso, Langewitz, Mulder, Van Roon, & Duschek, 2013)); flow condition/measure proxies and their limitations, see above (please be very careful with the wording here as for instance line 386 could be misunderstood as you confirming that high performance works as a proxy for measuring flow with a questionnaire). Each theory is now explained and discussed in the discussion section with more details. The contradicting results on flow and arousal are discussed in lines 693-730. We also discussed the utilization of HRV measures for the assessment of mental effort in lines 741-750. In the Task dependency section, we discuss the limitation of operationalization of skill-challenge balance and used flow measures as well as different paradigms by the studies. 9. The concept of immersion is brought up in the report of certain studies (lines 150, 400-402), but is never clearly defined (with references no less) and contrasted to flow. I believe this concept is still way more prominent than flow in virtual reality and gaming research, so I would like to actually see a small paragraph in the introduction dedicated to it and to its relationship to flow. This will help gaming researchers to connect with your paper and readers in general to understand studies that distinguish a flow from an immersion condition. Concerning immersion, we now explain immersion along with autonomy in lines 120-124. It has been stated that immersion presents structural differences from flow leading to different mental phenomena (Nacke et al. 2008, 2011), however Michailidis et al. (2018) argue that more evidence is needed to justify their separation. Due to this fact, we preferred to focus on flow experience in video games. Validity of the findings I believe that the conclusion drawn in this literature review are well developed and supported. I only have minor recommendations to clarify parts of the discussion: 1. I would suggest that you rename and restructure the subsection of your discussion according to the main hypothesis that will now be outlined in the theory paragraphs beforehand: arousal, effortless attention, hypofrontality, intrinsic enjoyment, and loss of self-awareness. This might require some changes to the structure as for instance effortless attention refers to your discussion of both findings on mental effort (lines 536 onwards) and attentional control (lines 595 onwards). I am certain that this will help the reader evaluate the in part contradictory findings. We restructured the discussion section according to the subfunctions recruited during flow experience which are inferred from the existing theoretical backgrounds and empirical studies. These subfunctions are outlined and discussed in lines 689-829 as: 1) state of positive valence and heightened arousal, 2) Joyous state of focused attention, 3) Synchronized activation of attentional and reward networks, 4) Automaticity, and 5) Loss of self-awareness. 2. I would like to see additional brief subsections on methodological conclusions: In lines 551-559, 679-681, 639-656 and 668-691 you nicely discuss the limitations and applications of certain methods in this research area. I believe that these are very important take-home massages for future studies, so these considerations should be expanded on and stressed by dedicating an entire paragraph of the discussion to them. Also, please make recommendations for future research more explicit. Since task-dependency seems to play an important role for this line of research, it should be discussed in some detail. Different methodological concerns are discussed now in the “Task dependency “section of the discussion (lines 830-862) as possible reasons of inconsistent results in the literature. In following subsection; “Remaining issues and future research considerations” (lines 863-896), we discuss the possible measures to take for disentangling internal experience of flow from external conditions enhancing this experience. In this part suggestions are made for future studies. 3. Similarly, one of the main conclusions I would draw from the research so far is what you state in lines 580-583 in connection to task-dependency. I think that this deserves a separate paragraph since it affects what can be considered a tangible research goal for future studies. I would also like to see it discussed more: What does that mean for psychophysiological flow and gaming research? If there probably is no such thing as a psychophysiological standard pattern for flow, why still study flow with psychophysiological methods? You may also want to consider Knierim et al.’s conclusion that only a co-activation of the parasympathetic and sympathetic system might serve as an objective indicator for flow experiences before completely debunking the possibility to find standard flow patterns, or come up with similar conclusions of your own. We discussed task dependency in lines 830-862. We believe that despite inconsistent result in some studies, one could still establish associations between flow and the five cognitive and physiological subfunctions which we summarized in the discussion including positive valence and heightened arousal, Joyous state of focused attention, synchronization of attentional and reward networks, automaticity, and loss of self-awareness. 4. I have gotten the impression that at times flow and absorption need to be differentiated more clearly. In lines 590-594 you discuss this in relation to automaticity and in lines 664-670 indirectly in relation to attention. However, I think that it needs to be clarified to the reader that high automaticity (which I for the sake of consistency would call effortless attention) can be achieved also under less than optimally challenging condition in overlearned tasks. Similarly, attentional focus can be high also with high challenges if a person is motivated and purposefully concentrates on the task at hand. This should be taken into consideration when discussing corresponding results. In how far does this for instance represent a potential limitation for dual-task designs? I would also like to see it discussed in general, maybe also in relation to immersion: Can we differentiate flow from absorption or immersion in terms of underlying physiological patterns? In this manuscript, we reviewed the studies investigated physiological and neural phenomenon of flow experience in the gaming context. In the Introduction section, we stated that additional factors such as importance of the task and personality characteristics affect the relationship between skill-challenge balance and flow. However, we believe that review of behavioral studies investigating factors modulating the level of flow experience is not in the scope of this review and should be investigated in a completely separate review. Concerning immersion, it has been stated that immersion presents subtle structural differences from flow leading to different mental phenomena (Nacke et al. 2008, 2011), however Michailidis et al. (2018) argue that more evidence is needed to justify their separation. Due to this fact, we preferred to focus on flow experience in video games. 5. The usefulness of performance as an indirect measure for flow, which is discussed in lines 670-679, should be marked more clearly as speculation. Ideally, I would also appreciate more references on the relationship between performance and flow, specifically in the field of computer gaming. Please keep in mind that the most straightforward conclusion is still that performance will be better for easier tasks, whereas flow requires a challenging task. The seemingly paradoxical thought that flow is related to peak performance needs to be explained properly (also already in the introduction, see above). We discuss the relationship between performance and flow and its considerations in lines 876-896 in more detail. 6. I think the conclusion presented in lines 582-583 needs clarification. I find the wording “to some extent” very vague without further explanations. Difference between patterns of ANS activity during flow and mental effort are discussed in lines 733-750. The wording “to some extent” has been deleted. 7. A minor observation, but please do not refer to flow as a feeling (line 664), but consistently as an experience or state. The correction is made. Comments for the Author 1. Please note that in line 582 it says Peifer (2012); I believe it should be Peifer (2014). The citation is correct and refers to “Peifer, C. (2012). Psychophysiological correlates of flow-experience. In Advances in flow research (pp. 139–164). Springer. “ 2. In regard to your tables, I was wondering why you sometimes use parenthesis when giving the m/f behind the sample size to indicate the sample’s gender distribution and sometimes you do not. If there is no reason to do this, I would prefer a more consistent style. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 3. Similarly, in your tables you sometimes indicate missing information with a blank space or with a dash (two dashes actually – maybe make it one longer one instead). Please stick to a consistent style. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 4. When you summarize conditions under design, you sometimes use capital letters in the beginning and sometimes not. Please also again consider using a consistent terminology whenever possible (e.g., ‘Overload’ instead of ‘Hard’, ‘Boredom’ instead of ‘Slow’, etc.). Sometimes the ‘/’ inbetween conditions got shifted to the beginning of the next line, which should be avoided. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 5. You use both ‘and’ and ‘&’ in your tables, but sometimes the ‘&’ is placed in the beginning of a new line. Either spell out ‘and’ consistently or if you use ‘&’ make sure that it does not shift into the next line as this should be avoided in written English. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 6. When giving the time frame under design, you sometimes write out ‘x minutes gameplay’ and sometimes just ‘x minutes’; please use a consistent style. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 7. At times, there seem to be free lines or broader spacing in your tables; please stick to one line spacing throughout all tables. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 8. Beware that I am not a native speaker myself, but I am fairly certain that when giving time frames hyphens and ‘long’ are not used (e.g., ‘2 min’ or ‘2 minutes’ instead of ‘2-min-long’). Please revise your tables accordingly. Also, make sure you stick with either ‘2 minutes’ or ‘2 minute’. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 9. When listing more than two measures, a comma should be used before the ‘and’. Again, revise your tables accordingly, please. We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 10. Table 1 seems to be missing the study of Mauri et al. (2011), which is cited in the text. Please make sure that each study is both described in text and appears in the corresponding table! Since the study conducted by Mauri et al. (2011) was not on the context of video game but on the social media usage, we decide not to mention the study in the table 1. 11. In the table note for Table 1, I would like you to add explanations for the abbreviations fMRI, fNIRS, and NIRS since they appear in this table. I would also like to encourage a more consistent terminology even though I am aware that in the papers themselves different terms are used; you might consider using one term in regard to cortisol/cortisol level and EDR/GRS, EDA/GSC (and then of course also use it consistently in case it appears in another table). One minor formal observation: there is a blank in the wrong space between the GSR and BP explanations. Full explanations of abbreviations are added to the tables. 12. In the table note for Table 2, you do not give explanations for the abbreviations fMRI, fNIRS, ECG, EDA, NIRS, PET, and tDCS. I believe each table should be understandable in its own right, so that a full explanation of all abbreviations is required for each table. Please also note that you write both ‘FNIRS’ and ‘fNIRS’, but it would be preferable to stick to one style of abbreviation. Full explanations of abbreviations are added to the tables. 13. In the table note for Table 3, an explanation for the abbreviations EEG is missing. Please also again consider using consistent terms for electrodermal indices. Full explanations of abbreviations are added to the tables. 14. In Table 3, there is a spelling mistake for ‘seconds’ when Wolf et al.’s study is presented. The mistake is corrected. 15. In Table 4, you start using a ‘+’ to add the dual task; I think it is a bit unfortunate to use a mathematical sign in a non-mathematical way, so maybe just stick to either using ‘and’ or ‘&’ (but consistently please, also in regard to the other tables). We now updated the tables using more consistent style. 16. The table note for Table 4 is missing; however, again all abbreviations used in the table should be explained. Full explanations of abbreviations are added to the tables. 17. One more minor observation: the font changes in Table 4 when Huskey et al.’s game is described. The font style is corrected.
paper_title_zh: 《玩电子游戏时心流体验的外周生理与神经相关因素：一项综合性综述》
paper_abstract_zh: 心流状态被定义为在高度集中和专注的活动中深度投入，并伴随愉悦感。视频游戏是引发心流的有效工具，保持玩家处于这种状态被认为是游戏设计的核心目标之一。许多研究聚焦于心流背后的生理和神经机制。在描述这一心理状态的统一机制时，结果并不一致。本文对心流的生理和神经相关因素进行了全面综述，并解释了所报告的生理标记与心流体验的神经标记之间的关系。尽管结果多样，但似乎可以建立所报告的标记与心流的认知和体验方面的关联，特别是在唤醒、注意力控制、奖励处理、自动化和自我参照处理方面。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1（Birte Thissen）基本报告

我赞赏作者对视频游戏过程中外围生理和神经相关流的文献进行了概述。我相信心理生理学方法代表了一种有前景的研究方法，既适用于特定的流体验研究，也适用于一般游戏体验的研究。鉴于目前部分相互矛盾的发现和采用的不同研究方法和设计，我认为这篇文献综述通过总结我们当前的知识和最新进展，将极大地惠及该领域。考虑到流研究在健康相关领域的各种可能应用以及对心理生理学方法论的聚焦，我进一步相信这篇文章将对PeerJ的读者具有高度兴趣。就英语语言和语法而言，手稿满足了PeerJ所要求的专业标准，可以允许发表。然而，在发表之前，我希望看到对手稿结构的重大修订，因为我发现有时阅读起来令人困惑，难以从文本中抓住主要信息。因此，我现在将提出详细的建议，说明如何改变报告：

1. 在给出流的定义时，未提及处理流畅性；然而，除了注意力沉浸和内在享受外，处理流畅性应被视为流的一个关键维度（Csikszentmihalyi, 1975），从中可以推导出许多心理和神经心理学的假设。因此，在38-40、46和120-124行中需要明确处理流畅性在流中的角色。我们已在手稿的40-44行中回应了这一评论：“在这种状态下，称为处理流畅性，即信息处理的容易程度，行动似乎毫不费力、流畅且几乎自动发生。根据这一理论，流的最明显标志是行动和意识的融合，以至于‘处于流中的人意识到自己的行动，但意识不到意识本身’（Csikszentmihalyi, 1975, pp 38）。”

2. 45-50行中给出的流因素应按前因和成分进行排序：流的主要前因是技能和挑战的最佳平衡（理论：Csikszentmihalyi, 1975；相关性：例如，Jackson & Marsh, 1996；实验：例如，Keller & Blomann, 2008；元分析：Fong, Zaleski, & Leach, 2015）；因此，我希望看到有一个小段落专门讨论它（也许直接引用流通道模型），讨论它所启发的实验方法（82-90行），以及调节其与流因果关系的个性特质（90-98行）。这样，一个段落就能总结你们即将报告的实验的理论背景。我也认为468-469行的声明应成为这段引言的一部分，以便读者立即了解潜在的方法论局限性。 我们根据审稿人的意见重新安排了流畅感的维度。在第54-84行中，我们讨论了这些流畅感维度，包括其前因和组成部分，解释了流畅感通道模型，并描述了一些会影响流畅感与技能-挑战平衡关系的人格特质。我们还在这段落的末尾解释了表现与流畅感之间的函数关系。3. 关于流畅感的组成部分，我建议将2)、3)、7)和8)归为一组，因为它们都与沉浸相关。相比之下，4)、5)和6)都与流畅性相关。在此需要澄清的是，4)-6)既可以被视为活动特征，从而成为流畅感的前因，也可以被视为流畅感过程中的主观感知，从而成为流畅感的组成部分。在提及这些流畅感组成部分时，请参考Jackson和Marsh（1996）的研究，因为4)-6)之间的区分源于他们的工作。此外，还应将内在享受作为另一个流畅感组成部分，有时它也被概念化为流畅感的前因或后果。这一点很重要，因为一些流畅感问卷将内在享受作为流畅感的组成部分（例如，Jackson的流畅感量表）。参考Jackson和Marsh（1996）的研究，流畅感问卷FSS的各个项目可以分配到流畅性和沉浸两个子量表中。由于我们的手稿重点在于流畅感体验的生理和神经现象，我们认为解释这些子量表会增加不必要的复杂性（在后续手稿中不再讨论这些特定的子量表）。此外，在Jackson和Marsh（1996）的研究中，我们未能找到将这两个子维度分别分配到上述2, 3, 7, 8和4, 5, 6两组的依据。我们在第49-53行中添加了自发性体验或内在享受作为流畅感的维度。4. 关于流畅感研究中的实验方法，除了创建中等挑战水平（第85-90行）之外，还应提及技能与挑战的动态匹配（您在第66-68行中提到；例如，Keller & Blomann, 2008）以及通过预测试技能来分配匹配的挑战水平（例如，Moller, Csikszentmihalyi, Nakamura, & Deci, 2007）。我还建议在此简要说明可能存在多于三种实验条件的情况，因为您即将报告的一些实验包含了另一个条件（沉浸；自主性），这可能会让读者后续感到困惑。此外，我知道在流畅感研究中术语使用并不一致，但我认为读者会从您为论文建立标准中受益匪浅，即说明类似于“当游戏难度设置为高水平时，玩家被认为会体验到压力、挫败感或焦虑，而不是流畅感”。 在以下内容中，当我们描述流量实验的结果时，将相应的实验条件称为超负荷条件。请确保在120-527行中使用一致的术语。正如审稿人在104-128行中建议的那样，现在将讨论在实验室环境中实施的实验范式，并提供更详细的信息。本段还讨论了自我选择水平（自主性），并解释了沉浸感。作者在本段末尾的128-130行中为所报告的实验建立了标准术语。5. 我还希望看到一段关于流量测量的内容，以便尽早让读者了解在即将报告的研究中是如何评估流量的。在这段内容中，应提及ESM和流量问卷作为直接的、但回顾性的流量测量方法，以及双重任务方法和生理指标作为间接的、但不干扰的流量测量方法。在此阶段，还应明确指出使用回顾性自我报告评估状态的局限性，从而为神经或外周心理指标提供依据。因此，请从69-73行、103-108行和469-479行中形成一段新的关于流量测量的内容。我还希望看到更多关于流量问卷的参考文献（73行），理想情况下是在表1-4中添加相应的列。关于流量测量的必要信息、任务后回顾性问卷以及这些措施的局限性已在手稿的85-103行中一并讨论。我们还增加了更多关于所审查文章使用的流量问卷的参考文献，见90-96行。6. 51-64行需要更明确地标记为推测，或者需要提供更多关于“流量对精神症状有益性质”的证据。还应提供更清晰的解释，说明流量在临床环境中为何有益。否则，我建议完全删除这部分内容。在131-148行中，我们更详细地阐明了通过玩电子游戏诱导流量可以造福精神疾病患者的观点。7. 在110行中，您将本手稿称为此类综述的第一篇。然而，我知道至少有一篇类似的综述（Knierim, Rissler, Dorner, Maedche, & Weinhardt, 2018）。虽然我认为您的工作仍然提供了有价值的信息并进行了重要的更新，但其他综述（可能还有更多？）应被正确引用，并解释您文献综述的附加价值。我们感谢审稿人的评论。我们找到了两篇综述；然而，它们都不是专门针对玩电子游戏这一背景，也没有同时考虑生理和神经相关因素。例如，Knierim等人提供的系统文献综述仅涉及外周神经系统流量的指标，并未专门针对电子游戏。 之前的综述以及本手稿的附加价值已在第159-171行中详细讨论。实验设计我相信手稿正确引用了相关文献，并符合PeerJ所要求的方法论和伦理标准。然而，我认为改进小节的组织以及手稿的整体结构是必要的，以便给读者一个更清晰的主题概述。此外，为确保全面、无偏见的覆盖，我强烈建议修订方法论方法。请考虑我的建议以改进结果部分：

1. 关于收集有关视频游戏过程中外围生理和神经相关流的论文的方法，我强烈建议遵循PRISMA指南（http://prisma-statement.org，参见清单和流程图）。这也有助于读者评估研究选择策略。具体而言，所使用的关键词组合应明确（例如，‘neural OR correlates OR brain activity AND flow’），以及所有资格标准。我也不相信Google Scholar可以用来获得全面的概述，因此强烈鼓励进一步使用PubMed和Web of Science。也许更具体的关键词，涉及某些方法/指标和流，也有助于确保找到所有相关论文。仅举一例，根据我自己的文献研究，我可以列举出你们在文献综述中未包括的关于流和心理生理学的论文：Kivikangas (2006), Drachen et al. (2010), Gaggioli et al. (2013), Bastarache-Roberge et al. (2015), Colzato et al. (2018), Plotnikov et al. (2012), Peifer et al. (2014b), 和 Tozman et al. (2017)。我认为修订你们的文献综述是至关重要的，以确保不会因缺少某些相关论文而得出无效结论。

我们同意审稿人的意见，我们应该提供使用其他数据库（如Web of Science和PubMed）的详细选择程序描述。关于收集研究和纳入及排除标准（使用两个数据库）的方法信息已在第173-184行中更新。根据PeerJ期刊的学科特定标准，我们的综述手稿不是系统综述或元分析，而是范围综述或文献综述。系统综述报告必须包括PRISMA流程图和完整的PRISMA清单。然而，对于范围综述，只需有一个调查方法学部分，其中应解释如何确保对文献的全面和无偏见覆盖。审稿人提到的一些参考文献未包括在手稿中，因为它们不符合本研究的纳入标准。2. 虽然我发现将你的报告分为关于心流的外周生理和神经相关性的子节非常有帮助，但我认为这些子节本身需要更清晰地组织结构。我建议先从一段总结关于心流的理论假设及其相应测量方法的段落开始，就像你在神经子节第266-280行所做的那样。在神经子节中，你提到了低前额叶活动假设（第273-274行，第358-359行）以及同步理论（第275-280行）；然而，我建议在同一段落中也提及无努力注意（第568-571行）、巅峰表现（第130-131行，第378-380行）以及心流成分中的自我意识丧失、注意力集中和内在享受（请确保在此使用一致的术语，因为你有时也称后者为集中或内在奖励），因为它们也提供了关于心流潜在神经相关性的信息。这将帮助读者在了解实际结果之前理解哪些神经相关性是预期的。请注意，心流与巅峰表现之间的联系应在引言中提出并解释（！），最好是在你写到处理流畅性和最佳挑战时。目前，当它被用来解释某些结果时，显得有些突兀，这正是我所说的“阅读起来令人困惑”的一个好例子。根据审稿人的评论，关于心流现有理论假设和假设的总结段落已被添加到心流神经相关性部分（第376-403行）。我们提到了在玩视频游戏的背景下得到支持或未能得到支持的理论（包括短暂性低前额叶活动、注意和奖励网络的同步以及自我参照处理）。无努力注意作为理论假设在外周生理心流相关性中被讨论。我们认为巅峰表现不应作为假设背景提及，因为尚不清楚是心流影响表现还是反之。我们在引言（第75-84行）和讨论（第876-896行）中都讨论了心流与巅峰表现之间的关系。此外，研究根据每个理论和假设进行了分类。3. 同样，我也建议在呈现结果之前，单独扩展一段关于外周生理心流相关性的理论基础。请包括Peifer等人提出的倒U形假设（第181-184行，第539-544行），De Manzano等人将心流概念化为积极情感和高唤醒状态的观点（第160-162行； 你称之为无努力注意力，但据我所知，德·曼扎诺（De Manzano）谈论的是唤醒，而布鲁亚（Bruya，2010）谈论的是无努力注意力，这两者不应混淆），以及流动状态下副交感神经和交感神经共同激活的概念（乌伦，德·曼扎诺，西奥雷尔，& 哈马特，2010），在这一段中，以及简要提及无努力注意力和巅峰表现，因为这两者将在神经子节中再次出现。在此处还需评论关于流动和高唤醒/压力的假设（第124-127行），但请在开头明确澄清，这很可能高度依赖于活动情境。你在神经子节的第324行才提到任务依赖性，但它适用于所有心理生理学结果，应在开头就强调！在流动的外周生理相关部分（第185-214行）中添加了一段总结现有理论假设和关于流动的假设。我们提到了在玩视频游戏情境下得到支持或未得到支持的 theories（积极效价和高唤醒、交感神经和副交感神经的共同激活、无努力或努力注意力，以及流动与压力系统活动之间的倒U型关系）。此外，研究根据每个理论和假设进行了分类。关于德·曼扎诺等人2010年的研究，他们在研究中提到“流动被提议为一种无努力注意力的状态，这种状态通过积极情感和高注意力的相互作用而产生”。所以他们在研究中提到的内容，也被布鲁亚（2010）和乌伦等人（2010）提到。在理论假设部分，我们也简要提到了任务依赖性（第213-214行），这在讨论中会详细讨论。4. 除了更清晰地呈现理论外，我也希望更清晰地呈现指标本身。尽管PeerJ的读者很可能熟悉心理生理学指标，你在文献综述中呈现了从眼动追踪到tDCS的多种方法，所以读者可能并不了解所有这些方法。目前，你在呈现相应结果时解释了一些指标（例如，LF-HRV，第146-149行），但我希望看到对所有使用的测量方法都进行一致的解释（外周生理子节：HR和HRV、EMG、皮质醇、呼吸、EDA和眼动追踪；神经子节：fMRI、灌注MRI、fNIRS、tDCS和EEG）。请确保在介绍测量方法时（例如，皮质醇、HPA轴、压力、佩费尔的假设）回溯到理论段落，以便读者立即知道每个测量方法如何与流动体验相关联。 我建议单独撰写一个段落来介绍所有指标，并将其放置在理论段落之后、报告所有结果之前，或者在介绍每个指标的结果之前撰写一个简短的免责声明。由于研究是根据每个理论假设提及的，我们现在试图在呈现实际结果之前，对所有研究中使用的指标和测量方法进行简短说明。像EEG或fMRI这样的一些方法并不是指标，而是独立的技术，在本次综述中解释它们会导致冗余。为了避免这些冗余，我们只提及技术名称。5. 请重新考虑您报告结果的组织方式：您似乎是根据研究进行的先后顺序来组织研究的；然而，鉴于采用了许多不同的方法，我建议根据a)评估的指标或b)理论背景来组织。根据您选择的方式，另一种方式应用于在段落内形成子节（例如，如果您选择按指标进行，首先呈现该指标对例如无努力注意假设提供的所有证据，然后是对唤醒假设的证据，依此类推……或者反过来。但请在整个报告中保持这种结构。这一点至关重要，因为在第179-180行中，您从刚刚报告的结果中得出结论，而后来又指出其他结果与此结论相矛盾；然而，应在同一句子或至少在同一段落中明确结论是否有效，因为只浏览文本的读者可能会获取错误信息。）这也意味着某些研究可能会多次提及，因为它们包含不同的指标或假设——在这种情况下，第一次应详细解释方法，之后只需简要提及。为了清晰起见，对于读者来说，在一个单独的段落中获取关于某个指标或假设的所有信息会非常方便，而不是需要来回切换。同样，当您报告EEG结果时，我希望有不同段落/子节专门介绍每个频段的结果。我们同意审稿人的意见。现在所有研究都根据相应的理论背景进行了组织和提及。对于每个理论，我们描述了按该研究评估的指标分类的研究结果。同样，这种分类也适用于EEG研究，并将该领域的所有研究按频段分组和提及。6. 请仔细检查第120-527行，关于您报告研究方法的方式。这应始终包括游戏刺激的名称、实验设计/条件或声明该研究是相关性研究，以及理想情况下流量测量（或其代理指标）的名称或信息。 在进行此操作时，您也可以参考您的表格。如果未使用适当的流量条件或流量测量方法，应始终指出并简要讨论，以告知读者潜在的限制。在稿件中，现在提到了每项研究中使用的游戏名称、实验设计/条件以及所使用的流量测量方法。7. 我发现对于某些研究，您在将结果与假设联系起来方面做得非常好（例如，第312-314行，第430-436行），但请确实详细说明理论背景（例如，指出可以用来解释结果的流量成分）。此外，请确保对报告中提到的每项研究都以类似的方式进行处理。我非常喜欢您在第521-524行中呈现理论构建与生理结构之间联系的方式（将后者放在前者的括号内），所以也许可以更全面地使用这种方式。我们现在将研究结果与相应的理论背景联系起来。8. 我认为某些结果需要您更清晰的解释：关于流量和唤醒水平的矛盾结果（您有时也称之为紧张或压力——再次请使用更一致的术语；第192-199行）；LF-HRV的含义（第146-147行，第563-564行；您没有提到大量证据表明这可能并不是交感副交感平衡的直接指标，除了讨论中的一句话！例如，Reyes del Paso, Langewitz, Mulder, Van Roon, & Duschek, 2013）；流量条件/测量代理及其局限性，见上文（请在此处非常小心措辞，例如第386行可能会被误解为您确认高性能可以作为用问卷测量流量的代理）。现在在讨论部分对每个理论进行了更详细的解释和讨论。关于流量和唤醒的矛盾结果在第693-730行进行了讨论。我们还在第741-750行讨论了HRV测量在评估心理努力中的使用。在任务依赖性部分，我们讨论了技能-挑战平衡的操作化以及所使用的流量测量方法和不同研究范式的局限性。9. 沉浸感这一概念在某些研究的报告中被提及（第150行，第400-402行），但从未明确界定（且没有引用），并与流量进行对比。我认为这一概念在虚拟现实和游戏研究中仍然比流量更为突出，因此我希望在引言中实际上能看到一个专门讨论它及其与流量关系的段落。这将帮助游戏研究人员与您的论文建立联系，并使一般读者理解区分流量和沉浸感条件的研究。关于沉浸感，我们现在在第120-124行解释了沉浸感以及自主性。 有研究表明，沉浸与流畅状态在结构上存在差异，导致不同的心理现象（Nacke等人，2008，2011），然而，Michailidis等人（2018）认为，需要更多证据来证明它们的分离是合理的。基于这一事实，我们更倾向于关注视频游戏中的流畅体验。

关于研究发现的效度，我认为这篇文献综述得出的结论是经过充分发展和支持的。我只有一些小的建议来澄清讨论的部分：

1. 我建议根据将在理论段落中预先概述的主要假设，重新命名和调整讨论部分的子节：唤醒、无努力注意力、前额叶功能低下、内在享受和自我意识的丧失。这可能需要对结构进行一些调整，例如无努力注意力涉及你对心理努力（从第536行开始）和注意力控制（从第595行开始）的发现讨论。我相信这将帮助读者评估部分相互矛盾的发现。我们根据流畅体验中涉及的子功能重新调整了讨论部分，这些子功能是从现有的理论背景和实证研究中推断出来的。这些子功能在689-829行中概述和讨论为：1）积极效价和高唤醒状态，2）专注注意力的愉悦状态，3）注意力和奖励网络的同步激活，4）自动化，以及5）自我意识的丧失。

2. 我希望看到关于方法论结论的额外简短子节：在第551-559行、679-681行、639-656行和668-691行中，你很好地讨论了这一研究领域中某些方法的局限性和应用。我认为这些是未来研究非常重要的带回家信息，因此应该通过在讨论中专门用一个段落来扩展和强调这些考虑。此外，请更明确地提出对未来研究的建议。由于任务依赖性似乎在这一研究线中扮演重要角色，因此应详细讨论。不同的方法论问题现在在讨论的“任务依赖性”部分（第830-862行）中被讨论，作为文献中不一致结果的可能原因。在接下来的子节“剩余问题及未来研究考虑”（第863-896行）中，我们讨论了为区分流畅的内在体验和增强这种体验的外部条件可能采取的措施。在这一部分，为未来研究提出了建议。

3. 同样，我从迄今为止的研究中得出的一个主要结论是你在第580-583行中与任务依赖性相关的内容。我认为这值得单独用一个段落来阐述，因为它影响了未来研究可以被视为切实研究目标的内容。 我也希望看到更多讨论：这对心理生理流动性和游戏研究意味着什么？如果可能并不存在一种心理生理标准模式来描述流动性，为什么还要用心理生理方法研究流动性？在彻底否定寻找标准流动性模式的可能性之前，你可能还想考虑Knierim等人得出的结论，即只有副交感神经和交感神经系统的共同激活可能作为流动性体验的客观指标，或者提出你自己的类似结论。我们在第830-862行讨论了任务依赖性。我们认为，尽管一些研究的结果不一致，但仍然可以建立流动性与我们总结的五个认知和生理子功能之间的关联，包括积极效价和高度唤醒、愉悦的专注状态、注意力和奖励网络的同步、自动化以及自我意识的丧失。4. 我觉得有时需要更清楚地区分流动性和沉浸感。在第590-594行，你将其与自动化联系起来讨论，在第664-670行间接地与注意力联系起来讨论。然而，我认为需要向读者澄清，高度自动化（为了保持一致性，我称之为无努力注意力）在次优挑战条件下通过过度学习的任务也能实现。同样，如果一个人有动机并有意专注于手头的任务，即使在高挑战下，注意力集中度也可以很高。在讨论相应结果时应考虑这一点。例如，这在多大程度上代表了双任务设计的潜在局限性？我也希望看到一般性的讨论，也许与沉浸感相关：我们能否根据潜在的生理模式区分流动性和沉浸感？在这篇手稿中，我们回顾了在游戏背景下研究流动性体验的生理和神经现象的研究。在引言部分，我们指出，任务重要性和人格特征等额外因素会影响技能-挑战平衡与流动性之间的关系。然而，我们认为，回顾研究调节流动性体验水平因素的行为研究不在本综述的范围内，应在一个完全独立的综述中进行研究。关于沉浸感，已有研究表明，沉浸感在结构上与流动性存在细微差异，导致不同的心理现象（Nacke等人，2008年，2011年），但Michailidis等人（2018年）认为，需要更多证据来证明它们的分离。基于这一事实，我们更倾向于关注视频游戏中的流动性体验。5. 将性能作为衡量心流的间接指标的有用性，在第670-679行中讨论的，应更明确地标记为推测。理想情况下，我也希望看到更多关于性能与心流之间关系的参考文献，特别是在电脑游戏领域。请记住，最直接的结论仍然是，对于较简单的任务，性能会更好，而心流则需要具有挑战性的任务。心流与巅峰性能相关这一看似矛盾的观点需要得到恰当的解释（也已在引言中提及，见上文）。我们在第876-896行中更详细地讨论了性能与心流之间的关系及其考虑因素。6. 我认为第582-583行中呈现的结论需要澄清。我发现“在一定程度上”这一措辞非常模糊，缺乏进一步的解释。在第733-750行中讨论了心流和心智努力期间ANS活动模式的差异。“在一定程度上”这一措辞已被删除。7. 一个小的观察，但请不要将心流称为一种感觉（第664行），而应一致地将其称为一种体验或状态。已进行修正。

2. 关于您的表格，我想知道为什么在给出样本大小后的m/f以表示样本的性别分布时，有时使用括号，有时不使用。如果没有理由这样做，我更倾向于使用更一致的风格。我们现在已更新表格，使用更一致的风格。
3. 同样，在您的表格中，有时用空白或破折号（实际上是两个破折号——也许可以改为一个更长的破折号）表示缺失信息。请保持风格一致。我们现在已更新表格，使用更一致的风格。

reasons: Ideally, I would also appreciate more references on the relationship between performance and flow, specifically in the field of computer gaming.
I commend the authors for giving an overview over the literature on peripheral-physiological and neural correlates of flow during video gaming.
I believe that psychophysiological methods represent a promising approach to both research on flow experiences in particular and on gaming experiences in general.

Considering the various possible applications of flow research in health-related areas and the focus on psychophysiological methodology, I further believe that this article will be of high interest for PeerJ’s readers.

When giving the definition of flow, processing fluency is not mentioned; however, apart from attentional absorption and intrinsic enjoyment, processing fluency should be considered a key dimension of flow (Csikszentmihalyi, 1975), from which many psycho- and neuropsychological hypotheses can be deduced.

the meaning of LF-HRV (lines 146-147, 563-564; you do not bring up the substantial evidence that this may not be a direct indicator of sympathovagal balance after all except for one sentence in the discussion!
for instance line 386 could be misunderstood as you confirming that high performance works as a proxy for measuring flow with a questionnaire).
Please note that in line 582 it says Peifer (2012); I believe it should be Peifer (2014).
In regard to your tables, I was wondering why you sometimes use parenthesis when giving the m/f behind the sample size to indicate the sample’s gender distribution and sometimes you do not.
Similarly, in your tables you sometimes indicate missing information with a blank space or with a dash (two dashes actually – maybe make it one longer one instead).
When you summarize conditions under design, you sometimes use capital letters in the beginning and sometimes not.
You use both ‘and’ and ‘&’ in your tables, but sometimes the ‘&’ is placed in the beginning of a new line.
When giving the time frame under design, you sometimes write out ‘x minutes gameplay’ and sometimes just ‘x minutes’; please use a consistent style.
At times, there seem to be free lines or broader spacing in your tables; please stick to one line spacing throughout all tables. \
but I am fairly certain that when giving time frames hyphens and ‘long’ are not used (e.g., ‘2 min’ or ‘2 minutes’ instead of ‘2-min-long’).
When listing more than two measures, a comma should be used before the ‘and’. Again, revise your tables accordingly, please.
In the table note for Table 1, I would like you to add explanations for the abbreviations fMRI, fNIRS, and NIRS since they appear in this table.
In the table note for Table 2, you do not give explanations for the abbreviations fMRI, fNIRS, ECG, EDA, NIRS, PET, and tDCS.
In the table note for Table 3, an explanation for the abbreviations EEG is missing.
In Table 3, there is a spelling mistake for ‘seconds’ when Wolf et al.’s study is presented.

In Table 4, you start using a ‘+’ to add the dual task; I think it is a bit unfortunate to use a mathematical sign in a non-mathematical way, so maybe just stick to either using ‘and’ or ‘&’ (but consistently please, also in regard to the other tables).
The table note for Table 4 is missing
One more minor observation: the font changes in Table 4 when Huskey et al.’s game is described.
However, I would like to see a major revision of the manuscript’s structure before publication as I found it at times confusing to read and hard to grasp the main information from the text.
However, I believe improving the organization of subsections and of the overall structure of the manuscript is necessary to give the reader a clearer overview of the topic.
Please consider my recommendations to improve the results section:

Please also reconsider the organization of your report of results: You seem to organize the studies according to when they were conducted; however, given the many different methodologies employed, I would recommend to organize them according to a) the indicators assessed or b) the theoretical background.
Similarly, I would recommend expanding on the theoretical background of peripheral-physiological flow correlates in a separate paragraph before presenting results.

I would suggest that you rename and restructure the subsection of your discussion according to the main hypothesis that will now be outlined in the theory paragraphs beforehand: arousal, effortless attention, hypofrontality, intrinsic enjoyment, and loss of self-awareness.
