paper_title: Understanding floral biology for CRISPR-based modification of color and fragrance in horticultural plants
paper_abstract: The global market of a total 42.4 billion US dollars of ornamental plants owes its worth to the color and fragrance associated with these plants. A lot of work has been done to understand the physiological, biochemical, genetic, and environmental factors responsible for the development of color and fragrance in flowers. The aim of these studies about the floral biology was to achieve the desired characters by manipulating all these factors to fulfill the changing demand of the global market. While, modifying flower color and fragrance, scientists moved from the traditional breeding methods to the comparatively modern genetic engineering techniques, yet limitations in results always remained a big issue for researchers. However, genome editing tools look promising to achieve the desired level of efficiency to modify the color and fragrance in the flowers. This review gives insight into the significance of floral characters, molecular factors responsible for these characters and applications of modern genome editing technologies for desirable modification.
review_content:
It is a very interesting review regarding the "Understanding floral biology for CRISPR-based modification of color and fragrance in horticultural plants". Authors has compiled all the previous research in a very good manner. However there are suggestions to improve this review for readers interest.
  * It is suggested to improve the Figure 1a to 4, all abbreviations should be mentioned in the figure.
  * The authors did not mention figure 1a-d in the text and there is no proper information about these figure in the manuscript.
  * Author need to redraw all figures.
  * Figure 1b shows some arrows, but there is no description below.
  * Some words are broken in the boxes in all figures which seems not good.
  * The authors should also give some information about the new genes which are important in different crops but are ignored regarding floral biology and future work should be carried out to improve the crop performance or resistance against changing climate conditions.
  * Author also suggested to add some studies regarding suppression of volatile compound for the control of some destructive pests during flowering or fruit maturation period in horticulture crops as well as color base transformation to other fruits or vegetables.
paper_title_zh: 理解花卉生物学以实现基于CRISPR的花色和香气改良在园艺植物中的应用
paper_abstract_zh: 全球观赏植物市场总额达424亿美元，其价值源于这些植物所具有的颜色和香气。为了理解影响花色和花香形成的生理、生化、遗传和环境因素，已经进行了大量研究。这些关于花卉生物学的研究旨在通过操纵这些因素来实现所需的特性，以满足全球市场的不断变化需求。在改良花色和花香的过程中，科学家们从传统的育种方法转向了相对现代的基因工程技术，但结果上的局限性一直是研究人员面临的一大问题。然而，基因组编辑工具在实现所需的花色和花香改良效率方面显示出良好前景。本综述深入探讨了花卉特性的重要性、决定这些特性的分子因素以及现代基因组编辑技术在理想改良中的应用。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇关于“理解花卉生物学以进行基于CRISPR的颜色和香味修饰在园艺植物中”的非常有趣的综述。作者以非常好的方式汇编了所有先前的研究。然而，为了提高读者的兴趣，有一些改进建议。
  * 建议改进图1a至4，所有缩写应在图中注明。
  * 作者在文本中未提及图1a-d，且手稿中关于这些图的信息不完整。
  * 作者需要重新绘制所有图表。
  * 图1b显示了一些箭头，但下方没有描述。
  * 所有图中的框内有些单词断裂，看起来不太好。
  * 作者还应提供一些关于新基因的信息，这些基因在不同作物中很重要，但在花卉生物学中被忽略，未来的工作应开展以提高作物性能或抵抗气候变化的能力。
  * 作者还建议添加一些关于在园艺作物开花或果实成熟期间抑制挥发性化合物以控制一些破坏性害虫的研究，以及基于颜色的转化应用于其他水果或蔬菜的研究。

paper_title: Mitochondrial DNA in human identification: a review
paper_abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) presents several characteristics useful for forensic studies, especially related to the lack of recombination, to a high copy number, and to matrilineal inheritance. mtDNA typing based on sequences of the control region or full genomic sequences analysis is used to analyze a variety of forensic samples such as old bones, teeth and hair, as well as other biological samples where the DNA content is low.
review_content: Reviewer 2 Comments for the author: The authors have reviewed the text with all the corrections that were made to them. But they should check: line 187. Regarding the nomenclature there are some errors. In the case of deletions, "del" is also accepted in addition to DEL or -. In addition N implies that the 4 bases appear and not that it is unambiguous. The authors should review that paragraph. Authors information to the Editor: As can be confirmed from line 184 to 188 we “del” was introduced. Regarding to N we introduce new and correct information “When any of the four bases are observed, N notation should be used”. line 348. The exclusion rules indicated do not correspond to the article by Parson et al., 2014. Indicate the correct reference. Authors information to the Editor: As can be confirmed from line 343 to 346 we present the rule generally accepted for all official forensic laboratories, although not published in any paper: “When the sequences are unequivocally different, the conclusion is that they can be excluded as being originated from the same source. Although not stated in any research paper or guideline text, forensic routine laboratories tend to accept as an exclusion scenario when more than two nucleotide differences exist between the two sequences” References. Please change the Rios reference. The corresponding reference to Rios et al. (2010) is: Identification process in mass graves from the Spanish Civil War I. Ríos L, Ovejero JI, Prieto JP. Forensic Sci Int. 2010 Jun 15;199(1-3):e27-36. doi: 10.1016/j.forsciint.2010.02.023. Authors information to the Editor: Since it was a mistake we replace for the correct reference. Additional information for both Reviewers Our inicial version compreends 3 figures: Figure 1 (a representation of the human mitochondrial molecule, adapted from Shokolenko et al., 2014); Figure 2 (the Phylogenetic Tree of global human mitochondrial DNA variation, available at http://www.phylotree.org/tree/index.htm); Figure 3 (a representation of geographical origin of mtDNA haplogroups, adapted from Kivisild et al., 2015) 1. Taking into account that PeerJ gave us the information on the necessity to require permissions from the original copyright owners of the figures we submit in our inicial version. 2. Taking into account that PeerJ inform us that the mentioned permissions aren’t mandatory if presented figures were from Open Acess papers; 3. Taking into account that the image we inicialy present as Figure 2, as mentioned by us at the manuscript, is directlly availlable at http://www.phylotree.org/tree/index.htm; We consider appropriate: 1. Eliminate the image we inicialy present as Figure 2, since it’s directlly availlable at http://www.phylotree.org/tree/index.htm 2. Change our inicial Figure 1 (available at Shokolenko et al., 2014) from an equivalent image available at an Open Acess paper. So, we change our inicial Figure 1 from present Figure 1 available at the Open Acess paper from Picard et al., 2016 (Picard, Wallace, & Burelle, 2016), now supplied as a confidential supplemental file. 3. Change our inicial Figure 3 (at this version Figure 2) from an equivalent image built by us based on information from page 20 of Lott et al., 2014 (Lott et al., 2014), now supplied as a confidential supplemental file.
paper_title_zh: 人类识别中的线粒体DNA：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 线粒体DNA（mtDNA）具有几个对法医学研究有用的特性，尤其是与其缺乏重组、高拷贝数以及母系遗传相关。基于控制区序列或全基因组序列分析的mtDNA分型被用于分析各种法医学样本，如古老骨骼、牙齿和头发，以及其他DNA含量低的生物样本。
review_content_zh: 审稿人2对作者的评论：作者已根据所有修改意见对文本进行了审查。但他们应检查：第187行。关于命名法存在一些错误。在删除的情况下，除了DEL或-之外，“del”也是可接受的。此外，N表示4个碱基都出现，而不是表示不明确。作者应审查该段落。作者给编辑的信息：从第184行到第188行可以确认，我们引入了“del”。关于N，我们引入了新的正确信息：“当观察到四个碱基中的任何一个时，应使用N表示法”。第348行。所列的排除规则与Parson等人2014年的文章不符。请指出正确的参考文献。作者给编辑的信息：从第343行到第346行可以确认，我们提出了所有官方法医实验室普遍接受的规则，尽管未在任何论文中发表：“当序列明确不同时，结论是它们可以排除来自同一来源。尽管在任何研究论文或指南文本中未提及，法医常规实验室倾向于将两个序列之间存在两个以上核苷酸差异的情况视为排除场景”。参考文献。请更改Rios的参考文献。Rios等人（2010）的相应参考文献是：西班牙内战大规模墓地识别过程I。Ríos L, Ovejero JI, Prieto JP. 法医科学国际。2010年6月15日；199(1-3):e27-36。doi: 10.1016/j.forsciint.2010.02.023。作者给编辑的信息：由于是错误，我们替换为正确的参考文献。给两位审稿人的额外信息：我们的初始版本包含3个图：图1（人类线粒体分子的表示，改编自Shokolenko等人，2014年）；图2（全球人类线粒体DNA变异的系统发育树，可在http://www.phylotree.org/tree/index.htm获取）；图3（线粒体单倍群地理起源的表示，改编自Kivisild等人，2015年）。1. 考虑到PeerJ向我们提供了需要从我们初始版本提交的图的原版权所有者处获取许可的信息。2. 考虑到PeerJ告知我们，如果所提交的图来自开放获取论文，则这些许可不是必须的；3. 考虑到我们初始作为图2呈现的图像，如我们在手稿中所述，可直接在http://www.phylotree.org/tree/index.htm获取；我们认为适当：1. 删除我们初始作为图2呈现的图像，因为它可直接在http://www.phylotree.org/tree/index.htm获取。2. 将我们初始的图1（来自Shokolenko等人，2014年）更换为来自开放获取论文的等效图像。因此，我们将初始的图1更换为来自Picard等人2016年开放获取论文（Picard, Wallace, & Burelle, 2016）的图1，现作为保密补充文件提供。3. 将我们初始的图3（在此版本中为图2）更换为基于Lott等人2014年（Lott等人，2014年）第20页信息构建的等效图像，现作为保密补充文件提供。

paper_title: A Review of the Applications of Deep Learning-Based Emergent Communication
paper_abstract: Emergent communication, or emergent language, is the field of research which studies how human language-like communication systems emerge de novo in deep multi-agent reinforcement learning environments. The possibilities of replicating the emergence of a complex behavior like language have strong intuitive appeal, yet it is necessary to complement this with clear notions of how such research can be applicable to other fields of science, technology, and engineering. This paper comprehensively reviews the applications of emergent communication research across machine learning, natural language processing, linguistics, and cognitive science. Each application is illustrated with a description of its scope, an explication of emergent communication's unique role in addressing it, a summary of the extant literature working towards the application, and brief recommendations for near-term research directions.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This review paper offers a survey of the field of deep learning-based emergent communication or emergent language, where neural network agents are trained to communicate with each other in simulated multi-agent environments, and the resulting communication protocols are then used, either as a testbed for cognitive or linguistic questions around language emergence and use, or more directly for downstream NLP tasks. The authors categorize this work into three sections: first, basic advances in improving the quality and capabilities of EC systems; second, the use of EC for downstream tasks relevant for NLP and ML; and finally, the use of EC to answer scientific questions on the origin and use of language in humans. The authors outline much of the current state-of-the-art in the area, and in each section conclude with outstanding challenges for the field.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
# Strengths - This paper is quite comprehensive and up-to-date. It could be a very useful reference for readers looking for relevant papers on EC. - Clear thought and care was put into organizing the paper across different applications (sections 2, 3, and 4), as well as presenting the current SoTA and missing work in each section (with the description/applicability/current state/next steps) framework. As a result, the paper is systematic and relatively easy to read.

**Requested Changes:**
# Too many walls of text; more figures and examples throughout. My main concern is that the paper could include more concrete examples and figures in many sections. There are basically no figures or examples between the first and last sections of the paper. Most of the intermediate sections are just “walls of text” with many citations and a cursory description of certain papers. This is bad for readability, but the lack of examples also means that a reader might not be able to understand how these papers work in detail, and hence understand what might be missing from the current SoTA. For example, “metrics for compositionality” (2.1) is one of the most important aspects in current EC research, but most metrics are described relatively briefly and none are explained in detail. Understanding the metrics more clearly will help the reader understand what the current limitations are of the metrics. It would be very clear upon understanding metrics, such as topographic similarity (a very common one), that there are clear limitations of current measures of compositionality—perhaps authors would then be able to make a more precise recommendation as to what is missing from the current set of metrics, rather than “we do not present any general recommendations.” I believe such section should also cite papers that reveal no clear link between current measures of compositionality and task performance, which helps the reader understand the current state of metrics for the field (https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.407/) Another example, “theoretical models” (2.3): it’s hard to understand what a concrete “theoretical model” looks like from just reading section 2.3. A concrete toy example of a theoretical model, either crafted by the authors, or simply taken from an existing paper, would go a long way in understanding this section. # Vague next steps I think as a result of the relatively cursory description of these sections, a lot of the sections end with “There are no general ‘next steps’ here.” I’m not sure how accurate this is—I think by more clearly describing the various sections and their limitations, it would be clearer what the next steps are for the field as a whole. For example in 2.1 “rederiving natural language”: authors state that next steps could include “identifying the most salient properties of human language and using these to develop a concrete problem definition of “rederiving human language.” Linguistics would be the primary resource for identifying such properties from a theoretical standpoint.” But not much more is said. While obviously the critical components of human language, and the specific aspects of such an agenda, are up for debate, the authors could better summarize what aspects are currently missing from the current EC literature if we were to propose a “rederiving human language” thrust (e.g. model scale, population size, embodiment, task realism, any linguistic constraints, etc) # Currently presumes familiarity with EC Related to the above discussion on how there are insufficient examples throughout, this also translates into the introduction, where I believe the paper wouldn’t be easily understandable to someone without existing familiarity with EC. The paper could set up a basic EC-style setup before going deep into applications/goals of sections 2, 3, and 4. Sketching what a typical EC setup looks like in Section 1 (perhaps around when the typical/necessary components of EC are sketched out) would be enormously helpful in situating the reader. For example consider Figure 3 in Lazaridou and Baroni (2020) which outlines a basic EC setup. # Should make a clearer distinction from other reviews of EC For example, the distinction between the Lazaridou and Baroni (2020) paper in Section 1.2 is a bit unclear. Lazaridou and Baroni is quoted as “presenting a much broader view of emergent language”, while this review is focused on “the goals and applications of emergent language research.”. This is a bit unclear to me—I would say the Lazaridou and Baroni paper is certainly interested in the goals/applications of emergent language research. It’s also possible that this review itself is broader/more up-to-date since it’s longer and has been released more recently. But I think any clarification of differences between this paper and others would be valuable (why do we need both?) # Section 4 specific: differences between non-deep-RL approaches (This is not as crucial of a blocker/recommendation, but something to consider) Computer simulations have been used for a very long time to try to simulate and understand certain properties of language use and emergence. I think the authors are aware of this—each individual subsection in Section 4 describes why deep learning might particularly be useful for understand e.g. language acquisition (since it’s currently the most “realistic” simulation we can set up)—but the overall effect is that the main reason(s) why practitioners might reach for DL tools when answering linguistic questions is buried/weaved throughout the various sections here. I would consider adding a specific section to Section 4 that explicitly describes why one might use DL methods to answer these linguistic questions. There are clear benefits, but also clear weaknesses (despite our best efforts, agents training in simulation don’t acquire anything close to human languages, and there are many outstanding artificialities in our current training paradigm). A centralized place to discuss the benefits/weaknesses of DL, and how DL fills in gaps left by the pre-deep-RL literature, would make Section 4 clearer. # Summary In summary I believe there was clearly a lot of effort put into this paper, and I believe it could make a useful contribution to the literature, but I would say it is not quite ready for publication just yet. The main blocker of my recommendation is that the middle is some ~20 continuous pages of text, and even after reading all of the text I don’t think the reader has the clearest sense of the work in some sections, due to a lack of figures or more concrete examples/explanations of some of the phenomena described in the text (e.g. lack of concrete discussion of metrics for emergent languages and their weaknesses, or key “results” figures from relevant papers in sections 3 and 4). Therefore, to secure my recommendation, I would likely want - (**most crucial**) Improvements in writing and paper structure in the main body of the text, with additional figures + examples, and more pointed explanations for what is lacking from current research; - (**nice to have**) some additional pedagogical context for new readers, - (**nice to have**) more context as to why we need this specific review of the EC literature, and not existing reviews (most notably Lazaridou & Baroni 2020, which is the closest paper to this one). # Other minor suggestions - I prefer “emergent communication” over “emergent language”—emergent language is the thing being studied but I find “emergent communication” to more commonly refer to the subfield itself - I think the de novo point in the abstract can be misleading since not all EC work studies emergence from scratch; there is plenty of work that uses EC-based techniques to augment existing systems trained with human languages, e.g. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13344 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04499, much of which the authors cite - I find “intermediate applications” a bit of a confusing word, since it’s not clear what the reference class is when saying something is “intermediate.” Case in point, the authors themselves claim that “Intermediate applications are not what we would typically consider applications at all.” It seems like a more appropriate term is something like basic/intrinsic advances in EC. I would consider rewording this (though I don’t feel very strongly either way) - page 6: “No work in the current body of literature has explicitly pursued the rederivation of human language.” It’s worth clarifying in this sentence why this is (ie that the full “rederivation of human language” is an extremely ambitious goal with too many moving pieces) - section 3.1 applicability: “Emergent language serves as a way to generate synthetic language data which more closely mimics the natural variation found in human language.” Is this true, given that existing studies show that such synthetic languages often look drastically different from human languages?

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Reply (2/2): ## Re: Section 4 specific: differences between non-deep-RL approaches > I would consider adding a specific section to Section 4 that explicitly > describes why one might use DL methods to answer these linguistic questions. > There are clear benefits, but also clear weaknesses (despite our best > efforts, agents training in simulation don’t acquire anything close to human > languages, and there are many outstanding artificialities in our current > training paradigm). A centralized place to discuss the benefits/weaknesses of > DL, and how DL fills in gaps left by the pre-deep-RL literature, would make > Section 4 clearer. This what we attempted (perhaps unsuccessfully) to do in Sec 4.1 ("General paradigm of knowledge-driven applications"). __Would you suggest that this section needs to elaborate further on the pros and cons DL or that DL itself, apart from EC, should be expanded upon in its own section?__ ## Re: Summary > key "results" figures from relevant papers in sections 3 and 4 __We are not quite sure what the "key 'results' figures" refers to. Could you give some specific examples?__ ## Re: Other minor suggestions > I prefer “emergent communication” over “emergent language”—emergent language > is the thing being studied but I find “emergent communication” to more > commonly refer to the subfield itself We are similarly aware that the field tends to favor "emergent communication" over "emergent language", so we are flexible on this point. Our particular rationale for using "emergent language" is that it emphasizes the type of communication that pursued in the discipline. > I think the de novo point in the abstract can be misleading since not all EC > work studies emergence from scratch; there is plenty of work that uses > EC-based techniques to augment existing systems trained with human languages, > e.g. https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13344 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04499, > much of which the authors cite While not every EC approach strictly studies "de novo" emergence, we believe it best characterizes the field of EC as a whole, distinguishing it from other areas of research like modelling historical language change directly from data, using RL and self-play to tune dialog agents, or studying emergent linguistic features in large language models. We are happy to loosen this definition. > I find “intermediate applications” a bit of a confusing word ... In light of this and other reviewers' comments, we will change the wording to something more straightforward. > section 3.1 applicability: “Emergent language serves as a way to generate > synthetic language data which more closely mimics the natural variation found > in human language.” Is this true, given that existing studies show that such > synthetic languages often look drastically different from human languages? We can edit sentence to emphasize the fact that EL is a _potential_ way to generate synthetic data, given appropriate design choices that push its structure towards that of human languages. Again, we thank your for your insightful and informed review! | Reply (1/2): Clarification questions for the reviewer are __bolded__ below. ## Re: Too many walls of text; more figures and examples throughout. > My main concern is that the paper could include more concrete examples and > figures in many sections. There are basically no figures or examples between > the first and last sections of the paper. Most of the intermediate sections are > just “walls of text” with many citations and a cursory description of certain > papers. This is bad for readability, but the lack of examples also means that > a reader might not be able to understand how these papers work in detail, and > hence understand what might be missing from the current SoTA. We acknowledge the paper will be more readable once we add: 1. More concrete examples 2. More illustrations We feel that the many references are necessary--this is a review paper--but we agree that adding more concrete detail about and illustration of SotA approaches would greatly strengthen the paper. We can definitely address this weakness and will make it a top priority. > For example, "metrics for compositionality" (2.1) is one of the most > important aspects in current EC research, but most metrics are described > relatively briefly and none are explained in detail. We could expand this section, although it is already one of the longest sections in the paper. One way to address this, then could to be explain a couple of the most salient metrics (like topographic similarity for compositionality) without giving a full explanation of every single metric. __Would you find this approach to be acceptable?__ > I believe such section should also cite papers that reveal no clear link > between current measures of compositionality and task performance, which > helps the reader understand the current state of metrics for the field > (https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.407/) Thank you for this suggestion. We will add this paper to this section. > Another example, “theoretical models” (2.3) ... A concrete toy example of > a theoretical model [should be added]. We have two examples in mind and will add one. ## Re: Vague next steps > I think as a result of the relatively cursory description of these sections, > a lot of the sections end with “There are no general ‘next steps’ here.” ... We will replace these vague "Next steps" sections with more specific recommendations. > For example in 2.1 "rederiving natural language" ... the authors could better > summarize what aspects are currently missing from the current EC literature > if we were to propose a “rederiving human language” thrust (e.g. model > scale, population size, embodiment, task realism, any linguistic constraints, > etc) We will also specifically address this concern. ## Re: Currently presumes familiarity with EC > Related to the above discussion on how there are insufficient examples > throughout, ... The paper could set up a basic EC-style setup ... Sketching > what a typical EC setup looks like in Section 1 We will add this as well. ## Re: Should make a clearer distinction from other reviews of EC > For example, the distinction between the Lazaridou and Baroni (2020) paper in > Section 1.2 is a bit unclear. ... I think any clarification of differences > between this paper and others would be valuable (why do we need both?) While Lazaridou & Baroni (2020) do briefly mention some of the goals of emergent communication, they do so as one small part of many facets of emergent language. This paper intends to give a detailed, systematic, and comprehensive review of the goals specifically and not the other facets of emergent language. While the former paper might spend 1-2 pages explicating the goals of emergent communication, the whole of this paper is dedicated to it. We will express this more clearly in the paper.
paper_title_zh: 基于深度学习的涌现通信应用综述
paper_abstract_zh: 涌现式通信，或称涌现式语言，是研究在深度多智能体强化学习环境中如何从头开始出现类似人类语言的通信系统的研究领域。复制如语言般复杂行为的涌现可能性具有强烈的直观吸引力，然而，有必要明确这种研究如何适用于科学、技术和工程的其他领域。本文全面回顾了涌现式通信研究在机器学习、自然语言处理、语言学和认知科学中的应用。每个应用都通过描述其范围、阐明涌现式通信在解决该应用中的独特作用、总结现有文献中对应用的研究进展，以及简要提出近期研究方向的建议来进行说明。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
这篇综述论文对基于深度学习的涌现通信或涌现语言领域进行了调研，其中神经网络代理在模拟的多代理环境中被训练相互通信，所形成的通信协议随后被用于认知或语言问题的测试平台，围绕语言的涌现和使用，或者更直接地用于下游自然语言处理任务。作者将这项工作分为三个部分：首先，改进EC系统质量和能力的基本进展；其次，EC在自然语言处理和机器学习相关下游任务中的应用；最后，使用EC回答关于人类语言起源和使用的科学问题。作者概述了该领域当前许多最先进的研究，并在每个部分结束时总结了该领域面临的突出挑战。

**优点和缺点：**
# 优点 - 这篇论文非常全面且更新及时。对于寻找EC相关论文的读者来说，它可能是一个非常实用的参考。 - 论文的组织清晰且用心，涵盖了不同的应用（第2、3和4节），并呈现了当前最先进的研究和每个部分缺失的工作（包括描述/适用性/当前状态/下一步框架）。因此，论文系统性强，相对易于阅读。

**请求的更改：**
# 文本段落过多；应在全文中增加更多图表和示例。我主要担心的是，论文在许多部分可以包含更多具体的示例和图表。在论文的第一部分和最后一部分之间基本上没有图表或示例。大多数中间部分仅仅是“文本墙”，包含许多引用和对某些论文的简要描述。这不仅影响可读性，而且缺乏示例也意味着读者可能无法详细了解这些论文的工作原理，从而无法理解当前最先进研究可能存在的不足。例如，“组合性指标”（2.1）是当前EC研究中最重要的一方面，但大多数指标描述相对简略，且没有详细解释。更清晰地理解这些指标将帮助读者了解这些指标的当前局限性。 在理解如地形相似性（一个非常常见的指标）等指标后，当前组合性度量方法的明显局限性将变得非常清晰——或许作者们届时能够更精确地推荐当前指标集中缺失的内容，而不是“我们不提出任何普遍性建议”。我认为该部分还应引用那些揭示当前组合性度量方法与任务性能之间无明显关联的论文，这有助于读者理解该领域当前指标的状况（https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.407/）。另一个例子，“理论模型”（2.3）：仅通过阅读2.3节很难理解一个具体的“理论模型”是什么样的。一个具体的理论模型示例，无论是作者自己构建的，还是直接取自现有论文的，都将大大有助于理解这一部分。

# 模糊的后续步骤
我认为由于对这些部分的描述相对粗略，许多部分以“这里没有普遍的‘后续步骤’”结尾。我不确定这是否准确——我认为通过更清晰地描述各个部分及其局限性，整个领域的后续步骤将变得更加清晰。例如在2.1“重新推导自然语言”中：作者指出后续步骤可能包括“识别人类语言最显著的特征，并利用这些特征来制定一个具体的‘重新推导人类语言’的问题定义”。语言学将是理论上识别这些特征的主要资源。”但并未多言。尽管人类语言的关键组成部分以及此类议程的具体方面尚有争议，但作者可以更好地总结当前EC文献中缺失的方面，如果我们提出一个“重新推导人类语言”的推动力（例如模型规模、种群大小、具身性、任务真实性、任何语言学约束等）。

# 目前预设了对EC的熟悉度
与上述关于全文示例不足的讨论相关，这也体现在引言中，我认为如果没有对EC的现有熟悉度，该论文对读者来说并不容易理解。论文可以在深入探讨2、3和4节的应用/目标之前，先设置一个基本的EC式框架。在第1节中勾勒出一个典型的EC设置（或许在概述EC的典型/必要组成部分时）将极大地帮助读者定位。例如参考Lazaridou和Baroni（2020）中的图3，它概述了一个基本的EC设置。

# 应更清晰地与其他EC综述区分开来
例如，第1.2节中与Lazaridou和Baroni（2020）论文的区分有些不清。 拉扎里杜和巴罗尼被引用为“呈现了对涌现语言的更为广泛的观点”，而本综述则专注于“涌现语言研究的目标和应用”。这一点对我来说有些不明确——我认为拉扎里杜和巴罗尼的论文当然对涌现语言研究的目标/应用感兴趣。也有可能本综述本身更为广泛/更新，因为它篇幅更长且发布时间更近。但我认为任何关于这篇论文与其他论文之间差异的澄清都是有价值的（为什么我们需要两者？）# 第4节特指：非深度强化学习方法的差异（这并不是一个关键的阻碍/建议，但值得考虑）计算机模拟已经使用了很长时间，试图模拟和理解语言使用和涌现的某些特性。我认为作者意识到这一点——第4节的每个小节都描述了深度学习可能特别有助于理解例如语言习得（因为它目前是我们能设置的最“现实”的模拟）——但总体效果是，实践者在回答语言问题时可能选择深度学习工具的主要原因被埋没/贯穿于各个小节中。我会考虑在第4节中添加一个特定部分，明确描述为什么可能会使用深度学习方法来回答这些语言问题。有明显的优势，但也有明显的劣势（尽管我们尽了最大努力，模拟中训练的代理并没有习得接近人类语言的东西，且我们当前的训练范式中有许多突出的人为因素）。一个集中讨论深度学习的优缺点以及深度学习如何填补前深度强化学习文献留下的空白的地方，会使第4节更加清晰。# 总结总之，我相信这篇论文显然投入了大量的努力，并且我认为它可以为文献做出有益的贡献，但我会说它目前还不完全适合发表。我推荐的主要阻碍是中间有大约20页连续的文本，即使阅读了所有文本，我认为读者对某些部分的工作仍没有最清晰的理解，这是由于缺乏图表或对文本中描述的某些现象更具体的例子/解释（例如，缺乏对涌现语言指标及其弱点的具体讨论，或第3节和第4节中相关论文的关键“结果”图表）。因此，为了确保我的推荐，我可能希望 - （**最关键**）改进正文中的写作和论文结构，增加图表+例子，并对当前研究缺乏的内容进行更有针对性的解释； - (**理想情况下**) 为新读者提供一些额外的教学背景，- (**理想情况下**) 更多关于为什么我们需要这篇特定的EC文献综述，而不是现有的综述（尤其是Lazaridou & Baroni 2020，这是与本文最接近的论文）。# 其他次要建议 - 我更倾向于使用“涌现通信”而非“涌现语言”——涌现语言是研究对象，但我发现“涌现通信”更常用来指代该子领域本身 - 我认为摘要中的de novo观点可能会产生误导，因为并非所有EC工作都是从零开始研究涌现的；有许多工作使用基于EC的技术来增强现有的人类语言训练系统，例如https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13344和https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04499，其中许多被作者引用 - 我觉得“中间应用”这个词有点令人困惑，因为当说某物是“中间”时，不清楚参考类别是什么。例如，作者自己声称“中间应用并不是我们通常认为的应用。”似乎一个更合适的术语是EC中的基本/内在进展。我会考虑重新措辞这一点（尽管我对此并没有很强的意见） - 第6页：“当前文献中没有工作明确追求人类语言的重新推导。”这句话值得澄清为什么是这样（即完全“重新推导人类语言”是一个极其雄心勃勃的目标，涉及太多变动因素） - 第3.1节适用性：“涌现语言作为一种生成合成语言数据的方式，更接近于人类语言中的自然变异。”这是否正确，考虑到现有研究表明这类合成语言通常与人类语言大相径庭？

**主张与证据：**
是的

**受众：**
是的

**反驳评论：**
回复（2/2）：## 关于第4节具体：非深度强化学习方法的差异 > 我会考虑在第4节中添加一个具体部分，明确描述为什么可能会使用DL方法来回答这些语言学问题。 > 有明显的优势，但也有明显的劣势（尽管我们尽了最大努力，代理在模拟中训练并没有获得接近人类语言的东西，并且在我们当前的训练范式中存在许多突出的人工性）。一个集中讨论DL的优缺点，以及DL如何填补前深度强化学习文献留下的空白的地方，会使第4节更加清晰。这是我们试图在4.1节（“知识驱动应用的通用范式”）中所做的（可能不太成功）。 __您是否建议这一部分需要进一步阐述深度学习（DL）的优缺点，或者DL本身，除了应急通信（EC）之外，应该在单独的章节中展开讨论？__ ## 关于：摘要 > 在第3和第4节中引用相关论文的关键“结果”数据 __我们不太确定“关键‘结果’数据”指的是什么。您能否提供一些具体的例子？__ ## 关于：其他次要建议 > 我更倾向于使用“应急通信”而不是“应急语言”——应急语言是研究对象，但我发现“应急通信”更常用来指代该子领域 本人也同样意识到该领域倾向于使用“应急通信”而非“应急语言”，因此我们在这一点上持灵活态度。我们特别选择使用“应急语言”的理由是，它强调了该学科所追求的通信类型。 > 我认为摘要中的“de novo”观点可能会产生误导，因为并非所有的EC研究都是从零开始研究应急；有很多工作使用基于EC的技术来增强已通过人类语言训练的现有系统，例如https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13344和https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04499，这些工作作者也有引用 尽管并非每一种EC方法都严格研究“de novo”应急，但我们认为它最能概括EC领域的整体特点，将其与其他研究领域如直接从数据建模历史语言变化、使用强化学习和自我博弈来调整对话代理，或研究大型语言模型中的应急语言特征区分开来。我们愿意放宽这一定义。 > 我觉得“中间应用”这个词有点令人困惑……鉴于这一点以及其他审稿人的评论，我们将更改措辞，使其更加直白。 > 第3.1节适用性：“应急语言作为一种生成合成语言数据的方式，更接近人类语言中发现的自然变异。”鉴于现有研究表明这类合成语言通常与人类语言差异巨大，这是否属实？我们可以编辑句子，强调EL是生成合成数据的_潜在_方式，前提是进行适当的设计选择，使其结构更接近人类语言。再次感谢您富有洞察力和见地的审稿！ | 回复（1/2）：对审稿人的澄清问题以__粗体__标示如下。 ## 关于：文本过于冗长；全文应增加更多图表和示例 > 我主要担心的是，论文可以在许多章节中包含更多具体的示例和图表。在论文的第一部分和最后一部分之间基本上没有图表或示例。大多数中间章节仅仅是“文本墙”，包含许多引用和对某些论文的简要描述。 这对可读性不利，但缺乏实例也意味着读者可能无法详细了解这些论文的具体内容，从而无法理解当前SoTA可能缺失的部分。我们承认在添加以下内容后，论文将更具可读性：1. 更具体的实例 2. 更多的插图。我们认为大量的参考文献是必要的——这是一篇综述论文——但我们同意添加更多关于SoTA方法的具体细节和插图将大大增强论文的力度。我们绝对可以解决这一弱点，并将其作为首要任务。

例如，“组合性度量”（2.1）是当前EC研究中最重要的一方面，但大多数度量方法描述得相对简略，且没有详细解释。我们可以扩展这一部分，尽管它已经是论文中最长的部分之一。解决这一问题的一种方法可能是解释几个最突出的度量方法（如组合性的地形相似性），而不对每一个度量方法进行完整解释。__您认为这种方法可以接受吗？__

我相信这一部分还应引用那些揭示当前组合性度量与任务性能之间没有明确联系的论文，这有助于读者理解该领域度量的现状（https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.407/）。感谢您的建议，我们将把这篇论文添加到这一部分。

另一个例子，“理论模型”（2.3）... 应添加一个具体的理论模型示例。我们有两个示例在考虑中，并将添加其中一个。

## 关于模糊的下一步

我认为由于这些部分的描述相对简略，许多部分以“这里没有一般的‘下一步’”结束... 我们将用更具体的建议替换这些模糊的“下一步”部分。

例如在2.1“重新推导自然语言”... 如果我们提出一个“重新推导人类语言”的推动力，作者可以更好地总结当前EC文献中缺失的方面（如模型规模、种群大小、具身性、任务真实性、任何语言约束等）。我们也将特别解决这一关切。

## 关于目前预设对EC的熟悉度

与上述关于实例不足的讨论相关... 论文可以在第1节中设置一个基本的EC式设置，勾勒出典型的EC设置是什么样的。我们也将添加这一点。

## 关于应更清楚地区分其他EC综述

例如，第1.2节中Lazaridou和Baroni（2020）论文的区别有些不清... 我认为任何关于本文与其他论文差异的澄清都是有价值的（为什么我们需要两者？）虽然Lazaridou & Baroni（2020）简要提到了涌现式通信的一些目标，但他们只是将其作为涌现式语言的众多方面之一进行讨论。本文旨在对特定目标进行详细、系统且全面的回顾，而不涉及涌现式语言的其他方面。尽管前一篇论文可能花费1-2页来阐述涌现式通信的目标，但本文的全部内容都致力于此。我们将在论文中更清晰地表达这一点。

paper_title: Effectiveness of contact tracing apps for SARS-CoV-2: an updated systematic review
paper_abstract:
Objective – To systematically review evidence on effectiveness of contact tracing apps (CTAs) for SARS-CoV-2 on epidemiological and clinical outcomes 
 Design – Update of a systematic review ( https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2021-050519 ) 
 Data sources - EMBASE (OVID), MEDLINE (PubMed), BioRxiv, and MedRxiv were searched up to June 9 th 2021 
 Study selection – Studies, empirical or model-based, assessing effect of CTAs for SARS-CoV-2 on quarantine rate, reproduction number (R), total number of infections, hospitalization, mortality, and other epidemiologically and clinically relevant outcomes, were eligible for inclusion. 
 Data extraction – Empirical and model-based studies were both critically appraised based on dedicated quality and risk of bias assessment checklists. Data on type of study (i.e., empirical or model-based), sample size, (simulated) time horizon, study population, CTA type (and associated interventions), comparator, and outcomes assessed, were extracted. Key findings were extracted and narratively summarized. Specifically for model-based studies, characteristics and values of important model parameters were collected. 
 Results – 5123 studies were identified, of which 27 studies (five empirical, 22 model-based studies) were eligible and included in this review. All empirical studies were observational (non-randomized) studies and either at unclear or high risk of bias, mostly due to uncontrolled confounding. Risk of bias of model-based studies was considered high for 7 of 22 studies. Most studies demonstrated beneficial effects of CTAs on R, total number of infections, hospitalization, and mortality. Effect size was dependent on other model parameter values (e.g., proportion of asymptomatic individuals, testing delays), but in general a beneficial effect was observed at CTA adoption rates of 20% and over. 
 Conclusions – CTAs are potentially effective at reducing SARS-CoV-2 related epidemiological and clinical outcomes, though effect size depends on other model parameter values. Methodologically sound comparative empirical studies on effectiveness of CTAs are lacking and would be desirable to confirm findings from model-based studies.
review_content:
Here are the key recommendations:

1. Incorporation and impact of new studies. This updated systematic review offers vital new insights into the effectiveness of CTAs. However, it would add value if the authors specifically indicated the number of additional studies included compared to the original review. Describing how these new inclusions have enriched the review in terms of the breadth and depth of analysis would substantiate the significance of this updated review.

2. Explanation of inclusion methods for new studies. For enhanced clarity, I recommend a more comprehensive description of the methods employed for the inclusion of newer studies, e.g., if the search criteria were extended or other relevant modifications.

3. Outcome variables in data extraction. In the phrase 'effectiveness of CTAs for SARS-CoV-2 on epidemiological and clinical outcomes,' there's a need to specify the outcomes evaluated. The use of 'most important' may seem subjective and can be further clarified to maintain objectivity.

4. Impact of new studies on review results. Kindly discuss how the inclusion of new studies might have impacted the results compared to the previous review. This could entail highlighting (if any) shifts in key findings, emergence of new trends, or reinforcement of previous conclusions.

5. Timeline and contextual factors. Given the rapidly evolving epidemiological trajectory of COVID-19, it's crucial to provide a timeline or chronological context of when each study was conducted and when the CTAs were implemented. This would offer a more robust understanding of the CTAs' effectiveness over time and across different epidemiological scenarios.

6. Supplementary Files Accessibility. It’s essential to ensure the provided link for supplementary materials is working and accessible.
paper_title_zh: "SARS-CoV-2接触者追踪应用程序的有效性：一项更新的系统综述"
paper_abstract_zh:
**目标** – 系统性回顾关于接触者追踪应用（CTAs）对SARS-CoV-2流行病学和临床结果有效性的证据。

**设计** – 对一项系统性回顾的更新（https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2021-050519）。

**数据来源** – 检索了EMBASE（OVID）、MEDLINE（PubMed）、BioRxiv和MedRxiv，截止至2021年6月9日。

**研究选择** – 符合纳入标准的研究包括实证或基于模型的研究，评估CTAs对SARS-CoV-2的隔离率、再生数（R）、总感染人数、住院率、死亡率以及其他流行病学和临床相关结果的影响。

**数据提取** – 实证和基于模型的研究均根据专门的质量和偏倚风险评估清单进行批判性评估。提取了研究类型（即实证或基于模型）、样本量、（模拟的）时间范围、研究人群、CTA类型（及相关干预措施）、比较组和评估结果的数据。关键发现被提取并进行叙述性总结。特别是对于基于模型的研究，收集了重要模型参数的特征和值。

**结果** – 共识别5123项研究，其中27项研究（5项实证研究，22项基于模型的研究）符合条件并纳入本回顾。所有实证研究均为观察性（非随机）研究，且存在不明确或高偏倚风险，主要由于未控制的混杂因素。22项基于模型的研究中有7项被认为偏倚风险高。大多数研究表明CTAs对R、总感染人数、住院率和死亡率有有益影响。效应大小依赖于其他模型参数值（例如，无症状个体比例、检测延迟），但总体上在CTA采用率达到20%及以上时观察到有益效应。

**结论** – CTAs在减少SARS-CoV-2相关的流行病学和临床结果方面具有潜在有效性，尽管效应大小取决于其他模型参数值。缺乏方法学上严谨的比较实证研究来验证基于模型研究的发现，此类研究是理想且必要的。
review_content_zh:
以下是关键建议：

1. 新研究的纳入及其影响。这份更新的系统综述提供了关于CTAs有效性的重要新见解。然而，如果作者能具体指出相较于原始综述新增的研究数量，将增加其价值。描述这些新纳入的研究如何在分析的广度和深度上丰富了综述，将有助于证实这份更新综述的重要性。

2. 新研究纳入方法的解释。为了提高清晰度，我建议更全面地描述用于纳入新研究的具体方法，例如，是否扩展了搜索标准或其他相关修改。

3. 数据提取中的结果变量。在“CTAs对SARS-CoV-2流行病学和临床结果的有效性”这一表述中，需要明确评估的具体结果。使用“最重要的”一词可能显得主观，可以进一步澄清以保持客观性。

4. 新研究对综述结果的影响。请讨论新研究的纳入可能如何影响了与之前综述相比的结果。这可能包括突出（如果有的话）关键发现的转变、新趋势的出现或对先前结论的强化。

5. 时间线和背景因素。鉴于COVID-19迅速演变的流行病学轨迹，提供每项研究的开展时间及CTAs实施的时间线或年代背景至关重要。这将有助于更全面地理解CTAs在不同时间点和不同流行病学情景下的有效性。

6. 补充文件的可访问性。确保提供的补充材料链接有效且可访问是必要的。

paper_title: Acedia, loneliness, and the mandatory celibacy of Catholic parish clergy: a theological-sociological exploratory analysis
paper_abstract: This article utilizes the analytical concept of acedia as the fundamental theoretical framework and applies a systematic literature review of peer-reviewed materials and documents on spiritual sloth, spiritual dryness, Catholic clerical celibacy, social bonding and communal spirituality. This article explores how the Catholic parish clergy’s mandatory celibacy intensifies loneliness and facilitates the spiritual sloth of parish clergy or what is theologically known as acedia. Unlike religious priests who live in religious communities, parish clerics fundamentally live, work, and pray alone in the parish, without strong communal support from fellow priests, bishops, and lay parishioners; thus, making them prone to loneliness, a main component of acedia. This article argues that mandatory celibacy further deprives parish clerics of the social and spiritual support necessary to enhance diocesan clerical spirituality and strengthen spiritual resistance against acedia. It recommends a structural adjustment in the social and spiritual life of parish priests, creating small communities of priests situated in similar territory or districts to allow them to live and work as a team with strong social and spiritual support in the spirit of “living baptismally” to overcome priestly acedia.
review_content:
This is an interesting article, but is basically a literature review aimed at supporting one thesis—that celibacy contributes to acedia, and with it additional problems that plague priests.

I’m familiar with the argument, but I had supposed there would be an empirical assessment of sorts, but the “data” here are just previous studies purported to be the data for a “qualitative research approach.” Don’t call it research per se; call it a literature review, a “state of the science” of sorts. (That said, it’s a pretty strong and ranging literature review.)

Some pressing questions, observations, and criticisms:

It’s redundant. The reader is told at least seven times that living alone in a parish predicts loneliness, and in turn leads to spiritual sloth (or acedia).

There is a tacit causal assumption that this process contributes to criminal sexual abuse (of either sex, though most of the recent troubles have concerned the molestation of pre- and adolescent boys) despite the fact that the various reports about such (John Jay, etc.) have taken pains to distance themselves from implying that celibacy contributes to such—so far as I can tell. The fact is—there is not ample research on this. It’s a difficult matter to study.

Acedia, as I understand it, is considered a personal vice. The article implies this about priests—that they are prone to it, but then elevates it to a congregational-level trait, even a diocesan one.

I agree that “behavioral monitoring by brother priests” (page 4) is a safeguard. It’s also not failsafe by any stretch. I’m aware of numerous incidences of priestly misconduct by men who were monitored by fellow priests.

There’s a causal order concern I have. The author blames celibacy, and claims it causes loneliness, which in turn prompts acedia. But others perceive a different etiology to it—that our habits (of thought, practice, etc.) can invite acedia, which in turn fosters despair (of God’s love and mercy) and sadness. Reinhard Hutter (2012, First Things) notes that such a sadness “that will always cause problems.” Hence, the causal order may not be as obvious as the author suggests.

The author poses an interesting answer—the end of priestly celibacy—that is arguably unnecessary if the Church enables the formation of the author’s back-up plan: the formation of communities for priests to live in. So is the problem a lack of access to marriage to a woman (and then a family)? Or is the problem lack of brotherhood? They are both forms of companionship, and both rich in satisfactions. But they are quite different. So then basically, is this about sex or is it about fellowship of a sort? I think the author points more frequently to the latter, but nevertheless considers the former the central problem.

Fewer of the globe’s men and women are marrying, and at later and later ages. Hence, it can hardly be said that the population of priests is rapidly declining because marriage has become more pivotally important in the society around them. No, celibacy has lost cultural respect among many, while the presumed pleasures of access to sex (variety? consistency?) seem too important to forego. Basically, the priestly shortage is a complex thing. Moreover, because of clergy sexual abuse (again, mostly of boys), the barrier to the priesthood has shifted in many locales—to include evidence of a stable heterosexual orientation (see the Dallas Charter).

Moreover, some priests do live in fellowship with other priests. The author seems to presume (page 3 of the pdf) a “lack of social bonding” is the reality in the Church. It may be for plenty of priests; it is not for many others. They form friendships with fellow priests, even those who don’t live with another priest, and/or they form friendships with parishioners’ families. Will this solve the acedia challenge? For many, yes. But it doesn’t rid one of temptation. Celibacy is a challenge even for the sociable priest. While the author blames celibacy for fostering acedia, other observers (like Hutter) blame pornography for the same. Would a spouse render pornography less attractive? Not by much, according to real data on the subject.

Bottom line is: celibacy is difficult, but hardly impossible. Sociability and friendship are important. Acedia is corrosive. But this study, lacking an empirical test, can only lean on previous studies to impugn celibacy. We can’t actually know from this study what is to blame for acedia (which is not a simple thing to measure, either.)
paper_title_zh: "懒惰、孤独与天主教教区神职人员的强制性独身：一项神学-社会学的探索性分析"
paper_abstract_zh: 本文采用“懒惰”（acedia）的分析概念作为基本理论框架，并系统性地回顾了关于精神懒惰、精神枯竭、天主教神职人员独身制、社会联结和共同体灵性的同行评审材料和文献。文章探讨了天主教教区神职人员强制性独身制如何加剧孤独感，并助长教区神职人员的精神懒惰，即神学上所称的“懒惰”。与生活在宗教团体中的宗教神父不同，教区神职人员基本上在教区内独自生活、工作和祈祷，缺乏来自其他神父、主教和教区平信徒的强大共同体支持；因此，使他们容易陷入孤独，这是“懒惰”的主要成分。本文认为，强制性独身制进一步剥夺了教区神职人员所需的社会和灵性支持，这些支持对于提升教区神职人员的灵性和增强对抗“懒惰”的精神抵抗力至关重要。文章建议对教区神父的社会和灵性生活进行结构性调整，创建位于相似地域或区域的小型神父共同体，使他们能够作为一个团队生活和工作，获得强大的社会和灵性支持，以“活出洗礼精神”来克服神职人员的“懒惰”。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇有趣的文章，但基本上是一篇旨在支持一个论点的文献综述——即独身会导致懒惰（acedia），并由此引发困扰神职人员的其他问题。

我对这个论点很熟悉，但我原以为会有某种实证评估，但这里的“数据”只是之前的研究，据称是“定性研究方法”的数据。不要称之为研究本身；称之为文献综述，某种“科学现状”。（话虽如此，这是一篇相当强大且广泛的文献综述。）

一些紧迫的问题、观察和批评：

它冗余。读者至少被七次告知，在教区独自生活预示着孤独，进而导致精神懒惰（或acedia）。

有一种隐含的因果假设，即这一过程会导致性犯罪（无论是男性还是女性，尽管最近的麻烦大多涉及对未成年男孩的猥亵），尽管关于此类问题的各种报告（如John Jay报告等）都尽力避免暗示独身会导致此类问题——据我所知。事实是——关于这一点的研究并不充分。这是一个难以研究的难题。

据我所知，懒惰被认为是一种个人恶习。文章暗示神职人员容易患上这种恶习，但随后将其提升为教区层面的特征，甚至是主教区的特征。

我同意“由兄弟神职人员进行行为监控”（第4页）是一种保障。但这绝非万无一失。我知道许多神职人员的不当行为，这些人都受到其他神职人员的监控。

我对因果顺序有疑问。作者归咎于独身，声称它导致孤独，进而引发懒惰。但其他人认为其病因不同——我们的习惯（思维、实践等）会招致懒惰，进而滋生绝望（对上帝的爱和怜悯）和悲伤。Reinhard Hutter（2012年，First Things）指出，这种悲伤“总会引发问题”。因此，因果顺序可能并不像作者所暗示的那样明显。

作者提出了一个有趣的解决方案——结束神职人员的独身制度——如果教会能够实现作者的备用计划：为神职人员建立社区，那么这一方案可能是不必要的。所以问题在于缺乏与女性的婚姻（以及随之而来的家庭）吗？还是缺乏兄弟情谊？它们都是陪伴的形式，且都富有满足感。但它们截然不同。所以这基本上是关于性，还是某种形式的团契？我认为作者更频繁地指向后者，但仍然认为前者是核心问题。

全球 fewer 的男性和女性正在结婚，且结婚年龄越来越晚。因此，很难说神职人员数量迅速减少是因为婚姻在他们周围的社会中变得更为重要。不，独身在许多人中失去了文化尊重，而获得性生活的假定乐趣（多样性？一致性？）似乎太过重要，不容放弃。基本上，神职人员的短缺是一个复杂的问题。此外，由于神职人员的性虐待（再次强调，主要是男孩），许多地方的圣职门槛已经改变——包括有稳定异性恋取向的证据（参见达拉斯宪章）。

此外，一些神职人员确实与其他神职人员共同生活。作者似乎假设（pdf第3页）“缺乏社会联系”是教会的现实。这对许多神职人员来说可能如此；对许多其他人来说并非如此。他们与同行的神职人员建立友谊，甚至那些不与另一名神职人员同住的人，以及/或者他们与教区居民的家庭建立友谊。这会解决懒惰的挑战吗？对许多人来说，是的。但这并不能消除诱惑。独身对社交型神职人员来说也是一个挑战。尽管作者指责独身助长懒惰，其他观察者（如Hutter）则将此归咎于色情。配偶会降低色情的吸引力吗？根据相关真实数据，并不会太多。

底线是：独身是困难的，但绝非不可能。社交和友谊很重要。懒惰是腐蚀性的。但这项研究缺乏实证检验，只能依赖先前的研究来诋毁独身。我们实际上无法从这项研究中得知懒惰的真正原因（这也不是一个简单衡量的事情）。

paper_title: Open science interventions proposed or implemented to assess researcher impact: a scoping review
paper_abstract:
Background 
     Several open science-promoting initiatives have been proposed to improve the quality of biomedical research, including initiatives for assessing researchers’ open science behaviour as criteria for promotion or tenure. Yet there is limited evidence to judge whether the interventions are effective. This review aimed to summarise the literature, identifying open science practices related to researcher assessment, and map the extent of evidence of existing interventions implemented to assess researchers and research impact. 
   
   
     Methods 
     A scoping review using the Joanna Briggs Institute Scoping Review Methodology was conducted. We included all study types that described any open science practice-promoting initiatives proposed or implemented to assess researchers and research impact, in health sciences, biomedicine, psychology, and economics. Data synthesis was quantitative and descriptive. 
   
   
     Results 
     Among 18,020 identified documents, 27 articles were selectedfor analysis. Most of the publications were in the field of health sciences (n = 10), and were indicated as research culture, perspective, commentary, essay, proceedings of a workshop, research article, world view, opinion, research note, editorial, report, and research policy articles (n = 22). The majority of studies proposed recommendations to address problems regarding threats to research rigour and reproducibility that were multi-modal (n = 20), targeting several open science practices. Some of the studies based their proposed recommendations on further evaluation or extension of previous initiatives. Most of the articles (n = 20) did not discuss implementation of their proposed intervention. Of the 27 included articles, 10 were cited in policy documents, with The Leiden Manifesto being the most cited (104 citations). 
   
   
     Conclusion 
     This review provides an overview of proposals to integrate open science into researcher assessment. The more promising ones need evaluation and, where appropriate, implementation. 
   
   
     Study registration 
     
      https://osf.io/ty9m7
review_content:
The authors survey interventions that support open science research practices, addressing a topic of high interest for the meta-research community. The article is clearly structured and concisely written.

I have a few minor suggestions for further improvement:

1. One main intervention are incentive structures. The article would benefit from a systematic overview of available funding options dedicated to open science research practices. This would also be of high practical relevance for the community.

2. To test the effectiveness of interventions, different study designs would be possible, although randomised controlled trials seem the most valid option. However, in the context of open science research practices as a complex behavior, conducting an RCT becomes challenging. Several authors have elaborated on this aspect, it would be informative for the reader if the authors summarise their views.

3. The Review touches on the importance of training, which is another important intervention. Again, a systematic (although likely not exhaustive) overview of training options would be informative and of immidiate practical relevance for readers.

4. On the topic of training, different stakeholders and suggestions to implement training in reproducible open science research practices should be mentioned, e.g. see this recent white paper: Eleven strategies for making reproducible research and open science training the norm at research institutions | eLife (elifesciences.org)

5. The authors mention preregistration as an important tool. In this context, the following evaluations should be mentioned:
Preregistration in practice: A comparison of preregistered and non-preregistered studies in psychology | Behavior Research Methods (springer.com);

Estimating the prevalence of discrepancies between study registrations and publications: a systematic review and meta-analyses | BMJ Open

6. Besides preregistration, Registered Report are a highly relevant open science research practice as they combine transparency with a clear benefit for authors and hance an incentive, a guarantee for publication (The past, present and future of Registered Reports | Nature Human Behaviour). Recent elaborations and findings on Registered Reports should be incorporated (e.g., Open science challenges, benefits and tips in early career and beyond | PLOS Biology; An Excess of Positive Results: Comparing the Standard Psychology Literature With Registered Reports - Anne M. Scheel, Mitchell R. M. J. Schijen, Daniël Lakens, 2021 (sagepub.com)).

7. Open science research practices are of high societal relevance, as the authors are pointing out, and their work can inform policy and/or inform funding initiatives that may themselve create new incentives for implementing open science research practices. Looking beyond academia, it may be worth mentioning the role of open science research practices in other science related fields (e.g. industry) with an immidiate impact on health care innovation (e.g., Open science saves lives: lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic | BMC Medical Research Methodology | Full Text (biomedcentral.com); S2666-3791(23)00608-0.pdf (cell.com)).

8. Another form of intervention that could be mentioned are guidelines and consensus papers that increasingly demand for open science across different research field. Some examples for different fields could be briefly discussed.

9. Lastly, the article mentions the increasing relevance of the topic, but could also point out more clearly that open science research practices are still only implemented in a fraction of research across fields, highlighting some examples from difference life science areas. This aspect could be integrated in the introduction and referred to again the discussion.
paper_title_zh: 开放科学干预措施：评估研究者影响力的提议或实施情况——一项范围综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
为了提高生物医学研究的质量，已经提出了多项促进开放科学的倡议，包括将研究人员开放科学行为作为晋升或终身教职评估标准的倡议。然而，判断这些干预措施是否有效的证据有限。本综述旨在总结文献，识别与研究人员评估相关的开放科学实践，并绘制现有干预措施的实施范围，以评估研究人员和研究影响。

方法
采用乔安娜·布里格斯研究所范围综述方法进行范围综述。我们纳入了所有描述在健康科学、生物医学、心理学和经济学领域提出或实施的任何促进开放科学实践倡议以评估研究人员和研究影响的研究类型。数据综合是定量和描述性的。

结果
在18,020份识别的文档中，选择了27篇文章进行分析。大多数出版物属于健康科学领域（n = 10），并被标记为研究文化、观点、评论、论文、研讨会会议记录、研究文章、世界观、意见、研究简报、社论、报告和研究政策文章（n = 22）。大多数研究提出了多模态（n = 20）的建议，以解决威胁研究严谨性和可重复性的问题，针对多种开放科学实践。一些研究基于对先前倡议的进一步评估或扩展提出了建议。大多数文章（n = 20）未讨论其提出干预措施的实施。在27篇纳入的文章中，有10篇被政策文件引用，其中《莱顿宣言》被引用最多（104次）。

结论
本综述提供了将开放科学整合到研究人员评估中的提案概览。更有前景的提案需要评估，并在适当的情况下实施。

研究注册
https://osf.io/ty9m7
review_content_zh:
作者综述了支持开放科学研究的干预措施，这一主题对元研究社区具有高度兴趣。文章结构清晰，文笔简洁。

我有几点小建议以供进一步改进：

1. 一个主要的干预措施是激励结构。文章将受益于对专门用于开放科学研究实践的可用资助选项的系统概述。这对社区也具有高度的实际相关性。

2. 为了测试干预措施的有效性，可以采用不同的研究设计，尽管随机对照试验似乎是最有效的选项。然而，在开放科学研究实践作为复杂行为的背景下，进行随机对照试验变得具有挑战性。几位作者已经对此方面进行了详细阐述，如果作者能总结他们的观点，对读者将是有益的。

3. 该综述涉及培训的重要性，这是另一个重要的干预措施。同样，对培训选项的系统（尽管可能不全面）概述将是有益的，并对读者具有直接的实际相关性。

4. 在培训主题上，应提及不同的利益相关者以及实施可复现开放科学研究实践培训的建议，例如参见这份最近的白皮书：在研究机构中将可复现研究和开放科学培训常态化的十一条策略 | eLife (elifesciences.org)

5. 作者提到预注册是一个重要工具。在此背景下，应提及以下评估：
预注册实践：心理学中预注册和非预注册研究的比较 | 行为研究方法 (springer.com);
估计研究注册与出版物之间差异的普遍性：系统综述和荟萃分析 | BMJ Open

6. 除了预注册，注册报告是另一个高度相关的开放科学研究实践，因为它们将透明度与对作者的明确益处相结合，从而成为一种激励，保证了出版（注册报告的过去、现在和未来 | 自然人类行为）。应纳入对注册报告的最新阐述和发现（例如，早期职业及以后的开放科学挑战、益处和提示 | PLOS生物学；阳性结果过多：标准心理学文献与注册报告的比较 - Anne M. Scheel, Mitchell R. M. J. Schijen, Daniël Lakens, 2021 (sagepub.com)）。

7. 开放科学研究实践具有高度的社会相关性，正如作者所指出的，他们的工作可以为政策提供信息，并/或为可能自身创造新激励以实施开放科学研究实践的资助倡议提供信息。超越学术界，可能值得提及开放科学研究实践在其他科学相关领域（例如工业）中的作用，这些领域对医疗保健创新具有直接影响（例如，开放科学拯救生命：来自COVID-19大流行的教训 | BMC医学研究方法学 | 全文 (biomedcentral.com); S2666-3791(23)00608-0.pdf (cell.com)）。

8. 另一种可以提及的干预形式是指导方针和共识论文，这些论文越来越多地要求在不同研究领域实施开放科学。可以简要讨论不同领域的一些例子。

9. 最后，文章提到了该主题日益增加的相关性，但也可以更清楚地指出，开放科学研究实践仍然只在少数研究领域中得到实施，突出一些来自不同生命科学领域的例子。这一方面可以整合到引言中，并在讨论中再次提及。

The article would benefit from a systematic overview of available funding options dedicated to open science research practices.

Again, a systematic (although likely not exhaustive) overview of training options would be informative and of immidiate practical relevance for readers.
This aspect could be integrated in the introduction and referred to again the discussion.

paper_title: A SWOT analysis of generative AI in applied linguistics: Leveraging strengths, addressing weaknesses, seizing opportunities, and mitigating threats
paper_abstract:
Background 
 The integration of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and Gemini, into the field of applied linguistics presents transformative opportunities alongside notable challenges. This study aims to evaluate the role of AI in applied linguistics through a SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis. 
 
 
 Methods 
 Using a sample derived from Scopus and Web of Science, we identified relevant studies by applying specific search terms. Our qualitative research design used the SWOT framework to systematically review and analyse studies, ensuring a robust synthesis of data. 
 
 
 Results 
 The results of our SWOT analysis revealed the following: 1) Strengths: Enhanced educational tools and resources through AI-driven personalization and interactive learning, increased efficiency and accessibility in generating educational materials, and innovative research applications leveraging semantic similarity measures and advanced linguistic analyses. 2) Weaknesses: Quality and accuracy concerns in AI-generated content, potential over-dependence on AI tools leading to diminished student creativity and ethical issues, and technical limitations in handling complex academic writing tasks. 3) Opportunities: Potential for educational innovation and pedagogical integration, advancements in AI technology to support linguistic research, and fostering global collaboration and access through AI tools. 4) Threats: Risks to academic integrity due to AI-generated content, technological and implementation challenges, and privacy and security concerns regarding data handling. 
 
 
 Conclusions 
 Based on the SWOT analysis, we introduced a strategic plan to maximize strengths and opportunities while addressing weaknesses and threats. The strategy includes promoting personalized learning through AI tools, streamlining the creation of educational materials, fostering innovative research applications, ensuring human oversight to maintain content quality, developing ethical guidelines to prevent misuse, investing in necessary infrastructure and training, and implementing robust data protection measures.
review_content:
1. The article addresses the integration of Generative AI (GenAI) tools in applied linguistics, employing a SWOT analysis framework. This approach aligns with existing literature and addresses a timely topic. However, the execution lacks depth and critical engagement, which limits its contribution to the field.

2. The review of existing literature is incomplete. Seminal works and foundational studies on GenAI's implications in applied linguistics are either overlooked or insufficiently integrated. Expanding the literature review to include these studies will strengthen the theoretical grounding.

3. While the qualitative design and SWOT framework are appropriate, the methodology section lacks sufficient details to ensure replicability. The inclusion of the PRISMA flowchart and data extraction templates is helpful, but more specifics about how themes were identified and synthesized are necessary.

4. The SWOT analysis, while structured, reads superficially. The identified strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats are presented without adequately linking them to the context of applied linguistics. In particular:
a. The discussion section lacks critical examination of the identified factors.
b.The strategic recommendations are generic and need concrete, actionable steps tailored to the applied linguistics domain.

5. The manuscript includes descriptions of GenAI applications, but some sections read as though they were generated by AI tools. This raises concerns about originality and depth. A more critical and reflective narrative is necessary, particularly in evaluating the role of these tools in fostering innovation versus their potential drawbacks.

6. The writing quality is uneven, with some sections lacking coherence and depth. Enhanced editorial refinement and restructuring are needed to improve readability and ensure alignment with academic standards.
paper_title_zh: 应用语言学中生成式AI的SWOT分析：发挥优势、应对劣势、抓住机遇与化解威胁
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
生成式人工智能（AI），特别是像ChatGPT和Gemini这样的大型语言模型（LLMs），在应用语言学领域的整合带来了变革性的机遇，同时也伴随着显著的挑战。本研究旨在通过SWOT（优势、劣势、机会、威胁）分析评估AI在应用语言学中的角色。

方法
使用从Scopus和Web of Science中提取的样本，我们通过应用特定的搜索术语识别相关研究。我们的定性研究设计采用SWOT框架，系统地回顾和分析研究，确保数据的稳健综合。

结果
我们的SWOT分析结果显示如下：1）优势：通过AI驱动的个性化和互动学习增强教育工具和资源，提高生成教育材料的效率和可及性，以及利用语义相似度测量和高级语言分析的创新研究应用。2）劣势：AI生成内容的质量和准确性问题，过度依赖AI工具可能导致学生创造力下降和伦理问题，以及处理复杂学术写作任务的技术限制。3）机会：教育创新和教学整合的潜力，AI技术进步支持语言学研究，以及通过AI工具促进全球合作和访问。4）威胁：AI生成内容对学术诚信的风险，技术和实施挑战，以及数据处理中的隐私和安全问题。

结论
基于SWOT分析，我们提出了一个战略计划，旨在最大化优势和机会，同时解决劣势和威胁。该策略包括通过AI工具促进个性化学习，简化教育材料的创建，促进创新研究应用，确保人工监督以维持内容质量，制定伦理指南以防止滥用，投资必要的基础设施和培训，以及实施强有力的数据保护措施。

paper_title: Effectiveness of acute L-arginine supplementation on physical performance in strength training: a systematic review and meta-analysis
paper_abstract:
Background:  The oral administration of L-arginine has been related to improved physical performance due to a likely reduction in muscle fatigue, resulting from the vasodilator effect of nitric oxide on skeletal muscle. However, there is no precise and quantitative analysis of the information in the literature. The main objective of this study was to assess the effectiveness of L-arginine supplementation on physical performance in strength training with a systematic review and meta-analysis. We hypothesized that L-arginine supplementation would improve performance capacity and the effects involved in strength training. 
 Methods:  The study period was from 2010 to 2020. The inclusion process established articles with well-designed human experiments that included only L-arginine supplementation (without any additional compounds) testing the effects of L-arginine supplementation on sports performance related to strength training; identical experimental conditions in placebo or control group; and publications in the last ten years (until December 31, 2020). Three studies were included that compared L-arginine supplementation with placebo in anaerobic performance tests. Test analysis supplementation with other supplements was removed and there was no gender, age, and ethnicity level. 
 Results:  There was no significant heterogeneity (p>0.05) in the analysis of the three selected articles and the effects of L-arginine supplementation in muscular endurance; performance had a mean of 0.26 (95% CI = -0.129; 0.649; p = 0.190), peak torque with a mean of -0.002 (95% CI = -0.531; 0.527; p = 0. 99) of the third series of exercises and, furthermore, when comparing the integrated effect (resistance rate with the peak torque) there was no difference with a mean of 0.168 (95% CI = -0.145; 0.481; p = 0.292). 
 Conclusions:  Acute L-arginine supplementation provides no ergogenic effect on strength training performance.
review_content: In my opinion, It's too hard to get strong conclusions, with only three articles included. In fact, the same authors stated in the conclusion "However, this study should not be considered exhaustive and further research will be substantially important to strengthen future results". My suggestion is to consider a wide laps or more criteria to include more studies. For example, it would be possible to include the 166 records with L-arginine and another supplement.
paper_title_zh: 急性L-精氨酸补充对力量训练中身体表现的有效性：系统综述与荟萃分析
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：口服L-精氨酸被认为能通过一氧化氮对骨骼肌的血管舒张作用，可能减少肌肉疲劳，从而提高身体表现。然而，文献中缺乏精确和定量的分析。本研究的主要目的是通过系统综述和荟萃分析评估L-精氨酸补充剂对力量训练中身体表现的有效性。我们假设L-精氨酸补充剂能提高运动能力和力量训练相关的效果。

方法：研究时间段为2010年至2020年。纳入标准为设计良好的人类实验文章，仅包含L-精氨酸补充剂（无其他附加化合物），测试L-精氨酸补充剂对与力量训练相关的运动表现的影响；安慰剂或对照组实验条件相同；且为近十年内的出版物（截至2020年12月31日）。共纳入三项研究，这些研究在无氧性能测试中比较了L-精氨酸补充剂与安慰剂的效果。排除了与其他补充剂联合使用的测试分析，且未考虑性别、年龄和种族水平。

结果：在选定的三篇文章的分析中，未发现显著异质性（p>0.05），L-精氨酸补充剂在肌肉耐力方面的效果平均值为0.26（95% CI = -0.129; 0.649; p = 0.190），第三组练习的峰值扭矩平均值为-0.002（95% CI = -0.531; 0.527; p = 0.99），此外，比较综合效果（阻力率与峰值扭矩）时，未发现差异，平均值为0.168（95% CI = -0.145; 0.481; p = 0.292）。

结论：急性L-精氨酸补充剂对力量训练表现无增强效果。
review_content_zh: 在我看来，仅包含三篇文章很难得出强有力的结论。事实上，同一作者在结论中也指出：“然而，本研究不应被视为详尽无遗，进一步的研究将对加强未来的结果至关重要。”我的建议是考虑更宽泛的时间范围或更多标准以纳入更多研究。例如，可以纳入166项含有L-精氨酸和另一种补充剂的记录。

paper_title: A Unified Survey on Anomaly, Novelty, Open-Set, and Out- of-Distribution Detection: Solutions and Future Challenges
paper_abstract: Machine learning models often encounter samples that are diverged from the training distribution. Failure to recognize an out-of-distribution (OOD) sample, and consequently assign that sample to an in-class label significantly compromises the reliability of a model. The problem has gained significant attention due to its importance for safety deploying models in open-world settings. Detecting OOD samples is challenging due to the intractability of modeling all possible unknown distributions. To date, several research domains tackle the problem of detecting unfamiliar samples, including anomaly detection, novelty detection, one-class learning, open set recognition, and out-of-distribution detection. Despite having similar and shared concepts, out-of-distribution, open-set, and anomaly detection have been investigated independently. Accordingly, these research avenues have not cross-pollinated, creating research barriers. While some surveys intend to provide an overview of these approaches, they seem to only focus on a specific domain without examining the relationship between different domains. This survey aims to provide a cross-domain and comprehensive review of numerous eminent works in respective areas while identifying their commonalities. Researchers can benefit from the overview of research advances in different fields and develop future methodology synergistically. Furthermore, to the best of our knowledge, while there are surveys in anomaly detection or one-class learning, there is no comprehensive or up-to-date survey on out-of-distribution detection, which our survey covers extensively. Finally, having a unified cross-domain perspective, we discuss and shed light on future lines of research, intending to bring these fields closer together.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This survey paper provides a consolidated review of three machine learning sub-fields: Anomaly/Novelty Detection (AD), Open-Set Recognition (OSR), and Out-of-Distribution Detection (OoD). The paper highlights the similar nature of these three tasks and the fact that they are currently investigated separately, motivating the utility of such a survey. Specifically, all three tasks involve detecting ‘novel/out-of-distribution/unseen/abnormal’ data at test time, and research efforts have been duplicated with the same ideas being proposed independently for each task. The paper describes a range of prior approaches for these tasks, at times highlighting the similarity between methods from different fields, and concludes by proposing future directions for the research community. Based on the TMLR's acceptance criteria, I make the following broad conclusions: * Are the claims made in the submission supported by accurate, convincing and clear evidence? Broadly, yes. The survey covers a substantial portion of the existing literature on these topics and accurately describes existing methods. However, I believe some additional information (e.g some missing methods and details on evaluation) is required to give an accurate depiction of the field. * Would some individuals in TMLR's audience be interested in the findings of this paper? Yes. The unifying perspective provided in this paper is interesting, relevant and timely.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strengths: * The main contribution of this paper is that it provides a unified perspective on three machine learning sub-fields which are currently tackled independently, but which all tackle the same underlying problem. By providing a single overview, researchers can view solutions proposed for very similar tasks and avoid duplication of effort. * The survey covers a wide range of methods which I think cumulatively reasonably represent the current understanding for this problem. It is also a strength of the paper that analogies between methods *between domains* are regularly drawn. * Quantitative comparison of a number of discussed methods is given for the OoD benchmarks. * The paper concludes by pointing out a range of interesting future directions for anomaly detection research. Weaknesses: * The paper lacks specific and clear definitions of the benchmark protocols for the tasks. I.e how each datasets are used for each task. This is done for OoD but not sufficiently for OSR and AD. * This paper misses some important methods which are relevant to its overall message. * It is my belief that the distinction/similarities between OoD and OSR is are not clearly enough stated in the paper. * The paper has a number of typos which should be corrected.

**Requested Changes:**
Critical changes: * Benchmark protocols: The paper does not make it sufficiently clear how evaluations are performed in the respective fields. The practical differences between the fields are ultimately defined by the evaluation protocols and this should be discussed. E.g how are the described datasets used for OoD and OSR, how are the usages different and how does this impact our understanding of methods? Furthermore, it is important to have some quantitative comparison of the described methods for the OSR and AD benchmarks (these could be re-reported from the literature if not re-implemented). * Difference between OoD and OSR: The papers OSR section mainly uses somewhat complicated terminology from canonical work on the problem [1]. While this terminology should be mentioned, the dominant evaluation protocol in the literature is simple: take a dataset; train a classifier on a subset of classes; detect the other classes as unseen at test-time. This is extremely similar to the setup in the OoD: train a classifier on a dataset, detect a different dataset as unseen at test-time. In fact, the CIFAR10 → CIFAR100 evaluations are virtually identical. This should be highlighted both for clarity, and because it accentuates the paper’s message that these tasks are related. * Important missing methods: 1. Sohn et al [2]: This paper analyzes the relationship between SSL methods and AD classifiers, which is related to many works discussed in the paper. 2. Kong at al [3]: This is mentioned briefly but I believe should be given a section. It is to my knowledge one of the strongest open-set methods and also demonstrates results on semantic segmentation/large-scale datasets. 3. Vaze et al [4]: This paper shows that a simple ‘maximum logit score’ baseline on top of a classifier with high closed-set accuracy can perform very strongly for OSR. It also discusses the similarities/differences between OoD and OSR, and proposes new challenging and large-scale benchmarks. 4. Sun et al [5]: This method is shown to consistently improve OoD performance on top of a number of methods discussed in this paper (e.g Energy, MSP, ODIN). It also demonstrates results on large-scale OoD benchmarks. *Note: [4] and [5] propose large-scale benchmarks for OSR and OoD respectively (targeted towards semantic shift and low-level distribution shift respectively). This is highlighted as an important future direction in this paper.* Other changes: * Typos: I found a number of typos throughout the manuscript. Though the paper is long, authors should make sure to clean these to improve readability. I have highlighted a small subset here for illustration: (Page4) MSE loss of generated image → MSE loss of a generated image; (Page8) model (h) can instantiate different architectures → model (h) can be instantiated by different architectures; (Page13) model half-space is not as tight enough → model half-space is not tight enough; (Page21) maxs1, …,sn → max(s1, …,sn); (Page32) the feature space of penultimate layer → the feature space of the penultimate layer. * Nice-to-have citations: 1. Yang et al [6]. This concurrent survey also covers AD/OSR/OoD. Though a pre-print, it is worth highlighting for the interest of the reader and to indicate the movement of the community in this direction. 2. The paper highlights ‘open world recognition’ as an important future direction. Based on the description, I believe the tasks of Novel Category Discovery [7]/ Open-World Semi-Supervised Learning [8] / Generalized Category Discovery [9] are relevant. 3. The ‘adversarial’ follow up to RPL should be mentioned [10]. Though related to RPL (which is discussed), it improves performance and also evaluates on OoD benchmarks (despite being an OSR method). * It is not clear how Figure 1 matches the caption. The figure should be labeled for AD/OSR/OoD with examples of ID/OoD for each. * It is stated that AUPR is 'usually' used in OSR. In my experience, this is not true, AUROC is predominantly reported. Furthermore ID accuracy often seems unreported in OSR papers, this could be mentioned? * The ‘OoD’ section (e.g description of Nalisnick et al.) mentions generative models assigning higher likelihoods to outliers. How does this reconcile with the successful use of generative models elsewhere in the literature (e.g the OpenHybrid OSR method which is discussed). * The metric is not specified in the caption of Table 6. [1] Probability Models for Open Set Recognition, Scheirer et al., TPAMI 2014 [2] Learning and Evaluating Representations for Deep One-Class Classification, Sohn et al, ICLR 2021. [3] OpenGan: Open-set Recognition via open data generation, ICCV 2021 [4]: Open-set Recognition: a Good Closed-Set Classifier is All You Need?, Vaze et al, ICLR 2022 [5] React: Out-of-distribution Detection With Rectified Activations, Sun et al, NeurIPS 2021 [6] Generalized out-of-distribution detection, Yang et al., ArXiv pre-print 2021 [7] Learning to Discover Novel Visual Categories via Deep Transfer Clustering, Han et al., ICCV 2019 [8] Open-World Semi Supervised Learning, Cao et al., ICLR 2022 [9] Generalized Category Discovery, Vaze et al., CVPR 2022 [10] Adversarial Reciprocal Points for Open Set Recognition, Chen et al, TPAMI 2021

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
I believe broader impacts have been sufficiently highlighted in the paper.
paper_title_zh: 异常、新奇、开放集及分布外检测的统一综述：解决方案与未来挑战
paper_abstract_zh: 机器学习模型经常遇到偏离训练分布的样本。未能识别出分布外（OOD）样本，并因此将该样本分配到类别内标签，会显著降低模型的可靠性。由于在开放世界环境中安全部署模型的重要性，这一问题已引起广泛关注。检测OOD样本具有挑战性，因为建模所有可能的未知分布是不可 tract 的。迄今为止，多个研究领域都在解决检测不熟悉样本的问题，包括异常检测、新颖性检测、单类学习、开放集识别和分布外检测。尽管分布外、开放集和异常检测具有相似和共通的概念，但它们一直是独立研究的。因此，这些研究途径未能相互借鉴，形成了研究壁垒。虽然一些综述旨在提供这些方法的概述，但它们似乎只关注特定领域，而未考察不同领域之间的关系。本综述旨在提供跨领域且全面的回顾，涵盖各领域内的众多杰出工作，并识别其共同点。研究人员可以从不同领域的研究进展概览中受益，并协同开发未来的方法。此外，据我们所知，尽管存在关于异常检测或单类学习的综述，但尚未有全面或最新的关于分布外检测的综述，而我们的综述对此进行了广泛覆盖。最后，基于统一的跨领域视角，我们讨论并阐明未来的研究方向，旨在使这些领域更加紧密地结合在一起。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
这篇综述论文对机器学习的三个子领域进行了综合回顾：异常/新奇检测（AD）、开放集识别（OSR）和分布外检测（OoD）。论文强调了这三个任务的相似性以及它们目前被独立研究的事实，从而论证了此类综述的实用性。具体而言，这三个任务都涉及在测试时检测“新奇/分布外/未见/异常”数据，并且研究工作存在重复，相同的想法被独立地提出用于每个任务。论文描述了这些任务的一系列先前方法，有时突出了不同领域方法之间的相似性，并在最后提出了未来研究方向。基于TMLR的接受标准，我得出以下广泛结论：* 提交论文中的主张是否得到了准确、有说服力和清晰的证据支持？总体而言，是的。该综述涵盖了这些主题现有文献的很大一部分，并准确描述了现有方法。然而，我认为需要一些额外信息（例如一些缺失的方法和评估细节）来准确描绘该领域。* TMLR的某些读者是否会对这篇论文的发现感兴趣？是的。这篇论文提供的统一视角是有趣、相关且及时的。

**优点和缺点：**
优点：* 这篇论文的主要贡献在于，它为目前独立处理的三个机器学习子领域提供了一个统一的视角，而这些领域都解决了相同的根本问题。通过提供单一概述，研究人员可以查看为非常相似的任务提出的解决方案，避免重复劳动。* 该综述涵盖了一系列广泛的方法，我认为这些方法累积起来合理地代表了当前对此问题的理解。论文还经常绘制不同领域之间方法的类比，这也是其优点之一。* 对所讨论的多种方法进行了定量比较，特别是在OoD基准测试中。* 论文最后指出了异常检测研究的一系列有趣未来方向。缺点：* 论文缺乏对任务基准协议的具体和清晰定义。即每个数据集如何用于每个任务。这在OoD中有所体现，但在OSR和AD中不够充分。* 这篇论文遗漏了一些与其整体信息相关的重要方法。* 我认为论文中对OoD和OSR之间的区别/相似性表述不够清晰。* 论文中有一些错别字需要纠正。

**请求的更改：**
关键更改：* 基准协议：论文没有足够清楚地说明各领域如何进行评估。领域的实际差异最终由评估协议定义，这应该进行讨论。例如，所描述的数据集如何用于OoD和OSR，使用方式有何不同，这对我们理解方法有何影响？此外，对所描述方法在OSR和AD基准测试中进行定量比较也很重要（如果未重新实现，可以从文献中重新报告）。* OoD和OSR之间的区别：论文的OSR部分主要使用了关于该问题的经典工作[1]中的一些复杂术语。虽然应该提及这些术语，但文献中的主导评估协议很简单：取一个数据集；在部分类别上训练分类器；在测试时将其他类别检测为未见。这与OoD的设置极其相似：在数据集上训练分类器，在测试时将不同数据集检测为未见。事实上，CIFAR10 → CIFAR100评估几乎是相同的。这应该被突出，以保持清晰性，并强调论文的观点，即这些任务是相关的。* 重要缺失方法：1. Sohn等人[2]：这篇论文分析了SSL方法与AD分类器之间的关系，这与论文中讨论的许多工作相关。2. Kong等人[3]：这被简要提及，但我认为应该给予一个章节。据我所知，这是最强的开放集方法之一，并在语义分割/大规模数据集上展示了结果。3. Vaze等人[4]：这篇论文表明，在具有高封闭集准确性的分类器之上的简单“最大logit分数”基线在OSR中表现非常强。它还讨论了OoD和OSR之间的相似性/差异，并提出了新的具有挑战性的大规模基准测试。4. Sun等人[5]：这种方法被证明在本文讨论的多种方法（例如Energy, MSP, ODIN）之上一致提高了OoD性能。它还在大规模OoD基准测试上展示了结果。*注：[4]和[5]分别提出了针对OSR和OoD的大规模基准测试（分别针对语义偏移和低级分布偏移）。这在论文中被强调为重要的未来方向.* 其他更改：* 错别字：我在手稿中发现了许多错别字。尽管论文很长，作者应确保清理这些以改善可读性。我在这里突出了一小部分以供说明：（第4页）生成的图像的MSE损失 → 一个生成图像的MSE损失；（第8页）模型（h）可以实例化不同架构 → 模型（h）可以由不同架构实例化；（第13页）模型半空间不够紧 → 模型半空间不够紧；（第21页）maxs1, …,sn → max(s1, …,sn)；（第32页）倒数第二层的特征空间 → 倒数第二层的特征空间。* 值得引用的内容：1. Yang等人[6]。这篇同时期的综述也涵盖了AD/OSR/OoD。尽管是预印本，但为了读者的兴趣和表明社区在此方向上的动向，值得强调。2. 论文强调“开放世界识别”是一个重要的未来方向。根据描述，我认为新奇类别发现[7]/开放世界半监督学习[8]/广义类别发现[9]的任务是相关的。3. 应提及RPL的“对抗性”后续工作[10]。尽管与RPL（已讨论）相关，但它提高了性能，并在OoD基准测试上进行了评估（尽管是OSR方法）。* 不清楚图1如何与标题匹配。该图应为AD/OSR/OoD标注，并给出每个的ID/OoD示例。* 论文中提到AUPR在OSR中“通常”使用。根据我的经验，这不是真的，AUROC是主要报告的。此外，OSR论文中通常未报告ID准确度，这可以提及吗？* “OoD”部分（例如对Nalisnick等人描述）提到生成模型为异常值分配更高的似然性。这与文献中其他地方成功使用生成模型（例如讨论的OpenHybrid OSR方法）如何协调？* 表6标题中未指定指标。[1] 开放集识别的概率模型，Scheirer等人，TPAMI 2014 [2] 深度单类分类的表示学习和评估，Sohn等人，ICLR 2021 [3] OpenGan：通过开放数据生成进行开放集识别，ICCV 2021 [4]：开放集识别：一个好的封闭集分类器就是你所需要的？Vaze等人，ICLR 2022 [5] React：利用整流激活进行分布外检测，Sun等人，NeurIPS 2021 [6] 广义分布外检测，Yang等人，ArXiv预印本2021 [7] 通过深度迁移聚类学习发现新奇视觉类别，Han等人，ICCV 2019 [8] 开放世界半监督学习，Cao等人，ICLR 2022 [9] 广义类别发现，Vaze等人，CVPR 2022 [10] 开放集识别的对抗互惠点，Chen等人，TPAMI 2021

**更广泛的影响关注：**
我认为论文中已经充分强调了更广泛的影响。
