paper_title: (Semi)automated approaches to data extraction for systematic reviews and meta-analyses in social sciences: A living review
paper_abstract:
Background 
     An abundance of rapidly accumulating scientific evidence presents novel opportunities for researchers and practitioners alike, yet such advantages are often overshadowed by resource demands associated with finding and aggregating a continually expanding body of scientific information. Data extraction activities associated with evidence synthesis have been described as time-consuming to the point of critically limiting the usefulness of research. Across social science disciplines, the use of automation technologies for timely and accurate knowledge synthesis can enhance research translation value, better inform key policy development, and expand the current understanding of human interactions, organizations, and systems. Ongoing developments surrounding automation are highly concentrated in research for evidence-based medicine with limited evidence surrounding tools and techniques applied outside of the clinical research community. The goal of the present study is to extend the automation knowledge base by synthesizing current trends in the application of extraction technologies of key data elements of interest for social scientists. 
   
   
     Methods 
     We report the baseline results of a living systematic review of automated data extraction techniques supporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses in the social sciences. This review follows PRISMA standards for reporting systematic reviews. 
   
   
     Results 
     The baseline review of social science research yielded 23 relevant studies. 
   
   
     Conclusions 
     When considering the process of automating systematic review and meta-analysis information extraction, social science research falls short as compared to clinical research that focuses on automatic processing of information related to the PICO framework. With a few exceptions, most tools were either in the infancy stage and not accessible to applied researchers, were domain specific, or required substantial manual coding of articles before automation could occur. Additionally, few solutions considered extraction of data from tables which is where key data elements reside that social and behavioral scientists analyze.
review_content:
This manuscript represents an important contribution to the evidence synthesis methodology. Given the rise of AI technology, a living evidence base on approaches to data extraction will be very useful. However, the manuscript could benefit from improved clarity. Below are my comments:
 1. Title:
     1. Clarify the type of data being extracted (qualitative, quantitative, or mixed).
     2. Since this review does not include any qualitative or quantitative synthesis per se, but rather provides an overview of the field (methods for semi-automated data extraction), I suggest removing "living systematic review" and adding "living systematic map."
 2. Abstract:
     1. The summary of methods could include more detailed information on searches, screening, critical appraisal, and synthesis. Please specify which standards for review conduct were followed.
     2. The summary of results could provide more information (briefly) about the included studies.
 3. Keywords:
     1. Avoid repeating terms already present in the title
 4. Introduction:
     1. The focus of this review—extraction tools for quantitative data—should be more explicitly stated. This emphasis needs to be clearer in the introduction and reflected in the title, as mentioned earlier. Specifically, the first paragraph of the Introduction should be revised to concentrate on the review topic—quantitative data extraction and existing tools—rather than a general introduction to meta-science or related areas.
     2. Additional details are needed on how this review contributes to and complements existing reviews on the topic. This information should be included in the "Related Research" section.
 5. Objectives:
     1. It would be helpful to define what is included under “social science research domains”.
 6. Methods:
     1. Authors should be transparent and explicit about the guidelines and standards for both conduct and reporting that were used. Please clarify this at the beginig of the Methods section.
     2. The methods section should begin by addressing any deviations from the protocol. If there were no deviations, this should be clearly stated as well.
     3. Did you use any automation technologies to screen or select studies for this review? If yes, please clarify.
 7. Methods/Eligibility criteria:
     1. The eligibility criteria should be explicit about the field within which methods for (semi)automated data extraction are applied.
     2. A definition of “(semi)automated” is needed. The eligibility criteria currently state that semi-automated approaches will be eligible but then refer to “any automated approach to data extraction” in the next sentence. This needs to be clarified—are the focus and criteria on semi-automated or automated approaches? Be more explicit and precise in the description of the eligibility criteria, and ensure alignment with the protocol.
     3. Instead of “We excluded studies labeled as editorials, briefs..” you may write “Editorials, briefs, …were not considered eligible” (and similar changes may be applied to the following sentence)
 8. Methods/Searches
     1. Be explicit about the citation indices included in your Web of Science subscription and note which library was used to access WoS. This will increase transparency and replicability of your searches.
     2. Clarify why following Schmidt et al.'s search strategy was important, given the different scope of this review. Consider including more social science databases to ensure comprehensive coverage. Did you include the Social Science Citation Index (within WoS)?
     3. Provide explanations for all abbreviations (IEEE, ACL, etc.) in the text.
 9. Methods/Study selection
     1. Clarify if three researchers simultaneously screened titles and abstracts (TA), and whether inter-rater reliability (IRR) was calculated for TA screening. How you trained reviewers to apply eligibility criteria?
     2. The sentence, “In cases where level of abstraction and potential for transferability could not be determined from the abstract alone, full text articles were reviewed and discussed by all three researchers until consensus was reached”, should more clearly state that there was NO full-text screening of all records (if this is correct), only of a sub-sample where abstracts did not clearly describe AI technology, etc.
     3. Relatedly, Figure 1 should be adjusted to avoid giving the false impression that all records were screened in full text.
     4. This review seems to involve META-data extraction rather than DATA extraction. Please adjust the text and figures accordingly.
     5. It is not clear if IRR assessments were conducted for meta-data extraction. Please clarify/be explicit. If IRR was not done, describe how researchers were trained to use the extraction form.
     6. The sentence, “coding forms allowed for input of “other” responses (e.g., APA data elements) that were not included in extant reviews that focus on medical and clinical data extraction (e.g., PICO elements)” is unclear. Consider removing or clarifying and linking it better with the rest of the text.
     7. Describe the procedure for screening and meta-data extraction of studies authored by the review team.
10. Methods/Critical appraisal and Synthesis
     1. These sections are missing. Please state clearly if a critical appraisal of included studies was conducted and if so, how was it performed. Also, describe how synthesis was conducted.
11. Results/Challenges
     1. Clarify that the described challenges reflect issues within the body of evidence included in this (baseline) review (otherwise this section can be mixed up with review limitations).
12. Conclusions/Limitations
     1. Organize limitations into those related to the methodology used and those related to the evidence base.
     2. Discuss limitations related to the focus on publications in English, the inexhaustive list of search sources, and the lack of grey literature.
paper_title_zh: 社会科学中系统综述和元分析的（半）自动化数据提取方法：一项动态综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
大量迅速积累的科学证据为研究人员和从业者提供了新的机遇，然而，这些优势往往被与寻找和整合不断扩展的科学信息体相关的资源需求所掩盖。与证据综合相关的数据提取活动被描述为耗时过长，以至于严重限制了研究的实用性。在社会科学各学科中，自动化技术的使用可以及时准确地合成知识，增强研究转化价值，更好地为关键政策制定提供信息，并扩展对人类互动、组织和系统的当前理解。围绕自动化的持续发展主要集中在基于证据的医学研究上，而关于在临床研究社区之外应用的工具和技术的证据有限。本研究的目的是通过综合当前社会科学感兴趣的关键数据元素提取技术的应用趋势，扩展自动化知识库。

方法
我们报告了一项针对支持社会科学系统评价和元分析的自动化数据提取技术的动态系统评价的基线结果。本次评价遵循PRISMA标准进行系统评价报告。

结果
社会科学研究的基线评价共获得23项相关研究。

结论
在考虑自动化系统评价和元分析信息提取过程时，社会科学研究相较于专注于PICO框架相关信息自动处理的临床研究显得不足。除少数例外，大多数工具要么处于初期阶段且不适用于应用研究人员，要么具有领域特异性，或者需要在自动化之前对文章进行大量手动编码。此外，很少有解决方案考虑从表格中提取数据，而社会科学和行为科学家分析的关键数据元素正存在于这些表格中。
review_content_zh:
该手稿对证据综合方法论做出了重要贡献。鉴于人工智能技术的兴起，关于数据提取方法的动态证据库将非常有用。然而，该手稿在清晰度方面仍有提升空间。以下是我的评论：

1. 标题：
   1. 明确所提取数据的类型（定性、定量或混合）。
   2. 由于该综述本身并未包含任何定性或定量综合，而是提供了该领域的概述（半自动化数据提取方法），我建议删除“动态系统综述”并添加“动态系统地图”。

2. 摘要：
   1. 方法总结可以包含更多关于检索、筛选、批判性评估和综合的详细信息。请指明遵循了哪些综述 conduct 标准。
   2. 结果总结可以提供更多关于所包含研究的简要信息。

3. 关键词：
   1. 避免重复标题中已出现的术语。

4. 引言：
   1. 该综述的重点——定量数据提取工具——应更明确地陈述。这一重点需要在引言中更清晰地体现，并在标题中反映出来，如前所述。具体而言，引言的第一段应修订为集中讨论综述主题——定量数据提取及现有工具，而非元科学或相关领域的泛泛介绍。
   2. 需要更多细节说明该综述如何对现有相关综述进行补充和贡献。这些信息应包含在“相关研究”部分。

5. 目标：
   1. 定义“社会科学研究领域”包含的内容将有所帮助。

6. 方法：
   1. 作者应透明且明确地说明所使用的 conduct 和报告指南及标准。请在方法部分开头澄清这一点。
   2. 方法部分应首先说明与方案的任何偏差。如果没有偏差，也应明确指出。
   3. 在本综述中是否使用了任何自动化技术来筛选或选择研究？如果有，请澄清。

7. 方法/资格标准：
   1. 资格标准应明确（半）自动化数据提取方法应用的领域。
   2. 需要“（半）自动化”的定义。资格标准目前指出半自动化方法将符合资格，但下一句提到“任何自动化数据提取方法”。这需要澄清——重点是半自动化还是自动化方法？在资格标准的描述中应更明确和精确，并确保与方案一致。
   3. 可以将“我们排除了标记为社论、简报...”改为“社论、简报...不被视为符合资格”（类似的修改可应用于下一句）。

8. 方法/检索：
   1. 明确包含在 Web of Science 订阅中的引文索引，并注明使用哪个图书馆访问 WoS。这将增加检索的透明度和可复制性。
   2. 澄清为何遵循 Schmidt 等人的检索策略很重要，鉴于本综述的不同范围。考虑包括更多社会科学数据库以确保全面覆盖。是否包括了社会科学引文索引（在 WoS 内）？
   3. 在文本中解释所有缩写（IEEE、ACL 等）。

9. 方法/研究选择：
   1. 澄清是否三名研究人员同时筛选标题和摘要（TA），以及是否计算了 TA 筛选的评分者间信度（IRR）。如何培训评审员应用资格标准？
   2. 句子“在仅从摘要中无法确定抽象层次和可转移性潜力的案例中，全文文章由三名研究人员审查和讨论直至达成共识”应更明确地说明没有对所有记录进行全文筛选（如果这是正确的），仅对摘要未明确描述 AI 技术等的子样本进行了全文筛选。
   3. 相关地，图 1 应调整以避免给人所有记录都进行了全文筛选的错误印象。
   4. 该综述似乎涉及元数据提取而非数据提取。请相应调整文本和图表。
   5. 不清楚是否对元数据提取进行了 IRR 评估。请澄清/明确。如果未进行 IRR，描述如何培训研究人员使用提取表。
   6. 句子“编码表允许输入‘其他’响应（例如，APA 数据元素），这些响应未包含在专注于医学和临床数据提取的现有综述中（例如，PICO 元素）”不清楚。考虑删除或澄清，并更好地与文本其余部分链接。
   7. 描述由综述团队撰写的研究的筛选和元数据提取程序。

10. 方法/批判性评估和综合：
    1. 这些部分缺失。请明确说明是否对所包含研究进行了批判性评估，如果是，如何进行的。同时描述综合是如何进行的。

11. 结果/挑战：
    1. 澄清所描述的挑战反映了本（基线）综述所包含证据体中的问题（否则该部分可能会与综述局限性混淆）。

12. 结论/局限性：
    1. 将局限性组织为与方法论相关的和与证据基础相关的两部分。
    2. 讨论与关注英语出版物、检索来源不全面以及缺乏灰色文献相关的局限性。

paper_title: Cardiovascular protection effect of chlorogenic acid: focus on the molecular mechanism
paper_abstract: Vascular endothelial cells have a variety of functions such as the control of blood coagulation, vascular permeability, and tone regulation, as well as quiesce of immune cells. Endothelial dysfunction is a cardiovascular events predictor, which is considered the initial stage in atherosclerosis development. It is characterized by alterations in endothelium functions due to imbalanced vasodilators and vasoconstrictors, procoagulant and anticoagulant mediators, as well as growth inhibitor and promotor substances. Chlorogenic acid (CGA) is the primary polyphenol in coffee and some fruits. It has many health-promoting properties, especially in the cardiovascular system. Many studies investigated the efficacy and mechanism of this compound in vascular health. CGA has several vascular benefits such as anti-atherosclerosis, anti-thrombosis, and anti-hypertensive. This review focuses on the molecular mechanism of CGA in vascular health.
review_content:
This is a very comprehensive review of CGA in cardiovascular health and diseases. By reading through the whole manuscript, the message conveyed is scattered and not focused. For example, the authors can divide the Atherosclerosis related mechanisms into sub-sections: endothelial dysfunction, macrophage inflammation and foam cell formation, VSMC dysfunction, platelet activation etc. How other CVD protective actions, the authors can talk about cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure, as CVD is very broad, it is hard to give concise review and discussion on all forms of CVD. I would suggest to focus on hypertension and atherosclerosis in particular. The detailed molecular targets of CGA can be given in a pictorial way as new figures which is very important.

It is also good to include are there any clinical trials of CGA in Clinicaltrial.gov? What are unexplored and important in CGA research? In particular, CGA functions as more than antioxidant, which failed in most clinical trials.
paper_title_zh: 氯原酸的心血管保护作用：聚焦分子机制
paper_abstract_zh: 血管内皮细胞具有多种功能，如控制血液凝固、血管通透性、张力调节以及免疫细胞的静止。内皮功能障碍是心血管事件的预测因子，被认为是动脉粥样硬化发展的初始阶段。其特征在于内皮功能的变化，这是由于血管扩张剂和血管收缩剂、促凝和抗凝介质以及生长抑制因子和促进物质的失衡所致。绿原酸（CGA）是咖啡和一些水果中的主要多酚。它具有许多促进健康的特性，尤其是在心血管系统中。许多研究探讨了该化合物在血管健康中的功效和机制。CGA具有多种血管益处，如抗动脉粥样硬化、抗血栓和抗高血压。本综述重点探讨了CGA在血管健康中的分子机制。
review_content_zh:
这是一篇关于CGA在心血管健康与疾病中的非常全面的综述。通读整篇手稿后，发现传达的信息较为分散且缺乏重点。例如，作者可以将动脉粥样硬化相关的机制分为几个小节：内皮功能障碍、巨噬细胞炎症和泡沫细胞形成、血管平滑肌细胞（VSMC）功能障碍、血小板激活等。对于其他心血管疾病（CVD）的保护作用，作者可以讨论心脏肥大和心力衰竭，因为CVD范围非常广泛，很难对所有形式的CVD进行简洁的综述和讨论。我建议特别关注高血压和动脉粥样硬化。CGA的详细分子靶点可以以图片形式作为新图呈现，这一点非常重要。

此外，还应包括Clinicaltrial.gov上是否有CGA的临床试验？CGA研究中尚未探索且重要的方面是什么？特别是，CGA的功能不仅仅是抗氧化剂，这在大多数临床试验中并未成功。

paper_title: Understanding fine dining restaurant dynamics in south Asia: A systematic review
paper_abstract:
Background 
 Globalization, urbanization, and economic development has had an influence on the dining out behaviour in general and fine dining in particular. The objective of this systematic review is identifying the factors affecting fine dining selection and to understand the fine dining restaurant dynamics. 
 
 
 Methods 
 In the context of fine dining, both quantitative and qualitative studies conducted in South Asian countries—Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka—were included in this review. The review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and summarised using narrative synthesis. The search was conducted on Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE (PubMed) and Google Scholar. The two-stage screening was independently done by two authors in two stages (titles/abstracts, and full texts) for inclusion, with discrepancies resolved by involvement of a third reviewer. Data was extracted using a piloted form and the results are presented as a narrative summary and in tabular format. 
 
 
 Results 
 Fourteen studies met the eligibility criteria after de-duplication and screening and were included in the review. These studies were conducted in Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan and were mostly quantitative in nature. The outcomes assessed in the studies were factors affecting decision to choose fine dine restaurant, customer satisfaction, customer loyalty, willingness to pay, and food wastage. 
 
 
 Conclusion 
 There is limited literature on types of evidence available related to fine dining in South Asia. The substantial gap extends to the methodological aspect and the outcomes assessed in the fine dining restaurant segment.
review_content:
I find the present article interesting and parsimonious. The authors have clearly stated the objective of identifying the factors affecting fine dining selection in South Asia. The authors also provided adequate justification for conducting the present literature review when two LRs existed. Still, none investigated South Asia, and one of the LRs only examined food service selection factors. Hence, the need for the study is apt and in line with the scope of the journal and extant literature.

PRISMA Methodology has been used to filter and select the articles, which is a standard methodology, and proper steps were taken to screen duplicate and irrelevant articles. Further, any other researcher can replicate the study.

The authors used thematic analysis to segregate the filtered key studies, and dominant themes were examined to find gaps and future research areas. The study aptly concludes that Despite the importance of restaurant choice criteria and growth in the hospitality sector, there are limited published empirical studies on fine dining in South Asia.

Based on rigour and deep analysis, I would recommend the study for acceptance in the journal.
paper_title_zh: 理解南亚精致餐饮业动态：系统综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
全球化、城市化和经济发展对一般外出就餐行为尤其是高档餐饮产生了影响。本系统综述的目的是识别影响高档餐饮选择的因素，并理解高档餐饮餐厅的动态。

方法
在高档餐饮的背景下，本研究综述包括了在南亚国家——阿富汗、孟加拉国、不丹、印度、马尔代夫、尼泊尔、巴基斯坦和斯里兰卡——进行的定量和定性研究。综述遵循系统综述和荟萃分析的首选报告项目（PRISMA）进行，并使用叙述性综合进行总结。搜索在Scopus、Web of Science、MEDLINE（PubMed）和Google Scholar上进行。两阶段筛选由两位作者独立进行（标题/摘要和全文），纳入标准不一致之处由第三位评审员解决。数据使用预先测试的表格提取，结果以叙述性总结和表格形式呈现。

结果
经过去重和筛选，共有14项研究符合纳入标准并纳入综述。这些研究在孟加拉国、印度、尼泊尔和巴基斯坦进行，且大多为定量研究。研究中评估的结局包括影响选择高档餐饮餐厅的因素、顾客满意度、顾客忠诚度、支付意愿和食物浪费。

结论
关于南亚地区高档餐饮的相关证据类型文献有限。这一显著差距延伸到方法论方面以及高档餐饮餐厅细分市场中评估的结局。

基于严谨和深入的分析，我建议接受该研究在期刊上发表。

paper_title: Osteokines and the vasculature: a review of the in vitro effects of osteocalcin, fibroblast growth factor-23 and lipocalin-2
paper_abstract: Bone-derived factors that demonstrate extra-skeletal functions, also termed osteokines, are fast becoming a highly interesting and focused area of cross-disciplinary endocrine research. Osteocalcin (OCN), fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF23) and lipocalin-2 (LCN-2), produced in bone, comprise an important endocrine system that is finely tuned with other organs to ensure homeostatic balance and health. This review aims to evaluate in vitro evidence of the direct involvement of these proteins in vascular cells and whether any causal roles in cardiovascular disease or inflammation can be supported. PubMed, Medline, Embase and Google Scholar were searched for relevant research articles investigating the exogenous addition of OCN, FGF23 or LCN-2 to vascular smooth muscle or endothelial cells. Overall, these osteokines are directly vasoactive across a range of human and animal vascular cells. Both OCN and FGF23 have anti-apoptotic properties and increase eNOS phosphorylation and nitric oxide production through Akt signalling in human endothelial cells. OCN improves intracellular insulin signalling and demonstrates protective effects against endoplasmic reticulum stress in murine and human endothelial cells. OCN may be involved in calcification but further research is warranted, while there is no evidence for a pro-calcific effect of FGF23 in vitro. FGF23 and LCN-2 increase proliferation in some cell types and increase and decrease reactive oxygen species generation, respectively. LCN-2 also has anti-apoptotic effects but may increase endoplasmic reticulum stress as well as have pro-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic properties in human vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells. There is no strong evidence to support a pathological role of OCN or FGF23 in the vasculature based on these findings. In contrast, they may in fact support normal endothelial functioning, vascular homeostasis and vasodilation. No studies examined whether OCN or FGF23 may have a role in vascular inflammation. Limited studies with LCN-2 indicate a pro-inflammatory and possible pathological role in the vasculature but further mechanistic data is required. Overall, these osteokines pose intriguing functions which should be investigated comprehensively to
review_content: Reviewer 3 (Anonymous) Basic reporting Thank you so much for taking the time to review our manuscript and for your suggestions which are very much appreciated. Please find replies to individual comments blow. In this review, the authors introduced and discussed the in vitro effects of OCN, FGF23 and LCN2. They focused on the function of these genes in vasculature including the effects on vascular-related cells. In general, this review was well written with sufficient information and discussion. I have only some suggestions: 1. LCN2 plays an important role in neuroinflammation as well as blood brain barrier. Currently the authors only mentioned these points in a pretty simple way. Could the authors talk more about this since blood brain barrier is related to the topic of vasculature? It should attract more researchers working in these fields. Thank you for this comment and your insight. Although LCN-2 has been indicated to be a major player in brain injury/inflammation such as after ischemia/reperfusion – this is attributed to local secretion of LCN-2, as opposed to skeletal excretion and transport through the BBB (e.g. see https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4126090/). As such, we didn’t feel it was within the scope of this review to go into further detail about these effects. I hope this is satisfactory but please don’t’ hesitate in letting us know if a more specific sentence should be added to benefit the manuscript. 2. Could the authors make a table and put OCN, FGF23 and LCN2 side by side to summarize the expression pattern of these three genes? Thank you for your comment. Upon reflection of another reviewer’s suggestion we have actually removed the data on expression of these osteokines. The reason for this is to try and keep the manuscript focused and we were encouraged to remove superfluous information that was not relevant to the interpretation of the in vitro data in vascular cells. We hope you will approve of this decision however do let us know if you think a table as suggested should still be included and would be beneficial for the review.
paper_title_zh: 骨因子与血管系统：骨钙素、成纤维细胞生长因子-23和脂质运载蛋白-2体外效应综述

review_content_zh:

paper_title: Automated language essay scoring systems: A Literature Review
paper_abstract: Background.Writing composition is a significant factor for measuring test-takers' ability in any language exam. However, the assessment (scoring) of these writing compositions or essays is a very challenging process in terms of reliability and time. The need for objective and quick scores has raised the need for a computer system that can automatically grade essay questions targeting specific prompts. Automated Essay Scoring (AES) systems are used to overcome the challenges of scoring writing tasks by using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques. The purpose of this paper is to review the literature for the AES systems used for grading the essay questions.Methodology.We have reviewed the existing literature using Google Scholar, EBSCO and ERIC to search for the terms "AES", "Automated Essay Scoring", "Automated Essay Grading", or "Automatic Essay" for essays written in English language. Two categories have been identified: handcrafted features and automatically featured AES systems. The systems of the former category are closely bonded to the quality of the designed features. On the other hand, the systems of the latter category are based on the automatic learning of the features and relations between an essay and its score without any handcrafted features. We reviewed the systems of the two categories in terms of system primary focus, technique(s) used in the system, the need for training data, instructional application (feedback system), and the correlation between e-scores and human scores. The paper includes three main sections.
review_content: Reviewer 1 Basic reporting The manuscript brings an excellent review on automated scoring systems, providing the most relevant items in the literature put into context. There is also a fair amount of discussion about the strengths and limitations of existing systems. Overall, the manuscript is likely to be useful for anyone investigating intelligent systems associated with text analytics. Experimental design The study was well designed with a systematic search of automated scoring systems, which were then divided into broad categories to facilitate readability. The review is also organized in a logical manner. Validity of the findings The findings were reported in a straightforward manner, making it easy for the readers to grasp the most important developments in the field. Comments for the author This is an excellent review, and my only recommendation is a careful proofreading of the manuscript. There are a few typos that need to be corrected, in addition to inadequate usage of some terms (e.g. "In the other hand", rather than "On the other hand").
paper_title_zh: 自动化语言作文评分系统：文献综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景。写作 composition 是衡量任何语言考试考生能力的重要因素。然而，这些写作 composition 或 essay 的评估（评分）在可靠性和时间方面是一个非常具有挑战性的过程。对客观和快速评分的需求引发了对一个计算机系统的需求，该系统能够自动评分针对特定提示的 essay 问题。自动作文评分（AES）系统通过使用自然语言处理（NLP）和机器学习技术来克服评分写作任务的挑战。本文的目的是回顾用于评分 essay 问题的 AES 系统的文献。

方法。我们通过使用 Google Scholar、EBSCO 和 ERIC 搜索“AES”、“Automated Essay Scoring”、“Automated Essay Grading”或“Automatic Essay”等术语，回顾了现有的关于用英语写作的 essay 的文献。确定了两个类别：手工特征和自动特征 AES 系统。前一类系统的性能与设计特征的质量密切相关。另一方面，后一类系统基于特征的自动学习和 essay 及其评分之间的关系，而无需任何手工特征。我们从系统主要关注点、系统使用的技术、对训练数据的需求、教学应用（反馈系统）以及 e-评分与人工评分之间的相关性等方面回顾了这两个类别的系统。本文包括三个主要部分。

paper_title: Research and development of new tuberculosis vaccines: a review
paper_abstract: Tuberculosis kills more people worldwide than any other single infectious disease agent, a threat made more dire by the spread of drug-resistant strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) . Development of new vaccines capable of preventing TB disease and new Mtb infection are an essential component of the strategy to combat the TB epidemic. Accordingly, the WHO considers the development of new TB vaccines a major public health priority. In October 2017, the WHO convened a consultation with global leaders in the TB vaccine development field to emphasize the WHO commitment to this effort and to facilitate creative approaches to the discovery and development of TB vaccine candidates. This review summarizes the presentations at this consultation, updated with scientific literature references, and includes discussions of the public health need for a TB vaccine; the status of efforts to develop vaccines to replace or potentiate BCG in infants and develop new TB vaccines for adolescents and adults; strategies being employed to diversify vaccine platforms; and new animal models being developed to facilitate TB vaccine development. A perspective on the status of these efforts from the major funders and organizational contributors also is included. This presentation highlights the extraordinary progress being made to develop new TB vaccines and provided a clear picture of the exciting development pathways that are being explored.
review_content:
The review article has covered the problem statement, the need for the development of new vaccines and the newer vaccines in phase 2 and 3 very well. This article covers the newer platform i.e. mRNA and new viral vector hCMV for vaccine delivery. The authors have also elaborated on immune mechanisms stimulated in response to Mtb including HLA E, CD1a, antibody response in addition to MHC I and II responses. These mechanisms are targeted by newer vaccine candidates to generate an immune response in adults and adolescents.

The review also covers the use of advanced assessment techniques, including transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics for identifying newer biomarkers for identifying active disease and can further be used to assess vaccine efficacy and safety. The article also highlights alternative routes of immunization and discusses BCG revaccination status.

However, it would be helpful if the following points are discussed in the review:
 1. Role of DNA vaccines (Tian et al., 20181 and Bruffaerts et al., 20142).
 2. 231 subcultures in place of 230 subcultures over 13 years to develop BCG on page 7 (Norouzi et al., 20123).
paper_title_zh: 新型结核病疫苗的研究与开发：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 结核病在全球范围内导致的死亡人数超过任何其他单一传染性疾病病原体，而耐药性结核分枝杆菌（Mtb）株的传播使得这一威胁更加严峻。开发能够预防结核病和新Mtb感染的新疫苗是应对结核病流行策略的重要组成部分。因此，世界卫生组织（WHO）将新结核病疫苗的研发视为重大公共卫生优先事项。2017年10月，WHO召集了结核病疫苗研发领域的全球领导者进行磋商，以强调WHO对此努力的承诺，并促进发现和开发结核病疫苗候选物的创新方法。本文综述了此次磋商中的报告，并更新了科学文献参考，包括对公共卫生对结核病疫苗需求的讨论；旨在替代或增强婴儿卡介苗（BCG）以及开发针对青少年和成人新结核病疫苗的努力现状；正在采用的多样化疫苗平台策略；以及为促进结核病疫苗研发而开发的新动物模型。此外，还包含了主要资助者和组织贡献者对这些努力现状的视角。此次报告突显了在开发新结核病疫苗方面取得的非凡进展，并清晰地描绘了正在探索的激动人心的发展路径。
review_content_zh:
该综述文章很好地涵盖了问题陈述、新疫苗开发的必要性以及处于2期和3期的新疫苗。本文介绍了较新的平台，即mRNA和用于疫苗递送的新病毒载体hCMV。作者还详细阐述了针对Mtb（结核分枝杆菌）的免疫机制，包括HLA E、CD1a以及抗体反应，除了MHC I和II的反应。这些机制是新疫苗候选物针对成人和青少年产生免疫反应的目标。

综述还涵盖了先进评估技术的使用，包括转录组学、蛋白质组学和代谢组学，用于识别新的生物标志物，以识别活动性疾病，并可用于评估疫苗的有效性和安全性。文章还强调了免疫的替代途径，并讨论了BCG复种的情况。

然而，如果综述中讨论以下内容将会有所帮助：

2. 在第7页上，用231次亚培养代替230次亚培养，历时13年开发BCG（Norouzi等，20123）。

paper_title: Stochastic computing in convolutional neural network implementation: A review
paper_abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) is an alternative computing domain for ubiquitous deterministic computing whereby a single logic gate can perform the arithmetic operation by exploiting the nature of probability math. SC was proposed in the 1960s when binary computing was expensive. However, presently, SC started to regain interest after the widespread of deep learning application, specifically the convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm due to its practicality in hardware implementation. Although not all computing functions can translate to the SC domain, several useful function blocks related to the CNN algorithm had been proposed and tested by researchers. An evolution of CNN, namely, binarised neural network, had also gained attention in the edge computing due to its compactness and computing efficiency. This study reviews various SC CNN hardware implementation methodologies. Firstly, we review the fundamental concepts of SC and the circuit structure and then compare the advantages and disadvantages amongst different SC methods.
review_content: Reviewer 3 Comments for the Author This review article introduces stochastic computing and deep learning, especially CNN based SC methods. This is quite helpful for these researchers in this field. 1, English writing should be improved. Some statistical results should be shown in tables instead of sentences. The author acknowledged that and will further improve the writing standard. As for the statistical results, an additional table is included for clarification on the statistical data stated in the previous sentences. 2, More recent researches should be introduced for better description. The author acknowledged the lacking of the contents and included more relevant and recent researches for a comprehensive description of the field of study.
paper_title_zh: 卷积神经网络实现中的随机计算：综述

paper_title: Effects of mental health interventions for students in higher education are sustainable over time: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
paper_abstract: Background. Symptoms of depression, anxiety, and distress are more common in undergraduates compared to age-matched peers. Mental ill health among students is associated with impaired academic achievement, worse occupational preparedness, and lower future occupational performance. Research on mental health promoting and mental ill health preventing interventions has shown promising short-term effects, though the sustainability of intervention benefits deserve closer attention. We aimed to identify, appraise and summarize existing data from RCTs reporting on whether the effects of mental health promoting and mental ill health preventing interventions sustained at least 3 months post-intervention, and to analyse how the effects vary for different outcomes in relation to follow-up length. Further, we aimed to assess whether the effect sustainability varied by intervention type, study-level determinants and of participant characteristics.
review_content: Reviewer 1(Anonymous) Basic reporting In general the language is clear and professional throughout. However, I have some comments and suggestions for improvements: - In the abstract, change the heading Conclusion to Discussion. We have changed the heading from “Conclusion” to “Discussion” in the abstract. - Line 58: To state that a thing is common or has high prevalence without specifying how common or high is annoying. Introduction, line 65: The two first sentences have been clarified and prevalence rates reported for depression, depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation have been added. Additionally, we have added two references on original studies (Steptoe et al. 2007, Garlow et al. 2008) and a reference to a recently published systematic review and meta-analysis on depression prevalence among nursing students (Tung et al. 2018). - Line 66: Is it really higher risk groups and not groups with higher risk? Introduction, line 78: We have revised the sentence as suggested: “Female students, minority groups and students with financial problems constitute groups with higher risks (Cvetkovski et al. 2012; Eisenberg et al. 2013; Said et al. 2013).” - Merge sentences lines 92-93 Introduction, 119: We have merged the last two sentences in the aims. - Check heading of Table 2 and Figure 3. The headings of Table 2 and Figure 3 have been clarified. To attain consistency in entitling tables and figures, we have also amended the headings for Table 3 and Figure 2. Finally, we have slightly amended the heading for Table 1 to make it more self-explanatory. - The layout of Tables could be improved by not using marked lines for every row and column. Also the authors could consider using background coloring of e.g. every other row. We agree and have removed the marked lines for columns and rows in all tables included in the manuscript. Further, we have used background colouring in order to visualise grouped categories. Introduction While the introduction gives the context to mental ill health – literature being well referenced and relevant – no corresponding context is given to positive mental health. There is no theoretical conceptualization of positive mental health, which would give the rationale for including (or not) certain outcomes as measures of positive mental health. Just because there are records of studies in the literature and methods to make effects of intervention sustainability across studies “statistically comparable” using standardized units, it doesn´t necessarily make them meaningful to include in a meta-analysis. Thus, if the authors want to keep positive mental health they should provide the relevant context and conceptualization that justify the outcomes included in the analyses and why they think they are meaningful to pool. If they do this my guess is that it will become evident that the scope of the study is better limited to mental ill health and related endpoints meaningful in a meta-analysis. Introduction, line 92: We realize that the concept of positive mental health could have been further described. To strengthen the rationale for including positive mental health outcomes in the review, we have introduced the theoretical conceptualization of positive mental health, and its suitability for mental health promotion. Further, we have explained the importance of including preventive as well as promoting interventions to form an integrative population mental health that includes both aspects; mental ill-health and positive mental health. Our effort to pool the positive mental health outcomes arose from our aim to describe the complete mental concept. The outcomes included in the latter are evidence based predictors and are further described line 133. Experimental design The research is original and within the aims and scope of the journal. However, the research question (s) could be better defined. It is unclear what is meant by mental health and mental ill health, for example. To clarify the research question, we have added information on the concept and aspects of positive mental health (line 92), its suitability for mental health promotion as well as on its relation to mental ill-health. The concept of mental ill health has been clarified on line 74. Our outcomes of interest are not diagnoses but self-reports, and restricted to symptoms of anxiety, symptoms of depression, psychological distress, worry, fatigue, sleeping problems, and perceived stress. The outcomes for positive mental health and mental ill health as part of the PICO have been earlier described, line 133. Also I do not like the part of the aim that addresses the implementation quality. While implementation quality is (!) important and should be brought to attention I do not think this is the way to do it. The reason is that RCT:s usually do not report implementation components which could lead to a bias in an assessment of such quality. We agree. Following your argumentation, we have reconsidered the appropriateness of our data collection for investigating the implementation quality. Therefore, we have removed the corresponding aim as well as all sentences/paragraphs that dealt with implementation quality and the corresponding references. Further, it could be stated more clearly how the present systematic review and meta-analysis differs from the previous ones (line 87). The authors refer to three previous reviews (Conley et al 2015, 2016, 2017) and it would have been easy to describe each of them more in detail. The present description makes it difficult to know what specifically their review adds. Since the referred reviews of Conley et al are recently published this becomes really important because it is the part where the novelty of the study should be stated clearly. We have revised the corresponding sentences to clarify the issue. In recently published reviews, Conley et al have proposed several directions for future research. One of them was a need for further investigation of intervention benefit sustainability during variable follow-up periods. It was based on the observations that the effects of interventions may change their direction and magnitude during follow-up (i.e. depending on intervention, the benefits may diminish or increase over time or only appear at follow-up) (Conley et al. 2015, 2016, 2017). Being inspired by Conley et al. ideas and, in order to address their call for further research, we have focused on assessing the effect sustainability at some post-intervention follow-up “landmarks”, i.e. 3 – 6 months, 7 – 12 months and 13- 18 months. First, our aim was to focus on the sustainability of intervention effects over time. This research expansion has been warranted by Conley et al. 2015. Second, we wanted to base our results on randomized controlled trials and not including quasi-experimental study designs as others have done. Third, the included original studies have undergone a thorough and transparent quality assessment which is presented. Point one and two are highlighted in our aims, and the sustainability issue has been further elucidated (line 107). Hopefully, this description will clarify what our review adds. The methods are described with sufficient detail and information to replicate. An exception though, is found on line 106. Since there are multiple guidelines the authors should specify which were used. We have clarified the issue of using multiple guidelines by referring to the Cochrane handbook for systematic reviews and interventions (Higgins et al. 2008) as the guideline for conducting the review. We have also referred to the PRISMA statement (Moher et al. 2009) as the guideline for reporting the results of our systematic review and meta-analysis (line 128). Validity of the findings The study deals with an important topic and it is evident that the authors have done an ambitions job trying to evaluate intervention sustainability of over time. That being said there are several limitations with the study, some of which are addressed by the authors in the discussion and some that I would like to stress further or add even. I have a major concern about collapsing so many types of outcomes into a single concept particularly for positive mental health. The studies included in the review or meta-analysis should be as homogeneous as possible. Now they introduce a potential bias that can be large. The high-to-moderate heterogeneity is a consequence of the broad outcome categories and an important limitation of the study. . We agree on your concern regarding collapsing several outcomes into the two concepts. Though, the group of positive mental health outcomes are evidence-based and in the literature they have been defined as predictors for positive mental health; e.g. subjective wellbeing (Diener et al. 2012), self-esteem, happiness (Huppert & Whittington 2003) self-esteem and self-compassion (Phillips 2018), active coping (Folkman & Moskowitz 2000). Academic performance is a related factor in higher education and was therefore included. To further clarify the issue how the collapsing of outcomes within those two outcome groups could have influenced our results we have added a sentence to the “Limitation” (line 484): Second, our intention to analyse two dimensions of mental health, that resulted in combining the original outcomes into the “mental ill health” and “positive mental health and academic performance” outcome categories, with a hierarchical approach applied, could have boosted heterogeneity. In a subsequent analyses, we attempted to reduce heterogeneity by pooling together the studies with the same specific outcomes reported, though for several outcomes it was not possible due to data scarcity. Collapsing outcomes also lead to other problems, like having to decide on a hierarchical order for positive outcomes - that in my mind do not make sense. Is academic performance a better indicator of positive mental health than well-being, for example? Our decision on applying a hierarchical approach for analysing outcomes combined within two dimensions of mental health was based on the idea of avoiding unit-of-analysis error if several outcomes from the same dimension was reported in the study (for example, if the same study reported ESs for both depression and anxiety or if the same study analysed self-esteem and active coping). Similar approach had been used in other meta-analyses (for example, by Yap et al 2016). In order to uniform the hierarchy, we based our choice of outcome solely on the descending order of how the outcomes were reported in the original studies that we selected. For example, in our study collection, most of the studies on mental ill health reported ESs for depression symptoms, slightly less studies reported ES for anxiety, etc. However, being fully aware of the limitations that can be induced by this approach, we supplemented the analysis of the combined outcomes by the analysis of the specific outcomes. For the latter, all outcomes reported in the original studies have been used. As a result, we have not lost any data on the specific outcomes reported in the studies selected for our review. Effect sizes have to be excluded when studies report in more than one domain, which is negative because they fulfill the inclusion criteria but the effect size for another outcome is used. Given our approach to analyse the specific outcomes (in addition to analysing the combined outcomes), no ESs had been lost from the studies that fulfilled the inclusion criteria. The results of our analyses on all specific outcomes from the trials included in the review are reported in Tables 2 and 3. In the fourth limitation of the study it is mentioned that 30% of the original studies were assessed as being of weak quality with selection bias as the most commonly identified weakness and what may have come out of this limitation. It would have been interesting to have the study quality distributed among the two major outcome categories, ill-health and positive. This would have helped the reader to evaluate the effects. To further describe the study quality and clarify how trials with different quality have been distributed within two categories of outcomes, we have made some amendments in the text and tables. Thus, we have added two columns, entitled “Intervention with at least one mental ill health outcome” and “Intervention with at least one positive mental health outcome, including academic performance” to the Table S2, where we indicated the number of studies with different quality. We have also described this distribution more in details in the “Results” - “Characteristics of included studies” (line 306). A description of what type of quality impairments that was most common for each outcome concept and would also provide a larger picture. This description had been added to the section “Results” - “Characteristics of included studies” (line 310). Lastly, I am skeptical about including the studies of weak quality in the meta-analysis. We fully acknowledge the fact that the trials with insufficient quality, when included in the analysis, may greatly influence the results. Unfortunately, the general scarcity of data on long-term follow-ups (e.g, 13-18 months) prevented us from initially excluding any studies from the analyses. In order to clarify the potential influence of low quality trials, we conducted sub-group analyses within each category of outcomes and stratified the studies by their quality (Tables 2 and 3). We have also amended the corresponding sentences in “Limitations” to further address our quality concerns (line 503). Dear
paper_title_zh: 高等教育学生心理健康干预效果的持续性：随机对照试验的系统综述与元分析
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。与同龄人相比，本科生中抑郁、焦虑和痛苦症状更为常见。学生中的心理健康问题与学业成绩受损、职业准备不足以及未来职业表现降低有关。关于促进心理健康和预防心理疾病的干预研究显示出有希望短期效果，但干预益处的可持续性值得更密切的关注。我们旨在识别、评估和总结来自随机对照试验（RCTs）的现有数据，报告心理健康促进和心理疾病预防干预的效果是否在干预后至少3个月持续存在，并分析这些效果如何因随访长度而异的不同结果。此外，我们旨在评估干预效果的可持续性是否因干预类型、研究层面的决定因素和参与者特征而有所不同。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1（匿名）基本报告总的来说，全文语言清晰且专业。然而，我有一些评论和建议以供改进：
- 在摘要中，将标题“结论”改为“讨论”。我们已将摘要中的标题从“结论”改为“讨论”。
- 第58行：指出某事物常见或高发，却不具体说明其常见程度或高发程度，令人不悦。引言，第65行：已澄清前两个句子，并添加了关于抑郁、抑郁症状和自杀意念的患病率。此外，我们添加了两篇原始研究的参考文献（Steptoe等人，2007年；Garlow等人，2008年）以及一篇最近发表的关于护理学生抑郁患病率的系统综述和元分析的参考文献（Tung等人，2018年）。

引言虽然引言提供了心理健康问题的背景——文献引用得当且相关——但没有提供积极心理健康的相应背景。没有对积极心理健康的理论概念化，这将提供包括（或不包括）某些结果作为积极心理健康衡量标准的依据。仅仅因为文献中有研究记录和方法使干预效果的可持续性在研究间“统计上可比”使用标准化单位，并不一定使它们有意义的包含在元分析中。因此，如果作者希望保留积极心理健康，他们应提供相关背景和概念化，以证明分析中包含的结果的合理性以及为什么他们认为将这些结果汇总是有意义的。如果他们这样做，我猜这将变得明显，即研究的范围最好限于心理健康问题及相关在元分析中有意义的结果。 引言，第92行：我们意识到，积极心理健康的概念本可以进一步描述。为了加强在综述中包含积极心理健康成果的合理性，我们引入了积极心理健康的理论概念化及其适用于心理健康促进的适宜性。此外，我们解释了包括预防性和促进性干预措施的重要性，以形成一个综合的群体心理健康，涵盖心理健康和积极心理健康两个方面。我们努力汇集积极心理健康成果源于我们描述完整心理概念的初衷。后者中包含的成果是基于证据的预测因子，并在第133行进一步描述。实验设计：该研究具有原创性，符合期刊的目标和范围。然而，研究问题（s）可以更好地定义。例如，心理健康和心理疾病的具体含义尚不清楚。为了澄清研究问题，我们添加了关于积极心理健康概念及其方面的信息（第92行），其适用于心理健康促进以及与心理疾病的关系。心理疾病的概念在第74行已得到澄清。我们感兴趣的成果不是诊断结果而是自我报告，限于焦虑症状、抑郁症状、心理困扰、担忧、疲劳、睡眠问题和感知压力。作为PICO一部分的积极心理健康和心理疾病的成果已在第133行提前描述。此外，我不喜欢目标中涉及实施质量的部分。虽然实施质量确实重要且应引起关注，但我认为这不是处理它的正确方式。原因是随机对照试验（RCT）通常不报告实施成分，这可能导致对这种质量的评估存在偏倚。我们同意。根据您的论证，我们重新考虑了我们的数据收集对于调查实施质量的适当性。因此，我们删除了相应的目标以及所有涉及实施质量和相应参考文献的句子/段落。此外，可以更清楚地说明当前的系统性综述和元分析与之前的综述有何不同（第87行）。作者提到了三项之前的综述（Conley等人，2015、2016、2017），本可以更详细地描述每一项。目前的描述使得难以了解他们的综述具体增加了什么内容。由于Conley等人的综述最近发表，这一点尤为重要，因为这是应该明确陈述研究新颖性的部分。我们已修订相应句子以澄清这一问题。在最近发表的综述中，Conley等人提出了几个未来研究的方向。 其中之一是需要进一步调查干预效益在可变随访期内的可持续性。这是基于以下观察：干预效果在随访期间可能会改变其方向和幅度（即，取决于干预，效益可能会随时间减少或增加，或仅在随访时出现）（Conley等人，2015、2016、2017）。受Conley等人观点的启发，为了响应他们进一步研究的呼吁，我们专注于评估某些干预后随访“里程碑”的效果可持续性，即3-6个月、7-12个月和13-18个月。首先，我们的目标是关注干预效果随时间的可持续性。这一研究扩展得到了Conley等人2015年的支持。其次，我们希望基于随机对照试验的结果，而不包括其他研究者所采用的准实验研究设计。第三，所包含的原始研究已经进行了彻底且透明的质量评估，并已呈现。第一点和第二点在我们的目标中得到了强调，并且可持续性问题已进一步阐明（第107行）。希望这一描述能澄清我们的综述所增加的内容。方法描述得足够详细，提供了可复制的信息。然而，第106行是一个例外。由于存在多套指南，作者应指明使用了哪一套。我们通过参考Cochrane系统评价和干预手册（Higgins等人，2008）作为进行综述的指南，澄清了使用多套指南的问题。我们还参考了PRISMA声明（Moher等人，2009）作为报告我们系统评价和元分析结果的指南（第128行）。

研究发现的效度
该研究涉及一个重要主题，显然作者们已经做了雄心勃勃的工作，试图评估干预随时间的可持续性。话虽如此，该研究存在一些局限性，其中一些在讨论中由作者们提出，还有一些我想进一步强调或补充。我对将如此多类型的结果合并为单一概念，尤其是对积极心理健康，感到非常担忧。纳入综述或元分析的研究应尽可能同质。现在他们引入了一个可能很大的潜在偏倚。高到中等程度的异质性是广泛结果类别的后果，也是该研究的一个重要局限性。我们同意您关于将多个结果合并为两个概念的担忧。尽管如此，积极心理健康结果组是基于证据的，并且在文献中已被定义为积极心理健康的预测因子；例如，主观幸福感（Diener等人）。 2012)，自尊，幸福感（Huppert & Whittington 2003），自尊和自我同情（Phillips 2018），积极应对（Folkman & Moskowitz 2000）。学术表现是高等教育中的一个相关因素，因此被纳入研究。为了进一步澄清这两个结果组内结果合并如何可能影响我们的结果，我们在“局限性”部分（第484行）添加了一句：其次，我们分析心理健康两个维度的意图，导致将原始结果合并为“心理健康问题”和“积极心理健康和学术表现”两个结果类别，并应用了层次分析法，这可能增加了异质性。在后续分析中，我们试图通过将报告相同特定结果的研究合并在一起来减少异质性，但由于数据稀缺，对于几个结果来说这是不可能的。结果合并还导致了其他问题，比如不得不决定积极结果的层次顺序——在我看来这并不合理。例如，学术表现是比幸福感更好的积极心理健康指标吗？我们决定对合并的两个心理健康维度结果应用层次分析法，是基于避免同一维度中报告多个结果时的单位分析错误的想法（例如，如果同一研究报告了抑郁和焦虑的效应量，或者同一研究分析了自尊和积极应对）。类似的方法在其他元分析中也曾使用（例如，Yap等人2016年）。为了统一层次，我们完全基于所选原始研究中结果报告的降序来选择结果。例如，在我们的研究集合中，大多数关于心理健康问题的研究报告了抑郁症状的效应量，略少的研究报告了焦虑的效应量，等等。然而，我们充分意识到这种方法可能带来的局限性，因此我们通过分析特定结果来补充合并结果的分析。对于后者，使用了原始研究中报告的所有结果。因此，我们并没有丢失所选研究中报告的任何特定结果的数据。当研究在多个领域报告时，效应量必须被排除，这是负面的，因为它们符合纳入标准，但使用了另一个结果的效应量。鉴于我们分析特定结果的方法（除了分析合并结果之外），符合纳入标准的研究中没有丢失任何效应量。我们关于综述中包含的所有试验的特定结果的分析结果报告在表2和表3中。 在研究的第四个局限性中提到，30%的原始研究被评估为质量较差，选择偏倚是最常识别的弱点，以及这一局限性可能带来的影响。如果将研究质量分布在两个主要结果类别——不良健康和积极健康——之间，将会很有趣。这将有助于读者评估效果。为了进一步描述研究质量并澄清不同质量的试验如何在两个结果类别中分布，我们对文本和表格进行了一些修订。因此，我们在表S2中添加了两列，分别题为“至少有一个心理健康不良结果的干预”和“至少有一个积极心理健康结果的干预，包括学术表现”，其中我们指出了不同质量的研究数量。我们还在“结果”部分——“纳入研究的特征”（第306行）中更详细地描述了这种分布。描述每种结果概念中最常见的质量缺陷类型，也将提供一个更全面的图景。这一描述已添加到“结果”部分——“纳入研究的特征”（第310行）。最后，我对将质量较差的研究纳入元分析持怀疑态度。我们完全承认，质量不足的试验在纳入分析时可能会极大地影响结果。不幸的是，长期随访数据（例如，13-18个月）的普遍缺乏，使我们无法从一开始就排除任何研究。为了澄清低质量试验的潜在影响，我们在每个结果类别内进行了亚组分析，并根据研究质量对研究进行了分层（表2和表3）。我们还修订了“局限性”部分的相关句子，以进一步解决我们的质量问题（第503行）。

paper_title: Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS): design and first-year review
paper_abstract: This article describes the motivation, design, and progress of the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS). JOSS is a free and open-access journal that publishes articles describing research software. It has the dual goals of improving the quality of the software submitted and providing a mechanism for research software developers to receive credit. While designed to work within the current merit system of science, JOSS addresses the dearth of rewards for key contributions to science made in the form of software. JOSS publishes articles that encapsulate scholarship contained in the software itself, and its rigorous peer review targets the software components: functionality, documentation, tests, continuous integration, and the license. A JOSS article contains an abstract describing the purpose and functionality of the software, references, and a link to the software archive. The article is the entry point of a JOSS submission, which encompasses the full set of software artifacts.
review_content: Reviewer 1. Further, see some points below. One repeated concern is about just having one reviewer for most of the works. This should be explained. How are conflicts of interest identified and addressed? How is having knowledgeable and skilled reviewers ensured? How is quality ensured if anyone can volunteer and review and that is the only checking done? How is correctness assessed in such cases? Has there been any review by others of the quality of the works accepted? We have made changes in response to many of the reviewer comments, as detailed in the rest of this document. Regarding the question of number of reviewers, we have responded to Reviewer #1 and #2’s comments. We believe that our efforts around reviewer selection and reviews meets (and in some cases surpasses) that of most other journals, since the entire process is open and transparent. Further, we add structure to the reviews, and feel that this helps ensure that our criteria for submission quality are met. Some editors do regularly assign two reviewers, and other editors get involved in the review nearly at the level of a reviewer to help ensure quality (particularly if a review occurs very quickly). We do also have a conflict of interest policy to which reviewers are required to agree; this represents a step further than most other journals, though we do generally place trust in the reviewer—the openness of the review process and reviewer identities helps ensure adherence to the COI policy. Page 1 of 10 Another concern is support for readers. This seems a weakness and should be discussed, with plans articulated as to how it will be addressed. It would be nice to know who reads JOSS works, what they do after, if there are statistics on cites resulting, if there are repeat submissions, if newer submissions cite older ones, etc. We have clarified that the journal is mainly designed to serve authors/software developers. However, we do plan to add better search features, including tagging based on language and domain, which would make finding software/articles easier. However, JOSS is not designed to be read as a typical journal, as the primary focus is to create citable entities for software. We do not have any information on readership for this reason. We have added some preliminary (and incomplete) information on citation statistics to the conclusions, and also evidence of two articles that cite older versions. Another concern is about contextual issues like open science, being US centric, changes needed in promotion/advancement priorities in academia and industry, target audience, etc. We have addressed the comments on these topics. Another concern is about novelty of JOSS, literature review of related efforts, and understanding how JOSS works fit into the broader infrastructure. See for example below about Calgo. Further, how does it fit into the world of education (are submissions uses by teachers or students) or software engineering? We have added some discussion of Calgo and other domain-specific journals to Section 3.4. Regarding education, JOSS specifically focuses on software that has a research application (see submission requirements http://joss.theoj.org/about#submission_requirements), and so software that targets educational applications would not be in scope. However, some of the JOSS editors have started a new, sibling journal, The Journal of Open Source Education, that will accept educational software and material. Another question is the reliance on Github and other parts of the assumed environment. The fact that most submissions are Python or R suggests that some discussion should be given as to broadening the universe from which submissions come. For example, with current interest in Jupyter notebooks growing, are submissions connected with such? We have added some discussion of issues related to GitHub notifications on page 13. We feel that the heavy Python and R representation reflect the popularity of these languages in modern scientific computing and the close connection to open research software communities. Furthermore, the partnership with rOpenSci has led to a large number of R submissions. We have added some discussion to Section 5. We have discussed notebooks as a submission type, but do not currently accept standalone notebooks. Please also see some marks in the manuscript copy attached. Regarding the note “Calgo”, please see http: // calgo. acm. org/ and http: // toms. acm. org/ algorithms-policy. cfm . Some discussion of this long-running algorithm venue seems necessary. Page 2 of 10 We have made the edits recommended in the marked manuscript, and added mention of CALGO to Section 3.4. Reviewer #1 It might be nice to include some information on how reviewers for JOSS submissions are identified and/or selected. It seems quite an open review system and I wonder if the editors have protocols in place to deal with multiple unsolicited reviewers jumping onto a submission’s review Github issue, potentially with conflicting opinions or biases in their experiences. We have added some additional details on reviewer selection in point 2 of Section 4.1. We have not seen many cases of unsolicited reviewers joining a submission’s review, although the few unsolicited comments that have appeared have been constructive in nature. Any problems that arise—or violations of the JOSS Code of Conduct—would be handled by the submission’s editor. Given the JOSS review happens entirely via a Github issue and presumably most reviewers are often working with their own projects on Github, do the JOSS editors make use of any special customisations or additions to try and help JOSS review comments stand out from the general “noise” of Github notifications a reviewer is likely exposed to? Or any other thoughts from the editors to try and help make sure JOSS review notifications are not missed, as briefly mentioned as a reason for some delayed reviews. We have added some discussion of issues related to GitHub notifications on page 13. Reviewer #2 This manuscript describes the design of the Journal of Open Source Software and describes experiences after the first year since its inception. Let me start by mentioning that I fully support the ambition to publish open source software in articles that describe the software and which reviews some quality metrics and which makes it possible to cite software in scientific literature, with proper acknowledgements of the authors. I also appreciate the openness of the process and I congratulate the authors of this manuscript with the success of JOSS so far. A paper like this can hardly be rejected on scientific merit, since it describes a process, and my comments are mostly an advice, sometimes a personal note and rarely a correction. Section 1 Firstly, the intended audience is not entirely clear. There is quite a bit of technical jargon regarding software development in the paper. I think the jargon relates to the community of research software engineers and possibly bit wider than that (including this reviewer). The subject of publishing software in articles, making it citable and having the reward and recognition system in place for research software engineers in a wider academic context is indeed insufficiently appreciated. This paper is not going to respond to this discussion directly, so I suggest to make clear in the beginning that the Page 3 of 10 targeted community is the already specialized research software community and readers who are likely to submit to this journal, rather than the wider academic community. We have added a sentence in the first paragraph on page 2 addressing the intended audience: “We expect this article to be of interest to two core audiences: (1) researchers who develop software and could submit their work to JOSS, (2) those in the community with an interest in advancing scholarly communications who may appreciate the technical details of the JOSS journal framework, and (3) those interested in possibilities for citing software in their own research publications.” Related to the above, a bit wider discussion on the open science aspects would be appreciated (still within the scope of this particular article). I support the open software movement related to open science, but there are drawbacks and criticisms as well. Which aspects do you explicitly not resolve in this set up? The authors mention the ethics of open source in the beginning and describe at the end the issue of software development, but not the openness part. How does this journal contribute to the wider development of open science practices (open access clearly, but beyond open data to open software)? This is a subject which could be described in the introduction a bit more rather than taking it for granted Open-source software is a core tenant of open science, and JOSS encourages the open sharing of software by providing an incentive to do so following best practices. In fact, we feel that JOSS mainly contributes in that area, rather than open access (although our articles are open access). We have added a sentence at the end of the introduction on page 2 to reflect this: “JOSS also supports the broader open-science movement by encouraging researchers to share their software openly and follow best practices in its development.” We appreciate that there are ongoing discussions about challenges and opportunities in open source. That has been discussed, extensively and well, elsewhere, and is beyond the scope of this article. This journal is meant to support those who have decided to make their software open source and encourage good practices in their open-source software work. Comparable journals do exist, also journals that keep discussion papers open (the abstract suggests this is the first journal), e.g. those of the European Geophysical Union, including software and data journals such as GMD. It would be good to highlight more what the niche of JOSS is wrt these domain journals with similar goals. It may also be relevant to refer and discuss instrumentation journals which have a similar goal. They don’t publish new scientific results, but rather describe instruments, calibrations etc. We have extended our discussion of other software journals in Section 3.4 to include some domainspecific journals and compare/contrast JOSS with them. A comment is that journal seems to be very US centered, with some exceptions, how does this reflect in article submissions? Is there a strategy in place to broaden it? We have added a new Figure 8 that shows the countries for all authors of papers published in the first year, and a discussion paragraph on page 15. Currently, out of our 19 editors, 6.5 are located outside the US (the 0.5 comes from one of our editors’ dual affiliation). We do believe that expanding the editorial board will help us reach authors in countries not yet well-represented, as will the natural growth and recognition of the journal. Page 4 of 10 Section 1 ends without giving a summary what the journal entails. It is described further. It is about publishing software, but it doesn’t say how far it goes in that (does it include the code, documentation, tests or is it just a description?). A summary is needed for the reader. We have added a sentence summarizing JOSS articles to the last paragraph of Section 1: “The article describes the software from a high level, and the software itself includes both source code and associated artifacts such as tests, documentation, and examples.” Section 2 While I agree with this section a number of comments: The authors mention that actual scholarship is the full software environment, code that produced the data. This is a very limited view of science and scholarly research. It is a very technological view of scientific research only that suggests that the whole creative process of research is in software development. Also, it takes the pure academic view only, while 21st century research has tight connections to societal, economical and ecological challenges which is not reflected in a code. I highly disagree with the statement and I suggest to phrase it much more carefully. This is a personal note. We are speaking in a purely technical context about computational research, and agree that in general research involves much more than software. However, for research involving software, our point is that the scholarship includes the software, and thus the efforts towards that should be fully credited. The motivation of this journal should not be the career of the research software engineers. It should be good scientific practice. As a side effect it could help the career development, but this problem relates more the reward and evaluation system in place in many academic institutions. Having this journal may solve one aspect, but not the actual cause of lack of career perspectives of software engineers in the scientific community. This is to be addressed in the academic system, in particular the leadership of it. That developers shun away from publishing a citable paper is not a strong argument. They should do so as part of good scientific practice since it contains an independent peer-review quality check, a time stamp and allows for referencing. The notion that a paper is also a time stamp recognizing the original contribution of the author to the scientific process could also be more clearly spelled out. Note that there are quite a few domain specific journals that do not require new scientific results. From my own personal experience, as an editor of one of them, it is more a problem of culture. The reviewers focus a lot on the scientific results and find it hard to review papers purely based on methodologies and tools. There are a number of challenges related to the culture of science (in many fields): how it recognizes digital products, provenance and reproducibility, and many sociological issues, including recognition of individuals outside publications, diversity, etc. JOSS is not trying to directly solve this complete problem, but focuses on a small part: recognition of software and software contributors. If we are successful in our part, this will impact the overall culture of science. Section 3 ‘dressed up as ...’ that sounds a bit weak. Page 5 of 10 We have replaced the phrase on page 4: “JOSS offers developers a venue to publish their complete research software, dressed up as software articles wrapped in relatively short high-level articles, thus enabling citation credit for their work.” It is unclear whether JOSS also checks whether the software is original, in the sense that it doesn’t re-invent a wheel. One of the goals of peer reviews of scientific papers is that the author is the first one to discover a result and puts a time stamp on it (see above). Section 6 The last paragraph is very long, a bit unclear and unsatisfactory in its ending. Is there a process foreseen to come to a choice to deal with this for JOSS? We have condensed the paragraph slightly, and revised the final sentence: “The editorial board will accept a new JOSS article published with each major version or even a minor version if the changes seem significant enough to the editor and reviewer(s), but we do not know if this will be satisfactory to the needs of both developers and users (corresponding to JOSS authors and readers, respectively).” Section 7 The first paragraph mentions the career perspective of RSEs, but this cannot be the reason to set up JOSS. It is set up because software is an essential part of the research process, and therefore it should be properly evaluated and published such that it is findable, with a measure of quality and originality. Thus, JOSS differs from traditional journals which evaluate originality and/or impact, although we do review for quality standards. Page 7 of 10 Furthermore, since JOSS is not designed as a journal one reads, we do not primarily intend it to serve as a mechanism to find software. (Though we do plan to improve searching and tagging capabilities somewhat.) I miss the open science perspective in this concluding section. We have added a sentence summarizing the main contribution of JOSS to open science in the first paragraph on page 17: “By encouraging researchers to develop their software following best practices, and then share and publish it openly, JOSS supports the broader open-science movement.” In conclusion, I have some remarks on the paper, but I strongly support JOSS as it is essential to publish research software and contribute to open science. I hope it will develop further in the near future! Thank you! Reviewer #3 Basic reporting The English is excellent, clear and unambiguous. The literature references provide the appropriate level of background and context. The article is self-contained and uses a professional article structure. Data are available from a figshare article. section 2 is a little repetitive (the final paragraph) as the case for garnering credit for software has been well made. As you point out, JOSS is designed primarily for the authors/software developers, not readers—the primary services are providing authors with a mechanism to receive credit for their software, and to improve the quality of this research software via peer review. We have clarified this by adding Page 8 of 10 the following sentence to Section 3.1 on page 4: “Unlike most journals, which ease discoverability of new research and findings, JOSS serves primarily as a mechanism for software developers/authors to improve and publish their research software. Thus, software discovery is a secondary feature.” Regarding author experiences, we have added links to (positive) blog posts from authors to page 18 (references 38 and 39), but do not have any additional feedback on author experiences. 2. The review process primarily uses 1 reviewer - what is the confidence that this is sufficient? The editor-in-chief (Arfon Smith) who initially created JOSS has a background in astrophysics, where a single reviewer is standard. However, we recognize that this is not normal for many research fields. Second reviews are possible, and some editors regularly solicit multiple reviews for the JOSS submissions they are handling, particularly when the editor is less confident about their own understanding of the area, software, and review. We would also like to point out that the goal of the review is to bring the paper to an acceptable standard, not to just to judge it for acceptance or rejection. Since this is the case, it’s not clear that any more than one reviewer is needed to provide this help and feedback, particularly if we can say that the editors are closely involved in checking the work of the reviewer. Validity of the findings The number of articles submitted and published is a clear indication of the justification and value of the Journal and its place in the ecosystem. The data presented is robust. Partnership with OSI and NumFOCUS is encouraging. The review of the first year gives useful information. Some points that would improve the paper 1. the statistics given are from the point of view of the editorial team. What would be more interesting would be an analysis the submissions in the first year, by article topic, community served, geographic distributions (is this USA or European focused?) and so on. It is hard to tell from the user interface at http: // joss. theoj. org/ papers We have added a new Figure 8 and paragraph on page 15 describing the geographic distribution of authors; in the first year, about 48% of authors come from the US, and 40% from Europe. However, categorizing the submissions by the community/topic is more challenging, since we do not currently have a tagging system in place. As described in review section 2, there is little discussion of the reader experience. For example, I could not easily find if the Whedon RubyGem Library has it own article. Recently we have been working on improving the reader experience, for example through more readable and informative article webpages, and the aforementioned tagging/searching capability. The Whedon RubyGem Library does not have its own article because we don’t believe that researchers will cite such an article. In other words, Whedon is not research software and does not fit in the scope of JOSS. Page 9 of 10 3. in addition to thoughts on versions, has the journal developed a strategy on software forking, in particular by different developer teams to the original developers? We have added a short paragraph to page 17 describing how we might handle submissions of software forks. Ultimately, we prefer to leave authorship decisions to the developers, though this could become challenging for forks. 4. although it is early days, is there any preliminary information on citation patterns for the articles? there is a hint only in “we may need to invest more effort into raising awareness of good practices for citing JOSS articles” Although JOSS does not yet appear to be fully indexed on Google Scholar, a number of articles do appear there, likely due to presence in the Astrophysics Data System (ADS). We have added this preliminary information to the conclusions section: “That said, we have some preliminary citation statistics: according to Google Scholar, corner.py [38] and Armadillo [39] have been cited the most at 116 and 79 times, respectively.
