paper_title: Peripheral-physiological and neural correlates of the flow experience while playing video games: a comprehensive review
paper_abstract: The flow state is defined by intense involvement in an activity with high degrees of concentration and focused attention accompanied by a sense of pleasure. Video games are effective tools for inducing flow, and keeping players in this state is considered to be one of the central goals of game design. Many studies have focused on the underlying physiological and neural mechanisms of flow. Results are inconsistent when describing a unified mechanism underlying this mental state. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the physiological and neural correlates of flow and explains the relationship between the reported physiological and neural markers of the flow experience. Despite the heterogeneous results, it seems possible to establish associations between reported markers and the cognitive and experiential aspects of flow, particularly regarding arousal, attention control, reward processing, automaticity, and self-referential processing.
review_content: Reviewer 1 (Birte Thissen) Basic reporting First, I would like to thanks the authors for extensively revising their manuscript according to both reviewers’ recommendations. I believe that the manuscript greatly improved as it now shows a clearer structure, a more in-depth discussion of both theoretical assumptions and observed findings, and a more comprehensive review of the literature. Therefore, I would only like to make some minor final remarks and recommendations before the manuscript can be published: 1) I noticed some grammatical errors and spelling mistakes throughout the manuscript, which is why I would recommend to have a native speaker proof-read its final version before publication. Examples: leave out ‘either’ (line 100); repeat ‘on’ after ‘as well as’ (line 162); use ‘for the creation of a flow state’ or ‘for creating a flow state’ (line 163); spell U-shaped either consistently with an uppercase or lowercase U (e.g., lines 207 & 211); ‘A significant effect was neither found for…, nor for…’ (lines 224-226); ‘noted’ instead of ‘considered’ (line 256); ‘associated with’ (line 321); ‘capacity’ (line 340) does not seem to be the right word (do you mean the skill to correctly judge the appropriate difficulty level for oneself or the opportunity to pick a difficulty level oneself?); plural ‘flow scores… were’ (lines 413-414); ‘flow as measured by…’ (line 430); ‘a mental arithmetic task’ since the task has not been described beforehand (line 464); ‘higher left temporal cortex alpha activity, which reflects decreased cortical activity in this region, is associated with improved performance, as it represents reduced internal verbalization and increased visual-spatial processing in the right hemisphere’ (lines 531-534); ‘a 7-second video clip’ ‘table tennis’ (line 549); ‘was to be expected in the more difficult condition’ (lines 574-575); ‘which increase with increasing difficulty’ (line 576); ‘the flow and anxiety condition’ (line 579); ‘as compared to’ rather than ‘than’ (line 580); leave out ‘alone’ or replace with ‘on its own accord’ (line 620); ‘playing in 2D’ (line 666); ‘The observed co-activation… aligns’ (line 756-757); ‘flow was found to be associated with’ (line 759); ‘a purely effortful mental experience’ (line 766); ‘practice’ instead of ‘exercise’ (line 789); ‘mind-wandering’ (line 801); ‘body- and self-awareness (line 807); ‘role’ (line 163 and 819); ‘some studies…, other studies…’ (lines 832-833); ‘in which’ instead of ‘where’ (line 833); leave out ‘of’ (line 840); ‘neural activity’ (line 849); ‘…, given the different physiological and cognitive demands of the flow-inducing activity, …’ (lines 850- 851). Moreover, ‘e.g.’ is normally followed by a comma and the gerund is preceded by one (e.g., lines 885-886 ‘…, reporting medium levels of performance’), and an enumeration of three or more things requires a comma before the ‘and’ (e.g., line 122); please make sure to put these commas throughout the manuscript. Also, check the blanks between words as you tend to sometimes either put too many (e.g., lines 236, 267, 486, 498, 513, 649, 660, 742, 841, 886, 892) or none (e.g., lines 44, 469, 470, 486). There are also some stylistic mistakes: In line 355, there is a semicolon that does not seem to make sense; FKS in line 91 is underlined for some reason; the dash once comes with blanks and sometimes without. I do not claim to have found everything, so I strongly recommend the authors to also proof-read their manuscript in terms of formal and stylistic requirements once more. We tried to address all grammatical errors and spelling mistakes. We sent the manuscript to a native speaker in order to be sure that the final manuscript is free of any mistake. 2) I have some remaining issues with the introduction: ‘Why do we seek activities that make us happy?’ does not inspire interest in the reader as the answer is in the question; I would suggest to just leave it out (line 37-38). Further, I believe there is still a misconception about processing fluency as well as about antecedents, components, and consequences of flow reflected in the text. Processing fluency is a dimension of flow, just like absorption and enjoyment (i.e., broader than the nine components), and is directly reflected in some of the flow components such as sense of clear goals and immediate feedback. Thus, there is no ‘state termed processing fluency’ (line 40-41), but processing fluency is part of the definition of the flow state and should appear together with enjoyment and absorption in lines 38-39. We believe that by “processing fluency” as one dimension of flow, the reviewer refers to “merging action and awareness during flow experience” which is described by Csikszentmihalyi (Csikszentmihalyi, 1975, pp 38). Since there is no dimension of flow named processing fluency in the literature, we have addressed this concern in lines 39-42:” Flow is a subjective experience of processing fluency in which actions seem to happen effortlessly, fluently, and almost automatically. According to this theory, the clearest sign of flow is the merging of action and awareness in a way that “a person in flow is aware of his actions but not of the awareness itself” . 3) ‘Stemming from intrinsic motivation’, however, in my opinion does not necessarily belong in the definition itself, as intrinsic motivation is an antecedent (and maybe also a consequence) of flow – therefore it should be mentioned later on together with the first three key components (not dimensions!) as potential antecedents in lines 54-55. Importantly, each antecedent of flow (e.g., clear goals when starting the flow activity) at the same time serves as an experiential component (e.g., the perception of clear goals during flow in this activity). To make this clearer, I would reword lines 54-56 as ‘Whereas all nine key components reflect the subjective experience during flow, the first three (balance between skills and challenges, clear goals, and immediate feedback) can in a more objective sense also be understood as activity-related preconditions for flow. Moreover, in relation to the person, intrinsic motivation for the activity can facilitate a flow experience (Csikszentmihalyi, 1975). Optimal skill-challenge balance, though, is considered to be the main antecedent for entering a flow state…’. We argue that intrinsic motivation of the task has already been mentioned as a dimension of flow in component 9 as autotelic experience. 4) I would also suggest to re-structure the introduction to make it easier to follow for the reader: After you introduce the flow channel model and potential modulators of the relationship it predicts between flow and skill-challenge balance (lines 59-75), explain how this theoretical framework can be relatively easily implemented in the context of computer gaming (‘…could facilitate the propensity to experience flow. – new paragraph – Despite such potential modulators, the relationship between skill-challenge balance and flow postulated in the flow channel model affords an approach for experimentally manipulating flow by presenting different challenge levels. Even though inducing flow under controlled laboratory conditions has been considered difficult (reference please!), game-based paradigms are especially promising as a) the difficulty level of a game can relatively easily be manipulated to achieve skill-challenge balance, and b) gaming can be considered a typical flow-inducing activity’; then go on with the reasons why video gaming is a great flow activity from lines 104-112 and 132-133, and follow up with the manipulation approaches from lines 113-118). Please make sure to include all three approaches, namely also the medium challenge level-approach (Rheinberg and Vollmeyer, 2003), in lines 113-117 – and then move lines 124-126 up as an example (‘For instance, Rheinberg and Vollmeyer…’). In the next paragraph, you can then give three interesting areas of application for experimental flow research with computer games: a) understanding peak performances, b) potential use of flow in therapeutic settings, and c) maximization of game enjoyment. Thus, put lines 75-84, lines 131-148 and lines 149-153 next, respectively (with appropriate connecting passages of course). Then, you can come to the methodological challenge this research faces and its potential solution in the form of psychophysiological or neural indicators for flow, pointing out why the reader should be interested in what is about to follow in your literature review (e.g., ‘In order to successfully study research questions related to flow and performance, therapeutic use, or gamer experience, the experimental paradigm must be accompanied by a valid measurement of the flow state.’; move lines 85-103 here – how flow used to be measured with self-reports, how this is problematic and warrants additional psychophysiological and neural measures; now also briefly mention the dual-task approach from line 156-158 and in doing so, please spell out ‘dual-task approach’). And then you can end with lines 158-171. We restructure this part in order to address this concern. Please see lines 75-102. 5) There are some minor unclarities left in the introduction: ‘Autotelic experience’ (line 52) – this term needs to either be explained (Greek: ‘auto’=self, ‘telos’=goal) or reworded as ‘intrinsic enjoyment, which is more self-explanatory. In lines 67-68, it is ‘activities that were subjectively evaluated as important to succeed in’ ¬– this way, the obtained result (low demands/flow) becomes more understandable. The FSS (lines 90-91) was developed in the context of sport, but can be and is often applied to other flow activities, just like the FKS. The FKS is called Flow Sort Scale in English and should therefore also be abbreviated to FSS and not FKS. The FQ (lines 668-669) is missing in this section and should be introduced with the ESM as it was originally developed for ESM studies (lines 85-88). Effectance motivation might as well be explained using the term ‘feeling of control’ instead of ‘empowerment’, pointing out the link to this flow component. The TOJ (lines 143-148) needs a bit more explanation, since the loss of a sense of time during flow would suggest that a flow experience actually diminishes the performance in a temporal judgement test. Similarly, the reasoning why autonomy is suggested as an important determinant of flow needs to be briefly given (lines 119-120, lines 340-341). And I am painfully aware of the difficulties to distinguish flow and immersion in video gaming, but since the term immersion is later brought up, there needs to be one or two comprehensive sentences about this (‘Some studies (ref.) implemented an additional immersion condition, which was aimed at transporting the player’s mind into the virtual world by manipulating factors like graphics, sound, and gameplay (ref.). Immersion is an important concept in VR and computer gaming research and seems closely connected to flow in these activity contexts, as both pertain to a pleasant, absorbed mental state common in gamers. However, flow and immersion can be distinguished due to subtle structural differences (for further information on this, please see Michailidis, Balaguer-Ballester, & He, 2018).’. We tried to clarify most of the ambiguities in the manuscript which are mentioned by the reviewer. Experimental design I am very happy to see that the authors put in the additional effort to extend their literature research to other databases and to revise the presentation of their inclusion criteria. The methodology is now much clearer and more convincing. I also find the new structure of the presentation of the findings much easier to follow for the reader. Again, I would like to commend the authors for the successful revision, and only have minor remarks to add: 1) I believe some section need a bit more clarification: In line 182, the term ‘exergames’ may need a short explanation and the confounding factors could be accompanied by examples (e.g., movement effects, processing of social interaction, …), in order to explain to the reader why the 35 papers were excluded, to be as transparent and detailed as possible with the exclusion criteria; in lines 204-205, I would write ‘that the experience of challenge during flow induces a certain amount of stress’ (lines 204-205) since ‘stress’ and ‘challenge’ cannot be used interchangeably in some theories; in line 206 and 207, I find ‘fast/slow response system’ to be better terms, respectively; in line 228 and 556, please leave out ‘emotional’ as flow is not an emotional state; in line 236, you state that flow was assessed in the study and later go on to say that flow was actually not assessed with a questionnaire (line 239); you may want to say that there was a flow, immersion, and boredom condition, but no measurement of self-reported flow?; in line 445, please write ‘a first person shooter (FPS) game’; lines 447-449 could use an example to clarify what is meant by ‘game events that contribute to factors described by Csikszentmihalyi’; in line 433 the name of the FPS game, in line 419 the name of the videogame, and in line 656 the name of the flow scale is missing. The additional information on each of the above-mentioned concerns was included in the manuscript to addionally clarify the issues. 2) I find it a bit adverse to first give interpretation of the HRV indices and later on discuss those interpretations. I would be upfront with the controversial aspects here: ‘To investigate the relationship between flow and ANS activation, cardiovascular measures are oftentimes assessed, given that heart rate variability, which pertains to fluctuations in the time intervals of adjacent heartbeats, is traditionally seen as an indicator to dismantle PSNS and SNS activation. Thus, high-frequency HRV can be considered a direct measure of parasympathetic activation, whereas low frequency HRV has long been interpreted as reflecting sympathetic influences, rendering the HF/LF ratio an indicator for autonomic balance between SNS and PSNS. However, it is important to note that this interpretation of LF-HRV and LF/HF ratio is controversial…’ and follow it up with the information from lines 293-301. After this clarification, you can go on to report De Manzano et al. (2010) and later Chanel et al. (2011). We appreciate the suggestion of the reviewer. However we believe that the part which explains the relationship between ANS and cardiovascular measures and the argument on these measures in the manuscript is clear. We think that explaining the assumptions used in the literature for these measures and following discussion will help to clarify the findings. 3) Sometimes it is unclear how certain constructs related to flow were measured, given that they could be measured both with self-reports and physiological indicators. For instance, in line 277 do you mean self-reported positive affect and effortless attention? Same for line 321: How was the decrease in mental effort assessed? In line 416 you mean the last 30 seconds of the flow condition, and in line 478, you mean the flow score? Similarly, in line 500, do you mean in the flow condition, and in line 501, correlations between the flow score and DMN activity? What is the attention score referred to in line 595? In line 868, I assume you mean ‘…does not guarantee that a person will enter a flow state in the flow condition.’. In line 489, you mean a flow score – or is the flow index something else? And in line 615, what do you mean by ‘moments of flow’ since as of now flow cannot be captured with high temporal accuracy? We tried to clarify most of the ambiguities in the manuscript which are mentioned by the reviewer. 4) I would re-structure and re-word certain lines to clarify their meaning: In lines 200-201, I would suggest. ‘In contrast to the notion that the attentional focus during flow is essentially effortless, Keller and colleagues (2011) argued that flow involves considerable mental effort due to the high degree of involvement along with the challenging nature of the task.’; in line 234, ‘EDA measures increased with the game’s difficulty level, indicating heightening arousal’; in lines 323-329, ‘The different findings show that during… participants may not perceive as much stress…. It should also be noted, that Keller’s study involved a relatively small number of participants and operationalized flow through the flow condition, without actually measuring self-reported flow experiences, which might affect the validity of their findings.’ (On a side-note, if this operationalization is used, the analyses is most likely not correlational.); in line 401, ‘the activity of the DMN is thought to decrease’ since you are still stating assumptions and not findings at this point; in line 459-461, ‘It should be noted, though, that in the second study, the subjective flow experience was assumed to be elicited by the flow condition, but this assumption was not checked using a self-report flow scale.’; in line 544, either say ‘once again’ or refer to the other studies; in line 491, ‘, indicating less self-related processing,’; in lines 556-560, ‘Chanel et al. (2011) tried to classify their three different challenge-skill conditions in a game of Tetris according to EEG signals. Even though their results indicated distinct theta power between conditions in some electrodes, no precise link to states of boredom, flow, and anxiety could be obtained.’; In line 843, I guess you mean the ‘flow channel model’; in line 856, leave out ‘would’ and go on to say ‘FPSs are three-dimensional games, in which spatial navigation is crucial, since at any given time, ….’ and delete the sentence (line 860) which merely repeats the part about spatial navigation; in line 868-869, since you give a recommendation, say ‘The subjective experience of flow in the flow condition should be assessed using self-report flow scales in future studies, to determine whether the participants were able to enter a full flow state or not.’. We tried to clarify most of the ambiguities in the manuscript which are mentioned by the reviewer. 5) I noticed that there is some repetition in the text (for instance, it is stated on multiple occasions that a flow condition does not guarantee a flow experience). Moreover, when describing a study, there is often a more general sentence first (e.g., line 412, ‘playing a video game’), followed by a more specific sentence (e.g., line 413 ‘while playing Tetris); this information could be presented in a more concise form in just one sentence. Finally, brackets are often used to insert full sentences (e.g., line 431-432); however, for fluent reading it is advisable to use brackets only to give short key words and to use a subordinate clause when more text is needed. Please revise the text once more according to these opportunities for improvement. Validity of the findings I am confident that the revised, more in-depth discussion of the findings together with explicit recommendations for future study designs makes this literature review an interesting read for PeerJ’s readership and clearly shows its added value to the field. In addition to some minor language- and grammar-related issues I have already brought up in the other sections of the review, my only remark here is, whether the ‘joyous state of focused attention’ should not be re-named as a ‘subjectively effortless state of focused attention’ in order to set it apart from a ‘state of positive valence and heightened arousal’. Other than that, I find the discussion section very well thought-out! Comments for the Author At this point, I have to stress the importance of proof-reading a manuscript multiple times to ensure a consistent and correct style; I myself have experienced that a manuscript can get rejected due to formal mistakes. I have put a lot of effort in trying to find these mistakes for you, but I do not claim to have found all of them, so please check again. A good example for persistent inconsistencies and formal mistakes are the tables: 1) For ‘Experimental type’, you write either ‘FPS Game/game:’ or ‘Game’ with no colon. Similarly, for ‘Design’, you write either ’40 minutes gameplay’, ’10 minutes’, or ‘3 minutes blocks of gameplay’. Stick to one way of reporting. I would suggest ‘(FPS) Game:’ and ‘Boredom/Flow/Anxiety, 10 minutes gameplay’. 2) For ‘Measures’, it happens quite often that the ‘&’ is in the beginning of a line or a comma is missing; to avoid these mistakes, I would suggest simply enumerating all indicators with commas (e.g., ‘EDA, HRV, fEMG’ instead of ‘EDA, HRV, & fEMG’). Same for multiple games under ‘Experimental Design’ – here, only for the dual tasks the ‘&’ should be used. 3) Still, some commas are missing when three or more items are enumerated throughout the tables. In the last column, I would also suggest to only use the ‘&’ when indicators are enumerated, but not for results – in this case, use ‘;’ (e.g., Table 1 ‘Inverted U-shaped relationship between LF-HRV & cortisol level with self-reported flow; positive linear relationship between parasympathetic activation & self-reported flow). 4) Some formal mistakes remain: in Table 1, for Chanel et al. the s in participants is shifted to the next line, there are superfluous blanks in the lines for Leger et al. and for Harmat et al. under ‘Design’, a bracket is missing in ‘77(40f)’, and the enumeration in the last column of Leger et al. should be ‘A, B, & C’. In Table 2, there is another superfluous blank in ‘Moreno et al. (2020)’, ‘autonomy condition’ in the last column of De Sampaio et al. should be lowercase as is flow condition in the other lines, and the enumeration in the last column of Klasen et al. should be ‘A, B, & C’. In Table 3, under ‘Design’ and DeKock et al. the font size changes. In Table 4, the ‘&’ is in the start of the line under ‘Experiment type’ and Castellar et al.. 5) Why not put ‘fEMG’ instead of ‘Facial EMG’ (of course explaining the abbreviation below)? Same for ‘RR’ and ‘Respiratory Rate’. 6) It is important to clarify in the last column how the findings were related to flow. Sometimes you write ‘for flow’ and ‘during flow’, sometimes ‘for flow condition’, ‘during flow condition’, and ‘at flow condition’ or ‘in the flow state’, ‘with the flow experience’, and ‘during self-reported experience of flow’. This is unnecessarily confusing. I would suggest you stick to ‘in the flow condition’ whenever the analysis was based on group differences, and to ‘during self-reported flow’ whenever it was based on correlations with a flow score. 7) ‘LF-HRV’ and ‘HF-HRV’ should consistently be spelled with the hyphen. 8) In Table 2, please put ‘Increased activity in the left IFG, left putamen, & posterior cortical regions during self-reported flow; decreased activity in MPFC, PCC, & AMY during self-reported flow’. All the Tables were checked and all inconsistencies were corrected. We are thankful for this effort by the reviewer!
paper_title_zh: 《玩电子游戏时心流体验的外周生理与神经相关因素：一项综合性综述》
paper_abstract_zh: 心流状态被定义为在高度集中和专注的活动中深度投入，并伴随愉悦感。视频游戏是引发心流的有效工具，保持玩家处于这种状态被认为是游戏设计的核心目标之一。许多研究聚焦于心流背后的生理和神经机制。在描述这一心理状态背后的统一机制时，结果并不一致。本文对心流的生理和神经相关因素进行了全面综述，并解释了所报告的生理和神经标志与心流体验之间的关系。尽管结果异质，但似乎有可能在所报告的标志与心流的认知和体验方面之间建立关联，特别是在唤醒、注意力控制、奖励处理、自动化和自我参照处理方面。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1（Birte Thissen）

基本报告

首先，我要感谢作者根据两位审稿人的建议对稿件进行了广泛的修订。我相信稿件已经有了显著的改进，现在结构更加清晰，对理论假设和观察结果的讨论更加深入，文献综述也更加全面。因此，在稿件发表之前，我只想提出一些最后的微小建议和意见：

1) 我注意到稿件中存在一些语法错误和拼写错误，因此建议在发表前请母语人士对最终版本进行校对。例如：删除“either”（第100行）；在“as well as”后重复“on”（第162行）；使用“for the creation of a flow state”或“for creating a flow state”（第163行）；U形拼写应保持一致，使用大写或小写U（例如，第207和211行）；“A significant effect was neither found for…, nor for…”（第224-226行）；用“noted”代替“considered”（第256行）；“associated with”（第321行）；“capacity”（第340行）似乎不是合适的词（您是指正确判断自身适当难度水平的技能，还是指自行选择难度水平的机会？）；复数“flow scores… were”（第413-414行）；“flow as measured by…”（第430行）；“a mental arithmetic task”由于任务之前未描述（第464行）；“higher left temporal cortex alpha activity, which reflects decreased cortical activity in this region, is associated with improved performance, as it represents reduced internal verbalization and increased visual-spatial processing in the right hemisphere”（第531-534行）；“a 7-second video clip”“table tennis”（第549行）；“was to be expected in the more difficult condition”（第574-575行）；“which increase with increasing difficulty”（第576行）；“the flow and anxiety condition”（第579行）；用“as compared to”而不是“than”（第580行）；删除“alone”或替换为“on its own accord”（第620行）；“playing in 2D”（第666行）；“The observed co-activation… aligns”（第756-757行）；“flow was found to be associated with”（第759行）；“a purely effortful mental experience”（第766行）；用“practice”代替“exercise”（第789行）；“mind-wandering”（第801行）；“body- and self-awareness”（第807行）；“role”（第163和819行）；“some studies…, other studies…”（第832-833行）；用“in which”代替“where”（第833行）；删除“of”（第840行）；“neural activity”（第849行）；“…, given the different physiological and cognitive demands of the flow-inducing activity, …”（第850-851行）。此外，“e.g.”通常后接逗号，动名词前也应加逗号（例如，第885-886行“…, reporting medium levels of performance”），列举三个或更多事物时，在“and”前需要加逗号（例如，第122行）；请确保在整个稿件中添加这些逗号。 此外，请检查单词之间的空格，因为你有时要么放得太多（例如，第236、267、486、498、513、649、660、742、841、886、892行），要么没有放（例如，第44、469、470、486行）。还有一些风格上的错误：第355行有一个分号，看起来没有意义；第91行的FKS不知为何被下划线标出；破折号有时带空格，有时不带。我不敢声称已经发现了所有问题，因此强烈建议作者再次校对他们的手稿，以满足形式和风格上的要求。我们试图解决所有语法错误和拼写错误。我们将手稿发送给了一位母语者，以确保最终手稿没有任何错误。

2) 我对引言部分仍有一些疑问：‘为什么我们追求能让我们快乐的活动？’这个问题并没有激发读者的兴趣，因为答案就在问题中；我建议直接删除（第37-38行）。此外，我认为文本中仍存在对处理流畅性以及流畅状态的前因、组成部分和后果的误解。处理流畅性是流畅状态的一个维度，就像专注和享受一样（即比九个组成部分更广泛），并且直接反映在流畅状态的一些组成部分中，例如清晰目标感和即时反馈感。因此，并没有所谓的‘处理流畅性状态’（第40-41行），而是处理流畅性是流畅状态定义的一部分，应该与享受和专注一起出现在第38-39行。我们认为，审稿人提到的“处理流畅性”作为流畅状态的一个维度，是指Csikszentmihalyi所描述的“在流畅体验中合并行动和意识”（Csikszentmihalyi, 1975, 第38页）。由于文献中没有名为处理流畅性的流畅状态维度，我们在第39-42行中解决了这一关切：“流畅是一种处理流畅性的主观体验，在这种体验中，行动似乎毫不费力、流畅且几乎自动发生。根据这一理论，流畅最明显的标志是行动和意识的合并，以至于‘处于流畅状态的人意识到自己的行动，但意识不到意识本身’。”

3) ‘源于内在动机’，然而在我看来，并不一定属于定义本身，因为内在动机是流畅状态的前因（也可能是后果）——因此应在稍后与前三项关键组成部分（不是维度！）一起提及，作为潜在的前因（第54-55行）。重要的是，流畅状态的每一个前因（例如，开始流畅活动时的清晰目标）同时也是一个体验组成部分（例如，在此活动中流畅状态中对清晰目标的感知）。 为了使这一点更清晰，我建议将第54-56行改写为：“尽管所有九个关键成分都反映了心流状态中的主观体验，但前三个成分（技能与挑战的平衡、明确的目标和即时反馈）在更客观的层面上也可以理解为心流的活动相关前提条件。此外，就个人而言，对活动的内在动机可以促进心流体验（Csikszentmihalyi, 1975）。然而，最佳的技能-挑战平衡被认为是进入心流状态的主要先决条件……”我们认为，任务的内在动机已经在第9个成分中作为自足体验的一个维度被提及。4）我还建议重新组织引言部分，以便读者更容易理解：在介绍了心流通道模型及其预测的技能-挑战平衡与心流之间关系的潜在调节因素（第59-75行）之后，解释这一理论框架如何在计算机游戏背景下相对容易地实施（“……可以促进心流体验的倾向。——新段落——尽管存在这样的潜在调节因素，心流通道模型中假设的技能-挑战平衡与心流之间的关系为通过呈现不同挑战水平来实验性地操纵心流提供了一种方法。尽管在受控的实验室条件下诱发心流被认为是很困难的（请提供参考文献！），基于游戏的研究范式尤其有前景，因为a）游戏的难度水平可以相对容易地调整以实现技能-挑战平衡，且b）游戏可以被视为一种典型的诱发心流的活动”；然后继续从第104-112行和第132-133行说明视频游戏为何是一种绝佳的心流活动，并接着从第113-118行介绍操纵方法）。请确保包括所有三种方法，即也包括中等挑战水平方法（Rheinberg和Vollmeyer, 2003），在第113-117行——然后将第124-126行提前作为例子（“例如，Rheinberg和Vollmeyer……”）。在下一个段落中，你可以给出计算机游戏在实验心流研究中的三个有趣应用领域：a）理解巅峰表现，b）心流在治疗环境中的潜在应用，c）游戏乐趣的最大化。因此，依次放置第75-84行、第131-148行和第149-153行（当然要有适当的连接段落）。然后，你可以探讨这项研究面临的方法论挑战及其以心理生理学或神经指标形式解决这一挑战的潜在方案，指出读者为何应对你即将进行的文献综述感兴趣（例如，“为了成功研究涉及心流和表现、治疗应用或游戏体验的研究问题，实验范式必须伴随对心流状态的有效测量。”）。 将第85-103行移至此处——如何通过自我报告测量心流，这种方式存在的问题以及为何需要额外的心理生理和神经测量；现在也简要提及第156-158行的双重任务方法（在提及时，请拼写出来‘双重任务方法’）。然后你可以以第158-171行结束。我们重新组织这部分内容以解决这一关切。请参见第75-102行。5) 引言中仍存在一些小的不明确之处：‘自足体验’（第52行）——这个术语需要解释（希腊语：‘auto’=自我，‘telos’=目标）或改写为‘内在享受’，这样更易理解。在第67-68行，是‘主观评估为成功重要的活动’——这样，获得的结果（低要求/心流）变得更易理解。FSS（第90-91行）是在体育背景下开发的，但可以且经常应用于其他心流活动，就像FKS一样。FKS在英语中称为Flow Sort Scale，因此也应缩写为FSS，而不是FKS。FQ（第668-669行）在此部分缺失，应与ESM一起介绍，因为它最初是为ESM研究开发的（第85-88行）。效能动机可以用‘控制感’来解释，而不是‘赋能’，指出其与心流成分的联系。TOJ（第143-148行）需要更多解释，因为心流期间时间感的丧失会暗示心流体验实际上会降低时间判断测试的表现。同样，为何自主性被认为是心流的重要决定因素也需要简要说明（第119-120行，第340-341行）。我深知在视频游戏中区分心流和沉浸的困难，但由于后面提到了沉浸这一术语，需要有一两句全面的说明（‘一些研究（参考文献）实施了一个额外的沉浸条件，旨在通过操纵图形、声音和游戏玩法等因素将玩家的思维带入虚拟世界（参考文献）。沉浸是VR和计算机游戏研究中的重要概念，似乎与这些活动情境中的心流密切相关，因为两者都涉及游戏者常见的愉快、专注的心理状态。然而，心流和沉浸可以通过微妙的结构差异来区分（关于此的更多信息，请参见Michailidis, Balaguer-Ballester, & He, 2018）。’）。我们尽力澄清了审稿人提到的手稿中的大多数模糊之处。实验设计我很高兴看到作者额外努力扩展了文献研究到其他数据库，并修订了纳入标准的呈现。方法论现在更加清晰和有说服力。我也发现新的结果呈现结构对读者来说更容易理解。 再次，我要称赞作者们对修订的成功，仅有几点小建议：1）我认为某些部分需要稍作澄清：在第182行，术语“运动游戏”可能需要简短的解释，并且混杂因素可以附上例子（例如，运动效果、社交互动的处理……），以便向读者解释为何排除了35篇论文，尽可能透明和详细地说明排除标准；在第204-205行，我会写成“在心流体验中挑战会引发一定程度的压力”（第204-205行），因为“压力”和“挑战”在某些理论中不能互换使用；在第206和207行，我认为“快速/慢速反应系统”是更合适的术语；在第228和556行，请删除“情绪的”，因为心流不是一种情绪状态；在第236行，你提到研究中评估了心流，但后来又说实际上没有用问卷评估心流（第239行）；你可能想说存在心流、沉浸和无聊的条件，但没有测量自我报告的心流？；在第445行，请写成“第一人称射击（FPS）游戏”；第447-449行可以用一个例子来澄清“对Csikszentmihalyi所描述因素有贡献的游戏事件”是什么意思；在第433行缺少FPS游戏的名称，在第419行缺少视频游戏的名称，在第656行缺少心流量表的名称。上述每个问题的额外信息已包含在稿件中，以进一步澄清这些问题。2）我觉得先给出HRV指数的解释，然后再讨论这些解释有些不妥。我会直接指出争议点：“为了研究心流与ANS激活之间的关系，通常评估心血管指标，因为心率变异性，涉及相邻心跳时间间隔的波动，传统上被视为区分PSNS和SNS激活的指标。因此，高频HRV可以被视为副交感神经激活的直接测量，而低频HRV长期以来被解释为反映交感神经的影响，使得HF/LF比值成为SNS和PSNS之间自主神经平衡的指标。然而，需要注意的是，对LF-HRV和LF/HF比值的这种解释是有争议的……”然后接着提供第293-301行的信息。在此澄清之后，你可以继续报告De Manzano等人（2010年）的研究，然后是Chanel等人（2011年）的研究。我们感谢审稿人的建议。然而，我们认为稿件中解释ANS与心血管指标关系及其对这些指标的论证是清晰的。我们认为解释文献中使用的这些指标的假设并随后进行讨论将有助于澄清研究结果。 3) 有时某些与心流相关的构念的测量方法并不明确，因为它们可以通过自我报告和生理指标来测量。例如，在第277行，您是指自我报告的正向情感和无努力注意力吗？第321行同样如此：心理努力的减少是如何评估的？第416行，您是指心流状态的最后30秒，而第478行，您是指心流得分吗？同样，在第500行，您是指心流状态，而在第501行，您是指心流得分与默认模式网络（DMN）活动之间的相关性吗？第595行中提到的注意力得分是指什么？在第868行，我假设您的意思是“……并不能保证一个人会在心流状态下进入心流状态。”在第489行，您是指心流得分——还是心流指数是其他某种东西？在第615行，您所说的“心流时刻”是指什么，因为目前心流无法以高时间精度捕捉？我们尝试澄清了审稿人提到的手稿中的大多数模糊之处。

4) 我建议重新结构和措辞某些行以明确其含义：在第200-201行，我建议改为“与心流期间注意力焦点本质上是无努力的观点相反，Keller及其同事（2011年）认为，由于高度投入以及任务的挑战性，心流涉及相当大的心理努力。”；在第234行，“EDA测量值随着游戏难度级别的增加而增加，表明唤醒水平升高”；在第323-329行，“不同的发现表明，在……期间，参与者可能不会感知到那么多的压力……还应注意的是，Keller的研究涉及相对较少的参与者，并通过心流状态来操作化心流，而没有实际测量自我报告的心流体验，这可能影响其发现的有效性。”（顺便提一下，如果使用这种操作化方法，分析很可能不是相关性的。）；在第401行，“默认模式网络（DMN）的活动被认为会减少”，因为您在此处仍在陈述假设而非发现；在第459-461行，“需要注意的是，在第二项研究中，主观心流体验被假设由心流状态引发，但这一假设并未通过自我报告的心流量表进行验证。”；在第544行，要么说“再次”，要么引用其他研究；在第491行，“，表明自我相关处理的减少，”；在第556-560行，“Chanel等人（2011年）试图根据EEG信号对俄罗斯方块游戏中的三种不同挑战-技能条件进行分类。尽管他们的结果表明在某些电极条件下存在明显的theta功率差异，但无法获得与无聊、心流和焦虑状态的精确联系。”；在第843行，我猜您是指“心流通道模型”。 在第856行，删除“would”，接着说“FPSs是三维游戏，其中空间导航至关重要，因为在任何给定时间，……”，并删除第860行 merely repeats the part about spatial navigation的句子；在第868-869行，由于你给出了一个建议，应该说“在未来的研究中，应使用自报告流畅度量表评估流畅状态下的主观流畅体验，以确定参与者是否能够进入完全的流畅状态。”我们尝试澄清了审稿人提到的手稿中的大多数模糊之处。5）我注意到文本中存在一些重复（例如，多次提到流畅状态并不保证流畅体验）。此外，在描述一项研究时，通常先有一个更普遍的句子（例如，第412行“玩电子游戏”），然后是一个更具体的句子（例如，第413行“在玩俄罗斯方块时”）；这些信息可以更简洁地在一个句子中呈现。最后，括号常用于插入完整的句子（例如，第431-432行）；然而，为了流畅阅读，建议括号仅用于给出简短关键词，并在需要更多文本时使用从句。请根据这些改进机会再次修订文本。研究发现的效度我相信，经过修订的、更深入的对研究发现的讨论，以及对未来研究设计的明确建议，使得这篇文献综述对PeerJ的读者来说具有趣味性，并清晰地展示了其对领域的增值。除了我在审稿的其他部分已经提到的语言和语法相关的小问题外，我唯一的意见是，是否应将“愉悦的专注状态”重新命名为“主观上无努力的专注状态”，以将其与“积极效价和高唤醒状态”区分开来。除此之外，我认为讨论部分非常深思熟虑！对作者的意见在此，我必须强调多次校对稿件的重要性，以确保风格的一致性和正确性；我自己也经历过因形式错误而被拒稿的情况。我已经尽力为你找出这些错误，但不声称已找到所有错误，所以请再次检查。一个持续不一致和形式错误的典型例子是表格：1）对于“实验类型”，你写的是“FPS Game/game:”或“Game”且没有冒号。同样，对于“设计”，你写的是“40分钟游戏时间”、“10分钟”或“3分钟游戏时间块”。请统一报告方式。我建议使用“(FPS) Game:”和“无聊/流畅/焦虑，10分钟游戏时间”。2）在“测量”中，经常出现“&”位于行首或缺少逗号的情况； 为避免这些错误，我建议简单地用逗号列举所有指标（例如，使用‘EDA, HRV, fEMG’而不是‘EDA, HRV, & fEMG’）。在“实验设计”下的多个游戏也应如此——仅在双重任务中使用‘&’。3) 仍然存在一些遗漏逗号的情况，当表格中列举三个或更多项目时。在最后一列，我也建议仅在列举指标时使用‘&’，而在结果中则使用‘;’（例如，表1中的‘LF-HRV与皮质醇水平呈倒U型关系，与自我报告的心流呈正相关；副交感神经激活与自我报告的心流呈线性关系’）。4) 一些形式上的错误仍然存在：在表1中，Chanel等人的“参与者”一词中的s移到了下一行，Leger等人和Harmat等人“设计”下的行中有多余的空格，‘77(40f)’中缺少一个括号，Leger等人最后一列的列举应为‘A, B, & C’。在表2中，‘Moreno et al. (2020)’中有多余的空格，De Sampaio等人最后一列的‘autonomy condition’应小写，与其他行的‘flow condition’一致，Klasen等人最后一列的列举应为‘A, B, & C’。在表3中，DeKock等人“设计”下的字体大小发生变化。在表4中，‘Experiment type’和Castellar等人下的行首有‘&’。5) 为什么不用‘fEMG’代替‘Facial EMG’（当然在下方解释缩写）？同样适用于‘RR’和‘Respiratory Rate’。6) 在最后一列中澄清发现与心流的关系很重要。有时你写‘for flow’和‘during flow’，有时‘for flow condition’，‘during flow condition’，和‘at flow condition’或‘in the flow state’，‘with the flow experience’，和‘during self-reported experience of flow’。这没有必要地造成了混淆。我建议在基于组间差异的分析时统一使用‘in the flow condition’，在基于与心流得分的相关性分析时统一使用‘during self-reported flow’。7) ‘LF-HRV’和‘HF-HRV’应始终带连字符拼写。8) 在表2中，请写‘在自我报告的心流期间，左侧IFG、左侧壳核和后皮质区域活动增加；在自我报告的心流期间，MPFC、PCC和AMY活动减少’。所有表格都已检查，所有不一致之处均已纠正。我们感谢审稿人的这一努力！

I am confident that the revised, more in-depth discussion of the findings together with explicit recommendations for future study designs makes this literature review an interesting read for PeerJ’s readership and clearly shows its added value to the field.
Other than that, I find the discussion section very well thought-out!

I believe that the manuscript greatly improved as it now shows a clearer structure, a more in-depth discussion of both theoretical assumptions and observed findings, and a more comprehensive review of the literature.

Examples: leave out ‘either’ (line 100); repeat ‘on’ after ‘as well as’ (line 162); use ‘for the creation of a flow state’ or ‘for creating a flow state’ (line 163); spell U-shaped either consistently with an uppercase or lowercase U (e.g., lines 207 & 211); ‘A significant effect was neither found for…, nor for…’ (lines 224-226); ‘noted’ instead of ‘considered’ (line 256); ‘associated with’ (line 321); ‘capacity’ (line 340) does not seem to be the right word (do you mean the skill to correctly judge the appropriate difficulty level for oneself or the opportunity to pick a difficulty level oneself?); plural ‘flow scores… were’ (lines 413-414); ‘flow as measured by…’ (line 430); ‘a mental arithmetic task’ since the task has not been described beforehand (line 464); ‘higher left temporal cortex alpha activity, which reflects decreased cortical activity in this region, is associated with improved performance, as it represents reduced internal verbalization and increased visual-spatial processing in the right hemisphere’ (lines 531-534); ‘a 7-second video clip’ ‘table tennis’ (line 549); ‘was to be expected in the more difficult condition’ (lines 574-575); ‘which increase with increasing difficulty’ (line 576); ‘the flow and anxiety condition’ (line 579); ‘as compared to’ rather than ‘than’ (line 580); leave out ‘alone’ or replace with ‘on its own accord’ (line 620); ‘playing in 2D’ (line 666); ‘The observed co-activation… aligns’ (line 756-757); ‘flow was found to be associated with’ (line 759); ‘a purely effortful mental experience’ (line 766); ‘practice’ instead of ‘exercise’ (line 789); ‘mind-wandering’ (line 801); ‘body- and self-awareness (line 807); ‘role’ (line 163 and 819); ‘some studies…, other studies…’ (lines 832-833); ‘in which’ instead of ‘where’ (line 833); leave out ‘of’ (line 840); ‘neural activity’ (line 849); ‘…, given the different physiological and cognitive demands of the flow-inducing activity, …’ (lines 850- 851). Moreover, ‘e.g.’ is normally followed by a comma and the gerund is preceded by one (e.g., lines 885-886 ‘…, reporting medium levels of performance’), and an enumeration of three or more things requires a comma before the ‘and’ (e.g., line 122); please make sure to put these commas throughout the manuscript. Also, check the blanks between words as you tend to sometimes either put too many (e.g., lines 236, 267, 486, 498, 513, 649, 660, 742, 841, 886, 892) or none (e.g., lines 44, 469, 470, 486). There are also some stylistic mistakes: In line 355, there is a semicolon that does not seem to make sense; FKS in line 91 is underlined for some reason; the dash once comes with blanks and sometimes without.
I do not claim to have found everything, so I strongly recommend the authors to also proof-read their manuscript in terms of formal and stylistic requirements once more.

I believe some section need a bit more clarification: In line 182, the term ‘exergames’ may need a short explanation and the confounding factors could be accompanied by examples (e.g., movement effects, processing of social interaction, …), in order to explain to the reader why the 35 papers were excluded, to be as transparent and detailed as possible with the exclusion criteria; in lines 204-205, I would write ‘that the experience of challenge during flow induces a certain amount of stress’ (lines 204-205) since ‘stress’ and ‘challenge’ cannot be used interchangeably in some theories; in line 206 and 207, I find ‘fast/slow response system’ to be better terms, respectively; in line 228 and 556, please leave out ‘emotional’ as flow is not an emotional state; in line 236, you state that flow was assessed in the study and later go on to say that flow was actually not assessed with a questionnaire (line 239); you may want to say that there was a flow, immersion, and boredom condition, but no measurement of self-reported flow?; in line 445, please write ‘a first person shooter (FPS) game’; lines 447-449 could use an example to clarify what is meant by ‘game events that contribute to factors described by Csikszentmihalyi’; in line 433 the name of the FPS game, in line 419 the name of the videogame, and in line 656 the name of the flow scale is missing. The additional information on each of the above-mentioned concerns was included in the manuscript to addionally clarify the issues.

I have some remaining issues with the introduction: ‘Why do we seek activities that make us happy?’ does not inspire interest in the reader as the answer is in the question; I would suggest to just leave it out (line 37-38).
I would re-structure and re-word certain lines to clarify their meaning: In lines 200-201, I would suggest.

‘In contrast to the notion that the attentional focus during flow is essentially effortless, Keller and colleagues (2011) argued that flow involves considerable mental effort due to the high degree of involvement along with the challenging nature of the task.’; in line 234, ‘EDA measures increased with the game’s difficulty level, indicating heightening arousal’; in lines 323-329, ‘The different findings show that during… participants may not perceive as much stress…. It should also be noted, that Keller’s study involved a relatively small number of participants and operationalized flow through the flow condition, without actually measuring self-reported flow experiences, which might affect the validity of their findings.’ (On a side-note, if this operationalization is used, the analyses is most likely not correlational.); in line 401, ‘the activity of the DMN is thought to decrease’ since you are still stating assumptions and not findings at this point; in line 459-461, ‘It should be noted, though, that in the second study, the subjective flow experience was assumed to be elicited by the flow condition, but this assumption was not checked using a self-report flow scale.’; in line 544, either say ‘once again’ or refer to the other studies; in line 491, ‘, indicating less self-related processing,’; in lines 556-560, ‘Chanel et al. (2011) tried to classify their three different challenge-skill conditions in a game of Tetris according to EEG signals. Even though their results indicated distinct theta power between conditions in some electrodes, no precise link to states of boredom, flow, and anxiety could be obtained.’; In line 843, I guess you mean the ‘flow channel model’; in line 856, leave out ‘would’ and go on to say ‘FPSs are three-dimensional games, in which spatial navigation is crucial, since at any given time, ….’ and delete the sentence (line 860) which merely repeats the part about spatial navigation; in line 868-869, since you give a recommendation, say ‘The subjective experience of flow in the flow condition should be assessed using self-report flow scales in future studies, to determine whether the participants were able to enter a full flow state or not.’. We tried to clarify most of the ambiguities in the manuscript which are mentioned by the reviewer.

paper_title: Osteokines and the vasculature: a review of the in vitro effects of osteocalcin, fibroblast growth factor-23 and lipocalin-2
paper_abstract: Bone-derived factors that demonstrate extra-skeletal functions, also termed osteokines, are fast becoming a highly interesting and focused area of cross-disciplinary endocrine research. Osteocalcin (OCN), fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF23) and lipocalin-2 (LCN-2), produced in bone, comprise an important endocrine system that is finely tuned with other organs to ensure homeostatic balance and health. This review aims to evaluate in vitro evidence of the direct involvement of these proteins in vascular cells and whether any causal roles in cardiovascular disease or inflammation can be supported. PubMed, Medline, Embase and Google Scholar were searched for relevant research articles investigating the exogenous addition of OCN, FGF23 or LCN-2 to vascular smooth muscle or endothelial cells. Overall, these osteokines are directly vasoactive across a range of human and animal vascular cells. Both OCN and FGF23 have anti-apoptotic properties and increase eNOS phosphorylation and nitric oxide production through Akt signalling in human endothelial cells. OCN improves intracellular insulin signalling and demonstrates protective effects against endoplasmic reticulum stress in murine and human endothelial cells. OCN may be involved in calcification but further research is warranted, while there is no evidence for a pro-calcific effect of FGF23 in vitro. FGF23 and LCN-2 increase proliferation in some cell types and increase and decrease reactive oxygen species generation, respectively. LCN-2 also has anti-apoptotic effects but may increase endoplasmic reticulum stress as well as have pro-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic properties in human vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells. There is no strong evidence to support a pathological role of OCN or FGF23 in the vasculature based on these findings. In contrast, they may in fact support normal endothelial functioning, vascular homeostasis and vasodilation. No studies examined whether OCN or FGF23 may have a role in vascular inflammation. Limited studies with LCN-2 indicate a pro-inflammatory and possible pathological role in the vasculature but further mechanistic data is required. Overall, these osteokines pose intriguing functions which should be investigated comprehensively to
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Sweta Maheshwari)  Thank you so much for taking the time to review and help us improve our manuscript. We really appreciate the detailed feedback and thank you for highlighting the issues, a tick mark has been placed beside each individual suggested comment, which indicates it has been corrected as suggested. Many thanks. Basic reporting The review article by Millar et al. summarizes the endocrine functions and in vitro effects of osteokines on vascular cells. This review article is clearly written and well organized with relevant subheadings. Tables are comprehensive and helpful. The review is cross-disciplinary and will be of interest to a wide audience including life science and medical researchers as well as clinicians. Some minor comments are stated below in the “Comments for the author” section. Experimental design The search strategy used to retrieve articles related to this literature review is excellent with search encompassing multiple databases. The review article is logically organized into relevant subsections for all the three osteokines described in the text. Validity of the findings The conclusions are well supported by the background and existing literature on osteokines. Furthermore, some knowledge gap existing in this field has also been highlighted well towards the end of conclusions. Comments for the Author Some minor comments and suggestions are as follows: 1. Lines 62, 93 & 96: Osteoprotegerin is misspelled (it should be ‘e’ instead of ‘o’ after ‘t’)  2. Line 63: RANKL should not have a hyphen between K & L.  3. Lines 69 & 95- use a semicolon to separate multiple references and order them chronologically as stated in the “Instructions for authors” submission guidelines on PeerJ website. This needs to be checked throughout the article.  4. Line 76: Abbreviate cardiovascular disease as CVD in addition to writing the full-form (as CVD has been used later in the text in line 377).  5. Line 122: The full-length osteocalcin (OCN) is 95 and 100 amino acid protein in mice and humans respectively. There is a signal peptide of 22 amino acids and a propeptide of 28 amino acids in humans. It’s the mature protein that has 49 amino acids in humans (see Chapter 2- Bone, matrix and mineralization-Pediatric bone-2nd edition-Marc D. McKee, William G. Cole 2012 OR search protein database in NCBI for full length protein sequence). So to say “OCN is 46 and 49 amino acid protein in mice and humans” as stated in this review is not fully correct. Either say “the mature OCN is 46 and 49 ….” OR state “the full-length OCN is 95 and 100… ”  edited to read ‘mature length…’. 6. Line 145: “fragment from proteolytic enzymes” sentence needs to be corrected as “fragments released by proteolytic cleavage” (the fragments are not from proteolytic enzymes but are from osteocalcin itself.)  7. Line 151: Hannemann is misspelled (it should be ‘nn’ after ‘Ha’ instead of ‘mm’).  8. Line 163: The suitable word is “identified” instead of “expressed”.  9. Line 241: It should be “suppressed these effects” instead of “suppressed these results”.  10. Lines 260-261: “deserve” instead of “deserves”.  11. Line 266: Change “251 amino acid peptide” to “251 amino acid protein” (its big enough to be called as a protein, in general less than 50 amino acids is designated as a peptide).  12. Line 268: “N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase” (delete the space between galactosa and minyl)  13. Line 284: It should be “measure” instead of “measures” (as the preceding words say C-terminus FGF23 assays, correct one or the other).  corrected to ‘measure’. 14. Line 335: Write also the full form of ERK as extracellular signal-regulated kinase (as ERK has been used later at multiple places, so would be useful to write its full form here)  15. Lines 338-339: Change “when soluble klotho and phosphate was” to “….were”.  16. Lines 397-398: It should read as “monomer, homodimer, or heterodimer by forming a complex with matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)”.  Also, LCN-2 stabilizes MMP-9 by preventing MMP-9 from autodegradation rather than increasing its activity. (See Chakraborty et al., Biochim Biophys Acta., 2012.) So to say LCN-2 increases its activity as in line 398 is rather conflicting.  now reads ‘which stabilizes MMP-9 by preventing autodegradation’. 17. Line 424: Change “though” to “through”. 18. Line 430: The full form of MC4R should be written (melanocortin 4 receptor).  19. Line 433: “present” instead of “presents”  20. Lines 455 & 460: H2O2 – It appears there is a 0 (zero) mistakenly typed there instead of O (capital letter O).  21. Line 467: CXCL10 should also be stated in its full form as C-X-C motif chemokine 10.  22. Line 501 & 32: It should read as “have” instead of “having”.  23. Table 2: Legend has “FGF-23”.It should be written as FGF23 just to be consistent with the rest of the text in the review.  Another minor correction- enter the units of concentration in the last entry of table 2 - “Richter et al., 2016” which is “10 ng/ml” in the concentration column. 
paper_title_zh: 骨因子与血管系统：骨钙素、成纤维细胞生长因子-23和脂钙蛋白-2体外效应综述
paper_abstract_zh: 骨源性因子，即表现出骨骼外功能的因子，也称为骨因子（osteokines），正迅速成为跨学科内分泌研究的一个高度有趣且备受关注的领域。骨钙素（OCN）、成纤维细胞生长因子-23（FGF23）和脂质运载蛋白-2（LCN-2），这些在骨骼中产生的因子，构成了一个重要的内分泌系统，该系统与其他器官精细调节，以确保体内平衡和健康。本综述旨在评估这些蛋白质在血管细胞中的直接参与作用的体外证据，并探讨它们在心血管疾病或炎症中是否存在因果关系。通过PubMed、Medline、Embase和Google Scholar检索了相关研究文章，这些文章探讨了外源性添加OCN、FGF23或LCN-2对血管平滑肌细胞或内皮细胞的影响。总体而言，这些骨因子在多种人类和动物血管细胞中具有直接的血管活性作用。OCN和FGF23均具有抗凋亡特性，并通过Akt信号通路增加人内皮细胞中eNOS的磷酸化和一氧化氮的产生。OCN改善细胞内胰岛素信号传导，并在小鼠和人类内皮细胞中显示出对抗内质网应激的保护作用。OCN可能参与钙化，但需要进一步研究，而体外实验中没有证据表明FGF23具有促钙化作用。FGF23和LCN-2在某些细胞类型中增加增殖，并分别增加和减少活性氧的产生。LCN-2也具有抗凋亡作用，但可能增加内质网应激，并在人类血管内皮细胞和平滑肌细胞中具有促炎和促血管生成特性。基于这些发现，没有强有力证据支持OCN或FGF23在血管中的病理作用。相反，它们实际上可能支持正常的内皮功能、血管稳态和血管舒张。没有研究探讨OCN或FGF23在血管炎症中是否发挥作用。有限的LCN-2研究表明其在血管中具有促炎和可能的病理作用，但需要进一步的机制数据。总体而言，这些骨因子具有引人注目的功能，应进行全面研究以
review_content_zh:
**审稿人2 (Sweta Maheshwari) **

非常感谢您抽出时间审阅并帮助我们改进手稿。我们非常感谢您详细的反馈，并感谢您指出这些问题。每个建议性评论旁边都已放置了一个勾号，表示已按建议进行更正。非常感谢。

**基本报告**

Millar等人撰写的综述文章总结了骨因子对血管细胞的内分泌功能及体外效应。该综述文章写作清晰，组织有序，相关小标题设置得当。表格内容全面且有帮助。该综述跨学科，将对包括生命科学和医学研究人员以及临床医生在内的广泛读者群体感兴趣。一些次要意见在下面的“对作者的意见”部分中列出。

**实验设计**

用于检索与该文献综述相关文章的搜索策略非常出色，涵盖了多个数据库。综述文章逻辑清晰地分为与文本中描述的三种骨因子相关的各个小节。

**结果的有效性**

结论得到了骨因子背景知识和现有文献的充分支持。此外，该领域存在的一些知识空白也在结论末尾得到了很好的强调。

**对作者的意见**

以下是一些次要意见和建议：

1. 第62、93和96行：Osteoprotegerin拼写错误（在“t”后应为“e”而非“o”）
2. 第63行：RANKL在K和L之间不应有连字符。

paper_title: Tapping into the plasticity of plant architecture for increased stress resilience
paper_abstract: Plant architecture develops post-embryonically and emerges from a dialogue between the developmental signals and environmental cues. Length and branching of the vegetative and reproductive tissues were the focus of improvement of plant performance from the early days of plant breeding. Current breeding priorities are changing, as we need to prioritize plant productivity under increasingly challenging environmental conditions. While it has been widely recognized that plant architecture changes in response to the environment, its contribution to plant productivity in the changing climate remains to be fully explored. This review will summarize prior discoveries of genetic control of plant architecture traits and their effect on plant performance under environmental stress. We review new tools in phenotyping that will guide future discoveries of genes contributing to plant architecture, its plasticity, and its contributions to stress resilience. Subsequently, we provide a perspective into how integrating the study of new species, modern phenotyping techniques, and modeling can lead to discovering new genetic targets underlying the plasticity of plant architecture and stress resilience. Altogether, this review provides a new perspective on the plasticity of plant architecture and how it can be harnessed for increased performance under environmental stress.
review_content:
The manuscript “Tapping into the plasticity of plant architecture for increased stress resilience” by Maryam Rahmati Ishka and Magdalena Julkowska has important and accurate information in each of its sections. It is an interesting review that will be useful for the plant development community.

Some comments: in bold are some phrases written by the authors and I wrote below the phrase, some comments on them.

Root architecture:
  * “Selective breeding or genetic engineering has been used to alter plant architecture, creating dwarf varieties of crops that are less likely to lodge, thereby providing significant contribution to yield increase”
  * It could be interesting to put more examples of using selective breeding or genetic engineering as it seems that this was the only goal of these kind of studies.
  * “while the final plant architecture depends on activation or dormancy of the axillary branches, which is controlled by internal and external signals”
  * Also, the primary root and shoot meristems depends on internal and external signals, you said this later in the text, but I suggest that you put this paragraph here: “Both primary and secondary growth respond to internal signals and external stimuli”.
  * “The absolute length of time required for permanent alterations in plant architecture will depend on the specific environmental factor, as well as developmental, genetic, and physiological contexts”
  * This is a very relevant information, please put references. It would be very interesting to know how this length is mechanistically determined.
  * “Current breeding strategies utilize the most heritable traits, with low interaction between the genotype and the environment, resulting in reliable plant performance across environmental conditions”
  * This phrase seems contradictory, the breeding strategies are meant to be useful in specific environments and not across different environmental conditions. Please comment on this.
  * “Lateral roots can develop into long non-determinant roots, which help with soil exploration, or shorter and thinner roots, which contribute directly to water and nutrient absorption”
  * Many lateral roots display contrasting development in homogeneous growth conditions, a phenomenon that has been called developmental instability (Muller et al., 2019). Please comment on this.
  * Figure 1. There are more genes that participate in root depth: XAL1 ref [4], XAL2 ref [3] and also, ANR1 ref [1], ref [2].
  * “Nutrient deficiency, drought, and salt stress, strigolactones promote the elongation of main root growth”
  * I do not completely understand this phrase.
  * I think it would be important to talk in general about the participation of the phytohormones in the control of development in general.
  * “when roots grow through large air-gaps in the soil (xerobranching). Of note, both processes seem to depend on ABA signaling”
  * The second one depends also on ethylene and auxin (Bennett M).
  * “combination of individual stresses often results in different root architectures compared to individual stress”
  * Use more than one stress under controlled conditions? This looks like a proposal to me that can be incorporated in the Conclusions section.
Shoot architecture
  * “Through a stochastic process, the first primordium develops at a random position within the shoot apical meristem”
  * It will be important to consider the stochasticity in modelling, please comment on this.
  * “and leaf number prior to flowering are highly influenced by the environment”
  * and after flowering?
  * “However, the genetic information within one species is not providing exhaustive representation of the mechanisms that contribute to plant productivity and environmental resilience across the plant kingdom” and in the same paragraph “This can be achieved through comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses of genes that were previously identified to be involved in regulating plant architecture, and their functional characterization”. Seems contradictory to me, the genes important in one species might be important in another.

Conclusions.
These two conclusions could be together “including more species in the study of resilience and plant architecture will provide more holistic understanding” “by performing discovery-based studies across various environmental conditions and wider variety of species, will provide better understanding of plant development, as well as improved selection of breeding targets for improved resilience”

Another conclusion could be: Using high-throughput phenotyping with genome approaches.

I suggest making a Table with the comparisons of the most important data on breeding programs and genetic engineering, that has been done in root, shoot and leaves.
paper_title_zh: 利用植物构型的可塑性提高抗逆性
paper_abstract_zh: 植物构型在胚胎后发育过程中形成，源于发育信号与环境线索的相互作用。自植物育种初期以来，营养组织和生殖组织的长度及分支一直是提高植物性能的重点。随着我们需要在日益严峻的环境条件下优先考虑植物生产力，当前的育种重点正在发生变化。尽管人们普遍认识到植物构型会随环境变化而改变，但其对变化气候下植物生产力的贡献仍有待全面探索。本文将总结先前关于植物构型性状的遗传控制及其在环境压力下对植物性能影响的发现。我们回顾了表型分析的新工具，这些工具将指导未来发现有助于植物构型、其可塑性及其对压力适应性的基因。随后，我们提供了一个视角，探讨如何通过整合新物种研究、现代表型分析技术和建模，发现植物构型可塑性和压力适应性的新遗传靶点。总体而言，本文为植物构型可塑性及其在环境压力下提高性能的潜力提供了新视角。
review_content_zh:
**审稿意见内容翻译：**

Maryam Rahmati Ishka和Magdalena Julkowska撰写的稿件《利用植物构型的可塑性提高抗逆性》在各个部分都包含了重要且准确的信息。这是一篇有趣的综述，对植物发育研究社区将非常有用。

**一些评论：**以下加粗的短语是作者所写，我在短语下方附上了对这些短语的一些评论。

**根构型：**
  * “选择性育种或基因工程已被用于改变植物构型，创造出不易倒伏的矮化作物品种，从而对产量增加做出了显著贡献”
  * 提供更多使用选择性育种或基因工程的例子可能会很有趣，因为这似乎是这类研究的唯一目标。
  * “而最终的植物构型取决于腋生分支的激活或休眠，这受内部和外部信号的调控”
  * 同样，主根和茎尖分生组织也依赖于内部和外部信号，你在后文提到了这一点，但我建议你在这里加上这段话：“初生和次生生长都对内部信号和外部刺激有响应”。
  * “植物构型发生永久性改变所需的绝对时间将取决于特定的环境因素，以及发育、遗传和生理背景”
  * 这是一条非常相关的信息，请提供参考文献。了解这一时间长度是如何在机制上确定的将非常有趣。
  * “当前的育种策略利用了最具遗传力的性状，基因型与环境之间的交互作用较低，从而在不同环境条件下都能保证植物的可靠表现”
  * 这句话似乎自相矛盾，育种策略的目的是在特定环境中发挥作用，而不是在不同环境条件下。请对此进行评论。
  * “侧根可以发育成长的非确定性根，有助于土壤探索，或者更短更细的根，这些根直接有助于水分和养分的吸收”
  * 许多侧根在均一的生长条件下表现出截然不同的发育，这一现象被称为发育不稳定性（Muller等人，2019年）。请对此进行评论。
  * **图1。**还有更多参与根深度的基因：XAL1参考文献[4]，XAL2参考文献[3]，以及ANR1参考文献[1]，参考文献[2]。
  * “在养分缺乏、干旱和盐胁迫下，独脚金内酯促进主根生长的伸长”
  * 我不完全理解这句话。
  * 我认为总体上谈谈植物激素在发育控制中的参与是很重要的。
  * “当根穿过土壤中的大空气间隙时（旱生根分支）。值得注意的是，这两个过程似乎都依赖于ABA信号通路”
  * 第二个过程还依赖于乙烯和生长素（Bennett M）。
  * “单一胁迫的组合通常会导致与单一胁迫不同的根构型”
  * 在受控条件下使用多种胁迫？这对我来说像是一个可以纳入结论部分的建议。
**茎构型**
  * “通过一个随机过程，第一个原基在茎尖分生组织内的随机位置发育”
  * 在建模中考虑随机性将很重要，请对此进行评论。
  * “以及开花前的叶片数量受环境影响很大”
  * 开花后呢？
  * “然而，一个物种内的遗传信息并不能全面代表在整个植物界中对植物生产力和环境抗逆性有贡献的机制”在同一段落中“这可以通过对先前鉴定为参与调控植物构型的基因进行比较基因组和系统发育分析，以及它们的功能表征来实现”。这对我来说似乎自相矛盾，一个物种中重要的基因在另一个物种中可能也很重要。

**结论。**
这两条结论可以合并：“在抗逆性和植物构型研究中包括更多物种将提供更全面的理解”“通过在各种环境条件和更广泛的物种中进行基于发现的研究，将更好地理解植物发育，以及改进育种目标的选择以提高抗逆性”。

另一个结论可以是：使用高通量表型分析与基因组方法。

我建议制作一个表格，比较在根、茎和叶中进行的育种项目和基因工程的最重要数据。

paper_title: A survey on sleep assessment methods
paper_abstract: Purpose. A literature review is presented that aims to summarize and compare current methods to evaluate sleep.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Anonymous) Comments for the Author The review is interesting, informative and coherent with the aims of the journal, but several major revisions are needed. Thank you very much for your constructive review. We really appreciate your work. All your suggestions have been considered in this new version. Major points - The main problem concerns the originality of the paper. Authors recently published a paper on the journal “Sleep Medicine” in which they reviewed the current methods to assess sleep based on questionnaires and diaries (cit. Ibanez V., Silva J., Cauli O. A survey on sleep questionnaires and diaries. Sleep Medicine, 2018; 42:90-96). Albeit the present paper is a more extensive and general survey on sleep assessment methods, I see an overlap with the “Sleep Medicine” review. Furthermore, such paper is not even cited. Clearly, a partial overlap is unavoidable, but I think that it should be reduced. The “Sleep Medicine” paper should be cited, and the originality of the dissertation on questionnaires and diaries should be improved. Moreover, Table 2, 3 and 4 contain information that are largely reported in the (very similar) tables in Ibanez et al., 2018, so they should be eliminated or strongly differentiated by the old ones (e.g. improving their informative value). Solved. First, the paper of “Sleep Medicine” was not cited because it was published after we submitted this paper (it was published on February 2018 Volume 42, Pages 90–96). Of course, we have now cited it. As you say, a partial overlap with that paper is unavoidable. However, the focus is different. The Sleep Medicine paper is entirely devoted to present the questionnaires from an historical perspective, and it deeply explains the validation studies performed over them. In contrast, the current paper presents the questionnaires as a sleep detection method. However, even in the less than one text page used for the questionnaires, the present paper fills a gap in the sleep medicine paper: It describes the contexts in which each questionnaire should be used (again, as a sleep detection method). This is summarized in Table 3. In the new version of the paper, following your advice, we have included new information in table 2 to add new value with respect to the Sleep Medicine paper. In particular, we have revised all questions of all questionnaires and marked them as “objective” or “subjective”. With this information we can label each questionnaire with the percentage of objective questions, providing an idea of the kind of information collected (objective/subjective) at a glance. In addition, this table now indicates the period of time evaluated by each questionnaire (this was also missing in the Sleep Medicine paper). Finally, we have corrected a typo in the structure of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) questionnaire (this typo appeared in the Sleep Medicine paper), and we have added the Mini Sleep Questionnaire (MSQ) to the table. All this information makes it different and a good complement to the Sleep Medicine paper. - I suggest a complete revision of the English across the text (it is often wrong, unclear or repetitive). It has been proofread by a native English speaker (Roger Nolan from Irland). We hope that the problems have been solved. If you still find errors, please, indicate them. We will correct all of them (and we will be very grateful for helping us to improve our work, and to learn from our errors). Abstract - The “results” section of the abstract actually does not report results, but methods. Yes. It has been rewritten. Medical Assistance methods - for each described method a) the principal studies should be cited (at present, I see references only for PSG, and they are not exhaustive); Done. All described methods include now the proper cites. b) the main sleep disorders/problems that can be assessed should be reported. Done. For each method, we have specified the main disorders it addresses, or the common usage, as in the case of MWT. - Lines 272-273: describe what sensors are used and how the device detects sleep stages. Done. The standard equipment used and its utility is now described. Hardware devices: - For both contactless and contact devices, a table reporting the devices specifics (the name of the devices, ranking/review, variables measured by the devices) could be useful. Done. We have added this table for the sleep apps, and we have included five more apps (there were five and now the table contains the top ten apps according to Google Play). This table is more informative because it also contains market prices and the developer company. In contrast to hardware devices, the information about software apps is very stable. It is almost the same (we have just updated the number of reviews). With regards to hardware devices, we have decided to remove the market data because the whole ranking, including products, reviews, and prices has changed completely in only two months. This particular market is so aggressive that most devices have changed their price or their selling strategy. For instance, Fitbit Charge 2 is now sold with a Fitness Wristband, which changes the price, and also affects the reviews. Similarly, Bellabeat Leaf Urban is sold as a different product, and thus the reviews counter has been restarted. Therefore, these data are so volatile that it will be outdated, or worst, misleading very soon, so we have removed it. We do not want the paper to contain useless or misleading information, and we think that this information (up-to-date market reviews) can be better found in independent expert’s reports, rather than in a technical paper. Contact hardware devices: - Lines 406-407: It seems that Zeo Personal Sleep Manager is presented as an actigraph, while it detects simplified EEG measures. Solved. Zeo was not an example of actygraph, but an example of “Contact hardware device”. However, it was confusing with its following sentence. Zeo has been removed and the next sentence has been rephrased. A critical discussion about accuracy and validation - lines 429-430: authors should cite the studies at the basis of their ranking Done. Figures - Fig. 2: the figure should be improved: a) it should be referred to a diagnostic classification system; b) for each disorder, authors should report at least one relevant study that use PSG for the assessment of that disorder. Moreover, the present figure is incomplete (e.g. insomnia is missing) and peculiar (medicalpsychiatric sleep disorders are reported as parasomnias?). Agreed. Done. We now use the last version of the International Classification of Sleep Disorders. The names of the disorders have changed to coincide exactly with those in the classification. The disorders in the figure are identified by two PSG reviews as those disorders that are frequently evaluated with a PSG. These papers were already cited in the text, but not associated to the figure. They are now properly cited to explain the figure. Minor points - line 205: the brief summary for each method is redundant, since the cited methods are described later. I suggest the removal of the summary and the integration of the information that it contains in the main description of the methods. Agreed. Done. The summary has been removed from the paper, and some of its information have been integrated in the sections that describe the methods. - line 305: “polysomnogram” should be abbreviated Right. Done. - Fig. 1: abbreviations should be reported in the figure legend Done. We want to thank again the editor and the reviewers for the thorough review and for their constructive comments, which has helped us to improve our work.
paper_title_zh: 睡眠评估方法综述
paper_abstract_zh: 目的。本文呈现了一篇文献综述，旨在总结和比较当前评估睡眠的方法。
review_content_zh:
审稿人2（匿名）对作者的评论

这篇评论有趣、信息丰富，并与期刊的目标一致，但需要进行几项重大修订。非常感谢您建设性的评审。我们非常感激您的工作。您的所有建议都已在这新版本中考虑。

主要问题：
- 主要问题涉及论文的原创性。作者最近在《睡眠医学》期刊上发表了一篇论文，其中回顾了基于问卷和日记评估睡眠的当前方法（引用：Ibanez V., Silva J., Cauli O. 睡眠问卷和日记的调查。睡眠医学，2018; 42:90-96）。尽管当前论文是对睡眠评估方法的更广泛和普遍的调查，但我认为它与《睡眠医学》的综述有重叠。此外，该论文甚至没有被引用。显然，部分重叠是不可避免的，但我认为应该减少。应引用《睡眠医学》论文，并提高关于问卷和日记的论文的原创性。此外，表2、3和4包含的信息在很大程度上已在Ibanez等人2018年的（非常相似的）表格中报告，因此应删除或与旧表格明显区分（例如，提高其信息价值）。

已解决：
首先，《睡眠医学》的论文没有被引用，是因为它在我们提交这篇论文之后才发表（发表于2018年2月第42卷，第90-96页）。当然，我们现在已经引用了它。如您所说，与那篇论文的部分重叠是不可避免的。然而，焦点不同。《睡眠医学》论文完全致力于从历史角度呈现问卷，并深入解释了对其进行的验证研究。相比之下，当前论文将问卷呈现为一种睡眠检测方法。然而，即使在用于问卷的不到一页文本中，当前论文填补了《睡眠医学》论文的空白：它描述了每种问卷应使用的情境（再次作为睡眠检测方法）。这在表3中进行了总结。在新版本的论文中，根据您的建议，我们在表2中添加了新信息，以增加相对于《睡眠医学》论文的新价值。特别是，我们修订了所有问卷的所有问题，并将它们标记为“客观”或“主观”。通过这些信息，我们可以用客观问题百分比来标记每个问卷，从而一目了然地提供所收集信息类型（客观/主观）的概念。此外，该表格现在还指出了每个问卷评估的时间段（这在《睡眠医学》论文中也是缺失的）。最后，我们更正了匹兹堡睡眠质量指数（PSQI）问卷结构中的一个错别字（该错别字出现在《睡眠医学》论文中），并在表格中添加了迷你睡眠问卷（MSQ）。 所有这些信息使其与众不同，并且是对睡眠医学论文的良好补充。- 我建议对全文的英文进行全面修订（它经常出错、不清晰或重复）。该文本已经由一位母语为英语的人士（来自爱尔兰的Roger Nolan）进行校对。我们希望问题已经得到解决。如果您仍然发现错误，请指出。我们将纠正所有错误（并且我们将非常感谢您帮助我们改进工作，并从错误中学习）。摘要 - 摘要中的“结果”部分实际上并未报告结果，而是方法。是的。已经重写。医疗辅助方法 - 对于每个描述的方法a）应引用主要研究（目前，我只看到PSG的参考文献，且不全面）；已完成。所有描述的方法现在都包含了适当的引用。b）应报告可以评估的主要睡眠障碍/问题。已完成。对于每种方法，我们都指出了其主要针对的障碍，或常见用途，如MWT的情况。- 第272-273行：描述使用的传感器以及设备如何检测睡眠阶段。已完成。现在描述了标准设备的使用及其效用。硬件设备：- 对于无接触和接触式设备，一个表格报告设备的详细信息（设备名称、排名/评论、设备测量的变量）可能会很有用。已完成。我们为睡眠应用添加了此表格，并包括了五个更多应用（之前有五个，现在表格包含了根据Google Play排名的前十个应用）。此表格更具信息性，因为它还包含市场价格和开发公司。与硬件设备相比，软件应用的信息非常稳定。几乎相同（我们只是更新了评论数量）。关于硬件设备，我们决定删除市场数据，因为整个排名，包括产品、评论和价格，仅在两个月内就完全改变了。这个特定市场如此激烈，以至于大多数设备都改变了价格或销售策略。例如，Fitbit Charge 2现在与健身手环一起销售，这改变了价格，也影响了评论。同样，Bellabeat Leaf Urban作为不同产品销售，因此评论计数器已重新开始。因此，这些数据如此不稳定，很快就会过时，或者更糟，误导性很强，所以我们将其删除。我们不希望论文包含无用或误导性的信息，并且我们认为这些信息（最新的市场评论）在独立专家报告中可以更好地找到，而不是在技术论文中。接触式硬件设备：- 第406-407行：似乎Zeo Personal Sleep Manager被呈现为活动记录仪，而它检测的是简化的EEG测量。已解决。Zeo不是活动记录仪的例子，而是“接触式硬件设备”的例子。然而，其后的句子造成了混淆。 Zeo已被移除，下一句已重新措辞。关于准确性和验证的批判性讨论——第429-430行：作者应引用其排名基础上的研究 已完成。图表——图2：该图应改进：a) 应参考诊断分类系统；b) 对于每种疾病，作者应报告至少一项使用PSG评估该疾病的相关研究。此外，当前图表不完整（例如缺少失眠）且特殊（医学精神病学睡眠障碍被报告为异睡症？）。同意。已完成。我们现在使用最新版的国际睡眠障碍分类。疾病的名称已更改为与分类中的名称完全一致。图中的疾病由两篇PSG综述确定为经常使用PSG评估的疾病。这些论文已在文本中引用，但未与图表关联。现在已正确引用以解释图表。次要问题——第205行：每种方法的简要概述是多余的，因为所引用的方法在后面有所描述。建议删除概述，并将其包含的信息整合到方法的主要描述中。同意。已完成。概述已从论文中删除，其中一些信息已整合到描述方法的章节中。——第305行：“多导睡眠图”应缩写 正确。已完成。——图1：缩写应在图例中报告 已完成。我们再次感谢编辑和审稿人的全面审查和建设性意见，这有助于我们改进工作。
