Response to Reviewer 64gv: Thank you very much for your thorough review and insightful feedback on our manuscript! We have carefully addressed each of your points and made necessary revisions, as outlined below: > (C1) Pointers to chapters in Causality. Thank you for your thoughtful feedback. In the updated manuscript, we have included more references to the Causality book and added pointers to the specific chapters being referenced." > (C2, 3) Improve the example and discussion on the distinction between RL and Causal RL. To better demonstrate the intersection of causality and RL, we have replaced the scurvy example with real-world applications more closely related to reinforcement learning (robot manipulation, medical treatment, and autonomous driving). We have included a new figure (figure 1 on page 2) and enhanced the discussion in Section 1 to better analyze the limitations inherent in traditional reinforcement learning (the second paragraph on page 2). > (C4) Remove the footnote of Markovian assumption. We have removed the footnote for clarity, retaining only the point that the Markovian assumption is prevalent in human discourse (the Causality book, Chapters 2.2 & 2.9.1). > (C6) Distributions $P(v_i | pa(v_i))$ are usually called Markov kernels. We have introduced the term causal Markov kernel [1] in the revised manuscript (the first paragraph on page 5). The term causal mechanism is reserved, as it is commonly used in some recent literature [2]. > (C7) Definition of submodels Thank you for your thoughtful suggestion! We have incorporated the relevant submodel descriptions into the Intervention section (page 5). > (C9，16，17) Different quantities that exist within Layer 3 and their identifiability In the revised manuscript, we have emphasized that there exist various types of counterfactual quantities within layer 3 (the second paragraph on page 6), and the AAP procedure is not always feasible in practice due to the lack of knowledge (the footnote on page 21). Furthermore, we have highlighted the identifiability challenges associated with counterfactual quantities in the last paragraph of Section 7.1 (page 27). > (C12) Isn't it also the case that Causal RL sometimes changes the objective of interest? We agree that RL sometimes changes the objective of interest, e.g., optimizing ETT-type quantity instead of the total effect. This aspect is explicitly emphasized in the revised manuscript for clarity (the third paragraph on page 8). The overall goal of causal RL remains consistent: enabling agents to make more informed and effective decisions. > (C13) Discussion on the difficulties of learning various elements of the causal structure would be desirable. Thank you for your suggestions regarding the identifiability issue. In the revised manuscript, we have added an introduction to the Causal Hierarchy Theorem (CHT) and cited the recommended reference to provide a clearer discussion of the difficulties of learning various elements of the causal structure (the last paragraph on page 8). > (C14) Discussion on Sontakke et al. (2021) The approach presented in this paper draws inspiration from the principle of independent causal mechanisms. This method induces experimental behavior aimed at facilitating the discovery of causal representations through clustering performance. Clustering, as a part of it, is not a causal approach. We have added a clearer description in the revised manuscript (the second paragraph on page 20). > (C15) The last column (Environments or Tasks) of the tables. This column is primarily intended to help the reader quickly navigate through common experimental environments or datasets in causal RL. We have categorized all the environments and datasets that appear in these tables in Appendix B, along with brief introductions, links, and references. For instance, a reader can quickly learn about MIMIC-III from Appendix B.4 Healthcare and directly access the associated codebase using the provided links (page 50). > (C18) Transportability worth mentioning Thanks for bringing up the topic of transportability! This is a very interesting but rarely studied topic in reinforcement learning, closely related to generalization ability. We have added a brief introduction to this topic and the related literature in the last paragraph of Section 3 (page 13). > (C19, 20) Highlight the idea of combining observational and experimental data In the revised manuscript, we have highlighted the importance of data fusion. In particular, we have summarized it as a notable trend that a number of causal RL methods have investigated, demonstrating promising initial results (the second paragraph on page 18).
paper_title_zh: 因果强化学习：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 强化学习是解决不确定性下序贯决策问题的重要范式。尽管近几十年来取得了许多显著成就，但在现实世界中应用强化学习方法仍然具有挑战性。主要障碍之一是强化学习代理缺乏对世界的基本理解，因此必须通过大量的试错交互从头开始学习。它们还可能面临为其决策提供解释和将所学知识泛化的挑战。然而，因果关系通过系统化地形式化知识并利用不变性实现有效知识转移，提供了显著优势。这导致了因果强化学习的出现，它是强化学习的一个子领域，旨在通过将因果关系融入学习过程来增强现有算法。在这篇综述中，我们对该领域的文献进行了全面回顾。我们首先介绍了因果关系和强化学习的基本概念，然后解释了因果关系如何帮助解决传统强化学习面临的关键挑战。我们对现有的因果强化学习方法进行了分类和系统评估，重点关注它们在提高样本效率、增强泛化能力、促进知识转移、减少虚假关联以及提升可解释性、公平性和安全性方面的能力。最后，我们概述了当前研究的局限性，并展望了这一快速演变领域的未来方向。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
总体而言，我饶有兴趣地阅读了关于因果强化学习的综述论文。在我看来，该论文很好地涵盖了该领域的各个方面。论文写作质量高，内容翔实，显然投入了大量的努力。

**优点与不足：**
我有几点建议可供考虑。其中一些是必须修正的错误，而且数量不少。为了提供背景，我对强化学习文献有一定了解，对因果性文献相当熟悉：*（C1）《为什么之书》（TBOW）在论文中被多次引用。这本身没问题，但我确实想指出，《因果性》一书在此处是权威参考。TBOW旨在为应用科学领域的读者提供较为非正式的论述。我认为指向《因果性》中相关章节的引用会比引用TBOW更有用。*（C2）第二段中的坏血病例子有些难以理解。从当前的表述来看，我的理解是“知道如何治疗一种疾病需要知道其病因”，这似乎是一个显而易见的陈述。我认为这一段可以改进，特别是突出各句如何与正式的因果模型相关联。*（C3）与（C2）相关，我也认为关于强化学习与因果强化学习区别的段落可以改进（第2页，第2段）。似乎CRL减少了探索中有趣的动作空间大小。然而，在我看来，当前的坏血病例子并未清晰地传达这一信息。*（C4）结构因果模型（SCM）段落的脚注：将马尔可夫假设视为因果推断中的共识是非常不寻常的。实际上并非如此，大量关于半马尔可夫模型以及存在潜在混杂因素时的推断文献可以佐证。这个脚注应完全删除。*（C5）乘积分解段落：V_i在给定pa(V_i)的情况下，并不独立于V \setminus {V_i, pa(V_i), ch(V_i)}。V_i可能存在非其子节点的后代，且条件于pa(V_i)并不能阻断到后代的路径。这句话不寻常，听起来像是对马尔可夫毯的描述，而这里并不相关。这部分手稿应予修订。*（C6）分布P(v_i | pa(v_i))通常称为马尔可夫核。因果机制通常指结构函数f_i。请仔细核对《因果性》一书。*（C7）干预段落：子模型的概念出现在反事实中。干预分布是通过子模型定义的。这一点应提前说明。*（C8）干预段落：常见表示为P(Y | do(X = x))，而不是P(Y | do(X) = x)。*（C9）反事实推理的描述相当简略（这可能是因为篇幅考虑）。 然而，在某些地方，作者需要强调反事实量的截然不同的性质。作者举了必要性概率（PN）的例子，而通常还会考虑许多其他更典型的类型。一个很好的例子是治疗对被治疗者的影响（ETT）。PN几乎无法识别，而ETT在无混杂假设下是可以的。*（C10）错别字：Bellman optimally equations -> Bellman optimality equations。*（C11）错别字：Rl methods -> RL methods。*（C12）因果RL的定义 -> 难道不是有时因果RL也会改变感兴趣的目标吗？我在这里想到了来自[2]的反事实随机化思想。也就是说，有时可能会优化ETT类型的量而不是总效应。*（C13）第9页，段落“我们注意到...”：这里再次提到了TBOW。更清晰地讨论学习因果结构各元素的困难是可取的。关于根据因果层级的第一、二、三层可以推断的各种量的讨论可以在[1]中找到。呼应这些讨论会非常有用。*（C14）第11页：“使用聚类结果作为因果表示” -> 在这里稍作扩展是可取的。从当前的写作来看，不清楚这究竟是一种因果方法还是仅仅是一种降维方法（有很多非因果的方法）。*（C15）表1：我不太清楚表的最后一列有多大用处，因为据我所知，文本中没有讨论。例如，MIMIC-III出现了。这是一个超级广泛的医院/ICU数据集，我不确定在当前的写作中指向这个数据集有多大用处。也许可以添加对表格的引用，或者调整内容。*（C16）第12页：溯因-行动-预测（AAP） -> 在整个文本中，反事实推理被作为一个单一的整体使用。在因果层级的第三层中存在的不同量的数量是巨大的。对于其中一些量，只有在真实的底层SCM可用时才能进行AAP。这样的要求非常强，因为SCM噪声参数化不是唯一的，且无法从任何数据中推断出来（再次参见[1]）。这些考虑应该明确指出。*（C17）局限性部分没有讨论反事实的识别性问题。这是这种方法的主要局限性之一，应该明确指出。*（C18）关于普适性的部分：密切相关文献中一个有趣的部分是关于可迁移性[3]的。可迁移性是一种图形方法，它精确地编码了SCM的哪些机制在新环境中保持未受扰动，并提供了利用这些不变性的规则。我认为在这里绝对值得一提。 * (C19) 第19页，解决混杂偏倚：Valtorta和Shpitser的参考文献证明了do-calculus在从观测数据中推断第二层量上的完备性。后续论文[4]证明了从观测数据中推断第三层量的完备性。最后，最近的论文[5, 6]展示了从观测和实验数据的组合中推断第二层/第三层的完备性。后者的工作似乎密切相关，因为强化学习（RL）通常同时具有观测和实验数据。* (C20) 第21页，最后一段：这部分讨论了结合观测和实验数据。我认为这一主题可以作为独立的思想加以强调。它在因果推断文献中占据重要地位，也许在综述中也值得突出。* (C21) 解决选择偏倚（SB）：在利用图形模型解决选择偏倚方面已有大量工作[7]。我很惊讶这项工作没有被提及，因为这些工具在因果强化学习（Causal RL）设置中可能非常有用。* (C22) HER设置真的构成选择偏倚吗？所描述的改变奖励分布的现象听起来与因果文献中通常考虑的选择偏倚不同。* (C23) 第23页，最后一段：TBOW参考文献再次出现用于反事实推理。此外，Kusner和Zhang的参考文献被提及用于公平性，这是可以的。然而，自那以后出现了许多其他结果，有些直接与决策环境中的公平性相关。例如，在因果多臂老虎机[8]的背景下，或在结果控制[9]的背景下。最近的综述出现在[10]中。* (C24) 第24页，第一段，“通过反事实推理我们可以探讨公平性...”：这里隐藏了大量的复杂性，反事实推理这一术语的使用非常简略。最近对文献中出现的各种量进行组织的工作可以在[11, 图12]中找到。* (C25) 第6.4.1节：引号内的“反事实”一词需要修正。* (C26) 第6.4.1节：关于反事实解释的说明：这一名称也被用于许多根本不涉及因果的方法，例如在算法补救文献中。这可能值得指出/明确说明。* (C27) 第6.4.2节：再次，可能可以找到更近且更相关的关于公平性+RL的参考文献。* (C28) 第7.1节：我个人认为结构学习（推断因果图）在实践中极其困难。我在实践中多次使用结构学习，从未获得任何在实践中略有价值的结果。我怀疑是否值得讨论一些局限性。半马尔可夫模型的结构学习非常复杂。此外，在这种情况下，部分定向图[12]可以作为未来的方向进行讨论/提及。* (C29) 第7.5和7.6段是非常有趣的讨论。### 参考文献 [1] Bareinboim, Elias, 等。 "论Pearl的层级结构与因果推断的基础。" 概率与因果推断：Judea Pearl的著作. 2022. 507-556. [2] Bareinboim, Elias, Andrew Forney, 和 Judea Pearl. "带有未观测混杂因素的强盗问题：一种因果方法。" 神经信息处理系统进展 28 (2015). [3] Pearl, Judea, 和 Elias Bareinboim. "外部效度：从do-演算到跨人群的可迁移性。" 概率与因果推断：Judea Pearl的著作. 2022. 451-482. [4] Shpitser, Ilya, 和 Judea Pearl. "哪些反事实可以被测试。" arXiv预印本 arXiv:1206.5294 (2012). [5] Lee, Sanghack, Juan D. Correa, 和 Elias Bareinboim. "使用任意代理实验的一般可识别性。" 人工智能中的不确定性. PMLR, 2020. [6] Correa, Juan, Sanghack Lee, 和 Elias Bareinboim. "从任意代理实验中嵌套反事实识别。" 神经信息处理系统进展 34 (2021): 6856-6867. [7] Bareinboim, Elias, Jin Tian, 和 Judea Pearl. "在因果和统计推断中恢复选择偏差。" 概率与因果推断：Judea Pearl的著作. 2022. 433-450. [8] Huang, Wen, Lu Zhang, 和 Xintao Wu. "为因果强盗问题实现反事实公平性。" AAAI人工智能会议论文集. 卷 36. 第 6 号. 2022. [9] Plecko, Drago, 和 Elias Bareinboim. "因果公平性：结果控制。" arXiv预印本 arXiv:2306.05066 (2023). [10] Carey, Alycia N., 和 Xintao Wu. "因果公平性领域指南：来自社会科学与形式科学的视角。" 大数据前沿 5 (2022): 892837. [11] Plecko, Drago, 和 Elias Bareinboim. "因果公平性分析。" arXiv预印本 arXiv:2207.11385 (2022). [12] Perkovic, Emilija. "在最大定向部分有向无环图中识别因果效应。" 人工智能不确定性会议. PMLR, 2020.

paper_title: Machine Learning for the Multi-Dimensional Bin Packing Problem: Literature Review and Empirical Evaluation
paper_abstract: The Bin Packing Problem (BPP) is a well-established combinatorial optimization (CO) problem. Since it has many applications in our daily life, e.g. logistics and resource allocation, people are seeking efficient bin packing algorithms. On the other hand, researchers have been making constant advances in machine learning (ML), which is famous for its efficiency. In this article, we first formulate BPP, introducing its variants and practical constraints. Then, a comprehensive survey on ML for multi-dimensional BPP is provided. We further collect some public benchmarks of 3D BPP, and evaluate some online methods on the Cutting Stock Dataset. Finally, we share our perspective on challenges and future directions in BPP. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic review of ML-related methods for BPP.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper is a survey on 3D bin packing using ML methods. The paper does a systematic review of both classical and modern ML-based methods for 3D bin packing. The paper also introduces 4 types of benchmark datasets, and conducts experiments to compare recent ML-based 3D bin packing algorithms.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strength: - The topics covered seem to be comprehensive - The challenges and progress of the area have been discussed - The benchmark and experiments can be very useful for future study Weakness: - The experiments are weak and not very convincing - In general, I find the discussion of previous works is technical-heavy, and high-level ideas/results are less discussed

**Requested Changes:**
- The second paragraph, “we can never apply the exact method” — maybe “never” is too strong? Couldn’t there be “easier” problem instances that may be solved exactly? For instance, there are integer programming solvers (which may be used for BPP), and good solvers can solve moderately large instances. - “Eliiyi & ELIIYI” why the second one is in capital letters - I think that the definition of the problem is not explained well enough. The authors try to define the problem using the big equation (1) in Section 2. However, I think that it would be more clear if the author could first list the constraints in words and/or simple notations, and then relate that to the formulation in (1). This is because (1) contains nontrivial equations, such as (1f), which is not easy to understand without knowing what it try to formulate (and it is appreciated if the author could explain this in detail). As an analogue, think about TSP, people usually define TSP in words and/or simple notations, but they rarely just say the TSP is defined using some complicated integer linear program. - A concrete question to (1): what’s \Gamma? You said this is number of usable bins, but you also said the goal is to minimize the number of bins used (which you use \gamma) — this is contradicting. Also, it seems \Gamma is not quantified as a variable in (1), so does this mean \Gamma is part of the input? This is very confusing. - In the first paragraph of Section 2.2, you ref to Figure 1 for online vs offline settings. However, Figure 1 is actually about a typical pipeline of ML method. - At the bottom of page 4, the notion of “performance ratio” is introduced. However, this is inside the subsection “Problem Variants”, but it seems this notion is already important/fundamental to the base problem. It is thus suggested to move this to the beginning of the entire section (or some other place that makes more sense). - The paragraph of “Placing Candidates” in page 5 — I have difficulty understanding the logic. You mentioned Martello et al. (2000) defined the notion of “corner point”, Crainic et al. (2008) defined “extreme point”, and Goncalves & Resende 2013 defined EMS. But what’s all these three notions about? How are they related to the “placing candidate”, especially why these notions are useful for the algorithm (e.g., used in which step)? I don’t find this clearly explained, and that’s why I’m confused. - I have a general comment about Section 2.2. This section is called “Problem Variants”, but the contents are not only about the “problems”, and they are also about “how to solve” the problems. It’s suggested to better separate the discussion to make the logic clear. - You mentioned a benchmark called “PackIt”. This actually has a virtual environment. Could you please elaborate on how this virtual environment helps in benchmarking the algorithms? - In the experiments, why DPPDRL does not generate a result for the “without stability” case? - In the experiments, how to interpret the running time? It looks very small to me, so I consider this very efficient. However, is it possible to use more time to generate better solutions? - I understand that the experiments only focus on online algorithms. However, there seems to be a lot of such algorithms available. It might make sense to add more as baselines. - It would be great to add the MIP (or some other accurate offline algorithm) as a baseline in the experiment since it gives the offline optimal solution, so that it is easier to justify the performance of online algorithms. Moreover, it also offers a baseline for the running time.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
None.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes
paper_title_zh: 机器学习在多维装箱问题中的应用：文献综述与实证评估
paper_abstract_zh: 装箱问题（Bin Packing Problem, BPP）是一个经典的组合优化（Combinatorial Optimization, CO）问题。由于它在我们的日常生活中有许多应用，例如物流和资源分配，人们一直在寻找高效的装箱算法。另一方面，研究人员在以高效著称的机器学习（Machine Learning, ML）领域不断取得进展。在本文中，我们首先对BPP进行公式化描述，介绍其变体和实际约束。然后，提供了一份关于多维BPP的ML方法的全面综述。我们进一步收集了一些3D BPP的公开基准数据，并在切割库存数据集上评估了一些在线方法。最后，我们分享了关于BPP中的挑战和未来方向的看法。据我们所知，这是第一份关于BPP的ML相关方法的系统性综述。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文是对使用机器学习方法进行3D装箱问题的综述。文章系统地回顾了经典和现代基于ML的3D装箱方法。文章还介绍了4种基准数据集，并进行了实验，比较了最近的基于ML的3D装箱算法。

**优点和缺点：**
优点：
- 涵盖的主题似乎很全面
- 讨论了该领域的挑战和进展
- 基准和实验对未来研究非常有用

缺点：
- 实验薄弱，不够有说服力
- 总的来说，我发现对先前工作的讨论技术性过强，而高级思想和结果讨论较少

**请求的修改：**
- 第二段，“我们永远不能应用精确方法”——“永远”可能太绝对了？难道没有“更容易”的问题实例可以用精确方法解决吗？例如，有整数规划求解器（可用于BPP），好的求解器可以解决中等规模的问题。
- “Eliiyi & ELIIYI”为什么第二个是大写字母
- 我认为问题的定义不够清晰。作者试图在第二节中使用大方程（1）来定义问题。然而，我认为如果作者能首先用文字和/或简单符号列出约束条件，然后再将其与（1）中的公式联系起来，会更清晰。这是因为（1）包含非平凡的方程，如（1f），如果不了解其试图表述的内容，则不易理解（如果作者能详细解释这一点将不胜感激）。类比一下，想想TSP，人们通常用文字和/或简单符号定义TSP，但很少仅说TSP是用某种复杂的整数线性规划定义的。
- 对（1）的一个具体问题：什么是\(\Gamma\)？你说这是可用箱子的数量，但你又说目标是最小化使用的箱子数量（你用\(\gamma\)表示）——这是矛盾的。此外，\(\Gamma\)似乎在（1）中没有作为变量量化，这是否意味着\(\Gamma\)是输入的一部分？这非常令人困惑。
- 在第2.2节的第1段中，你引用图1来说明在线与离线设置。然而，图1实际上是关于典型ML方法的流程。
- 在第4页底部，引入了“性能比”的概念。然而，这位于“问题变体”小节中，但这个概念似乎对基本问题已经很重要/基础。因此，建议将其移至整个部分的开始（或其他更合理的位置）。
- 第5页的“放置候选”段落——我难以理解其逻辑。你提到Martello等人（2000年）定义了“角点”的概念，Crainic等人（2008年）定义了“极点”，Goncalves & Resende（2013年）定义了EMS。但这三个概念是什么？它们与“放置候选”有何关系，特别是为什么这些概念对算法有用（例如，用于哪个步骤）？我没有找到清晰的解释，因此感到困惑。
- 我对第2.2节有一个总体评论。这一节称为“问题变体”，但内容不仅涉及“问题”，还涉及“如何解决”问题。建议更好地分开讨论，以使逻辑清晰。
- 你提到了一个名为“PackIt”的基准。这实际上有一个虚拟环境。你能详细说明这个虚拟环境如何帮助基准测试算法吗？
- 在实验中，为什么DPPDRL在“无稳定性”情况下没有生成结果？
- 在实验中，如何解释运行时间？在我看来它很小，因此我认为这非常高效。然而，是否可能使用更多时间生成更好的解决方案？
- 我理解实验只关注在线算法。然而，似乎有很多这样的算法可用。也许添加更多作为基线是有意义的。
- 在实验中添加MIP（或某种其他精确离线算法）作为基线将是非常好的，因为它给出了离线最优解，从而更容易证明在线算法的性能。此外，它也为运行时间提供了基线。

**更广泛的影响问题：**
无。

**主张和证据：**
是

**受众：**
是

paper_title: Review of the nutritional composition, medicinal, phytochemical and pharmacological properties of Citrus reticulata Blanco (Rutaceae)
paper_abstract: Citrus reticulata Blanco is a moderately-sized fruit tree widely used as herbal medicine worldwide. The nutritional composition, medicinal uses, phytochemistry and pharmacological properties of C. reticulata were critically reviewed in the current study. The literature linked to C. reticulata properties was obtained from multiple internet sources including Elsevier, Google Scholar, SciFinder, Web of Science, Pubmed, BMC, Science Direct, and Scopus. Ethnopharmacological research identified antioxidants such as vitamin C, carotenoids and phenolic compounds, also a source of sugars, organic acids, amino acids, pectins, minerals and volatile organic compounds as components of C. reticulata . As a medicinal plant, C. reticulata is used for the treatment of dyspepsia, gastro-intestinal distension, cough with profuse phlegm, hiccup and vomiting. The crude extracts of C. reticulata fruits have depicted anti-inflammatory, anticholesterolemic, analgesic, antiasthmatic, antiscorbutic, antiseptic, antitussive, carminative, expectorant, stomachic. With more people becoming nutrition-conscious, there has been an increase in the demand for the use of citrus fruits and their by-products as traditional medicines for conventional healthcare in developing countries.
review_content:
Manuscript is relevant for indexing, but it needs major changes. Please see the comments below:

Abstract
  * Authors have not mentioned why this review is necessary. Is it because this species is important as medicine, food or any other things? Please write aims.
  * In the abstract, mention how many compounds were found until now. How many diseases are treated? What pharmacological studies are carried out?
  * What is the conclusion of your review, which is quite not clear in abstract?
Introduction
  * I suggest authors to start with importance of plant species as medicine and food. Then mention about Citrus reticulata which is used as food and medicine. Mention some figures about uses, production and trade. Then in separate section mention about varieties in brief (too much detail is not required). Introduction should be followed by aims of your study. I guess it will be wise to see some good review papers if you want to write up to the indexable standard.
  * Botanical description is not very necessary but if you want to keep, make it brief.
  * Justification of the study should be at the end of Introduction not as separate section.
Method
  * Literature review was from March 2020-June 2020. Rather than this, mention how many literatures were considered and mention the oldest and newest literature. Again, please see some review papers to write your text in indexable way.
Nutritional composition
  * Were these components from the same species or from same species but with different varieties? Need to mention this very clearly.
  * Table 1 is redundant.
Chemical constituents, oil and aroma
  * Not in detail and needs much more elaboration. From which plant parts were they extracted? Mention in detail. I know it is mentioned in Table 2 but it should be written in detail. Please categorize compounds into different groups so that it will be easy for readers to follow.
  * In the beginning mention how many compounds have been isolated so far.
  * Give chemical structures of all the compounds.
  * Antioxidant property is considered as property with no pharmacological relevance (Gafner, 2018). So, discuss according to this.
Pharmacological properties
  * In this section, only information about extracts and results are mentioned, which is not enough. It is also necessary to write about what methods were used. The doses, type of experimental animal/cell/bacteria, controls (positive/negative if any) are required. Please write results in detail but remember that it should be concise. Also make a table to show all these. Please follow some good review papers on specific plant species published elsewhere and to help improve your manuscript.
  * Conclusions should directly link to your findings. Write about its importance and future prospective. What are the study gaps and what more is needed?
Overall, this manuscript should undergo Major revision.
paper_title_zh: "柑橘属植物Citrus reticulata Blanco（芸香科）的营养成分、药用价值、植物化学及药理特性综述"
paper_abstract_zh: 柑橘属植物Citrus reticulata Blanco是一种中等大小的果树，在全球范围内被广泛用作草药。本研究对C. reticulata的营养成分、药用用途、植物化学和药理特性进行了批判性综述。与C. reticulata特性相关的文献资料来源于多个互联网资源，包括Elsevier、Google Scholar、SciFinder、Web of Science、Pubmed、BMC、Science Direct和Scopus。民族药理学研究识别出C. reticulata含有抗氧化剂如维生素C、类胡萝卜素和酚类化合物，同时也是糖类、有机酸、氨基酸、果胶、矿物质和挥发性有机化合物的来源。作为一种药用植物，C. reticulata用于治疗消化不良、胃肠胀气、痰多咳嗽、呃逆和呕吐。C. reticulata果实的粗提物显示出抗炎、降胆固醇、镇痛、抗哮喘、抗坏血病、防腐、镇咳、驱风、祛痰和健胃等作用。随着越来越多的人开始关注营养，发展中国家对柑橘类水果及其副产品作为传统药物用于常规医疗保健的需求不断增加。
review_content_zh:
手稿适合索引，但需要重大修改。请见以下评论：

摘要
  * 作者未提及为何需要进行此综述。是因为该物种在医药、食品或其他方面具有重要性吗？请写出研究目的。
  * 在摘要中，提及迄今为止已发现的化合物数量。治疗了多少种疾病？进行了哪些药理学研究？
  * 你综述的结论是什么，这在摘要中并不清晰？
引言
  * 我建议作者从植物物种作为医药和食品的重要性开始。然后提及作为食品和药物的柑橘（Citrus reticulata）。提供一些关于用途、生产和贸易的数据。然后在单独的部分简要提及品种（不需要过多细节）。引言后应接着说明研究目的。如果你想写到可索引的标准，看看一些好的综述文章会是个明智的选择。
  * 植物学描述并非非常必要，但如果想保留，请简短。
  * 研究的合理性应在引言末尾说明，而不是作为单独的部分。
方法
  * 文献综述的时间为2020年3月至2020年6月。与其这样，不如提及考虑了多少篇文献，并说明最老和最新的文献。再次建议参考一些综述文章，以便以可索引的方式撰写文本。

paper_title: A Survey of Recent Backdoor Attacks and Defenses in Large Language Models
paper_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), which bridge the gap between human language understanding and complex problem-solving, achieve state-of-the-art performance on several NLP tasks, particularly in few-shot and zero-shot settings. Despite the demonstrable efficacy of LLMs, due to constraints on computational resources, users have to engage with open-source language models or outsource the entire training process to third-party platforms. However, research has demonstrated that language models are susceptible to potential security vulnerabilities, particularly in backdoor attacks. Backdoor attacks are designed to introduce targeted vulnerabilities into language models by poisoning training samples or model weights, allowing attackers to manipulate model responses through malicious triggers. While existing surveys on backdoor attacks provide a comprehensive overview, they lack an in-depth examination of backdoor attacks specifically targeting LLMs. To bridge this gap and grasp the latest trends in the field, this paper presents a novel perspective on backdoor attacks for LLMs by focusing on fine-tuning methods. Specifically, we systematically classify backdoor attacks into three categories: full-parameter fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and no fine-tuning. Based on insights from a substantial review, we also discuss crucial issues for future research on backdoor attacks, such as further exploring attack algorithms that do not require fine-tuning, or developing more covert attack algorithms.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
The authors present a survey on backdoor attacks and defenses targeting LLMs. Their study focuses on fine-tuning methods and provides a systematic categorization of these approaches. Lastly, they identify current gaps and highlight opportunities for future research.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
**Strengths** * Extensive survey on an area of research that is currently missing similar surveys * Important aspects from the methodological approach used by different attacks, to the necessary evaluation benchmarks, to current defenses are all covered * Categorizations provided in the paper can help to position new works in this domain. This can, in turn, make it easier to identify contributions of novel papers in comparison to existing works. * Claims made in the introduction are all covered by sections in the paper. However, I expected a more extensive discussion of crucial issues of current works based on the abstract and introduction. * I believe that this survey will be helpful to the research community **Weaknesses** * The introduction is a bit unfocused. It starts with motivation and gives a brief introduction on the topic, but then the third paragraph feels like a shortened related work section, and it was not clear to me why specific works were highlighted. Maybe the third paragraph could be considerably shortened and only provide a brief categorization of methods? Would improve the flow to the "limitations" that are discussed in the subsequent paragraph. * Current research aims to improve the robustness of neural networks against tampering through fine-tuning (e.g., [1]). As far as I can see this form of defense is currently missing in the paper but is arguably relevant in the current open-source research landscape. [1] Tamirisa et al., "Tamper-resistant safeguards for open-weight llms", 2024

**Requested Changes:**
* Could the authors provide some arguments for the structure in the introduction or trim down the third paragraph? * "Additionally, we believe that future research should focus more on developing backdoor attack algorithms that without fine-tuning, which could help ensure the safe deployment of LLMs." --> Fix this sentence * The phrase "We hope our review [...]" might be a bit to informal and could be replaced with a clear statement of the paper's objectives * In 2.1, maybe highlight the difference between pertaining and posttraining more explicitly (since it's mentioned). * 2.2 introduces some critical properties of backdoor attacks but as far as I could see they were not referred to in the remainder of the paper to further categorize attacks. If the purpose of introducing these elements is just to give some background, I would recommend to put less emphasize on them (i.e., not a bullet list that takes a lot of space)

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Response to Reviewer JrX1: **Question 4:** "Additionally, we believe that future research should focus more on developing backdoor attack algorithms that without fine-tuning, which could help ensure the safe deployment of LLMs." --> Fix this sentence **Response 4:** Thank you for your suggestions; we reorganize the aforementioned sentence: >Additionally, we believe that future research should focus more on developing backdoor attack algorithms that operate without fine-tuning, which could explore more mechanisms of backdoor attacks and provide new perspectives for ensuring the safe deployment of LLMs. *** **Question 5:** The phrase "We hope our review [...]" might be a bit to informal and could be replaced with a clear statement of the paper's objectives **Response 5:** Thank you for your suggestions. We restate the objective of this paper, with the revised version as follows: >Our review systematically examines backdoor attacks on LLMs, aiming to help researchers capture new trends and challenges in this field, explore security vulnerabilities in LLMs, and contribute to building a secure and reliable NLP community. Additionally, we believe that future research should focus more on developing backdoor attack algorithms that operate without fine-tuning, which could explore more mechanisms of backdoor attacks and provide new perspectives for ensuring the safe deployment of LLMs. Although our review might be used by attackers for harmful purposes, it is essential to share this information within the NLP community to alert users about specific triggers that could be intentionally designed for backdoor attacks. *** **Question 6:** In 2.1, maybe highlight the difference between pertaining and posttraining more explicitly (since it's mentioned). **Response 6:** Thank you for your comments. The motivation for Section 2.1 is to introduce the differences between LLMs and foundational language models. Therefore, we focus solely on knowledge related to LLMs. Thank you for your suggestions; we further elaborate on the differences between perturbation and post-training: >Benefiting from advanced training methods and high-quality training data, LLMs exhibit superior performance in handling downstream tasks through fine-tuning. Pre-training and fine-tuning are two critical phases in LLM development. During pre-training, LLMs acquire general language patterns from extensive of high-quality data, establishing a broad linguistic foundation. In the fine-tuning, the model is tailored to specific tasks using smaller, targeted datasets, which enhances task-specific performance. Notably, backdoor attacks frequently target the fine-tuning phase. *** **Question 7:** 2.2 introduces some critical properties of backdoor attacks but as far as I could see they were not referred to in the remainder of the paper to further categorize attacks. If the purpose of introducing these elements is just to give some background, I would recommend to put less emphasize on them (i.e., not a bullet list that takes a lot of space) **Response 7:** Thank you for your suggestions. We revise the introduction to background knowledge about backdoor attacks in Section 2.2, simplifying unnecessary character definitions: > We present the formal definition of backdoor attacks in text classification, while this definition can be extended to other tasks in natural language processing, such as question answering and knowledge reasoning. Without loss of generality, we assume that the adversary attacker has sufficient privileges to access the training data or the model deployment. Consider a standard training dataset $D_{train}$. The attacker splits the training dataset $D_{train}$ into two subsets, including a clean set $D_{train}^{clean}$ and a poisoned set $D_{train}^{poison}$. Therefore, the victim language model is trained on poisoned dataset $D_{train}^{*}$. *** **References:** [1] Cao, Bochuan, et al. "Defending against alignment-breaking attacks via robustly aligned llm." arXiv preprint arXiv:2309.14348 (2023). [2] Tamirisa, Rishub, et al. "Tamper-resistant safeguards for open-weight llms." arXiv preprint arXiv:2408.00761 (2024). [3] Liu, Sijia, et al. "Rethinking machine unlearning for large language models." arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.08787 (2024). [4] Huang, Tiansheng, Sihao Hu, and Ling Liu. "Vaccine: Perturbation-aware alignment for large language model." arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.01109 (2024). *** **In the end, we express our sincere gratitude for your detailed comments, which have been instrumental in improving our work. We greatly appreciate your insights and look forward to further discussions. If there are any additional questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to share them with us.** | Response to Reviewer JrX1: Dear Reviewer JrX1, **Thank you for your review!** We have endeavored to address all your questions and concerns below. Please let us know if there are any aspects that require further clarification. **If you feel that your concerns have been satisfactorily addressed, we would be grateful if you would consider revising your decision.** Please do not hesitate to reach out with any additional questions. We appreciate your input and encourage any further queries. *** **Question 1:** The introduction is a bit unfocused. It starts with motivation and gives a brief introduction on the topic, but then the third paragraph feels like a shortened related work section, and it was not clear to me why specific works were highlighted. Maybe the third paragraph could be considerably shortened and only provide a brief categorization of methods? Would improve the flow to the "limitations" that are discussed in the subsequent paragraph. **Response 1:** Thank you for your suggestions. We reorganize the third paragraph in the Introduction. This paragraph now solely contains the necessary classification of backdoor attacks and an introduction to backdoor attacks on LLMs, which we integrate into the second paragraph: >For backdoor attacks, an intuitive objective is to manipulate the model's response when a predefined trigger appears in the input samples. Attackers are required to optimize the effectiveness of their attacks while minimizing the impact on the overall performance of the model. Specifically, attackers embed malicious triggers into a subset of the training samples to induce the model to learn the association between the trigger and the target label. In model inference, when encountering the trigger, the model will consistently predict the target label, as shown in Figure 1. The activation of backdoor attacks is selective. When the input samples do not contain the trigger, the backdoor remains dormant, increasing the stealthiness of the attack and making it challenging for defense algorithms to detect. **Existing research on backdoor attack algorithms can be categorized based on the form of poisoning into data-poisoning and weight-poisoning, and additionally based on their method of modifying sample labels into poisoned-label and clean-label attacks. With the development of LLMs, a variety of backdoor attack algorithms targeting LLMs have been proposed, which include instruction poisoning and in-context learning poisoning. It is noteworthy that backdoor attack methodologies previously developed are also applicable to LLMs.** *** **Question 2:** Current research aims to improve the robustness of neural networks against tampering through fine-tuning (e.g., [1]). As far as I can see this form of defense is currently missing in the paper but is arguably relevant in the current open-source research landscape. **Response 2:** Thank you for your suggestions. Enhancing the tamper-resistant robustness of neural networks holds constructive implications for defending against backdoor attacks, therefore we include discussions of the following works in the manuscript: >Additionally, some studies attempt to construct safeguards in LLMs to enhance their security. Cao et al. [1] leverage a robust alignment checking function to defend against potential alignment-breaking attacks. This function does not require any fine-tuning of the LLM to identify adversarial queries, which potentially could defend against instruction-based backdoor attacks. Tamirisa et al. [2] design the TAR algorithm to defend against attacks, leveraging approaches from meta-learning. This algorithm can continuously safeguard the model even after thousands of steps of fine-tuning. Liu et al. [3] explore an effective assessment framework for LLM unlearning and its applications in model safeguards. Huang et al. [4] propose a perturbation-aware alignment algorithm to mitigate the security risks posed by harmful data. This algorithm adds crafted perturbations to invariant hidden embeddings, which enhances these embeddings' resistance to attacks. *** **Question 3:** Could the authors provide some arguments for the structure in the introduction or trim down the third paragraph? **Response 3:** Thank you for your valuable suggestions. We condense the third paragraph. It now contains only the essential classification of backdoor attacks and an introduction to backdoor attacks on LLMs, which we integrate into the second paragraph. For details, please refer to Response 1.
paper_title_zh: 大型语言模型中近期后门攻击与防御综述
paper_abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）弥合了人类语言理解与复杂问题解决之间的差距，在多项自然语言处理（NLP）任务中，尤其是在少样本和零样本设置下，取得了最先进的性能。尽管LLMs的效能已得到证明，但由于计算资源的限制，用户不得不使用开源语言模型或将整个训练过程外包给第三方平台。然而，研究表明，语言模型容易受到潜在安全漏洞的影响，尤其是在后门攻击中。后门攻击旨在通过毒化训练样本或模型权重，向语言模型引入针对性的漏洞，使攻击者能够通过恶意触发器操纵模型响应。尽管现有的后门攻击综述提供了全面的概述，但它们缺乏对专门针对LLMs的后门攻击的深入探讨。为了填补这一空白并把握该领域的最新趋势，本文通过聚焦微调方法，提出了针对LLMs后门攻击的新视角。具体而言，我们系统地将军门攻击分为三类：全参数微调、参数高效微调和无微调。基于大量综述的见解，我们还讨论了未来后门攻击研究的关键问题，例如进一步探索不需要微调的攻击算法，或开发更隐蔽的攻击算法。
review_content_zh:

作者对针对大型语言模型（LLMs）的后门攻击和防御进行了综述。他们的研究重点在于微调方法，并提供了这些方法的系统分类。最后，他们识别了当前的研究空白，并强调了未来研究的机遇。

**回复1：** 感谢您的建议。我们重新组织了引言中的第三段。 对于后门攻击，一个直观的目标是在输入样本中出现预定义触发器时操纵模型的响应。攻击者需要在优化攻击效果的同时，尽量减少对模型整体性能的影响。具体而言，攻击者将恶意触发器嵌入到一部分训练样本中，以诱导模型学习触发器与目标标签之间的关联。在模型推理过程中，当遇到触发器时，模型将一致地预测目标标签，如图1所示。后门攻击的激活是选择性的。当输入样本不包含触发器时，后门保持休眠状态，增加了攻击的隐蔽性，使得防御算法难以检测。**现有的后门攻击算法研究可以根据中毒形式分为数据中毒和权重中毒，此外还可以根据修改样本标签的方法分为中毒标签攻击和清洁标签攻击。随着大型语言模型（LLMs）的发展，针对LLMs的各种后门攻击算法已被提出，包括指令中毒和上下文学习中毒。值得注意的是，先前开发的后门攻击方法也适用于LLMs。** *** **问题2：** 当前研究旨在通过微调（例如，[1]）提高神经网络对篡改的鲁棒性。据我所见，这种形式的防御目前在论文中缺失，但在当前的开源研究环境中显然是相关的。**回复2：** 感谢您的建议。增强神经网络的抗篡改鲁棒性对于防御后门攻击具有建设性的意义，因此我们在手稿中包括以下工作的讨论：>此外，一些研究试图在LLMs中构建防护措施以增强其安全性。曹等人[1]利用一个鲁棒的校准检查函数来防御潜在的校准破坏攻击。该函数不需要对LLM进行任何微调即可识别对抗性查询，这可能防御基于指令的后门攻击。塔米里萨等人[2]设计了TAR算法来防御攻击，利用元学习的方法。该算法即使在经过数千步微调后也能持续保护模型。刘等人[3]探索了一个有效的LLM遗忘评估框架及其在模型防护中的应用。黄等人[4]提出了一种扰动感知的校准算法，以减轻有害数据带来的安全风险。 该算法向不变隐藏嵌入添加精心设计的扰动，从而增强了这些嵌入对攻击的抵抗能力。*** **问题3：** 作者能否为引言中的结构提供一些论据，或者缩减第三段？**回复3：** 感谢您的宝贵建议。我们缩减了第三段。现在它仅包含对后门攻击的基本分类以及对大语言模型（LLM）后门攻击的介绍，我们将这些内容整合到第二段中。详情请参阅回复1。

paper_title: State-of-the-art violence detection techniques in video surveillance security systems: A systematic review
paper_abstract: We investigate and analyze methods to violence detection in this study to completely disassemble the present condition and anticipate the emerging trends of violence discovery research. In this systematic review, we provide a comprehensive assessment of the video violence detection problems that have been described in state-of-the-art researches. This work aims to address the problems as state-of-the-art methods in video violence detection, datasets to develop and train real-time video violence detection frameworks, discuss and identify open issues in the given problem. In this study, we analyzed 80 research papers that have been selected from 154 research papers after identification, screening, and eligibility phases. As the research sources, we used five digital libraries and three high ranked computer vision conferences that were published between 2015 and 2021. We begin by briefly introducing core idea and problems of videobased violence detection; after that, we divided current techniques into three categories based on their methodologies: conventional methods, end-to-end deep learning-based methods, and machine learning-based methods. Finally, we present public datasets for testing video based violence detectionmethods' performance and compare their results. In addition, we summarize the open issues in violence detection in videoand evaluate its future tendencies.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Pedro Palos-Sanchez) Basic reporting This systematic review provide a comprehensive assessment of the video violence detection problems that have been described in state-of-the-art researches. This paper deals with an interesting topic especially in context of video violence. Therefore, it requires revisions to improve the quality of work. 1. The abstract should be ordered by answering questions such as Originality of the manuscript, Objectives, Method (indicate how many papers you located in the different stages of the SLR and how many you were finally left with) and Finding. By considering the reviewer’s recommendation we used different terms in Title and Keywords. Moreover, we changed the Abstract of the systematic analysis by considering observer’s recommendations. Experimental design 2. I suggest a new Table with SLR and bibliometric analysis have been used in ``several previous research papers''. A flowchart should be added to the article to show the research methodology. In this sense, I propose to update the methodology as this paper does: B. Kitchenham and S. Charters, "Guidelines for performing sandstematic literature reviews in software engineering version 2.3", Engineering, vol. 45, no. 5, pp. 1051, 2007. R., & Rus-Arias, E. (2020). Working in virtual teams: a systematic literature review and a bibliometric analysis. IEEE Access, 8, 168923-168940. Answer: The proposed correction by the reviewer has been introduced. 6. It is suggested to include a SLR protocol and question research. Answer: We inserted four research questions for further research of the SLR. In addition, we included SLR protocol as a supplementary material. 7. It is suggested to compare the results of the present research with some similar systematic literature review which is done before. paper_title_zh: 视频监控安全系统中最新暴力检测技术：系统综述
paper_abstract_zh: 在本研究中，我们调查并分析了暴力检测的方法，以全面剖析当前状况并预测暴力发现研究的未来趋势。在这篇系统综述中，我们对现有研究中描述的视频暴力检测问题进行了全面评估。这项工作的目的是解决视频暴力检测中的最新方法问题，开发并训练实时视频暴力检测框架的数据集，讨论并识别给定问题中的开放性问题。在本研究中，我们从154篇研究论文中经过识别、筛选和资格审核阶段后选取了80篇进行分析。作为研究来源，我们使用了五个数字图书馆和三个在2015年至2021年间发表的高排名计算机视觉会议。我们首先简要介绍了基于视频的暴力检测的核心思想和问题；随后，根据方法学将当前技术分为三类：传统方法、基于端到端深度学习的方法和基于机器学习的方法。最后，我们介绍了用于测试基于视频的暴力检测方法性能的公开数据集，并比较了其结果。此外，我们总结了视频暴力检测中的开放性问题，并评估了其未来趋势。
review_content_zh:

paper_title: Natural disaster and medication preparedness among elderly: a scoping review
paper_abstract:
Introduction 
 The increasing number of older people and their vulnerability to disaster and medication preparedness as the primary elements of disaster mitigation are necessary to reduce the impact of a disaster. Nevertheless, research on natural disasters and medication preparedness in the elderly population is still lacking. This review aimed to explore all reported research and publications related to natural disasters and medication preparedness among the elderly. 
 
 
 Methods 
 A scoping review was performed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A literature search was conducted using the following four databases: Scopus, PubMed, Sage, and Google Scholar. Screening was conducted using the following criteria: articles written in English, open access, and published between 2020 and 2024. Articles must discuss natural disasters and medication preparedness. In the data search, we input several keywords that include “elderly,” “natural disaster,” “preparedness,” and “medication.” Snowballing was then conducted to find articles on preparedness interventions. Data extraction and analysis were then performed. 
 
 
 Results and conclusion 
 The findings from this literature review are the majority of studies showing that most elderly people are not well prepared in facing disasters; however, through various programs that have been implemented by either the government or community, the elderly show more preparation when they encounter any natural disaster.
review_content:
The article “Natural disaster and medication preparedness among elderly: a scoping review” aims to explore disaster and medication preparedness among the elderly, including the prerequisites and the impediments to disaster preparedness as well as interventions to support their preparedness. This is highly relevant topic considering the growing disaster risk associated with climate change and the vulnerability of the studied population. The authors performed a literature review of original research articles on the topic. 20 eligible articles were identified and further analyzed. The main conclusion states that more efforts are needed to improve disaster preparedness of the older people. The elements needed for disaster preparedness are identified:
  * Medication preparedness
  * Mobility assistance
  * Communication support
  * Social support
  * Shelter and other facilities
  * Education and training programs
Factors affecting disaster preparedness are formulated:
  * Education
  * Disability
  * Income
  * Communication and information technology
  * Family
  * Access to health services
Interventions to improve preparedness are proposed:
  * Enhance disaster preparedness through food bar
  * Enhance disaster preparedness through education
  * Enhance disaster preparedness through assistive technology
In my opinion this study provides valuable viewpoint on disaster preparedness of the older people. The information that is provided could be useful for policymakers and should fuel further research.
My comments on the article are as follows:
  * There are two objectives provided for the study: “This review aimed to explore all reported research and publications related to natural disasters and medication preparedness among the elderly” and “This review aims to explore disaster and medication preparedness among the elderly, including what the elderly need to prepare in facing disaster, as well as the factors that inhibit them from fulfilling the preparedness and certain interventions to support them to be more prepared”. The title is designed according to the first one but the content better matches the second one.
  * More comprehensive explanation of the search strategy could be given. The keywords are listed in Table 1 of the Supplementary Materials but the exact strategy is not quite clear and reproducible. Also, there are synonyms and related terms that are not captured by the keywords.
  * Figure 2 from the Supplementary Materials could provide all numbers.
  * Database and search approach states that the review was conducted following (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. This guideline is meant to direct only the reporting not the conducting of a review.
  * In the chapter “Enhance disaster preparedness through assistive technology” there is no information that two of the presented tools are assessed for being useful for older people. The third one reports that additional assistance could be needed by the older people for proper use of the application. As it is stated in the current research: “Despite the widespread use of smartphone apps, social media, and other online communication by various institutions and organizations for rapid information dissemination, these channels remain inaccessible to many seniors, especially those lacking internet access or mobile devices.” Could be noted that more specific research is needed in this otherwise very promising field.
Minor comments:
  * Some of the citations in the text have no corresponding number according to the reference list.
  * In the paragraph: “Fathoni et al. (2020) through his research invented an application named “application Bromo alert.” The application has several features: weblogs that offer information about Mount Bromo, including its history and past eruption events; shelters that provide details about shelters, including building names, locations, and proximity to disaster-prone areas; healthcare facilities that contain information about healthcare facilities available in the area; vlogs that provide informative content, especially targeted towards foreign tourists; and CCTV, which allows the public to view live updates of current conditions, particularly the latest situation at Mount Bromo.20” the reference that is cited is not number 20 but 16.
  * Consider rephrasing the sentences to avoid reiteration: “To the best of our knowledge, this literature review is the first to examine disaster preparedness among the elderly preparedness towards disaster.”, “Two reviewers collaborated to develop an approach to search for and determine a suitable determination for the search.”, “The findings of this study need to be prepared to support disaster preparedness for the elderly (medication, mobility assistance, communication support, social support, shelter, education, and training).”.
In conclusion, the issue examined in this study is highly relevant and remains far from being resolved. I praise the authors for their efforts to enrich the scientific literature on the subject.
paper_title_zh: 自然灾害与老年人药物准备情况：一项范围综述
paper_abstract_zh:
引言
随着老年人口数量的增加及其在灾害和药物准备方面的脆弱性，作为灾害减缓的主要元素，减少灾害影响是必要的。然而，关于老年人口在自然灾害和药物准备方面的研究仍然不足。本综述旨在探讨所有已报道的与老年人在自然灾害和药物准备相关的研究和出版物。

方法
采用系统综述和元分析扩展范围综述的首选报告项目（PRISMA-ScR）进行范围综述。通过以下四个数据库进行文献检索：Scopus、PubMed、Sage和Google Scholar。筛选标准如下：英文撰写、开放获取、发表于2020年至2024年间的文章。文章必须讨论自然灾害和药物准备。在数据搜索中，我们输入了包括“老年人”、“自然灾害”、“准备”和“药物”在内的多个关键词。随后进行滚雪球法以查找关于准备干预的文章。然后进行数据提取和分析。

结果与结论
本次文献综述的发现是，大多数研究表明，大多数老年人在面对灾害时准备不足；然而，通过政府或社区实施的各种项目，老年人在遭遇任何自然灾害时表现出更多的准备。
review_content_zh:
### 翻译内容

**文章“自然灾害与老年人药物准备：范围综述”旨在探讨老年人中的灾害和药物准备情况，包括灾害准备的先决条件、障碍以及支持其准备工作的干预措施。考虑到与气候变化相关的灾害风险日益增加以及研究对象群体的脆弱性，这是一个高度相关的话题。作者对有关该主题的原创研究文章进行了文献综述，确定了20篇符合条件的研究文章并进行了进一步分析。主要结论指出，需要更多努力来提高老年人的灾害准备能力。灾害准备所需的要素包括：**
  * **药物准备**
  * **行动辅助**
  * **通信支持**
  * **社会支持**
  * **庇护所及其他设施**
  * **教育和培训项目**
**影响灾害准备的因素包括：**
  * **教育**
  * **残疾**
  * **收入**
  * **通信和信息技术**
  * **家庭**
  * **获取卫生服务**
**提出了提高准备工作的干预措施：**
  * **通过食品棒增强灾害准备**
  * **通过教育增强灾害准备**
  * **通过辅助技术增强灾害准备**
**在我看来，这项研究为老年人的灾害准备提供了宝贵的观点。所提供的信息对政策制定者可能有用，并应推动进一步研究。**

**我对文章的评论如下：**
  * **研究提供了两个目标：“本综述旨在探讨所有与自然灾害和老年人药物准备相关的研究和出版物”和“本综述旨在探讨老年人中的灾害和药物准备情况，包括老年人在面对灾害时需要准备的内容，以及阻碍他们完成准备工作的因素和某些支持他们更好准备的干预措施”。标题是根据第一个目标设计的，但内容更符合第二个目标。**
  * **可以更全面地解释搜索策略。关键词列在补充材料中的表1中，但具体策略并不十分清晰且不可复制。此外，还有一些同义词和相关术语未被关键词捕获。**
  * **补充材料中的图2可以提供所有数字。**
  * **数据库和搜索方法中提到，综述是按照（PRISMA-ScR）指南进行的。该指南旨在指导报告的撰写，而非综述的进行。**
  * **在“通过辅助技术增强灾害准备”章节中，没有信息表明所展示的两个工具被评估为对老年人有用。第三个工具报告称，老年人可能需要额外帮助才能正确使用该应用程序。正如当前研究所述：“尽管各种机构和组织广泛使用智能手机应用程序、社交媒体和其他在线通信手段进行快速信息传播，但这些渠道对许多老年人，尤其是那些缺乏互联网接入或移动设备的老年人来说，仍然不可及。”可以指出，在这一非常有前景的领域需要更具体的研究。**

**次要评论：**
  * **文本中的一些引用在参考文献列表中没有对应的编号。**

paper_title: The gap is still here: Access to physical and mental health care for children and adolescents 15 years after the Affordable Care Act
paper_abstract:
In 2009 a review of the state of child and adolescent physical and mental health care in the United States, appeared hopeful with the possibility of addressing the unmet health needs of our nation’s children in schools (Manning, 2009). Major legislation and sweeping strides for addressing the affordability of health care in the United States with The Affordable Care Act (ACA) which was codified into law and signed by President Obama, opening the possibility that the unmet physical and mental health needs of America’s youth may be reduced through the availability and affordability of health insurance for everyone (Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, 2010). 
 Over the past 15 years, the health and mental health of children and adolescents in the United States have undergone notable changes, reflecting both progress and persistent challenges. While public health initiatives and policy advancements have improved access to care and contributed to reductions in asthma prevalence and teen pregnancy rates, other areas continue to demonstrate systemic challenges. The rising incidence of obesity, Type 2 diabetes, depression, suicidality and ADHD highlight the ongoing need for comprehensive health interventions at the public health level. Additionally, disparities in healthcare access, particularly among rural and low-income populations, remain significant barriers to the overall well-being of children and youth. The shortage of primary care providers, gaps in insurance coverage and the increasing burden on school-based health clinics further complicate care accessibility. This paper examines the evolving trends in child and adolescent health, emphasizing the critical role of policy, environmental changes and healthcare innovations in shaping outcomes. 
 After almost 15 years of this call to action and implementation of the ACA we have made strides towards healthy outcomes for children and youth, evidencing that transformative, systemic change is not only possible, but necessary to ensure the well-being of future generations.
review_content:
Reviewer Comments
This is an important paper, and I enjoyed reading it. It is extremely well-written, and adds a great deal to the current knowledge base. I have specific comments below to improve this paper, but I highly recommend this paper for indexing after addressing the comments below, as this paper significantly adds to the literature.

Specific Comments:
 1. First sentence of abstract currently reads “In 2009 a review of the state of child and adolescent physical and mental health care in the United States, appeared hopeful with the possibility of addressing the unmet health needs of our nation’s children in schools (Manning, 2009).” Please add a comma after 2009, but remove the comma after the word ‘States’.
 2. The second sentence needs revision because it is not understandable as written.
 3. First sentence of Introduction states: “To attempt to address this formative question”, but as it is the first sentence of the paper, no question has been asked yet. Please clarify.
 4. It is unclear why the author chose the particular areas of concern (i.e., asthma, teen pregnancy, etc.) as opposed to other areas of concern. Please clarify as to why these particular areas were chosen for this article.
 5. This sentence: “through systemic changes including comprehensive sexual health education, access to health care through the ACA, and access to long term birth control options such as birth control implants and IUDs, the reduction in teen pregnancy rates have been highly impacted by policy, practice and shifts in social norms.” Please cite this.
 6. For every issue until ADHD: actual numbers are discussed and shown in terms of increase or decrease in the issue since the ACA. For ADHD, only current rates are shown, not what it used to be before ACA. Same issue for Violence.
 7. Impact on education: A few issues here: 1) Does not support the overall mission of the paper, which is to address health disparities since the advent of ACA. (I think? If this isn’t the mission of the paper, then this too needs to be made clearer.) 2) This section appears to only concentrate on pandemic and post pandemic issues, which is only 4.5 years old, not the 15 year mark that the paper is striving for. 3) Later in the paper, the author makes a compelling argument for school-based health clinics, and this would tie in neatly to the educational issues addressed in this section, if the author can connect these two.

General Strengths of the Paper:
 1. Relevance and Contribution: The study successfully highlights the importance of community engagement in health interventions, particularly within underserved populations.
 2. Clarity and Organization: The introduction and literature review sections provide a comprehensive background, clearly outlining the research objectives and situating the study within the broader field of public health.
 3. Policy Implications: The author provides some excellent ideas that are concrete ways to actually put forth public policy that would be helpful from a preventative perspective.


General Areas for Improvement:
 1. Grammar and Sentence Structure: This article needs some proof-reading. Several passages contain unclear phrasing or simple grammatical errors.
 2. Additional Literature Support: Some recent studies on digital health outreach and social media-based community engagement are missing from the literature review as well as the recommendations for prevention towards the end of the article. Including these sources would enhance the study's contemporary relevance.


Recommendation:
[ ] Accept as is
[X] Accept with minor revisions
[ ] Accept with major revisions
[ ] Reject
Final Comments: This article makes an important contribution to understanding the role of community engagement in public health, and is a good addition to the scientific knowledge base on this subject.
paper_title_zh: 《差距依然存在：儿童和青少年在《平价医疗法案》实施15年后的身心医疗服务获取》
paper_abstract_zh:
2009年，对美国儿童和青少年身心健康护理状况的回顾显得充满希望，有可能通过学校解决我国儿童未满足的健康需求（Manning，2009）。随着《平价医疗法案》（ACA）的重大立法和全面进展，该法案被编纂成法律并由奥巴马总统签署，开启了通过普及和负担得起的健康保险减少美国青少年未满足的身心健康需求的可能（患者保护与平价医疗法案，2010）。
在过去15年中，美国儿童和青少年的健康和心理健康经历了显著变化，反映了进步和持续的挑战。虽然公共卫生倡议和政策进步改善了护理的可及性，并有助于降低哮喘患病率和青少年怀孕率，但其他领域仍显示出系统性挑战。肥胖、2型糖尿病、抑郁症、自杀倾向和注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）的上升发病率凸显了在公共卫生层面进行综合健康干预的持续需求。此外，医疗保健可及性的不平等，尤其是在农村和低收入群体中，仍是儿童和青少年整体福祉的显著障碍。初级保健提供者的短缺、保险覆盖的缺口以及学校基础健康诊所日益增加的负担进一步加剧了护理可及性的复杂性。本文考察了儿童和青少年健康的演变趋势，强调政策、环境变化和医疗保健创新在塑造结果中的关键作用。
在近15年的行动号召和ACA实施之后，我们在儿童和青少年的健康结果方面取得了进展，证明变革性的、系统性变革不仅是可能的，而且是确保未来几代人福祉的必要条件。
review_content_zh:
审稿人意见

这是一篇重要的论文，我很享受阅读它。文章写得非常好，为当前的知识库增添了大量的内容。我在下方有具体的意见以改进这篇论文，但我强烈推荐在解决下方意见后对这篇论文进行索引，因为这篇论文显著地丰富了文献内容。

具体意见：
1. 摘要的第一句目前为：“In 2009 a review of the state of child and adolescent physical and mental health care in the United States, appeared hopeful with the possibility of addressing the unmet health needs of our nation’s children in schools (Manning, 2009).” 请在2009后添加逗号，但删除“States”后的逗号。
2. 第二句需要修改，因为目前的表述难以理解。
3. 引言的第一句为：“To attempt to address this formative question”，但作为论文的第一句，尚未提出任何问题。请澄清。
4. 不清楚作者为何选择特定的关注领域（即哮喘、青少年怀孕等）而非其他领域。请澄清为何选择这些特定领域作为本文的内容。
5. 这句话：“通过系统性变化，包括全面的性健康教育、通过ACA获得医疗保健以及获得长期避孕选项如避孕植入物和IUDs，青少年怀孕率的降低受到了政策、实践和社会规范变化的高度影响。”请引用相关文献。
6. 对于每个问题直到ADHD：实际数字被讨论并显示了自ACA以来问题的增减情况。而对于ADHD，只显示了当前比率，未显示ACA之前的状况。暴力问题也存在同样情况。
7. 对教育的影响：这里有几个问题：1）不支持论文的整体使命，即探讨自ACA实施以来的健康差距。（我认为？如果这不是论文的使命，那么这也需要更清晰。）2）这一部分似乎只关注大流行和后大流行问题，这只有4.5年的历史，而非论文所力求的15年。3）在论文后部分，作者为学校基础健康诊所提出了有力的论据，如果作者能将这两者联系起来，这将与这一部分所讨论的教育问题紧密相关。

论文的总体优点：
1. 相关性和贡献：研究成功突出了社区参与在健康干预中的重要性，特别是在服务不足的群体中。
2. 清晰性和组织性：引言和文献综述部分提供了全面的背景，清晰地概述了研究目标，并将研究定位在公共卫生的更广泛领域内。
3. 政策影响：作者提供了一些优秀的想法，这些是实际提出有助于预防视角的公共政策的具体方式。

总体改进领域：
1. 语法和句子结构：本文需要一些校对。几段文字包含不清晰的表述或简单的语法错误。
2. 额外的文献支持：文献综述以及文章末尾的预防建议中缺少一些关于数字健康外展和基于社交媒体的社区参与的最新研究。包括这些来源将增强研究的当代相关性。

推荐：
[ ] 直接接受
[X] 接受但需小修
[ ] 接受但需大修
[ ] 拒绝

最终意见：本文对理解社区参与在公共卫生中的作用做出了重要贡献，是这一主题科学知识库的良好补充。

paper_title: Incentives for pregnant mothers during antenatal care for better maternal and neonatal health outcomes in low and middle income countries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract:
Background 
 Universal access to maternal, newborn, and child healthcare is essential for achieving Sustainable Development Goal 3, but the effectiveness of various incentive-based programs for pregnant mothers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains uncertain. Objective of this systematic review was to determine if incentive-based interventions influenced maternal and neonatal health outcomes. 
 
 
 Methods 
 We conducted a search in various databases from inception. All incentive-based interventional studies conducted on pregnant women in LMICs were included. Evidence from the included trials was synthesized using risk ratios (RRs) to compare the outcomes between groups receiving incentives and not receiving incentives. The meta-analysis was conducted using random-effects model. We assessed the quality of the included studies using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and reviewed the collected data to determine its suitability for meta-analysis. This study is registered in PROSPERO (CRD42021247681). 
 
 
 Results 
 Of the 3,897 records that were identified, 11 met eligibility criteria, all of which exhibited varying degrees of risk of bias, ranging from high to some concerns. Analysis of maternal outcomes across studies revealed no significant differences in the likelihood of delivering at a healthcare facility (RR 1.13, 95% CI: 0.86 to 1.47) and in frequency of prenatal care (RR 0.99, 95% CI: 0.88 to 1.12) between intervention and control groups. However, high levels of statistical heterogeneity were observed for both outcomes indicating variability among study results. Similarly, analysis of tetanus vaccine coverage showed no significant difference between groups (RR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.92 to 1.08), with moderate statistical heterogeneity observed. 
 
 
 Conclusion 
 The maternal and neonatal outcomes examined in this review did not have any significant differences in intervention group when compared to the control group. The interventions to address maternal health concerns need to follow a multifactorial approach. There is a need for extensive primary research studies in the future.
review_content:
Thank you for the opportunity to review this interesting paper. It reports the findings of a systematic review that searched for papers evaluating the impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes of offering incentives to pregnant women in low and middle income countries.
Overall this paper is very well written and interesting to read. My suggestions for edits are mainly for overall clarification not specific issues, to set the scene for the reader before you go into your well written sections. This is often the case when you know you subject well, but a few small clarifications and scene setting sentences would improve what is interesting and relevant research.


Minor
Introduction
Please could you move the detail of the SDG (MMR less than 70 per 100000 live deaths) to earlier on in the first paragraph in the Introduction? At the moment the reader has to wait till the sentence about Liberia to find out what the detail is.
I think this section would benefit too from a sentence or two on the overall issue with LMICs – you start off with describing South Africa and Asia in the second sentence. Could you add a bit to the first sentence along the lines of ‘…..countries and regions, particularly between higher and LMICs’ – or something similar.
I was also confused by the last sentence in the first paragraph: ‘The model also forecasts that 13 countries would achieve the target between 2030 to 2050; while the remaining 13 countries are likely to succeed after 2050’. In the previous sentence you stated that the study looks at data from 31 countries, the 2 comments about 13 countries would suggest that the study you cite looks at 26 countries. Please could you clarify why the 2 amounts in your last sentence don’t add up to 31?

In the Introduction you focus on maternal and neonatal mortality rates. It is not immediately obvious to me why you have chosen these outcomes to discuss. Please consider adding a short explanation of why you chose these specific outcomes, you might say that they are key outcomes that are linked to other important maternal/neonatal outcomes, or that they are proxy’s for other outcomes? For example in the second paragraph of the ‘Rationale: Why is this important?’ section in the Introduction in the first sentence you introduce some relevant outcomes such as pregnancy and childbirth-related complications, maybe introduce some of these in the first paragraph of the Introduction?

The ‘What is already known’ section could benefit from a short introduction paragraph. At the moment it starts with smoking cessation incentives, it would be good to set the scene with saying something along the lines of how incentives could benefit this area (in terms of reducing smoking and improving engagement with antenatal care for example) and improve maternal and child outcomes. This would help orientate the reader to what to expect in this section before it starts with more specific details. The last paragraph closes this section really nicely, starting with something similar as suggested would benefit it.

In the research questions section please could you write out in full what ‘IFA’ and ‘Inj TT’ refer to in 1b?

Methods

The Methods section is clear and very well written, it included everything I would expect to see in a systematic review. I was unable to see the search strategy in the repository – only PRISMA checklists and flowchart. Please could you check that the strategy is included – I just many not be able to see it - this is why I answered 'partly' to the question - Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?

In Outcomes – please could you clarify your definition of preterm delivery – i.e. born alive before 37 weeks, also for perinatal and neonatal deaths, and maternal deaths.
Discussion

Fourth paragraph in the Discussion section – the last 2 sentences are very similar – could this be a duplication?

Would it be possible to highlight that previously there were a small number of studies and with small sample sizes – and this study has not found a large number of studies – but most studies were RCTs – so assumably suitably powered? It would be good to have that additional information.

I really liked your last paragraph in the Discussion section about poverty not being the sole barrier for pregnant women to access healthcare services. Would it be possible to add another sentence or two to this paragraph if there is more evidence available similar to the violence you discussed in the second sentence?

In the ‘Implications for research’ section please could you consider moving the 4th and 5th paragraphs (evidence limited to LMIC and limited study resources for searching for non-English records) to the ‘Strengths and limitations of the study’ section – they read more like strengths and limitations rather than implications.

Typos/grammar
I only found a few typos/grammatical errors and mainly in the Results section:
In ‘Neonatal outcomes – 2. Perinat and neonatal deaths’ – ‘the data has not been adequate to conduct any analysis’ would read better as ‘the data was not adequate to conduct any analysis’
You also mix present and past tense in the Discussion:
Second paragraph – ‘there is no separate data on the same’ should read ‘there was no separate data on the same’, and ‘there is no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives…’ should read ‘there was no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives……’
paper_title_zh: 低收入和中等收入国家产前护理期间对孕妇的激励措施以改善母婴健康结果：系统综述与荟萃分析
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
普遍获得孕产妇、新生儿和儿童保健是实现可持续发展目标3的关键，但在低收入和中等收入国家（LMICs）中，针对孕妇的各种基于激励的计划的有效性仍不确定。本系统综述的目的是确定基于激励的干预措施是否影响了孕产妇和新生儿健康结果。

方法
我们从数据库建立之初进行了检索。纳入了在LMICs中针对孕妇进行的所有基于激励的干预研究。通过风险比（RRs）综合纳入试验的证据，比较接受激励和不接受激励组之间的结果。使用随机效应模型进行荟萃分析。我们使用Cochrane偏倚风险2.0工具评估了纳入研究的质量，并审查了收集的数据以确定其是否适合荟萃分析。本研究已在PROSPERO注册（CRD42021247681）。

结果
在识别的3,897条记录中，有11条符合纳入标准，所有研究均表现出不同程度的偏倚风险，从高风险到有一定关注。跨研究的孕产妇结果分析显示，在医疗机构分娩的可能性（RR 1.13，95% CI: 0.86至1.47）和产前护理频率（RR 0.99，95% CI: 0.88至1.12）方面，干预组和对照组之间无显著差异。然而，这两个结果均观察到高度统计学异质性，表明研究结果之间存在变异性。同样，破伤风疫苗覆盖率的分析显示两组之间无显著差异（RR 1.00，95% CI: 0.92至1.08），观察到中等程度的统计学异质性。

结论
本综述中考察的孕产妇和新生儿结果在干预组与对照组之间无显著差异。解决孕产妇健康问题的干预措施需要遵循多因素方法。未来需要大量原发性研究。
review_content_zh:
感谢有机会审阅这篇有趣的论文。该论文报告了一项系统综述的研究结果，该综述搜索了评估在低收入和中等收入国家向孕妇提供激励措施对母婴结局影响的论文。

总体而言，这篇论文写得非常好，读起来也很有趣。我的修改建议主要是为了整体上的澄清，而非具体问题，旨在为读者在你进入写得很好的部分之前设定背景。这通常在你对主题非常了解的情况下会发生，但一些小的澄清和背景设定句子会提升这项有趣且相关的研究。

次要问题
引言
你能否将可持续发展目标（每10万活产中孕产妇死亡率低于70）的细节提前到引言第一段的前面部分？目前读者需要等到关于利比里亚的句子才能了解具体细节。
我认为这一部分也可以从一两句话中受益，概述低收入和中等收入国家（LMICs）的整体问题——你在第二句开始描述南非和亚洲。你能否在第一句中添加一些内容，类似于“……国家和地区，特别是在高收入国家和低收入及中等收入国家之间”——或类似的内容。

paper_title: Pollen report: Quantitative review of pollen crude protein concentrations offered by bee pollinated flowers in agricultural and non-agricultural landscapes
paper_abstract: To ease nutritional stress on managed as well as native bee populations in agricultural habitats, agro-environmental protection schemes aim to provide alternative nutritional resources for bee populations during times of need. However, such efforts have so far focused on quantity (supply of flowering plants) and timing (flower-scarce periods) while ignoring the quality of the two main bee relevant flower-derived resources (pollen and nectar). As a first step to address this issue we have compiled a geographically explicit dataset focusing on pollen crude protein concentration, one measurement traditionally associated with pollen quality for bees. We attempt to provide a robust baseline for protein levels bees can collect in-(crop and weed species) and off-field (wild) in agricultural habitats around the globe. Using this dataset we identify crops which provide sub-optimal pollen resources in terms of crude protein concentration for bees and suggest potential plant genera that could serve as alternative resources for protein. This information could be used by scientists, regulators, bee keepers, NGOs and farmers to compare the pollen quality currently offered in alternative foraging habitats and identify opportunities to improve them. In the long run we hope that additional markers of pollen quality will be added to the database in order to get a more complete picture of flower resources offered to bees and foster a data-informed discussion about pollinator conservation in modern agricultural landscapes.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Anonymous) Basic reporting Overall the reporting is clear and professional. I only have suggestions on two minor corrections, and the inclusion of one extremely pertinent citation. Thank you for the overall positive evaluation. Comments: L63-65: This sentence as written is not 100% clear. Consider revising, “However, in all cases INCREASING the quantity of flowering plants, and LENGTHENING the timing of flower alone are likely…” changed L93: It would be worth citing the recent large study of pollen secondary metabolites – Palmer-Young et al. (2018) Chemistry of floral rewards: intra: and interspecific variability of nectar and pollen secondary metabolites across taxa. Ecological Monographs 89(1). E01335. Cited (thank you for pointing out this interesting paper). L232: “a” should be “and” done Experimental design Though the authors have decided to only report summary statistics, I still feel that treating each observation as independent is fundamentally flawed. I have detailed my reasoning, suggested a solution, and have detailed specific lines in the manuscript where there are issues. Further, the authors need to report the number of species represent in each genus (and report the methods they actually used for generating figure 2 - see comment below). Comments: L178-180: Though the authors have chosen to not use any statistical hypothesis testing, there is still an issue with treating multiple observations of the same plant species as independent. Is there evidence that within species variation (due to the factors described in the text) is higher than among species variation? There is no issue reporting multiple values for a single plant, but there is an issue treating each observation as independent as it clearly is not. Instead of treating each measurement from a species as an independent observation when calculating summary statistics, the authors should consider calculating the mean of each species first, then calculate the genus means based on each species level mean. This is a major issue if any given species differs from the true genus level mean and is overrepresented in the sample. In this case the genus level measurement will always be biased in the direction of the more sampled group. I have done some simple simulations (PDF of some code and figures attached) that demonstrate the issue here. First of all, we thank the reviewer for the time, afford and thought invested in this manuscript. We agree that phylogenetic relatedness can be a very important and often overlooked grouping variable and that it could influence the observed pollen quality patterns. However, “species” in general and in the context of this paper is a somewhat tricky concept. In the case of many crop-varieties breeding has likely substantially altered flower rewards either intentionally or as a byproduct of selection on other traits. This is becoming clear when looking at the protein concentration in Helianthus (13.4 -36.6% protein concentration) which spans almost the entire quality range (excluding the two high quality genera). Consequently, we would argue that variety is the relevant level of replication for crop plants in terms of flower resources quality. In order to be consistent and compare apples with apples we would have to resort to subspecies (an even more difficult concept than species in the case of wild & weed species. This leaves us in a tricky situation we would either sacrifice all most (likely relevant) information on crop genera by reducting it to one “species” or use subspecies as level of replication in all cases with is very unreliable in our opinion. In order to address the justified concerns raised by reviewer 2 we have chosen a pragmatic approach. We have calculated the mean genus pollen protein concentration based all observations as well as species/variety means (see Tab. S1). We found that the obtained results vary by less than 2% protein concentration and have consequently decided to keep the original Figure in the MS. We hope that Table S1 adequality addresses the remaining concerns of reviewer 2 as it includes both mean estimates of both analytical approaches as well as underlying sampling sizes. L187-188: The authors say here that they only used genera that had observations for at least 3 species, but this is pretty clearly still not the case in figure 2. For example, they have 5 observations for Echium, but these are only from two species and 3 observations for Lupinus but from only one species. If the authors are going to include the genera with less than three species represented they should not only report the number of observations for each genus, but also the number of species represented in each genus (at line 201, Table 1, and/or Figure 2). We have now corrected this sentence. It now states correctly that we used genera with more than 3 observations for the presented analysis (Fig. 2) and refer to Table S1 for the species/variety based analysis and for the number of species/varieties per genus.
paper_title_zh: 花粉报告：农业和非农业景观中蜜蜂授粉花朵提供的花粉粗蛋白浓度的定量综述
paper_abstract_zh: 为了缓解农业生境中人工饲养和本地蜜蜂种群的营养压力，农业环境保护计划旨在在蜜蜂需求时期为其提供替代性营养资源。然而，迄今为止此类努力主要集中在数量（开花植物供应）和时机（花朵稀缺期）上，而忽略了两种主要与蜜蜂相关的花源性资源（花粉和花蜜）的质量。作为解决这一问题的第一步，我们编制了一个地理明确的数据库，重点关注花粉粗蛋白浓度，这是传统上与蜜蜂花粉质量相关的一项测量指标。我们试图为蜜蜂在全球农业生境中田间（作物和杂草种类）和田间外（野生）可收集的蛋白水平提供一个稳健的基准。利用这一数据集，我们识别出在粗蛋白浓度方面为蜜蜂提供次优花粉资源的作物，并建议潜在的植物属作为蛋白质的替代资源。这些信息可供科学家、监管机构、养蜂人、非政府组织和农民使用，以比较目前替代觅食生境中提供的花粉质量，并识别改善这些生境的机会。从长远来看，我们希望数据库中能增加更多花粉质量指标，以便更全面地了解提供给蜜蜂的花朵资源，并促进基于数据的关于现代农业景观中传粉者保护的讨论。
review_content_zh: 审稿人2（匿名）基本报告总体而言，报告清晰且专业。我只对两处小修正和一处极为相关的引用提出建议。感谢总体积极的评价。评论：L63-65：这句话的表述并不完全清晰。考虑修改为，“然而，在所有情况下，增加开花植物的数量，以及延长花朵的开放时间本身可能……”已修改L93：引用最近关于花粉次生代谢物的大型研究将是有价值的——Palmer-Young等人（2018）花部报酬的化学：类群间和类群内花蜜和花粉次生代谢物的变异性。生态学专论89(1)。E01335。已引用（感谢指出这篇有趣的论文）。L232：“a”应改为“and”已修改实验设计尽管作者决定只报告汇总统计，我仍认为将每个观察视为独立的是根本错误的。我已详细说明了我的理由，提出了一个解决方案，并详细指出了手稿中存在问题的具体行数。此外，作者需要报告每个属中代表的物种数量（并报告他们实际用于生成图2的方法——见下评论）。评论：L178-180：尽管作者选择不使用任何统计假设检验，但将同一植物物种的多次观察视为独立的问题仍然存在。是否有证据表明物种内的变异（由于文中描述的因素）高于物种间的变异？报告单个植物的多个值没有问题，但将每个观察视为独立的是明显不合理的。在计算汇总统计时，作者应考虑先计算每个物种的平均值，然后基于每个物种水平的平均值计算属的平均值。如果某个物种与真实的属水平平均值不同且在样本中过度代表，这将是一个重大问题。在这种情况下，属水平的测量将总是偏向于样本较多的群体。我进行了一些简单的模拟（附上了一些代码和图表的PDF），展示了这里的问题。首先，我们感谢审稿人为这篇手稿投入的时间、精力和思考。我们同意，系统发育相关性可以是一个非常重要且常被忽视的分组变量，它可能影响观察到的花粉质量模式。然而，“物种”在一般情况和本文的背景下是一个有些棘手的概念。在许多作物品种的情况下，育种很可能极大地改变了花部报酬，无论是故意还是作为对其他性状选择副产物。这在观察向日葵的蛋白质浓度（13.4-36.6%蛋白质浓度）时变得清晰，其跨度几乎涵盖了整个质量范围（排除两个高质量属）。因此，我们认为品种是作物植物花部资源质量的相关复制水平。为了保持一致并比较同类事物，我们不得不诉诸亚种（在野生和杂草物种的情况下，这是一个比物种更难的概念）。这使我们处于一个棘手的境地，我们要么通过将其缩减为一个“物种”而牺牲几乎所有（可能相关的）作物属信息，要么在所有情况下使用亚种作为复制水平，这在我们的观点中非常不可靠。为了解决审稿人2提出的合理关切，我们选择了一个务实的方法。我们计算了基于所有观察的属花粉蛋白质浓度平均值以及物种/品种平均值（见Tab. S1）。我们发现获得的结果在蛋白质浓度上变化小于2%，因此决定保留手稿中的原始图。我们希望Tab. S1充分解决了审稿人2的剩余关切，因为它包括了两种分析方法的平均估计值以及相应的样本大小。L187-188：作者在这里说他们只使用了至少有3个物种观察的属，但图2中显然仍不是这种情况。例如，他们有5个关于Echium的观察，但仅来自两个物种，以及3个关于Lupinus的观察，但仅来自一个物种。如果作者要包括代表物种少于三个的属，他们不仅应报告每个属的观察数量，还应报告每个属中代表的物种数量（在行201、表1和/或图2中）。我们现在已更正这句话。它现在正确地说明我们使用了具有超过3个观察的属进行呈现的分析（图2），并参考Tab. S1进行基于物种/品种的分析以及每个属中物种/品种的数量。
