paper_title: The extent to which cancer patients trust in cancer-related online information: a systematic review
paper_abstract: Background. The use of the internet to satisfy information needs is widespread among cancer patients. Patients' decisions regarding whether to act upon the information they find strongly depend on the trustworthiness of the information and the medium. Patients who are younger, more highly educated and female are more likely to trust online information. The objectives of this systematic review were to examine the extent to which cancer patients trust in cancer-related online information, internet websites as a source of cancer-related information or the internet as a medium of cancer information.
review_content: Reviewer 1: Basic Reporting 1 This manuscript should be reviewed by a native English speaker to review multiple errors (grammar and tenses). The authors should also proof-read the manuscript to correct errors e.g. Line 39: “therefore, physicians and other health care providers have to should…”, Line 370: “…between females and males was quiet small” Thank you for your comment. We have asked American Journal Experts (https://www.aje.com/certificate; Certifi-cate Verification Key: D850-D9C9-6F1B-96E2-AFA8) to proofread and edit the manuscript to improve grammar. 2 The introduction supports the rationale for the study. However, in line 100, the authors state that credibility is only one trust component but do not elaborate on their stance (definition or description) on trust Thank you very much for this comment. We have added a definition of trust and credibility and explained the connection between the terms trust and credibility. Additionally, we now include a detailed description of the process that may lead to cancer patients trusting in online cancer information (the 3S-model), cancer information websites as a source of cancer information or the internet as the medium of cancer information. (Lines 101-110; lines 118-160) 3 The results are relevant to the hypothesis. The authors rightly point out that the available evidence does not support conclusions on the second part of their hypothesis Thank you for your comment. Experimental design 4 The research meets the standards for conducting systematic reviews. However, the authors’ method for rating the quality of studies is questionable. The RTI item bank used requires studies to clearly state their inclusion criteria. However, as stated in Line 267, four of the included studies did not provide details on their inclusion criteria. The authors should clarify what they hoped to achieve by using the RTI criteria to assess the studies. They should also provide reasoning for choosing some of the criteria and not others. Thank you very much for this comment. This comment encouraged us to perform extra research on ‘risk of bias’ assessments. We have added the following information: 1. the reasons for choosing the RTI item bank (lines 256-259); 2. an explanation for using only 7 of the 13 available criteria (Table S4); and 3. additional discussion of how the detected bias might influence the quality of the included studies and, therefore, our conclusions (Lines 491 -497). Additionally, we do not think that the RTI item bank requires studies to clearly state their inclusion criteria. In our opinion, not reporting the inclusion criteria is an indicator of poor reporting quality and not of poor study quality (line 493) (Margulis et al. 2014). We chose the RTI item bank because we thought that the instrument, despite its shortcomings (e.g., extensive tailoring), is more capable of illustrating the "risk of bias" of the included studies than its main competitor, the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) (which is endorsed by the Cochrane Collaboration). Our main problem with the NOS was the best-quality answer (which will be assigned a star) system. This system suggests to base the rating of the study quality only on the quality of the analysis and forget to rate the quality of the reporting of the study, which is encouraged by the Cochrane Collaboration, but not included in the NOS (Margulis et al. 2014). The RTI item bank response structure (mostly “Yes,” “No,” “Partially,” “Cannot determine,” and “Not applicable”) encourages the classification of the risk of bias for each item as follows: 1. low risk of bias; 2. high risk of bias; and 3. unclear risk of bias (possibly due to low quality of reporting). 5 In line 152 the authors state 'participants' trust' and later 'active trust', how do they distinguish between the two? Thank you very much for this comment. We used the term active trust because one of the seven included articles (Crutzen et al. 2014) used this term for the outcome that we were interested in. Active trust is defined as the confidence in acting on the information provided by a website (Cugelman et al. 2009). Cugelman et al. (2009) see active trust as the result of credibility evaluation. After conducting additional research on the concept of trust to respond to the reviewers' comments, we conclude that there is no conceptual difference between the concepts of active trust and trust. Therefore, we deleted the term active trust from the manuscript. 6 In line 156, the full text screening was divided into 'study characteristics' and 'report characteristics'. Yet, the authors do not specify which criteria falls into which group in the subsequent text. Thank you very much for your comment. We have revised the manuscript to show which criteria belong to which category (lines 226-238). As recommended by Liberati et al. (2009), we have specified study characteristics and report characteristics used as criteria for eligibility. 7 In line 135, the authors should define what PICOS stands for and their reasoning for choosing certain aspects of the acronym and not others Thank you very much for your suggestion. We planned to include studies of any study type in our review. None of the terms in our search strategy (Table S2) served to limit the amount of studies by excluding studies of a certain study design (Methley et al. 2014). Therefore, the ‘S’ (study design) from PICOS is obsolete, and we switched to the PICO criteria. Additionally, we added a definition of the PICO criteria and added explanations why we focused on certain aspects of the acronym and not others (lines 201-207). 8 There is some redundancy between the information in 'Eligibility criteria' (line 146) and 'data extraction and quality assessment (line 166). E.g. both line 154 and 179 states that two researchers reviewed the studies Thank you very much for this comment. The paragraph ‘Eligibility criteria’ contains the following information: (1) titles and abstract screening (performed by one researcher); and (2) full text screening (performed by two researchers independently). The paragraph ‘data extraction and quality assessment’ includes the following topics: (1) data extraction (performed by one researcher and cross-checked by another); (2) actions taken to seek additional information from the original researchers; and (3) the methodological quality assessment of the included papers (performed by two researchers independently). We do agree that particularly in these two paragraphs there is much reporting on who did what. However, we followed the PRISMA statement for reporting systematic reviews. The statement encourages you at different points to state if task were completed by one or multiple individuals and how disagreements were resolved: Item 9: Study selection; item 10: data collection process; Item 12: risk of bias in individual studies (Liberati et al. 2009). 9 In line 111, the sentence isn't clear and may be misconstrued Thank you for this comment. We have revised the sentence and provide additional information on how prior experience and familiarity may influence trust in online websites (lines 170-177). Validity of the findings 10 The hypothesis of this study is relevant given that it approaches the topic from a systematic review perspective. However, since the quality of the studies included in the review is somewhat questionable, it dilutes the value of conducting a systematic review. Thank you very much for your suggestion. As stated in our reply to one of your comment 4, we added a more detailed discussion of the risk of bias within the included studies and how it might influence the conclusions of our review. 11 The conclusion rightly stated that there is little evidence to answer the second question they sought to answer. However, going by Table 2, it appears the other conclusions may be overstated. Rather than attempting to make broad conclusions, the authors should be more subtle about the generalisability of their findings Thank you very much for sharing your opinion with us. We have revised the first part of our Conclusion section. Now, the focus of this paragraph is more on possible future research that is necessary to answer questions that cannot be answered by this review.
paper_title_zh: 癌症患者对癌症相关在线信息的信任程度：系统综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。癌症患者广泛使用互联网来满足信息需求。患者是否根据所找到的信息采取行动的决策在很大程度上取决于信息的可信度和媒介。年轻、教育程度较高和女性患者更有可能信任在线信息。本系统评价的目的是考察癌症患者对癌症相关在线信息的信任程度、将互联网网站作为癌症相关信息来源的信任程度，或对互联网作为癌症信息媒介的信任程度。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1：基本报告

1. 这篇手稿应由母语为英语的人士进行审阅，以纠正多处错误（语法和时态）。作者也应校对手稿以纠正错误，例如第39行：“因此，医生和其他医疗保健提供者必须应该……”，第370行：“……女性和男性之间的差异非常小”。

感谢您的评论。我们已经请美国期刊专家（https://www.aje.com/certificate；证书验证密钥：D850-D9C9-6F1B-96E2-AFA8）对手稿进行校对和编辑，以改进语法。

2. 引言部分支持了研究的合理性。然而，在第100行，作者指出可信度只是信任的一个组成部分，但没有详细阐述他们的立场（定义或描述）关于信任。

非常感谢这一评论。我们已经添加了信任和可信度的定义，并解释了信任和可信度之间的联系。此外，我们现在还包括了对可能导致癌症患者信任在线癌症信息（3S模型）、癌症信息网站作为癌症信息来源或互联网作为癌症信息媒介的详细描述。（第101-110行；第118-160行）

3. 结果与假设相关。作者正确指出，现有证据不支持对其假设第二部分的结论。

感谢您的评论。实验设计

4. 该研究符合进行系统综述的标准。然而，作者评估研究质量的方法值得商榷。所使用的RTI项目库要求研究明确说明其纳入标准。然而，如第267行所述，四项纳入研究未提供其纳入标准的详细信息。作者应澄清他们希望通过使用RTI标准来评估研究的目的。他们还应提供选择某些标准而不选择其他标准的原因。

非常感谢这一评论。这一评论促使我们进行了关于“偏倚风险”评估的额外研究。我们已经添加了以下信息：1. 选择RTI项目库的原因（第256-259行）；2. 解释仅使用13个可用标准中的7个（表S4）；3. 进一步讨论检测到的偏倚如何影响纳入研究的质量，从而影响我们的结论（第491-497行）。此外，我们认为RTI项目库并不要求研究明确说明其纳入标准。在我们看来，未报告纳入标准是报告质量差的表现，而不是研究质量差（第493行）（Margulis等人，2014年）。 我们选择了RTI条目库，因为我们认为尽管该工具存在一些缺点（例如，广泛的定制），但它比其主要竞争对手纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表（NOS）（由Cochrane协作网认可）更能说明所包含研究的“偏倚风险”。我们对NOS的主要问题是其最佳质量答案（将被分配一颗星）系统。该系统建议仅基于分析质量来评定研究质量，而忽略了评定研究报告质量的重要性，这是Cochrane协作网所鼓励的，但并未包含在NOS中（Margulis等人，2014年）。RTI条目库的响应结构（主要是“是”、“否”、“部分”、“无法确定”和“不适用”）鼓励对每个项目的偏倚风险进行如下分类：1. 低偏倚风险；2. 高偏倚风险；3. 不明确的偏倚风险（可能由于报告质量低）。在第152行中，作者提到“参与者的信任”和后来的“积极信任”，他们是如何区分这两者的？非常感谢您的评论。我们使用“积极信任”这一术语是因为我们所感兴趣的七篇包含文章之一（Crutzen等人，2014年）使用了这一术语。积极信任被定义为对网站提供信息采取行动的信心（Cugelman等人，2009年）。Cugelman等人（2009年）认为积极信任是信誉评估的结果。在进行额外的研究以回应审稿人的评论后，我们得出结论，积极信任和信任之间没有概念上的区别。因此，我们从手稿中删除了“积极信任”这一术语。在第156行中，全文筛选被分为“研究特征”和“报告特征”。然而，作者在后续文本中未具体说明哪些标准属于哪一组。非常感谢您的评论。我们已经修订了手稿，以显示哪些标准属于哪一类别（第226-238行）。按照Liberati等人（2009年）的建议，我们已具体说明了用作资格标准的研究特征和报告特征。在第135行中，作者应定义PICOS代表什么，以及他们选择该缩写中某些方面而非其他方面的理由。非常感谢您的建议。我们计划在我们的综述中包含任何类型的研究。我们搜索策略（表S2）中的任何术语均未用于通过排除某种研究设计的研究来限制研究数量（Methley等人，2014年）。因此，PICOS中的“S”（研究设计）是多余的，我们转而使用PICO标准。此外，我们添加了PICO标准的定义，并解释了为什么我们关注该缩写中的某些方面而非其他方面（第201-207行）。 8 “纳入标准”部分（第146行）和“数据提取和质量评估”部分（第166行）之间存在一些冗余信息。例如，第154行和第179行都提到两名研究人员审查了研究。非常感谢您的评论。 “纳入标准”段落包含以下信息：（1）标题和摘要筛选（由一名研究人员执行）；（2）全文筛选（由两名研究人员独立执行）。“数据提取和质量评估”段落包括以下主题：（1）数据提取（由一名研究人员执行，另一名研究人员进行交叉核对）；（2）采取的行动以从原始研究人员处寻求额外信息；（3）纳入论文的方法学质量评估（由两名研究人员独立执行）。我们确实同意，特别是在这两个段落中，有很多关于谁做了什么的报告。然而，我们遵循了PRISMA声明来报告系统评价。该声明鼓励你在不同点说明任务是由一个还是多个个体完成的，以及如何解决分歧：第9项：研究选择；第10项：数据收集过程；第12项：单个研究的偏倚风险（Liberati等人，2009年）。

9 第111行的句子不清楚，可能会被误解。感谢您的评论。我们已经修订了该句子，并提供了关于先前经验和熟悉度如何影响对在线网站信任的额外信息（第170-177行）。

10 本研究假设的相关性在于它从系统评价的角度探讨了该主题。然而，由于纳入评价的研究质量有些可疑，这削弱了进行系统评价的价值。非常感谢您的建议。正如我们在对您第4条评论的回复中所说，我们增加了一个关于纳入研究内部偏倚风险及其可能如何影响我们评价结论的更详细讨论。

11 结论正确地指出，几乎没有证据来回答他们试图回答的第二个问题。然而，根据表2，其他结论似乎可能被夸大了。作者不应试图做出广泛的结论，而应更谨慎地对待其发现的可推广性。非常感谢您与我们分享您的意见。我们已经修订了结论部分的第一部分。现在，这段落的重点更多地放在未来可能需要进行的研究上，这些研究对于回答本次评价无法回答的问题是必要的。

However, the authors’ method for rating the quality of studies is questionable.

However, as stated in Line 267, four of the included studies did not provide details on their inclusion criteria.

paper_title: Individuality, phenotypic differentiation, dormancy and ‘persistence’ in culturable bacterial systems: commonalities shared by environmental, laboratory, and clinical microbiology
paper_abstract: For bacteria, replication mainly involves growth by binary fission. However, in a very great many natural environments there are examples of phenotypically dormant, non-growing cells that do not replicate immediately and that are phenotypically ‘nonculturable’ on media that normally admit their growth. They thereby evade detection by conventional culture-based methods. Such dormant cells may also be observed in laboratory cultures and in clinical microbiology. They are usually more tolerant to stresses such as antibiotics, and in clinical microbiology they are typically referred to as ‘persisters’. Bacterial cultures necessarily share a great deal of relatedness, and inclusive fitness theory implies that there are conceptual evolutionary advantages in trading a variation in growth rate against its mean, equivalent to hedging one’s bets. There is much evidence that bacteria exploit this strategy widely. We here bring together data that show the commonality of these phenomena across environmental, laboratory and clinical microbiology. Considerable evidence, using methods similar to those common in environmental microbiology, now suggests that many supposedly non-communicable, chronic and inflammatory diseases are exacerbated (if not indeed largely caused) by the presence of dormant or persistent bacteria (the ability of whose components to cause inflammation is well known). This dormancy (and resuscitation therefrom) often reflects the extent of the availability of free iron. Together, these phenomena can provide a ready explanation for the continuing inflammation common to such chronic diseases and its correlation with iron dysregulation. This implies that measures designed to assess and to inhibit or remove such organisms (or their access to iron) might be of much therapeutic benefit.
review_content:
Kell, Potgieter and Pretorius present a stimulating and argumentative review ranging from the interrelationships between the culturablilty of bacteria and their viability and any links these descriptions may have to defined physiological states, through a discussion of environmental bacteria and ultimately focusing on the human-associated microbiota, particularly those found in blood (without associated symptoms of sepsis) and their proposed roles in disease. Two central themes are developed beyond those that have been discussed extensively elsewhere: 1) the proposal that failure to culture bacteria from many samples often reflects dormancy and 2) that such dormant bacteria interact with host iron regulation to contribute to or directly cause a panoply of chronic diseases largely labelled as non-communicable.

At a general level I support the provocative stance taken by the authors. With 861 cited references, at the very least they provide a valuable resource for anyone wishing to consider the potential microbial contribution to diseases traditionally considered free of this aetiological component. Of course Helicobacter infection stands as a monument to the stupidity of dismissing this possibility in the face of carefully assembled evidence. Indeed this reviewer, who many years ago, was presented with a case of duodenal ulcer in his final medical exams, would probably have experienced quite a different career had he claimed a role for infection in causing his patient’s pathology.

In considering the specific points presented I have multiple concerns, the most significant of which I will indulge in outlining below.

Semantics present a central problem in considering bacterial viability and physiology and I broadly support the approach taken here. The authors do try to define their terms but some problems remain. In particular I take issue with the very broad application of term “Persisters” which should be reserved for cells that survive (have the potential to replicate) after exposure to an antimicrobial stress to which kills most cells in an actively growing culture of the organism concerned. Conflation of this term with “Dormancy” implies on the one hand that the persisting cells must have been dormant and on the other that dormancy and persistence represent the same physiological state in bacteria. This difficulty resurfaces later when they define dormancy but other problems emerge before then.

I was next concerned by the extensive use of the term “Differentiation”. I completely agree that what we used to think of as uniform bacterial populations are probably never so but the degree to which subpopulations may be considered differentiated rather than reflecting a range of adaptive responses or indeed, some degree of injury, is not considered here and again I think this leads to problems in considering their hypotheses under a unitary banner downstream. I consider differentiation to require phenotypic changes that are not directly reversible, as in the case of sporulation, whereas adaptation can involve expression of a single gene that can be reversed by its subsequent repression. I do agree that cell cycle contributes to the range of phenotypes in a pure bacterial culture and that this is not the only reason for their diversity (but was not enlightened by use of the term “modulo” in this regard).

The operational definition of dormancy given deliberately leaves open the possibility of metabolic activity and seems only to require that the cell so defined should not divide; this did not allow me to recognise which operational tests might be applied to enumerate or detect dormant cells. Subsequently the detection of molecular signals indicative of bacterial presence in samples from which they were not isolated in culture is taken as evidence of dormancy. In the first case do we accept any non-dividing cell as dormant and in the second I can (and will) offer multiple alternate explanations other than dormancy. Moreover, returning briefly to the conflation between dormancy and persisters, the recent work of John McKinney and colleagues shows that antibiotic exposed persisting cells are not necessarily non-dividing cells in the mycobacterial system he studied.

Alternative interpretations of the presence of bacterial 16SrDNA sequences in blood when culture fails to detect the organisms from which they derive, include the presence of dead, injured or moribund cells. If they are shown to be repeatedly present then they must either be able to persist in the face of clearance mechanisms or be supplied at a rate equal to their clearance; both seem equally plausible to the dormancy explanation to me. Moreover, why the first three explanations offered for “Not-yet-cultured” should apply to environmental bacteriology but not to clinical samples escapes me.

I am led to the conclusion that the authors have chosen to label evidence for discrepancies between culture and nucleic acid detection of bacteria in blood to give their hypotheses a simple headline. I have no problem with the proposal that human blood and tissues classically considered sterile in the absence of overt symptoms of infection are frequently exposed to bacteria and bacterial products that in many cases contribute to serious chronic disease. However, I consider the burden of available evidence currently provides many potential explanations within the field of microbiomics/metagenomics in contrast to the dormancy hypothesis offered here. Further, I feel this broad application of dormancy to bacterial phenotypes which, even in the case of Rpf dependency, have not been shown to result from a programme of gene expression that could be considered as differentiation, diminishes the value of the term. Indeed there remains no direct proof that dormancy of Mycobacterium tuberculosis underpins what we call latent tuberculosis infection and it is not essential to the observed clinical or pathological pattern, notwithstanding the widespread acceptance of this view by most researches, including me.

I am not fundamentally opposed to the ideas presented by Kell and colleagues but I do not think they are assisted by lack of attention to the contradictions I have identified above.

Finally I come to the iron dysregulation hypothesis and its pro-inflammatory consequences. It is beyond my expertise to comment on the plausibility of the inorganic chemistry deployed here or to review the evidence relating to more than a fraction of the conditions listed. The importance of the struggle between pathogens and host for access to iron is beyond question. When I entered the medical field of infectious disease it was fully recognised that depriving bacteria from iron was a potential therapeutic angle and indeed iron chelation was studied. Desferioxamine, a widely used agent in iron overload, was investigated and found to effectively deliver iron to the pathogen and the approach was set aside. More recently this agent has been identified as a major risk factor in serious fungal infection and guidance specifically recommends its avoidance. Newer agents seem not to suffer from this problem and the approach deserves renewed attention. However, I would not underestimate the ability of pathogens to outwit our pharmaceutical industry in the battle to sequester iron. While there are reasons beyond the host –pathogen tug-of war for iron to consider chelation as a therapeutic option, the potential for adverse effects is significant and I think the suggestion that omission of iron chelation from recent guidance on sepsis management is “shocking” is not justified.
Focussing briefly on the specific diseases cited and their relation to bacterial exposure in one form or another, I find that evidence cited frequently rests on what can be considered “fringe” hypotheses that have little currency in their respective fields. This is not to discourage their continued pursuit but it does weaken the strength of the authors’ argument when investigation of the supporting literature frequently leads to papers that are given little credence in the specialist field. Of course “cave Helicobacter” must remain on the table. But there, an accidental technical breakthrough led to an avalanche of convincing laboratory and clinical data.

In summary Kell, Potgieter and Pretorius have produced an interesting read which bring many important ideas to our attention. I am not convinced of the breadth of conditions to which they argue their ideas are applicable and I await with interest, demonstration of of how they may be practically pursued and some selected definitive proofs that iron-driven inflammatory disease is as important as they claim.
paper_title_zh: 个体性、表型分化、休眠及“持久性”在可培养细菌系统中的表现：环境、实验室及临床微生物学的共性
paper_abstract_zh: 对于细菌而言，复制主要通过二分裂生长实现。然而，在许多自然环境中，存在大量表型上休眠、不生长的细胞，这些细胞不会立即复制，并且在通常允许其生长的培养基上表现为“不可培养”。因此，它们通过常规的培养方法逃避检测。这种休眠细胞在实验室培养和临床微生物学中也可以观察到。它们通常对诸如抗生素等压力更具耐受性，在临床微生物学中通常被称为“持留菌”。细菌培养必然具有高度的亲缘关系，包容性适应度理论暗示，在生长速率的变化与其平均值之间进行权衡，具有概念上的进化优势，类似于对冲策略。大量证据表明，细菌广泛利用这一策略。本文汇集了数据，展示了这些现象在环境、实验室和临床微生物学中的普遍性。大量证据（使用类似于环境微生物学中常见的方法）现在表明，许多所谓的非传染性、慢性炎症性疾病是由休眠或持留细菌的存在加剧的（如果不是主要引起的话），这些细菌成分引发炎症的能力是众所周知的。这种休眠（及其复苏）通常反映了游离铁的可利用程度。综合来看，这些现象可以轻易解释这类慢性疾病中常见的持续炎症及其与铁调节失衡的相关性。这意味着设计用于评估、抑制或去除这些生物体（或其获取铁的能力）的措施可能具有显著的治疗益处。
review_content_zh:
Kell、Potgieter和Pretorius呈现了一篇激发思考和富有争议的综述，内容涵盖细菌可培养性与其生存能力之间的相互关系，以及这些描述与定义明确的生理状态之间可能存在的联系。通过讨论环境细菌，最终聚焦于与人类相关的微生物群，尤其是那些在血液中发现的（且无败血症相关症状）及其在疾病中的假定角色。文章发展了两个核心主题，这两个主题超出了其他地方广泛讨论的范围：1）未能从许多样本中培养出细菌通常反映了细菌的休眠状态；2）这种休眠细菌通过与宿主铁调节的相互作用，导致或直接促成一系列被广泛标记为非传染性的慢性疾病。

在总体层面上，我支持作者们所采取的挑衅性立场。凭借861篇引用文献，至少他们为任何希望考虑微生物对传统上认为无此病因成分疾病的潜在贡献的人提供了宝贵资源。当然，幽门螺杆菌感染成为在面对精心汇编的证据时，轻率否定这一可能性的愚蠢行为的纪念碑。事实上，本评审人多年前在最终医学考试中遇到一例十二指肠溃疡病例，如果他当时声称感染在其患者病理中起作用，他的职业生涯可能会大不相同。

在考虑所提出的具体观点时，我有多个担忧，其中最显著的将在下方详细阐述。

在考虑细菌生存能力和生理学时，语义呈现了一个核心问题，我大体上支持这里采取的方法。作者确实试图定义他们的术语，但一些问题仍然存在。特别是，我对“持留菌”（Persisters）这一术语的广泛应用持保留意见，该术语应保留用于在暴露于杀死大多数活跃生长培养物中细菌的抗菌压力后仍能存活（具有复制潜力）的细胞。将这一术语与“休眠”混淆，一方面暗示持留细胞必须是休眠的，另一方面暗示休眠和持留代表细菌中相同的生理状态。这一困难在后续他们定义休眠时再次浮现，但在此之前还出现了其他问题。

接下来，我对“分化”这一术语的广泛使用感到担忧。我完全同意，我们过去认为的统一细菌种群可能从未如此，但亚种群被认为分化的程度，而不是反映一系列适应性反应或某种程度的损伤，在这里并未考虑，我认为这导致在后续统一旗帜下考虑其假设时出现问题。我认为分化需要不可直接逆转的表型变化，如孢子形成的情况，而适应可以涉及单一基因的表达，该表达可以通过其后续的抑制而逆转。我确实同意细胞周期有助于纯细菌培养中的表型范围，而这并非其多样性的唯一原因（但并未因使用“模数”这一术语而有所启发）。

所给出的休眠的操作定义故意留出了代谢活动的可能性，似乎只要求如此定义的细胞不应分裂；这并未让我识别出哪些操作测试可能应用于计数或检测休眠细胞。随后，将检测到指示细菌存在的分子信号作为样本中未培养出细菌的证据。在第一种情况下，我们是否接受任何非分裂细胞为休眠细胞？在第二种情况下，我可以（并且会）提供除休眠之外的多重替代解释。此外，简要回顾休眠与持留菌的混淆，John McKinney及其同事的最新研究表明，在抗生素暴露下的持留细胞在所研究的分枝杆菌系统中并不一定是非分裂细胞。

当培养未能检测到衍生出16SrDNA序列的细菌时，对血液中细菌16SrDNA序列存在的替代解释包括死亡、受伤或垂死的细胞。如果它们被反复显示存在，那么它们要么能够面对清除机制而持续存在，要么以等于其清除速率的速率供应；在我看来，这两种情况都与休眠解释同样合理。此外，为什么“尚未培养”的前三个解释适用于环境细菌学而不适用于临床样本，我不得而知。

我得出的结论是，作者选择将培养与核酸检测细菌之间差异的证据标签化，以给他们的假设一个简单的标题。我并不反对人类血液和组织在无明显感染症状的情况下，经常暴露于细菌和细菌产品，并在许多情况下促成严重慢性疾病的观点。然而，我认为目前可用的证据负担在微生物组学/宏基因组学领域提供了许多潜在解释，与这里提出的休眠假设形成对比。此外，我觉得将休眠广泛应用于细菌表型，即使在Rpf依赖性情况下，也并未显示出由可被视为分化的基因表达程序所致，这削弱了该术语的价值。事实上，仍无直接证据表明结核分枝杆菌的休眠是我们所称的潜伏性结核感染的基石，且并非所观察到的临床或病理模式所必需，尽管包括我在内的多数研究者普遍接受这一观点。

我并非从根本上反对Kell及其同事提出的观点，但我不认为他们因未关注我上述指出的矛盾而得到帮助。

最后，我谈谈铁失调假设及其促炎后果。超出我的专业范围，无法评论此处部署的无机化学的合理性，或审查与所列条件中一小部分相关的证据。病原体与宿主之间争夺铁的重要性毋庸置疑。当我进入传染病医学领域时，完全认识到剥夺细菌铁是一个潜在的治疗角度，确实研究了铁螯合作用。去铁胺，一种在铁过载中广泛使用的药物，被研究并发现能有效将铁递送给病原体，该方法被搁置。最近，该药物被发现是严重真菌感染的主要风险因素，指南特别建议避免使用。较新的药物似乎没有这个问题，该方法值得重新关注。然而，我不会低估病原体在与制药业争夺铁的斗争中智胜我们的能力。尽管有超出宿主-病原体拉锯战的理由考虑螯合作为治疗选项，但潜在的不良影响是显著的，我认为最近关于败血症管理指南中省略铁螯合的建议是“令人震惊的”并不合理。

简要聚焦于所引用的特定疾病及其与某种形式的细菌暴露的关系，我发现所引用的证据经常依赖于可以被认为是“边缘”的假设，这些假设在其各自领域内鲜有流通。这并非要阻止其继续追求，但当调查支持性文献时，频繁引向在该专业领域内鲜有信誉的论文，这确实削弱了作者论点的力度。当然，“幽门螺杆菌之洞”必须保留在桌面上。但那里，一个偶然的技术突破引发了一系列令人信服的实验室和临床数据。

总之，Kell、Potgieter和Pretorius呈现了一篇引人入胜的读物，将许多重要观点带到我们面前。我并不确信他们主张其观点适用的条件范围，我满怀兴趣地期待他们如何实际追求这些观点，以及一些选择性确凿的证据，证明铁驱动的炎症性疾病如他们所声称的那么重要。

reasons: With 861 cited references, at the very least they provide a valuable resource for anyone wishing to consider the potential microbial contribution to diseases traditionally considered free of this aetiological component.

Focussing briefly on the specific diseases cited and their relation to bacterial exposure in one form or another, I find that evidence cited frequently rests on what can be considered “fringe” hypotheses that have little currency in their respective fields.

This is not to discourage their continued pursuit but it does weaken the strength of the authors’ argument when investigation of the supporting literature frequently leads to papers that are given little credence in the specialist field.
At a general level I support the provocative stance taken by the authors.
In considering the specific points presented I have multiple concerns, the most significant of which I will indulge in outlining below.
I am led to the conclusion that the authors have chosen to label evidence for discrepancies between culture and nucleic acid detection of bacteria in blood to give their hypotheses a simple headline.
However, I consider the burden of available evidence currently provides many potential explanations within the field of microbiomics/metagenomics in contrast to the dormancy hypothesis offered here.

Further, I feel this broad application of dormancy to bacterial phenotypes which, even in the case of Rpf dependency, have not been shown to result from a programme of gene expression that could be considered as differentiation, diminishes the value of the term.

Indeed there remains no direct proof that dormancy of Mycobacterium tuberculosis underpins what we call latent tuberculosis infection and it is not essential to the observed clinical or pathological pattern, notwithstanding the widespread acceptance of this view by most researches, including me.
In summary Kell, Potgieter and Pretorius have produced an interesting read which bring many important ideas to our attention.

I am not convinced of the breadth of conditions to which they argue their ideas are applicable and I await with interest, demonstration of of how they may be practically pursued and some selected definitive proofs that iron-driven inflammatory disease is as important as they claim.
Semantics present a central problem in considering bacterial viability and physiology and I broadly support the approach taken here.
The authors do try to define their terms but some problems remain.
I was next concerned by the extensive use of the term “Differentiation”.
This difficulty resurfaces later when they define dormancy but other problems emerge before then.
I am not fundamentally opposed to the ideas presented by Kell and colleagues but I do not think they are assisted by lack of attention to the contradictions I have identified above.
I am led to the conclusion that the authors have chosen to label evidence for discrepancies between culture and nucleic acid detection of bacteria in blood to give their hypotheses a simple headline.

paper_title: The effect of surface treatments on the bond strength of polyetheretherketone posts: a systematic review protocol
paper_abstract:
Background 
 Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) is widely used in the biomedical field due to its outstanding biological and mechanical properties. Originally employed as a temporary abutment in implantology, recent research has expanded its indications for more definitive applications, such as frameworks and dental post and core. However, PEEK’s inert nature and low surface energy pose challenges for adhesion, necessitating surface modifications. Various physical and chemical modification techniques, including acid etching (e.g., 98% sulfuric acid), sandblasting with alumina oxide (Al₂O₃), plasma treatment, laser irradiation, silanization, and air abrasion with silica-coated particles, have been proposed to enhance PEEK’s bonding performance. Despite numerous clinical investigations, standardized protocols for surface treatment remain lacking. This systematic review aims to assess the impact of surface treatments on the bonding performance of PEEK posts. 
 
 
 Methods 
 A detailed search of the literature will be conducted across several databases including PubMed, Scopus and clinical trial registries. Additional databases such as Cochrane Central, EMBASE, Web of Science and EBSCO will also be included. The search strategy will target controlled randomized studies and non-randomized clinical trials evaluating the impact of surface treatments on PEEK post adhesion strength. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) will be used to assess bias in non-randomized studies, while the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB II) tool will be employed for evaluating randomized controlled trials. Data extraction will focus on study design, treatment methods, outcomes and results. 
 This systematic review protocol will adhere to the guidelines for systematic reviews outlined in the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). 
 
 
 Discussion 
 The discussion will explore the implications of findings on clinical practice, highlighting the importance of enhancing PEEK’s bioactivity and surface energy to improve bonding efficacy in dental procedures. Moreover, it will suggest areas for future research to advance dental materials science, aiming to optimize the utilization of PEEK in dental applications 
 
 
 Systematic review registration 
 PROSPERO: CRD42024529783 (Registered on 08/04/2024).
review_content:
Review report for the submitted manuscript “The effect of surface treatments on the bond strength of polyetheretherketone posts: a systematic review protocol”

I would like to thank the authors for submitting their protocol for review. The use of PEEK posts in dental applications is a developing subject, so a systematic assessment of surface treatment procedures is extremely important. PEEK's biocompatibility and mechanical strength make it excellent for dental posts, but the inert surface makes bonding challenging. This review could fill a crucial gap in clinical practice.
Overall, the language is clear, but minor editing of English language might be required in the final submitted review. Author might want to explore options for refining their text to improve its flow and readability. This can make their article more engaging and clear.
1. Title: - Approved as is.
2. Abstract: Kindly give a hint on the different surface treatment techniques of PEEK for the reader.
3. Introduction: -I think the introduction is a bit shallow. I would prefer the introduction to begin with PEEK material (history, chemical composition and properties) as it is the main objective of the study. Then going through the different applications quickly and concentrating on the endodontically treated teeth and post indications and PEEK post (ready & custom made) as one of the options available for clinicians. Finally, stating PEEK adhesion properties as a weakness that different surface treatments aim to improve.
-Kindly connect short paragraphs into paragraphs of 6-7 lines paragraphs.
-Kindly add references to the second & third paragraph.
- The authors could elaborate on the therapeutic relevance of PEEK's bond strength as compared to conventional materials like metal, zirconia or fiber posts.
4. Methods: -The protocol is well-structured and follows known principles for systematic reviews (PRISMA). The use of numerous databases (e.g., PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central) will ensure a thorough literature review. The intended use of risk-of-bias tools (ROB II and NOS) and data extraction procedures demonstrates a commitment to evidence of excellent quality synthesis.
Intervention types:
There is no mention of the surface treatments of PEEK aimed for exploration. Only 2 examples were mentioned so kindly give more details regarding treatments to be studied.
Outcomes:
More precise definitions would be useful in the outcomes section. While bond strength and retention are indicated, it is unclear how they would be tested. Providing additional details on the anticipated outcomes and their clinical significance could enhance the protocol.
Evaluation of methodological quality and risk of bias:
-The protocol’s description of bias assessment tools (ROB II and NOS) is good, but how will studies with unclear risks of bias be handled in the analysis? Also kindly give more details regarding the “standardized tools” you have mentioned as means of evaluation.
Meta analysis:
While the authors highlight the possibility of meta-analysis, it would be interesting to describe how they intend to deal with possible heterogeneity among studies (e.g., differences in surface treatments, study designs).
5. Conclusions: Although this protocol presents a well-designed systematic review that is expected to yield useful information about the surface treatments of PEEK posts in dental applications, it would be strengthened by adding the details addressed in the comments above for further enhancement.
paper_title_zh: 表面处理对聚醚醚酮桩粘接强度的影响：系统综述方案
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
聚醚醚酮（PEEK）因其卓越的生物和机械性能而在生物医学领域得到广泛应用。最初作为种植学中的临时基台使用，近期研究已将其适应症扩展到更确定的应用，如支架和牙科桩核。然而，PEEK的惰性本质和低表面能对粘接构成挑战，需要表面改性。为提高PEEK的粘接性能，提出了多种物理和化学改性技术，包括酸蚀（例如98%硫酸）、氧化铝（Al₂O₃）喷砂、等离子处理、激光照射、硅烷化和使用二氧化硅涂层颗粒的空气喷磨。尽管进行了众多临床研究，但表面处理的标准协议仍缺乏。本系统综述旨在评估表面处理对PEEK桩粘接性能的影响。

方法
将在多个数据库中进行详细的文献检索，包括PubMed、Scopus和临床试验注册库。还将包括Cochrane Central、EMBASE、Web of Science和EBSCO等额外数据库。检索策略将针对评估表面处理对PEEK桩粘接强度影响的对照随机研究和非随机临床试验。非随机研究的偏倚评估将使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表（NOS），而随机对照试验的评估将采用Cochrane偏倚风险（ROB II）工具。数据提取将集中在研究设计、处理方法、结果和成果。
本系统综述协议将遵循系统综述和荟萃分析优先报告项目（PRISMA）中概述的指南。

讨论
讨论将探讨研究结果对临床实践的影响，强调提高PEEK的生物活性和表面能以改善牙科程序中粘接效果的重要性。此外，还将提出未来研究的方向，以推进牙科材料科学，旨在优化PEEK在牙科应用中的使用。

系统综述注册
PROSPERO: CRD42024529783（注册于2024年4月8日）。
review_content_zh:
**提交的手稿“表面处理对聚醚醚酮桩粘接强度的影响：系统综述方案”的评审报告**

感谢作者提交其方案进行评审。聚醚醚酮（PEEK）桩在牙科应用中是一个发展中的课题，因此对表面处理程序的系统性评估极为重要。PEEK的生物相容性和机械强度使其成为牙科桩的理想材料，但其惰性表面使得粘接具有挑战性。本综述可能填补临床实践中的一个关键空白。

总体而言，语言清晰，但最终提交的综述可能需要稍作英文语言编辑。作者可能希望探索优化文本以提高其流畅性和可读性的选项，这可以使文章更具吸引力和清晰度。

1. 标题：- 同意原样。
2. 摘要：请为读者提供关于PEEK不同表面处理技术的提示。
3. 引言：- 我认为引言略显浅显。我更倾向于引言从PEEK材料（历史、化学成分和性质）开始，因为这是研究的主体目标。然后快速介绍不同应用，集中讨论根管治疗后的牙齿和桩的指征，以及PEEK桩（成品和定制）作为临床医生可选方案之一。最后，指出PEEK的粘接性能作为不同表面处理旨在改善的弱点。
- 请将短段落合并为6-7行的段落。
- 请在第二和第三段添加参考文献。
- 作者可以进一步阐述PEEK粘接强度与金属、氧化锆或纤维桩等传统材料的治疗相关性。

4. 方法：- 该方案结构良好，遵循了系统综述（PRISMA）的已知原则。使用多个数据库（如PubMed、Scopus、Cochrane Central）将确保文献综述的全面性。计划使用偏倚风险评估工具（ROB II和NOS）和数据提取程序，显示了致力于高质量证据合成的承诺。

干预类型：
未提及旨在探索的PEEK表面处理。仅提到了2个例子，请提供更多关于待研究处理的详细信息。

结果：
在结果部分，更精确的定义将是有用的。虽然指出了粘接强度和保留率，但尚不清楚将如何测试它们。提供关于预期结果及其临床意义的额外细节可以增强该方案。

方法学质量评估和偏倚风险：
- 方案中对偏倚评估工具（ROB II和NOS）的描述良好，但将如何处理分析中偏倚风险不明确的研究？也请提供更多关于所提及的“标准化工具”作为评估手段的详细信息。

Meta分析：
虽然作者强调了Meta分析的可能性，但描述他们如何处理研究间可能存在的异质性（如表面处理差异、研究设计差异）将是有趣的。

5. 结论：尽管该方案呈现了一个设计良好的系统综述，预计将提供关于PEEK桩在牙科应用中表面处理的有用信息，但通过添加上述评论中提到的细节，可以进一步强化该方案。

paper_title: Bibliometric assessment and key messages of sporotrichosis research (1945-2018)
paper_abstract:
Background: Sporotrichosis has recently emerged as an important mycosis worldwide, with diverse transmission and epidemiologic profiles. For instance, in Brazil most cases are related to zoonotic transmission from naturally infected cats, and the majority of cases in China are due to external injury with environmental materials. Publications on sporotrichosis and on its etiologic agent may guide the direction of the research in this field. It can also define priorities for future studies. 
 Methods: In this study, we evaluated the trends of global research in Sporothrix and sporotrichosis, based on publications records retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science databases for the period of 1945 to 2018. The overall productivity in the field, its geographical and temporal distribution, research themes, co-authorship networks, funding sources, and if audience and research findings are addressed in the abstracts. 
 Results: A total of 4,007 unique publications involving 99 countries were retrieved, most of them published after 2000. Authors based on institutions from the United States of America and Brazil accounted for 57.4% of the publications. Brazil was the leading country in terms of research collaboration and networking, with co-authorship with 45 countries. The thematic mapping revealed a temporal shift from clinical to applied research. Despite the large number of countries publishing in this field, most of funded studies came from Brazil, Mexico, China, South Africa, or the United States of America. The analysis of content identified few specific public health recommendations for prevention, case-management, or research. Moreover, most papers do not have a clearly defined intended audience. 
 Conclusion: As the research in this field is emerging in several countries, with the generation of a large amount of data, it is necessary that scientists strengthen efforts to translate the research results into practice to curb this neglected infection.
review_content:
Congratulations to the authors. Despite sporotrichosis remains a neglected disease in terms of research interest, funding and medical attention, to which the authors have made significant contributions. However, this study has several major observations:

Methods.
The literature search is limited to two databases. Fig. 1. Present a flow, and follow the guidelines of a scoping review.
MedLine / Pubmed and Abstracts of Scientific Conference should be reviewed.
There are several published studies on sporotrichosis in journals indexed in SCIELO, LiLACS, etc. These papers have not been included in the study.

I don’t think that this article contains enough robust data to evidence the implications for practice. The strategy and organization of the information about Implications for practice is not appropriate. A set of words related to tentative language is biased. Furthermore, only the abstracts have been reviewed. To evaluate the implications in practice, it is necessary to organize the different types of published studies: case series, observational study, clinical trials and systematic review, diagnostic test, etc. Furthermore, studies not related to the clinical practice of sporotrichosis should be excluded.

Results:
Paragraph 1. I suggest include in Results section include the statistical test.
Scientific production by hyperendemic areas of sporotrichosis should be presented.

Table 3. I suggest to make a comparison between Brazil, USA, Mexico, China, or hyperendymic areas of sporotrichosis.

The authors should include the different types of published articles: review, original, short communication, case reports, clinical trial, systematic, review, correspondece, Research Letters, etc.

Research trends. It would be interesting to know how these trends vary between Latin America. Europe and Asia.

Implications for practice
I suggest organizing the published studies: case series, observational study, clinical trials and systematic review, diagnostic test, etc. Although there are very few clinical trials and systematic reviews on sporotrichosis, this evidence should be presented in tables. Furthermore, studies not related to the clinical practice of sporotrichosis should be excluded.
Finally, sporotrichosis is not limited to dermatology.

Discussion
In the “Discussion” section I would have wished to see more information on implicance practic .
Limitations should be described and discussed such as: the number of databases included in the study, the studies were not classified, to differentiate the type of scientific evidence for clinical practice, etc.
paper_title_zh: "孢子丝菌病研究的文献计量评估及关键信息（1945-2018）"
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：孢子丝菌病近年来在全球范围内成为重要的真菌病，具有多样的传播和流行病学特征。例如，在巴西，大多数病例与自然感染的猫的动物源性传播有关，而在中国，大多数病例是由于与环境材料的体外损伤有关。关于孢子丝菌病及其病原体的出版物可以指导该领域的研究方向，并确定未来研究的优先事项。

方法：在本研究中，我们基于从Scopus和Web of Science数据库中检索到的1945年至2018年的出版物记录，评估了全球对Sporothrix和孢子丝菌病的研究趋势。分析了该领域的总体产出、地理和时间分布、研究主题、合著网络、资金来源，以及摘要中是否提及受众和研究发现。

结果：共检索到涉及99个国家的4,007篇独特出版物，其中大多数发表于2000年之后。来自美国和巴西的机构作者占出版物的57.4%。巴西在研究合作和网络方面领先，与45个国家有合著关系。主题映射显示研究从临床向应用研究的时态转变。尽管有许多国家在该领域发表文章，但大多数受资助的研究来自巴西、墨西哥、中国、南非或美国。内容分析发现，针对预防、病例管理或研究的具体公共卫生建议较少。此外，大多数论文没有明确界定的目标受众。

结论：随着该领域研究在多个国家的兴起，并产生了大量数据，科学家们有必要加强努力，将研究结果转化为实践，以遏制这种被忽视的感染。
review_content_zh:
祝贺作者们。尽管孢子丝菌病在研究兴趣、资金和医疗关注方面仍然是一种被忽视的疾病，但作者们为此做出了重要贡献。然而，这项研究有几个主要观察结果：

方法。
文献检索仅限于两个数据库。图1。呈现了一个流程，并遵循了范围综述的指南。

在SCIELO、LiLACS等索引的期刊上有几篇关于孢子丝菌病的研究论文。这些论文未包含在研究中。

我认为这篇文章没有包含足够有力的数据来证明对实践的启示。关于实践启示的信息策略和组织不恰当。一组与试探性语言相关的词汇存在偏见。此外，仅审查了摘要。要评估实践中的启示，有必要组织不同类型的已发表研究：病例系列、观察性研究、临床试验和系统综述、诊断测试等。此外，应排除与孢子丝菌病临床实践无关的研究。

结果：
第一段。我建议在结果部分包括统计检验。
应呈现孢子丝菌病高流行区的科学产出。

表3。我建议比较巴西、美国、墨西哥、中国或孢子丝菌病高流行区。

作者应包括不同类型的已发表文章：综述、原创、简讯、病例报告、临床试验、系统综述、通信、研究快报等。

研究趋势。了解这些趋势在拉丁美洲、欧洲和亚洲之间的变化会很有趣。

对实践的启示
我建议组织已发表的研究：病例系列、观察性研究、临床试验和系统综述、诊断测试等。尽管关于孢子丝菌病的临床试验和系统综述非常少，但这些证据应在表格中呈现。此外，应排除与孢子丝菌病临床实践无关的研究。
最后，孢子丝菌病不仅限于皮肤科。

讨论
在“讨论”部分，我希望看到更多关于实践启示的信息。

paper_title: Cigarette consumption in adult dual users of cigarettes and e-cigarettes: a review of the evidence, including new results from the PATH study
review_content:
Summary: The authors conducted secondary analysis of cross-sectional and longitudinal PATH data to compare cigarette consumptions among dual users of cigarettes and e-cigarettes. The authors also present a review of published literature on this topic.
These reviewers has the following comments.
 1. The authors describe e-cigarettes as “reduced-risk tobacco products (RRP)”. While there is no doubt that e-cigs have considerably lower exposure to many of the HPHCs compared to combustible cigarettes and therefore present lower risks relative to cigarettes, the evidence is still emerging regarding these products. The authors should therefore consider identifying these products as “Potential Reduced-Risk Products” (PRRP).
 2. While we understand that recall bias may complicate inferences on tobacco product use history and the “correction” applied by the authors seems reasonable, the authors should consider including a results table for descriptive statistics (with and without correction) in the Supplement, to allow the reader judge for themselves regarding impact of this correction.
 3. The authors conclude that “smokers who become duals users will reduce their disease risk to some extent”. This is an extremely broad generalization, particularly given the authors own conclusion that the reduction in cigarettes is “fairly modest”. There is no empirical evidence to support this statement of risk reduction among the entire category of dual users, even to “some extent”. A recent report indicates that dual users are a very heterogenous group[ref-1],[ref-2]. Indeed, established every day frequent e-cigarette users may smoke far fewer cigarettes than current smokers thereby substantially reducing exposure to many of the HPHCs. This may lead to lowering of disease risks. In order to achieve the optimum outcome of reducing smoking related diseases, adult smokers must switch completely from cigarettes to e-cigs. We recommend that the authors either delete or modify the statement with appropriate caveats.
 4. There are several points for consideration to refine the methodology used in this manuscript:
     1. In the method section, the authors describe that the analysis is limited to every day cigarette smokers. The authors described “all the analyses were weighted, based on weighting factors for Wave 1”. In PATH user guide (Section 5), there are various types of weights. It is not clear whether the cross-sectional analysis (Q1) was conducted separately using cross-sectional weights of each wave to ensure the representativeness of the results. Longitudinal analysis should be conducted using longitudinal weights. In this case, wave 3 weights should be applied to answer research questions 2 and 3. The authors must clearly specify which weight was used for each analysis (Q1-Q3).
     2. The data is limited to ‘current everyday cigarette smokers at each Wave with data available on CC’. As reported by Borland et. al. (2019)[ref-3] and Smith et al. (2021)[ref-1] cigarette consumption differs significantly between every day and some day cigarette smokers and different segment of dual users. To obtain a complete picture of the current cigarette smoker population, the authors should consider including some day smokers in the analysis. This group more likely represents a larger proportion of dual users and provides a more comprehensive view of the cigarette consumption data for dual users. We note that indeed, there are cigarette consumption data in PATH for some day smokers.
     3. To answer Q3, the cigarette consumption was “compared in those who did or did not become dual users”. However, since Q3 is asking “is baseline consumption related to later initiation of e-cigarettes”. A logistic regression model with e-cigarette initiation as the outcome measure and cigarette consumption being the covariate would be more appropriate to answer Q3.
     4. Based on the current analysis description for Q3, the analysis will compare exclusive cigarette smokers who did or did not become dual users. A clearer description of ‘dual user’ needs to be given as it is shown in Table 3 there are three types of ‘Definition of Use’. Does the heading ‘Became users’ in the ‘Ever Established’ row mean exclusive daily smokers who became ever established users of e-cigarette? Please clarify.
     5. The authors should clearly describe if R survey package is used in the analysis. While the R-program is appropriate to conduct statistical analysis, R survey package allows the researcher to utilize the full-sample weight, variance estimation method, BRR-Fay replicate weights, and that Fay’s factor are correctly specified (See PATH User Guide, Appendix B for example R program code). The authors must specify whether replicate weights and Fay’s correction factor were used in current analyses.
     6. Authors state that “nine predictor variables [were] selected, using a forward stepwise approach, including variables significant at p<0.05”. It is not clear what variables were considered and the rationale for selection of the variables... The age range category “55+ years” for the variable ‘age range when first started smoking cigarettes every day’ should not be included as the data analysis is limited to 18 to 54 years.
     7. Authors only included respondents “aged 18 to 54 years at Wave 1 (as e-cigarette use proved to be very uncommon in those aged 55+ years”. A quick analysis revealed that by excluding individuals aged 55 or older, around 14% of the sample size is excluded among both current established and former established e-cigarette users at Wave 1. This phrase “(as e-cigarette use proved to be very uncommon in those aged 55+ years)” should be deleted since the data does not appear to support the statement.
 1. In the result section, the table captions should include more detail descriptions and definitions. For all result tables, the phrase ‘among every day smokers’ should be added if the analysis is only conducted among every day smokers. Does the table footnote ‘NS’ mean ‘not significant’? If yes, the corresponding footnote should be ‘p>0.05’ instead of ‘p<=0.05’. The ‘dual use’ term becomes very confusing when it is corresponding to three meanings (i.e., current establish e-cigarette use, ever established e-cigarette use and current every day e-cigarette use). The authors should be more precise.
     1. Table 1. Table caption should include ‘among every day smokers’ if the analysis is only conducted among every day smokers. There are three columns of ‘dual users’. The author needs to clarify the definitions of these three types of ‘dual users’.
     2. Table 2. The word ‘e-cigarette’ should be added to ‘current established use’, ‘ever established use’, and ‘current every day use’. The ‘No No’, ‘Yes Yes’, ‘No Yes’, ‘Yes No’ combinations should be clearly labeled with CS and ECIG to clearly identify the groups being considered.
     3. Table 3. The word “e-cigarette” should be specified in the ‘Definition of Use’ column. And the dual use needs to be clearly defined (see previous comments in the method section).
 2. Literature review results
     1. Results related to Q2
        In the literature review section, some of the findings were drawn from studies with adolescent data. Five out of 13 studies (Table 6) referenced in the results include adolescent data. The authors should be consistent with the literature search criteria and either exclude studies on youth as that was considered out of scope for the review, modify their search criteria or provide a rationale regarding inclusion of only select publications with adolescent data.
     2. Results related to Q3.
        Based on Andler et al. 2016, the authors state that ‘heavier smokers were more likely to start vaping’. However, this does not accurately represent the results from the publication. Andler et al. 2016, state that ”82 % of dual users reported that vaping had enabled them to reduce their cigarette consumption, with a mean reduction of 8.9 cigarettes per day. These individuals were initially heavy smokers, smoking 21 cigarettes per day on average (the mean overall among smokers was 11.3 in 2014.” Just because the participants in the study were heavy smokers that does not establish causality. Furthermore, Andler et al. 2016, included adolescents (age 15+) in their study. The authors should consider providing more context around the statement on heavy smokers.
paper_title_zh: 香烟和电子烟双重使用成年人群的香烟消费：证据综述，包括PATH研究的新结果
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：建模电子烟使用对疾病风险的影响需要了解电子烟的普及对吸烟者香烟消费的影响。通过美国PATH研究的第1-3波数据和其他证据，我们试图回答三个问题：（Q1）双重使用者与单一吸烟者的消费是否有差异？（Q2）开始使用电子烟是否会影响香烟消费？（Q3）基线消费是否与后期电子烟的起始使用相关？

方法：PATH中的消费数据经过校正以消除明显的记录错误，电子烟使用被分类为已确立或每日使用，并针对人口统计学特征、酒精、药物和其他烟草产品的使用以及开始吸烟的年龄进行了调整。搜索识别了自2008年以来发表的其他研究，Q1通过横断面研究回答，Q2和Q3也通过前瞻性研究回答。

结果：（Q1）在PATH中，当前每日使用电子烟的双重使用者消费比单一吸烟者低2-3支/天，而在已确立使用者中未见到差异。从31项已发表研究中，当前或曾经使用电子烟的双重使用者消费并未降低。（Q2）在PATH研究中，成为每日双重使用者的个体消费持续减少，而回归单一吸烟的个体消费增加。13项已发表研究一致显示成为双重使用者的个体消费减少。（Q3）三项研究一致显示随后开始使用电子烟的吸烟者消费更高，但PATH中未见到显著差异。

结论：评估因PATH中每日电子烟使用者较少以及各研究在量化电子烟使用和结果呈现上的变异性而复杂化。由于开始使用电子烟与减少消费相关，未发现双重使用者和单一吸烟者之间明显的横断面差异，这表明开始使用电子烟的吸烟者最初消费较高，但支持这一点的证据有限。鉴于电子烟相比香烟的疾病风险低得多，成为双重使用者的吸烟者应能一定程度上降低其疾病风险。
review_content_zh:
### 摘要

作者对横断面和纵向的PATH数据进行了二次分析，以比较同时使用香烟和电子烟的双重用户的香烟消费情况。作者还对该主题的已发表文献进行了综述。

审稿人提出以下意见：

1. 作者将电子烟描述为“降低风险烟草产品（RRP）”。毫无疑问，与可燃香烟相比，电子烟对许多有害和潜在有害成分（HPHCs）的暴露显著降低，因此相对于香烟而言风险较低，但关于这些产品的证据仍在不断涌现。因此，作者应考虑将这些产品标识为“潜在降低风险产品”（PRRP）。

2. 我们理解回忆偏倚可能会使烟草产品使用历史的推断复杂化，作者所应用的“修正”似乎合理，但作者应在补充材料中包括一个描述性统计结果的表格（有和没有修正），以便读者自行判断这一修正的影响。

3. 作者得出结论认为“成为双重用户的吸烟者将在一定程度上降低其疾病风险”。这是一个极其宽泛的概括，尤其是考虑到作者自己得出的结论是香烟减少的幅度“相当有限”。没有实证证据支持在整个双重用户类别中存在风险降低的情况，即使是“在一定程度上”。最近的一份报告指出，双重用户是一个非常异质化的群体[ref-1],[ref-2]。事实上，每天频繁使用电子烟的已建立用户可能比当前吸烟者吸食的香烟少得多，从而大幅减少对许多HPHCs的暴露。这可能导致疾病风险的降低。为了实现减少吸烟相关疾病的最优结果，成年吸烟者必须完全从香烟转向电子烟。我们建议作者要么删除该声明，要么在适当的警告下进行修改。

4. 有几个要点需要考虑以完善本文所使用的方法：
   1. 在方法部分，作者描述了分析仅限于每天吸烟的吸烟者。作者描述了“所有分析均根据第一波的权重因子进行了加权”。在PATH用户指南（第5节）中，有各种类型的权重。尚不清楚横断面分析（Q1）是否分别使用了每波的横断面权重以确保结果的代表性。纵向分析应使用纵向权重。在这种情况下，第三波的权重应应用于回答研究问题2和3。作者必须明确说明每个分析（Q1-Q3）使用了哪种权重。
   2. 数据仅限于“每个波次当前每天吸烟且在CC上有数据的吸烟者”。正如Borland等人（2019年）[ref-3]和Smith等人（2021年）[ref-1]所报告的，每天吸烟和某些天吸烟的吸烟者以及不同双重用户群体的香烟消费存在显著差异。为了全面了解当前吸烟者群体，作者应考虑将某些天吸烟者纳入分析。这一群体更有可能代表更大比例的双重用户，并提供更全面的关于双重用户香烟消费数据的视图。我们注意到，PATH中确实有某些天吸烟者的香烟消费数据。
   3. 为了回答Q3，香烟消费是在“成为或未成为双重用户的人”之间进行比较的。然而，由于Q3询问的是“基线消费是否与后期开始使用电子烟相关”。使用电子烟开始作为结果变量，香烟消费作为协变量的逻辑回归模型更适合回答Q3。
   4. 根据当前对Q3的分析描述，分析将比较成为或未成为双重用户的独家香烟吸烟者。需要更清楚地描述“双重用户”的定义，因为如表3所示，有三种“使用定义”。在“Ever Established”行中的“Became users”标题是否意味着成为电子烟的已建立用户的独家每天吸烟者？请澄清。
   5. 作者应明确描述是否在分析中使用了R调查包。虽然R程序适合进行统计分析，但R调查包允许研究人员利用全样本权重、方差估计方法、BRR-Fay复制权重，并确保Fay因子正确指定（参见PATH用户指南，附录B中的示例R程序代码）。作者必须说明当前分析中是否使用了复制权重和Fay修正因子。
   6. 作者指出“选择了九个预测变量，使用前向逐步方法，包括在p<0.05时显著的变量”。尚不清楚考虑了哪些变量以及选择这些变量的理由……对于变量“开始每天吸烟时的年龄范围”中的“55+岁”年龄范围类别不应包括在内，因为数据分析仅限于18至54岁。
   7. 作者仅包括“在第一波时年龄在18至54岁之间的受访者（因为电子烟使用在55岁及以上人群中非常罕见）”。快速分析显示，排除55岁或以上的人后，在第一波中当前已建立和以前已建立的电子烟用户中，约有14%的样本量被排除。由于数据似乎不支持该声明，因此应删除该短语“（因为电子烟使用在55岁及以上人群中非常罕见）”。

1. 在结果部分，表格标题应包括更详细的描述和定义。对于所有结果表格，如果分析仅限于每天吸烟者，应添加短语“在每天吸烟者中”。表格脚注“NS”是否意味着“不显著”？如果是，相应的脚注应为“p>0.05”而不是“p<=0.05”。“双重使用”一词在对应三种含义（即当前已建立电子烟使用、曾经已建立电子烟使用和当前每天电子烟使用）时变得非常混淆。作者应更精确。
   1. 表1。如果分析仅限于每天吸烟者，表格标题应包括“在每天吸烟者中”。有三列“双重用户”。作者需要澄清这三种“双重用户”的定义。
   2. 表2。应在“当前已建立使用”、“曾经已建立使用”和“当前每天使用”中添加“电子烟”一词。应明确标记“No No”、“Yes Yes”、“No Yes”、“Yes No”组合，并使用CS和ECIG清楚地识别所考虑的组。
   3. 表3。应在“使用定义”列中指定“电子烟”一词。并且需要明确定义双重使用（见方法部分之前的评论）。

2. 文献综述结果
   1. 与Q2相关的结果
      在文献综述部分，一些发现来自包含青少年数据的研究。在结果中引用的13项研究中有5项（表6）包括青少年数据。作者应保持文献检索标准的一致性，要么排除关于青少年的研究，因为这在综述中被认为超出范围，要么修改其检索标准，或提供关于仅包括含有青少年数据的选定出版物的理由。
   2. 与Q3相关的结果
      基于Andler等人2016年的研究，作者指出“重度吸烟者更有可能开始使用电子烟”。然而，这并不准确反映该出版物中的结果。Andler等人2016年指出，“82%的双重用户报告称，使用电子烟使他们能够减少香烟消费，平均每天减少8.9支香烟。这些个体最初是重度吸烟者，平均每天吸21支香烟（2014年吸烟者的平均值为11.3支）。”仅仅因为研究中的参与者是重度吸烟者，并不能确立因果关系。此外，Andler等人2016年的研究包括了青少年（15岁及以上）。作者应考虑在关于重度吸烟者的声明中提供更多背景信息。

If yes, the corresponding footnote should be ‘p>0.05’ instead of ‘p<=0.05’.

The ‘dual use’ term becomes very confusing when it is corresponding to three meanings (i.e., current establish e-cigarette use, ever established e-cigarette use and current every day e-cigarette use).
The authors should be more precise.

The authors should consider including a results table for descriptive statistics (with and without correction) in the Supplement, to allow the reader judge for themselves regarding impact of this correction.
Table 1. Table caption should include ‘among every day smokers’ if the analysis is only conducted among every day smokers.
Table 2. The word ‘e-cigarette’ should be added to ‘current established use’, ‘ever established use’, and ‘current every day use’.
The ‘No No’, ‘Yes Yes’, ‘No Yes’, ‘Yes No’ combinations should be clearly labeled with CS and ECIG to clearly identify the groups being considered.
Table 3. The word “e-cigarette” should be specified in the ‘Definition of Use’ column.
And the dual use needs to be clearly defined (see previous comments in the method section).
It is not clear whether the cross-sectional analysis (Q1) was conducted separately using cross-sectional weights of each wave to ensure the representativeness of the results.
Longitudinal analysis should be conducted using longitudinal weights.
In this case, wave 3 weights should be applied to answer research questions 2 and 3.
The authors must clearly specify which weight was used for each analysis (Q1-Q3).
To answer Q3, the cigarette consumption was “compared in those who did or did not become dual users”.
However, since Q3 is asking “is baseline consumption related to later initiation of e-cigarettes”.
A logistic regression model with e-cigarette initiation as the outcome measure and cigarette consumption being the covariate would be more appropriate to answer Q3.
A clearer description of ‘dual user’ needs to be given as it is shown in Table 3 there are three types of ‘Definition of Use’.
The authors should clearly describe if R survey package is used in the analysis.
The authors must specify whether replicate weights and Fay’s correction factor were used in current analyses.
It is not clear what variables were considered and the rationale for selection of the variables...

paper_title: A systematic review of the direct and indirect effects of herbivory on plant reproduction mediated by pollination
paper_abstract: Background. Plant reproduction is influenced by the net outcome of plant-herbivore and plant-pollinator interactions. While both herbivore impacts and pollinator impacts on plant reproduction have been widely studied, few studies examine them in concert.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (Anonymous) Basic reporting 1. The introduction is long, a little jumbled, and not quite focused on the same thing as the rest of the paper, and as a result it feels disconnected from the rest of the paper. For example, there’s more than a full single spaced page of background on just herbivory in isolation, which seems like too much since that’s not the main point of this paper. I think the introduction needs to be made more concise, with relevant material shifted to the discussion section for more exploration and unnecessary material removed. >We have slimmed down the introduction and removed some redundant information, moving information that was not already there to the discussion. 2. The introduction also probably needs to be restructured/reorganized. You want to give enough background information to directly lead into the topic of herbivory affecting plant fitness by affecting pollinator visitation, and lead up to your purpose in writing this review. >The introduction has been largely restructured and slimmed down to flow in a more logical way. 3. Related, there are a couple of places, especially in the introduction, that still cover several topics in one long paragraph, and probably need to be split up. For example, the second paragraph in the introduction (beginning at line 50) could be split into three paragraphs: one paragraph from line 50 to 56; a second paragraph from line 56 (starting with “Most typically…”) to line 67; and a third from line 67 (starting with “In this systematic review…”) to the end at line 72. >The introduction has been largely restructured and slimmed down with some paragraphs split, such as the one suggested. 4. Compared to the first version of this paper, there have been significant improvements to content and organization of discussion section. I especially liked the first paragraph in the discussion. However, by adding so much material, it’s easy to get lost in all of the details when reading it. I suggest adding subheadings to split up the material (e.g. “Effects of florivory on pollination” and “Effects of vegetative herbivory on pollination” etc). >Subheadings have been added 5. Line 354: “Folivory, root damage, and stem damage were found to negatively impact several floral traits, as well as pollinator visitation and reproduction.” You don’t really get into the details of what these effects are. I would prefer to see each of these types of vegetative damage talked about separately, with the kinds of effects on floral traits, pollination, and reproduction that are generally seen. If there is enough information, they may each get their own paragraph. If there is little information, they may just be separate sentences in the same paragraph. >A few sentences have been added to list which traits were affected, but there is not much data to go into each in depth. 6. Figure 3 is a nice addition. However, the red dots showing study sites are so small I didn’t see them at first even in color. In grayscale, they are completely gone. >Thank you for catching that, the dots have been made larger 7. I still have trouble with Figure 4. It’s very hard to read, with so many thing lines connecting names in small font, and having the lines behind the text makes the names harder to read. That said, it is improved from the last version in that I can at least (with some effort) tell which name each line is supposed to connect to. >We have reworked this graph once again and believe it is now much easier to read. Smaller comments: • In the very first sentence in the introduction (line 50), “Plant fitness is determined by the net outcome of interactions with other species.” – while it’s true that interactions with other species partially determine plant fitness, they aren’t the only thing that affects plant fitness. Resource availability or abiotic factors, for example. >You are of course correct, this wasn’t meant to be an exclusionary statement. We qualified the statement by adding “in part.” • Lines 44-46: “interactions between two species do not represent the net outcome of relationships” – these are typically called non-additive effects. >The descriptor “non-additive” was added. • Line 75: “rob the plant of resources” – the term “robbing” in the context of plant-insect interactions, especially involving flowers, may be confused for nectar robbing. >We rephrased to change “rob” to “reduce” • Paragraph from line 73-85: in this paragraph introducing types of herbivory that can affect pollination, you talk about complete florivory, but not partial florivory – even though later you say partial florivory was more often studies. >We now also introduce partial florivory in this paragraph. • Line 169-171: You say that partial florivory can affect pollination by changing flower symmetry, but that’s far from the only effect of partial florivory on floral display. Published research has demonstrated partial florivory can affect flower size, color, VOCs, lifespan, sex ratio, nectar production, defenses in flowers, etc. >While its true that these effects have been found, they are largely not tested within these studies. Therefore, since many of these effects are also caused by vegetative herbivory we simply mentioned partial florivory in this part of the introduction. • Line 309: This is a comma splice at the comma between “potential to impact pollinators” and “for instance patches” >Fixed. • Line 373: “directly comparing individual species” – species of what? Plants? Herbivores? Pollinators? >“Species of herbivores” was added for clarity. • Lines 438-439: This is a comma splice at the comma between “focal herbivores” and “those that looked” >Fixed. Experimental design My comments on the design of the previous version were mostly addressed. My only comments now are: • You spend a lot of time talking about complete florivory versus partial florivory, but when you give stats (e.g. line 245, Figure 5) you don’t separate them out. This might be useful for comparison, especially since (as you point out) most florivory studies focus on partial florivory. >We mention later on in the discussion that every study that examined florivory looked at partial florivory except one that also looked at complete florivory. We now mention it in the results as well. • I feel like I need to know a little more about your exclusion criteria, since there are a few citations I can think of that seem to measure direct effects of herbivory on pollination that aren’t included in your review. >More detail has been added to the methodology. Validity of the findings • The part of your title after the colon (theories, methods, and challenges) doesn’t really reflect your findings or your purpose. You don’t cover current theories about resource allocation, pollinator selection criteria, or other theoretical frameworks that might have an impact on this topic. Similarly, you don’t really go over the methods for studies that test these kinds of questions. Challenges are only obliquely addressed, by pointing out what kind of studies haven’t yet been attempted much. >The subheading has been removed. • Lines 298-301: You mentioned compensating for or shifting phenology in response to florivory, but there are also examples of species shifting mating system (i.e. from outcrossing to selfing in plants with mixed mating systems) that led to no overall reduction in reproductive output. >This method has now also been listed. • Paragraph 363-383: Another potential explanation for the limited effect of vegetative damage on floral traits etc is that plants preferentially allocate resources to reproduction (since it’s so important), including flowers, and may suffer in other ways instead. >This was meant to be included in the statement about vegetative herbivory being more heavily regulated by plant physiological responses near the end of this paragraph. We have made this clearer. • You summarize your main findings at the end of the paper twice, in the paragraph beginning at line 448 and in the Conclusions section. Consider combining them into one conclusion section instead. >Done. Comments for the Author The authors’ revisions have, in my opinion, significantly improved this manuscript from the previous version. In particular, they added a lot more information overviewing previous findings on the topic in the discussion section, which lends itself much more to a review. However, despite significant edits, the introduction section still feels disconnected from the rest of the paper, and a little jumbled. The discussion would benefit from subheadings to provide structure. Revising the introduction may require major revision, but all of the other suggestions I’ve made are intermediate to minor revisions.
paper_title_zh: "对植食性动物通过授粉对植物繁殖直接和间接影响的系统综述"
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。植物繁殖受植物-食草动物和植物-传粉者相互作用净结果的影响。尽管食草动物对植物繁殖的影响和传粉者对植物繁殖的影响都已得到广泛研究，但很少有研究将它们结合起来进行考察。
review_content_zh:
审稿人2（匿名）基本报告

1. 引言部分过长，略显混乱，且与论文其他部分的主题不太一致，因此感觉与论文其他部分脱节。例如，仅关于食草性的背景介绍就超过了一整页单倍行距的内容，这似乎过多，因为这不是本文的主要论点。我认为引言需要更加简洁，将相关材料移至讨论部分进行更深入的探讨，并删除不必要的材料。>我们已经缩减了引言部分，删除了一些冗余信息，并将原本不在那里的信息移至讨论部分。

2. 引言部分可能还需要重新结构和组织。你需要提供足够的背景信息，直接引出食草性通过影响传粉者访问从而影响植物适应性的主题，并逐步引出你撰写这篇综述的目的。>引言部分已经进行了大幅度的重新结构和缩减，使其逻辑更加流畅。

3. 相关地，有几处地方，尤其是在引言中，仍然在一个长段落中涵盖了多个主题，可能需要拆分。例如，引言中的第二段（从第50行开始）可以拆分为三个段落：第一个段落从第50行到第56行；第二个段落从第56行（以“最典型的是…”开头）到第67行；第三个段落从第67行（以“在这篇系统综述中…”开头）到结尾的第72行。>引言部分已经进行了大幅度的重新结构和缩减，并拆分了一些段落，如你所建议的。

4. 与第一版相比，本文在讨论部分的内容和组织上有显著改进。我特别喜欢讨论部分的第一段。然而，由于添加了如此多的材料，阅读时容易迷失在细节中。我建议添加小标题来拆分材料（例如“花食性对传粉的影响”和“营养器官食草性对传粉的影响”等）。>已添加小标题。

5. 第354行：“叶食性、根部损伤和茎部损伤被发现对几种花部特征以及传粉者访问和繁殖有负面影响。”你并没有真正深入探讨这些影响的具体内容。我更希望看到每种类型的营养器官损伤分别讨论，包括它们对花部特征、传粉和繁殖的一般影响。如果有足够的信息，它们可以各自成段。如果信息较少，它们可以在同一段落中作为独立的句子。>已添加几句话列出受影响的特征，但数据有限，无法深入探讨每一个。

6. 图3是一个很好的补充。然而，显示研究地点的红色圆点太小，我一开始甚至没看到，即使在彩色图中也是如此。 在灰度图中，它们完全消失了。>感谢您指出这一点，我们已经将点放大了7倍。我仍然对图4有疑问。它非常难以阅读，因为有太多细线连接小字体的名称，而且线条在文字后面使得名称更难辨认。尽管如此，与上一版本相比已有改进，至少（经过一些努力）我能分辨出每条线应该连接到哪个名称。>我们已经再次修改了这张图，相信现在阅读起来会容易得多。

较小的评论：
• 在引言的第一句（第50行）中，“植物的适应性由与其他物种互动的净结果决定。”——虽然与其他物种的互动确实部分决定了植物的适应性，但它们并不是唯一影响植物适应性的因素。例如，资源可用性或非生物因素。>您当然是对的，这并不是一个排他性的陈述。我们通过添加“部分”来限定这一说法。
• 第44-46行：“两种物种之间的互动并不代表关系的净结果”——这些通常被称为非加性效应。>已添加描述符“非加性”。
• 第75行：“剥夺植物的资源”——在植物-昆虫互动的背景下，尤其是涉及花朵时，“剥夺”一词可能会被误认为是花蜜剥夺。>我们重新措辞，将“剥夺”改为“减少”。
• 从第73行到第85段的段落：在这段介绍可能影响授粉的食草类型的段落中，你提到了完全食花，但没有提到部分食花——尽管后来你说部分食花更常被研究。>我们现在也在这一段落中介绍了部分食花。
• 第169-171行：你说部分食花可以通过改变花对称性来影响授粉，但这远非部分食花对花展示的唯一影响。已发表的研究表明，部分食花可以影响花的大小、颜色、挥发性有机化合物、寿命、性别比例、花蜜产量、花中的防御等。>虽然确实发现了这些效应，但它们在这些研究中大多未经过测试。因此，由于许多这些效应也由营养器官食草引起，我们仅在引言的这部分提到了部分食花。
• 第309行：在“影响授粉者的潜力”和“例如斑块”之间的逗号是一个逗号拼接。>已修复。
• 第373行：“直接比较个体物种”——什么物种？植物？食草动物？授粉者？>添加了“食草动物的物种”以明确。
• 第438-439行：在“焦点食草动物”和“那些看起来”之间的逗号是一个逗号拼接。>已修复。

实验设计
我对上一版本设计的评论大多得到了解决。我现在唯一的评论是：
• 你花了大量时间讨论完全食花与部分食花，但在给出统计数据时（例如第245行，图5），你没有将它们分开。 这可能对比较有用，特别是（如您所指出的）大多数花食性研究都集中在部分花食性上。>我们在讨论的后面提到，每一项研究花食性的研究都考察了部分花食性，除了一项也考察了完全花食性的研究。我们现在也在结果部分提到了这一点。• 我觉得我需要更多地了解你们的排除标准，因为我能想到一些引用，似乎测量了植食性对授粉的直接影响，但并未包含在你们的综述中。>方法部分已增加更多细节。发现的有效性• 你们标题中冒号后的部分（理论、方法和挑战）并没有真正反映你们的发现或目的。你们没有涵盖关于资源分配、传粉者选择标准或其他可能对这一主题有影响的理论框架的当前理论。同样，你们也没有真正概述测试这类问题的研究方法。挑战只是间接地通过指出哪些类型的研究尚未大量尝试来提及。>已删除副标题。• 第298-301行：你们提到了为应对花食性而补偿或改变物候，但也有一些物种改变交配系统（例如，从异交到自交的混合交配系统植物）的例子，这并未导致总体繁殖输出的减少。>现在也已列出这种方法。• 第363-383段：对叶部损伤对花部特征等有限影响的另一个潜在解释是，植物优先将资源分配给繁殖（因为这非常重要），包括花朵，并可能以其他方式受损。>这原本应包含在段落末尾关于叶部植食性受植物生理反应更强烈调控的陈述中。我们已将其表述得更清楚。• 你们在论文末尾两次总结了你们的主要发现，一次是从第448行开始的段落，一次是在结论部分。考虑将它们合并为一个结论部分。>已完成。对作者的评论在我看来，作者的修订显著改善了这篇手稿，相较于之前的版本。特别是，他们在讨论部分增加了很多概述该主题先前发现的信息，这更有助于综述。然而，尽管进行了大量编辑，引言部分仍然感觉与论文其他部分脱节，且有些混乱。讨论部分将受益于副标题以提供结构。修订引言可能需要重大修改，但我提出的所有其他建议都是中等至轻微的修订。

paper_title: A literature survey on healthcare supply chain management
paper_abstract: Supply Chain Management (SCM) is a practice that has rapidly spread across industries. SCM may boost output while simultaneously satisfying customers. Despite SCM's recognition as a key factor in enhancing healthcare efficiency, widespread adoption remains in its infancy. Hospitals, a crucial element of the healthcare supply chain (HSC), have failed to fulfill the primary goals of lowering costs and providing high-quality treatment due to their inadequate knowledge of supply chain management (SCM). This research was conducted to fill in the blanks in the current HSC literature. Achieving the healthcare supply chain's goal of reducing costs will be greatly aided by the thorough literature study completed for this report. This review of healthcare supply chain management can quantify the benefits of supply chain initiatives and identify opportunities for improvement. Healthcare institutions can make informed decisions on optimizing their supply chains by understanding customer and supplier needs. This includes making strategic decisions on how to improve inventory management, streamline processes and reduce costs. The focus of this study is on the relationship between supply chain practices, the efficiency of supply chain performance, and the financial outcomes for healthcare organizations. By highlighting certain key research issues that are shared by supply chain management and healthcare management, this article contributes to the literature in both areas.
review_content:
The authors proposed a review paper on healthcare supply chain management. The topic is too general. The contributions of this review paper are not clear.

Most importantly, after reading the abstract and the introduction, I was unable to see the period of the review. What is the review period? The authors must compare the contributions of this research with existing review papers in this field.

It appears that several important papers in the area of healthcare supply chain management may not have been considered by the authors. I would like to suggest that they review the works of Prof. Fathollahi-Fard, Prof. Hajiaghaei-Keshteli, and Prof. Paydar, among others, to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the field
This review paper could benefit from further development and refinement.. No analysis is done on the authors, countries, journals, and so on.

This review paper does not provide some conceptual and theoretical models and methods for healthcare supply chain management.
paper_title_zh: 医疗供应链管理文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 供应链管理（SCM）是一种迅速在各行业中普及的实践。SCM可以在提高产出的同时满足客户需求。尽管SCM被公认为提升医疗保健效率的关键因素，但其广泛应用仍处于起步阶段。作为医疗供应链（HSC）的重要组成部分，医院由于对供应链管理（SCM）的理解不足，未能实现降低成本和提供高质量治疗的主要目标。本研究旨在填补当前HSC文献中的空白。为实现医疗供应链降低成本的目标，本报告所完成的全面文献研究将提供极大帮助。这一医疗供应链管理的综述可以量化供应链举措的益处，并识别改进机会。通过了解客户和供应商的需求，医疗机构可以做出优化其供应链的明智决策。这包括在如何改进库存管理、简化流程和降低成本方面做出战略决策。本研究的重点在于供应链实践、供应链绩效效率与医疗组织财务成果之间的关系。通过突出供应链管理和医疗管理共同关注的某些关键研究问题，本文为这两个领域的文献做出了贡献。
review_content_zh:
作者提出了一篇关于医疗供应链管理的综述论文。主题过于宽泛。这篇综述论文的贡献不明确。

最重要的是，在阅读了摘要和引言后，我无法看到综述的时间范围。综述的时间段是什么？作者必须将这项研究的贡献与该领域现有的综述论文进行比较。

paper_title: COVID-19, Cation Dysmetabolism, Sialic Acid, CD147, ACE2, Viroporins, Hepcidin and Ferroptosis: A Possible Unifying Hypothesis
paper_abstract:
Background: iron and calcium dysmetabolism, with hyperferritinemia, hypoferremia, hypocalcemia and anemia have been documented in the majority of COVID-19 patients at later/worse stages. Furthermore, complementary to ACE2, both sialic acid (SA) molecules and CD147 proved relevant host receptors for SARS-CoV-2 entry, which explains the viral attack to multiple types of cells, including erythrocytes, endothelium and neural tissue. Several authors advocated that cell ferroptosis may be the core and final cell degenerative mechanism. 
 Methods : a literature research was performed in several scientific search engines, such as PubMed Central, Cochrane Library, Chemical Abstract Service. More than 500 articles were retrieved until mid-December 2021, to highlight the available evidence about the investigated issues. 
 Results : based on COVID-19 literature data, we have highlighted a few pathophysiological mechanisms, associated with virus-based cation dysmetabolism, multi-organ attack, mitochondria degeneration and ferroptosis. Our suggested elucidated pathological sequence is: a) spike protein subunit S1 docking with sialylated membrane glycoproteins/receptors (ACE2, CD147), and S2 subunit fusion with the lipid layer; b) cell membrane morpho-functional changes due to the consequent electro-chemical variations and viroporin action, which induce an altered ion channel function and intracellular cation accumulation; c) additional intracellular iron concentration due to a deregulated hepcidin-ferroportin axis, with higher hepcidin levels. Viral invasion may also affect erythrocytes/erythroid precursors, endothelial cells and macrophages, through SA and CD147 receptors, with relative hemoglobin and iron/calcium dysmetabolism. AB0 blood group, hemochromatosis, or environmental elements may represent possible factors which affect individual susceptibility to COVID-19.     
 Conclusions : our literature analysis confirms the combined role of SA molecules, ACE2, CD147, viroporins and hepcidin in determining the cation dysmetabolism and final ferroptosis in the cells infected by SARS-CoV-2. The altered ion channels and electrochemical gradients of the cell membrane have a pivotal role in the virus entry and cell dysmetabolism, with subsequent multi-organ immune-inflammatory degeneration and erythrocyte/hemoglobin alterations.
review_content:
Based on the literature background a possible unifying hypothesis related COVID-19 to cation dysmetabolism, sialic acid, cd147, ACE2, viroporins, hepcidin, and ferroptosis were presented. It indicates three main receptors and their role in the spike docking approach and virus fusion. Further, the role of hepcidin in the accumulation of intracellular ferritin and blocking iron transport then activation of the voltage-dependent cation channels, and the action of viroporins, resulting in oscillations is discussed. The possible ferroptosis consequences were shown.

The presented hypothesis seems to be reasonable and certainly, it has a valuable unifying role. Regarding medical practice, I think that in the future it will be necessary and interesting to relate this hypothesis to the covid cytokine storm, by a mathematical kinetic model. As some diagnostic advantage one may consider measurements of artery-vein electromotive force oscillations in normal and covid patients.

I am sure that this a very good paper worth to be indexed as fast as possible with no major revision.

paper_title_zh: COVID-19、阳离子代谢紊乱、唾液酸、CD147、ACE2、病毒孔蛋白、肝素和铁死亡：一个可能的统一假说
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：在大多数晚期/重症COVID-19患者中，已记录到铁和钙代谢紊乱，表现为高铁蛋白血症、低铁血症、低钙血症和贫血。此外，除了ACE2外，唾液酸（SA）分子和CD147也被证明是SARS-CoV-2进入宿主细胞的相关受体，这解释了病毒对包括红细胞、内皮和神经组织在内的多种类型细胞的攻击。一些作者主张细胞铁死亡可能是核心和最终的细胞退变机制。

方法：在多个科学搜索引擎（如PubMed Central、Cochrane Library、化学文摘服务）进行了文献研究。截至2021年12月中旬，检索到500多篇相关文章，以突出所研究问题的现有证据。

结果：基于COVID-19的文献数据，我们突出了几种与病毒引起的阳离子代谢紊乱、多器官攻击、线粒体退变和铁死亡相关的病理生理机制。我们提出的病理序列为：a）S1刺突蛋白亚基与唾液酸化的膜糖蛋白/受体（ACE2、CD147）结合，S2亚基与脂质层融合；b）由于随后的电化学变化和病毒孔蛋白作用导致的细胞膜形态功能变化，诱导离子通道功能改变和细胞内阳离子积累；c）由于肝细胞素-铁转运蛋白轴失调导致细胞内铁浓度进一步增加，肝细胞素水平升高。病毒入侵还可能通过SA和CD147受体影响红细胞/红系前体细胞、内皮细胞和巨噬细胞，导致相应的血红蛋白和铁/钙代谢紊乱。AB0血型、血色病或环境因素可能是影响个体对COVID-19易感性的可能因素。

结论：我们的文献分析证实了SA分子、ACE2、CD147、病毒孔蛋白和肝细胞素在决定SARS-CoV-2感染细胞中阳离子代谢紊乱和最终铁死亡中的联合作用。细胞膜上改变的离子通道和电化学梯度在病毒进入和细胞代谢紊乱中起关键作用，随后导致多器官免疫炎症退变和红细胞/血红蛋白改变。
review_content_zh:
基于文献背景，提出了一个将COVID-19与阳离子代谢紊乱、唾液酸、CD147、ACE2、病毒孔蛋白、肝素和铁死亡相关联的统一假设。该假设指出了三种主要受体及其在刺突蛋白停靠和病毒融合中的作用。此外，还讨论了肝素在细胞内铁蛋白积累和阻断铁运输中的作用，进而激活电压依赖性阳离子通道，以及病毒孔蛋白的作用，导致振荡现象。展示了可能的铁死亡后果。

所提出的假设似乎合理，并且无疑具有宝贵的统一作用。关于医疗实践，我认为未来有必要且有趣地将这一假设与COVID细胞因子风暴相关联，通过数学动力学模型进行研究。作为一种诊断优势，可以考虑测量正常和COVID患者动静脉电动势振荡。
