paper_title: Neural Graph Reasoning: A Survey on Complex Logical Query Answering
paper_abstract: Complex logical query answering (CLQA) is a recently emerged task of graph machine learning that goes beyond simple one-hop link prediction and solves the far more complex task of multi-hop logical reasoning over massive, potentially incomplete graphs. The task received significant traction in the community; numerous works expanded the field along theoretical and practical axes to tackle different types of complex queries and graph modalities with efficient systems. In this paper, we provide a holistic survey of CLQA with a detailed taxonomy studying the field from multiple angles, including graph types (modality, reasoning domain, background semantics), modeling aspects (encoder, processor, decoder), supported queries (operators, patterns, projected variables), datasets, evaluation metrics, and applications. Finally, we point out promising directions, unsolved problems and applications of CLQA for future research.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper surveys recent work on neural methods for complex query answering. It captures the main aspects of (i) graph / data models, (ii) neural query processing, (iii) query types, (iv) evaluation. Generally, the survey is comprehensive and fills a gap in the literature. I feel that such a survey is a valueable contribution to TMLR, and I'd ultimately would like to see it accepted. At present, however, I feel that the survey needs revision in two key directions: (W1) presentation and (W2) discussion.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
I'll briefly state the strengths/weaknesses of this survey, and will then focus more on areas that I feel require work. S1. Comprehensive: captures the quite large amount of recent work in this area S2. Timely: this is a highly active reserach field at the moment S3. In need: there is no such survey, as far as I know S4. Useful taxonomy S5. Many useful overview tables W1. Presentation: let down by suboptimal structure/focus and, partly, lack of intuition W2. Discussion: rarely provides thoughtful discussion or criticism W3. Related areas ignored On W1. There are three main issues with the presentation. (i) The survey lacks focus. Most notably, there is a more than 15-page long disucssion on preliminaries, which is largely not needed (and especially in this level of formality) for the later chapters. In contrast, the discussion of the key techniques (Ch. 5) and training (Ch. 7.3) falls short. The amount of space allocated to a topic should match its relevance for this survey. (ii) The structure of the presentation is not optimal. The presentation is strictly sequential (first all kinds of graph models, then all kinds of neural models, then all kinds of query models, then training/evaluation). While this may make sense at first glance, this makes the survey quite painful to read and quite repetitive. For example, when discussing neural methods in Ch. 5, the dicussion is very hard to follow without some of the notions introduced in Ch. 6 (e.g., that the models represent partial query results as embeddings). I feel that the discussion makes sense when the key points are already known, but it otherwise quite inaccessible. I feel that Ch. 2 can mostly go and Ch. 4--7 need to be more tightly integrated (and hence rewritten). It may help to start with plain KGs + tree-graphs and then expand from there, for example, or to start off with a much higher-level discussion of the key points for neural query processing before delving into details (e.g., in a new overview chapter with forward pointers). (iii) Intuition party lacking. The paper quite often describes what is done, but does not convery the intuition behind the approaches or why certain things are done in certain ways. Although this is often clear to me (as I know some of the literature), it is not cleary exposed in the paper. As a simple example: why are relations translated by addition? Why does Query2Box use boxes and what do these boxes represent? On W2. Many of the methods are presented in a descriptive style, but there is little comparitive discussion and little criticism and unclear takeways. After reading the survey, one wonders how all the methods compare to each other, what their respective strengths and weaknesses are, and where the general limitations lie. I understand that this is immensely difficult to do, but I do feel that a survey should strive for at least some insightful dicussion or identify limitations. On W3. This work is related to KGQA (knowledge graph question answering, in particular, textual queries/features) and link prediction (single-hop queries). Many of the issues raised in this work also appear in these related areas (e.g., handling unseen entities or textual features such as entity names/descriptions). It's clear that this survey does (and needs to) focus on CQA, but it still should work out connections to these related lines of work. Detailed comments: D1. In principle, single-hop and rule-based methods can be used to "complete" the graph and perform CQA then. Clearly, this is limited but should be mentioned / related to CQA. D2. The description of graphs is overly formal. That's not at all needed for the purpose of this survey. D3. Hyper-Relational KGs and Hypergraph KGs are quite esoteric, as the tables of works that use them given in the survey also show. They have way too much focus in the presentation. (Also, I wonder about the concept of a "main relation" instead of simply using k-ary relations.) D4. I suggest to always present intuition/high-level ideas before the details. E.g., for Def 2.7., first say that a query is a positive pattern and a negative pattern, then give the definition. D5. Var_Q as defined on p. 7 does not contain the variables in the relation slots. D6. The discusson of query expressiveness/types is scattered throughout chapter 2, but then also arises later on again. I feel that it would help to define the noteion of a query answer (exact, approximate) ONCE and generally; right now it's defined multiple times (e.g., Def 2.9 and 2.17) and answer and query types are mingled together. D7. The answer semantics seems to use the CWA assumption, but it's not mentioend discussed. This matter in particular since the assumption is then broken later on. D8. The query processing problem is not really well defined. Especially, G and Ghat clearly need to be related in some way. This is even more relevant when queries have negations, since Ghat can invalidate any query result on G. D9. There is no diucssion around why approximate methods procude scores. Also, some methods may not; e.g., certain generative methods, and the practical implications of this choice ar not discussed. (It's clear that this is how the methods currently work, but a survey should provide context and point out potential limitations.) D10. The mix of query languages (SPARQL, FOL, relation projections later on) is quite confusing. D11. Approximate query answering raises all kind of questions around semantics and consistency. I think a key point is that there is often no well-defined semantics and answers can be inconsistent across queries, the methods just procude scores along Def. 2.17. This is very different to, say, probabilistic databases. D12. The t-norm discusison is only used once much later, and would be better placed there. D13. Multi-modal QA has been addressed in, say, the NLP and CV communities. It's weird that this field is empty in Tab. 2. D14. TAb 2/3/4 do not feel particularly insightful, as few methods actually do this. The discussion around these tables feels more like a side note, but is placed very prominently before the actual neural methods are discussed. I'd prefer a survey that puts key points first and potential extensions/directions later. D15. Fig 11: use subfigures, the boxes are hard to spot. D16. The difference between "shallow embedding" and "transductive encoder" is unclear to me. D17. Generally, it does not become sufficently clear in Fig. 11/Sec. 5.1 what the output of the encoder actually is (or can be). This relates to point W1(ii). D18. Tables like Tab 5 are hard to read. I'd find it more insightful if rows were methods and columns properties. This way, multiple tables (e.g., Tab 5 and Tab 6) could be integrated and provide a more holistic overview of the considered methods. D19. More generaelly, the methods are often mentioned "in passing", but there is no accessible general overview. D20. Downside (1) of shallow methods is unclear to me. D21. The distinction between neural and neural-symbolic processors is not clear to me. D22. Tables on top, not in text, improve readability. D23. The survey argues that union and negation are not well-defiend in latent space, hence many methods only support relation projection and intersection. But are those well-defined in latent space? How? D24. Fig 12 (esp. left) is confusing and not sufficiently discussed in text. D25. When talking about neural processors, relation projection and, say, conversion to DNF have not been discussed yet, but are already used throughout. This is an example of suboptimal structure. D26. Tab 7, DistMult-m/ComplEx-m -- relation projection correct? (L2Norm would destroy the embedding and produce a single real) D27. In Tab 7, cklickable refs + conference would be helpful. D28. Before discussion geometric/probaiblistic processors, the notion of representing possible values of a variable needs to be present, but that's (again) discussed only later. D29. Unclear to me: "probabilitic processors are similar to geometric processors" D30. Ch. 5.3 uses the word "non-parametric" in a non-standard fashion. What is meant is "learned/pre-defined" instead of "paramteric/non-parameteric". D31. At the end of Ch. 5, I wondered: so what? There is no discussion about the expressibity/quality/cost of these methods. D32. For discustions, the theorem of Ren et al should be paraphrased to be self-contained. Also, what is M? (Defined in Ren et al., but not here.) D33. Footnote 7 is incomplete. D34. In principle, regular path queries (i.e., a single relation type) can be handled by all methods by adding a relation R+ for the transitive closure of R. D35. Fig 19 has the right level of detail/formalism required for query types. D36. It's stated that neural methods "assume that the underlying graph is incomplete and queries may have some missing answers". I am not sure I'd agree: It appears that quite some of these methods are trained with CWA, but have limited capacity and hence can generalize. D37. Fig 19/20/21 can be merged. D38. The common term for "zero projected variabels" is Boolean queries. Also, at least in principle, all other quries can be reduced to Boolean queries by "trying" all possible answers. D39. Ch. 7 introduces a new notation for answers. Why not use this before? D40. Training comes very hort, just a paragraph. Isn't there more to say? Are there differences in training methods other than loss (e.g., query sampling stategies, negative sampling) and what's the general cost? D41. Inductive (superset) / inductive (disjoint) is termed semi-inductive / fully-inductive in the literature. D42. Tab 15 is a useful overview of datasets. An overview like this for methods would be great (see comment D18). D43. Tab 16 appears incomplete. For example, there are methods to handle unseen entities in KGQA/single-hop methods. D44. The application section is disappointing. The methods are claerly not used so far. That's ok, but: why not? what's missing? D45. Likewise, the summary/conclusion falls short. It list mainly features that would be nice to have, but does not work out / ask to address key weaknesses of current methods.

Response: Thank you for the detailed comments. We uploaded a revision addressing the weaknesses and comments. In particular: We moved a significant portion of theory in Section 2 to the Appendix only keeping the most important definitions in the main part We added Appendix B linking a tangentially related KGQA in the NLP area. Generally, we deem KGQA as a different task in the different subfield where the queries are posed in the natural language and the graphs are assumed to be complete (no link prediction needed). Addressed a lot of your smaller comments, thanks for the suggestions In this survey, we strived for a general overview of CLQA theory, methods, and datasets without going into the details of each method – mostly due to the size concerns: the manuscript is already 50+ pages of content. Comments on issues not addressed by the changes mentioned above: D1. Addressed in the introduction D2 - D3. We moved a significant portion of Section 2 in the appendix. Indeed, there are not that many works on hypergraph KGs, but we believe that hyper-relational KGs are of higher importance - at least because (1) Wikidata uses this representation formalism with main facts and qualifiers; (2) the upcoming standards RDF-star and SPARQL-star will increase the adoption of hyper-relational KGs in industry D4/ D6 We moved much of the details to the appendix with the intention that the reader gets now less confused by them. Those interested can then still find them there. D5. This was a mistake indeed. $\texttt{Var}_Q = \gE' \cap \texttt{Var}$ should have been $\texttt{Var}_Q = ( \gE' \cup \gR' ) \cap \texttt{Var}$ instead. D7. This is a tricky point, indeed. The answer semantics are indeed according to a closed world assumption. In a way, we expect the system to take a graph with unknown parts, thus according to OWA, and coerce it into making a decision about the truthfulness of the unknown, in the context of the query, and then provide the answers. The query could also provide (or rather assert) information; it could include statements which are not in the knowledge graph. D8. We elaborate on visible (training) and complete graphs in Section 5.2 (Processors) D10. SPARQL is a standard query language for KGs and we used it more for mapping to practical cases. FOL, on the other hand, is more for the definitions and mathematic rigor. D15. Added more visual separation to the figure and caption, thanks for the suggestion. D16. Shallow encoders do not explicitly encode the graph structure and operate on directly on vectors corresponding to entities and relations. Technically, shallow encoders are a subset of transductive encoders but due to the sheer volume of related works we put them into a separate category. D17. The output for all CLQA methods is a scalar distribution over all entities that indicates the probability of an entity to be a correct answer (Section 5.3) D18/D42. We think it is more of a style preference. In the suggested way, you would get very sparse checkmarks as almost nothing belongs in multiple categories. D20. In simpler words, shallow methods need much longer time to encode the graph structure in the representations. In transductive encoders GNNs provide this inductive bias from the start. D25. DNF conversion has been introduced in the definitions section (prev. 2.4, now in the Appendix) D26. This refers to element-wise vector normalization using the L2 norm: $v_i / ||v|| $ D27. We cite these already in the text and in the other table. Adding these citations here again makes the table really crowded. We could make the names clickable and make them navigate to the relevant citations, but that worked rather confusingly. D29. Reworded in the paper
paper_title_zh: 神经图推理：复杂逻辑查询回答综述
paper_abstract_zh: 复杂逻辑查询回答（CLQA）是图机器学习领域新近出现的任务，它超越了简单的单跳链接预测，解决了在庞大且可能不完整的图上进行多跳逻辑推理的更为复杂的任务。该任务在社区中获得了显著的关注；众多研究沿着理论和实践轴线扩展了该领域，以高效系统应对不同类型的复杂查询和图模态。在本文中，我们提供了对CLQA的全面综述，并通过详细的分类法从多个角度研究该领域，包括图类型（模态、推理域、背景语义）、建模方面（编码器、处理器、解码器）、支持的查询（运算符、模式、投影变量）、数据集、评估指标和应用。最后，我们指出了CLQA未来研究的潜在方向、未解决的问题和应用。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文综述了近年来关于复杂查询回答的神经方法的研究工作。它涵盖了以下主要方面：（一）图/数据模型，（二）神经查询处理，（三）查询类型，（四）评估。总体而言，该综述全面且填补了文献中的空白。我认为这样的综述对TMLR是一个有价值的贡献，最终希望看到它被接受。然而，目前我认为该综述需要在两个关键方向上进行修订：（W1）呈现方式和（W2）讨论。

**优点和缺点：**
我将简要说明该综述的优缺点，然后重点讨论我认为需要改进的领域。S1. 全面：涵盖了该领域大量的近期工作 S2. 及时：目前这是一个非常活跃的研究领域 S3. 需要：据我所知，目前还没有这样的综述 S4. 有用的分类法 S5. 许多有用的概述表格 W1. 呈现方式：由于次优的结构/焦点和部分缺乏直觉而受到影响 W2. 讨论：很少提供深思熟虑的讨论或批评 W3. 忽略了相关领域 关于W1。呈现方式存在三个主要问题。（一）综述缺乏焦点。最明显的是，有一个超过15页的预备知识讨论，这在后续章节中 largely 不需要（尤其是这种形式化程度）。相比之下，关键技术的讨论（第5章）和训练（第7.3章）显得不足。分配给某一主题的空间应与其对综述的相关性相匹配。（二）呈现结构不理想。呈现方式严格按顺序进行（先讨论所有类型的图模型，然后是所有类型的神经模型，接着是所有类型的查询模型，最后是训练/评估）。虽然乍一看这可能是有意义的，但这使得综述读起来非常痛苦且重复性很高。例如，在第5章讨论神经方法时，如果没有第6章中介绍的一些概念（例如，模型将部分查询结果表示为嵌入），讨论就非常难以理解。我认为在已知关键点的情况下讨论是有意义的，但否则相当难以理解。我认为第2章可以大部分删除，第4-7章需要更紧密地整合（因此需要重写）。例如，可以从简单的知识图谱+树图开始，然后逐步扩展，或者先从更高层次讨论神经查询处理的关键点，然后再深入细节（例如，在带有前向指针的新概述章节中）。（三）直觉部分缺失。论文经常描述所做的工作，但没有传达方法背后的直觉或为什么某些事情以特定方式完成。虽然这些对我来说通常很清楚（因为我了解一些文献），但在论文中并没有清晰地展现出来。举一个简单的例子：为什么关系通过加法进行转换？ 为什么Query2Box使用盒子，这些盒子代表什么？在W2中，许多方法以描述性风格呈现，但缺乏比较性讨论、批评以及不清晰的结论。阅读完这篇综述后，人们会想知道所有方法之间的比较情况，它们各自的优缺点以及普遍的局限性在哪里。我理解这非常难以做到，但我确实认为一篇综述至少应该努力提供一些有洞察力的讨论或指出局限性。在W3中，这项工作与KGQA（知识图谱问答，特别是文本查询/特征）和链接预测（单跳查询）相关。这项工作中提出的许多问题也出现在这些相关领域（例如，处理未见实体或文本特征如实体名称/描述）。显然，这篇综述确实（并且需要）专注于CQA，但它仍然应该梳理与这些相关工作之间的联系。详细评论：D1.原则上，单跳和基于规则的方法可以用来“完成”图谱，然后进行CQA。显然，这是有限的，但应该提及/与CQA相关联。D2.图谱的描述过于形式化。这对于这篇综述的目的来说完全不需要。D3.超关系知识图谱和超图知识图谱相当晦涩，正如综述中给出的使用它们的表格所显示的。它们在呈现中占据了过多的关注。（此外，我对“主关系”的概念而不是简单地使用k元关系感到疑惑。）D4.我建议在细节之前总是先呈现直觉/高层次想法。例如，对于定义2.7，首先说明查询是一个正模式和一个负模式，然后给出定义。D5.在第7页定义的Var_Q不包含关系槽中的变量。D6.关于查询表达能力/类型的讨论散布在第2章中，但后来又再次出现。我觉得一次性定义查询答案（精确、近似）的概念会有帮助；目前它被多次定义（例如，定义2.9和2.17），答案和查询类型混在一起。D7.答案语义似乎使用了CWA假设，但未提及讨论。这一点尤为重要，因为该假设在后面被打破了。D8.查询处理问题并未真正明确定义。特别是，G和Ghat显然需要以某种方式相关联。当查询包含否定时，这一点更为重要，因为Ghat可以使G上的任何查询结果无效。D9.没有讨论为什么近似方法会产生分数。此外，某些方法可能不会；例如，某些生成方法，以及这种选择的实际影响未讨论。（显然，这是当前方法的工作方式，但一篇综述应该提供背景并指出潜在的局限性。）D10. 查询语言（SPARQL、FOL、后续的关系投影）的混合相当令人困惑。D11. 近似查询回答引发了关于语义和一致性的各种问题。我认为一个关键点是，通常没有明确定义的语义，答案在不同查询之间可能不一致，方法只是根据定义2.17产生分数。这与概率数据库非常不同。D12. t-范数的讨论只在后面使用了一次，最好放在那里。D13. 多模态QA已经在NLP和CV社区中得到解决。奇怪的是，表2中这一领域是空的。D14. 表2/3/4并没有特别有见地，因为很少有方法实际这样做。围绕这些表格的讨论更像是一个旁注，但放在实际讨论神经方法之前非常显眼。我更倾向于先列出关键点，然后再讨论潜在的扩展/方向。D15. 图11：使用子图，盒子很难找到。D16. “浅层嵌入”和“归纳编码器”之间的区别对我来说不清楚。D17. 通常，图11/第5.1节中并不清楚编码器的输出实际上是什么（或可能是什么）。这与W1(ii)点相关。D18. 像 表5 这样的表格很难阅读。如果行是方法，列是属性，我会觉得更有见地。这样，多个表格（例如，表5和表6）可以整合，提供对所考虑方法的更全面概述。D19. 更普遍地说，方法经常是“顺便提及”，但没有可访问的总体概述。D20. 浅层方法的缺点（1）对我来说不清楚。D21. 神经处理器和神经符号处理器之间的区别对我来说不清楚。D22. 表格放在顶部，不在文本中，提高可读性。D23. 调查认为并集和否定在潜在空间中定义不明确，因此许多方法只支持关系投影和交集。但它们在潜在空间中定义明确吗？如何定义？D24. 图12（尤其是左侧）令人困惑，文本中讨论不足。D25. 在讨论神经处理器时，关系投影和，比如说，转换为DNF尚未讨论，但已经到处使用。这是结构不优的一个例子。D26. 表7，DistMult-m/ComplEx-m -- 关系投影正确吗？（L2范数会破坏嵌入并产生一个实数）D27. 在表7中，可点击的引用+会议会有帮助。D28. 在讨论几何/概率处理器之前，需要先介绍表示变量可能值的观念，但那（再次）只在后面讨论。D29. 对我不清楚：“概率处理器类似于几何处理器”。D30. 第5.3节使用“非参数”一词的方式非标准。其意思是指“学习到的/预定义的”，而不是“参数/非参数”。D31. 在第5章末尾，我感到疑惑：那又怎样？ 对这些方法的表达能力/质量/成本没有讨论。D32. 对于讨论部分，Ren等人的定理应进行改写以使其自包含。另外，M是什么？（在Ren等人的论文中定义，但此处未定义。）D33. 脚注7不完整。D34. 原则上，正则路径查询（即单一关系类型）可以通过所有方法处理，只需添加一个关系R+来表示R的传递闭包。D35. 图19具有查询类型所需的适当详细程度/形式化水平。D36. 文中提到神经方法“假设底层图是不完整的，查询可能有一些缺失的答案”。我不太同意：似乎相当多这些方法是用CWA训练的，但容量有限，因此可以泛化。D37. 图19/20/21可以合并。D38. “零投影变量”的常用术语是布尔查询。此外，原则上，所有其他查询都可以通过“尝试”所有可能的答案来简化为布尔查询。D39. 第7章引入了一种新的答案表示法。为什么之前不使用这种表示法？D40. 训练部分非常简短，仅有一段。难道没有更多内容可说吗？除了损失函数之外，训练方法还有其他差异吗（例如，查询采样策略，负采样）以及一般成本如何？D41. 文献中将归纳（超集）/归纳（不相交）称为半归纳/全归纳。D42. 表15是对数据集的有用概述。类似的方法概述将会很棒（参见评论D18）。D43. 表16似乎不完整。例如，有方法可以处理KGQA/单跳方法中的未见实体。D44. 应用部分令人失望。这些方法显然尚未被使用。这可以接受，但：为什么？缺少什么？D45. 同样，总结/结论部分也不够充分。它主要列出了一些希望具备的特性，但没有详细阐述/要求解决当前方法的关键弱点。

**请求的更改：**
在可行范围内解决W1；W2+W3

**主张和证据：**
是

**受众：**
是

**反驳评论：**
回复：感谢您的详细评论。我们上传了修订版，解决了弱点和评论。特别是：我们将第2节中的大量理论内容移至附录，仅在正文部分保留最重要的定义；我们添加了附录B，链接了NLP领域中一个相关但不直接相关的KGQA。总的来说，我们认为KGQA是不同子领域中的不同任务，其中查询是以自然语言提出的，图被认为是完整的（无需链接预测）。我们解决了很多您的小评论，感谢建议。在这篇综述中，我们力求对CLQA理论、方法和数据集进行一般性概述，而没有深入探讨每种方法的细节——主要是由于篇幅考虑：手稿已有50多页内容。对上述更改未涉及的问题的评论：D1. 在引言中已解决 D2 - D3. 我们将第2节的很大一部分移到了附录中。实际上，关于超图知识图谱（KGs）的研究并不多，但我们认为超关系知识图谱更为重要——至少因为（1）Wikidata使用这种表示形式来处理主要事实和限定词；（2）即将推出的标准RDF-star和SPARQL-star将增加超关系知识图谱在工业D4/D6中的应用。我们将许多细节移至附录，目的是让读者现在不会因它们而感到困惑。感兴趣的读者仍然可以在那里找到这些内容。D5. 这确实是一个错误。$\texttt{Var}_Q = \gE' \cap \texttt{Var}$ 应该是 $\texttt{Var}_Q = ( \gE' \cup \gR' ) \cap \texttt{Var}$。D7. 这确实是一个棘手的问题。答案语义确实基于封闭世界假设。在某种意义上，我们期望系统能够处理一个包含未知部分的图，根据开放世界假设（OWA），并在查询的上下文中强制其做出关于未知的真实性的决策，然后提供答案。查询也可以提供（或更确切地说是断言）信息；它可能包含知识图谱中不存在的陈述。D8. 我们在第5.2节（处理器）中详细讨论了可见（训练）图和完整图。D10. SPARQL是知识图谱的标准查询语言，我们更多地用它来映射实际案例。而一阶逻辑（FOL）则更多地用于定义和数学严谨性。D15. 根据建议，增加了图和标题的视觉分隔，谢谢建议。D16. 浅层编码器不显式编码图结构，而是直接在对应于实体和关系的向量上操作。从技术上讲，浅层编码器是归纳编码器的一个子集，但由于相关工作的数量庞大，我们将它们归为一个单独的类别。D17. 所有复杂问答（CLQA）方法的输出是一个对所有实体的标量分布，表示实体成为正确答案的概率（第5.3节）。D18/D42. 我们认为这更多是风格偏好问题。按照建议的方式，你会得到非常稀疏的勾选标记，因为几乎没有什么属于多个类别。D20. 简单地说，浅层方法需要更长的时间将图结构编码到表示中。在归纳编码器中，图神经网络（GNNs）从一开始就提供了这种归纳偏置。D25. DNF转换已在定义部分引入（之前是2.4节，现在在附录中）。D26. 这是指使用L2范数进行逐元素向量归一化：$v_i / ||v||$。D27. 我们已经在文本和另一个表格中引用了这些内容。在这里再次添加这些引用会使表格显得非常拥挤。我们可以使名称可点击并导航到相关引用，但这种方式容易造成混淆。D29. 已在论文中重新措辞。

reasons: It captures the main aspects of (i) graph / data models, (ii) neural query processing, (iii) query types, (iv) evaluation.
Generally, the survey is comprehensive and fills a gap in the literature.
This work is related to KGQA (knowledge graph question answering, in particular, textual queries/features) and link prediction (single-hop queries).
It's clear that this survey does (and needs to) focus on CQA, but it still should work out connections to these related lines of work.
Multi-modal QA has been addressed in, say, the NLP and CV communities.
It's weird that this field is empty in Tab. 2.
Tab 16 appears incomplete.
Many of the methods are presented in a descriptive style, but there is little comparitive discussion and little criticism and unclear takeways.
After reading the survey, one wonders how all the methods compare to each other, what their respective strengths and weaknesses are, and where the general limitations lie.
I understand that this is immensely difficult to do, but I do feel that a survey should strive for at least some insightful dicussion or identify limitations.
At the end of Ch. 5, I wondered: so what?
There is no discussion about the expressibity/quality/cost of these methods.
Most notably, there is a more than 15-page long disucssion on preliminaries, which is largely not needed (and especially in this level of formality) for the later chapters.
While this may make sense at first glance, this makes the survey quite painful to read and quite repetitive.

For example, when discussing neural methods in Ch. 5, the dicussion is very hard to follow without some of the notions introduced in Ch. 6 (e.g., that the models represent partial query results as embeddings).
I feel that the discussion makes sense when the key points are already known, but it otherwise quite inaccessible.
The paper quite often describes what is done, but does not convery the intuition behind the approaches or why certain things are done in certain ways.
Although this is often clear to me (as I know some of the literature), it is not cleary exposed in the paper.
The description of graphs is overly formal.
Tables like Tab 5 are hard to read.
Fig 11: use subfigures, the boxes are hard to spot.
Fig 12 (esp. left) is confusing and not sufficiently discussed in text.
Tables on top, not in text, improve readability.
The mix of query languages (SPARQL, FOL, relation projections later on) is quite confusing.
The structure of the presentation is not optimal.
The presentation is strictly sequential (first all kinds of graph models, then all kinds of neural models, then all kinds of query models, then training/evaluation).
I feel that Ch. 2 can mostly go and Ch. 4--7 need to be more tightly integrated (and hence rewritten).

It may help to start with plain KGs + tree-graphs and then expand from there, for example, or to start off with a much higher-level discussion of the key points for neural query processing before delving into details (e.g., in a new overview chapter with forward pointers).
The discusson of query expressiveness/types is scattered throughout chapter 2, but then also arises later on again.

I feel that it would help to define the noteion of a query answer (exact, approximate) ONCE and generally; right now it's defined multiple times (e.g., Def 2.9 and 2.17) and answer and query types are mingled together.
When talking about neural processors, relation projection and, say, conversion to DNF have not been discussed yet, but are already used throughout.
This is an example of suboptimal structure.
Ch. 7 introduces a new notation for answers.
Why not use this before?

paper_title: Dynamics of Zika virus outbreaks: an overview of a mathematical modeling approach
paper_abstract: Background. The Zika virus was first discovered in 1947. It was neglected until a major outbreak occurred on Yap Island, Micronesia, in 2007. Teratogenic effects resulting in microcephaly in newborn infants is the greatest public health threat. In 2016, the Zika virus epidemic was declared as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Consequently, mathematical models were constructed to explicitly elucidate related transmission dynamics.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (John Palmer) Basic reporting This literature review article provides a nice introduction to mathematical modeling in the context of Zika. The body of literature that it gathers and synthesizes provides a very useful starting point for anyone wishing to enter this area of research. That said, I think it needs to be improved significantly before it is ready to be published. 1. Much of the writing is difficult to follow and should be revised and closely edited. ### Response ### We have revised the manuscript. The manuscript has been edited by Elsevier Language Editing Services. 2. The literature is properly referenced in the text, but some important sources appear to be missing (for example Adams and Kapan. 2009. “Man Bites Mosquito: Understanding the Contribution of Human Movement to Vector-Borne Disease Dynamics.” Edited by Alison P. Galvani. PLoS ONE 4 (8).) ### Response ### We have included the recommended paper. The following sentences have been added on Page 14: “Another example is the contributions of the human mobility patterns and the subpopulation of mosquitoes to the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases (Adams & Kapan, 2009). The model suggested that the places people visit frequently but for a short amount of time are at risk for the spread of diseases. However, the distribution patterns of the mosquitoes and human movement characteristics are also important.” In addition, we have also added some other papers. 3. The structure is fine, although I recommend making it clearer in the beginning of the Abstract that this is a review article. ### Response ### Revised as suggested. We have re-titled the manuscript to “Dynamics of Zika Virus Outbreaks: An Overview of a Mathematical Modeling Approach”. We have also added “In this review article…” in the abstract. 4. I am also not sure the authors need to go into such detail about how they selected the articles -- or that they need to limit the literature to that found in this type of methodical survey. ### Response ### We were asked from the journal to declare our search criteria before proceeding to the revision step. So, we have to put this clarification. Experimental design This is not primary research but rather a literature review, summarizing and synthesizing existing work in this area. It appears to fall within the aims and scope of PeerJ. The research question is broad (essentially the article asks what has been done with respect to mathematical modeling relevant to Zika dynamics). It is not entirely clear that it fills a real knowledge gap, although it is surely helpful to have this body of literature synthesized. The methods in this case are the search criteria. They are clearly described, but I am not convinced that this type of formal survey is needed. I would opt for looser search criteria in order to ensure that all relevant literature has been located. For instance, there are probably important sources that do not contain the term "mathematical model" (even if that is what they provide). ### Response ### We were asked from the journal to declare our search criteria before proceeding to the revision step. So, we have to put this clarification. Indeed, we used some other few search teams but the results were not much different. We have added two other search terms; “dynamics” and “modeling”. A sentence on Page 6 now reads “In the first step, we used the search terms “dynamics,” “mathematical model,” “modeling,” and “vector-borne” together with the names of vector-borne diseases such as chikungunya, dengue, malaria, West Nile, and Zika.” We tried our best to cover all aspects. However, some important papers may be still missed. We tried to add some according to the reviewer’s suggestion. Validity of the findings The main conclusion is the summary of existing models. From this, the authors note that there has been a lack of application of these models in the field by health professionals, and they suggest some ways in which that might be changed. This is an interesting discussion, but the authors might expand on different ways in which this field implementation could occur, as well as different uses of simple versus complex models. ### Response ### Revised as suggested. We have added the following sentences to the last paragraph of the perspective section (Page 24): “To fully implement mathematical modeling, one must persuade policy makers to include the methods and try to prove that they are necessary. In this case, the translation of mathematical language into political contexts is crucial. Moreover, simple and complex models should be exploited differently. Simple models can be produced in a timely fashion to provide an estimation of the possible impacts. In contrast, complex models require more time to develop but are far more realistic. The models are much more powerful in terms of predictive capability. The preparation of complicated models before outbreaks is recommended.”
paper_title_zh: 寨卡病毒爆发的动力学：数学建模方法概览
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。寨卡病毒最早发现于1947年。直到2007年在密克罗尼西亚的雅浦岛上发生大规模爆发，该病毒才受到关注。其导致的胎儿小头畸形等致畸效应是最大的公共卫生威胁。2016年，寨卡病毒疫情被宣布为国际关注的公共卫生紧急事件（PHEIC）。随后，构建了数学模型以明确阐释相关的传播动力学。
review_content_zh:
### 审稿人2（John Palmer）的基本评价

这篇文献综述文章在寨卡病毒背景下对数学建模提供了良好的入门介绍。它所汇集和综合的文献为任何希望进入该研究领域的人提供了非常有用的起点。尽管如此，我认为在发表之前还需要进行显著的改进。

1. 许多写作内容难以理解，应进行修订和仔细编辑。### 回应 ### 我们已修订了手稿。手稿已由Elsevier语言编辑服务进行了编辑。

2. 文献在文本中得到了适当的引用，但似乎缺少了一些重要来源（例如Adams和Kapan. 2009. “Man Bites Mosquito: Understanding the Contribution of Human Movement to Vector-Borne Disease Dynamics.” 由Alison P. Galvani编辑。PLoS ONE 4 (8)）。### 回应 ### 我们已包括推荐的论文。在第14页添加了以下句子：“另一个例子是人类移动模式和蚊子亚群对虫媒传染病流行病学的影响（Adams & Kapan, 2009）。该模型表明，人们频繁但短暂访问的地方有疾病传播的风险。然而，蚊子的分布模式和人类移动特征也很重要。”此外，我们还添加了一些其他论文。

3. 结构尚可，尽管我建议在摘要开头更清楚地说明这是一篇综述文章。### 回应 ### 按建议进行了修订。我们将手稿重新命名为“寨卡病毒爆发的动态：数学建模方法概览”。我们还在摘要中添加了“在这篇综述文章中……”。

4. 我也不确定作者是否需要如此详细地描述他们选择文章的过程——或者他们是否需要将文献限制在这种系统调查中找到的范围内。### 回应 ### 杂志要求我们在进行修订步骤之前声明我们的搜索标准。因此，我们必须提供这一澄清。

### 实验设计

这不是一项原始研究，而是一篇文献综述，总结和综合了该领域的现有工作。它似乎符合PeerJ的目标和范围。研究问题较为广泛（本质上文章询问了在寨卡动态相关的数学建模方面已经做了哪些工作）。尚不清楚它是否填补了真正的知识空白，尽管将这批文献综合起来无疑是有帮助的。在这种情况下，方法就是搜索标准。它们描述得很清楚，但我不确定是否需要这种正式的调查。我会选择更宽松的搜索标准，以确保找到所有相关文献。例如，可能有一些重要来源不包含“数学模型”这一术语（即使它们提供了相关内容）。### 回应 ### 杂志要求我们在进行修订步骤之前声明我们的搜索标准。因此，我们必须提供这一澄清。事实上，我们使用了一些其他搜索术语，但结果差异不大。我们在第6页添加了两个其他搜索术语；“动态”和“建模”。现在该页的一句话读作：“在第一步中，我们使用了‘动态’、‘数学模型’、‘建模’和‘虫媒’等搜索术语，以及如基孔肯雅热、登革热、疟疾、西尼罗河和寨卡等虫媒疾病的名称。”我们尽力涵盖所有方面。然而，可能仍有一些重要论文被遗漏。我们根据审稿人的建议尝试添加了一些。

### 研究结果的可靠性

主要结论是对现有模型的总结。由此，作者指出这些模型在实地应用中存在不足，并建议了一些可能改进的方法。这是一个有趣的讨论，但作者可以进一步探讨实地实施的不同方式，以及简单模型与复杂模型的不同用途。### 回应 ### 按建议进行了修订。我们在展望部分最后一段（第24页）添加了以下句子：“要完全实施数学建模，必须说服政策制定者纳入这些方法，并证明其必要性。在这种情况下，将数学语言转化为政治背景至关重要。此外，简单和复杂模型应有所不同地利用。简单模型可以及时制作，以提供可能影响的估计。相比之下，复杂模型需要更多时间开发，但更为现实。这些模型在预测能力方面要强大得多。建议在疫情爆发前准备复杂的模型。”

reasons: The body of literature that it gathers and synthesizes provides a very useful starting point for anyone wishing to enter this area of research.

The literature is properly referenced in the text, but some important sources appear to be missing (for example Adams and Kapan. 2009. “Man Bites Mosquito: Understanding the Contribution of Human Movement to Vector-Borne Disease Dynamics.” Edited by Alison P. Galvani. PLoS ONE 4 (8).)
I would opt for looser search criteria in order to ensure that all relevant literature has been located.
It is not entirely clear that it fills a real knowledge gap, although it is surely helpful to have this body of literature synthesized.
The main conclusion is the summary of existing models.
This is an interesting discussion, but the authors might expand on different ways in which this field implementation could occur, as well as different uses of simple versus complex models.
Much of the writing is difficult to follow and should be revised and closely edited.
That said, I think it needs to be improved significantly before it is ready to be published.
The structure is fine, although I recommend making it clearer in the beginning of the Abstract that this is a review article.

paper_title: Manifestations of muscle fatigue in baseball pitchers: a systematic review
paper_abstract: Background. Fatigue in baseball pitchers is a process linked to lowered physical and mental performance, injury, and changes in kinematics. Numerous studies have associated fatigue with overuse, high ball velocities, lack of rest time, poor mechanics, and degree of self-satisfaction. The aim of this study was to systematically review the literature to identify a theoretical framework for the relationship between outcomes and the manifestation of fatigue on baseball pitching. The synthesized data may identify areas requiring further research. Methodology. This protocol was registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD42018114194). SPORTDiscus, Medline, PubMed, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Google Scholar were searched, using keywords such as fatigue in pitchers and changes in kinematics (e.g. pitching mechanics, valgus elbow torque), performance (e.g. pitch count, pitch type), and injury (e.g. pain, elbow and shoulder soreness). Three reviewers independently screened the articles, selected relevant literature based on abstract eligibility, and assessed the methods described therein for final inclusion.
review_content: Reviewer 1 (Anonymous) Basic reporting Reporting can be improved to make sure this review meets the standard expected of systematic reviews, based on the PRISMA guidelines, i.e. introduction should be more concise, methods and results should include risk of bias assessment, justify weighted average approach to data synthesis, ensure flow chart numbers are correct, provide a table with study characteristics for all included studies, avoid duplication of information in tables and text, ensure information in the discussion is consistent with the results. Please see General Comments section for specific details and strategies to address these issues. We would like to thank the reviewer for providing a detailed and insightful review of our work. These suggestions have greatly improved our manuscript and the quality of the work. In an attempt to clearly summarize the changes, many of the comments listed above have been addressed in the general comments below. However, we will summarize some of the major points here: 1. We have significantly improved the rigor of our review and have clarified in numerous places how we have met the standards of systematic reviews based on the PRISMA guideline. We feel that our review meets the standards, however, we needed to do a better job of identifying our process in the manuscript. This should now be much clearer in the methods section. Lines 145-181. 2. Our introduction is now more concise and directed (we removed over 100 words). 3. We have included a full section on methodology quality assessment (lines 154-166). This includes a new table (table 1) with a Downs and Black 1998 quality assessment. 4. We have also included a risk bias assessment (lines 168-181) and a new table (table 2) that following the work of Lopes et al. 2012. 5. All of our included papers were divided up into 3 categories (kinematics, performance and injury). Each paper and the findings specific to that category is listed in tables 3, 4 and 5. Along with some additional information on each study. 6. We have double checked our flow chart numbers, improved the image, and have removed any duplication from the results (text and tables). 7. Despite adding a methodological quality and bias assessment section to the results section, we have still removed almost 700 words. This reflects our approach to remove duplicate information from text and tables. Experimental design The major concerns with the design are the lack of risk of bias assessment and inclusion of non-pitcher based studies (i.e. swimmers, volleyball, tennis players). These other sports were included in the search methodology but then they are not mentioned in the results and discussion, so it is unclear how they have been integrated. I strongly suggest removing these studies from the eligibility criteria and results. Please see General Comments section for specific details and strategies to address these issues. We agree with the reviewer and have removed all mention of non-pitcher-based studies. Our initial thought process was to include all athletes with a “throwing” motion, or “arm swing” motion to gain a comprehensive list. However, our search criteria and eligibility criteria meant that we ended up with pitcher related articles. Thus, we have went back and revised our search metrics (flow chart) to reflect this change. Only 1 article was removed. We have spent considerable time including a methodological quality and risk bias assessment component to our work. We have included a full section on methodology quality assessment (line 154-166). This includes a new table (table 1) with a Downs and Black 1998 quality assessment. We have also included a risk bias assessment (lines 168-181) and a new table (table 2) that following the work of Lopes et al. 2012. Validity of the findings The authors offer interesting insights based on the findings of their review, but greater care needs to be taken to clearly identify when there is and is not strong evidence to support their claims. It is important to know when evidence is weak or non-existent because it provides direction for future research. Please see General Comments section for specific details and strategies to address these issues. We have spent time looking through the original classification of all our included articles. We had 3 prospective/longitudinal studies, 3 randomized crossover studies, 2 retrospective, 1 epidemiological, 1 cross-sectional. The bulk of our included articles (15) were descriptive/controlled laboratory studies. Given that the bulk of our included work had very similar study designs and no meta-analysis or RCT’s were included, we decided to treat all of this work equally. Granted, we acknowledge that our included longitudinal and epidemiological studies provide evidence via surveys, we use those to support the work of our laboratory/biomechanical studies throughout the manuscript. Comments for the Author The authors have chosen an interesting topic to review and I congratulate them on the effort involved in screening 31,860 abstracts. I think this manuscript needs to be improved for publication and I have provided the following specific feedback for the authors that I hope they will find useful. Thank you once again for the very helpful comments that will certainly improve this work. ABSTRACT “is a primary reason for injury in baseball pitchers” – too strong a conclusion based on the evidence you have collated We certainly agree that our work should not conclude or infer that fatigue is the “primary” reason for injury in baseball. On lines 40-41: we have changed to the following: “is a contributing factor of injury in baseball pitchers”. However, as evident from some of the literature (cited below), we are of the opinion that fatigue is certainly a big contributor to this issue. In a review by Bruce and Andrews, (2014), the authors identified fatigue as a mechanism for injury of the Ulnar Collateral Ligament. Their work states: “When dynamic stabilizers (e.g. flexor pronator muscles) become fatigued, even more stress is placed on the UCL. The UCL approaches maximum varus torque allowable with every pitch, which explains why UCL injuries are so common in competitive pitchers”. Page 318, Bruce & Andrews, 2014 – Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injuries in the Throwing Athlete Furthermore, a case control study by Olsen et al., 2006 examined the risk factors for shoulder and elbow injury in adolescent pitchers. Amongst the injured group, 51.5% of pitchers reported throwing with arm fatigue regularly, compared to 11.1% in the control group. Pitchers who threw with regular arm fatigue were 36 times more likely to sustain an injury (Fleisig et al., 2009). Flesig GS, Weber A, Hassell N, Andrews JR. Prevention of elbow injuries in youth baseball pitchers. Curr. Sports Med. Rep., Vol. 8, No. 5, pp. 250-254, 2009. Olsen et al. The American Journal of Sports Medicine, Vol. 34, No. 6 DOI: 10.1177/0363546505284188 “Findings of interest were not limited to baseball pitchers” – this does not make sense, given the aim and the conclusion, the review should be limited to pitchers. We agree with the reviewer and have removed this statement from the manuscript. In line with other comments, all reference to non-pitcher work has been removed. INTRODUCTION Line #64: “Fatigue can lead to performance decrements and the corresponding cumulative loading…” – I don’t think the “performance decrements” component fits in this sentence, I suggest just focusing on cumulative loading or better explain how the performance decrements are associated with the cumulative loading. We agree that performance decrements may not fit in this statement, given the focus on fatigue and tissue loading. We have removed performance decrements from this statement and on line 61, it now reads, “The cumulative loading caused by fatigue can result in microtrauma… “. Line #68-74: restructure this information so that it flows better from the preceding sentences. This paragraph is long, so it will be easy to lose the reader if you jump around too much. These final 2 sentences need to be clearer and more concise to improve readability. I don’t believe Table 1 is needed. Tables are not expected in the introduction of a journal article. We agree that the paragraph should be more concise. We have reworked this paragraph and shortened substantially, as shown starting on line 64:” In the 2018 season, there were 86 cases of Tommy John surgeries across professional baseball (Roegele, 2018) …”. Table 1 has been removed from the manuscript (the data from this table is referred to in the text with a citation). Line #79: “factors involving the brain and central nervous system” – this is too vague. Please be more specific or just say “due to central and peripheral neural mechanisms”. We agree that this sentence was too vague. Given the complexity of neuromuscular fatigue and our attempt to not go into extreme detail about the mechanisms of fatigue or the process, we have attempted to revise this statement, yet continue to keep it concise. On lines 74-77, we now state that “Muscle fatigue is a process that occurs due to central and/or peripheral mechanisms, which can emerge due to numerous decrements from motor centers to the muscle fiber.” We have also provided an operational definition of fatigue for our work, in the methods section, lines 119-124. Line #78-109: Too much detail here about each individual study. Please make this paragraph more concise so that the important information is better highlighted to the reader e.g. studies showing similar findings can be described together. Introduction sections of literature reviews do not need to be long. We have reorganized the paragraph to make it more concise as opposed to providing detail on each individual study. Details are found in the tables. Line #92-93: Good point. Thank you. METHODS You should provide an operational definition of fatigue in the methods section. In the intro you define fatigue as “as a decrease in force generating capacity” but throughout the review you indirectly infer fatigue from high pitch counts, lack of rest, etc. Given the importance of fatigue to our work, we have given this comment considerable thought. We have added our operational definition of fatigue to the end of the search strategy section of the manuscript (lines 119-124) and it includes… Fatigue is operationally defined as an exercise induced loss in muscle force generating capacity. This can result in decreased strength (Enoka & Stuart, 1992; Fitts, 1994, Vollestad, 1997), joint stability (Webster & Nussbaum, 2016), postural control (Gribble & Hertel, 2004, Bizid et al., 2009), and altered kinematics (Apriantono et al., 2006; Becker et al., 2017; Niederer et al., 2016). Gribble, P. A., & Hertel, J. (2004). Effect of lower-extremity muscle fatigue on postural control. Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation, 85(4), 589-592. Bizid, R., Margnes, E., François, Y., Jully, J. L., Gonzalez, G., Dupui, P., & Paillard, T. (2009). Effects of knee and ankle muscle fatigue on postural control in the unipedal stance. European journal of applied physiology, 106(3), 375-380. Apriantono, T., Nunome, H., Ikegami, Y., & Sano, S. (2006). The effect of muscle fatigue on instep kicking kinetics and kinematics in association football. Journal of sports sciences, 24(9), 951-960. Becker, S., Fröhlich, M., Kelm, J., & Ludwig, O. (2017). Change of muscle activity as well as kinematic and kinetic parameters during headers after core muscle fatigue. Sports, 5(1), 10. Niederer, D., Vogt, L., Pippig, T., Wall, R., & Banzer, W. (2016). Local muscle fatigue and 3D kinematics of the cervical spine in healthy subjects. Journal of motor behavior, 48(2), 155-163. Webster, C. A., & Nussbaum, M. A. (2016). Localized ankle fatigue development and fatigue perception in adults with or without chronic ankle instability. Journal of athletic training, 51(6), 491-497 Vøllestad, N. K. (1997). Measurement of human muscle fatigue. Journal of neuroscience methods, 74(2), 219-227. Fitts, R. H. (1994). Cellular mechanisms of muscle fatigue. Physiological reviews, 74(1), 49-94. Enoka, R. M., & Stuart, D. G. (1992). Neurobiology of muscle fatigue. Journal of applied physiology, 72(5), 1631-1648. All references have been added. Line #122: There is no risk of bias assessment, so the review is not consistent with PRISMA. Please justify why this was not done and revise the statement about PRISMA guidelines accordingly. We apologize for the confusion on risk bias assessment. We did in fact follow PRISMA guidelines and a risk bias assessment was completed. We failed to clearly state our approach and have done so in the revised section ““Risk Bias Assessment” and table 2 (lines 168-181). In addition, we have separated our data extraction and study selection section (lines 145-152). We have also added details about our methodological quality assessment in table 1 and lines 154-164. In total, these additions are found in the methods section, on lines 145-181. Line #139-140: “not limited to baseball (swimmers, volleyball, and tennis players)” – I strongly disagree with the use of other sports. Your review objective and search terms are baseball specific, so it does not make sense for your included studies to not be baseball specific. Reviews need to be specific otherwise it is too difficult to draw strong conclusions. Additionally, there is no mention of non-baseball specific findings in the results so it is not clear how they have been incorporated. You should remove the non-baseball studies from the review. We understand your point regarding the need to keep this systematic review specific to baseball pitching. For that reason, we removed all studies which looked at either softball players or other overhead throwing athletes. Starting at line133: “Articles were excluded if the study did not include baseball pitchers, therefore studies examining a population of softball players or other overhead throwing athletes were not included in the review.” As we removed all articles related to sports outside of baseball, we were left with 25 articles instead of 26. One article was removed and all results/figures have been updated as a result. Line #147: separate the data extraction and study selection paragraphs as per the PRISMA checklist. Please also make it clear that data extraction was done by one or multiple reviewers. It is unclear from the current wording. We have now separated the two paragraphs in order to follow PRISMA guidelines. A single reviewer extracted the original data and scanned for our eligibility criteria. After that, the remaining articles were evaluated by 3 reviewers, where agreement across all were required. This process was used to determine included articles. For data extraction, one reviewer extracted the relevant data and this was checked by two reviewers. This new data extraction section is found on lines 145-152. RESULTS Line #165-166: 74 minus 7 does not equal 65. Please clarify the numbers here. Figure #1: several values do not add up. i.e. In the ‘Initial Screening Process” section, 38+10+11+6+6 = 71 not 72; in the ‘Secondary Screening…” section it is not clear how you go from “abstracts screened for eligibility (n=29)” to “full-text articles screened for eligibility (n=9)” to “Articles included (n=26)”. It would be clearer if the side arrows branched off of the descending arrows so that it is clearer which step they came before and after. In general, these errors suggest that you should undertake a thorough cross-checking of you values to make sure there are no other errors/discrepancies in the final publication. Thank you for recognizing our mathematical error. We have checked our math once more and realized that we did in fact have 71 articles left following the initial screening process. We then removed 6 duplicate articles, leaving us with 65 articles. In the secondary screening process, each of the three reviewers independently screened each of the 65 remaining papers. Following this process, we were left with 25 articles as we have also removed one study related to various overhead throwing athletes. Figure 1 has been updated with the correct numbers and we have adjusted the figure based on the reviewer suggestion for arrows. Line #169: not sure what is meant by “full-text was unavailable for use”. Please make this clearer. Participants and Study Designs: this information should be in a table summarising the general characteristics of the included studies. The table should have (at a minimum) sample size, participant info, study design and duration (if relevant), outcome measures, key findings. This information is needed to be consistent with PRISMA. By “full-text unavailable for use”, we meant to say that we were unable to locate the study outside of the abstract. From line 193 and onward, we have noted that a second article was omitted as only an abstract was available, since the entire paper was not accessible to the reviewers. In regards to the inclusion of a table of participants and study design, we decided to not include one specific table to address this. We now have tables 3-5 in the manuscript that outline a similar request. Each table breaks down the extracted data for our three primary categories, Kinematics, Performance and Injury. The tables include author, year, sample size, methods and outcomes. Line #187-189: “The study designs varied within the selected literature, among which included four epidemiological studies, three retrospective analyses studies, two included crossover designs, and one longitudinal study.” – this begs the question, what was the study design of the other 16 included studies? We have made sure to reference each article listed in the review and the type of study that it entails. This is found on lines 225-242. Line #192: “tiredness” – vague term, please clarify/define further. We replaced the word “tiredness” with “fatigue”. Line #208-233: Much of this information is straight repetition of findings and values from Table 2. This paragraph should be condensed to avoid duplication of information from the table. i.e. synthesise the findings and make statements relating to the overall trends i.e. “There were significant changes in kinematics at the shoulder in X studies, elbow in X studies, hip in X studies … The variables that were most commonly affected were X, Y, and Z.” Table 2: Include a description of the fatigue protocol used in each study. Switch the table to landscape orientation to facilitate this. Describe the age/level of pitchers for each study. Report key null findings (if relevant) as well as significant findings, otherwise it’s a biased representation. Thank you for the feedback, we agree that this section should be condensed, as the material is already in the summary tables. We reformatted the section starting at line 244. We have removed much of the data that is included in the tables. In addition, our tables are much more comprehensive than the previous submission. We have also updated table 2 (now table 3) with the recommended changes for the inclusion of the fatigue protocol information. Line #238-263: same feedback from Line #208-233/Table 2 applies here with regards to Table 3. Table 3: you present weight averages here (i.e. a form of meta-analysis) but this is not described in the methods or highlight in the results texts. We agree with your feedback and have condensed the section starting at line 250, since most of this is duplicate with table 3 (originally table 2). We have also updated table 3. Line #270-274: This is too descriptive to be in the results section. Include in the introduction/discussion if you must. Thank you for your input. We agreed and moved this to our revised introduction. Line #274-298: Summarise these studies in a table and then succinctly highlight the key findings in-text to improve readability. You should present the findings based on the hierarchy of evidence i.e. RCT first (high quality evidence), survey last (low quality evidence). Talk about the results of studies that used similar study designs together i.e. currently you jump back and forth between longitudinal studies and survey studies and RCTs. Similar to the previous two sections, we agree that we needed to summarize this work in a table. We have done so in tables 3-5, and we also condensed each section to improve readability and remove duplicate information from text and tables. We have attempted to cluster studies design types together when talking about the results. However, given that we have grouped our findings into 3 main categories (Performance, Kinematics and Injury) sometimes, a category featured different study design. Regardless, we have worked to improve this in the results section. DISCUSSION #304-306/Figure 2: you don’t have strong enough evidence to claim this. You have studies showing fatigue effects biomechanics and fatigue effects performance but nothing demonstrating that biomechanical changes caused by fatigue are causing performance changes or injury risk (if this information exists it does not appear to be included in your review). You can still propose your theoretical framework but need to highlight the parts that are based on evidence and the parts that are not. This is not necessarily a bad thing because it highlights areas of future research (i.e. the parts of your framework that lack evidence). Please revise the discussion section accordingly. The reviews, and case control studies conducted by Bruce & Andrews, Olsen et al., and Flesig & Andrews have all identified that pitching while fatigued is a precursor to injury. In the laboratory-based studies included in this review, which have examined acute fatigue levels during pitching, (acute fatigue levels meaning, a fatigue level during a pitching session, and not that which is accumulated over the course of a season), the primary findings have been alterations in kinematics, and decreases in ball velocity. The magnitude of change in these two parameters is much greater in the kinematic changes than the velocity changes. Furthermore, none of the papers that have been included in this review have identified that a pitcher has become injured while performing the study. Thus, we strongly believe the pathway we have suggested in this review is supported by the research we have examined, though we have made a clear focus in the revised discussion to highlight what is theoretical in this model and what is lab-based. Line #310: This explanation does not fit with your results which suggest “results showed not only a significant reduction in ball velocity with fatigue,” (Line #254). We believe that clarification for our original statement on line 310 (now 298) is needed. This should help with the apparent contradiction highlighted by the reviewer. We understand the confusion about the original statement and the statement that followed. Thus, we have changed our line 310 statement to the following: “This work suggests that changes in performance likely decay at a lesser rate than changes in kinematics, suggesting that modifications to a pitcher’s kinematics are made to limit the decrements of fatigue.” Line #311: Not sure what you mean by “command” here. Please make this clearer? We have removed the comment “whether that is velocity or command” entirely. Line #313: these subsequent sentences don’t fit with the start of the paragraph. It’s not clear why you are even bringing up EMG at this point because you haven’t mention it once in your review up until this point. I suggest removing (or condensing and moving to later in the discussion) and elaborating more on the opening concept of this paragraph, which was relationship between fatigue, biomechanics and injury. Line #337-340: as above, why are you now bringing up EMG. While this review aimed to evaluate directly measurable outcomes in kinematics and performance, it is acknowledged that a more in-depth evaluation of kinetics, joint forces and loading in relation to changes in kinematics is a valuable next step. Given this important point, we decided to discuss Kinetics in our discussion. Electromyography has long been used as a surrogate for muscle force production (Dowling, 1997). Thus, we have included this section in the review to discuss the kinetic implications for pitching related changes in the forces acting on the body. We have included a precursor to this section explaining how EMG is used to predict force, and how this is relevant to the study. Surface electromyography is the recording of electrical signals transmitted from the brain to the neuromuscular junction, resulting in the contraction of the muscle, and the production of a force at the end effector (Dowling, 1997; De Luca, 1997). While consideration must be made surrounding factors of movement, fatigue, skin impedance, and a variety of other physiological and environmental factors related to the interpretation of EMG, the use of surface EMG in sports is a non-invasive method of predicting internal forces as a result of human movement (Clarys et al., 2010). C. J. De Luca, 1997, “The use of surface electromyography in biomechanics”, Journal of Applied Biomechanics, 13 (2): 135-163. Clarys, J. P., Scafoglieri, A., Tresignie, J., Reilly, T., & Van Roy, P. (2010). Critical appraisal and hazards of surface electromyography data acquisition in sport and exercise. Asian journal of sports medicine, 1(2), 69 Dowling, J. J. (1997). The use of electromyography for the noninvasive prediction of muscle forces. Sports Medicine, 24(2), 82-96 Line #350-352: need to be careful with matching references to statements like this. The study you have referenced did not investigate injuries so doesn’t support your statement. Thank you for catching our oversight, the reference has been replaced with the correct one on line 345. Line #356-363: again, this does not support your statement in line #310 that biomechanics change to maintain performance, i.e. here biomechanics have led to reduced force. We believe that clarification for our original statement on line 310 (now 298) was needed. This should help with the apparent contradiction highlighted by the reviewer. We understand the confusion about the original statement and the statement that followed. Thus, we have changed our line 310 statement to the following: “This work suggests that changes in performance likely decay at a lesser rate than changes in kinematics, suggesting that modifications to a pitcher’s kinematics are made to limit the decrements of fatigue.” Line #363-370: This section is meant to be about kinetics (i.e. based on the subheading) but here you are talking about muscle activity. You’ve only referred to one study about kinetics. Electromyography has long been used as a surrogate for muscle force production (Dowling, 1997). Thus, we have included muscle activity work in this section of the review to discuss the kinetic implications for pitching related changes in the forces acting on the body. We have included a precursor to this section explaining how EMG is used to predict force, and how this is relevant to the study. Line #373-374: again, this does not support your interpretation at line #310 about biomechanical changes helping to maintain performance. We believe that clarification for our original statement on line 310 (now 298) was needed. This should help with the apparent contradiction highlighted by the reviewer. We understand the confusion about the original statement and the statement that followed. Thus, we have changed our line 310 statement to the following: “This work suggests that changes in performance likely decay at a lesser rate than changes in kinematics, suggesting that modifications to a pitcher’s kinematics are made to limit the decrements of fatigue.” Table 4 – this appears to be results copied from 1-study that has been published previously. It would be more appropriate to summarise the findings of this study in-text and include a reference. This table should be deleted. It does not add anything to the interpretation. We agree and have deleted Table 4 entirely. We summarized the results in-text starting at line 368-372. Our new Table 4 is something entirely different than the previous submission. Line #401 – this is probably the key paragraph (i.e. injury seems to be a big focus of your overarching review objectives) so you need to make it clearer what the current interpretation of the literature is, i.e. do we have any studies that actually link fatigue with increase injury risk? They must be highlighted first at the beginning of the paragraph. The weaker, survey-based studies can be mentioned later because they provide a low level of evidence that is not convincing in this case. We certainly agree that our work should not conclude or infer that fatigue is the “primary” reason for injury in baseball. In fact, in response to an earlier comment on lines 40-41: we have changed to the following: “is a contributing factor of injury in baseball pitchers”. However, as evident from some of the literature (cited below), we are of the opinion that fatigue is certainly a big contributor to this issue. In a review by Bruce and Andrews, (2014), the authors identified fatigue as a mechanism for injury of the Ulnar Collateral Ligament. Their work states: “When dynamic stabilizers (e.g. flexor pronator muscles) become fatigued, even more stress is placed on the UCL. The UCL approaches maximum varus torque allowable with every pitch, which explains why UCL injuries are so common in competitive pitchers”. Page 318, Bruce & Andrews, 2014 – Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injuries in the Throwing Athlete Furthermore, a case control study by Olsen et al., 2006 examined the risk factors for shoulder and elbow injury in adolescent pitchers. Amongst the injured group, 51.5% of pitchers reported throwing with arm fatigue regularly, compared to 11.1% in the control group. Pitchers who threw with regular arm fatigue were 36 times more likely to sustain an injury (Fleisig et al., 2009). Flesig GS, Weber A, Hassell N, Andrews JR. Prevention of elbow injuries in youth baseball pitchers. Curr. Sports Med. Rep., Vol. 8, No. 5, pp. 250-254, 2009. Olsen et al. The American Journal of Sports Medicine, Vol. 34, No. 6 DOI: 10.1177/0363546505284188 As a result, we feel that our conclusion to this section acknowledges that they survey and subjective fatigue measures must be met with caution when distinguishing a definitive link between fatigue and injury risk. Line #426: “This can lead to an increased risk of injury in baseball pitchers.” – you have not provided strong enough evidence to make this claim, i.e. please soften your wording e.g. indirect evidence suggests there is a relationship, but there have been few longitudinal studies that have directly investigated it, and fatigue is often inferred from pitch counts, etc. We agree that we need to be careful with our statements when making a leap from fatigue to injury. As per other comments in this review, our language has been softened. Here, we have reformatted the sentence as seen on line 425 “This can indirectly suggest, despite the few longitudinal studies that have directly investigated it, that there is a relationship between fatigue and increased risk of injury.”
paper_title_zh: 棒球投手肌肉疲劳的表现：系统综述
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。棒球投手的疲劳是一个与体能和心智表现下降、受伤以及运动学变化相关联的过程。众多研究已将疲劳与过度使用、高球速、休息时间不足、不良机械动作以及自我满意度程度联系起来。本研究旨在系统回顾文献，以识别棒球投球中结果与疲劳表现之间关系的理论框架。综合数据可能识别出需要进一步研究的领域。方法。该方案已在PROSPERO（ID: CRD42018114194）注册。通过SPORTDiscus、Medline、PubMed、Cochrane系统评价数据库和Google Scholar进行检索，使用关键词如投手疲劳和运动学变化（例如投球机械动作、外翻肘部扭矩）、表现（例如投球次数、投球类型）以及受伤（例如疼痛、肘部和肩部酸痛）。三位评审员独立筛选文章，根据摘要资格选择相关文献，并评估其中描述的方法以确定最终纳入。
review_content_zh:
审稿人1（匿名）基本报告
报告可以改进以确保该综述符合基于PRISMA指南的系统综述标准，即引言应更加简洁，方法和结果部分应包括偏倚风险评估，证明数据合成中加权平均方法的合理性，确保流程图数字正确，提供包含所有纳入研究特征的表格，避免表格和文本中的信息重复，确保讨论中的信息与结果一致。请参阅“一般评论”部分以获取具体细节和解决这些问题的策略。我们感谢审稿人为我们的工作提供了详细且有见地的评审。这些建议极大地改进了我们的手稿和工作的质量。为了清晰地总结所做的更改，上述许多评论已在下文的“一般评论”中进行了回应。然而，我们在此总结一些主要要点：
1. 我们显著提高了综述的严谨性，并在多个地方澄清了如何根据PRISMA指南满足系统综述的标准。我们认为我们的综述符合标准，但我们需要在手稿中更好地识别我们的过程。现在方法部分（第145-181行）应该更加清晰。
2. 我们的引言现在更加简洁和有针对性（我们删除了超过100字）。
3. 我们增加了一个完整的方法学质量评估部分（第154-166行）。这包括一个新的表格（表1），采用了Downs和Black 1998年的质量评估。
4. 我们还增加了一个偏倚风险评估（第168-181行）和一个新的表格（表2），遵循Lopes等人2012年的工作。
5. 我们纳入的所有论文被分为3类（运动学、表现和损伤）。每篇论文及其特定类别的发现分别列在表3、4和5中，并附有一些关于每项研究的额外信息。
6. 我们已经仔细检查了流程图数字，改进了图像，并从结果（文本和表格）中删除了任何重复内容。
7. 尽管在结果部分增加了方法学质量和偏倚评估部分，我们仍然删除了将近700字。这反映了我们删除文本和表格中重复信息的方法。

实验设计
设计的主要问题是缺乏偏倚风险评估和纳入非投手相关研究（即游泳运动员、排球运动员、网球运动员）。这些其他运动项目被纳入了搜索方法中，但在结果和讨论中未提及，因此不清楚它们是如何被整合的。我强烈建议从资格标准和结果中删除这些研究。请参阅“一般评论”部分以获取具体细节和解决这些问题的策略。 我们同意审稿人的意见，并已删除所有与非投手研究相关的提及。我们最初的思路是包括所有具有“投掷”动作或“手臂摆动”动作的运动员，以获得一个全面的列表。然而，我们的搜索标准和资格标准意味着我们最终得到了与投手相关的文章。因此，我们回过头来修订了我们的搜索指标（流程图）以反映这一变化。仅删除了1篇文章。我们花费了大量时间在我们的工作中加入了方法学质量和风险偏倚评估部分。我们包括了一个完整的方法学质量评估部分（第154-166行）。这包括一个新的表格（表1），采用了Downs和Black 1998年的质量评估标准。我们还包括了一个风险偏倚评估（第168-181行）和一个新的表格（表2），遵循Lopes等人2012年的工作。

研究结果的有效性
作者根据其综述的发现提供了有趣的见解，但需要更加谨慎地明确指出何时有强有力的证据支持他们的主张，何时没有。了解证据何时薄弱或不存在是很重要的，因为它为未来的研究提供了方向。请参阅“一般评论”部分，了解具体的细节和解决这些问题的策略。

我们花费时间审查了我们所有纳入文章的原始分类。我们有3项前瞻性/纵向研究，3项随机交叉研究，2项回顾性研究，1项流行病学研究，1项横断面研究。我们纳入的大部分文章（15篇）是描述性/受控实验室研究。鉴于我们纳入的大部分工作具有非常相似的研究设计，且未包括元分析或RCT，我们决定对所有这些工作平等对待。诚然，我们承认我们纳入的纵向和流行病学研究通过调查提供了证据，我们在整个手稿中用这些证据来支持我们的实验室/生物力学研究。

对作者的评论
作者选择了一个有趣的主题进行综述，我祝贺他们在筛选31,860篇摘要中所付出的努力。我认为这篇手稿需要改进才能发表，我为作者提供了以下具体反馈，希望他们会觉得有用。再次感谢这些非常有帮助的评论，它们无疑将改进这项工作。

摘要
“是棒球投手受伤的主要原因”——基于你们收集的证据，这个结论过于强烈
我们当然同意，我们的工作不应得出或暗示疲劳是棒球投手受伤的“主要原因”。在第40-41行，我们已改为如下：“是棒球投手受伤的一个促成因素”。然而，正如一些文献（如下所引）所示，我们认为疲劳确实是这一问题的重大影响因素。 在布鲁斯和安德鲁斯（2014年）的综述中，作者将疲劳识别为尺侧副韧带损伤的机制。他们的研究指出：“当动态稳定器（例如屈肌旋前肌）疲劳时，尺侧副韧带（UCL）承受的压力会更大。每次投掷时，UCL接近最大允许外翻扭矩，这解释了为什么UCL损伤在竞技投手中的发生率如此高。”（第318页，布鲁斯和安德鲁斯，2014年——《投掷运动员的尺侧副韧带损伤》）。此外，奥尔森等人于2006年进行的一项病例对照研究考察了青少年投手肩部和肘部损伤的风险因素。在受伤组中，51.5%的投手报告经常在手臂疲劳时投掷，而对照组中这一比例为11.1%。经常在手臂疲劳时投掷的投手受伤的可能性要高出36倍（弗莱西格等人，2009年）。弗莱西格GS，韦伯A，哈塞尔N，安德鲁斯JR。《预防青少年棒球投手的肘部损伤》。《当前运动医学报告》，第8卷，第5期，第250-254页，2009年。奥尔森等人。《美国运动医学杂志》，第34卷，第6期，DOI: 10.1177/0363546505284188。“有趣发现不仅限于棒球投手”——鉴于研究目的和结论，这一说法不合逻辑，综述应限于投手。我们同意审稿人的意见，已从手稿中删除该声明。根据其他意见，所有关于非投手工作的引用也已删除。

引言
第64行：“疲劳可能导致性能下降和相应的累积负荷……”——我认为“性能下降”部分不适合这句话，建议只关注累积负荷，或更好地解释性能下降与累积负荷的关系。我们同意在关注疲劳和组织负荷的情况下，性能下降可能不适合这一声明。我们已从该声明中删除性能下降，并在第61行改为：“由疲劳引起的累积负荷可能导致微创伤……”。第68-74行：重新组织这些信息，使其更好地与前文衔接。这段文字较长，如果跳跃太多，容易让读者失去兴趣。最后两句话需要更清晰、更简洁以提高可读性。我认为不需要表1。期刊文章的引言部分不期望有表格。我们同意这段文字应更简洁。我们已重新整理这段文字并大幅缩短，如第64行所示：“在2018赛季，职业棒球中共有86例汤米·约翰手术（罗杰尔，2018年）……”。表1已从手稿中删除（该表中的数据在文本中通过引用提及）。第79行：“涉及大脑和中央神经系统的因素”——这太模糊了。请更具体，或直接说“由于中枢和外周神经机制”。 我们同意这句话过于模糊。鉴于神经肌肉疲劳的复杂性以及我们试图不深入细节地讨论疲劳机制或过程，我们已尝试修改这一声明，同时保持其简洁性。在第74-77行，我们现在表述为：“肌肉疲劳是一个由于中枢和/或外周机制而发生的过程，这些机制可能由于从运动中枢到肌纤维的多种减退而出现。”我们还为我们的研究在方法部分（第119-124行）提供了疲劳的操作性定义。

第78-109行：此处关于每个单独研究的细节过多。请使该段落更加简洁，以便重要信息更好地突出给读者，例如，可以将显示相似发现的研究一起描述。文献综述的引言部分不需要过长。我们已经重新组织了该段落，使其更加简洁，而不是提供每个单独研究的细节。详细内容见表格。

第92-93行：好观点。谢谢。

方法

你应该在方法部分提供疲劳的操作性定义。在引言中，你将疲劳定义为“力量生成能力的下降”，但在整个综述中，你间接地从高投球次数、缺乏休息等方面推断疲劳。鉴于疲劳对我们工作的重要性，我们对此评论进行了认真思考。我们已将我们的疲劳操作性定义添加到手稿的搜索策略部分末尾（第119-124行），其中包括……疲劳操作性定义为运动引起的肌肉力量生成能力的丧失。这可能导致力量下降（Enoka & Stuart, 1992; Fitts, 1994, Vollestad, 1997）、关节稳定性下降（Webster & Nussbaum, 2016）、姿势控制改变（Gribble & Hertel, 2004, Bizid et al., 2009）以及运动学改变（Apriantono et al., 2006; Becker et al., 2017; Niederer et al., 2016）。

含糊不清的术语，请进一步澄清/定义。我们将“tiredness”一词替换为“fatigue”。第208-233行：这部分信息大多直接重复了表2中的发现和数值。应缩减此段落，以避免与表格中的信息重复。例如，综合发现并陈述与整体趋势相关的内容，即“在X项研究中，肩部的运动学发生了显著变化；在X项研究中，肘部发生了显著变化；在X项研究中，髋部发生了显著变化……受影响最普遍的变量是X、Y和Z。”表2：包括每项研究中使用的疲劳协议的描述。将表格切换为横向布局以方便这一操作。描述每项研究中投手的年龄/水平。报告关键的无显著发现（如果相关），以及显著发现，否则这是有偏见的表述。感谢您的反馈，我们同意这一部分应进行缩减，因为材料已在总结表中呈现。我们从第244行开始重新格式化了这一部分。我们删除了表格中包含的大部分数据。此外，我们的表格比之前的提交版本更为全面。我们还根据建议更新了表2（现为表3），增加了疲劳协议信息。第238-263行：与第208-233行/表2相同的反馈适用于此处关于表3的内容。表3：您在此处呈现了体重平均值（即一种元分析形式），但未在方法中描述或在结果文本中突出显示。我们同意您的反馈，并从第250行开始缩减了这一部分，因为大部分内容与表3（原表2）重复。我们还更新了表3。第270-274行：这部分描述性过强，不适合放在结果部分。如果必须保留，请放入引言/讨论部分。感谢您的意见。我们同意并将这部分移至修订后的引言中。第274-298行：将这些研究总结在表格中，然后在正文中简洁地突出关键发现，以提高可读性。应根据证据的层级呈现发现，即首先呈现RCT（高质量证据），最后呈现调查（低质量证据）。讨论使用相似研究设计的各项研究结果，即目前您在纵向研究、调查研究和RCT之间来回跳跃。与前两个部分类似，我们同意需要将这些工作总结在表格中。我们已在表3-5中完成这一操作，并缩减了每个部分，以提高可读性并删除文本和表格中的重复信息。我们尝试在讨论结果时将研究设计类型进行聚类。 然而，鉴于我们将研究结果分为三个主要类别（性能、运动学和损伤），有时一个类别会包含不同的研究设计。尽管如此，我们已在结果部分努力改进这一点。讨论#304-306/图2：你没有足够强的证据来支持这一说法。你有研究显示疲劳影响生物力学和疲劳影响性能，但没有证据表明由疲劳引起的生物力学变化导致了性能变化或损伤风险（如果存在此类信息，似乎并未包含在你的综述中）。你仍然可以提出你的理论框架，但需要突出哪些部分是基于证据的，哪些部分不是。这未必是坏事，因为它突出了未来研究的领域（即你框架中缺乏证据的部分）。请相应修改讨论部分。由Bruce & Andrews、Olsen等人以及Flesig & Andrews进行的综述和病例对照研究均指出，疲劳投球是损伤的前兆。在本综述中包含的实验室研究中，考察了投球过程中的急性疲劳水平（急性疲劳水平指的是投球期间的疲劳水平，而非整个赛季累积的疲劳），主要发现是运动学的改变和球速的下降。这两个参数的变化幅度在运动学变化中远大于速度变化。此外，本综述中包含的论文均未指出投球手在研究过程中受伤。因此，我们强烈认为本综述中提出的路径得到了我们所考察研究的支持，尽管我们在修订的讨论中明确强调了该模型中哪些是理论性的，哪些是基于实验室的。第310行：这一解释与你的结果不符，你的结果显示“疲劳导致球速显著下降”（第254行）。我们认为需要对第310行（现为第298行）的原声明进行澄清。这应有助于解决评审者指出的明显矛盾。我们理解对原声明及其后续声明的困惑。因此，我们将第310行的声明修改为：“这项工作表明，性能变化可能以低于运动学变化的速率衰减，这表明对投球手运动学的调整是为了限制疲劳的减退。”第311行：不确定此处“控制”的意思。请澄清这一点？我们已完全删除了“无论是速度还是控制”的评论。第313行：这些后续句子与段落开头不符。 1997）。因此，我们在综述中包含这一部分，以讨论投掷相关变化对作用在身体上的力的动力学影响。我们在此部分前加入了前言，解释了如何使用EMG预测力量，以及这与研究的关联性。表面肌电图是记录从大脑传输到神经肌肉接头的电信号，导致肌肉收缩，并在末端执行器产生力量的过程（Dowling, 1997; De Luca,
