J. De Luca, 1997, “表面肌电图在生物力学中的应用”，应用生物力学杂志，13（2）：135-163。Clarys, J. P., Scafoglieri, A., Tresignie, J., Reilly, T., & Van Roy, P. (2010). 表面肌电图数据采集在体育和锻炼中的关键评估和风险。亚洲体育医学杂志，1（2），69。Dowling, J. J. (1997). 使用肌电图非侵入性预测肌肉力量的方法。体育医学，24（2），82-96。第350-352行：在匹配此类陈述的参考文献时需谨慎。您引用的研究并未调查损伤，因此不支持您的陈述。感谢您指出我们的疏忽，第345行已替换为正确的参考文献。第356-363行：同样，这并不支持您在第310行（现为298行）中的陈述，即生物力学变化以维持性能，而此处生物力学导致了力量的减少。我们认为需要对第310行（现为298行）的原始陈述进行澄清。这应有助于解决审稿人指出的明显矛盾。我们理解对原始陈述和后续陈述的困惑。 因此，我们将第310行的声明修改为如下：“这项研究表明，性能变化可能以低于运动学变化的速率衰减，这表明对投手运动学的修改是为了限制疲劳的减退。”第363-370行：这一部分本应讨论动力学（即基于小标题），但此处却在讨论肌肉活动。你只引用了一项关于动力学的研究。肌电图长期以来一直被用作肌肉力量产生的替代指标（Dowling, 1997）。因此，我们在综述的这一部分中包含了肌肉活动研究，以讨论与投球相关的力量变化对身体的动力学影响。我们在此部分前加入了前言，解释了如何使用EMG预测力量，以及这与研究的关联性。第373-374行：同样，这并不支持你在第310行关于生物力学变化有助于维持性能的解释。我们认为需要对第310行（现为第298行）的原始声明进行澄清。这应有助于解决审稿人指出的明显矛盾。我们理解对原始声明和后续声明的困惑。因此，我们将第310行的声明修改为如下：“这项研究表明，性能变化可能以低于运动学变化的速率衰减，这表明对投手运动学的修改是为了限制疲劳的减退。”表4——这似乎是从已发表的1项研究中复制的结果。更合适的做法是在文本中总结该研究的发现并附上参考文献。此表应删除，它对解释没有增加任何内容。我们同意并已完全删除表4。我们在第368-372行开始在文本中总结结果。我们的新表4与之前的提交内容完全不同。第401行——这可能是关键段落（即伤害似乎是你们综述目标的重点），因此你需要更清楚地说明当前对文献的解释，即我们是否有任何研究实际上将疲劳与增加的伤害风险联系起来？它们必须在段落开头首先突出。较弱的、基于调查的研究可以稍后提及，因为它们提供的证据水平较低，在这种情况下并不令人信服。我们当然同意我们的研究不应得出或暗示疲劳是棒球伤害的“主要原因”。事实上，在回应之前对第40-41行的评论时，我们已修改为如下：“是棒球投手伤害的一个促成因素”。然而，正如一些文献（如下所引）所示，我们认为疲劳确实是这一问题的重大影响因素。 在布鲁斯和安德鲁斯（2014年）的综述中，作者将疲劳确定为尺侧副韧带损伤的机制。他们的研究指出：“当动态稳定器（例如屈肌旋前肌）疲劳时，尺侧副韧带（UCL）承受的压力会更大。每次投掷时，UCL接近最大允许的尺侧扭矩，这解释了为什么UCL损伤在竞技投手中的发生率如此高。”（第318页，布鲁斯和安德鲁斯，2014年——《投掷运动员的尺侧副韧带损伤》）。此外，奥尔森等人于2006年进行的一项病例对照研究探讨了青少年投手肩部和肘部损伤的风险因素。在受伤组中，51.5%的投手报告经常在手臂疲劳时投掷，而对照组中这一比例为11.1%。经常在手臂疲劳时投掷的投手受伤的可能性要高出36倍（弗莱西格等人，2009年）。弗莱西格GS，韦伯A，哈塞尔N，安德鲁斯JR。《预防青少年棒球投手的肘部损伤》。《当前运动医学报告》，第8卷，第5期，第250-254页，2009年。奥尔森等人。《美国运动医学杂志》，第34卷，第6期，DOI: 10.1177/0363546505284188。因此，我们认为本节的结论承认，在区分疲劳与损伤风险之间的确切联系时，必须谨慎对待调查和主观疲劳测量。第426行：“这可能导致棒球投手受伤风险增加。”——您提供的证据不足以支持这一说法，即请软化您的措辞，例如间接证据表明存在关联，但很少有纵向研究直接调查了这一问题，且疲劳通常是从投掷次数等推断出来的。我们同意在从疲劳到损伤的跳跃中，我们的表述需要谨慎。根据本综述中的其他评论，我们的语言已经软化。在这里，我们将第425行的句子重新格式化为：“这可以间接表明，尽管很少有纵向研究直接调查了这一问题，疲劳与增加的损伤风险之间存在关联。”

reasons: Line #350-352: need to be careful with matching references to statements like this.
The study you have referenced did not investigate injuries so doesn’t support your statement.
Report key null findings (if relevant) as well as significant findings, otherwise it’s a biased representation.
The authors offer interesting insights based on the findings of their review, but greater care needs to be taken to clearly identify when there is and is not strong evidence to support their claims.
It is important to know when evidence is weak or non-existent because it provides direction for future research.
#304-306/Figure 2: you don’t have strong enough evidence to claim this.
You can still propose your theoretical framework but need to highlight the parts that are based on evidence and the parts that are not.

Line #426: “This can lead to an increased risk of injury in baseball pitchers.” – you have not provided strong enough evidence to make this claim, i.e. please soften your wording e.g. indirect evidence suggests there is a relationship, but there have been few longitudinal studies that have directly investigated it, and fatigue is often inferred from pitch counts, etc.
These final 2 sentences need to be clearer and more concise to improve readability.
This paragraph is long, so it will be easy to lose the reader if you jump around too much.
Line #78-109: Too much detail here about each individual study.
Please make this paragraph more concise so that the important information is better highlighted to the reader e.g. studies showing similar findings can be described together.
It would be clearer if the side arrows branched off of the descending arrows so that it is clearer which step they came before and after.
This is too descriptive to be in the results section.
Summarise these studies in a table and then succinctly highlight the key findings in-text to improve readability.

Reporting can be improved to make sure this review meets the standard expected of systematic reviews, based on the PRISMA guidelines, i.e. introduction should be more concise, methods and results should include risk of bias assessment, justify weighted average approach to data synthesis, ensure flow chart numbers are correct, provide a table with study characteristics for all included studies, avoid duplication of information in tables and text, ensure information in the discussion is consistent with the results.
Line #147: separate the data extraction and study selection paragraphs as per the PRISMA checklist.
Participants and Study Designs: this information should be in a table summarising the general characteristics of the included studies.
Talk about the results of studies that used similar study designs together i.e. currently you jump back and forth between longitudinal studies and survey studies and RCTs.
You should present the findings based on the hierarchy of evidence i.e. RCT first (high quality evidence), survey last (low quality evidence).

paper_title: Association between IL-1B (-511)/IL-1RN (VNTR) polymorphisms and Type 2 Diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
paper_abstract: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) plays an essential role in the immune pro-inflammatory process, which is regarded as one of many factors in the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
review_content: Reviewer 2: Basic reporting Clear, unambiguous language • The first sentence of the abstract states that “Interleukin-1 (IL-1) plays an essential role in the immune pro-inflammatory process, inducing the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).” In this form, the statement appears to suggest that IL-1 levels are causal for T2D. However, T2D is a complex disease influenced by multiple environmental, ethnic and genetic factors. This sentence needs to be rephrased so that it is clear that immune inflammation is one factor among many in T2D development. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have revised the sentence: “Interleukin-1 (IL-1) plays an essential role in the immune pro-inflammatory process, which is regarded as one of many factors in the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).” • The variant identifiers used throughout the manuscript are acceptable, however, it would be helpful for readers if a dbSNP identifier or chromosome: position coordinates were provided for the first mention of the variant, particularly in the abstract. In addition, for missense variants please indicate where in the amino acid sequence the substitution takes place, and which amino acid is substituted and what it is replaced with. E.g., Arg358Pro. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have modified the sentence in the abstract and introduction: “Several case-control studies have illustrated the association of the IL-1B (-511) (rs16944, Chr 2:112,837,290, C/T Intragenic, Transition Substitution) and IL-1RN (VNTR) (gene for IL-1 receptor antagonist, IL-1RA, 86 bp tandem repeats in intron 2) polymorphisms with T2DM risk.” and “In the promoter region, IL-1B (-511) (rs16944, Chr 2:112,837,290, C/T Intragenic, Transition Substitution) has a bi-allelic polymorphism at position -511, representing the C/T transition. IL-1RN (VNTR) (gene for IL-1 receptor antagonist, IL-1RA, 86 bp tandem repeats in intron 2) has 5 different alleles: 1* (4 repeats), 2* (2 repeats), 3* (5 repeats), 4* (3 repeats) and 5* (6 repeats).” Since the IL-1B (-511) is intragenic and the IL-1RN (VNTR) is 86 bp tandem repeats, they cause no substitution of amino acid. • Line 66 change “sensitive” to “sensitivity” Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have changed “sensitive” to “sensitivity”. (Line 70) • Line 87: the word “epidemic” does not make sense here. Consider changing this to “prevalent” Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have changed “epidemic” to “prevalent”. (Line 89) • Line 94: add the word “pancreatic” before “β-cells” Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the word “pancreatic” before “β-cells”. (Line 97) • I disagree with the following statement (line 95): “The most typical characteristic of T2DM is chronic and low-grade inflammation”. The most typical characteristic of T2D, insulin resistance, is mentioned in the previous sentence. I do agree that inflammation is widely observed in T2D, however, it is not the most typical characteristic. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have revised the sentence: “The chronic and low-grade inflammation in metabolic organs including the liver, brain, pancreas and adipose tissue is known as metaflammation (metabolism-induced inflammation), which can be widely observed in T2DM.” (Line 98-101) • The statement: “Many genetic association studies have been performed to estimate the relationship of the IL-1B (-511) and IL-1RN (VNTR) polymorphisms with T2DM risk” needs to reference the association studies that have investigated this relationship. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added references. Many genetic association studies have been performed to estimate the relationship of the IL-1B (-511) and IL-1RN (VNTR) polymorphisms with T2DM risk (Achyut et al. 2007; Muktabhant et al. 2013). Muktabhant B, Duangjinda M, Sanchaisuriya P, Kananit S, and Schelp FP. 2013. Association of the polymorphism of interleukin-1B (-511C/T) with type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with and without family history of a first degree relative with diabetes mellitus. International Journal of Diabetes in Developing Countries 33:236-240. 10.1007/s13410-013-0155-x Achyut BR, Srivastava A, Bhattacharya S, and Mittal B. 2007. Genetic association of interleukin-1beta (-511C/T) and interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (86 bp repeat) polymorphisms with Type 2 diabetes mellitus in North Indians. Clin Chim Acta 377:163-169. 10.1016/j.cca.2006.09.012 Literature references, sufficient field background/context • Currently, the introduction outlines why inflammation is involved in T2D and what the role of IL- β in T2D may be. However, greater emphasis on findings from previous observational studies such as Spranger 2003 and genetic studies needs to be highlighted. In addition, the findings from previous genetic studies need to be discussed in more detail. i.e. Provide estimates of the association between IL-1 levels and T2D risk from several studies. Critically evaluate why previous analyses showed such contrasting results etc. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the studies and the details: “A previous observational study demonstrated that a combined elevation of IL-1β and IL-6 was associated with a roughly threefold increased risk of T2DM, and IL-1β might induce insulin resistance via activating the IκB kinase β (Spranger et al. 2003).” and “Several results suggest that there is no relationship between them (Borilova Linhartova et al. 2019; Muktabhant et al. 2013), whereas B.R Achyut et al. showed that both the IL-1B (-511) and IL-1RN (VNTR) polymorphisms were associated with susceptibility to T2DM as well as complications, and he indicated that T2 (IL-1β −511T/IL-1RN*2) haplotype was associated with a roughly twofold increased risk of T2DM (Achyut et al. 2007). Considering the small sample sizes (n＜600) and varying population characteristics (ethnic differences) in different studies, the results are conflicting.” • Related to the point above, currently, there is no discussion of clinical trial data in this context. Several large clinical trials have evaluated the role of IL-1 antagonism in preventing CAD, with T2D as a secondary endpoint. E.g. CANTOS and TRACK trials. The findings from these studies need to be discussed as they are highly relevant. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the findings from clinical trials: “Furthermore, CANTOS and TRACK trials have evaluated the role of IL-1 inhibition in the treatment of several inflammatory disorders, such as coronary artery disease, T2DM and rheumatoid arthritis (Qamar & Rader 2012; Ruscitti et al. 2019). According to the results from CANTOS trials, canakinumab (a fully humanized monoclonal antibody) could selectively block IL-1β, and its efficacy in suppressing both levels of inflammatory markers and clinical symptoms in patients with autoinflammatory disease such as T2DM and impaired glucose tolerance has been observed in this trial (Aday & Ridker 2018; Rissanen et al. 2012).” “Qamar A, and Rader DJ. 2012. Effect of interleukin 1β inhibition in cardiovascular disease. Curr Opin Lipidol 23:548-553. 10.1097/MOL.0b013e328359b0a6” “Ruscitti P, Masedu F, Alvaro S, Airò P, Battafarano N, Cantarini L, Cantatore FP, Carlino G, D'Abrosca V, Frassi M, Frediani B, Iacono D, Liakouli V, Maggio R, Mulè R, Pantano I, Prevete I, Sinigaglia L, Valenti M, Viapiana O, Cipriani P, and Giacomelli R. 2019. Anti-interleukin-1 treatment in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and type 2 diabetes (TRACK): A multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial. PLoS Med 16:e1002901. 10.1371/journal.pmed.1002901” “Aday AW, and Ridker PM. 2018. Antiinflammatory Therapy in Clinical Care: The CANTOS Trial and Beyond. Front Cardiovasc Med 5:62. 10.3389/fcvm.2018.00062” “Rissanen A, Howard CP, Botha J, and Thuren T. 2012. Effect of anti-IL-1β antibody (canakinumab) on insulin secretion rates in impaired glucose tolerance or type 2 diabetes: results of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial. Diabetes Obes Metab 14:1088-1096. 10.1111/j.1463-1326.2012.01637.x” • The reference provided for the following statement: “Moreover, the increased level of IL-1β in human pancreatic cells due to the elevated glucose concentrations and decreased level of IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) in islets of T2DM patients result in impaired insulin secretion, decreased cell proliferation, and apoptosis of β-cells.” Does not mention any of the following: impaired insulin secretion, decreased cell proliferation, and apoptosis of β-cells. Either a more suitable reference needs to be found that demonstrates these effects, or this statement needs to be amended with demonstrable findings from the literature. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have changed the reference: “Böni-Schnetzler M, and Donath MY. 2013. How biologics targeting the IL-1 system are being considered for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. Br J Clin Pharmacol 76:263-268. 10.1111/j.1365-2125.2012.04297.x”. • The following statement in the discussion (lines 257-260): “Eventually, it was suggested that IL-1β can induce the inflammatory microenvironment of islets, leading to impaired insulin secretion, decreased cell proliferation and apoptosis of β-cells, ultimately contributing to the development of T2DM.” references an article about IDDM which is type 1 diabetes. Therefore, this statement is factually incorrect as the reference does not concern T2D. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have changed the reference for this statement in the discussion (now in line 305): “Rhodes CJ. 2005. Type 2 diabetes-a matter of beta-cell life and death? Science 307:380-384. 10.1126/science.1104345”. Professional article structure, figures, tables. Raw data shared • When assessing the quality of the included studies using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale, the final scores for each study are included in Table 1, however, it would be helpful to include a full breakdown of the scoring for each study in a supplemental table as well. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have created a Supplementary file, named “Supplementary materials”, Table S1 includes the detailed scores for each part of NOS of each 12 included studies. • Table 1: T2D ascertainment in each study needs to be captured in more detail and where an explanation provided in cases where the diagnostic criteria were NA. In addition, the covariates used in each study need to be summarized. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the details about T2DM ascertainment in Table 1: “NA=Not Available (the diagnosis of T2DM was originally based on the presence of clinical symptoms and biochemical)”, “ADA=American Diabetes Association (fasting blood glucose ≥126mg/dL or 2 h blood glucose after overload with 75 g of glucose≥ 200mg/dL in oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) or glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) ≥6.5 in patients with classic symptoms of hyperglycemia)”, “WHO=World Health Organization (fasting glucose levels [7.0 mmol/L or [126 mg/dL after a minimum 12-h fast or 2-h post glucose level (oral glucose tolerance test or 2-h OGTT) [11.1 mmol/L or 200 mg/dL] on more than one occasion)”. All ORs in the included studies were not adjusted by age, sex, lifestyle etc. and the ORs in meta-analysis were calculated by using the numbers of individuals under each genetic phenotype in each included study. So, there were no covariates, we therefore performed stratified and sensitivity analyses, both of which were conducted to remove the impact of potential confounding factors to ensure our results reasonable and convincing. Self-contained with relevant results to hypotheses • The results presented are self-contained and relevant to the hypotheses, however, serious methodological issues are present (as outlined in the experimental design section) that cast doubt on the validity of the results. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have revised “Materials and Methods” section carefully according to your comments. This meta-analysis followed the principle of PRISMA: “This systematic review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) statement guidelines (Moher et al. 2009). A protocol was registered before commencing this review on PROSPERO (CRD42021268494).” Experimental design Original primary research within scope of journal • This study does represent original research within the scope of this journal. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. Research question well defined, relevant and meaningful • The original research question was well defined, meaningful and relevant but was not convincingly assessed due to issues with the statistical methodology. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have revised the description of statistical methodology in Section 2 (Materials and Methods: (2.1-2.5)) to make readers understand our methods better. Rigorous investigation performed to a high technical & ethical standard • Most genetic association studies are performed using an additive model, with dominant or recessive models considered as sensitivity analyses. It is concerning that no additive model has been considered for this analysis. This needs to be added to provide estimates that are comparable with the rest of the literature. In addition, the various models used need to be substantiated in the methods. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the analysis about the allele and additive model (codominant+overdominant model), and we revised the abstract, method, result, discussion sections, and the Table 2, 3: “The meta-analysis showed that IL-1RN (VNTR) was related to the increasing development of T2DM risk in the recessive model (OR=1.62, 95% CI: 1.09-2.42, Phet=0.377, Pz=0.018) and in the homozygous model (OR=2.02, 95% CI: 1.07-3.83, Phet=0.085, Pz=0.031), and the IL-1RN 2* allele was found a significant association with evaluated T2DM risk in all ethnicities (OR=2.08, 95% CI: 1.43-3.02, Phet＜0.001, Pz＜0.001) and in EA (OR=2.01, 95% CI: 1.53-2.66, Phet=0.541, Pz＜0.001). Moreover, stratification by ethnicity revealed that IL-1B (-511) was associated with a decreased risk of T2DM in the dominant model (OR=0.76, 95% CI: 0.59–0.97, Phet=0.218, Pz=0.027) and codominant model (OR=0.73, 95% CI: 0.54–0.99, Phet=0.141, Pz=0.040) in the East Asian (EA) subgroup.”; “We used original genotypic distribution data without any adjustment to measure the strength of the association between IL-1B (-511)/IL-1RN and T2DM risk by ORs (odds ratios) with 95% CIs (confidence intervals) under dominant, recessive, additive (overdominant+codominant) and homozygous models.”; “and codominant model (OR=0.73, 95% CI: 0.54–0.99, Phet=0.141, Pz=0.040) (Table 3)”; “Overall, a significantly increased T2DM risk was found to be associated with 2* allele in all ethnicities (OR=2.08, 95% CI: 1.43-3.02, Phet＜0.001, Pz＜0.001) and in EA (OR=2.01, 95% CI: 1.53-2.66, Phet=0.541, Pz＜0.001) (Table 3).”; “significantly elevated risk of developing T2DM was observed to be associated with the 2* allele in all ethnicities and EA subgroup, and its carriers of the IL-1RN (VNTR) polymorphism had an increased risk of developing T2DM among all ethnicities” HWE =Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium; IL-1=interleukin-1; IL-1RN=interleukin–1 receptor antagonist gene. For IL1B (-511) polymorphism: dominant (TT + TC vs CC), recessive (TT vs TC + CC), overdominant (CT vs CC+TT), codominant (CT vs CC), codominant# (CT vs TT) and homozygote (TT vs CC). For IL1RN (VNTR) polymorphism: dominant (2*2* + 2*1* vs 1*1*), recessive (2*2* vs 2*1* + 1*1*), overdominant (2*1* vs 1*1*+2*2*), codominant (2*1* vs 1*1*), codominant# (2*1*vs 2*2*) and homozygote (2*2* vs 1*1*). • It is unclear whether between study heterogeneity was only considered significant when both the Cochran’s Q test and the I2 test statistics were significant. I would argue that if either were significant, one should perform a sub-group analysis. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have modified the expression in the method section: “Between-study heterogeneity among the studies was tested with Cochran’s Q and the I2 test statistics. I2 was calculated based on the formula I2=100%×(Q-df)/Q. Heterogeneity was regarded as significant when Phet < 0.1 or I2 > 50%. For those with significant heterogeneity, we performed stratified analyses to examine the statistical significance of the difference in ORs according to ethnicity (East Asian, South Asian, North African and Caucasian).” • I disagree with using different association test methods in the presence of significant heterogeneity vs without significant heterogeneity. The authors should use a single test for association and in the case of heterogeneity, perform sub-group analyses. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. Our analyses were all used random model, and we have revised the description in the method section: “We used the random-effects model (DerSimonian and Laird method) to calculate the pooled OR and 95% CI, with Pz < 0.05 considered statistically significant” • Genetic associations are known to vary widely by ancestry due to differing allele frequencies. As cohorts from East Asia, South-East Asia and North Africa have been included in this analysis, results should be stratified by ethnicity. Table 3 shows the results for “total” vs “EA” while Figure 2 shows the results within each ancestry subgroup. The association estimates for each ancestry are robust to confounding by ancestry but the total meta-analysis estimate is likely to be confounded and should therefore not be presented in Table 3. Related to this, the heterogeneity estimates for the total meta-analysis show significant heterogeneity, which is contributing to the non-significant effect of IL-1 levels in the total meta-analysis. The methods also do not mention whether stratifying by ancestry was considered. In order to accurately ascertain the association between genetically mediated IL-1 levels and T2D risk, the authors need to present their findings in Table 3 stratified by ancestry. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the stratified results in Table 3, and we have added the description of stratifying by ancestry in the method section: “For those with significant heterogeneity, we performed stratified analyses to examine the statistical significance of the difference in ORs according to ethnicity (East Asian, South Asian, North African and Caucasian).” • It is unclear how the significance thresholds for statistically significant heterogeneity between studies were ascertained. The authors should provide an indication of whether this was determined by the number of included studies or another method. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have written “Between-study heterogeneity among the studies was tested with Cochran’s Q and the I2 test statistics. I2 was calculated based on the formula I2=100%×(Q-df)/Q. Heterogeneity was regarded as significant when Phet < 0.1 or I2 > 50%.” in the method section. • The sensitivity analyses described in the discussion are not mentioned in the methods section. These should be fully explained for a thorough understanding of the analyses conducted. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the description of the sensitivity analyses in the mothed section: “When the heterogeneity was significant, sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the influence of each single study by omitting one study at a time and checking the pool effect size for the remainder of the studies.” • The raw data from each of the publications was used in each case, without controlling for established confounders such as age, sex, lifestyle etc. While the authors acknowledge this in the discussion, it does emphasize that the estimates from this study are likely to be highly confounded and potentially invalid. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. All ORs in the included studies were not adjusted by age, sex, lifestyle etc. and the ORs in meta-analysis were calculated by using the numbers of individuals under each genetic phenotype in each included study. In this study, we performed stratified and sensitivity analyses, both of which were conducted to remove the impact of potential confounding factors to ensure our results more reasonable and convincing. Methods described with sufficient detail & information to replicate • The following basic reporting guidelines are followed: the authors who performed the systematic search are identified, PRISMA flow diagram is figure 1, PRISMA checklist is present. However, the authors have not provided a completed checklist outlining information about the genetic meta-analysis (genetics checklist). In addition, it is not clear where the systematic review has been registered (registration number: 268494). It is not registered at PROSPERO or CAMARADES Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have registered at PROSPERO, and the ID is CRD42021268494. We have provided the NOS scale to assess the scoring of the included articles. In addition, according to your comments, we also performed the STREGA scale (genetics checklist) which can be seen in the method section （line182-187） and Table S2 (Supplementary Materials). “And the STREGA (Strengthening the REporting of Genetic Association) system was also performed to assessed the methodological quality of all included studies, which includes 22 items with scoring from 0 to 22 (detailed scores see Table S2) (Little et al. 2009). And the score of high quality was 18-22; the score of moderate-high quality was 13-17; the score of low quality was 0-12 (Duan et al. 2018).” • It is unclear how the significance thresholds for statistically significant heterogeneity between studies were ascertained. The authors should provide an indication of whether this was determined by the number of included studies or another method. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have revised according to your comments: “Between-study heterogeneity among the studies was tested with Cochran’s Q and the I2 test statistics. I2 was calculated based on the formula I2=100%×(Q-df)/Q. Heterogeneity was regarded as significant when Phet < 0.1 or I2 > 50%.” (line195-198). • It is unclear from the methods section whether inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to estimate the effect of IL-1 levels on T2D risk. This needs to be clarified in the methods. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have revised the description in the methods section: “We used the random-effects model (DerSimonian and Laird method) which was combined by applying inverse variance-weighted meta-analysis to calculate the pooled OR and 95% CI, with Pz < 0.05 considered statistically significant.” Validity of the findings As outlined in previous sections, the authors used the raw data from each of the publications to conduct their analysis. As they outline in the discussion, they did not correct for any study level covariates, leading to serious methodological questions about the validity of the results which are likely confounded. In addition, some of the statistical methodology concerning stratification by ancestry and between study heterogeneity needs to be reconsidered. All details of my suggestions are outlined above. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have modified the descriptions in the Abstracts, Introduction, Method, and Result sections based on the reviewers’ comments, and have revised the issues raised by the reviewers accordingly. To reviewer 3: Basic reporting The article is well written and easy to read. The background and references provided are exhaustive, I found only one reference missing when commenting on the VNTRs frequency (line 107). Figures and tables are well detailed. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. We have added the reference about the VNTRs frequency: “IL-1RN 1* (4 repeats) and IL-1RN 2* (2 repeats) are the most common, whereas the others occur much less frequently (< 5%) (Santtila et al. 1998)” (line 131) Santtila S, Savinainen K, and Hurme M. 1998. Presence of the IL-1RA allele 2 (IL1RN*2) is associated with enhanced IL-1beta production in vitro. Scand J Immunol 47:195-198. 10.1046/j.1365-3083.1998.00300.x Experimental design The aim of the study is clearly stated, as well as the strategy (e.g. inclusion criteria) used to perform the analysis. The statistical approach used seems appropriate and all the analyses performed are well described. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. Validity of the findings The results are well presented, discussion and conclusions are exhaustive. The meta-analysis performed in the present study is comprehensive, well performed from a statistical point of view, and provides new evidences in favor of the association of IL-1B and IL-1RN variants with T2DM risk. Thank you very much for your kindly comments. Best regards! Sincerely yours, Huiping YUAN, MD & Ph.D. The MOH Key Laboratory of Geriatrics, Beijing Hospital, National Center of Gerontology, Beijing, P.R. China. paper_title_zh: IL-1B (-511)/IL-1RN (VNTR) 多态性与2型糖尿病的关联：系统综述与Meta分析
paper_abstract_zh: 白细胞介素-1（IL-1）在免疫促炎过程中发挥重要作用，被认为是2型糖尿病（T2DM）发展的众多因素之一。
review_content_zh:
审稿人2：基本报告
清晰、无歧义的语言
• 摘要的第一句指出“白细胞介素-1（IL-1）在免疫促炎过程中起着至关重要的作用，诱导2型糖尿病（T2DM）的发展。”这种表述形式似乎暗示IL-1水平是T2D的致病原因。然而，T2D是一种受多种环境、种族和遗传因素影响的复杂疾病。这句话需要重新措辞，以明确免疫炎症是T2D发展的众多因素之一。非常感谢您的宝贵意见。我们已经修改了这句话：“白细胞介素-1（IL-1）在免疫促炎过程中起着至关重要的作用，这被认为是2型糖尿病（T2DM）发展的众多因素之一。”
• 手稿中使用的变异标识符是可以接受的，然而，如果能在首次提及变异时提供dbSNP标识符或染色体：位置坐标，尤其是摘要中，将对读者有所帮助。此外，对于错义变异，请指明在氨基酸序列中的哪个位置发生替换，以及被替换的氨基酸和替换后的氨基酸。例如，Arg358Pro。非常感谢您的宝贵意见。我们已经修改了摘要和引言中的句子：“几项病例对照研究已经阐明了IL-1B（-511）（rs16944，Chr 2:112,837,290，C/T基因内，转换替换）和IL-1RN（VNTR）（IL-1受体拮抗剂基因，IL-1RA，内含子2中的86 bp串联重复）多态性与T2DM风险的相关性。”和“在启动子区域，IL-1B（-511）（rs16944，Chr 2:112,837,290，C/T基因内，转换替换）在-511位置有一个双等位基因多态性，代表C/T转换。IL-1RN（VNTR）（IL-1受体拮抗剂基因，IL-1RA，内含子2中的86 bp串联重复）有5种不同的等位基因：1*（4次重复），2*（2次重复），3*（5次重复），4*（3次重复）和5*（6次重复）。由于IL-1B（-511）是基因内的，而IL-1RN（VNTR）是86 bp串联重复，它们不会导致氨基酸的替换。”
• 第66行将“sensitive”改为“sensitivity”
非常感谢您的宝贵意见。我们已经将“sensitive”改为“sensitivity”。（第70行）
• 第87行：“epidemic”一词在这里不合逻辑。考虑将其改为“prevalent”
非常感谢您的宝贵意见。我们已经将“epidemic”改为“prevalent”。（第89行）

However, greater emphasis on findings from previous observational studies such as Spranger 2003 and genetic studies needs to be highlighted.
In addition, the findings from previous genetic studies need to be discussed in more detail.
Either a more suitable reference needs to be found that demonstrates these effects, or this statement needs to be amended with demonstrable findings from the literature.

The following statement in the discussion (lines 257-260): “Eventually, it was suggested that IL-1β can induce the inflammatory microenvironment of islets, leading to impaired insulin secretion, decreased cell proliferation and apoptosis of β-cells, ultimately contributing to the development of T2DM.” references an article about IDDM which is type 1 diabetes.

The original research question was well defined, meaningful and relevant but was not convincingly assessed due to issues with the statistical methodology.

Figures and tables are well detailed.
The aim of the study is clearly stated, as well as the strategy (e.g. inclusion criteria) used to perform the analysis.

paper_title: Dance/movement therapy as a holistic approach to diminish health discrepancies and promote wellness for people with schizophrenia: a review of the literature
paper_abstract: Individuals with a diagnosis of schizophrenia face a myriad of obstacles to wellness, beginning with diagnostic discrepancies including over- and misdiagnoses on the schizophrenia spectrum. People with schizophrenia experience profound amounts of stigmatization from the general population, their healthcare providers, and even themselves. Such stigmatization creates a barrier for wellness, poorer prognoses, and often limits adherence to physical and mental healthcare. Moreover, it can exacerbate the already stifling symptomatology of their diagnoses, including specific bodily-related symptomatology. Oftentimes, a diagnosis of schizophrenia disrupts one’s relationship with their body including a diminished mind-body connection, decreased interoceptive awareness, and thus unsuccessful intra- and interpersonal relationships. Some recent research suggests the use of mind-body therapies, however, if these practices are internalizing, they may not be appropriate for people with schizophrenia experiencing more acute symptomatology excluding them from treatment. Dance/movement therapy (DMT) is an embodied psychotherapeutic treatment option that can support participants in improving mind-body connection, social relationships, and self-regulatory skill development. Research on DMT has shown promising results for people with schizophrenia, however such research is limited and would benefit from increased studies that particularly measure the effects of DMT on mind-body connection and increased interoception for people with schizophrenia. Moreover, integrative and collaborative treatment models that couple DMT and biofeedback may further our understanding of the physiological and neurological effects of DMT interventions for people with schizophrenia and beyond. This review will examine the recent literature on health inequities for people with schizophrenia, their specific body-based disruptions and needs, and DMT as a promising treatment model, particularly when coupled with biofeedback.
review_content:
The scope of this paper is impressive and the arguments for providing care for individuals with schizophrenia that is aligned with care for the whole person continues to be a worthy topic for research and practice. The decades-long focus of pharmacotherapy as the primary treatment for schizophrenia continues to show progress, but the need for other treatment modalities such as dance/movement therapy (DMT) to address social and psychological components of the illness such as trauma are still required. This review will combine comments with a focus on strengthening the content to help achieve the worthy goals of the paper.

Introduction – I am not completely clear about the meaning of the sentence “Through a strengths- and body-based approach, dance/movement therapy (DMT) surpasses traditional verbal communication, establishing inclusion for many forms of preferred communication styles (Biondo et al., 2021).” especially for readers who may not have an understanding of DMT. I think here in the introduction – an introduction to the field of DMT is warranted. The section that is on page 5 (of the pdf version of the article) could be moved to the introduction and I believe it would be very useful in tying together other sections of the paper for the reader new to DMT. The sections on body symptomatology, interoception, and mind-body treatments could be helped by setting the context early on with what DMT is and the fact that it has been used for decades with seriously mentally ill patients as well as others.

Discussion – I feel that there needs to be more research cited, and more diversity of sources for the important discussion of mental health disparities. Currently there is sole dependence on Metzl & Roberts (2014). In addition the mention of the changes in rates of diagnosis over time fails to mention the important fact that diagnostic criteria have changed quite drastically over time as well. To cite myself (Cruz, 1995, p. 38), “Yet a narrowing of diagnostic criteria for schizophrenia has taken place during the last 50 years, changing the determination of who is diagnosed schizophrenic. The DSM-III (1980) represented the sharpest break with previous editions in the definition and diagnostic criteria for schizophrenia (Andreasen & Flaum, 1991). Many forms of the disorder were removed and included in other categories, most notably psychosis not elsewhere classified, affective disorders, and related personality disorders. In spite of this narrowing, research on movement disorders has not regularly included the removed disorders.”

In 1952 DMS I was published and the criteria for schizophrenia as noted above included other disorders that later were winnowed out. DSM II was published in 1968 and DSM III in 1980 – in spite of these changes, it would be good to note if disparities in diagnosis by race continued across the changing symptom criteria.

Also the discussion on stigmatization – other sources should be cited as there is dependence on Rossler (2016). It could be helpful also to make a connection between the discussion on stigmatization and stigmatizing behaviors – it is possible combining the paragraph that begins “Stigmatization also affects people with schizophrenia on personal and social levels.” with the section located under the heading “physical health disparities” could be helpful for the reader.

Think about the sections in “Mental Health Disparities” and “Physical Health Disparities” as setting up the reader for better understanding of why DMT has the potential to promote wellness for this group. I think it is necessary to distinguish better between “Body symptomatology” and “Bodily disturbances…” as what is described under body symptomatology are abnormal involuntary movements which can be naturally occurring or side effects of pharmacology but are related to dysfunction of neurotransmitters of the extrapyramidal system (Cruz, 1995; 2009). I also think that the text in the “Bodily disturbances section could more meaningfully be combined with the “Interoception” section of the paper – they cross-over in ways that might be confusing to the reader not familiar with these terms.

I am curious what the real purpose of the “Mind-body treatments” section is and if the author thinks of DMT as a mind-body treatment? If so this needs to be clarified for the reader so that the DMT research section (which is brief and does not include any meta-analyses that have been conducted) is clear and then clearly separated from the theoretical sections that follow. These theoretical areas “embodied aesthetics framework and embodied neurology need better framing as theoretical frameworks. How those frameworks might directly impact work with schizophrenic patients needs more obvious connection for the reader.

I am also curious about the inclusion of biofeedback which is a bonafide technique and neurofeedback with seems to be theoretical – what could be learned or achieved with it? They don’t seem to “fit” very well with this paper.

Conclusion – may serve as a good guide for the reorganizing that I’ve suggested in this review. It is comprehensive of the major points in a very clear manner that serves the paper well.
paper_title_zh: 舞蹈/动作疗法作为减少精神分裂症患者健康差异并促进其整体健康的整体方法：文献综述
paper_abstract_zh: 被诊断为精神分裂症的个体在追求健康的过程中面临着诸多障碍，首先是从诊断上的差异，包括对精神分裂症谱系的过度诊断和误诊。精神分裂症患者从普通人群、他们的医疗保健提供者甚至自身经历着深重的污名化。这种污名化构成了健康的障碍，导致预后较差，并常常限制了对身体和心理健康保健的依从性。此外，它还可能加剧他们诊断中已经令人窒息的症状学，包括特定的与身体相关的症状学。通常情况下，精神分裂症的诊断会破坏个体与其身体的关系，包括心身连接的减弱、内感觉意识的下降，从而导致内在和人际关系的失败。一些近期研究表明，心身疗法的使用可能有益，然而，如果这些实践是内化的，它们可能不适合经历更急性症状的精神分裂症患者，从而将他们排除在治疗之外。舞蹈/动作疗法（DMT）是一种体现心理治疗的治疗选择，可以支持参与者改善心身连接、社会关系和自我调节技能的发展。关于DMT的研究对精神分裂症患者显示出有希望的结果，然而这类研究有限，并将从更多特别测量DMT对精神分裂症患者心身连接和内感觉增加影响的研究中受益。此外，将DMT与生物反馈相结合的综合和协作治疗模式，可能进一步加深我们对DMT干预对精神分裂症患者及更广泛人群的生理和神经效应的理解。本综述将考察关于精神分裂症患者健康不平等的近期文献，他们特定的基于身体的干扰和需求，以及DMT作为一种有前景的治疗模式，尤其是当其与生物反馈结合时。
review_content_zh:
本文的研究范围令人印象深刻，主张为精神分裂症患者提供与整体护理相一致的关怀，这一议题在研究和实践中仍具有重要价值。尽管数十年来以药物治疗作为精神分裂症的主要治疗方法取得了进展，但仍然需要其他治疗方式，如舞蹈/动作治疗（DMT），以解决疾病的社会和心理成分，如创伤。本评论将结合评论内容，重点强化文章内容，以帮助实现论文的崇高目标。

引言——我对“通过基于优势和身体的 approach，舞蹈/动作治疗（DMT）超越了传统的言语交流，为多种偏好的交流风格建立了包容性（Biondo 等人，2021）”这句话的含义不太清楚，尤其是对于那些可能不了解 DMT 的读者。我认为在引言部分——对 DMT 领域的介绍是必要的。文章第 5 页（pdf 版本）的部分可以移至引言，我相信这对将文章的其他部分联系起来，对初次接触 DMT 的读者非常有用。关于身体症状学、内感觉和身心治疗的部分，可以通过早期介绍 DMT 的内容和其数十年来在严重精神疾病患者及其他人群中的应用，来帮助设定背景。

讨论——我认为需要引用更多研究，并在心理健康差异的重要讨论中增加更多来源的多样性。目前完全依赖于 Metzl & Roberts (2014) 的研究。此外，提及诊断率随时间的变化时，未能提到诊断标准也随时间发生了巨大变化这一重要事实。引用我自己的话（Cruz, 1995, p. 38），“然而，在过去 50 年中，精神分裂症的诊断标准已经缩小，改变了谁被诊断为精神分裂症的决定。DSM-III（1980）在精神分裂症的定义和诊断标准上与之前版本有最明显的断裂（Andreasen & Flaum, 1991）。许多形式的疾病被移除并归入其他类别，最明显的是未分类的精神病、情感障碍和相关的人格障碍。尽管如此，关于运动障碍的研究并未经常包括被移除的疾病。”

1952 年发布的 DMS I 中，精神分裂症的诊断标准如上所述，包括后来被剔除的其他疾病。1968 年发布 DSM II，1980 年发布 DSM III——尽管有这些变化，但应指出是否种族间的诊断差异在变化的症状标准中持续存在。

此外，关于污名化的讨论——应引用其他来源，目前依赖于 Rossler (2016) 的研究。将污名化讨论与污名化行为联系起来也可能有帮助——将“污名化还影响精神分裂症患者的个人和社会层面”开头的段落与“身体健康差异”标题下的部分结合起来，可能对读者有帮助。

将“心理健康差异”和“身体健康差异”部分视为为读者更好地理解 DMT 如何有潜力促进这一群体健康做铺垫。我认为有必要更好地区分“身体症状学”和“身体紊乱……”因为在身体症状学下描述的是异常不自主运动，这些可能是自然发生的或药物副作用，但与外锥体系统神经递质的功能障碍有关（Cruz, 1995; 2009）。我还认为“身体紊乱”部分的内容可以更有意义地与文章的“内感觉”部分结合——它们在方式上有交叉，可能会让不熟悉这些术语的读者感到困惑。

我对“身心治疗”部分的真实目的感到好奇，作者是否认为 DMT 是一种身心治疗？如果是这样，需要为读者澄清，以便 DMT 研究部分（内容简短且未包括已进行的任何元分析）清晰，并与随后的理论部分明确区分。这些理论领域“具身美学框架和具身神经学”需要更好地作为理论框架来构建。这些框架如何直接影响精神分裂症患者的治疗，需要为读者提供更明显的联系。

我还对生物反馈的纳入感到好奇，这是一种公认的技巧，而神经反馈似乎更具理论性——通过它们可以学到或实现什么？它们似乎与本文不太“契合”。

结论——可以作为我在这篇评论中建议的重构的良好指南。它以非常清晰的方式综合了主要观点，对文章很有帮助。

paper_title: The imperative to find the courage to redesign the biomedical research enterprise
paper_abstract: Medical research aims to improve health for everyone. While its advances are undeniable, the pace and cost of the progress are not optimal. For example, independent analyses concluded that at least half of the published biomedical research findings are irreproducible, and most scientific papers are never read or cited. This paper examines biomedical research holistically, as a system of incentives that shape the behavior of scientists, administrators, publishers, and funders, and are detrimental to medical progress. We identify opportunities to change and improve those incentives by altering the way research output is disseminated and evaluated, and recommend transparent, data-driven measures of methodological rigor, reproducibility, and societal value of scientific discoveries. Embracing these opportunities would maximize our investments in biomedical research and optimize its value to human health, while simultaneously increasing freedom, creativity, and satisfaction of the scientific workforce.
review_content:
Thank you for inviting me to review the Opinion Article by Drs. Bielekova and Brownlee, entitled "The imperative to find the courage to redesign the biomedical research enterprise".

In this piece, the authors argue that the incentive structure of modern biomedical research does not align with its supposed mission, and propose a series of changes that could reform this incentive structure in a way that they believe will "maximize our investments in biomedical research and optimize its value to human health".

The authors build their argument on the now quite mature literature documenting the so-called "reproducibility crisis". I tend to agree with the authors that this is a serious and urgent issue, and indeed many of the reforms proposed by the authors strike me as sensible. Despite this, however, I find a number of elements of the authors' argument hard to follow or poorly supported.

The authors begin by using the NIH as their dominant institutional example, and compare it to the Apollo Mission and the Manhattan Project, which they present as two enterprises with clearer, mission-driven management. I find this comparison, at minimum, unhelpful. First, let's be clear that the mission of one of these projects was the production of an instrument of mass death, which makes for a poor comparison to the NIH. That aside, both were much more defined projects with clear end-points, making any comparison to the NIH hard for me to really engage with. I think, in any analysis, the NIH and the research it has funded would be found to have had a far more positive impact on humanity than either of these projects.

I would prefer to see a more informed comparison between the NIH and other organizations of similar scale or purpose. Can the authors support their argument that the NIH's system of organization is non-optimal by providing more relevant examples of organizations that have been able to more efficiently advance human health research?

The authors then propose a framework of radical changes to the way that scientific publications are published, assessed, and to how they are used to evaluate research programs and researchers. Before I address the authors' specific proposal, I would like to note that at this point I have lost the connection to the authors' original argument that the NIH's organizational system should be more mission-driven. The changes being proposed here reach far beyond the NIH's scope and its leverage to implement.

Central to the authors' proposal is a network based, multi-criteria method for assessing the value of scientific publications, which they call the BRN for "biomedical research network". I like some of the ideas embedded in this concept, but as a whole I remain far from convinced that this is technically feasible or that the ratings of a such system would better align with the NIH's mission. I appreciate that this is an opinion paper, but the BRN proposal being put forward is relatively specific, and I think should be supported with some evidence of feasibility for a scholarly work of this kind.

I question whether reviewers could reliably quantify "methodological rigor", in a manner that would be meaningful across topics and disciplines. I am also not convinced that an automated system could identify related publications with sufficient semantic rigor to allow any calculations of reproducibility, in the manner proposed by the authors. Similarly, how would one rate social or commercial impact objectively in the short term, when these kinds of impacts often take years or even decades to mature?

These concerns are not trivial in my mind, since we have already seen the harm that poorly designed metrics have done to the scientific enterprise. I share the authors' concern about the reproducibility crisis, but I think there are very legitimate concerns in the scientific community that a rush to create new reproducibility metrics, could end up causing further harm, for example, by de-incentivizing cutting edge or interdisciplinary research where standards are still evolving and sparser research networks means that reproducibility is harder to assess.

In the rest of the paper, the authors make further recommendations, endorsing rating reviewers, open peer-review, dynamic publications, and data sharing, among other ideas. These are sensible recommendations, although I feel the authors do not manage to relate all of them directly back to their idea that biomedical science organizations should be more mission-driven.

Overall, I am sympathetic to many of the authors' ideas and the overall sense of urgency that pervades the piece, but I am not convinced at this stage that the authors have made a coherent argument for how biomedical research could be reformed.

My advice, were the authors to consider developing this further, would be to think more critically about how the NIH or a similar organization could specifically enact change, using the tools and leverage available to it, and expounding more on how such an organization could concretely use mission-driven assessments to improve its outputs. As a reader, I personally would like to see this supported with more relevant organizational management comparisons, and some consideration of the costs of the proposed reforms relative to current organizational systems.

The BRN itself, while interesting, feels too underdeveloped at this stage. For such a proposal, I would like to see at least some evidence of feasibility, including numerical rankings and networking-building with actual papers.

Finally, I would like to note that this paper at present is generally well written, after setting aside my more conceptual criticisms above.
paper_title_zh: 重设计生物医药研究体系的勇气之必要性
paper_abstract_zh: 医学研究的目的是改善每个人的健康状况。尽管其进步不可否认，但进展的速度和成本并非最优。例如，独立分析得出结论，至少有一半已发表的生物医学研究成果无法重现，而且大多数科学论文从未被阅读或引用。本文全面审视生物医学研究，将其视为一个激励系统，这些激励塑造了科学家、管理者、出版商和资助者的行为，并对医学进步产生不利影响。我们识别了通过改变研究成果的传播和评估方式来改变和改进这些激励的机会，并推荐透明、数据驱动的方法来衡量方法论严谨性、可重现性以及科学发现的社会价值。抓住这些机会将最大化我们在生物医学研究中的投资，优化其对人类健康的价值，同时增加科研人员的自由度、创造力和满意度。
review_content_zh:
感谢您邀请我审阅Bielekova博士和Brownlee博士撰写的观点文章，题为“寻找勇气重新设计生物医学研究体系的必要性”。

在这篇文章中，作者认为现代生物医学研究的激励机制与其所谓的使命不相符，并提出了一系列改革措施，他们认为这些改革将“最大化我们对生物医学研究的投资，并优化其对人类健康的价值”。

作者基于现已相当成熟的文献，论证了所谓的“可重复性危机”。我倾向于同意作者的观点，认为这是一个严重且紧迫的问题，事实上，作者提出的许多改革措施在我看来是合理的。尽管如此，我还是发现作者论证中的某些要素难以理解或缺乏支持。

作者首先以美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）作为其主要机构案例，并将其与阿波罗计划和曼哈顿计划进行比较，这两个计划被他们描绘为具有更清晰、使命驱动型管理的项目。我认为这种比较至少是无益的。首先，我们必须明确，其中一个项目的使命是制造大规模杀伤性武器，这与NIH的比较并不恰当。除此之外，这两个项目都是定义更明确、有明确终点的项目，使得与NIH的比较让我难以真正参与。我认为，在任何分析中，NIH及其资助的研究对人类的影响都远比这两个项目更为积极。

我更希望看到NIH与其他类似规模或目的的组织之间进行更有见地的比较。作者能否通过提供更多相关组织的例子来支持其观点，即NIH的组织体系并非最优？

作者随后提出了对科学出版物发布、评估方式以及如何用于评估研究项目和研究人员的一系列根本性变革框架。在我讨论作者的具体建议之前，我想指出，在这一点上，我已经失去了与作者最初论点——即NIH的组织体系应更具使命驱动性——的联系。这里提出的变革远远超出了NIH的范畴及其实施的影响力。

作者建议的核心是一个基于网络的、多标准方法来评估科学出版物的价值，他们称之为“生物医学研究网络”（BRN）。我喜欢这一概念中包含的一些想法，但总体上，我远未信服这在技术上是可行的，或者这种系统的评级能更好地与NIH的使命相一致。我理解这是一篇观点文章，但提出的BRN建议相对具体，我认为应该提供一些可行性的证据，以支持这类学术作品。

我质疑评审者是否能够可靠地量化“方法论的严谨性”，并以一种在各个主题和学科中都具意义的方式进行。我也不相信自动化系统能够以足够的语义严谨性识别相关出版物，从而允许进行作者所提议的可重复性计算。同样，如何在短期内客观地评估社会或商业影响，当这些影响往往需要数年甚至数十年才能显现？

在我看来，这些担忧并非微不足道，因为我们已经看到了设计不当的指标对科学事业的危害。我认同作者对可重复性危机的担忧，但我认为科学界有非常合理的担忧，即急于创建新的可重复性指标可能会造成进一步的伤害，例如，通过降低对前沿或跨学科研究的激励，这些领域中的标准仍在演变，稀疏的研究网络意味着可重复性更难评估。

在文章的其余部分，作者进一步提出建议，支持评级评审者、开放同行评审、动态出版物和数据共享等想法。这些建议是合理的，尽管我觉得作者未能将所有建议直接与其观点——即生物医学科学组织应更具使命驱动性——联系起来。

总体而言，我对作者许多想法以及文章中弥漫的紧迫感表示同情，但在此阶段，我尚未被作者关于如何改革生物医学研究的连贯论证所说服。

如果作者考虑进一步发展这一观点，我的建议是更批判性地思考NIH或类似组织如何具体实施变革，利用其可用的工具和影响力，并更详细地阐述此类组织如何具体使用使命驱动的评估来改善其产出。作为读者，我个人希望看到更多相关组织管理比较的支持，以及对所提议改革相对于当前组织系统的成本的考虑。

BRN本身虽然有趣，但在这一阶段感觉过于不成熟。对于这样的提议，我希望至少看到一些可行性的证据，包括实际论文的数值排名和网络构建。

最后，我想指出，撇开我上述更多的概念性批评不谈，这篇文章目前在写作上总体上是良好的。

paper_title: A Survey of Temporal Credit Assignment in Deep Reinforcement Learning
paper_abstract: The Credit Assignment Problem (CAP) refers to the longstanding challenge of Reinforcement Learning agents to associate actions with their long-term consequences. Solving the CAP is a crucial step towards the successful deployment of RL in the real world since most decision problems provide feedback that is noisy, delayed, and with little or no information about the causes. These conditions make it hard to distinguish serendipitous outcomes from those caused by informed decision-making. However, the mathematical nature of credit and the CAP remains poorly understood and defined. In this survey, we review the state of the art of Temporal Credit Assignment (CA) in deep RL. We propose a unifying formalism for credit that enables equitable comparisons of state-of-the-art algorithms and improves our understanding of the trade-offs between the various methods. We cast the CAP as the problem of learning the influence of an action over an outcome from a finite amount of experience. We discuss the challenges posed by delayed effects, dilution, and a lack of action influence, and analyse how existing methods aim to address them. Finally, we survey the protocols to evaluate a credit assignment method and suggest ways to diagnose the sources of struggle for different methods. Overall, this survey provides an overview of the field for new-entry practitioners and researchers, it offers a coherent perspective for scholars looking to expedite the starting stages of a new study on the CAP, and it suggests potential directions for future research.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper surveys the area of temporal credit assignment in deep reinforcement learning. This paper seeks to organize and compare different types of credit assignment, challenges to credit assignment, methods for learning credit assignment, and credit assignment evaluation procedures from the literature. Toward this end, this paper formalizes notions of action influence and credit assignment, describes desirable properties for an action influence, and organizes contributions by building on these theoretical foundations.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
The first three sections of the paper are an effective setup for a survey on this topic. Section 4 is an interesting discussion and formalization of credit assignment. Section 5 thoughtfully teases apart different types of challenges for effective credit assignment in MDPs. Unfortunately, Sections 6 and 7 do not make the best use of these foundations. For example, Table 4 contains some interesting claims about the types of challenges defined in Section 5 that different methods address, but it is unclear to me how this table was constructed and I could not find any reference to the table in the text for further discussion. The paper varies significantly in quality and attention to detail across sections. The paper is largely well written up to Section 4. Section 4 is careful about defining common terms such as "goal", "outcome", "(action) influence", and "(credit) assignment", while the sections that follow are more ambiguous in their language, particularly around the terms "value" and "return". It is often unclear to me if these "values" and "returns" are meant to reference only cumulative or discounted future rewards, and thus only pertain to state value, action value, or advantage credit assignments only or if they are referring to "values" and "returns" in a more general sense. The method descriptions in Section 6 can be effective in that they describe how a method works and how it relates to previously discussed concepts. For example, the RUDDER subsection in Section 6.2 is effective in this way (in spite of some shortcomings, see items in Requested Changes on this subsection). These method descriptions can also be poor in that they do little more than present a reference and a high level description of the algorithm, without highlighting its relationship to credit assignment. For example, the PGIF subsection in Section 6.4.2. The summaries at the subsections in Section 6 are confusing. Related, summaries or later parts of the paper may make strong declarative statements that are surprising given the previous content. For example, in the summary of Section 6.2, it states that a measure of action influence is not a satisfactory quantification of credit and cites Section 4.3, but Section 4.3 defines a general notion of assignment that each quantity talked about so far fits within. Another example is in the third paragraph of Section 8.1 where it states that "we highlighted that current benchmarks are not fit for the purpose". While "the purpose" could be clarified, my sense of the discussion of benchmarks in the previous section were that each benchmark had something different to offer, not that all of them were critically lacking.

**Requested Changes:**
Please improve Section 6 to explain how each learning method relates or could be combined with each type of assignment described in the previous Section. Please improve the summaries in Section 6. Please make the paper more consistent across Sections in terms of the claims that are made. Please edit the paper to correct typos, improve wording, add missing words, and clarify references. Some examples in no particular order: 1. At the end of Section 4.1, the last bullet point is missing an "s" and a word. I expect is should read "Section 4.6 distils the properties that existing measure*s* of action influence **exhibit**." 2. There appears to be a hat missing from $V$ in Equation (30). 3. In the summary of Section 6.2, it is unclear to what "their" is referring in the sentence, "Despite their measure of action influence not being a satisfactory quantification of credit . . ." 4. In the last sentence of the summary of Section 6.2, it is unclear to what "these models" refers. 6. In the RUDDER subsection in Section 6.2 just after Equation (20), what is $\mathcal{M}^*$? 7. In the RUDDER subsection, you have $g = z^* \in \mathbb{R}$ at the end of the sentence as if it's describing an optimal policy but I think you meant to describe the maximum expected return. In addition to this confusion, I do not understand why the symbols $g$ and $z^*$ are used here, especially when $g$ is used for the function that returns the discounted sum of rewards along a trajectory, $d$. I also do not understand how $g$ can generate that output without being an explicit function of $d$. 8. Section 5.4 is particularly confusing. The second paragraph of Section 5.4 especially contains many typos and awkward wordings. 9. The first sentence in Section 8.1, "tree" -> "three". All of these issues should be addressed for me to recommend acceptance.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
No broader impact concerns.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Official response to Reviewer 3PaG: Thank you very much for the constructive review and the valuable insights on the manuscript. To address the concerns raised above: > Please improve Section 6 to explain how each learning method relates or could be combined with each type of assignment described in the previous Section. - We have thoroughly improved Section 6 and increased its level of detail. In particular, we ensured that the foundational concepts laid out in the initial sections are consistently applied throughout. - We have added a more rigorous definition of a credit assignment method that uses the foundations laid in Section 4. - We have added details to the classes of methods about which measure of influence they use and better highlighted pros and cons of the methods. > Please improve the summaries in Section 6. > Please make the paper more consistent across Sections in terms of the claims that are made. - We have removed the unsupported claims from the summary of Section 6 and checked all the other summaries for consistency, making sure that they contain only claims that are well-supported. > Please edit the paper to correct typos, improve wording, add missing words, and clarify references. > Some examples in no particular order: $[\ldots]$ - Finally, we went through the entire document to correct typos, improve wording, add missing words, and clarify equations and references as per the examples provided by the reviewers.
paper_title_zh: 深度强化学习中时间信用分配综述
paper_abstract_zh: 信用分配问题（CAP）指的是强化学习代理将行动与其长期后果相关联的长期挑战。解决CAP是实现强化学习在现实世界中成功部署的关键步骤，因为大多数决策问题提供的反馈是噪声大、延迟长，且几乎不提供或完全不提供关于原因的信息。这些条件使得难以区分偶然结果与由知情决策导致的结果。然而，信用的数学本质以及CAP仍然未被充分理解和定义。在这篇综述中，我们回顾了深度强化学习中时间信用分配（CA）的最新研究进展。我们提出了一种统一的信用形式化方法，使得可以对最先进算法进行公平比较，并提高我们对各种方法之间权衡的理解。我们将CAP表述为从有限经验中学习行动对结果影响的问题。我们讨论了延迟效应、稀释以及缺乏行动影响所带来的挑战，并分析了现有方法如何旨在解决这些问题。最后，我们综述了评估信用分配方法的协议，并提出了诊断不同方法困境来源的途径。总体而言，这篇综述为新入门的实践者和研究人员提供了该领域的概览，为希望加速新CAP研究起步阶段的学者提供了一个连贯的视角，并指出了未来研究的潜在方向。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文综述了深度强化学习中时间信用分配的领域。本文旨在组织和比较文献中不同类型的信用分配、信用分配的挑战、学习信用分配的方法以及信用分配评估程序。为此，本文形式化了动作影响和信用分配的概念，描述了动作影响的理想属性，并通过这些理论基础来组织贡献。

**优点和缺点：**
论文的前三节为该主题的综述提供了有效的铺垫。第4节是对信用分配的有趣讨论和形式化。第5节深入剖析了在马尔可夫决策过程（MDP）中有效信用分配的不同类型挑战。遗憾的是，第6节和第7节并未充分利用这些基础。例如，表4包含了一些关于第5节定义的不同方法所应对挑战类型的有趣论断，但我不清楚这张表是如何构建的，并且在文本中找不到任何关于该表的进一步讨论。论文在各个章节的质量和细节关注上差异显著。直到第4节，论文总体上写得很好。第4节在定义“目标”、“结果”、“（动作）影响”和“（信用）分配”等常见术语时非常谨慎，而后续章节在语言上更为模糊，尤其是在“价值”和“回报”等术语上。我常常不清楚这些“价值”和“回报”是否仅指累积或折现的未来奖励，从而仅涉及状态价值、动作价值或优势信用分配，或者它们是在更一般的意义上使用。第6节中的方法描述在解释方法如何工作及其与先前讨论概念的关系方面可能是有效的。例如，第6.2节的RUDDER子节在这方面是有效的（尽管存在一些不足，见“请求的更改”中对这一子节的条目）。这些方法描述也可能较差，因为它们只是提供了一个参考文献和算法的高级描述，而没有突出其与信用分配的关系。例如，第6.4.2节的PGIF子节。第6节各子节的总结令人困惑。相关地，论文后部分的总结或声明可能会因前文内容而显得出人意料。例如，在第6.2节的总结中，提到动作影响的度量不是信用的满意量化，并引用了第4.3节，但第4.3节定义了一个一般的分配概念，迄今为止讨论的每个量都符合这一概念。另一个例子是在第8.1节的第三段中，提到“我们强调当前的基准不适合这一目的”。虽然“这一目的”可以澄清，但我觉得前文对基准的讨论是每个基准都有不同的贡献，而不是所有基准都严重不足。

**请求的更改：**
请改进第6节，解释每种学习方法如何与前一节描述的每种分配类型相关或可以结合。请改进第6节的总结。请使论文在各个章节中的论断更加一致。请编辑论文以纠正错别字、改进措辞、添加缺失的词语并澄清参考文献。以下是一些例子（不分顺序）：1. 在第4.1节末尾，最后一个项目符号缺少一个“s”和一个词。我预计应该是“第4.6节提炼了现有动作影响度量**所展示**的性质。”2. 方程（30）中的$V$似乎缺少一个帽子符号。3. 在第6.2节的总结中，句子“尽管他们的动作影响度量不是信用的满意量化……”中的“他们的”指代不明。4. 在第6.2节总结的最后一句话中，“这些模型”指代不明。6. 在第6.2节的RUDDER子节中，方程（20）之后，$\mathcal{M}^*$是什么？7. 在RUDDER子节中，句末的$g = z^* \in \mathbb{R}$似乎在描述一个最优策略，但我想您 meant to describe the maximum expected return. 除了这种混淆之外，我不明白为什么在这里使用符号$g$和$z^*$，尤其是当$g$用于表示沿轨迹$d$的折现奖励总和的函数时。我也不明白$g$如何在不显式依赖于$d$的情况下生成该输出。8. 第5.4节特别令人困惑。第5.4节的第二段尤其包含许多错别字和awkward wordings。9. 第8.1节的第一句话，“tree”应改为“three”。所有这些问题都应解决，以便我推荐接受。

**更广泛的影响关切：**
无更广泛的影响关切。

**论断和证据：**
是

**受众：**

paper_title: Osteokines and the vasculature: a review of the in vitro effects of osteocalcin, fibroblast growth factor-23 and lipocalin-2
paper_abstract: Bone-derived factors that demonstrate extra-skeletal functions, also termed osteokines, are fast becoming a highly interesting and focused area of cross-disciplinary endocrine research. Osteocalcin (OCN), fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF23) and lipocalin-2 (LCN-2), produced in bone, comprise an important endocrine system that is finely tuned with other organs to ensure homeostatic balance and health. This review aims to evaluate in vitro evidence of the direct involvement of these proteins in vascular cells and whether any causal roles in cardiovascular disease or inflammation can be supported. PubMed, Medline, Embase and Google Scholar were searched for relevant research articles investigating the exogenous addition of OCN, FGF23 or LCN-2 to vascular smooth muscle or endothelial cells. Overall, these osteokines are directly vasoactive across a range of human and animal vascular cells. Both OCN and FGF23 have anti-apoptotic properties and increase eNOS phosphorylation and nitric oxide production through Akt signalling in human endothelial cells. OCN improves intracellular insulin signalling and demonstrates protective effects against endoplasmic reticulum stress in murine and human endothelial cells. OCN may be involved in calcification but further research is warranted, while there is no evidence for a pro-calcific effect of FGF23 in vitro. FGF23 and LCN-2 increase proliferation in some cell types and increase and decrease reactive oxygen species generation, respectively. LCN-2 also has anti-apoptotic effects but may increase endoplasmic reticulum stress as well as have pro-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic properties in human vascular endothelial and smooth muscle cells. There is no strong evidence to support a pathological role of OCN or FGF23 in the vasculature based on these findings. In contrast, they may in fact support normal endothelial functioning, vascular homeostasis and vasodilation. No studies examined whether OCN or FGF23 may have a role in vascular inflammation. Limited studies with LCN-2 indicate a pro-inflammatory and possible pathological role in the vasculature but further mechanistic data is required. review_content: Reviewer 1 (Anonymous) Basic reporting Thank you so much for taking to time to review our manuscript and for the helpful comments which we hope have now considerably improved the focus and reading of our review. Please find responses below to individual comments. - The tables are a good idea and makes it very easy to interpret each study, however, in general the results and conclusion sections are too long, they should be a summary of what occurs in each study, otherwise it is no different to reading about the study in the main text. Thank you for highlighting this, we have now accordingly reduced the results/conclusions sections and hope you will find them better representative of a summary now. - In the Tables, please ensure a consistent measure of concentration is chosen (for example: ng/ml), to assist the reader in interpreting the differences between the studies. Thank you for highlighting this, all concentrations are now in ng/mL. Experimental design - Too much background information is provided on each osteokine in comparison to the discussion on each osteokine and the vasculature effects. A suggestion would be to remove the subheadings ‘circulating concentrations of…., expression of ….. and endocrine functions of…) and only include background information that is needed to discuss and interpret the vasculature effects. Thank you so much and we agree with your comment. We have removed ‘expression of’ and ‘endocrine function’ sections. We have adjusted the introduction and removed broad information on bone/blood vessels and instead have focused more on the proteins of interest and briefly mention their endocrine history there instead. We have left circulating concentration information as we feel this is useful for interpretation of data and they are quite short sections. - Given that this is not a systematic review why have you included a section on the search strategy? If it was review systematically then that will need to be reflected in the title and follow the appropriate guidelines for systematic reviews. Thank you for your suggestion. Although we searched rather systematically for the studies to be included, the searches and data extraction were completed by only one researcher so the conditions of the review do not satisfy wholly those required for systematic reviews. However, we wish to include the search strategy as suggested in PeerJ guidelines for literature reviews (‘Survey Methodology: Explain how you ensured comprehensive and unbiased coverage of the literature.) and to give confidence to the readership that there is limited chance that papers were overlooked due to the comprehensive search. - At the end of the introduction the aims of the article include a section on the endocrine functions of each osteokine, however, the title for this review is ‘osteokines and the vasculature’ as you pointed out in the text, recent reviews have been completed on the endocrine functions of OCN and FGF-23. It may be beneficial to rethink how much information should be included on the endocrine functions of each osteokine and what is novel about this review, compared to previous ones. Thank you for you highlighting this point. We have tried to significantly re focus and cut down on sections included within the manuscript. We have removed therefore this sentence in the aims of the manuscript which now reads: ‘In order to assess the relevance of these osteokines to cardiovascular health, we aimed to provide an analysis of the direct effects of OCN, FGF23 and LCN-2 on micro- and macro-vascular cells in vitro, and to highlight gaps in the literature which need addressing, for use by clinicians and researchers.’ Validity of the findings - Please describe what is novel about the section on OCN and the vasculature. A recent review ‘Tacey, A., Qaradakhi, T., Brennan-Speranza, T., Hayes, A., Zulli, A., & Levinger, I. (2018). Potential Role for Osteocalcin in the Development of Atherosclerosis and Blood Vessel Disease. Nutrients, 10(10), 1426’ described the effect of OCN on atherosclerosis development and included all of the studies that were included in your discussion. As there have not been any new studies published since the previous review, what is this section adding to the body of knowledge that was not discussed in the recent review? Thank you for a comment. We acknowledge the recent review mentioned and have referenced it in our paper. However our aim was to provide a summary and overview of osteokines and the vasculature, and we feel it is not justified to exclude OCN from the review. We aimed to present a summary of the vasoactive properties of bone derived hormones to give an inclusive view of the novel concept of the skeleton affecting the vascular system. Additionally, we highlight some further areas of interest to clinicians and researchers including circulating levels, and background information of observational human data between osteocalcin and cardiovascular endpoints, and finally highlights gaps in current knowledge which require addressing. - In the summary and conclusion section, line 492 – 493 you describe that the evidence points towards direct vasoactive properties of the osteokines in human and animal cells. However, in the FGF-23 section you describe in lines 376 - 379 ‘The results presented encourages the hypothesis that the associations and correlations between FGF23 and CVD are most likely due to deleterious effects of altered phosphate and mineral metabolism and indeed that FGF23 levels likely follow, as oppose to direct, cardiovascular disturbances.’ Thank you for your comment and we apologise for not being clear. In the conclusion I wish to state that FGF23 has direct vasoactive properties – in that it incurs responses and cell signalling etc. – however this does not appear to indicate a direct relationship with cardiovascular pathologies, and that the correlations seen between FGF23 and CVD are likely due to the altered phosphate/mineral metabolism. I hope this is clear, please let me know if that satisfies your query or whether a further explanation within the text is required. - Several of the studies that are referred to, especially in the FGF-23 and LCN-2 sections involve microvascular vessels (some examples on lines – 352, 360, 467), yet the focus throughout the text is on atherosclerosis and calcification, which are macrovascular diseases. You may need to clarify whether you are looking at one/both micro- and macro-vascular diseases and adjust the included articles accordingly. Thanks for highlighting this, we wish to include all vascular cell studies to give a comprehensive view and have reflected this within the search strategy to now read ‘To retrieve articles concerning the exogenous administration of OCN, FGF23 and LCN-2 to micro- or macro-vascular cells, the following…’, and additionally in the introduction aim which now reads ‘In order to assess the relevance of these osteokines to cardiovascular health, we aimed to provide an analysis of the direct effects of OCN, FGF23 and LCN-2 on micro- and macro-vascular cells in vitro, and to highlight gaps in the literature which need addressing, for use by clinicians and researchers.’. Comments for the Author - in the introduction there is too much background on the skeleton and blood vessels as a whole and not enough specificity on what you are discussing. The 3 osteokines you are discussing are only mentioned in ~ 2 sentences of the whole introduction. Further, things that you are not discussing in the main text (osteopontin, osteoprotegerin, sclerostin and DKK1) do not need to be discussed in the introduction. The introduction needs to be shortened and more focused, describing more background and rationale for the review. Thank you for your comment and we have endeavoured to adjust the manuscript accordingly. Please see the revised version and we hope this satisfies any further query. We have largely removed areas about the skeleton and blood vessels and included more information on the osteokines of interest. - lines 125 – 128 – There is several mistakes in the reporting of the different forms of OCN, please refer to ‘Li, J.; Zhang, H.; Yang, C.; Li, Y.; Dai, Z. An overview of osteocalcin progress. J. Bone Miner. Metab. 2016, 34,367–379’. My apologies for not understanding your comment correctly, what are the mistakes in the reporting? Much appreciated in advance.
paper_title_zh: 骨因子与血管系统：骨钙素、成纤维细胞生长因子-23和脂质运载蛋白-2体外效应综述
paper_abstract_zh: 骨源性因子，即表现出骨骼外功能的因子，也称为骨因子（osteokines），正迅速成为跨学科内分泌研究的一个高度有趣且备受关注的领域。骨钙素（OCN）、成纤维细胞生长因子-23（FGF23）和脂质运载蛋白-2（LCN-2），这些在骨骼中产生的因子，构成了一个重要的内分泌系统，该系统与其他器官精细调节，以确保体内平衡和健康。本综述旨在评估这些蛋白质在血管细胞中的直接参与作用的体外证据，并探讨它们在心血管疾病或炎症中是否存在因果关系。通过PubMed、Medline、Embase和Google Scholar检索了相关研究文章，这些文章探讨了外源性添加OCN、FGF23或LCN-2对血管平滑肌细胞或内皮细胞的影响。总体而言，这些骨因子在多种人类和动物血管细胞中具有直接的血管活性作用。OCN和FGF23均具有抗凋亡特性，并通过Akt信号通路增加人内皮细胞中eNOS的磷酸化和一氧化氮的产生。OCN改善细胞内胰岛素信号传导，并在小鼠和人类内皮细胞中显示出对抗内质网应激的保护作用。OCN可能参与钙化，但需要进一步研究，而体外实验中没有证据表明FGF23具有促钙化作用。FGF23和LCN-2在某些细胞类型中增加增殖，并分别增加和减少活性氧物种的产生。LCN-2也具有抗凋亡作用，但可能增加内质网应激，并在人类血管内皮细胞和平滑肌细胞中具有促炎和促血管生成特性。基于这些发现，没有强有力证据支持OCN或FGF23在血管中的病理作用。相反，它们实际上可能支持正常内皮功能、血管稳态和血管舒张。没有研究探讨OCN或FGF23在血管炎症中是否发挥作用。有限的LCN-2研究表明其在血管中具有促炎和可能的病理作用，但需要进一步的机制数据。总体而言，这些骨因子具有引人注目的功能，应进行全面研究以
review_content_zh:
审稿人1（匿名）基本报告

非常感谢您抽出时间审阅我们的稿件，并提供了有益的评论，我们希望这些评论已经显著改善了我们综述的焦点和可读性。以下是对个别评论的回应。

- 表格是一个好主意，使得每个研究的解读变得非常容易。然而，总的来说，结果和结论部分太长，它们应该是每个研究内容的总结，否则与在正文中阅读研究内容没有区别。感谢您指出这一点，我们已经相应地缩减了结果/结论部分，希望您现在会认为它们更好地代表了总结。

- 在表格中，请确保选择一致的浓度度量单位（例如：ng/ml），以帮助读者解读各研究之间的差异。感谢您指出这一点，现在所有浓度均以ng/mL表示。

实验设计

- 与每个骨因子及其血管效应的讨论相比，提供了过多的背景信息。建议删除小标题“循环浓度……，表达……和内分泌功能……”，仅包括讨论和解读血管效应所需的背景信息。非常感谢，我们同意您的评论。我们已经删除了“表达”和“内分泌功能”部分。我们调整了引言，删除了关于骨骼/血管的广泛信息，而是更多地关注感兴趣的蛋白质，并在那里简要提及它们的内分泌历史。我们保留了循环浓度信息，因为我们认为这对数据的解读很有用，而且这些部分相当简短。

- 鉴于这不是一篇系统综述，为什么您要包括关于搜索策略的部分？如果是系统综述，那么需要在标题中体现出来，并遵循系统综述的相应指南。感谢您的建议。尽管我们相当系统地搜索了要包括的研究，但搜索和数据提取仅由一名研究人员完成，因此综述的条件并不完全满足系统综述的要求。然而，我们希望按照PeerJ关于文献综述的指南（“调查方法：解释您如何确保文献的综合和无偏覆盖。”）包括搜索策略，并向读者保证，由于全面的搜索，遗漏论文的可能性很小。

- 在引言的最后，文章的目标包括关于每个骨因子内分泌功能的部分，然而，正如您在文本中指出的，这篇综述的标题是“骨因子与血管”，最近的综述已经完成了关于OCN和FGF-23的内分泌功能。重新思考每个骨因子的内分泌功能应包括多少信息，以及与之前的综述相比，这篇综述的新颖之处可能是有益的。感谢您指出这一点。我们已尽力重新聚焦并缩减手稿中包含的部分。因此，我们删除了手稿目标中的这句话，现在读作：“为了评估这些骨因子与心血管健康的相关性，我们旨在提供OCN、FGF23和LCN-2对微血管和大血管细胞体外直接效应的分析，并突出文献中需要解决的空白，供临床医生和研究人员使用。”

发现的有效性

- 请描述关于OCN和血管部分的新颖之处。最近的综述“Tacey, A., Qaradakhi, T., Brennan-Speranza, T., Hayes, A., Zulli, A., & Levinger, I. (2018). Osteocalcin在动脉粥样硬化和血管疾病发展中的潜在作用。营养素，10(10), 1426”描述了OCN对动脉粥样硬化发展的效应，并包括了您讨论中包含的所有研究。由于自上次综述以来没有发表任何新研究，这一部分在知识体系中增添了什么未被讨论的内容？感谢您的评论。我们承认提到的最近综述，并在我们的论文中引用了它。然而，我们的目标是提供骨因子和血管的总结和概述，我们认为不应将OCN排除在综述之外。我们旨在总结骨骼衍生激素的血管活性特性，以全面展示骨骼影响血管系统的新概念。此外，我们向临床医生和研究人员突出了一些进一步感兴趣的领域，包括循环水平，以及OCN与心血管终点之间观察性人类数据的背景信息，并最终指出当前知识中需要解决的空白。

- 在总结和结论部分，第492-493行，您描述证据指向骨因子在人类和动物细胞中的直接血管活性特性。然而，在FGF-23部分，您在第376-379行描述道：“呈现的结果支持以下假设：FGF23与CVD之间的关联和相关性最可能是由于改变的磷酸盐和矿物质代谢的有害效应，实际上FGF23水平可能是跟随而非直接的心血管扰动。”感谢您的评论，我们为表达不清道歉。在结论中，我希望指出FGF23具有直接的血管活性特性——即它引发反应和细胞信号等——然而，这并不表明与心血管病理有直接关系，FGF23与CVD之间观察到的相关性可能是由于改变的磷酸盐/矿物质代谢。我希望这已经很清楚，请告知这是否满足您的疑问，或者是否需要在文本中进一步解释。

- 所引用的几项研究，特别是在FGF-23和LCN-2部分，涉及微血管（一些例子在第352、360、467行），然而，整个文本的重点是动脉粥样硬化和钙化，这些都是大血管疾病。您可能需要澄清您是在研究微血管疾病、大血管疾病还是两者，并相应地调整所包含的文章。感谢您指出这一点，我们希望包括所有血管细胞研究，以提供全面的观点，并在搜索策略中反映了这一点，现在读作：“为了检索关于外源性给予OCN、FGF23和LCN-2对微血管或大血管细胞影响的文章，以下……”，此外，在引言目标中现在读作：“为了评估这些骨因子与心血管健康的相关性，我们旨在提供OCN、FGF23和LCN-2对微血管和大血管细胞体外直接效应的分析，并突出文献中需要解决的空白，供临床医生和研究人员使用。”

对作者的评论

- 在引言中，关于骨骼和血管的整体背景太多，而关于您所讨论内容的特异性不够。您所讨论的3种骨因子在整个引言中仅提及约2句话。此外，您在正文中未讨论的内容（骨桥蛋白、骨保护素、硬化素和DKK1）不需要在引言中讨论。引言需要缩短并更加聚焦，描述更多背景和综述的合理性。感谢您的评论，我们已经尽力根据您的建议调整了手稿。请参阅修订版本，我们希望这能满足您进一步的疑问。我们大量删除了关于骨骼和血管的内容，并包括了更多关于感兴趣骨因子的信息。

- 第125-128行——在报告OCN的不同形式时存在几处错误，请参考“Li, J.; Zhang, H.; Yang, C.; Li, Y.; Dai, Z. 骨钙素进展概述。J. Bone Miner. Metab. 2016, 34, 367–379”。我为未能正确理解您的评论道歉，报告中的错误是什么？提前感谢您的指正。
