paper_title: Video Diffusion Models - A Survey
paper_abstract: Diffusion generative models have recently shown great potential for video generation and editing tasks. This survey provides a systematic overview over relevant aspects of video diffusion models such as applications, architecture, and temporal dynamics. Developments in the field are outlined through paper summaries. The review concludes with an examination of remaining challenges and an outlook on the future of the field.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
The paper presents a survey on video diffusion methods for video generation and editing that have been developed in the last two years. It introduces a taxonomy of applications (Section 2), discusses architectural variants of image diffusion models (Section 3), outlines how those can be extended to video diffusion (Section 4), and discusses evaluation metrics (Section 5). The second part of the survey (Section 6) focuses on a literature review on text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-video, as well as multimodal synthesis and long video generation.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strengths: + Video synthesis is a topic of increasing popularity, lacking a solid survey on recent trends with diffusion models so far (there is a concurrent work from Xing et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10647). This survey should thus be of significant interest to the TMLR audience. + The survey covers a large number of relevant works and summarizes them in Section 6. This will be helpful for practitioners and researchers for getting an overview of the current state of the field. Specifically, Table 1 is a valuable resource (however, it should be better discussed in the text, for instance many/one/zero-shot is not sufficiently detailed) + The authors provide helpful illustrations in the figures that support understanding the concepts discussed in the survey. Weaknesses: - Organization of the paper: the first half (page 1-10) contains very few references to relevant work. Many statements are not supported by appropriate citations. The relevant works are then discussed in the second half (page 11-17), but this disconnect is suboptimal for a survey. Ideally, the first and second half should be merged in a major revision of the paper such that the literature overview is naturally blended with the discussions of taxonomy, architectures, datasets, and tasks. - Scope: The paper should also discuss works from "unconditional video synthesis" and "video completion". Moreover, it should relate diffusion-based approaches to prior, non-diffusion based approaches such as GANs (that "they have quickly overtaken GAN-based approaches in popularity" is not a sufficient discussion) . Also the related field of "video understanding with diffusion models" could be mentioned. - Phrasing: the authors repeatedly use phrases like "it seems to be the case" or "it might be". A survey should not reflect subjective impressions or speculations (as indicated by these phrases) but well supported observations about a field. The corresponding statements should be rephrased (if they are well supported observations) or be removed (if too subjective). Moreover, the introduction lacks a critical distance to the topic but "buys into" the hype with phrases like "tremendous ability" or "progress is being made on a daily basis". - Since arguably the most important ingredient for a video diffusion model is its training data, a survey should discuss existing datasets and their properties in detail. This is missing at the moment. - While difficult, it would still be desirable to compare different approaches quantitatively on a benchmark, in terms of metrics such as FVD. - Figure 1: the "architecture" dimension conflates the denoising architecture (U-Net vs. ViT) with the diffusion approach (latent vs. cascaded) - a general introduction of diffusion models including some formulas would be helpful for readers that do not yet have a background in the field. Section 3.1 is too high-level for this in its current form. - Section 3.3: The linear output projection is missing in the self-attention. Moreover, "Even though far less commonly used, this approach might have distinct advantages, such as lower computational costs and, in the case of generative video models, more flexibility in regard to the length of the generated video sequence." Could the authors explain why this might be the case? - Section 3.5: citing only a single work (Rombach et al., 2022) for LDMs and no follow-up work is too shallow. - Figure 8 lacks a clear message. It shows different settings that differ in various ways; why are those grouped into a single figure? - "The task of editing an existing video can be viewed as less demanding than text-to-video generation." An explanation why it can be viewed that way would be desirable. - The section on "Long Video Generation" might also include hybrid auto-regressive/diffusion approaches such as GAIA-1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17080) - "While labeled images can be be scraped in large quantity from the internet, there is no comparable source of labeled video data." Is this statement true? There a millions of videos on the internet on platforms like YouTube that come with a summary text. They might be problematic in terms of usage license, but suchchallenges should be discussed in more detail.

**Requested Changes:**
The paper requires a major revision in which the literature review is better integrated into the first paper (see above). Besides that, addressing the points list above under weaknesses would be needed.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
no concerns

**Claims And Evidence:**
No

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Revision (part 2): >"The task of editing an existing video can be viewed as less demanding than text-to-video generation." An explanation why it can be viewed that way would be desirable. We have removed this line. Upon reflection, it is not clear to us whether video editing is indeed less demanding than text-conditioned generation, especially in cases that go beyond simple style editing. >The section on "Long Video Generation" might also include hybrid auto-regressive/diffusion approaches such as GAIA-1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17080) We have added it to our review. > "While labeled images can be be scraped in large quantity from the internet, there is no comparable source of labeled video data." Is this statement true? There a millions of videos on the internet on platforms like YouTube that come with a summary text. They might be problematic in terms of usage license, but suchchallenges should be discussed in more detail. We have adjusted the wording to reflect that the main problem lies in the size of the publicly available video data sets when compared to image data. | Revisions (part 1): Dear reviewer, thank you very much for your time and thoughtful feedback. A version of the updated paper where the main revisions have been marked in blue can be found in the supplementary material. Unfortunately, we were not able to mark the new tables. >Organization of the paper: the first half (page 1-10) contains very few references to relevant work. Many statements are not supported by appropriate citations. The relevant works are then discussed in the second half (page 11-17), but this disconnect is suboptimal for a survey. Ideally, the first and second half should be merged in a major revision of the paper such that the literature overview is naturally blended with the discussions of taxonomy, architectures, datasets, and tasks. >Phrasing: the authors repeatedly use phrases like "it seems to be the case" or "it might be". A survey should not reflect subjective impressions or speculations (as indicated by these phrases) but well supported observations about a field. The corresponding statements should be rephrased (if they are well supported observations) or be removed (if too subjective). Moreover, the introduction lacks a critical distance to the topic but "buys into" the hype with phrases like "tremendous ability" or "progress is being made on a daily basis". We substantiated our claims in the first part of the survey with appropriate citations. We have added cross-references to make comprehensive understanding easier. >Scope: The paper should also discuss works from "unconditional video synthesis" and "video completion". Moreover, it should relate diffusion-based approaches to prior, non-diffusion based approaches such as GANs (that "they have quickly overtaken GAN-based approaches in popularity" is not a sufficient discussion) . Also the related field of "video understanding with diffusion models" could be mentioned. We added more information towards unconditional video synthesis and provided some relevant benchmarks (see Fig. 4, Section 5.4). We find it difficult to completely separate it from text-conditioned synthesis, since most of the relevant papers deal with both. >Since arguably the most important ingredient for a video diffusion model is its training data, a survey should discuss existing datasets and their properties in detail. This is missing at the moment. We have added a new section on representative training data sets (Sections 5.1, 5.2). >While difficult, it would still be desirable to compare different approaches quantitatively on a benchmark, in terms of metrics such as FVD. We have added a section with benchmarks on unconditional and text-conditioned video generation (see Fig. 4, Section 5.4). >Figure 1: the "architecture" dimension conflates the denoising architecture (U-Net vs. ViT) with the diffusion approach (latent vs. cascaded) We have made a clearer separation between the denoising architecture and method for increasing resolution (CDM, LDM) in Fig. 1 and other parts of the review. >a general introduction of diffusion models including some formulas would be helpful for readers that do not yet have a background in the field. Section 3.1 is too high-level for this in its current form. We have expanded the methods section on DDPMs (3.1) to include the formal foundations (mainly adapted from Ho et al, 2020). >Section 3.3: The linear output projection is missing in the self-attention. Moreover, "Even though far less commonly used, this approach might have distinct advantages, such as lower computational costs and, in the case of generative video models, more flexibility in regard to the length of the generated video sequence." Could the authors explain why this might be the case? The ViT section (3.3) now includes a mention of the linear output projection for multi-head attention. We have removed the mention of lower computational cost as it lacks suitable evidence. We have added an explanation that the flexible length of generated video sequences is due to the auto-regressive nature of token predictions in transformer models at time of inference. >Section 3.5: citing only a single work (Rombach et al., 2022) for LDMs and no follow-up work is too shallow. We have added a brief mention of follow-up work on LDM models to section 3.5. >Figure 8 lacks a clear message. It shows different settings that differ in various ways; why are those grouped into a single figure? We have simplified figure 8 to focus on the main aspect we wanted to convey.
paper_title_zh: 视频扩散模型综述
paper_abstract_zh: 扩散生成模型最近在视频生成和编辑任务中显示出巨大潜力。本综述系统地概述了视频扩散模型的相关方面，如应用、架构和时间动态性。通过论文摘要概述了该领域的发展。综述最后对剩余挑战进行了考察，并对该领域的未来进行了展望。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文对近两年开发的视频扩散方法在视频生成和编辑方面的应用进行了综述。介绍了应用分类（第2节），讨论了图像扩散模型的架构变体（第3节），概述了这些模型如何扩展到视频扩散（第4节），并讨论了评估指标（第5节）。综述的第二部分（第6节）重点对文本到视频、图像到视频、视频到视频以及多模态合成和长视频生成的文献进行了回顾。

**优点和缺点：**
优点：+ 视频合成是一个日益流行的主题，目前缺乏对近期扩散模型趋势的 solid 综述（有一篇 Xing 等人的并行工作，https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10647）。因此，这篇综述对 TMLR 读者应具有显著兴趣。+ 综述涵盖了大量相关研究，并在第6节进行了总结。这对实践者和研究人员了解该领域的当前状态非常有帮助。特别是，表1是一个宝贵的资源（然而，应在文本中更好地讨论，例如 many/one/zero-shot 的描述不够详细）+ 作者提供了有助于理解综述中讨论概念的插图。

缺点：- 论文组织：前半部分（第1-10页）很少引用相关研究。许多陈述没有适当的引文支持。相关研究在第二部分（第11-17页）进行了讨论，但这种脱节对综述来说是不理想的。理想情况下，应在论文的主要修订中将前半部分和后半部分合并，使文献概述自然地与分类、架构、数据集和任务的讨论融合。- 范围：论文还应讨论“无条件视频合成”和“视频补全”的工作。此外，应将基于扩散的方法与先前的非扩散方法（如 GANs）进行比较（“它们在流行度上迅速超越了基于 GAN 的方法”这一讨论是不充分的）。还可以提及“使用扩散模型的视频理解”的相关领域。- 表述：作者反复使用“似乎是这样的”或“可能是”等短语。综述不应反映主观印象或推测（如这些短语所示），而应是对一个领域的 well supported 观察。相应的陈述应重新措辞（如果是 well supported 观察）或删除（如果过于主观）。此外，引言缺乏对主题的批判性距离，而是用“巨大的能力”或“每天都在取得进展”等短语“buy into”了 hype。 - 由于视频扩散模型最重要的成分无疑是其训练数据，因此综述应详细讨论现有数据集及其属性。目前这一点缺失。- 尽管困难，但仍然希望在基准测试上对不同的方法进行定量比较，例如使用FVD等指标。- 图1：“架构”维度混淆了去噪架构（U-Net与ViT）与扩散方法（潜在与级联）- 对于尚未具备该领域背景的读者来说，包含一些公式的扩散模型的一般介绍将是有帮助的。第3.1节在当前形式下过于宏观。- 第3.3节：自注意力中缺少线性输出投影。此外，“尽管远不如常用，这种方法可能具有独特的优势，例如计算成本更低，并且在生成视频模型的情况下，对生成视频序列长度的灵活性更高。”作者能否解释为什么可能会这样？- 第3.5节：仅引用Rombach等人（2022）的一项工作来讨论LDMs，且没有后续工作，显得过于浅薄。- 图8缺乏明确的信息。它展示了不同设置的差异；为什么将这些组合在一张图中？- “编辑现有视频的任务可以被视为比文本到视频生成的要求低。”希望有一个解释说明为什么可以这样认为。- “长视频生成”部分也可以包括混合自回归/扩散方法，如GAIA-1（https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17080）- “尽管可以从互联网上大量抓取标记图像，但没有可比的标记视频数据来源。”这一说法是否正确？在YouTube等平台上存在数百万带有摘要文本的视频。它们在许可使用方面可能存在问题，但此类挑战应更详细地讨论。

**请求的更改：**
论文需要进行重大修订，其中文献综述应更好地整合到第一篇论文中（见上文）。除此之外，还需要解决上述弱点中列出的问题。

无关注

无

**受众：**

图1：“架构”维度将去噪架构（U-Net与ViT）与扩散方法（潜在与级联）混淆在一起。我们在图1和综述的其他部分更清晰地划分了去噪架构和增加分辨率的方法（CDM，LDM）。

对于尚未具备该领域背景知识的读者来说，包含一些公式的扩散模型的一般介绍将是有帮助的。当前形式的第3.1节对此来说过于高阶。我们扩展了关于DDPMs的方法部分（3.1），包括形式基础（主要改编自Ho等人，2020年）。

第3.3节：自注意力中缺少线性输出投影。此外，“尽管这种方法远不如常用，但它可能具有独特的优势，例如计算成本较低，以及在生成视频模型的情况下，对生成视频序列长度的灵活性更大。”作者能否解释为什么可能会这样？ViT部分（3.3）现在提到了多头注意力的线性输出投影。我们删除了关于较低计算成本的提及，因为它缺乏合适的证据。我们增加了解释，即生成视频序列长度的灵活性是由于在推理时变压器模型中标记预测的自回归性质。

第3.5节：仅引用一项工作（Rombach等人，2022年）来介绍LDMs，且没有后续工作，显得过于浅显。我们在第3.5节中简要提到了关于LDM模型的后续工作。

图8缺乏明确的信息。它展示了在不同方面有所不同的不同设置；为什么将这些组合在一张图中？我们简化了图8，以专注于我们想要传达的主要方面。

paper_title: Taxonomy of interventions at academic institutions to improve research quality
paper_abstract:
Background 
     Research waste has become an increasing issue for research institutions and researchers due to poor research reproducibility and replicability. Interventions to improve research quality at research institutions are important to reduce research waste. This review aims to identify and classify possible interventions to improve research quality, reduce waste, and improve reproducibility and replicability within research-performing institutions. 
   
   
     Methods 
     Steps to develop the taxonomy were 1) Use an exemplar paper looking at journal-level interventions to improve research quality, 2) Adapt intervention titles to align with Michie’s behaviour change wheel, 3) Conduct a 2-stage search in PubMed using seed articles and reviews, and a forward and backward citation search to identify articles that evaluated or described the implementation of interventions to improve research quality, 4) Pilot draft taxonomy with researchers at an openscience conference workshop, and 5) Iterative drafting and revisions by the research team. 
   
   
     Results 
     Overall, 93 individual interventions were identified through the peer-review literature and researcher reporting. Eleven peer-reviewed articles were identified. Interventions identified covered research stages from before, during, and after study conduct, and whole of institution. Types of intervention included: Tools, Education & Training, Incentives, Modelling and Mentoring, Review & Feedback, Expert involvement, and Policies & Procedures. The taxonomy identified areas for research institutions to focus on to improve research quality, reproducibility, and replicability. 
   
   
     Conclusions 
     Areas of focus and future research include improving incentives to implement quality research practices, evaluating current interventions, encouraging no- or low-cost and high-benefit interventions, examining institution culture and individual research ethos, and encouraging researcher mentor-mentee relationships.
review_content:
Thank you for inviting me to review this manuscript on a very important topic. However, I have a number of concerns and would be glad if the authors could address them:
There is no reference for Michie’s behaviour change wheel provided until the last page of the manuscript. There could be (in general) more references throughout the introduction and methods section.
The paragraph “What might research institutions …” on page 3 is a bit confusing. The order of the sentences seems not follow a clear argumentation.
The objectives of the paper are neither described in the introduction nor in the methods section. The taxonomy is presented as given, instead it could be described that the objectives were to develop and evaluate such a taxonomy. On page 3, a sentence in the middle of a paragraph starts with “This review aims (…)” which let´s the reader guess that a review was conducted. It is not introduced that the/ a taxonomy will be developed from findings of the literature review.
There are no clear in- and exclusion criteria provided.
How was the set of seed articles and reviews identified?
In which databases was the forward and backward citations search conducted? Where do I find the information to reproduce stage 1 and 2?
Page 3: ” This Stage 1 search identified a key review article on interventions to improve adherence to reporting guidelines for journals, which included a suggested taxonomy. We then drafted an initial taxonomy and used the other interventions identified from the searches to test and modify this proposed intervention taxonomy.” – it is not described based on which criteria the key article was identified/classified as key, and it is not described based on which method or criteria how the initial taxonomy was drafted and how (and which) other interventions were used to test and modify it.
Page 4: I have concerns that the taxonomy and review from 2021 and 2022 are still timely, because meta-research and reproducibility are a very active and timely field. The authors may have missed important developments from the last 3 years? Usually (systematic) reviews should be published within 6 months after the end of the literature search in order to be timely.
Page 5: If the results of the review, and the taxonomy, are supposed to be applied, how can they be used? Table 1 only provides short notes/headlines, without references? For example: “Create research teams with effective mix of research expertise” – if I want to do that, how does this statement (and the manuscript) help me to concretely do it? What is an effective mix? Without a reference to a text that provides more information for each of the aspects it is impossible to use the information provided in the taxonomy. Can the authors add that?
I couldn´t find an overview of the 93 different possible interventions and no list of excluded papers/interventions. Can the authors provide it? In terms of replicability and reproducibility this should be the foundation of their own review.
How many raters/authors conducted the literature search, and the “data extraction”? Was this conducted by two raters and was the interrater reliability computed? This is usually a fundamental quality criterion for reviews.
Page 8: Why was Michies wheel and not Noseks pyramid chosen?
Thank you!
paper_title_zh: 学术机构提升研究质量干预措施分类学
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
由于研究可重复性和可复制性较差，研究浪费已成为研究机构和研究人员日益关注的问题。在研究机构中实施提高研究质量的干预措施对于减少研究浪费至关重要。本综述旨在识别和分类可能用于提高研究质量、减少浪费以及提升研究机构内研究可重复性和可复制性的干预措施。

方法
开发分类法的步骤如下：1）使用一篇关于期刊层面干预措施以提高研究质量的示例论文；2）调整干预措施标题以与Michie的行为改变轮相一致；3）在PubMed中进行两阶段搜索，使用种子文章和综述，以及前向和后向引文搜索，以识别评估或描述实施提高研究质量干预措施的文章；4）在开放科学会议工作坊中与研究人员进行试点草案分类法；5）研究团队进行迭代起草和修订。

结果
总体而言，通过同行评审文献和研究人员报告共识别出93项个体干预措施。确定了11篇同行评审文章。识别出的干预措施涵盖了研究的前期、中期、后期以及整个机构。干预类型包括：工具、教育与培训、激励、建模与指导、审查与反馈、专家参与以及政策与程序。该分类法为研究机构提供了提高研究质量、可重复性和可复制性的重点领域。

结论
重点关注领域和未来研究方向包括改善激励措施以实施高质量研究实践、评估当前干预措施、鼓励无成本或低成本且高收益的干预措施、审视机构文化和个人研究理念，以及鼓励研究人员导师-学徒关系。
review_content_zh:
感谢您邀请我审阅这篇关于非常重要主题的手稿。然而，我有一些担忧，如果作者能够解决这些问题，我将不胜感激：

1. 直到手稿的最后一页才提供了关于Michie行为改变轮的参考文献。在引言和方法部分通常可以增加更多的参考文献。

2. 第3页上的“研究机构可能会……”段落有些令人困惑。句子的顺序似乎没有遵循清晰的论证逻辑。

3. 论文的目标既未在引言中描述，也未在方法部分中描述。分类法被呈现为既定事实，而实际上可以描述目标是为了开发和评估这样的分类法。第3页中，一个段落中间的句子以“本综述旨在（…）”开头，让读者猜测进行了综述。并未介绍将从文献综述的发现中开发出分类法。

4. 没有提供明确的纳入和排除标准。

5. 种子文章和综述是如何确定的？

6. 在哪些数据库中进行了前向和后向引文搜索？我在哪里可以找到重现第1阶段和第2阶段的信息？

7. 第3页：“第1阶段搜索确定了一篇关于改善期刊报告指南依从性干预措施的关键综述文章，其中包含了一个建议的分类法。然后我们起草了初步分类法，并使用从搜索中确定的其他干预措施来测试和修改这一提议的干预分类法。”——未描述基于哪些标准确定该关键文章/将其分类为关键，也未描述基于哪种方法或标准起草初步分类法，以及如何（以及哪些）其他干预措施被用来测试和修改它。

8. 第4页：我担心2021年和2022年的分类法和综述是否仍然及时，因为元研究和可重复性是一个非常活跃和时效性强的领域。作者可能错过了过去3年的重要进展？通常（系统）综述应在文献搜索结束后的6个月内发表，以保持时效性。

9. 第5页：如果综述的结果和分类法将被应用，它们如何被使用？表1仅提供了简短的注释/标题，没有参考文献？例如：“创建具有有效研究专长混合的研究团队”——如果我想这样做，这一声明（和手稿）如何具体帮助我实现它？什么是有效的混合？如果没有引用提供更多信息的文本，无法使用分类法中提供的信息。作者能否补充这一点？

10. 我找不到93种不同可能干预措施的概览，也没有排除的论文/干预措施的列表。作者能否提供？在可复制性和可重复性方面，这应是其自身综述的基础。

11. 有多少评分者/作者进行了文献搜索和“数据提取”？这是由两名评分者进行的吗，是否计算了评分者间信度？这通常是综述的基本质量标准。

12. 第8页：为什么选择Michie的行为改变轮而不是Nosek的金字塔？

谢谢！

paper_title: A review of the opportunities to support pollinator populations in South African cities
paper_abstract: Globally insects are declining, but some guilds of pollinators are finding refuge in urban landscapes. The body of knowledge on urban pollinators is relatively mature, which means it is now possible to begin to make generalization. Unfortunately, studies do not represent climatic regions evenly and there is a gap in research from the African continent and a bias towards Hymenoptera. This study aimed to address some of the gaps on urban pollination knowledge in South Africa and to identify opportunities to improve urban habitats for pollinators. We reviewed the international literature on urban pollinators and the South African literature on pollinators with a landscape ecology focus, drawing on literature with an emphasis on agricultural and ecosystem services. The findings show that some taxa (e.g. large-bodied, cavity nesting bees) will exploit urban environments increasing in abundance with urban intensity. Moderately sensitive taxa (such as smallbodied, ground-nesting bees) take advantage of urban environments only if local habitats are supportive of their needs for resource provision and habitat connectivity. The South African urban poor rely on pollination services for subsistence agriculture and the reproduction of wild-foraged medicines and food. Potential interventions to improve habitat quality include strategic mowing practices, conversion of turf-grass to floral rich habitats, scientific confirmation of lists of highly attractive flowers, and inclusion of smallscale flower patches throughout the urban matrix. Further research is needed to fill the Africa gap for both specialized and generalized pollinators (Diptera, Halictids, Lepidoptera and Hopliini) in urban areas where ornamental and indigenous flowering plants are valued.
review_content: Reviewer 3 highlighted some important areas where clarity was required in the text. We provide below a detailed table of how we responded to each of the comments. We believe that the revisions have improved the overall quality of the manuscript and that it is now suitable for publication in PeerJ. Peta Brom Dept. of Biological Sciences. University of Cape Town On behalf of all authors Detailed Comment Responses Rev # Reviewer Comment Author Response 1 The authors data is shared but it is not really clear to me why they did the literature search if they do not use the results thereof. The international literature was systematically reviewed and synthesized thematically. The systematic component replicated the work of Wenzel et al. and our initial findings were not in conflict with their published findings. 1 It is one of the first reviews putting it into a Southern African context, so I am not disagreeing with the conclusions but the way how they get to them should be more detailed and focused. We have added the summary data but are concerned that it is unnecessary and makes the paper too long for publication. 1 the link / transition of agriculture vs urban land-use to being able to add the international studies is rather weak in my opinion and should be one of the more detailed aspects, convincingly showing that one can interchange agri and urban, especially looking at line 505 “… structural differences between agriculture and urban…” We have provided additional explanation to justify the comparisons in the text. 1 Since the review wants to have a more South African perspective I am surprised that the authors only relied on published papers from South Africa and not included thesis work or conference proceedings. I am sure Anderson is doing work on that topic for a while and there is more data available. Pippin Anderson supervised the masters thesis of the corresponding author. We made contact with her directly to find out who, other than the current authors, are doing thesis research in this work. She confirmed that there is nothing that is of a level or quality that we would be able to incorporate meaningfully into the review beyond what has already been included. Instead we have incorporated work on plants and flowers in urban environments, work on urban agriculture and contextualized the discussion with input from the socio-cultural context. We have also added thesis work on Acacias. 1 I suggest that either broaden it and delete “South African” from the title, or find more South African data and show that one can actually make conclusion based on agricultural studies to an urban setting. Another option would be by expanding it to “African” cities and include the data from Africa, rather than South Africa. We have shifted the scope in several places and would value your feedback on whether you still think we need to broaden the focus to discuss Africa more generally, or if the additional discussion on South African city structure has addressed this. 1 Why limited the agricultural aspect to indigenous plants - what about citrus industry? Why only Eucalyptus, that seems only important in the Western Cape. What about the rest of the country. The Melin review makes no mention of Eucalyptus use being limited to the Western Cape. Eucalyptus spp. are used nationally…Sugar gum is mainly used in the Western Cape and saligna in the rest of the country. It is the main source of honey and is used to rear queens. - See for more: https://www.elsenburg.com/bee%20industry%20strategy%20mip%20may2018/Strelitzia_37_2016.pdf Also see this: https://bee-effect.co.za/beekeepers-choice/ We have made this a bit more explicit in the text. We have also added some information about Acacia spp. from emerging research. 1 Why did you actually do the literature search if you do not really use it and analysis it. Table 1 is a selective summary of the literature We have included more detail from the initial global systematic review. 1 Also, I miss the importance of Apis for Fynbos Two subspecies of Apis mellifera are endemic to the region. Apis mellifera capensis and Apis mellifera scutellata - now mentioned in text; capensis is a fynbos specific variant, but overall, we are not particularly clear what the reviewer is asking for here. 1 Several places were Apis mellifera is misspelled Corrected throughout, thank you. 1 Line 276 could have more South African Examples see below 1 A summary graph would be helpful to better capture the results in the supp We have added figures about the distribution of research and a table summarising the overall findings of responses to urban intensity. 1 Spelling line 181, Corrected, thank you. 1 Archer, C.R., Pirk, C.W.W., Carvalheiro, L.G., and Nicolson, S.W. (2014). Economic and ecological implications of geographic bias in pollinator ecology in the light of pollinator declines. OIKOS 123, 401-407.10.1111/j.1600-0706.2013.00949.x Carvalheiro, L.G., Seymour, C.L., Veldtman, R., and Nicolson, S.W. (2010). Pollination services decline with distance from natural habitat even in biodiversity-rich areas. Journal of Applied Ecology 47, 810-820.10.1111/j.1365-2664.2010.01829.x Carvalheiro, L.G., Veldtman, R., Shenkute, A.G., Tesfay, G.B., Pirk, C.W.W., Donaldson, J.S., and Nicolson, S.W. (2011). Natural and within-farmland biodiversity enhances crop productivity. Ecology Lett. 14, 251-259.10.1111/j.1461-0248.2010.01579.x This is the "below" to which review refers for additional studies. We considered all three of these papers and incorporated the Archer reference. 2 A bit more effort could be made to access some of the literature and evidence about urban pollinator programs and conservation more widely in Africa. While some of this is in what would be considered 'grey literature' it provides an important context on what the current state of things are - which is what the review intends to do. This is a super suggestion for a separate paper. There is an incredible volume of both formal and informal stewardship going on in civic society and the NGO sector nationally and continentally and we think examining this and assessing efficacy in terms of impact on society, restoration of urban pollinator networks, challenges to successful implementation and widespread changes in practices from a norms and cultural perspective, as well as potential conflict from disservices would be a great follow on study. In Cape Town alone, we list the following organizations formalized and informal volunteers which have urban pollinator programs: Communitree, Ncquncqu sunbird project, Greenpop, Weltevreden city impovement district, City of Cape Town grow don't mow campaign, WESSA's Big Friends Group, Friends of Rondebosch Common, Friends of Harfield Village Parks, Fynbos Life, Wynberg Neighbourhood Garden projects, Salt-river urban gardens, Babylonstoren, Edith Stephens... To assess activities at a National or continental scale could be an entire PhD thesis and far beyond the scope of the current paper. 2 One aspect that is lacking is the bias towards both western urban areas and a lack of detail about the different urban cultures in South Africa. Given the history of South Africa, it would be prudent to present this context, as it has serious impacts for human settlements and thus where biodiversity is conserved, or not, within urban areas. paper_title_zh: 南非城市支持授粉昆虫种群机会的综述
paper_abstract_zh: 全球范围内昆虫数量正在下降，但一些传粉者类群在城市化景观中找到了避难所。关于城市传粉者的知识体系相对成熟，这意味着现在可以开始进行概括性总结了。不幸的是，研究在气候区域上的代表性并不均匀，非洲大陆的研究存在空白，且研究偏向于膜翅目昆虫。本研究旨在填补南非城市传粉知识的一些空白，并识别改善城市传粉者栖息地的机会。我们回顾了关于城市传粉者的国际文献和以景观生态学为重点的南非传粉者文献，借鉴了强调农业和生态系统服务的文献。研究结果表明，某些类群（例如大型体型的洞穴筑巢蜜蜂）会利用城市环境，其数量随城市强度的增加而增加。中等敏感类群（如小型体型的地面筑巢蜜蜂）只有在当地栖息地能够满足其资源供给和栖息地连通性需求时，才会利用城市环境。南非城市贫困人口依赖传粉服务进行自给农业以及野生药用和食物植物的繁殖。潜在的改善栖息地质量的干预措施包括战略性的割草实践、将草坪转换为花卉丰富的栖息地、科学确认高吸引力花卉清单，并在城市基质中纳入小规模花斑块。需要进一步研究以填补非洲在城市地区对专业和泛化传粉者（双翅目、隧蜂科、鳞翅目和跳甲族）的研究空白，这些地区重视观赏性和本土开花植物。
review_content_zh:
审稿人3强调了一些文本中需要澄清的重要区域。我们在下方提供了一个详细的表格，说明我们对每条评论的回应。我们相信这些修订提高了手稿的整体质量，现在适合在PeerJ上发表。

Peta Brom
生物科学系
开普敦大学
代表所有作者

详细评论回应
审稿编号 审稿人评论 作者回应
1 作者的数据是共享的，但我不太清楚他们为什么要进行文献检索，如果他们不使用检索结果的话。 国际文献经过了系统的回顾和主题综合。系统部分复制了Wenzel等人的工作，我们的初步发现与他们的已发表发现没有冲突。 1 这是首次将其置于南非背景下的综述之一，所以我并不反对结论，但得出结论的方式应该更详细和专注。我们已经添加了汇总数据，但担心这是不必要的，并且会使论文过长，不适合发表。 1 在我看来，农业与城市土地利用之间的联系/过渡相当薄弱，应该是一个更详细的方面，令人信服地展示可以互换农业和城市，特别是查看第505行“…农业和城市之间的结构差异…” 我们在文本中提供了额外的解释来证明比较的合理性。 1 由于综述希望有更多的南非视角，我很惊讶作者仅依赖于南非的已发表论文，而没有包括学位论文或会议论文。我相信Anderson在这个话题上已经研究了一段时间，应该有更多数据可用。 Pippin Anderson指导了通讯作者的硕士论文。我们直接与她联系，了解除了当前作者之外，还有谁在进行这方面的学位研究。她确认除了已经包含的内容外，没有达到我们能够有意义地纳入综述的水平和质量的研究。相反，我们纳入了关于城市环境中植物和花卉的工作，关于城市农业的工作，并在社会文化背景的输入下进行了讨论。我们还添加了关于金合欢的学位论文。 1 我建议要么扩大范围并从标题中删除“南非”，要么找到更多南非数据，展示实际上可以基于农业研究得出城市环境的结论。另一个选择是通过将其扩展到“非洲”城市，并包括非洲的数据，而不是南非的数据。 我们在几个地方调整了研究范围，并希望您能反馈意见，看看您是否仍认为我们需要扩大讨论范围以更广泛地探讨非洲，或者新增的关于南非城市结构的讨论是否已解决了这一问题。

1. 为什么将农业方面仅限于本土植物——柑橘产业如何？为什么只讨论桉树，这似乎只在西开普省重要。其他地区呢？梅林综述中并未提到桉树的使用仅限于西开普省。桉树属植物在全国范围内使用……糖桉主要在西开普省使用，而斜叶桉则在其他地区使用。它是蜂蜜的主要来源，并用于培育蜂王。——更多信息请见：https://www.elsenburg.com/bee%20industry%20strategy%20mip%20may2018/Strelitzia_37_2016.pdf 也请参考这个：https://bee-effect.co.za/beekeepers-choice/ 我们在文本中对此进行了更明确的说明。我们还添加了一些关于金合欢属植物的新兴研究信息。

1. 如果您实际上并不真正使用和分析文献，为什么还要进行文献检索？表1是对文献的选择性总结。我们从最初的全球系统性综述中包含了更多细节。

1. 此外，我遗漏了Apis对Fynbos的重要性。Apis mellifera的两个亚种是该地区的特有种。Apis mellifera capensis和Apis mellifera scutellata——现已在文本中提及；capensis是Fynbos特有的变种，但总体而言，我们不太清楚审稿人具体要求什么。

1. 几处Apis mellifera拼写错误 已全文更正，谢谢。

1. 第276行可以增加更多南非的例子，见下文。

1. 摘要图表有助于更好地捕捉补充材料中的结果。我们已添加了关于研究分布的图表和总结城市强度响应总体发现的表格。

1. 第181行拼写错误 已更正，谢谢。

1. Archer, C.R., Pirk, C.W.W., Carvalheiro, L.G., and Nicolson, S.W. (2014). Economic and ecological implications of geographic bias in pollinator ecology in the light of pollinator declines. OIKOS 123, 401-407.10.1111/j.1600-0706.2013.00949.x Carvalheiro, L.G., Seymour, C.L., Veldtman, R., and Nicolson, S.W. (2010). Pollination services decline with distance from natural habitat even in biodiversity-rich areas. Journal of Applied Ecology 47, 810-820.10.1111/j.1365-2664.2010.01829.x Carvalheiro, L.G., Veldtman, R., Shenkute, A.G., Tesfay, G.B., Pirk, C.W.W., Donaldson, J.S., and Nicolson, S.W. (2011). Natural and within-farmland biodiversity enhances crop productivity. Ecology Lett. 14, 251-259.10.1111/j.1461-0248.2010.01579.x 这是审稿人所指的“下文”中提到的额外研究。我们考虑了这三篇论文，并纳入了Archer的参考文献。

2. 可以再努力一些，获取更多关于非洲城市传粉者项目和保护的文献和证据。 尽管其中一些内容属于所谓的“灰色文献”，但它为当前状况提供了重要的背景信息——这正是本综述旨在实现的目标。这是一个关于单独论文的极好建议。在公民社会和全国及大陆范围内的非政府组织部门中，正在进行着大量正式和非正式的托管活动，我们认为研究这些活动并评估其在社会影响、城市传粉网络恢复、成功实施的挑战以及从规范和文化角度的广泛实践变化方面的有效性，以及潜在的服务不足引发的冲突，将是一个很好的后续研究。仅在开普敦，我们就列出了以下拥有城市传粉项目的正式和非正式志愿者组织：Communitree、Ncquncqu太阳鸟项目、Greenpop、Weltevreden城市改善区、开普敦市“种植而非修剪”运动、WESSA的大朋友集团、Rondebosch Common之友、Harfield Village公园之友、Fynbos Life、Wynberg邻里花园项目、Salt-river城市花园、Babylonstoren、Edith Stephens……要在国家或大陆范围内评估这些活动，可能需要一篇完整的博士论文，远超出当前论文的范围。

一个缺失的方面是对西方城市地区的偏见以及对南非不同城市文化细节的缺乏。鉴于南非的历史，呈现这一背景是明智的，因为它对人类定居点有着严重影响，从而影响城市区域内生物多样性的保护与否。例如，历史上城市的隔离对当前绿地模式和谁能接触这些绿地有着重大影响。虽然这不是综述的重点，但它对当前城市地区的实际情况有着非常真实的影响。我们已包括了几段关于历史空间规划背景及其导致的不平等，以及这对植被结构影响的论述。

关于撒哈拉以南非洲和其他发展中国家的城市农业有着丰富而广泛的文献。我建议添加这些内容，因为它提供了更广泛的背景，并指出在城市-农村或保护-开发之间的感知边界在许多地区是模糊的：我们认为这些内容过于广泛且偏离主题，难以恰当融入并公正处理。

Foeken, D.W.J., Owuor, S., de Bruijn, M.E. and Dijk, R.A., 2001. Multi-spatial livelihoods in sub-Saharan Africa: rural farming by urban households-the case of Nakuru town, Kenya. 我们认真考虑了这些建议。在规划学科中，前两点会因为政治和规划背景的不断变化而被认为过时，当前研究的有效期为五年，除非是对历史发展和活动的评论。在过去的二十年里，尤其是南非，发生了巨大的变化。2 在西非和东非的许多地区，人们正在努力建设多功能公共绿地，许多地方保护组织或公民组织也参与其中。虽然这些内容大多不在核心科学文献中，但值得在论文中提及，因为它提供了一个更细致和全面的当前情况图景：通讯作者目前正在南非背景下进行多功能绿色基础设施设计的研究，并将在未来几年内发表相关成果。2 https://friendsofcitypark.org/pollinator-garden-gets-a-jump-start-with-a-boscowen-makeover/ 这很好。如果有机会，我们有很多可以和项目组织者讨论的内容——这非常适合一项关于公民和社会行动的研究。2 有一些更近期的综述提供了更广泛的传粉者保护、管理和与之相关的许多复杂问题的背景。我建议将这些参考文献添加到稿件中：Hall, D.M.和Martins, D.J.，2020。《昆虫传粉者保护的人类维度》。《昆虫科学当前观点》，38，第107-114页。Potts, Simon G.等。《传粉者、传粉和食物生产的评估报告：政策制定者摘要》。政府间科学-政策平台生物多样性和生态系统服务秘书处，2016年。我们阅读了这些论文并考虑了其观点，但未能直接引用。Potts的论文（或非常类似的一篇）已经被引用。2 人们越来越认识到密集城市养蜂活动对城市景观中野生或非管理传粉者物种的潜在影响。鉴于在许多地区对生物多样性及其与人类生活和生计的联系仍缺乏理解这一更广泛问题，这个主题在综述中可能值得更多讨论。似乎更适合另一篇论文，并且目前阶段可以引入讨论的工作较少。3 引言难以理解，我建议作者或许可以将他们的实际引言与他们综述的第一部分“分析移动代理（传粉者）相互作用的概念模型”合并，主要基于Kremen等人2007年的工作。我们已经编辑了引言并缩短了MABES部分。我们希望现在读起来更清晰。 3 关于引言部分，我认为可以包含更多关于传粉者衰退的信息，以及为什么城市景观可能对某些类群有利。请详细说明对哪些类群有利或不利，并补充一些关于Wenzel 2020年工作的精确描述，该工作在L51-54中有描述（见审稿人意见）。已完成。

3 引言的第三段对于读者来说不太容易理解，我不完全明白为什么会有从城市到农业景观的转换。我理解某些因素在城市和农业景观中可能起类似作用，但我认为进行这种类比是有风险的。最好重新表述这一段。已对此进行编辑，以提高清晰度和流畅性。

3 我不明白图1的输入是什么，它与Kremen等人2007年的图相同。我们不清楚审稿人在此评论中的意思。MABES图是为了方便读者而复制的（现在为图3）。如果审稿人/编辑认为它对论文没有增加价值，我们将删除它。

3 也许作者可以提供他们综述中包含的论文总数（158篇）。已添加了全球综述和本地综合的详细信息。

3 综述强调了关于城市化对南非传粉者影响的知识的缺乏。作者仅在文末提供了一些蜜蜂类群和昆虫类群的信息，而他们可以在正文中提及一些研究。有一个专门讨论昆虫类群的章节，标题为：“传粉者群落结构：野生蜜蜂和非蜜蜂传粉者在不同景观系统中的重要性”，这在全文654行中的第382-441行。我们不清楚审稿人还希望了解什么。

3 南非昆虫保护的发展与未来 https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-94-007-2963-6_12
南非鳞翅目学：过去、现在与未来 https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-94-007-2963-6_12

paper_title: Foundational Competencies and Responsibilities of a Research Software Engineer
paper_abstract: The term Research Software Engineer, or RSE, emerged a little over 10 years ago as a way to represent individuals working in the research community but focusing on software development. The term has been widely adopted and there are a number of high-level definitions of what an RSE is. However, the roles of RSEs vary depending on the institutional context they work in. At one end of the spectrum, RSE roles may look similar to a traditional research role. At the other extreme, they resemble that of a software engineer in industry. Most RSE roles inhabit the space between these two extremes. Therefore, providing a straightforward, comprehensive definition of what an RSE does and what experience, skills and competencies are required to become one is challenging. In this community paper we define the broad notion of what an RSE is, explore the different types of work they undertake, and define a list of foundational competencies as well as values that outline the general profile of an RSE. Further research and training can build upon this foundation of skills and focus on various aspects in greater detail. We expect that graduates and practitioners will have a larger and more diverse set of skills than outlined here. On this basis, we elaborate on the progression of these skills along different dimensions. We look at specific types of RSE roles, propose recommendations for organisations, give examples of future specialisations, and detail how existing curricula fit into this framework.
review_content:
# Summary

The paper addresses many aspects of working as an RSE in different roles and the skills required or recommended to work effectively and to a high standard in this area. As outlined, RSEs work in a wide variety of roles and as such the inclusion of many contributors helps to ensure that many different aspects are covered and considered.
In addition, the authors outline future scenarios on how the current situation can be systematically shaped and improved. The paper is well structured and readable and makes a significant contribution to the understanding and future development of different RSE roles, required skills and training and career paths. The authors also outline future publications based on this article.


# Minor corrections and suggestions.

I think the title of the publication only describes part of the content and does not include the proposed suggestions and scenarios for the future of RSE skills development and support. A different title, along the lines of "Foundational Competencies and Responsibilities of a Research Software Engineer: Current State and Suggestions for Future Directions" might better describe the content of the article.

This sentence appears to be corrupted due to editing:

values for good scientific practice commit to the health, safety and welfare of the public and act in the interest of society, their employer and their clients.”

“RSEs also adhere to the SE Code of Ethics”: As much as I agree with the proposed values, I would prefer the subjunctive/conjunctive form here, as used in other parts of the document. The teaching of these values could be strengthened in the later section proposing bachelor and master curricula.

RSEs are also mentoring colleagues (see also Section 3.1.2). This necessitates giving good advice that fits to a project’s
stage in its life cycle, thereby requiring knowledge of ( SWLC), and its context in its research domain and thus ( RC).
**END OF PARAGRAPH HERE**
Research software can often start out as a tool to answer a personal research question, becoming more important
when other researchers start to rely on it. At the other end of the scale, research software can sometimes underpin key
processes that deal with critical questions such as weather forecasting or medical diagnosis.

paper_title: Recycling of collagen from solid tannery waste and prospective utilization as adhesives.
paper_abstract:
Abstract 
   This study explores the innovative potential of recycled collagen derived from tannery waste for use in high-performance adhesive formulations. The leather industry generates significant amounts of solid waste, primarily from chromium-tanned leather, which poses substantial environmental challenges. Recent advancements in recycling techniques have opened new avenues for repurposing this waste, particularly through collagen extraction, which comprises about 30-35% of tannery residues. This research systematically reviews the methods and applications of collagen extraction, highlighting the material’s versatility and environmental benefits when used as a bio-adhesive. 
   The review identifies key challenges such as low water resistance, shear strength, and adhesiveness in collagen-based adhesives compared to synthetic counterparts. However, innovative solutions are emerging, including the incorporation of silane coupling agents and cross-linking technologies that significantly improve the water resistance and mechanical properties of these adhesives. Economic analyses further support the viability of using tannery waste-derived collagen in adhesive production, aligning with global sustainability goals and reducing reliance on petrochemical-based adhesives. 
   Despite these advancements, the transition from laboratory research to commercial applications remains a significant challenge. Current studies primarily focus on small-scale experiments, with limited pilot-scale studies available. Nonetheless, the potential for collagen-based adhesives to replace harmful chemicals in industrial applications is promising, especially in sectors requiring biodegradable and non-toxic materials. This review concludes that while significant progress has been made, further research is necessary to overcome existing limitations and fully realize the commercial potential of collagen-based adhesives derived from tannery waste.
review_content:
The manuscript titled as ‘‘"Recycling of collagen from solid tannery waste and prospective utilization as adhesives" for F1000Research” was reviewed.
I have evaluated the paper in light of the F1000Research scope. The submission was made as Review Paper. The manuscript discusses the extraction and application of collagen from solid tannery waste as an adhesive. This topic aligns well with current sustainability objectives, particularly within the leather industry. The authors provide a comprehensive review of collagen extraction methods, adhesive formulation, and potential applications, supported by recent advancements in the field.
However, while the paper is informative, it faces several scientific and structural limitations. Key aspects require refinement to ensure clarity and to meet the publication standards of F1000Research.
The study addresses an important topic in the circular economy and sustainable waste management. Converting tannery waste into adhesives could reduce landfill waste and minimize reliance on petroleum-based adhesives. This aligns with the increasing need for sustainable materials and methods in various industrial applications.
While the study is comprehensive in discussing various collagen extraction and adhesive production techniques, it lacks specific experimental data or case studies to support some of its claims. The paper would benefit from quantitative data that compares the performance of collagen-based adhesives with traditional adhesives in specific applications.
The authors briefly mention the limitations of collagen adhesives, particularly in water resistance and durability. However, more detailed discussion and proposed solutions for overcoming these limitations are necessary to make the paper more practical and applicable to real-world scenarios.
The manuscript is structured logically, yet certain sections (e.g., Background, Methods) could be more concise. In some parts, especially the discussion on different adhesive applications, the information appears repetitive. A clearer distinction between current findings and future directions could improve readability. Moreover, methods section should be removed. Review papers rarely include a method section since they do not report on original research.
Author needs to send this manuscript for English proofread as I found some grammatical errors while reviewing the article.
In the Abstract: "This research systematically reviews the methods and applications of collagen extraction, highlighting the material’s versatility and environmental benefits when used as a bio-adhesive." The phrase “when used as a bio-adhesive” could be simplified to “as a bio-adhesive.”
In the Methods: "Only documents in English," which should be “Only English-language documents were included.”
Further editing for grammatical accuracy and flow would enhance the manuscript’s clarity and professionalism.
After these revision, the paper can be considered publication
paper_title_zh: 从固体制革废弃物中回收胶原蛋白及其作为粘合剂的潜在应用
paper_abstract_zh:
摘要
本研究探讨了源自制革废物的再生胶原蛋白在高性能粘合剂配方中的创新潜力。皮革行业产生了大量固体废物，主要来自铬鞣皮革，这对环境构成了重大挑战。近年来，回收技术的进步为重新利用这些废物开辟了新途径，特别是通过胶原蛋白提取，这约占制革残渣的30-35%。本研究系统地回顾了胶原蛋白提取的方法和应用，强调了将该材料用作生物粘合剂时的多功能性和环境效益。
综述识别了胶原蛋白基粘合剂与合成粘合剂相比存在的主要挑战，如低水 resistance、剪切强度和粘附性。然而，创新解决方案正在涌现，包括引入硅烷偶联剂和交联技术，这些技术显著提高了这些粘合剂的水 resistance 和机械性能。经济分析进一步支持了使用制革废物衍生的胶原蛋白进行粘合剂生产的可行性，这与全球可持续发展目标一致，并减少了对石油化工基粘合剂的依赖。
尽管取得了这些进展，但从实验室研究过渡到商业应用仍是一个重大挑战。当前研究主要集中在小规模实验，有限的试点规模研究可供参考。尽管如此，胶原蛋白基粘合剂在工业应用中替代有害化学品的潜力是令人期待的，尤其是在需要可生物降解和无毒材料的领域。本综述得出结论，尽管已取得显著进展，但仍需进一步研究以克服现有局限，并充分实现源自制革废物的胶原蛋白基粘合剂的商业潜力。
review_content_zh:
标题为“‘从固体制革废料中回收胶原蛋白及其作为粘合剂的前景应用’的F1000Research论文”已审阅。
我根据F1000Research的范围对该论文进行了评估。该投稿作为综述论文提交。手稿讨论了从固体制革废料中提取胶原蛋白并将其作为粘合剂的应用。这一主题与当前的可持续目标高度契合，特别是在皮革行业。作者对胶原蛋白提取方法、粘合剂配方和潜在应用进行了全面综述，并得到了该领域最新进展的支持。
然而，尽管该论文信息丰富，但仍存在一些科学和结构上的局限性。关键方面需要进一步完善，以确保清晰度并符合F1000Research的出版标准。
该研究探讨了循环经济和可持续废物管理中的一个重要话题。将制革废料转化为粘合剂可以减少填埋废物并降低对石油基粘合剂的依赖。这与各工业应用中对可持续材料和方法的日益增长的需求相一致。
尽管该研究在讨论各种胶原蛋白提取和粘合剂生产技术方面较为全面，但缺乏具体的实验数据或案例研究来支持其部分论点。论文将受益于定量数据，这些数据比较了胶原蛋白基粘合剂与传统粘合剂在特定应用中的性能。
作者简要提到了胶原蛋白粘合剂的局限性，特别是在耐水性和耐用性方面。然而，为了使论文更具实用性和适用于现实场景，需要更详细的讨论和提出克服这些局限性的解决方案。
手稿结构合理，但某些部分（如背景、方法）可以更加简洁。在某些部分，尤其是对不同粘合剂应用的讨论中，信息显得重复。更清晰地区分当前发现和未来方向可以提升可读性。此外，应删除方法部分。综述论文很少包含方法部分，因为它们不报告原创研究。

进一步的语法准确性和流畅性编辑将提升手稿的清晰度和专业性。
经过这些修订后，论文可以考虑发表。

paper_title: A scoping review of determinants of performance in dressage
paper_abstract: As a first step in achieving an evidence-based classification system for the sport of Para Dressage, there is a clear need to define elite dressage performance. Previous studies have attempted to quantify performance with able-bodied riders using scientific methods, however definitive measures have yet to be established for the horse and/or the rider. This may be, in part, due to the variety of movements and gaits that are found within a dressage test and also due to the complexity of the horse-rider partnership. The aim of this review is therefore to identify objective measurements of horse performance in dressage and the functional abilities of the rider that may influence them to achieve higher scores.
review_content: Reviewer 2 Basic reporting See below Experimental design See below Validity of the findings See below Comments for the author General comments The manuscript presents a review of scientific evidence related to dressage performance. The text is well written, with very few typographical errors. Thank you for your comments. The aim of providing a scientific background for classification of disability levels in para-dressage is legit, but this goal is little touched upon in the discussion. I started my reading with the search strategy, and read through to the end of discussion before I returned to the introduction, and I was rather surprised when I read the incentive for the study. I also wondered whether this review of the literature was asked for by the Paralympic committee or if this was an initiative by the authors themselves. The review adds moderately to the existing body of literature. Similar material is available in book chapters and previous reviews mentioned in the current manuscript, though all of this information is not available in the same paper, as the authors point out. The review is part of a larger study commissioned by the FEI. The review was conducted in order to provide knowledge from which objective measures of performance could be chosen in a future study. These measures will be used to evaluate performance and the effect of impairment on performance in an experimental study on able bodied and para riders at a later date. The review did not yield any literature where para riders had been tested in relation to performance, hence the lack of information and discussion within the manuscript itself. The study is reported as a systematic review, but I would argue that what has been undertaken here is not a systematic review, rather it’s a scoping review. A systematic review summarizes multiple studies that have addressed the same research question, while a scoping review maps the existing literature relevant for a particular question or area of interest. It is obvious already from the aims, that this study addresses a broader area rather than a single focused question and the results section does not present evidence to inform practice, rather it’s presents mapping of the literature available and overview of study findings. This is not suggesting a lower value of the publication, but I feel that it’s important to present it in the correct framework, and this review also does not benefit from trying to squeeze itself into the systematic review framework where it clearly doesn’t fit. The guidelines of this journal refers to the following publication for guidance whether a review is a systematic review or a scoping review. Munn Z, Peters MDJ, Stern C, Tufanaru C, McArthur A, Aromataris E. 2018. Systematic review or scoping review? Guidance for authors when choosing between a systematic or scoping review approach. BMC Medical Research Methodology 18:143 DOI: 10.1186/s12874-018-0611-x. I suggest that you read this publication. Related to this issue, use of the PICO formula does not fit a scoping review, this search strategy is mainly tailored towards systematic review of intervention studies and in your form you state intervention was non-applicable in your case. Many thanks for your advice and directing us towards a suitable literature source on this topic. We have consulted our review experts at UCLan and they agree that the manuscript is probably better placed as a scoping review. We have modified the title and supporting documentation accordingly. Materials and methods The initial search strategy appears non-optimal, the chosen combination of words could pose a risk that relevant papers are missed. However, I interpret that you extended the search using keywords that appeared relevant when you went through your search results. Is that a correct interpretation? Our search strategy was designed to capture all of the literature, but as is clear from the extended part of this review, we extended our search. Actually, we hand searched all of the included papers and review papers that were relevant for additional literature. We have included a sentence in the limitations. It is difficult to follow the search development from the supplement. I am not sure what the numbers listed actually mean, it seems it’s the number of hits for each word. I think some explanatory notes would be good to make this more interpretable. Apologies, it was not our intention to illustrate search strategy development in Table S3, rather it illustrated our final search strategy across all databases searched. Table S3 originally included a tab for each database searched and served as a tracking sheet for the number of hits from each search term. These values should not have been included in the first instance, as they are not relevant to the reader and do not take into account things like the duplicates that were removed to get to our final values in the PRISMA flow chart. Table S3 now includes only the search terms/ strategy, which is in accordance with systematic database searches where individual terms are initially searched and then the correct Boolean operators are applied to combine the terms/ grouped terms accordingly. Also, why is the VetMed sheet empty? The VetMed sheet has only the combined hits recorded. Two of the co-authors were responsible for reporting the search results. One reported all of the results whilst the second reported only the combined results from the VetMed search (found at the bottom of the sheet). Neither were relevant to the final results – as indicated in the comments above. I miss the prisma checklist, which is mandatory for systematic reviews according to the journal guidelines. But as I understand this is not mandatory for scoping review. The Prisma checklist is Supplemental Table S10. We have updated this with a PRISMA checklist (PRISMA-ScR) for Scoping reviews. Your inclusion criteria seem to suggest that every paper needs to contain something on both horse and rider. Is that really the case? These criteria are also not easy to understand. I suggest that you include an example after each except the first one. For number two you can for example write e.g. optic motion capture/ kinematic data. Apologies if this is unclear. We have included examples within the text and clarified that the search had to contain rider and/or horse performance measures. It would be good if you state when the search was performed, even though this information is given implicitly by the time span of the search. We have included the date range within the manuscript. Results Please add journal, volume and page numbers to your list of included papers if feasible. This will make the supplements more valuable resources for readers. Journal, volume and page number have been added to supplemental tables S6 and S7. For me, figure 2 is difficult to read, there is a lot of arrows crossing. Are the relationships illustrated in figure 2 based on findings in the reviewed papers or suggestions by authors of these papers, and/or your own reasoning? Please be clear about this in the text and figure legend. Regardless, I think these interrelationships are open questions, apart from the few that we have data on. For example, in the text you say that ’stiller leg will improve the rider’s ability to provide consistent and precise aids to the horse, resulting in more finite speed, gait and/or movement changes’ in trot while the figure suggests that less knee flexion-extension does not have an influence on joint kinematics. We have discussed and considered your comments here at length and opted for enhancing the explanation and justification of the diagram. This is included as part of the legend, but also as additional supplementary information Text S1. We agree that these are open questions where limited data exists, hence this is a ‘theoretical model’ that can be tested in future work. Discussion: I feel the discussion could be more condensed and be more concluding and interpreting rather than just reporting. There is no clear connection or reference to figure 2. I don’t mean that you have the rewrite the whole discussion, but I suggest that you go over the text with this in mind. We have re-reviewed the manuscripts within this review and considered your advice on reducing the discussion. However, we feel that the descriptions relate directly to figures 2 and 3 and as such are justifications of the development of these figures. In addition, none of the manuscripts provide the extent of the detail we have included that specifically described determinants of performance. As such, we have focused on revising detailed comments from both reviewers rather than re-writing this section. Line 245: please add that the comparison between a smaller and a taller horse is only applicable if they are walking at the same speed. Unless I misunderstood this in someway. Added to this sentence to clarify. Line 267: please add a reference for rider pelvis pitch rotation. Done Line 268: I’m not sure if I agree with this. Further, depending on the speed of the respective gaits, walk step frequency is not that much higher compared to trot. As this comment could be misleading we have removed the text related to frequency in the sentence. The conclusions are comprehensive and well written, and seem relevant. But the discussion lacks connection to the conclusions. If you go through the discussion according to my suggestion above, I hope this will improve. Thank you. Please also see above. paper_title_zh: 盛装舞步表现影响因素的范畴综述
paper_abstract_zh: 作为实现帕拉马术运动基于证据的分类系统的第一步，明确界定精英马术表现的需求显而易见。先前的研究试图使用科学方法量化有身体能力骑手的马术表现，然而，对于马匹和/或骑手的明确衡量标准尚未建立。这在一定程度上可能是由于马术测试中存在的多种动作和步态，以及马匹与骑手合作的复杂性所致。因此，本综述的目的是识别马术比赛中马匹表现和骑手功能能力方面的客观测量指标，这些指标可能影响他们获得更高的分数。
review_content_zh:
审稿人2 基本报告 见下 实验设计 见下 研究结果的可靠性 见下 给作者的意见 一般意见 该手稿综述了与马术表演相关的科学证据。文本撰写良好，几乎没有排版错误。感谢您的评论。为残奥马术中的残疾等级分类提供科学背景的目的是合理的，但在讨论中这一点几乎没有涉及。我从搜索策略开始阅读，一直读到讨论的结尾，然后才回到引言，当我读到研究的动机时感到相当惊讶。我也想知道这篇文献综述是否是应残奥委员会的要求而写的，还是作者们自己的倡议。该综述对现有文献体有所补充。正如作者所指出的，类似的材料在书章节和当前手稿中提到的先前综述中都有，但所有这些信息并未在同一篇论文中出现。该综述是国际马术联合会委托的一项更大研究的一部分。进行该综述是为了提供知识，以便在未来的研究中选择客观的绩效衡量标准。这些衡量标准将用于评估在后期对健全骑手和残障骑手进行的实验研究中绩效和障碍对绩效的影响。该综述没有发现任何关于残障骑手在绩效方面进行测试的文献，因此手稿本身缺乏信息和讨论。该研究被报告为系统综述，但我认为这里所进行的工作并非系统综述，而更像是一个范围综述。系统综述总结了对同一研究问题进行的多项研究，而范围综述则绘制了与特定问题或兴趣领域相关的现有文献。从研究目的来看，很明显该研究涉及的是一个更广泛的领域，而不是一个单一集中的问题，结果部分并未提供用于指导实践的证据，而是呈现了现有文献的映射和研究发现的概述。这并不是说该出版物的价值较低，但我认为将其置于正确的框架中呈现是很重要的，而且这篇综述也不适合硬塞进系统综述的框架中。本期刊的指南提到了以下出版物，以指导作者选择系统综述或范围综述的方法。Munn Z, Peters MDJ, Stern C, Tufanaru C, McArthur A, Aromataris E. 2018. Systematic review or scoping review? Guidance for authors when choosing between a systematic or scoping review approach. BMC Medical Research Methodology 18:143 DOI: 10.1186/s12874-018-0611-x。我建议您阅读这篇出版物。 关于此问题，使用PICO公式并不适合范围审查，这种搜索策略主要针对干预研究的系统审查，而在您的表格中您指出干预在您的情况下不适用。非常感谢您的建议，并指引我们找到了关于这一主题的合适文献来源。我们已经咨询了UCLan的审查专家，他们也同意该稿件更适合作为范围审查。我们已相应修改了标题和支持性文件。

材料与方法
初步的搜索策略似乎不够理想，所选词汇的组合可能导致遗漏相关论文。然而，我理解您在浏览搜索结果时扩展了搜索，使用了看似相关的关键词。这种理解正确吗？我们的搜索策略旨在捕获所有文献，但从本审查的扩展部分可以看出，我们扩展了搜索。实际上，我们手动检索了所有包含的论文和相关的综述论文，以寻找额外文献。我们在局限性部分增加了一句说明。

从补充材料中难以追踪搜索的发展过程。我不确定所列数字的实际含义，似乎是每个词的命中次数。我认为增加一些解释性注释会使这部分更易理解。抱歉，我们并非有意在表S3中展示搜索策略的发展过程，而是展示了我们在所有数据库中的最终搜索策略。表S3最初包含了每个数据库的标签，并作为追踪每个搜索词命中次数的工作表。这些值本不应包含在初稿中，因为它们对读者不相关，且未考虑到如删除重复项以获得PRISMA流程图中的最终值等因素。表S3现在仅包含搜索词/策略，这与系统数据库搜索相符，即首先单独搜索各个术语，然后应用正确的布尔运算符相应地组合术语/分组术语。

此外，为什么VetMed表格是空的？VetMed表格仅记录了组合后的命中结果。两位共同作者负责报告搜索结果。一位报告了所有结果，而另一位仅报告了VetMed搜索的组合结果（位于表格底部）。两者均与最终结果无关——如上述评论所示。

我找不到PRISMA清单，根据期刊指南，这是系统审查的必备项。但据我所知，这对范围审查并非强制要求。PRISMA清单是补充表S10。我们已经更新了适用于范围审查的PRISMA清单（PRISMA-ScR）。 您的纳入标准似乎表明每篇论文都需要包含关于马和骑手的内容。真的是这样吗？这些标准也不容易理解。我建议您在每个标准之后（除了第一个）附上一个例子。例如，在第二条标准后您可以写上“例如，光学运动捕捉/运动学数据”。如果这表述不清，请见谅。我们已经在文本中包含了例子，并澄清了搜索必须包含骑手和/或马的性能指标。如果能说明搜索的日期会更好，尽管这一信息已经通过搜索的时间跨度隐含给出。我们已经在手稿中包含了日期范围。

结果：请在您列出的包含论文列表中添加期刊、卷号和页码（如果可行）。这将使补充材料对读者更有价值。期刊、卷号和页码已添加到补充表S6和S7中。

对我来说，图2难以阅读，有很多交叉的箭头。图2中所示的关系是基于所审查论文中的发现，还是这些论文作者的提议，以及/或者您自己的推理？请在文本和图例中明确这一点。无论如何，我认为这些相互关系是开放性问题，除了我们已有数据的少数情况。例如，在文本中您说“静止腿将提高骑手提供一致和精确辅助的能力，从而在快步中产生更精细的速度、步态和/或动作变化”，而图示则表明较少的膝关节屈伸对关节运动学没有影响。我们已详细讨论并考虑了您的意见，并选择增强对图表的解释和论证。这包含在图例中，也作为补充信息文本S1的一部分。我们同意这些都是存在有限数据的开放性问题，因此这是一个可以在未来工作中进行测试的“理论模型”。

讨论：我觉得讨论可以更加精简，更多地总结和解释，而不仅仅是报告。讨论中没有明确联系或引用图2。我不是说您需要重写整个讨论，但我建议您带着这个思路重新审视文本。我们已经重新审查了这篇综述中的手稿，并考虑了您关于精简讨论的建议。然而，我们认为这些描述直接关联到图2和图3，并作为这些图表发展的依据。此外，没有任何手稿提供了我们包含的具体描述性能决定因素的详细程度。因此，我们专注于修订来自两位评审员的详细意见，而不是重写这一部分。

第245行：请添加说明，比较小马和高马的适用性仅限于它们以相同速度行走时。 除非我在这方面理解有误。为澄清此句，已添加。第267行：请为骑手骨盆俯仰旋转添加参考文献。已处理。第268行：我不确定我是否同意这一点。无论是慢步还是快步，每步都有两个骑手俯仰周期，且快步的步频更高。此外，根据各自步态的速度，慢步的步频与快步相比并没有高出很多。由于此评论可能产生误导，我们已删除句子中与频率相关的文本。结论全面且写得很好，似乎相关。但讨论部分缺乏与结论的联系。如果你按照我上述的建议修改讨论部分，我希望会有所改进。谢谢。也请参见上文。补充一点，一项实验研究被归类为前后对比。根据我的理解，前后对比研究是非实验性的。如果你有不同的理解，请提供（给我）参考文献。抱歉，已更正。

paper_title: Graph Neural Networks Designed for Different Graph Types: A Survey
paper_abstract: Graphs are ubiquitous in nature and can therefore serve as models for many practical but also theoretical problems. For this purpose, they can be defined as many different types which suitably reflect the individual contexts of the represented problem. To address cutting-edge problems based on graph data, the research field of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) has emerged. Despite the field’s youth and the speed at which new models are developed, many recent surveys have been published to keep track of them. Nevertheless, it has not yet been gathered which GNN can process what kind of graph types. In this survey, we give a detailed overview of already existing GNNs and, unlike previous surveys, categorize them according to their ability to handle different graph types and properties. We consider GNNs operating on static and dynamic graphs of different structural constitutions, with or without node or edge attributes. Moreover, we distinguish between GNN models for discrete-time or continuous-time dynamic graphs and group the models according to their architecture. We find that there are still graph types that are not or only rarely covered by existing GNN models. We point out where models are missing and give potential reasons for their absence.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper is a survey that categorized existing GNNs according to what graph types they could handle. First, they gave mathematical definitions of various graph types and basic GNN architectures. Then, for each graph type, they gave representative GNNs that could handle it. Based on these classifications, the paper identified graph types that many GNNs supported and ones that few GNNs supported and discussed the reasons for the differences. According to the authors, the contributions of this paper are as follows (P2, Section 1): 1. gave a comprehensive definition of the various graph types 2. classified existing GNNs by graph types they can handle 3. related GNNs to each other based on their architectures 4. identified graph types that current GNN research is missing

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
**Strengths** 1. Few survey papers focused on the graph topology (semantic) and classified GNNs according to which topology they can handle (Section 6) 2. The paper not only listed GNNs that support each graph type but also discussed how much and why GNN research for the type was active or not. 3. The paper is well-organized and clearly written. **Weaknesses** 1. There is room for improvement in the description of graph-type definitions. 2. Contributions 1 and 3 above could be stronger in terms of novelty. **Soundness** [S-1] I think the above contributions are well-supported. [S-2] Contribution 1 is discussed in Section 3. Specifically, graph types such as elementary properties (simple graph/hypergraph), temporal properties (static/discrete-time dynamic/continuous-time dynamic graph), and semantic properties (e.g., bipartite/complete.) This paper considered graph types for each property, such as undirected/directed, node-/edge- attributed, and node-/edge- heterogeneous. In addition, special examples of their combinations were discussed, such as knowledge graphs, multi-relational graphs, and multiplex graphs. These definitions are reasonable, although there are some minor suggestions (see Requested Changes). [S-3] Contribution 2 is discussed in Sections 4--7: Section 4 for simple graphs and hypergraphs, Section 5 for static and dynamic graphs, Section 6 for graphs with semantic properties, and Section 7 for combined graphs. I am afraid I have yet to be able to check all GNN models this paper referred to. However, as far as I know, there were no major errors in the paper's classification of GNNs. [S-4] Contribution 3 is discussed in Section 3.2, although it is not explicitly stated in the text. Since the contents mostly relied on Bronstein et al. (2021), this part is not the contribution of this paper. [S-5] Contribution 4 is discussed in Section 8. I agree that for node-heterogeneous static graphs, graphs with duplicated nodes/edges, and continuous-time dynamic graphs, few GNNs support these graph types. Also, the reasons for this phenomenon were reasonable. **Novelty and significance** [N-1] For Contribution 1, giving mathematical definitions of the graph types was preferred because the definitions of these graph types often vary from paper to paper. It certainly increased the readability of the paper. On the other hand, the graph types were not new in themselves. Also, this unification of terminology was mainly for the preparation of the following sections (especially, Contribution 2). Therefore, novelty is limited on its own. Nevertheless, this classification of the graph types serves as a foundation on which subsequent studies will be developed. [N-2] For Contribution 2, I agree with the authors' claim that although there were many GNN surveys for individual graph types (or some of them), few studies comprehensively classified them based on graph types. In addition, surveys of GNNs focusing on semantics are rare. From these points, I think we can recognize the novelty in this respect. [N-3] For Contribution 3, since the discussion follows that of Bronstein et al. (2021), I do not think this part is novel. [N-4] For Contribution 4, the discussion is novel. To the best of my knowledge, little literature has analyzed the relationship between graph types and the amount of GNNs models that supported them. However, I have several questions regarding the discussion on continuous dynamic graphs (see Requested Changes).

**Requested Changes:**
[R-1] P1, Section 1: ,,structure'' -> I do not think using such quotations in English papers is common. "structure" or $\textit{structure}$ are more suitable. [R-2] P3, Section 3.1: >In this sense, a directed hypergraph is a directed graph that simultaneously is a hypergraph In Definition 3.1, hypergraphs are described as elementary. However, this sentence described them as a composition of elementary objects. Therefore, they need to look more consistent. [R-3] P4, Figure 1: I would like to confirm the source of the dog image. [R-4] P5, Definition 3.3: In the definition of growing, $\mathcal{E}\_i \subseteq \mathcal{E}\_{i+1}$ implicitly assumed $\mathcal{V}\_i \subseteq \mathcal{V}\_{i+1}$. Therefore, it is weird that these conditions were connected by the "or" expression. The same is true for the definition of shrinking. [R-5] P6, Definition 3.6: I would like to clarify how the paper used the following terms: structure, topology, and semantics. It looks strange to call graph properties such as complete, regular, bipartite, and so on "semantic ." Also, I could not understand the following sentence in P18: > Although semantic graph properties typically do not explicitly affect the graph's topology, [...] I want to know what the authors intended to mean by a graph's topology -- I think that the properties such as complete are something that I imagine the topology of the graph: [R-6] P6, Definition 3.6: 7. recursive and 10. hyperbolic were not well defined. Therefore, it is difficult to understand these concepts from these descriptions alone. I suggest the authors guide the readers to the reference therein. [R-7] P6, Definition 3.6, 8: Edges in $H$ correspond to ... -> $G$ [R-8] P7, Definition 3.7, 4: The notations $v\in e$ in 1 and $e\subseteq \mathcal{V}$ implied that the graph is interpreted as a hypergraph. It is better to state this explicitly. [R-9] P7, Definition 3.7, 7: random -> randomly [R-10] P7, Definition 3.7, 8: It would be difficult for someone unfamiliar with the concept of metapaths to understand its meaning from this definition alone. It is preferable to provide appropriate definitions or references. [R-11] P7, Definition 3.7, 1: indegree -> in-degree [R-12] P8, Eq. (2): Strictly speaking, GAT cannot be formulated in the form Eq. (2). $\mathrm{att}$ corresponds to $a_{ij}$ of an equation in P.9. However this function depends not only on $x_u$ and $x_v$ but also on all $x_i$'s for $i\in \mathcal{N}(v)$. Nevertheless, it would be too complicated to describe this in a rigorous mathematical manner. Therefore, I think it is sufficient to explain it as a supplement to Eq. (2). [R-13] P9, Section 3.2.4: I think it is better to use a more special character to denote the set of real numbers (e.g., $\mathbb{R}$) [R-14] P9, Section 3.2.4: $\boldsymbol{X}$ -> $\boldsymbol{X}^{(0)}$ [R-15] P10, Section 4.1: > The number of GNNs for simple graphs [...], so the following table does not list all of them [...] I think it is better to write explicitly which table this sentence refers to (Table 1?). The same applies to Table 2 in Section 4.2. [R-16] P10, Section 4.1: The authors referred to GenRecN as an example of GNN for directed edges. Certainly, this paper has 723 citations (google scholar, 2023/1/14) and is a very important study. However, this paper was published in 1997 and is not positioned in the GNN studies starting from the late 2000s. Since one of the criteria for selecting GNN models in this paper is that they are relatively new, I would recommend mentioning other models, such as DimeNet [1]? paper_title_zh: 针对不同图类型的图神经网络设计：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 图在自然界中无处不在，因此可以作为许多实际和理论问题的模型。为此，它们可以被定义为多种不同类型，以适当地反映所代表问题的个别情境。为了解决基于图数据的尖端问题，图神经网络（GNNs）的研究领域应运而生。尽管该领域尚年轻且新模型发展迅速，但已有许多近期综述发表以跟踪这些进展。然而，尚未汇总哪些GNN能够处理何种类型的图。在本综述中，我们详细概述了现有的GNNs，并且与之前的综述不同，我们根据它们处理不同图类型和属性的能力进行分类。我们考虑了在具有不同结构组成的静态和动态图上操作的GNNs，无论其是否具有节点或边属性。此外，我们区分了用于离散时间或连续时间动态图的GNN模型，并根据其架构对模型进行分组。我们发现，仍有一些图类型未被现有GNN模型覆盖或仅很少涉及。我们指出了模型缺失的地方，并给出了其缺失的潜在原因。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文是一篇综述，根据图神经网络（GNNs）能够处理的图类型对现有GNNs进行分类。首先，给出了各种图类型和基本GNN架构的数学定义。然后，针对每种图类型，列举了能够处理该类型的代表性GNNs。基于这些分类，文章识别了被许多GNNs支持的图类型和被少数GNNs支持的图类型，并讨论了差异的原因。根据作者的观点，本文的贡献如下（第2页，第1节）：1. 给出了各种图类型的全面定义；2. 根据GNNs能够处理的图类型对现有GNNs进行分类；3. 根据架构将GNNs相互关联；4. 识别了当前GNN研究中缺失的图类型。

**优点与缺点：**
**优点** 1. 很少有综述文章关注图拓扑（语义）并根据GNNs能够处理的拓扑进行分类（第6节）；2. 文章不仅列举了支持每种图类型的GNNs，还讨论了该类型GNN研究的活跃程度及其原因；3. 文章组织良好，写作清晰。**缺点** 1. 图类型定义的描述有改进空间；2. 上述贡献1和3在创新性方面可以更强。**可靠性** [S-1] 我认为上述贡献得到了很好的支持。[S-2] 贡献1在第3节中讨论。具体而言，图类型包括基本属性（简单图/超图）、时间属性（静态/离散时间动态/连续时间动态图）和语义属性（例如，二分图/完全图）。本文考虑了每种属性的图类型，如无向/有向、节点/边属性和节点/边异构。此外，还讨论了它们的组合的特殊例子，如知识图谱、多关系图和多层图。这些定义是合理的，尽管有一些小建议（见请求的更改）。[S-3] 贡献2在第4至7节中讨论：第4节讨论简单图和超图，第5节讨论静态和动态图，第6节讨论具有语义属性的图，第7节讨论组合图。恐怕我还没有检查本文引用的所有GNN模型。然而，据我所知，本文对GNNs的分类没有重大错误。[S-4] 贡献3在第3.2节中讨论，尽管文本中没有明确说明。由于内容主要依赖于Bronstein等人（2021年）的研究，这部分不是本文的贡献。[S-5] 贡献4在第8节中讨论。我同意，对于节点异构静态图、具有重复节点/边的图和连续时间动态图，很少有GNNs支持这些图类型。此外，这一现象的原因是合理的。 **创新性与重要性** [N-1] 对于贡献1，给出图类型的数学定义是首选的，因为这些图类型的定义在论文之间往往有所不同。这无疑增加了论文的可读性。另一方面，这些图类型本身并不是新的。此外，这种术语的统一主要是为后续部分（尤其是贡献2）的准备。因此，其创新性本身是有限的。尽管如此，这种图类型的分类为后续研究的发展奠定了基础。 [N-2] 对于贡献2，我同意作者的观点，尽管有许多针对单个图类型（或其中一些）的GNN综述，但很少有研究基于图类型对它们进行全面的分类。此外，专注于语义的GNN综述也很少。从这些角度来看，我认为我们可以认识到这方面的创新性。 [N-3] 对于贡献3，由于讨论遵循Bronstein等人（2021）的研究，我认为这部分并不新颖。 [N-4] 对于贡献4，讨论是新颖的。据我所知，很少有文献分析图类型与支持它们的GNN模型数量之间的关系。然而，我对关于连续动态图的讨论有几个疑问（见请求的修改）。

**请求的修改：**
[R-1] 第1页，第1节：,,structure'' -> 我认为在英文论文中使用这样的引号并不常见。"structure" 或 $\textit{structure}$ 更为合适。 [R-2] 第3页，第3.1节：>在这种意义上，有向超图是一个同时是超图的有向图 在定义3.1中，超图被描述为基本的。然而，这句话将它们描述为基本对象的组合。因此，它们需要看起来更一致。 [R-3] 第4页，图1：我想确认狗图像的来源。 [R-4] 第5页，定义3.3：在生长的定义中，$\mathcal{E}\_i \subseteq \mathcal{E}\_{i+1}$ 暗示了 $\mathcal{V}\_i \subseteq \mathcal{V}\_{i+1}$。因此，这些条件用“或”表达式连接是很奇怪的。缩小的定义也是如此。 [R-5] 第6页，定义3.6：我想澄清论文是如何使用以下术语的：结构、拓扑和语义。将完全、正则、二分等图属性称为“语义”看起来很奇怪。此外，我不理解第18页的以下句子：>尽管语义图属性通常不会明确影响图的拓扑，[…]我想知道作者所指的图的拓扑是什么意思——我认为像完全这样的属性是我所想象的图的拓扑： [R-6] 第6页，定义3.6：7. 递归和10. 双曲定义得不够清楚。因此，仅凭这些描述很难理解这些概念。 我建议作者引导读者参考其中的参考文献。[R-7] 第6页，定义3.6，第8行：$H$中的边对应于... -> $G$ [R-8] 第7页，定义3.7，第4行：符号$v\in e$在第1行和$e\subseteq \mathcal{V}$暗示了该图被解释为超图。最好明确指出这一点。[R-9] 第7页，定义3.7，第7行：random -> randomly [R-10] 第7页，定义3.7，第8行：对于不熟悉元路径概念的人来说，仅从这一定义中理解其含义是困难的。最好提供适当的定义或参考文献。[R-11] 第7页，定义3.7，第1行：indegree -> in-degree [R-12] 第8页，公式(2)：严格来说，GAT不能以公式(2)的形式表述。$\mathrm{att}$对应于第9页中方程的$a_{ij}$。然而，这个函数不仅依赖于$x_u$和$x_v$，还依赖于所有$i\in \mathcal{N}(v)$的$x_i$。尽管如此，以严格的数学方式描述这一点会过于复杂。因此，我认为将其作为公式(2)的补充说明是足够的。[R-13] 第9页，第3.2.4节：我认为使用更特殊的字符来表示实数集（例如，$\mathbb{R}$）更好。[R-14] 第9页，第3.2.4节：$\boldsymbol{X}$ -> $\boldsymbol{X}^{(0)}$ [R-15] 第10页，第4.1节：> 简单图的GNN数量[...]，因此下表并未列出所有[...]我认为最好明确指出这句话所指的表格（表1？）。第4.2节中的表2同样适用。[R-16] 第10页，第4.1节：作者引用GenRecN作为有向边GNN的例子。当然，这篇论文有723次引用（谷歌学术，2023/1/14），是一项非常重要的研究。然而，这篇论文发表于1997年，并不属于从2000年代末开始的GNN研究。由于本文选择GNN模型的标准之一是相对较新，我建议提及其他模型，例如DimeNet [1]？[R-17] 第10页，第4.1节：添加对HAN的参考文献。[R-18] 第13页，第5节：[...]，定义3.4 第一个[...] -> [...] 定义3.4 第一个[...] -> [...] [R-19] 第13页，第5节和第16页，第5.2节：本文解释了连续时间图/GNN比离散时间图/GNN更紧凑。然而，我认为这并不是动态图的离散性或连续性的问题。而是图的表示问题。有两种表示动态图的方法：在每个时间步对图进行快照或保存图的变化。后者预计是更紧凑的表示。尽管离散时间图可以采用两种方法，连续时间图只能采用后者。因此，紧凑表示不是连续时间图的优势，而是表示方法的优势。 [R-20] P18，第6节：过度平滑是图神经网络（GNNs）背景下具有特殊意义的技术术语，因此应提供参考文献，例如[2]。[R-21] P21，第8节：此外，[…]它们如何处理这些。-> 它们。[1] https://openreview.net/forum?id=B1eWbxStPH [2] https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/11604

Nevertheless, it would be too complicated to describe this in a rigorous mathematical manner. Therefore, I think it is sufficient to explain it as a supplement to Eq. (2).
